title: Kendrick Bourne Press Conference 8.11.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: I know that uh Mike said that the rest of these next couple weeks are an extension of camp, but as a player, is there something about leaving this and leaving the hotel that >> Yeah. >> Is there a delineation for you? >> Yeah. Yeah, it's actually been new for me. Um this is my first time kind of traveling, going to a different space for camp uh in my recent years. So, it's been new, but um definitely practicing in a stadium has been a joy for me and just like energy, like just the lights, being able to get used to that and stuff. It's you usually don't get that all the time. So, like practicing on another field or at Tempe, um you don't get that feel, but it's been good. It's been helpful. Um and a new experience for me. >> As a veteran guy, do you like playing in the preseason? I know Mike was talking about how some of the guys will get a handful of reps into this game. >> Yeah. Yeah. No, it's exciting to get the rust knocked off. Um camp is definitely for that too, but you get tired of going against your teammates. You know, I'm tired of hitting Buddha. I'm tired of hitting, you know, Dewey. It's It gets annoying. You start to want to take care of each other. Like, we can start to feel like, all right, we're going in between this gap, but we love each other, bro. And you start to feel like, all right, we're starting to get closer to competing against somebody else. So, it's exciting to have that feeling running routes against somebody that hasn't seen it every day. It, you know, you get like tired of running the same route cuz now he knows the route, too. So, those things start to get annoying. So, it makes it more exciting to go against a different opponent. >> Having a previous relationship with Mike before, >> how can you kind of be his how can you kind of help? >> Yeah. Yeah, great question. Me and Mike have a great relationship. Um, he uses me as an example all the time. you know, that's the guy I want to be. Like, he can put me on the spot and I understand where he's coming from. And I want to be coached hard. I want to be coached, you know, real. Like, don't it's not it's not fake. We have a good relationship, but it's not fake, you know, when he's trying to use me as an example to maybe get a point across to somebody else. Like, that relationship's there. So, how I respond and how I take coaching can help another player. Not that he's trying to get a specific player or anything like that. It's just the relationship is there. he can use me as an example and he know I will apply it whatever he's coaching me up on the next time and it just helps the camaraderie of the group of how he's approaching coaching and his intent of like how he's coaching us and um it's been good man he's helped me a lot and uh he's a big reason I'm I'm at where I'm at right now >> about this team during camp >> um I love the energy man um it's funny I I love building man I'm I'm a I'm a builder that's what I've learned about myself over the years um and you say this is a rebuild, but the pieces are there, which is kind of crazy. Um, in my past experiences and uh early in my career, I've been on rebuilds and teams that needed to grow, and I love that process. Honestly, last year, I feel like I was in New England and just to bring up a point, like they made it to the Super Bowl. I missed like the the flowers growing, but just to go through that process with them, that's how I feel here. Like we're building something to get somewhere. And and I love being a part of that process. I love laying the bricks and um going through the camp days, the hard days and building these relationships. It's been fun. Um I've been getting really close with the guys. This receiver room has been one of the best I've been a part of the personalities and so that's kind of how I would answer. I love building and I think that's what we're doing. >> You bring the energy. How would you describe the energy as a whole? >> I think it's great. I have handshakes with everybody. So I'm I'm completely finished with handshakes in the whole receiver room across the board, which is just dope to me. like those type of things mean a lot. You know, I'm I'm building individual connections and um that's something that I take, you know, personal and like how I can speak to Marv or Mike, you know, it's it's different and I'm learning that as I go through even an undrafted guy, Trey or, you know, BG, like it's a different approach and it's been fun. I think the guys know I genuinely mean it. You know, it's not it's not fake. It's not I'm trying to fit in. It's just who I am. And you take it how you want as a player. Like, what's wrong with him? But it's the energy. It's being positive. It's wanting good things to happen for somebody. And we're all competing. So, I try to make it as as comfortable with each other as it already not is like it's we're competing. We're trying to take each other's jobs. So, why make it harder and things like that? So, that's why I try to be positive and have that energy. >> During camp, >> one more time. >> Still vlogging during camp on the on the YouTube. >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, I've been vlogging. I've been so busy, though. It's It's been fun, though. Like, I just had a baby, too. That was fun. So, more short vlogs. More short vlogs, not YouTube vlogs. I have to focus. I got ADHD, bro. I'll be all over the place. So, having being locked in on the playbook um different things, but definitely have joy in everything I do. Trying to have a personality off the field um helps me um on the field. >> Speaking of some of those younger guys, uh the other day, obviously, Brooks had a nice game, Virgil had some big plays. Um even Bryson looks like made to play like how do you kind of see that younger group all trying to as you said trying to find a job? >> Yeah, absolutely. The greatest thing we've all been saying we're making it hard on the coaches. Like that's all we can do. Like we don't want to have a group that's tearing each other down. Like like she I want to build people up. We want to build each other up to make plays. And I think that's what's been happening. So you see it it's it's a lot of encouragement going on. So when the ball's in the air, everybody's rooting for you. you you can feel when you're being rooted for and when you're like being doubted. It's a different feel when the ball's in the air. And I think that's what we've been building as a group. Everybody's confident that they will make the play that we're rooting for each other. I think that's important. So, we got a strong room, man. And and I I tell them every I tell each other we tell each other every day like we're making it hard on them. It's going to be hard decisions and that's just the nature of the game. But that's how we play the game is to make it as hard on cut day as possible for the coaches. Is it when you have those conversations with younger guys especially that haven't made it in the league. >> Do you ever get push back? Do you ever get okay Kendrick, but you've been in the league this many years, you got your bank account like it's easy for you to say that. >> Absolutely. >> No. Yeah, it's real. So, I actually had Trey and Reggie with me in the offseason and it was great. And they were trying to learn me and like learn how I got to where I was at. And um I spent a good week with them and it was it was powerful. But that knowledge of like, hey, you got to go through the process. Like I'm here, you're there. Like you're trying to get to where I'm at. I can't go back. Like, you know, sometimes I wish I could feel I want to feel like you, but um I think it's that like they're trying to learn how to get there. Soaking game and and different things is important. But they've been having those two specific guys been having good energy. Um some guys have been in the league two years, you know, a couple years. Um, I think they have experience and and sometimes when you go through years, you you know how it goes. You know how gritty the game is and how how tough it is. So, I think those young guys have been great of soaking game, not like getting too caught up in, well, I'm not getting no reps. They've been really good of like, hey, when you go in, you got to make a play. And that's why you see our group. Like, I said it the other day, we haven't had a lot of balls on the ground. I don't want to make no jinxes or nothing, but it's the focus. It's it's the intent of our opportunities and I think that's what we're creating in the room. >> Your impressions of Jacobe as a leader at that position and then how did the vibe change when he came back? >> Yeah, great question. Um Jacobe I I was with him in New England and it was great and it's the same model. It's crazy. I seen him in a time where, you know, he lost the job and it was tough for him and I was actually going through ACL so I was in a tough season too and he motivated me a lot and so that experience with him was was different and so to see him over there and now see him here in a position that he deserves honestly I believe and that he's worked for um it's awesome to see him operate in that space and uh it's it's been a process you know he he's still working through like getting connected with us you know we've been having some good days, struggling days, but it's the process. It's the process of contract negotiations, what he went through. But I love the mentality he's in now of being the guy and like leading us, operating, and having good energy, man. Like today, I score my first touchdown in camp finally. Last day, bro, I score my touchdown. I haven't scored in a year, even in practice, and it was long, but to connect with him today was dope. And what was your second question? the vibe around him, I guess, around when he came back. >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. The the the change was it was it was cool. You know, we we know as a group how it goes, you know, money controls a lot in this league and it's just the truth of it, you know, and um that's that's the position he's in. And I'm glad he got it done. You know, contract negotiations are tough and we have to understand as a team like that's what goes on. So, there's no like entitlement to nothing and when you're the guy, you're the guy. And so, we have to all play a role. And I think it was a good transition and we're just working on getting those kinks out of the time missed and I think it's been good so far. >> Congrats on the new addition. What What are you seeing out of Carson so far? >> Carson's great, man. Um just confident. Um really really calm in the pocket and and different things. Seeing his first game is just >> dope to break that ice for him, you know. Um I've seen some reports about, you know, his arm and when he was hurt and, you know, him throwing bombs was just dope to see him kind of put that to bed a little bit. You know, that stuff is is encouraging as an individual. >> Did they show the no look pass in in the beating room? >> Nah. No, he didn't show it. But it's all over Twitter, though, so it was it was that stuff is impressive, bro. Like, and he's having fun, so that's what makes it even better. It's like he's not like forcing it. It's it's instinct and it's natural. So, that's what makes it cool. >> You talked about practicing under the lights and inside the stadium. from a wide receivers perspective, like just how much does depth perception truly matter when you're practicing inside and how much of a benefit is that when most of your games are going to be inside a stadium? >> Yeah, like coaches try to tell us, you know, go out and get touches, throw the ball high, like and see it. And it it's hit or miss though. Like Jacobe has moonballs though, so like he can get it up there. So like with your quarterback, you have to know like sometimes he might be right in that light and it can get tricky. So just focusing your eyes, hand eye coordination is very important. Um, but I think ultimately comes down to running good routes, strong routes, and making the catch as easy as possible. It's never going to be easy, but if you be aggressive, play, we dictate. We try to dictate, and I think that's when you're most comfortable and powerful. But if you're just out there going through the motions and different things, those things can get to you. Like sometimes you got to catch the sun. Like if you're playing outside too, you you have to they say catch the sun. So stuff like that is hard. But when you're focused and locked in, sometimes it just falls your way.

title: Jacoby Brissett Press Conference 8.11.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: So, Mike said that everybody's going to get a chance to play a little bit. What what's your thought process on the preseason? I know Carson Palmer used to tell us that he actually liked getting hit once and to know what it felt like. Are you a like to get hit at least once to know what it feels >> Uh yeah, for sure. Uh you know, I think my last hit was when we played last, January 7th, 8th? So, that was my last time I got hit besides today. Uh I got hit. No, I'm just kidding. Uh yeah, definitely that and then obviously new coach, new system, operation hearing them in the headset, going out there in the game and and you know, just clean communication and operation in and in and out of the huddle. I think that's the the the mindset of this game. >> When we spoke to you last, you had said it was your first day back, but you had said like you you were not fully caught up on the changes in this offense. Where are you at now at a rate? >> Uh I'm catching up uh for sure. But uh no, I definitely uh feel like I've made leaps and bounds from where I was when I first spoke to you guys. Uh but you know, the the thing is it's like we're we're you learn every day in this job and in this position. Uh new coach, new system. Uh so, we're learning stuff new about each other every day, but I feel like my familiarity and my comfortability with the with the offense, calling the plays, getting in and out of huddles, seeing what he's saying uh as he's saying it. Uh I think that's getting better. >> What's the process like [snorts] with learning it? Are you is it actual I mean, are you meetings, studying on your own, flash cards? Like how do you how do you do >> Uh that's a little bit of everything. Uh you know, when he's presenting, trying to call out the plays as he's doing it in my head and we do a bunch of walk-throughs, practice, walk uh then the actual walk-throughs for practice. trying to find you know, every different way to to learn the plays and then as you say it more and more and more, you get more uh comfortable with it and you kind of kind of beat him to the punch on some of the plays. Uh so, it's it's finding new ways to learn the same stuff, yeah. >> What you can tell us what you like most about this offense. >> Uh I think the the the cool thing is how we can do the same thing in 25, 30 different ways. Uh, you know, and it's not new for us and it's new for the de- defenses how we present it and stuff like that. I think that's uh been one of the pretty cool things. >> How [snorts] cool's it been just to reunite with K.J. out here? >> Oh, yeah, it's good. I mean, y'all see. I mean, it's crazy. Uh, legit. Like, I don't think it's another word for him and uh, but the the the I will say the best thing about him is like those are the guys you want on your team. You know what I mean? He comes to work every day smile on his face and a good mood. Uh, you know, sometimes you want him to shut up and stop joking cuz we're getting our ass kicked in practice, but uh, you know, he he keeps it light, but you need you need that around. >> [snorts] >> What what do you like about his kind of skill set out of the slot and what that gives you as a quarterback? >> Yeah, I think I think he's smart. Uh, he's been in the system before. He knows what Mike's looking for. Uh, so he can I mean, he helps a lot of us out uh, at times in the huddle and things of that nature. Uh, his ability to kind of see the the the field through our lens as a quarterback, I think uh helps uh helps get him open a lot cuz he understands the coverages and and things of that like that. >> Do you [snorts] Do you have your own individual handshake with him? >> No, I don't cuz it's going to involve some type of dancing and I'm not I'm not dancing. >> [laughter] >> You seem to be putting in a lot of side work with Marvin before practice, after practice. How's that relationship kind of grown? >> Uh, yeah, I think it's it's I usually try to stay out there with a with a with him, other guys, just depending on the day. I think as a quarterback, I think you the the main thing is the relationship uh aspect of it. I mean, some days we just go out there and we're just playing pitch and catch and some days we're actually working on something. Uh, so I think it's just more of like continuing to learn each other. Uh, you know, and and and putting those reps where there's on the field, off the field and just so that, you know, I I I think I think so much of this football game is about relationship more than it is about actually what you're doing. You know what I mean? If I if I know that he has my back and know, and I have his back, like he's going to go the extra mile and I'm going to go the extra mile, whoever that is. >> You mentioned [snorts] the necessity of a quarterback having good relationships in multiple instances since you've been in Arizona. Is that something you just learned by your time or was there a quarterback when you were young where you realized that's a really important aspect of this job? >> Uh I think uh Parcells and my high school coach kind of like ingrained that to me like as a as a as a a young kid, you know what I mean? It's more of like like you're probably never going to be the team or whoever it is first pick on the team. I mean, you're probably going to get picked, but you won't be the quote-unquote guy, so you better be a good teammate, you know? And I think that's that's helped me stay in this league a long time uh it's the relationship that I've been able to to build with not only players, but the coaches and and staff that I've been a part of. And I think, like I said, when I signed my deal, it's more so like that currency is worth more than me than than anything else because I know when I put my head down at night, I know that those guys trust me that that I'm going to be one of the best teammate that I can be and two, a guy that they can count on. >> Being the starter, does that give you more ownership of being a leader too? Like can you can you approach any differently or just >> a little bit more strong? >> Um no, I I try not to uh more so because then I'm that means who I was before wasn't genuine, you know what I mean? I'm not trying to say, "Oh, I'm the starter, so I can curse you out and stuff like that." That's just not me, you know? I think I think you in the the times of when you don't get what you want, that's who you need to really show who you are as a as a man and as a player and uh and then when you do get pushed into the light or whatever the thing may be that that it only reassures the guys around them that around you that you are who you were when you didn't have it, you know what I mean? So, I don't carry any extra weight as far as like being a leader or anything like that. I think I just go out there and just be me. >> Coming to the end of the part here at the stadium, like the kickoff >> [clears throat] >> Is that a meaningful milestone for you or because we have so much time before the regular season, you're kind of it's you're just moving places now, it's not that big of a deal. >> Yeah, I think it's just moving places and we got more space to to do stuff. I think that's probably the main thing. Uh we're still in training camp, you know, it's not like training camp's over. I mean we what we've been in training camp about two, three weeks and other teams are a week and a half, so uh you know, we we still got a a lot a lot of room to go to grow, uh get better and and uh you know, I'm excited about the the transition to to the other facility because the work doesn't stop. >> It seemed like in the middle of the camp there there was a portion where Marlon was getting getting open pretty constantly. What what have you seen out of him in this camp and where do you think he's at? >> Uh yeah, I think that's the like that's what you're striving for uh is putting us in different situations and see how we come out on top, uh how how we >> react and how do we compete to what it is like get open on this time or or you got to cover this time and things like that, so you learn about each other. I think he's he's taken tremendous steps as far as understanding like this is a long process, the end result is not going to be tomorrow. Uh you know, and that's a battle, that's a battle for him, me, uh everybody on the team is the the hard part is is is you want the results now. You want to go out there and do everything the right way. Uh but that's why we're in the room that we're in and and we have the opportunity to go out there and play in the National Football League because we know we can, it's just a matter of you know, now you got to sustain that competitive edge uh on a day in and day out process. >> What was it like seeing your jersey in the Hall of Fame last >> Uh it was sweet. Uh I mean we were like I mean Marlon we were there like scavenging around trying to find it. It was like tucked away, which is all right. but uh it was cool. I mean just to see like that's my second time there, but actually having my jersey there was the first time and so like it was just so cool to go out there and go there and like guys were like, "Jacoby, where's your jersey?" And I was like that meant a lot just because I mean we got our ass kicked that day, but it's actually a cool moment. And uh I saw Trey's jersey in there and I was just like, damn, like we I mean, technically in the Hall of Fame, you know what I mean? Hopefully nobody breaks the record. But uh you know, I thought that was pretty cool. >> You have you've played a lot of football, but knowing you're going to be suiting up for the first time this season, albeit in a preseason game, do you get any jitters or butterflies? >> Oh, for sure. Oh, for sure. I probably won't eat probably until after the game now. Um but uh yes, I mean, I'm 33 and I'm playing a game that I started when I was five. You know, it's like not a day goes by that when I walk out on that practice field I don't have a little nerves going through me. >> You had mentioned that, you know, you weren't going to lose any more sleep now that you have the contract stuff behind you and you can just focus on learning the playbook, but after that was all kind of said and done, is creating pressure in your eyes as far as like showing that you were worth that deal? >> Wait, what's the question? >> Question is like, do you feel any extra added pressure after after signing a new contract? >> No, I wouldn't say no pressure. >> How would you assess where your relationship with Mike has gotten? Which Mike? Laflour over the last couple years. >> Uh it's been good. I think um you know, like not only do when you go to like when you put us in situations where there's two minutes is first second down, third down, red zone, stuff like that. Like we're still learning each other and like what he likes to call, like what do I like and stuff like that. So, being able to be vulnerable enough to say like, man, I don't like that and him say like, oh, I messed up or I like this right here because of this, you know what I mean? And that that part of the learning part of the relationship, uh I think it's cool. I think I wouldn't say we're best friends because that'll be a lot, you know what I mean? But I do like where our relationship is and you know, the his willingness and my willingness to, you know, merge our relationship and and what he's doing with all the players on the team, you know, he's building his own relationship with guys and um you know, it's been a joy to work with him, you know what I mean? And you see his um you know, he you see his excitement for the team and for us individually is going out there and playing well. >> How's the [snorts] time is good for like a quarterback and a coach to disagree and >> Say that again? >> Like those times to go through the fire and disagree on things to figure out is is that like a must for a quarterback and a play caller? >> Uh a must? I mean maybe, you know what I mean? Sometimes you're going to disagree. Uh I think the the the main thing is is it's like any relationship. Are you going to go to sleep mad? You know what I mean? You going to you might as well get it uh figured it out. But uh you know, I think that's been cool. It's like we've had some type of like I didn't like that or he he's like, "Oh, I like this, but I didn't like what you did." And you got to be man enough to listen to the next person the other person and and what you do after that is is telling, you know?

title: J.P. Shadrick Press Conference 8.11.26| AZ Cardinals
text: This is really I got to say this. This is like I'm used to sitting out here and asking questions. So, um, so be nice. It's awesome. Great to be here. How we doing? >> JP, could you just talk a little bit about the the process and, you know, what your thought process was when you applied and and just kind of your emotions when you went through the whole thing? >> Well, um, you know, it was a little later in the offseason. I mean, it's summertime. Everybody's off. You guys are off. Everybody's kind of doing vacation type things. And and I I saw that um Dave Pashes was moving on full-time to to ESPN. It's like, well, you reach out and see what happens. And lo and behold, it that the process moved along and we uh we got to a conclusion here fairly recently. Um so, it's been um quite a whirlwind just to get over here. I got in here in town yesterday. uh here today, going with the team tomorrow, calling the game Thursday. So, wrapping up life in Jacksonville and then learning the Cardinals all at the same time. It's kind of a crash course. So, that's that's a little synopsis of how it's been really since um since July. >> What got you into uh playbyplay? >> Well, I mean, I I grew up in Alabama, right? So, just outside of Birmingham and I was always a huge sports fan. I was a kid. Uh, I wasn't playing a lot of sports, but always wanted to be around it and didn't really realize that you could, you know, do it until you got to college. I went to Alabama and they have a great student radio program there or did 25 years ago, a long time ago. Um, so I was fortunate to to be on the air for almost every sport except football at at Alabama, softball, volleyball, bad just got experience doing games. And then I graduated and I was I got a job in minor league baseball. So I I worked for a bunch of different minor league baseball teams for about nine years. Five of those in double A and Jacksonville, another in AAA and Oklahoma City. Um so I was on I thought the path to try to be you know Arizona Diamondbacks announcer but not the Arizona Cardinals. Um so that's how it started and then it kind of morphed back into you know with the Jaguars they had an opening and to do pregame and postgame and other content digital content you know that every team in the league does now. but we were kind of on the the front end of that and we helped build that department. There were a bunch of great people over the years from three people when I started to like 40 people running it now. So, uh I've covered a team um every single day in the building for 14 years in the Jaguars, but then started doing playbyplay on the side with Touchdown Radio Network. was some college football games where it where it worked with the Jag schedule similar to Dave and then um that turned into some Westwood one opportunities on college at first and then some NFL games because the Jaguars are in London every year so I would do those games since I'm twiddling my thumbs during the game might as well call one, right? Um so that's kind of the the path in general but uh very fortunate to be here today for sure. >> JP Bob Brock PH Sports welcome. Um who are some of your influences that you kind of follow you want to? Well, I mean, there's so many I, you know, I grew up in Alabama, so it's like Eli Gold, Alabama radio forever, you know, from like 88 until not that long ago. Um, so that's one that was every day. Keith Jackson was television guy, right? If if he wasn't on TV, we would turn down the sound and turn on Eli, right, to listen to Alabama games. Um, but then, you know, when I got into school, you're studying like how do you how do you want this to be? What are your core principles? Like what should it sound like and feel like? And that's I go way back to like Mel Allen, original voice of the Yankees, um, Mutual Broadcasting, all these things. Uh, this weekend baseball at the end, passed in 96, but he's an Alabama guy. He went to Birming, he's from Birmingham, went to Alabama. Um, and then Red Barber was another one, too. He wrote this great book called The Broadcasters. And it's half of it's kind of his life story. The other half is how do you do this business? Like what are how did preparation and and everything that went into his work. So I I study those two guys. But then when I was in college, I started working on the side with CBS Sports on the SEC games as a production assistant, a runner, and then graduated and stayed on with them. And for five years, I was in the booth as Vern Lungquist spotter every Saturday on the SEC on CBS. And I got to watch him. I got to stand right beside him every Saturday. This is Tibo era. LSU's good. Alabama's resurgent. Sabin's coming back from Miami. I mean, there are some banger games every week. I mean, this is big time. I mean, for especially from where I'm from. Um, so I got to stand by him every Saturday and watch how he prepared for games, built his chart, interacted with people in and out of the booth, coaches, ads, the truck, and just how this business should be approached, you know, uh, and whether you know he does it or not, knows it or not, uh, that was a huge influence of, and I'm still trying to prepare like Vernon. I mean, those, you know, I can't quite get there because he was so meticulous on everything. How do you go into Thursday's game? >> Kind of blind, right? And calling this and learning their names, learning everything. Like, how do you go about that? >> I am going to bug the heck out of AQ Shipley for the next two days, and I am going to just be in his hip pocket. You know, he's been here. He's played the game at a high level. Uh, everybody on PR staff is is awesome, too, in the building. Jim Omahandro is like he's back there doing the audio right now, but um he's he's a been so helpful in the transition so far. So, honestly, for me, I'll learn as much as I can the next two days. I've been working already on it, but let's roll the ball out and play. It's a football game, right? And there's going to be 90 guys out there. Starters, you just heard the coach, they're playing. That's exciting, okay, for a little bit. Um, and then we're we're just calling ball at that point. Um, we we'll get deeper into the storylines and and things probably in the second half. That's usually how that goes. Uh, and I'll have more familiarity after as the weeks go here. I'm not concerned about the um there'll be some learning growing pains and that's fine. It's not going to be perfect and show me a perfect broadcast, I'll show you one that's not, you know, and that's kind of how this is going to have to go at least early and um but I'm excited because it's u when the ball's on the tea and there's he score that's always fun. >> Did two of you uh your first visit here actually wasn't yesterday but years ago called a minor league game at Tucson. >> Yeah. So, >> I was in Oklahoma City, which was a a uh Astros affiliate at the time, and the Tucson I think had the Padres's at the time. Uh I think they were called the Padres's. It's a long time. Sorry >> inside the mind of a coach. Um Marv started camp with with a couple of those drops that we talked about in here but then seemed to bounce back. I guess how do you assess his camp overall? >> Um steady improvement. Um, again, I I you know, it's like you could go like very elementary and it's like catch the football, never drop a ball. title: Tua Tagovailoa and Alex Van Pelt speak to the media following practice at AT&T Training Camp
text: two, you were looking good out there. Um, how do you feel like you are playing at this point in training? >> Yeah, I feel good out there. Um, I don't think it's necessarily how good one person or one individual is doing. Uh, that's not how I look at it. It's a culmination of the aspect within the team, how the team's doing, what the run fits looking like defensively, what the run fit feels like for us offensively. And then in a pass game, is everyone where they need to be um when they need to be there within the timing of the play? then you want to look at protections as well. So I think that's that's the starting point with how to look at it. Um from a team perspective without without that I mean you you can't go out there and do your job. So just me being able to go out there it's my job to to get guys the ball. Um you know it's my job to be able to handle the motions, be able to handle the checks at the line and and put us in really good situations offensively. >> I know this is a new offense for you. So, where is your comfort level with those checks, with the command, with with kind of everything? >> With the walkthroughs that we we've had, uh, you start to get more and more comfortable with the terminology, with seeing what the calls would be within the structure of the defense. So, getting comfortable, but it's still something that I need to look over, need to continue to study, and continue to process. What role does the preseason, actually playing in preseason games, you know, play in that getting comfortable with everything? >> Yeah, preseason plays a big role, I would say, um, for your team collectively. Um, you don't have the coaches out there. You got to go out there, you got to make the calls, whether it's right or wrong, you got to live with them. And then from there, you you know, you you come in the next day, you watch film, you talk about it, and and you go from there. But with it being a new staff for a lot of the guys um that were on the team last year as well, I I think they would say the same. >> What's your expectation with playing in the preseason? Pardon? the preseason? >> Whatever whatever is asked of me, whatever is asked of the guys. I think that's that's what what we're going to go with with whatever Stfansky has. >> How did it work in Miami? What do you think got you most prepared for the regular season, preseason down there? Well, I I think the time that I had with with uh those guys and and with Mike from 22 all the way to last year, um you know, we we had a good amount of time together. So, that was a long way to working on timing and and understanding the terminology with what we wanted to get done offensively there. Um but we knew we we were going to play in at least one. So, yeah. >> Right tackle, you guys are kind of working through guys with injuries, different players being over there. How much communication do you have to have with them for maybe your launch point, how they're going to get into their pass sets? Does that change player for player? >> I don't think it changes player for player. Uh, we understand the launch point for for our quarterback position and it's relayed to the entire offensive line. So, I'm not going to the right tackle and saying, "Hey, I'm going to be at this spot." or or Jake and say, "Hey, just know I'm going to be on this spot um on this play." Each play has its own marker for for us in changing the launch point. So, that's something that's communicated in in in our meetings. >> So, we were speaking to Mike last week and he he kind of made the joke that in the quarterback room, he said, "Just be you. If if you kind of get in trouble, get the ball to number seven, let him do the work." You have experience playing with players who are really dynamic after the catch. When you're surrounded by guys like that, do you almost like approach getting them the ball a little bit differently? Do you say, "Hey, let let me get it to him quicker so he's got the space. Let me get it in front of him so he's got the real" Like, what is that like when you have a dynamic after the catch player? >> Yeah, no doubt. I would say just finding a way to get him the ball. Um yeah, you you want to certain balls you want to lead them a little bit, but you know that certain players once they have the ball in their hands a lot of the times the first guy they're going to make miss and we'll see with how it how it goes from there. But um those kind of rack guys that's that's the guys you you want to be able to just get the ball to any which way you can. >> We were talking to ADP out there and he said that the last few days it feels like you're the the system is really clicking with you. Do do you feel the same way and and was there a moment where that kind of clicked? >> Again, I I would say just with the walkthroughs and and being able to I guess get my feet under myself from from the first couple days of of missing training camp. Um feeling comfortable with the system, but it's it's a day in and day out kind of thing where I I got to continue to to study it. Um there's there's some things that you know were terminology wise that we had in Miami that we have here that I still got to get out. And so th those are the things that that I'm working through. >> Anything else? >> You've been asked this already. What's it like working with AP? >> It's cool. Yeah. AP chill guy. Just relaxed in there. Cool, calm, collected. Um, but yeah, it's it's cool. >> What are some of the things that you've taken away from your conversations with AVP so far? >> Well, AP's thing is he he just wants to make sure that we have all the answers before we go out to practice, all the answers before we go out to um to walk through, and that's with communicating the run game to the receivers, making sure our motion landmarks are correct um and where we want them to be, our drops. Um and then kind of to add with with or to to to your point with um the specific point in the pocket where we need to be. Uh so yeah th those those conversations that's that's what it's kind of like with AVP before practice and then during practice it's just let you guys do your thing and then we'll talk about it after practice. >> Have there been any advantages to having two lefty quarterbacks in the room for you? you know, I've I've never experienced uh two lefty quarterbacks in a room uh before, so this is my first time. >> How how has that played out? Is like is it is it a good thing? Like is it positive? >> Well, I think it is it is uh positive uh because you look at the film, you look at everything. Um it's basically Mike and how he's seeing things and how the defense is reacting to him being a lefty. I think it's unique with uh you know with me being a lefty as well and then also like when we're installing too like it's it's an install for lefties for the most part so that's also fun. >> So for the first time in your career the other guys got to adjust not the lefty the righties got to adjust. >> Yeah for the first time. Yes. Yes. Yeah. >> We're getting you on a day it looked like Tuf was looking pretty good out there. What has uh been your impressions so far? >> Oh he he's uh he's getting better every day. I think he's becoming more comfortable with the system and you know the play calls and the protection adjustments and everything. It's uh you know it's tough always come into a new system. So picking that up um you know missing a first part of camp like set him back just a little bit but really the last three or four days he's really come on >> when you're acclimating a quarterback into a new offense. What are the things that you're looking for along the way? Is it confidence in his throws? Is it command in the huddle? What what are those? >> It's a little bit of everything. It really starts with the operation. being able to get in out of the huddle with the proper play call um and then taking the proper footwork or you know the proper action in the run game um and then reading it out properly and making accurate passes. So it's a little bit of everything but it really starts with operation being able to get in and out of the huddle. >> When you say two has really come on what has he done in the last couple of practices to make >> I think the biggest thing that you can tell he's a veteran. He can see the field really well and uh you know if a defense makes a mistake he can he could see that and exploited that a few times yesterday with some throws. Obviously Mike, >> sorry. >> Obviously Mike's not doing team Joels right now. But how do you balance the reps between the pair of them and seven on seven? >> Yeah, it's tough. And right now Mike's taking the majority of the seven on reps because he's missing the team rep. So we'll start to uh you know, we'll start to see where that goes as moving forward. We're starting to get two in a little bit more in the seven on seven reps now. Um but Mike's mainly been the guy that's taking the seven ons. >> How does Michael look to you? >> Really good. Uh you know, throwing it really well right now. I love his footwork. We've done a lot of under center work with him in these seven periods to get him comfortable from under center. Just really proud of the way he's progressed. Can't wait for him to get back. >> Yeah. How much has he, you know, improved in that regard cuz he hadn't really run a whole lot of that handful of years here. I mean, how much has he improved in that aspect? >> I mean, greatly. Yeah. He he was familiar with it. He had some of it in college early on in his career and he looks great and I think it's only going to help us in the run game and the play action game and the keeper game if we can get our quarterbacks to play under center. >> Is is his knee hindering him at all right now? Like is he planting the same, driving the same? Does he look fine? >> I I think he's healthy. You know, he has not uh said anything about it. He'll have, you know, good days and bad days where he doesn't feel great, but I think he's progressing where he should be. >> We've seen some short yardage red zone work from the offense uh this weekend last. As a quarterback, how does your approach change when the field condenses? >> Red zone's its own animal down there. You know, coverage is so much tighter. Um you know, generally you'll have points on the board, so you have to be safe with the ball. Um you know, the timing happens a lot faster. Um you know, open in the red zone is different than open out in the field. You know, it's it's a lot of a tight window throws. So, uh, being precise with your footwork and timing in the pass game down there, then making great decisions, not turning the ball over in the red zone. Those are critical aspects. >> What do you like about the way each of them are digesting this offense right now? >> Yeah, it's been great. You know, we've had some great meetings. Um, the, you know, the room is awesome. Really work hard together, I think, is the the coolest thing. You know, guys will help each other out in the room. Um, you know, it's a system that that has some verbiage to it. So, learning the verbiage has been something they've done a great job. I'm really happy with everybody at this point as far as, you know, making the play calls in the huddle, getting out and getting us in the right play at the line of scrimmage. It's been good. >> Obviously, it takes some time for quarterbacks and receivers to develop that connection. But what have you seen with those guys so far? >> Yeah, it's a work in progress. It always is. Um, you know, those guys have, you know, working hard on the routes, you know, versus air and then taking it on to one-on- ones. You know, we've had some good days on one-on- ones. Um, it's just getting a familiarity with how these guys run routes and, you know, what type of balls they like to catch. You know, is it a back shoulder throw? was it uh you know lay it over the top throw. So just getting to know these guys and working with them day in and day out to try to get that you know that camaraderie. >> I saw one of those back shoulder throws yesterday to Drake. What's it like having a receiver like that that they can throw to? >> It's a big body target, you know, and a guy that can go up and make the play above the rim. So um you know, it's a great weapon for us in the red zone to be able to throw him, you know, multiple routes and they all look the same at the start. You know, one's a fade, then it's a slant and it's it's tough to to defend a big guy like that. When you have one QB who's only running 11s, primarily running 11s, and one who's only running sevens, how do you how do you weigh it? Like when you're evaluating them, how I would imagine you place a little bit higher of a value on 11 on 111, but how how do you weigh it? >> Yeah, it's tough to weigh. You can't really say it's an equal uh you know, scale, you know, team. You got all the bodies around you seven on seven. You don't. It's a little bit uh less stressful in a sevenon seven situation, but you still have to make the right reads and accurate throws. And I think that's what we're looking for when we watch Mike in seven on. when you talked in in May or June, whatever it was, you mentioned that you want to see guys be aggressive and and it's not just completion rate, it's are they trying to push the ball. Um, how I would imagine when you when there isn't a pass rush around you, it's easier to be more aggressive, but it looks to me like with Mike, he is really trying to be aggressive. He's really trying to Yes, >> I would say we Yeah, with Mike right now, he's trying to take the the, you know, the top down throws, trying to throw it down the field a little bit more. And, you know, that's a strength of Mike is to be able to push the ball down the field with his arm strength. So, you see that come out in his play. Do you believe that if he's not cleared for 111 until like late August that over the course of May, June, July, August, you guys have enough reps to evaluate him? >> Yeah, I feel like we do. I I really do. I think uh you know, he's done everything he could possibly do to put himself in position uh to compete. So, you know, it'll be a matter of time when that comes and you know, and then we'll we'll reset and kind of take a look at it from big picture once he's available. >> Do you have a time of when it would help you if you have a quarterback on? >> I couldn't say. That's a medical question. You know, I'm just waiting for them to tell us he's got the green light and then we'll go from there. I don't think we've talked to you since that first like day of camp where it was like okay not cleared Mike not cleared for 11 >> Jack Strand the only guy who can throw bring in Cooper Russian here. >> Can you talk to me about what those like three day that three-day period was like for you and your role in getting and meeting each guy where they were? >> Yeah, it's uh it was a challenge and you know really a tribute to Jack uh being able to go in and operate with the first unit. um a lot of lot of pressure for a young player to come out, especially from a smaller school, but uh he's done a great job. You know, he's super smart guy. He can really rattle the plays off. He knows the reads. He he spends the time and and it showed, you know, he he got us out there and put us in good situations with the first offense. So, really, hats off to him and his work. You know, Jordan Reed does a lot of work with him on the side. Uh you know, a lot of studying with him. That's that's really paid off. And then uh Coupe coming in, man, he's guy came in on a on a morning and practiced and took reps in that morning practice. So that now there's a guy that's a true vet. He's been around the league. He can, you know, he's seen a lot of a lot of defense. He understands, you know, protections. Um makes protection calls already uh you know, in in his first week of being here. So it's it's been impressive. But those guys have worked hard and again Jordan Reed's done a great job with him after after meetings staying spending extra time with him to get them ready. So Kevin said that he he's probably going to like give us an idea of what playing starters in the preseason just like the reps that are going to be given to let us know tomorrow about what that looks like. What's your role in in those conversations because I know Kevin talked a lot about like having conversations with the whole staff to really decide what is needed from each other. >> Yeah. But ultimately Kevin makes those decisions but it's definitely collaborative. You know speaking to Tommy and um you know seeing how much we want these guys to play early on if at all. You know, that's that's something that's collaborative, but ultimately Kevin will make that call.

title: Atlanta Falcons rookies speak to the media following practice at AT&T Training Camp
text: A lot of jugs action for you, Zechariah. >> Oh, yeah. That's daily, man. I got to >> How much you catch? >> I try to do 200. >> 200. >> 200 every day. >> What's the rhyme or reason behind it? >> Um, you know, I just, you know, you never know how many opportunities you'll get in practice. Um, you know, when it gets a lot of bullets flying and things like that. So, uh, you know, I just want to make sure I catch the ball. That's what we get paid to do. Um, you know, we have a lot of talent um, you know, on this team, not even just quarterback room everywhere. Um, but it's just been great to get a chance to, you know, catch the ball from all of them. It makes us want to go harder as receivers. >> What's it been like for you getting to just work with Drake more and learn from him in this camp? >> It's been great. um you know his locker is right next to mine. So when everything uh you know I want to learn from him and just pick his brain on and just stuff he he just reaches out to me and says like oh this whatever on the field or just off the field just talking to me as a regular person. So how does it do you feel like it's I wouldn't say easier but like you were well prepared coming in. I would definitely say well prepared for sure. Um just the way that coach Smart does his practices and just, you know, holds everybody to a high standard. He's on the mic every day making sure everybody's flying around from drill to drill. Um you know, it's pretty much fast-paced the whole time. The whole time. Uh you know, from special teams to team and then we might go live, we might go stud and he going to make sure you getting thuted and wrapped up and you know, you're not running out of bounds, anything like that. So I feel like he did a great job. You know, the coaching staff over there at Georgia has made it a smooth transition for me. Sure. >> Obviously been a mix of thud and live tackling here. I know that you don't know this because you're a rookie, but a bunch of different coaches here have not done live tackling in a long time in training camp. How much does that help you, especially heading into Friday's preseason game? >> I think that definitely helps us. Um, you know, just because it's not going to be the first time that we're getting tackled, um, you know, in a game on Friday, the preseason game. So, it just gets guys to, you know, really hone in and actually help us compete a little bit more, too. Like, once we get out there on the field, it's like, okay, I'm not trying to get tackled by him and that guy's not trying to make, uh, you know, get missed or or get jked or whatever the case may be. So, it really raises the standard for us to, you know, really attack practice as well. Um, and, uh, it makes it fun for sure. Just competitiveness. >> Bejian out there talking a little smack today. What are you like on the field? Are you participating in some of that stuff? >> Um, I think I'm I'm really more I let my game speak for the most part, but if somebody's going to, you know, start something, I'm I'm going to finish it for sure. Um, but I think I'll just let my game play for the most part, get back and try to be be there for my team. But if if my guys into it, then I make sure you know everything is good. For sure. >> Apparently Vjon started it, which is a [laughter] little surprising. And when you see Vjon doing stuff like that, what's going through your head? >> Oh, yeah. I mean, uh, that shows fire and that shows passion. Um, you know, how you play the game and how [laughter] >> somebody's having fun over there. Um, but but that's just cool to see. Um, you know, that's the competitiveness coming out of him. Um, you know, just to go out there and just, you know, make make the others better as well. um you know because some of that chippiness definitely does get certain things going like oh you want to talk to me like that okay let's do it so um you know it gets practice going a little bit and stuff especially from a player like that he's very electrifying >> the relationship with a quarterback especially when it comes to route running it has to develop over time and you're doing that with a bunch of different guys right now how do you work on specifically that relationship >> um you know it kind of just goes to the details I would say I just try to pride myself in the details and being where I'm supposed to be when I'm supposed to be there um just so the quarterbacks can be like okay maybe I didn't get the ball on this play, but they can look back on on film and see like, okay, he was open in this in this point, so maybe next time we get the play, I can go back to him. Um, and then kind of goes to what he asked me earlier with the jugs and things like that. Whenever the ball comes my way, I try to make it uh the best opportunities I can cuz if you're coming down with certain plays, then the QB is going to want to keep coming back to you. So, I always try to, you know, take advantage of those. >> Obviously, you and Drake, two totally different sizes, two totally different receivers. And I think that, uh, goes to account of USC and Georgia as well, preparing me to get ready to go on the field and just, you know, show me how the standard is. Um, you know, but I think I can I can be electrifying and just try to take advantage of my opportunities when my numbers go up. There's been a lot of people that have held you at a high standard from USC to Kirby Smart to now here obviously. What's the personal standard you hold yourself at? >> Um I I definitely hold myself to a high standard for sure. Um you know I'm still mad about that that the 101 earlier. Um you know I should have got that you know it it hit my hands. So whenever it hits my hands I got to be able to come down with it. So um you know always I always do my push-ups every time and I'm like man I'm over here doing too many push-ups. I'm getting swole. I'm tripping. Um, but that's that's goes to the jugs as well. Just keeps me grounded. Like, um, you know, we can always get better. I'm not perfect, but I can always get better. And there's days where you be like, "Oh, I don't feel like doing it." Um, and then there's days where you're like, "I don't feel like doing it." But you still do it, which is going to help you get better for the next opportunity. So, I definitely hold myself to a high standard. Um, and just try to be the best version of myself every day. >> The push-ups are a self accountability thing. >> Oh, yeah. Definitely. Um, I think I started from a young age with my dad. Um, you know, in high school I used to like catch one hand a lot and stuff, too. But now I try to just go two hands. But if I drop one hand, I got to do 20 push-ups. But if I drop two, I got to do 10. So, it's always been like something I've done since I was a young age, and I just been carrying it over to hold myself accountable. >> What were you at today? 10. >> Yeah, I was at 10. Yeah. [laughter] >> How much are you looking forward to just the first preseason game and facing other guys? >> Oh, I'm excited. They've been coming to practice and things like that. So, um, you know, it's always cool and then just to get out there with my guys and just, you know, finally go versus somebody else is something that's pretty cool. So, I'm excited for for that opportunity and and can't wait for it. >> Has there been a rookie teammate that you've kind of really like bonded with or paired up with maybe throughout the camp that's just kind of helping you get through the grind? >> Um, I'll probably say the receivers honestly. So um it's been pretty cool just to get to connect with everybody. Um you know I do a lot of walkthroughs and things like that just to put myself in position. Um you know so when I go on the field I've already done it and I try to be in the right spot for the quarterback and things like that and build the trust of the offensive coordinator and you know the head coach and initially and the team just to be able to you know get more opportunities. No, it definitely is super super valuable. Um, you know, some people may look at it like, oh, we're doing extra meetings, the vets get to leave, but I kind of look at it like I'm getting a a head start. Um, you know, initially, just extra notes. Um, you know, no matter how many times I hear something, I kind of write it down every single time. Uh it may be the first play we ever installed and coach is talking about it again for a play that's tomorrow like I'll rewrite it like I've never heard it just so it like can I've seen myself write it like 50 times. Um so I think that definitely does help us go out there um you know. Oh I'm sorry about that. We're on the field and just be prepared for those moments for sure. >> So you're a notetaker like you have to write it. >> Oh yeah. I think I've had like four notebooks already um throughout [laughter] camp. Um, and I I try to make sure I keep him too cuz I saw I was watching quarterback. Um, so I've been trying to make sure I keep all my notes uh from camp and everything, >> So, did it just start? What are we singing? >> I'm I'm probably singing cuz they said it we they said it can't be a beat or anything. Um, it has to be ac cappella. So, >> uh, you know, I'm going have to try to get the crowd involved for sure. [laughter] >> Who's gone already? Like, have you been impressed or do you feel like you can step it up a notch? So when your name is called you'll be able to perform. >> What has the conversation been about? Just kind of rolls especially when you see a guy like Jaylen Walker going down. just what was your initial reaction and how do you feel like you guys >> you know it was devastating you know seeing him and and you know he's helped me out a lot playing the position playing that edge so it was it was real good and you know it was it was bad seeing him go down but I haven't talked to about to coach Rude or anybody about any role change or anything I'm just going in and I'll do whatever they tell me to do. >> What do you feel like kind of the identity of this offense wants or defense wants to be? fast and physical, you know, and and different and versatile and we want to be feared and we have to install that this Friday when we have a preseason game, you know, we don't take preseason games off. That type of mentality, just a pit bull mentality, always wanting to uh practice hard and go against the offense. >> You appear really comfortable just talking, being loud out there. Why is that? like kind of where does that come from do you think in your game? >> I feel like I've always been like that since I played high school basketball. Uh a quiet defense is a bad defense and so just growing and and you can I was that young guy before like in college not knowing a play and then somebody talking loud it just reassures you of what you got to do. So just being able to communicate helps a lot of things. Even saying stuff during the play or after play you know you're tired but it helps you out a lot. Wearing the green dot of the >> having to say the call. Having to say the call is probably the hardest thing when you're tired having to get a long call to the defense and once you get the call you still have to make the checks and set the front talk to the back end. So, you know, everybody's depending on you to to get the call in. If you're dead tired and you can't get the call out, nobody performs well. >> So, what's the the longest or hardest call you have? >> I can't tell y'all what [laughter] it's called, but it's it's long. It's you just it's saying it the second time. You have to say something one time, you have to say it again, and that's when that's when it comes out as very tired. >> How do you practice it? >> Yeah, I practiced it the first time I ever had to do it cuz in college we did signals. And I would just say it out loud over and over and over because it's something that I never did. So, this will be fun and get a preseason game and get my routine going cuz it's very different in in the NFL. I'm uh I was told that it's very different than a game day in college. There's not a lot of meetings. So, you have a lot of time to prepare your body and do all those type of things. So, it'll be good for uh a lot of the rookies to get into that routine and see my bad. see what they they're good at and what works and what doesn't work. >> All right, Ethan, it seems like you've kind of put some things together over the last couple of days. I feel like the biggest thing is just like attention to detail with everything, you know, like at the end of day like we're athletes, but at the same time to do our jobs at the maximum level, we have to have perfect detail, you know. >> What's the describe for us what it's like stepping from college into a Bill Callahan meeting room? >> I feel I feel like the biggest thing is just really kind of what I was saying earlier, the attention to detail. Like everything's just a lot more detailed and a lot more professional, you know? Like I feel like in college like I mean you rely more on like your athleticism and just how big and strong you are. But here I mean everyone else is just as big as you and like possibly more athletic you know especially like Han. Um but you know just the attention to detail and just like when it comes to the players just like knowing everything that you're supposed to be doing. >> Has hand been the guy that's really open your eyes in terms of that's an >> everyone's been standing out like it's just it's most definitely a higher higher level you know. You seem like you did okay. Kind of. How did that feel? What went into that snap? >> I feel like the biggest thing is just like at the end of the iron sharpens iron. That's what camp is really about is just about getting better, getting ready for the season. So, >> how much are you looking forward to >> I'm excited, you know, like it's really like a dream come true cuz I mean this is a place I've always wanted to be at and kind of see like all my dreams kind of like come together is really an amazing thing. It's truly a blessing. Yeah. >> What's it been like to pick the brands of like a Chris Lynstrom or a Jake Matthews and what have you been able to learn from them? >> Um, I feel like the biggest thing is just like being a professional. Like they're always like on top of like the routines. Like they have a routine pre-practice, postpractice, before they go to bed. Um, and like just like talking to them about just like football and like their experiences are just like kind of like open my eyes to the game. I feel like kind of like coming in is just like you see all this new stuff. It's kind of like Star Wars out there and um like with just like even like Burge like they're all just like great resources that really help me kind of like slow the the game down, you know? >> What is Star Wars look like on the football field? Um you know, Vinnie, um Lamechi, like Riley, um Cam, like they're all just like great people that like we even hang out like outside of here. Like we watched um the Spider-Man movie um last week, you know, together. It was like a rookie group and that was a really awesome experience. Has there been kind of a development of of confidence like, hey, I think I can handle myself at this level just as far as as far as the way the practice has gone so far. >> Yeah, absolutely. Cuz like kind of like what I was saying before about like kind of like it feeling like Star Wars like first coming in. Um being able to like rely on Callahan and Burge and and Chris and Jake. like I've been able to like learn so much and now I have more confidence in like going into team and going into individual and one-on- ones just because, you know, I've prepared for this and like I I've really come a long way since I first came here. >> Ethan, I know you're drinking information from a fire hose right now, but what are some of the more valuable things that you've learned from Bill Callahan so far? I feel like the biggest things are really just like that initial contact, you know, cuz like with guys here like and how athletic they are like if you just give them time to like build up like a rush like it makes your job a whole lot harder. So like you know like fast feet fast hands are like really like the biggest things especially in past pro and also just like being professional like just being on top of everything that you're doing like you not knowing what you knowing like not um your job but also like the guy next to you too and the overall purpose like what we're trying to do and how that kind of like may affect like the defense you know um so really just like a lot more detail on everything that I do. >> You also mentioned a couple of the veterans that you leaned on a bit. I mean, you're in a room with some guys that have played a lot of football. How valuable is that for you? >> It's incredibly valuable cuz I mean, every day I feel like I'm learning something new, not only from Callahan, but also from them, too, cuz like they have their own personal experiences like playing and like they're always like open to for questions and they're always like ready to help, especially like Chris. Like Chris is like a really great guy that I've been leaning on, you know, like I ask him questions like almost every single day and um I'm just really grateful to be in a room like that. When did you have your moment where you thought, "Okay, this is the dream that I've waited for." >> aside from obviously getting drafted. >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. That's what I was about to say. But honestly, I guess like really just like getting to the dorms, you know, like being in the dorms and putting my stuff and I was like, man, like this is really happening. Like I'm really like my first NFL training camp and like how much of a busting it is. So even though the days are long, like this is exactly like what I prayed for, you know, and I'm just so grateful. >> Are you a big Star Wars guy? I'm a good guy. Uh, honestly not a whole lot. Um, movie guy, like I'm kind of starting to get into it, you know, like my favorite movie like Scarface, you know, um, The Irishman, but yeah, like I'm not a huge Star Wars guy. I just had that one reference. >> And then every year we talk about um, you know, the rookies coming in and sometimes they have to put like rookie reports together, conspiracy theories, that kind of stuff. What's going on for the rookies in this class? What have you guys had to do? >> Honestly, like we really haven't done much. I mean, I feel like the biggest thing is like we have to get up in front of the team room and sing a song. Um, like like we just started that, so like but we haven't really done anything like rookie wise. >> Who's already like sang and what song was it? >> Uh, Jack Ving sang um Candy Shop. >> Was he good? >> He wasn't bad. You know, he he tried. >> What's yours going to be? >> Um, that's a really good question. I got to figure that out. >> Has perk point yet? >> No, not yet. That's going to be like musty. >> Yeah. Yeah, that's must see TV right there. I wish I could record that, but >> Nathan, how would you describe this rookie? >> Cool. Appreciate that. Um, honestly, like I feel like the biggest thing is just like brotherhood. Um, I feel like my like my biggest worry kind of like coming in was just like, oh, like this is going to be so business-like that everyone kind of like keeps to themselves, but um like the rookies like we're all like we like all in this together. and even the older guys and the best on the team like like we're really like a brotherhood and I feel like um that that's kind of like rare to find you know I feel like not all places are like this and I'm really grateful for it like I feel like anyone in the locker room like you can just like sit down and talk to you know >> awesome >> Ethan what what's it like going through uh NFL one-on-one drills against uh you know pass rushers kind of the frequency the intensity can you help me understand what that's like >> honestly like the intensity is a lot higher for sure and like you know initially I was kind of like oh man like this is like one-on- ones, I guess, like you know, just like like great guys like Pierce, you know, but um as like I continue to like lean on like the guys in the room and coach Callahan and and um just like and even like the other guys on the other side of the ball, you like I kind of like got more comfortable and learned a lot. So, you know, I'm starting to kind of like settle down and like know and try to like experiment with things, too. Have the defensive lineman after a rep or anything kind of come back to you and been like, "Hey, I saw you did this it, you know, maybe try this next time." Like has >> Um, not necessarily after rep, but like in like the locker room like I'll go to Pierce like, "Okay, like what did you see?" You know, and like stuff like that. Like cuz at the end of the day, like we're trying to make each other better. Yeah.
