title: Ben Johnson: Right now, it's all about building trust | Press Conference
text: Quick update here on Kobe. I got to uh see him today. He had surgery on Friday and uh looks like he's going to be more of a four to six month timeline and so you know he's going to be in a hurry to get back to to help us out there at the end of the year. Um just closing the loop on that one. Uh in terms of where we're at right now, we had a great day yesterday. Uh I think all of our players enjoyed going over to Stevenson High. Um the crowd was outstanding and uh we really felt their love out there. Um got some good work in. And then today we're gonna we're going to rank it. We're going to crank it up a little bit with a scrimmagel like mentality. So um for a lot of these guys on Saturday it'll be their first time going through pregame. So we'll simulate that to a degree and then we we'll have some really good uh team uh call it periods as well throughout the day. So looking forward to that. Go ahead and open it up from there. What happened with uh Kobe that kind of changed it to more of an extended timeline there? >> Um this was what I have been told all along. We we were getting uh opinions on it and so it's four to six months is is what I've been told. >> And that was a knee surgery. >> Yeah. >> With with Luther and Trapillo. Can you offer some updates that on where each of those guys are there? >> Yeah. Uh Luther's going to be, you know, uh hopefully by the the start of the season and Azie still on PUP right now. He he's hitting his hurdles though and he's doing a good job. >> You think he could be back for for training camp because Ryan pulls it? >> Yeah, I mean we'll see how things go, but he he's he's doing a good job working right now. >> The fact that that's even a possibility seems like a quicker than we had thought it might be. Is that obviously a positive? >> Yeah, I mean it's it's a he he's been attacking this thing um headon. He's been here pretty much all summer. I've get gotten to see him every single day it seems like and uh you know he's he's doing a great job with the rehab process. So like I said there's still a lot of things that he's got to hit in terms of making himself available for practice but he's done a really nice job with the rehab. >> Dennis Allen had basically said that Kobe Bryant was like kind of the template for the way he wants other guys to play on defense. That said, how big of a blow is this now? Yeah, I mean Kobe Kobe's the template for how we all want our team to play. Like this is he he was a big part of uh offense, defense, and special teams. The mentality, the mindset, his approach. Um we loved everything about him. And so yeah, it uh certainly takes us back a little bit, but it also provides opportunity for other guys to fill that void. And uh might be guys that we we hope to prod along a little bit, might be other guys that just naturally gravitate to that. But um I think that's the best thing about team sports is normally when when there's a little bit of um open air some guys will step up to the plate and say you know no one else is going to do it so I am. And u and I think that's going to be a fun thing to watch. >> In these last two weeks where have you seen Caleb take or make strides with his problem solving so making calls at the line of scrimmage adjusting protections those sorts of things pre- snap? Yeah, you know, I I think at this point of camp um offense and defense has 98% of their their installs in it and and so you get a really good feel for um just where he's at. I know defensively DA challenges him almost every single day. I think today is going to be a true test to that and we're off the scripts. it's going to be pretty much all call it throughout the day. And so there's there's that organic, you know, matter being able to recognize cover zero when it when it presents itself and any adjustments that we may or may not make within the context of a play. So I think that that'll come to light today. Um, and really going forward. Up to this point, it's been a lot more get the plays in, let's get them repped once or twice, and and now they can actually go out there and execute and play ball. So, um, it's hard to assess where everyone is. I I told the unit today um and Caleb's a part of this as well that today is a big day at creating evidence. We we'll go and we'll meet as a staff and and with Ryan and his crew tomorrow and and uh today will weigh a lot in terms of kind of where everyone stands on the roster right now. You have >> an idea of how much they'll play in the preseason on Saturday. Do you have >> We haven't gotten there yet. We've been, you know, we've had these four day block, four day the block, four day block. We're at the end of that third four-day block right now. Um we'll we'll talk about that as a staff tomorrow and uh probably on Thursday we'll be able to update everybody in the room here with with the plans for Saturday. >> What's your vision see uh Caleb's and Garrett's uh communication uh what the status is and uh do you let that grow organically that or do you get involved in that? >> Yeah, I mean I think that's the beauty of having a guy like Garrett who's been around a few different offensive systems now extremely sharp. um phenomenal communicator. I mean, he's loud, he's clear, he's decisive. Uh love where he's at with all that. I think more than anything, his he he's just been trying to feel us out in terms of the expectations that Roshar, myself, Press Taylor, um that we need out of that center position. And so, it's a little bit different from other places that he's been. And yet, he's doing a phenomenal job uh getting after it. And so the more reps we get, whether it's protection-wise, run gamewise, where Caleb can help, um, he might see things that Garrett doesn't see, and vice versa, so that we we all are aligned and and in the best position to execute the play. So, it's good. It's It's really good. Um, I think they get along really well. >> What's your vision for what entire group? >> Say it again. >> What's your vision for what today will be for the entire group? >> Yeah. No, I mean, it's it's going to be it's going to be a big time practice. It's uh like I said, we're going to simulate the uh the pregame for a lot of those guys that haven't been a part of that yet. Um you know, we're going to start right out of the gate with a short yardage goal line, period. And and uh you know, that was an area that we felt like both sides of the ball could improve from a year ago. And so we're putting a lot of emphasis on that. And hopefully that'll carry over to a lot of these call-up periods, just intensity, competition. Um, we'll have some sometimes where the number one offense goes against the number two defense and and uh, you know, we'll have some some instances of good verse good throughout practice as well. So, it gives everybody a chance to really show show where they're at. Um, and you know, like I said, we're trying to assess may maybe it determines who's playing on Saturday as well and how how good we feel at certain positions. which one we give as >> you guys search for consistency day in and day out. How has he done so far in camp? >> He's done a really good job. I mean, he he came out of the the gate hot there. Um those first four practices I thought were really really good and then as the volume has continued to go up and uh it it's my fault as much as anything just because I I think I put in more this year on offense than I did a year ago um by design. And I just I I want it to feel like a lot right now that there's been a level of plateau up to this point. Now that things will slow down from an installation point, I I think we're going to see him continue to to go on the upswing. >> The fact that he's been that he went through that last year of the handling everything and then it gets whittleled down a little more as the season gets closer. Is that so you felt this is something he can handle now even if it did plateau? >> Yeah. Yeah. I mean and and really it's it's to see how much more he can handle this year than he did a year ago. So we're able to judge that and gauge it. Um he's embracing it really well. I love the process he has right now. I mean, he's he's coming in early. He's staying late after practice, getting extra reps with the route runners. Um he just he's taken complete control of of what we're trying to do and so we're on the right track. >> You said last week that you hope maybe this week you'd have a little more clarity of tackle. >> That'll be a big discussion point tomorrow. Yeah. Go ahead. >> Understood there's a lot of action that's about to unfold on the field. What have you seen from Jedric specifically and then the group as a whole? >> That Yeah. Uh, you know, Jed was a guy that supremely talented coming out of Alabama. Um, started off really well in Cleveland and then obviously the injuries slowed him down. Um, but to me, it's it's the case of a player who is still gaining his confidence and strength levels back up. Um, I think he's starting to understand, man, I I still can play at a really really high level. And um you know, I I keep going back. How well can he pass protect one-on-one? Well, he's got the traits. Long arms, he's able to to mirror uh pass rushers. And so, uh it's all there. It's just a matter of consistency right now. Um and familiarity with what we're doing. He's a little bit behind the other guys just because he hasn't been in the system for a year. So, we're trying to play that all out. And uh and I I I think he's doing a pretty good job. And like I said, we'll we'll have some in-depth conversations tomorrow. Hopefully have a little clarity on on what direction we need to go at that spot. >> Last three, herb, Courtney, and Stacy. >> Coach, usually when we get injury updates in here, it comes from either you or Ryan. When you have a report, a quote unquote credible report that cites sources inside your building that is also so very far from the truth, like we heard with Kobe Bryant. Does that create a need for you to say maybe we need to have some internal conversations about communication or make sure everybody's on the same page with messaging? >> Nope. I'm good. >> You said earlier in camp that the end of half two-minute drill is going to be a big point of emphasis. We haven't talked to you since that Saturday. Caleb and Rome finished off that um inside the red zone. I think it was like a 17 yard touchdown. What do you like or what have you seen from Caleb in the end of half situations that either leads you to believe they're on the right track or there's more that they can improve on? >> Yeah, I mean I think it's it's going to be a lot of u times we got to get in those scenarios too over the course of the next few weeks. And so um we've had a few so far. I think the first time we did it, the ones nailed it. The next time we might have gone three and out. And so it's been a little bit of back and forth. Here's what I love. I love the fact that our offensive unit and defensive unit, they they're all they're taking these situations really seriously right now. Like they know how critical this is for our success. They know how many games come down to the one scores and so um it's a huge deal. >> Can you elaborate on creating evidence? >> Yeah, it's to me it's uh these guys are going out there right now and some practices are weighed a little bit more than others and so this one we're we're there is no script. We had a we sent out a game plan last night or as close to a game plan uh that it would be for a normal game last night so they could study it last night and this morning. And so this will this will come through for us. Who can who can play fast, not knowing what's coming, who can react, who can adjust, and like we talked about, I think it was the first day I was up here. It's it's all about building trust right now. So, not just for the coaching staff, but but for each other's teammates right now. So, um, you know, we got some new faces as we've dealt dealt with some attrition here. And so, what I want to see too is like there'll be some guys on the back end of our defense that haven't played a whole lot for us and who can help them out, who can help them with some of the calls and and things that are coming like that. So, I I expect to see some leadership show up as well today. >> Thank you. >> Yeah. Thank you.

Uh really threw some amazing balls today. So, really proud of Kyle and just I love him. I just spent so much time with him. We had such a good time in Tampa. It's so it's so amazing for me to have another opportunity to be with him uh do this on a daily basis. >> Status moving forward? >> Yeah, week to week. >> Uh we saw Claude out there calling the defense and how with a a a mix-match group, what has he shown you growth-wise over these last few years that makes you trust him in that sort >> Comfortability, command, um standing in front of the huddle, making the calls, uh communicating it to the back half, you know, just talking. Um and then just like his this physical style of play uh continues to show up. So, uh love that about Claude. Uh Trevyn's doing a great job as well. You know, I can't talk about Claude without talking about Trevyn and um you know, just he looks great. I mean, he just continues to just be really comfortable in the defense and finding his shots, finding his ways to make play. So >> Is that a Is that a competition? >> Yes. Yeah. >> You seemed a bit out of breath today. Was something unusual? I was Was something up today? >> Uh had a great workout before and then it's hot, you know, and really this is one of my favorite days of camp. We had live gunner drills today. So, we had the vice, the gunners out there. We had some 20-yard covers for the core, but like in my history, you know, this is one of my favorite drills. It's just there's technique involved, but it it just comes down to who wants it more. Um and so it's a it's a fitness drill. It's a technique drill. It's a toughness drill. Um and I love to see guys emerge and see like when you're exhausted, who's going to win right at the end of it. And um so I get to be out there barking at them. And so yeah, a little little bit more in in this one. >> You got to talk about the ball now today. Devin Lloyd got one on Jaylen. What have you seen from him in in that regard just in his ability to create? >> That's been a part of his game, whether it's intercepting it or causing fumbles. It's It's a reason why he's here. Uh ball production. Um and really affecting the runners and the receivers. It influences the rest of the group. That's exactly what we talk about, what we preach about. And so who better than the Mike linebacker, you know, the guy that's in front of the huddle chasing everything down, punching at it in seven-on, in team, uh different situations. It goes both ways. It affects the defense. It teaches the offense how to secure the ball and not relax after the catch. They have to transition and get their mindset that people are coming for me. I need to secure the ball. >> Uh Dave, going back to the linebacker competition that you said, why um how how have those two approached this competition? Cuz obviously for a moment Trevon was the starter and Claude was kind of learning from him, but also Claude has been in a lot of these systems and has been in the league for a while. So, can you kind of describe how they approached this competition? >> Well, we've needed both of them over the last 2 years. Um with different injuries that have happened to both guys. Got Both guys have have have had to step in there. Um they enter this with a lot of mutual respect. Um I can honestly say those guys really enjoy being around each other, challenging each other. Um so in that regard and with any other guys we tell them like you're not competing against each other, you're competing to become your best and then all the other decisions take care of themselves and I see those guys approaching it that way. They want to help the team in whatever way they can. That's the way they're approaching it and they're challenging each other by how they play and finding new ways uh to try to you know find an edge and grow in what they're doing. So I love the way they're doing it. >> You talked a lot about physicality. How has Trayvon helped set that tone not just this summer but his first year with the Atlanta Falcons? >> Yeah, that's why he's here. Uh we just loved his play style coming out of Las Vegas. Um you know, playing on the edge in the run game, the blitz ability um in the back half disrupting passes with his physicality uh and just the tireless relentless way that he plays with. Not a guy that says a lot, man of few words, um but he speaks with his pads. Uh he speaks with the physicality that he plays with and that's exactly what Dan and I saw in him and wanted a reason why we wanted to get him here and then you had a guy like Layton Ransom, you know, then you know, Zig Wheatley showed in in the game that he'll take shots at guys and you know, he capped off some nice some nice runs where guys were trying to get extra yards and seems to be in really good position. That showed up in his college film as well. So we're just building that room. Nick Scott certainly Nick Scott plays with a physical style. He's not the biggest guy but he's going to hit you with everything he has and uh I just love that mentality. Renaldo Hill's done a fantastic job with that group bringing them along, helping them communicate and use their tools. >> With Dean Peesly other than just calling the games here and now during the preseason, how has he sort of folded himself into this staff? For example, you said yesterday like you and Brad and Gurdy have kind of built this offense over the last three years. On the defensive side, how has Peesly factored into it? >> Uh his history, his years of experience in scheme, understanding the issues of every coverage, and understanding how teams are trying to attack us. That's a valuable asset for E, and they have a ton of conversations about how they should match this, what tools should they use against this. This team is a little different. Um analyzing formations, Cooley's he's a student of the game, so he studies offenses in the off season to see what the trends are. You know, picks our brain, and you know, it's even to the point where, you know, we have a couple of concepts that Cooley saw as trends in the league that we're able to try to incorporate to see if that fits us. So, brings a lot of a real rich experience to the whole staff. >> From when Jalen got here to now to this point, where did you kind of see him change and kind of make his mark on that defense? >> It's just his effort. And this these are things that I heard about him coming out of Miami. Watch um People Darrell Bevell was with him in Miami talking about the tireless way that he practiced, the way that he trains, to take care of his body, professionalism, what a great human he is, all those things. It's real, you know, that's who he is every day, and um and he sets the bar. I love when our when our top guys set the bar for effort and strain because then everybody else has no excuse. Like, this is how we do things, and so um he's he's living up and setting that standard, upholding it, and uh really proud really glad that he's here. >> Any update on Xavier? >> Uh Leggett looked great. Yeah, he he we kept him out of one-on-ones, practiced the rest of the day. Uh he's feeling great. Look looked awesome today. >> Dave, we didn't get a chance to talk uh to S and S yesterday, but AJ Dillon showed up late yesterday. >> Yes. What was the reason behind >> Yes, so uh congrats to AJ and Gabrielle. They had a baby girl named Blair. 8 lb 19 19 uh inches long. Um beautiful little girl, sweetest face. We popped it up in the team meeting, and the guys went nuts. Uh so, big day for AJ. Uh big day for him at the Hall of Fame game, some really nice plays, and then comes home and immediately is, you know, at the hospital, and uh has a new new type of wristband he wore out to practice. I don't know if you guys saw, but he had the hospital wristband still on, so uh but a really awesome moment and a great opportunity for us to kind of see like, hey, that there's life outside of this thing, real people with real things going on. Uh love to factor that in, but congrats to them. >> Any other questions? >> Were you expecting him to come late to practice? >> I wasn't expecting him to make practice, um but he was able to get things settled enough and um they had help there, so he popped out here. We got him warmed up, moved him around yesterday. He didn't practice, uh but today he was back to back rolling. >> All right, thank you. >> [music] [music]

title: Panthers Live Press Conference
text: [music] Heat. Heat. Heat. Heat. [music] Heat. Hey, Heat. >> [music] >> Heat. Heat. fingernails. Down. One easy. >> Coach, >> good morning. How you doing? >> Good. How are you? >> I'm doing great, thank you. >> Awesome. Would you like to start with an opening statement? >> Yeah, first of all, just thanks for coming in on the players day off. I know we didn't have practice today. I made this a little more difficult on you guys, but um no, it's been a great first couple weeks of camp. Uh really excited about the guys. um you know, and the progress they've made, the the details they're pouring into and and uh you know, really Bryce driving the ship and and um the guys doing a great job of understanding like the big picture stuff that we're trying to accomplish. So, uh excited for another opportunity this week in Buffalo to put it all together and and uh make it to come to life. >> Awesome. Thank you, coach. Yep. Uh let's start off with Jeff Hawkins, followed by Alex Zetlo. >> Hey, Greetings, coach. How are you? >> Good. How you doing, Jeff? >> Hey, good. Hey, I'm doing a piece on on offensive line depth. Uh the third and fourth stringers really stood out in the fourth quarter uh in a Hall of Fame game. Um but uh Sam Hec appeared to struggle um to maintain his blocks against 98. What did you see in in Hec's first start and on the overline overall offensive line depth? Yeah, I think anytime you have a young center who's who's making his first, you know, NFL, you know, game time, uh, decisions and communications, uh, he did a great job driving the ship and get everyone on the same page. So, that's always the the first box you want to check as a center. Um, and then the size and speed of the game. I think that's that's something that everybody has to adjust with. Uh, Sam's done a great job going against our guys uh, here. We got some some big ones with Cam Jackson and Derek Brown when he's in there and and uh some of those guys in the interior that he gets great work with them. So, I I have full confidence that uh you know, he's going to catch up to that that piece of it. And and he did they I think they all did settle in like you said, Jeff, like that last drive. Those guys uh doing a great job. And that's a big testament to uh Harold Goodwin, uh Jonathan Goodwin, and uh Dean Ping and and Joe Gilbert getting those guys ready uh at a really quick pace. uh you come back and you have what eight or nine days to get these rookies ready for their first NFL action and and they did a really good job and they they played all the way through the uh the very end and uh really proud of the progress they've made. >> And regarding the running back depth, it's um Miles Davis, has she has he shown enough to be considered for a practice squad spot? >> Oh, Miles done a great job. He picked it up really fast. Uh he does a really good job of of catching the ball out of the back field. um understanding what we're coaching. Um he's uh he's one of those brideeyed guys uh that he he comes in the room, he's always smiling, he's happy to be here. Um but you can also coach him hard and and he puts in the work to make sure he's he's making the corrections he needs to make. Uh that came to life in the game. He had an explosive run there and and then uh you know, you challenge him and trying to stay on the ball. Hey, hey, do we need to take Miles out here? He just had a big 40 yarder. Uh no, no, keep him in there. Try to get him another touch and and uh really really proud of the progress he's made, too. uh is kind of a kind of a late comer in that in that group. >> Hey, thanks. Good luck. >> Thank you. >> Hey Brad, thanks for doing this, man. >> Yeah, absolutely. Alex, >> um so Dave yesterday, or maybe it was two days ago, said that while you were calling the plays at the Hall of Fame game on Thursday night, the headset went out. Can you take me through what that was like and how you kind of navigated that problem? >> Oh, it's everything you ever want, you know, just uh second drive backed up. Um, you know, trying to establish good communication with with Kenny Picket and and uh I got nothing. So, you get you really you try to touch the button and and there's a little beep that that lets you know that you're you're live with the quarterback and I wasn't getting it. So, um just kudos for for Kenny. I mean, having a pro out there and and us us meeting halfway, trying to run out into the field, give him the play, and and get out of the backed up situation and him helping me out, too, uh, communicating to those guys like, "Hey, here's a situation. Let's get back on the ball." Uh, we go to empty to try to steal a completion there. And then, and then he understands, too, a a great opportunity to take a shot when you're backed up and he he took one down the field and and uh that was a little bit on him, too. We we called a uh a completion play and then he ended up, you know, being able to get to the double move to take a shot down the field and get us out of that situation. We get a little bit more field space and now we're end up able to uh send a receiver in, communicate the play with the receiver, kind of old school high school ball there. Um but it it was a cool little wrinkle uh that you don't wish to uh have to go go through, but I'm glad it happened in the preseason. >> Yeah, absolutely. Um kind of sticking on uh the the play calling uh sort of sphere, how do you balance wanting to show who you are as a play caller and also kind of fully evaluate the offense um with also the fact that you don't want to give away too much going into week one. Obviously, this is a point of um consideration considering the starters will be playing this week. Yeah, I think the the biggest thing is um we're we're out here to prove as an offense that we can operate together and it's not about me. It's not about, you know, one player uh making his plays. It's about how the whole thing feels. Um and that comes back to when we meet as an offensive unit and we bring the group into the room. Um I tell them, hey, I'm responsible for how this whole thing feels. So, if anything doesn't feel like it's it's jelling, if the run's not jelling with the pass and the things aren't married up well or we're not uh you know coming off the ball we need the way we need to or it's not urgent enough in the pre- snap. Um that's the stuff that I want to address right away. Um and I'm just really proud of the group whether it was the ones, twos, or threes, the urgency they played with, how everything felt. Uh that's a testament to them to buying into what what I'm trying to, you know, preach in front of the room, what Dave's trying to preach to the whole team. Um, and you know, it starts with those quarterbacks driving the ship, getting the play call in there and letting the the skills and the O line and all those guys digest what that is. And then after that, it's it's the the crisp communication and and the urgency pre- snap. Uh, that's really been putting my thumb down on that. Those guys own that and that's that's what makes it come to life. It's uh, you know, the plays are on the sheet. We teach them throughout the week. Uh, and then those guys make them come to life. So, from top to bottom, those guys kind of buying into the messaging that I'm trying to give in those offensive unit meetings. Um, that's that's really what I'm proud of. >> Great. Thanks, man. >> Yep. >> Uh, let's go with Mike K followed by Cassidy Hill. >> Good morning, Brad. >> Morning, Mike. >> I have kind of an off thebeaten path sort of deep deep cut for you. Obviously, blitz pickup is a really important aspect of pass pro running backs taking on linebackers that are much bigger than them. Um, who is your teach tape that you've worked with from a running back perspective on Blitz Pickup? And why do you think that is such a tough job that not everybody can kind of do? >> Uh, what was the first part of the question? Who's my >> who who who's like your teach player like that you've worked with the or or a couple of players Yeah. that you think do very well and maybe who's who's a guy that stands out in your room and why is that so important? >> Yeah. Well, for one, we have one in the building. His name's Chuba. And Chuba with his eye progression. It all starts with your eye progression. So, um, understanding the importance of going to Joe Gilbert's protection meetings on Monday and Tuesday early in the week and then we get all these, uh, walkthrough reps and getting that eye progression right before you get a live rep. Um, that just puts you in position to not be off balance when you're, you know, when someone's coming through the gap. So, Trouba does a great job of driving that ship and making sure that the rest of the running backs are there with him. Uh, he's done a great job in the past. Uh, you can go back to a guy like Travis Homer in Seattle was really good at it. Rashad White was actually very good at it in Tampa for us. Um, and then there's always there's always an avenue to get on the field by doing that stuff, right? But it all starts with your eye progression, understanding, hey, what's the O line communication that I might not get, but I know where they're going. Um, what are the small signals that you get from from the guys up front that help put you in the right eye progression so you can be aggressive uh to go meet your guy at the line of scrimmage and not let him get into the pockets. But Chuba done has done a phenomenal job. Um, ironically too, I know JB, you know, has dealt with injuries the last two years, but I really commend him too. He's always at those walkthrough uh those walkthroughs at practice. He's getting all those mental reps. Uh, that's going to help him stay on the field all three downs. Uh Trevor's taken a huge step this off seasonason. We've really challenged him with that. We know he can catch the ball really well, but his eye progression was I think uh last year was the one thing kind of holding him back from just going ahead and shooting his gun uh in pass pro and he's done a phenomenal job of taking a huge step that way uh this fall. >> And then from the other side of that, we know Devin Lloyd is a very good blitzer um and a good communicator. What have you as the offensive play caller in practice? What have you seen about Devin Lloyd that has stood out to you when calling plays against him? >> Yeah. Uh he is a very good blitzer. He's a very good pick stunt guy, too. Um because he's just a bigger body, longer limb, so you got to worry about getting your hands on them early so they can't pick off uh for some of the Dline stunts. Um but when he punches out, uh he's a guy who doesn't punch out to a spot. Uh he relates to players. So, there's certain that linebackers out there, they just punch out vertically and you can still rip a ball, you know, in between hook droppers or hole droppers. Um, Devin Lloyd is is playing the game within the game and, uh, he's trying to get a beat on your concepts and he's usually dropping to a spot to start, but then relating to receivers. Um, so you got to be wary of guys like that where they they they run their white line on the page, all right, and then they start to drift with the concept. Uh, so you can't always trust that he's going to be stagnant once he gets to the top of his drop. And that's what Devin does a phenomenal job of. Um, we have great conversations, me and Devin, uh, about, okay, if we're trying to hit an intermediate play pass behind the linebackers or, uh, or any drop back or anything like that, I'm like, okay, what's giving it away that allows you to relate to this receiver so quickly or this tight end so quickly? Um, help us get better, too. And, uh, he'll give me a little bit. if it's if it's not for the next practice, I'm not going to hold him back. Um, but I think going into the season, those are going to be great conversations that carry over and help us as an offense. >> Thanks, bro. >> Yep. And congrats to Mike and Alex. I know there's been some shifting around in your world, too. Uh, big big kudos to you guys. Uh, job well done. You guys earned it. >> Hey, Brad. How's it going? >> Good morning, Cassie. Good morning. Sorry, my video is not working. >> I was like, which box is talking to me? >> I cannot figure out how to make the camera work on my Zoom, so I just I stopped trying. Couple of things here. Canales talked this off seasonason a lot about wanting Bryce to kind of take more ownership of that moment between breaking the huddle and the ball snap at the line, you know, that 10 seconds or whatever it might be. In a perfect world, like what does that look like? What what does taking ownership of that little window look like? >> Um, it's snap point timing. It's it's uh making sure your guys are urgent to the line of scrimmage. Bryce is such a a good processor pre- snap. He can start to read uh what are the intentions of the defense. Um but he needs to get everybody set so we're threatening the defense that we hey uh a legitimate stance by a wide receiver. O line is in an athletic position, not just standing up waiting for, okay, when when does the real true cadence start. Um, those guys need to be in legitimate threat uh, you know, the second they get to the line of scrimmage so the defense starts showing their hands so Bryce can work his magic in pre pre- snap process of seeing, okay, what coverage do I think it is? Where do I think they're bringing pressure? Um, all that stuff is tied in. So him pushing the urgency of breaking the huddle and getting to the line of scrimmage is only going to help him uh you know kind of open up his book of of being able to process pre- snap. And then looking at another guy, Felipe Franks has has had like, you know, a moment every practice or every other practice, like what is it? What is his progression been like? Not only just from a quarterback to a tight end, but kind of into the NFL and and having a couple of different seasons with this offense now, like why is it this camp that he's starting to kind of put things together basically? >> Well, I I love Felipe. he has a good moment of catching and talking trash and maybe being in the middle of a scuffle every single practice. Um that's the first thing he brings his energy. Um so we love his energy on special teams on offense. Um he he brings it you feel it in the team room and uh you always want to have guys that you got to you got to pull the reins back a little bit in the practice setting because you know they're just going to go balls to the wall uh you know in practice and in the game. Um, but then as far as a tight end's concerned, um, every year he's gotten a little bit better with technique, um, we're trying to, you know, get him involved in the run game because he is a physical guy. Um, but then you watch him in the pass game. He's a fluid athlete and he's he's a really long and levered uh, athlete, but he has the ability to get out of breaks. He has ability to set things up. uh he ran a a a crossing route yesterday where it was tight man match coverage and he snapped it off uh clean and it wasn't the perfect look to get him the ball because they had help. Um but just his progression of being able to win verse press um you know has has taken a step. So really proud of like the work that Pat's done with him. Um knowing that sometimes those guys that are in special teams roles, they don't get all those reps that you you would love for them to get on offense. Uh, but here's a guy who, you know, if he's a depth guy for us behind Tommy and Mitch and and possibly JT, then, uh, you know, when those reps come up, uh, you know, he's got to make the most of him, and he has. He's done a a really good job. And then we'll continue to pull back the dog in the practice setting when when he gets a little bit too fiery. >> Awesome. Thank you. >> We will wrap things up with Daryl Horowitz, followed by Joe Pson. >> Awesome. Joe, you want to jump in? >> Yeah. Yeah, I'm gonna jump right in here. Sorry, Darl. >> Joe. >> Um, Brag, good morning. um our um I'm helping one of my colleagues out with kind of a a trend story, but the NFL had a real spike last year in number of plays that were snap offensive plays snapped like with one second left on the play clock. What do you attribute that to? and and you guys were you guys were among the leaders, maybe fifth or sixth, but your number went down as the season uh went along. >> Yeah, you know, I think I attribute to defenses trying to hold shell and trying to disguise pre- snap. Uh long gone are the days where you get very clear man zone indicators. You get very clear one high, two high or pressure uh triggers. Like defenses do such a good job of making it muddy pre- snap. um that I think a lot of a lot of teams are just trying to uh absorb as much info as they can to see if they can get a beat on what the defense is doing. So, it's it's uh I know our defense does a phenomenal job of it and that's why we have to press on our end, the urgency of getting to the line of scrimmage, the urgency of if we have a motion, there's a reason for it to try to get the the defense to undress as fast as possible uh so we're not up against the clock. Um that's a that is definitely a huge trend that we keep track of. Uh and we don't want to be on the back end of of snapping that thing with one second every time cuz uh that'll be the O lineman's worst friend when the defensive line knows, okay, they either snap it now or they're delay a game. Uh they can roar off the ball. We want to stay ahead of the clock and continue to be attacking nature as as much as we can. >> Good stuff. Um thank you. And real quick, um, Kyle Tras, a guy you were with in Tampa, what what does he bring to to you guys? >> He's really tall. He's got a strong arm. Uh, Kyle Kyle's great. He's he's played a lot of ball. He's familiar with our concepts. He's he's relearning our words. Uh Will's working with him on the side. Uh, getting all that extra time to make sure, you know, he can operate uh try to get us through the end of this game and then and then be more comfortable going into next week. Uh but Kyle's he's soaking it up and and I think the arm comes to life, you know, give him a couple play action shots uh yesterday and and uh people see that arm when he has a chance to to stand tall in the pocket and see over the O line and get that thing down the field. Uh now it's just for him it's just catching up with the rhythm of our feet and how we operate uh you know and all the other stuff. So um there's some natural natural stuff that he's used to because he's been with us. Um but we've also expanded since the Tampa days. So, uh, I think he's going to have fun, you know, learning what's new. >> Thanks. >> Yep. Thank you. >> We're going to do one final question from Mike K. >> Hey, Brad. Um, [clears throat] from the dynamics of 12 and 13. You know, Mitch kind of talked about it. How important is it to have the talent level to perform that 13 personnel package that's become popular for a few teams and blending the different talents together >> to use it? >> Yeah. No, no 21 pony questions. No. Okay. Um but yeah, for >> we'll talk about what the pony package is later, but 12 and 12 and 13 are huge and the talent level is absolutely necessary. you're trying to take advantage of of teams that are trying to stay in nickel more often than not. Um, and I think that's the the case around the league. Um, for those teams that do want to go to base, sometimes their their call sheet gets smaller when they're in base because it's not as much of an investment. So, I think you you go and watch the McVeys of the world and and they're in 13 trying to take advantage of base personnel and simple coverages. Um, for us, if you get uh, you know, your core concepts and you feel great about all, you know, whoever is out there uh, in a tight end group running our core concepts, when we have those opportunities for them to to run a smaller version of their coverage playbook, um, then we can take advantage of it by, you know, developing that trust. The Titans have done a phenomenal job this camp. It's been great having I know Tommy and Mitch were out early, but getting them back so we can get more of those plays called um and repped um take advantage of any of the anytime those those defenses don't have, you know, a plethora of coverages or if they want to play nickel and we feel good about our 13 personnel run game, then we can take advantage of them in the past, too, if they ever want to adjust back to base. So, it's kind of playing the cat-and- mouse game. Um but for us, it's just getting those core concepts, uh you know, familiarity with. We really just have our our first week this past week of having all those guys back. So, how many reps can we get as as camp goes to to develop that trust? >> Awesome. Thank you so much, coach, for your time. >> Yep. Thank you guys. We'll see you.

title: Panthers LIVE Press Conference
text: [music] >> Mhm. >> [music] >> All right. Oh, fantastic practice. Um physical, competitive, uh passionate, all that stuff. Um The better each group each side of the ball gets, you know, the more it challenges each other to find those wins. It's in the margins. Um and it takes it to another level. I mean, I'm just seeing verse seeing a lot of even the response we had a little bit of a scuffle out there and the response afterwards was more physicality. Um and that's exactly where we should be. We got to play on that on that tip till that line where we're in pads. We got to play football. That's the bottom line. Um and but there's some situations where we can be smarter and take care of each other. So, I think that's what the frustration ultimately was about. Um I'm all for it and you know I talked to the defensive guys like don't back off on that. Let's just see where our wideouts, receivers, etc. where they're at in those situations, you know, if they if they can't see you, tie them up and hold them up. You know, if they can see you, I want it to be like football other than just we're not going to the legs and all that. So some teachable moments um on both sides really. Defense had a phenomenal bounce back day. Offense won the day yesterday took I think three out of four periods and today defense did did the opposite. So they took three out of four. So just an an amazing response by the guys and and to challenge each other and they're certainly making a conscious effort of working the ball, punching at it and all that. So that's teaching the offense the right way. >> On that specific play what led to the scuffle? Did you have a problem with them defensive backs going at Jonathan >> Oh yeah, I'll keep all that private. That's just for us. >> Luke Corner seems like a pretty mild-mannered guy but we've seen a few times where he's kind of defended a quarterback, defended a teammate. What he did today kind of was a a little over the top but like what what is it about him that you know, he feels like he can I guess defend guys that are smaller than him? >> He's a veteran and I'm sensing and getting to know Luke he's got a real justice streak about him and he just wants things to be the right way. So watching that emerge it's a cool thing. Loyalty to his teammates and all that and so I love the fact that he wants to make sure he's in there and the guys aren't just standing there, you know, to getting whatever type of you know, verbal or physical altercations making sure he gets in there to be a part of it. So >> Did you pull either of the corners off the field after it just to calm things down at all? >> No, I talked to them all. We had a nice break after that period. So we just talked and then hit it again afterwards just as a team and just kind of again just continuing to like sharpen hey these are the couple moments I think that led to the frustration. Here's how we can do better. I don't want you guys backing off. I love this and offense you don't don't to complain about getting hit. It's football. so it goes both ways and guys got to understand that. We're not out here practicing for a different sport. Our sport's physical and so but we can do it the right way. >> Impressive to the quarterback room. What does that do and what what do you know about King? >> Kyle's done a great job in the last couple days just showing up here. A guy that certainly knows the system for the most part with a with the outside of a couple of wrinkles, but you know, being able to distribute the ball so we can evaluate our team. That's what it's all about with the depth at the quarterback position and Kenny's done a great job of that and now Kyle steps in. Really threw some amazing balls today, so really proud of Kyle and just I love him. I just spent so much time with him. We had such a good time in Tampa. It's so it's so amazing for me to have another opportunity to be with him do this on a daily basis. >> Status moving forward? >> Yeah, week to week. >> We saw Claude out there calling the defense out with a mix match group. What has he shown you growth wise over these last few years that makes you trust him in that sort? >> Comfortability, command, standing in front of the huddle, making the calls, communicating it to the back half, you know, just talking. And then just like his this physical style of play continues to show up, so love that about Claude. Trevin's doing a great job as well. You know, I can't talk about Claude without talking about Trevin and you know, just he looks great. I mean he just continues to just be really comfortable in the defense and finding his shots, finding his ways to make plays, so >> Is that a is that a competition? >> Yes. Yeah. >> today more so than usual Who slept today? >> I had a great workout before and then it's hot, you know, and really this is one of my favorite days of camp. We had live gunner drills today. So we had the vice, the gunners out there. We had some 20 yard covers for the core, but like in my history, you know, this is one of my favorite drills. It's just there's technique involved, but it it just comes down to who wants it more. And so it's a it's a fitness drill. It's a technique drill. It's a toughness drill. And I love to see guys emerge and see like when you're exhausted, who's going to win right at the end of it and um so I get to be out there barking at them and so yeah, a little little bit more in this one. >> We saw a lot of pop in the ball last today. Devin Lloyd got one on Jaylen. What have you seen from him in in that regard just in his ability to create? >> That's been a part of his game whether it's intercepting it or causing fumbles. It's it's a reason why he's here. Ball production and really affecting the runners and the receivers. It influences the rest of the group. That's exactly what we talk about, what we preach about and so who better than the Mike linebacker? You know, the guy that's in front of the huddle, chasing everything down, punching at it in seven-on in team, different situations. It goes both ways. It affects the defense. It teaches the offense how to secure the ball and not relax after the catch. They have to transition and get their mindset that people are coming for me. I need to secure the ball. >> Dave, going back to the linebacker competition that you said, why how how have those two approached this competition? Cuz obviously for a moment Trevon was the starter and Claude was kind of learning from him but also Claude has been in a lot of systems and has been in the league for a while. So can you kind of describe how they approached this competition? >> Well, we've needed both of them over the last 2 years with different injuries that have happened to both guys. Both guys have have have had to step in there. They enter this with a lot of mutual respect. I can honestly say those guys really enjoy being around each other, challenging each other. So in that regard and with any other guys, we tell them like you're not competing against each other. You're competing to become your best and then all the other decisions take care of themselves and I see those guys approaching it that way. They want to help the team in whatever way they can. That's the way they're approaching it and they're challenging each other by how they play and finding new ways to try to you know, find an edge and grow in what they're doing. So I love the way they're doing it. >> You talked a lot about physicality. How has Trevon helped set that tone Uh, not just this summer but his first year with the organization. >> Yeah, that's why he's here. Uh, we just loved his play style coming out of Las Vegas. Um, you know, playing on the edge in the run game, the blitz ability, um, in the back half disrupting passes with his physicality, uh, and just the tireless, relentless way that he plays with. Not a guy that says a lot, man of few words, um, but he speaks with his pads. Uh, he speaks with the physicality that he plays with and that's exactly what Dan and I saw in him and wanted a reason why we wanted to get him here and then you had a guy like Layton Ransom, you know, then, you know, Zig Wheatley showed in in the game that he'll take shots at guys and, you know, he capped off some nice some nice runs where guys were trying to get extra yards and seems to be in really good position. That showed up in his college film as well. So, we're just building that room. Nick Scott, certainly Nick Scott plays with the physical style. He's not the biggest guy, but he's going to hit you with everything he has and, uh, I just love that mentality. Ronaldo Hill's done a fantastic job with that group bringing them along, helping them communicate and use their tools. >> With Cooley, other than just calling the games here and now during the preseason, how has he sort of folded himself into this staff? For example, you said yesterday like you and Brad Idzik have kind of built this offense over the last 3 years. On the defensive side, how has Cooley factored in? >> Uh, his history, his years of experience in scheme, understanding the issues of every coverage, and understanding how teams are trying to attack us. That's a valuable asset for E and, uh, they have a ton of conversations about how they should match this, what tools should they use against this. This team is a little different. Um, analyzing formations, Cooley's he's a student of the game, so he studies offenses in the off-season to see what the trends are. You know, picks our brain and, you know, it's even to the point where, you know, we have a couple of concepts that Cooley saw as trends in the league that we're able to try to incorporate to see if that fits us. So, brings a lot of, uh, a real rich experience to the whole staff. >> From when Jalen got here to now to this point, where did you kind of see him change and kind of make his mark on that defense? >> It's just his effort and this these are things that I heard about him coming out of Miami. Watch um people Darrell Bevell was with him in Miami talking about the tireless way that he practiced, the way that he trains to take care of his body, professionalism, what a great human he is, all those things. It's real, and that's who he is every day and um and he sets the bar. I love when our when our top guys set the bar for effort and strain because then everybody else has no excuse. Like this is how we do things and so um he's he's living up and setting that standard, upholding it and uh really proud really glad that he's here. >> Any update on Zier? >> Uh Leggett look great. Yeah, he he we kept him out of one-on-ones, practiced the rest of the day. Uh he's feeling great. Look looked awesome today. >> Dave, we didn't get a chance to talk uh to ask you this yesterday, but AJ Dillon showed up late yesterday. What was the reason behind it? >> so uh congrats to AJ and Gabrielle. They had a baby girl named Blair. 8 lb 19 19 uh inches long. Um beautiful little girl, sweetest face. We popped it up in the team meeting and the guys went nuts. Uh so big day for AJ. Uh big day for him at the Hall of Fame game, some really nice plays and then comes home and immediately is, you know, at the hospital and uh has a new new type of wristband he wore out to practice. I don't know if you guys saw, but he had the hospital wristband still on. So um but a really awesome moment and a great opportunity for us to kind of see like, "Hey, that there's life outside of this thing, real people with real things going on." Uh love to factor that in, but congrats to them. >> Last question. Were you expecting him to come late to practice? >> I wasn't expecting him to make practice, um but he was able to get things settled enough and um they had help there, so he popped out here. We got him warmed up, moved him around yesterday. He didn't practice, uh but today he was back to back rolling. All right, thank you. >> Thank you. >> [laughter] >> Well, >> no, in all honesty though, it's uh it's great to be back at camp and uh certainly um appreciate you all and the job you guys do covering the the Panthers and I know you guys are telling our story the right way and so I really do appreciate you all. And uh I want to give a little shout out, you know, camp in the dog days and we're fighting through uh practice and guys are injured and banged up and they're trying to get the recoveries done and all these things and you know, I just think our athletic performance staff is doing a great job, uh especially the athletic trainers, um Danny and his crew, uh Kaylin, Corey, Harrison, Katie, Karen, they're just phenomenal and obviously all the interns as well, but um they're just doing a hell of a a job with this crew and uh yeah, we've been able to get a lot of quality practice and I just think it's a tribute to the athletic performance staff and the work they're doing. >> EJ, how is Devin Lloyd elevating your defense from a communication standpoint, but also from a physicality and maybe speed standpoint? >> Yeah, he he certainly has uh you know, we knew what we're going to get in terms of the the on the field player and you know, we do our research and so we knew he was a quality guy, smart, all those things and uh you know, we know he's going to be physical, he's going to get off blocks, he's going to tackle at a high level, uh he's going to be great getting the ball out, forcing uh fumbles and interceptions and things like that, but the communication has been off the charts and uh the one thing he does a hell of a job of is he always comes up to me every practice and hey coach, what are you looking for? What do you need to see from me? And then any calls that he's uncertain of in terms of what the situation's going to be, when it's going to be used, when the application's going to happen, he he wants to know. And so, I feel like when I'm on the headset with them, I'm talking to another coach. And I just know that the level of you know, checks and audibles and things like that that we're going to be able to use because of him is going to be it's going to it's going to take us to a different level. So, excited about him and I know it's just it just feels to me like we have another coach on staff. >> On that topic, I mean, you mentioned getting the ball out. He punches one out today. How much does that impact both in front of and behind the other players around his >> Oh, yeah. I mean, it's tremendous. I mean, that's the name of the game. And one it's infectious. He sets a standard for the rest of our defense. Two, he makes our offense better by the way he practices and forces their ball security. And so, yeah. I just value add in so many ways what he brings to our team. >> DJ, how has Will Lee looked so far? >> He's been he's been good. He's been really good. You know, there's obviously he's a rookie and he's fighting through a lot of things. He's learning a new environment. He's learning a new playbook. He's learning new coaches. But, he's doing a heck of a job and you know, one thing that is just like since the day he got here that really stands out is the confidence, right? There's been so many good plays and there's been some plays that obviously he's going to learn and grow from, but his confidence never wavers. He's very coachable. He's optimistic. He's confident about what he's going to do. And we just know that the more he practices, especially going against our receivers and getting a lot of those game type reps, he's going to get better and better and better. And it's only going to help our team. >> How did you feel about your pass rush Thursday night? What stood out, good or bad? >> I thought it was good. You know, we had two sacks. So, we like a little bit more sack production, but I thought we did a good job of affecting the quarterback and I really like the organization between the the rush and the communication up front. Coach Andrew Carter and Coach Washington are doing a great job and that's a big part of our pass rush emphasis this year is just making sure that we're coordinated. We're four or five rushing as one because you know, look at our schedule. We got Caleb Williams to start, we got Lamar Jackson, we got Baker Mayfield and just on and on and on. We got all these guys and so we've got to do a great job of containing the quarterback. >> DJ, you've you've shown a lot of confidence in Clowney over the years being with you pretty much since you got here. Why open up this competition to Trev right now and how do you think both will handle it? >> Well, first of all, they're they're really good friends. They're they're great teammates. They work well together. They're supporting each other. They're challenging each other in all the right ways and so so that's been really positive and look, this is not a knock on anybody. This is just how we feel how highly we I should say we feel about both guys and both guys have over the last couple years have grown a lot in terms of their play and both of them have done a lot a good job of putting some good tape out there and they've also found opportunities to get better from some of the things that they have that hasn't worked out their way. So, you know, I just think that's nature of the beast and really you're always in a competition and I think Trev sees it that way. He knows that he has to play his best and Clowney sees it the same way as well. >> DJ, you've been with Jonathan for a while now. What he's tells us sometimes about how such a numbers guy like he likes to look at the math of it. What does having a mind like that do for your staff? >> Well, yeah, I mean it's tremendous. We we got a such a great staff and obviously Jonathan's one of them and you know, it's kind of funny. We're all almost like a old married couple like we're we finish each other sentences and like we just kind of kind of give each other a look and we know what the other's thinking and but yeah, he he's a tremendous coach. He he sees football at a high level. He can coach obviously the secondary to a high level, but he sees the big picture as well. You know, it's only a matter of time before he'll get his opportunity to be a coordinator. He'll do a hell of a job. But, yeah, it's just such an asset. And he's not the only one. We've got a lot of outstanding coaches and it certainly is good for me to have that support. >> When Dave was up here a few minutes ago, one of the things he was celebrating was the physicality on defense. From a teaching perspective, especially in this environment, what do you share about how to handle that opponent? >> Yeah, no, you know, the first thing is we're on the same team and we always want to be a great teammate. And so, we we want to we want to strive to practice the way we're going to play. And we know that at the end of the day though, we got to protect our team. We don't want to take any side shots. We don't want to hit in the back and those type of things. We don't want to take guys down to the ground. But, you know, at the same time, we've got to get ready to play football and play real football. And so, we've got to be physical. We've got to use our hands. We've got to put our face on people at times. And I know that makes the offense better as well. >> TJ, the safety room just seems to get deeper and deeper the more you see this team in training camp, specifically as a key player. How has he kind of developed this spring and summer? >> Oh, he's doing a tremendous job and really similar to Will Lee. Very confident, very good athlete. He's working through the playbook and you know, it's a little bit more challenging at the safety spot. Just the communication aspect of it, the checks and adjustments, the formation recognition and things like that. And so, he's got a a lot on his plate and he's trying to catch up to the veterans, but the one thing that I really admire about this young man is that he gets out there and regardless of you know, he doesn't make the right call or doesn't make the right play, the confidence doesn't waver and he continues to just battle and and he really did a nice job the other night of playing football, so it was good to see. >> Sorry, another another safety. How much How much input did you have before y'all signed Trevon? And what did you know about his game before he came here? >> Well, I I've been a big fan of his for a long time when he came out of TCU. And so, I've always admired him from afar and watching his career at the Raiders. And so, as soon as he hit free agency, we knew that's the type of player we liked. In terms of what he brings from the physicality standpoint, the feel for the game, the instincts, the ability to make plays on the ball. And so, you know, I I just think Dan and Brent and the the rest of the staff, they do a great job of listening and you know, not to say that I'm going to get my way, but there's always great conversation conversations about what we're going to do with the roster. Whether it's in free agency or the draft or making these cuts in training camp. And and so, and that's all you can hope for and we all know what direction we want to head to. And we do a good job of kind of talking through things and so, and I'm really happy that it worked out with Trevon. >> Was there a moment last year I'm kind of thinking about the joint practice in Houston where he laid out a receiver where where he kind of like where you were like, "Now, that's going to set a tone on our defense." >> Uh yeah, that was that was certainly one of them. But like there's been a a couple of moments in training camp last year where he probably, you know, we're talking about physicality at practice where he probably went over the line, you know, but you know, the thing about Trevon, he don't say much, right? So, he's very quiet and he keeps himself and he's always got a nice smile on his face, so you just you're going to assume that he's a really really nice guy and he is, but he's a killer on the field he's not never going to shy away from contact. >> Are those the ones off the field, the ones you have to watch out for more on? >> Uh only if they're not on your side. No, he he he's great. He's uh There's There's no concerns from that standpoint, but he's uh He's just He definitely brings the personality that you want on the field. >> What did you notice about Willie after he gave up uh the the passing the double move? Like how he responded to that? >> Oh, he doesn't flinch. I mean, and and you know, that wasn't the first time. There's been plays he's given up to T-Mac or Leggett in practice, and and that's what you're looking for first and foremost because there's never going to be a corner in the league that is never going to give up a play. And so, we're looking for the no flinch, no blink, and that's him. He's He's right back to work. He takes the corrections, he takes the coaching points, and uh and I'm I'm loving it that he's getting those experiences now um uh when we have a little room for error. >> Without Turk out there throughout camp, Derek's missing time lately, what are you learning about the rest of that group and and maybe who you can trust that you didn't realize coming into camp? >> Yeah, it's it's been a blessing in disguise. I mean, obviously, we're not uh we don't want injuries, but um you know, that's the nature of it. And we have to adjust. And uh so, it's been really good to see uh the work that uh Jared has done, Harrison Hutton's done, Cam Jackson, um you know, Lee Hunter, uh uh um Elijah Garcia, all of these guys that have come in and uh just they've been working their butts off. You've seen the growth and development in their game, and uh it's good for them to get a lot of these reps against our our starting offensive line and obviously in the preseason game. So, um I've learned a lot. >> It's a lot of fun. >> My opinion, it's the cornerback position. Moving J.C. to the slot, what What is that process been like for you as a coach to convince him and maybe I'm assuming that there's also a humbling process to put him there. And can you just talk about that that >> Yeah, uh you know, that's kind of uh um a sensitive area that I'm I'm trying to finesse in terms of not giving up too much information for our game plan, but uh I will say that uh you know, when J.C. came out of college, uh we did a a of work on him, and um you know, he was the same draft as uh a pastor tan and uh Caleb Farley and you know there's a lot of different opinions around the league in terms of how you would rank those guys but if you guys as you guys all I'm sure know he played a lot of nickel in college and so you saw the blitz and you saw the the run fits you saw the instincts on inside and so nothing foreign there you know we've we've utilized them the way we felt best the last couple years and you know he's obviously one of our best players and so it's my job and our job as a staff to make sure we get them in winning positions. >> Thanks coach. >> All right, thank you all. >> Trying to yeah. >> I'm not to get into your combos but was that about the physicality we were talking a lot from day to day about you guys need to get your physicality in when not to hit when to hit if they can see you was that were you guys kind of clearing the air over there? >> Yeah we just kind of talking that through obviously at this point in camp there's just a level of physicality that naturally happens you know part of that is you know we haven't seen a different color in a long long time the pads have been on it's hot and everything like that so that's part of the game you want it but at the same time there's an aspect of protecting the team and guys that you're going to need on Sunday, for sure. >> What have you seen from How's Devin Lloyd kind of raised the the talent level or the communication on this >> Oh, he's been doing a phenomenal job. I mean, I just give a lot of praise to his leadership skills, his athleticism, and things like that. He's got great cover ability as a linebacker, so he's really been adding to just the efficiency of our our pass game, for sure, getting to his spot and making plays on the ball. >> You've been able to work around Claude and Trev for a few years now. How was that competition kind of brewed and how have you seen them kind of support each other and you guys throughout this process? >> Yeah, I mean, all those guys are just natural leaders. Their presence is always felt when they get that out there on the field. They make the plays that they're supposed to. So, I mean, that in and of itself is just pushing guys day in and day out. We got a really good group of guys that are smart, guys that are physical and know what kind of brand of football we want to play here. So, as long as those guys keep doing their job, pushing guys to the fullest, the best guy is going to be on the field, for sure. >> Did you help organize that conversation just now? >> A little bit, yeah. I mean, some of that stuff just naturally happens, right? Some of the leaders on either side of the ball get together and talk about the things that need to be talked about. That's not the only time we've done something like that. Sometimes it's facilitated by Bryce, myself, Chuba, whoever. When things need to be talked about, we take pride in this being a player-led team. So, we're just making sure that there's constant communication across both sides of the ball. So, we're coming out here and being as competitive and as efficient as possible. >> I just asked Coach G about that. Realistically, how easy or difficult is it for you to I don't want to say pull back, but to tow that line with physicality, knowing what you need on the defensive side of the ball, but also protecting your teammates? >> Yeah, I just look at it like, you know, making it as realistic as possible. I was just talking with Bryce about kind of how I determine whether or not I'm really going to take a shot on somebody or not, and it's kind of like it of like a defensive receiver. If I feel like I have an opportunity to really lay into somebody and I would do it in a game, I'm going to do it here in practice with the exception of wrapping up and bringing them down, right? Um if it's a situation where, you know, it's a leverage tackle or something like that and it's going to be more of a wrap and roll or deal, I'm probably just going to air on a tag off. But anytime we get square to square, face to face, like that's got to be a thud and everybody understands that. Um the running backs do a great job with bringing it each and every play when you get chest to chest. Um and that's the nature of it. I mean, you can't shy away from it. We'll be going up against a different color here in a couple days. Um so, you know, I I I think this team is is a really physical team and takes a lot of pride in that. Um I'm not overly worried about the direction that practice is headed. Um we just got to make sure that we keep doing what we're doing and checking in and making sure that uh we're keeping guys as safe as >> I have another question. Uh it seemed like Bryce took offense to Brooks being uh the the runner on that play where where guys were coming up to take a shot on. >> Yeah. >> How hard is it for you in the moment to know that oh, it was Jonathan Brooks. He happens to be coming off two ACLs or does that even factor in if you knew it was Jonathan? >> Yeah, I I don't think that really factors in. >> Um >> you know, Jonathan's out here. He's with pads on. He's been doing a great job running downhill, running behind his pads. Spoke with him after that and anytime there is spillover like that after a play um and especially if I'm involved involved, I always try to go check in and say like, "Hey, man, like where where you at with that? You felt like that was cheap?" His answer is like, "No, man, like that's it's football." I got to put my pads down. Like that's just the nature of it. As long as we can keep having those conversations, like I I'm not worried about it. I feel like it's starting to turn into something bigger than it is. This is not like the the the sitcom of the Panthers like we're hitting too hard. Like we're we're having fun. Camp is going really well. Um and we're physical a physical physical team, and that's what we love about this team. I feel like day in and day out, um we bring it. And that's what you want. You rather have guys talking about, "Hey, was that too much?" rather than we got to turn it up a notch. Like, this is the least of our worries. We're having a lot of fun. Guys are progressing. We're getting physical, and we're right where we want to be. >> Do you feel like that physicality and competition is evident in the fact that it seems to be alternating every day which side of the ball? >> Yeah, I mean, that's definitely part of it. We We just try to compete to the best of our ability. And like I said, like I I think one of the things that Dave has done an extremely good job of from day one, he's established a standard of physicality like on offense and defense. So, it's just the nature of it. We compete every single day. We get guys that are, you know, going back and forth after the play and everything like that. We try to keep it within the confines of the game, but um when you got the right guys on your team, like spillover is going to happen like that. Like, that's how much people care. Um if if practice was all Kumbaya all day, I'd be a little worried, but it's not cuz we we we're coming out we're trying to do something that hasn't been done here in a long time. And when the stakes are as high as that, the blood pressure raises. Um and if you can simulate camp feeling as serious as it does playing it play out for guys that are going to be out there. Like, that that's best case scenario. >> Depending on who is out there, whether it be Devin Lloyd, Trevon Wallace, um Claude Cherilus, it seems from the outside that those three guys are calling the defense. How has the communication been um from those three guys from you? >> It's been great from my perspective. Um you know, really impressed with um the the step that Trevon and Claude have taken, and then um really impressed with how uh Devin has has walked into this defense and been phenomenal with communication. Um and then obviously the standard with myself and Trey and Layton and the guys that are out there. Um we really take that communication and put it on our shoulders. There's a lot of talking that we have to do. Um so, we're pushing each other day in and day out, but um we try to drive the bus from that standpoint and make sure that we're getting everybody in the right position and helping out whoever's on the field as much as possible. >> Nick, how has Will Levis done so far in your opinion? >> He's done really well. Um he's come in, you know, the first thing I want to see from rookie when they come in is just be confident. Um and he's been playing with a lot of confidence. He hasn't backed down from anybody. He's been making plays on the ball. >> How about uh go ahead. >> I was just going to say, when you have a a coach like Cooley who's so analytical, like what does that do for a defense and especially like defensive backs? >> Oh, I think it does a lot, man. Um he he has a lot of great qualities. Um he does a great job of helping guys learn the game, understanding splits, and uh what the offense is doing, and um we we have been doing a great job of taking that information and applying it. So, what it does is just kind of helps guys simplify the game um and look at the things that are necessary. There's a saying that you guys have probably all heard, see a little, see a lot, see a lot, see a little. Um just trying to shrink that focus and make sure that we're looking at the right keys. And if we're looking at the right stuff, it it simply simplifies the game. We can play a little bit faster. >> What did you know about Tre Avery before he got here? What did you learn about him like right away? >> Marig? Oh. What did I learn about him? And then what did I know right away? I knew he was physical. Um I had no idea that he loves like alternative rock music. I I wouldn't have guessed that. Um but he you know, he knows just about any band or anything like that, any song, but um love what he brings to this team from a personality standpoint. Um love the physicality that he brings. Obviously something that's in his brand. What I also didn't know was just how versatile he was in being able to play on the line of scrimmage at linebacker depth or in the deep end of the field. So, when anytime you have a guy that can make an impact on all three levels, pretty special. >> How much does his play style match his music choice? >> I would say like right on, man. Like it's it's he hits the nail on the head with the rock music, the head banging, physicality. Like he's you know Bash Brothers from the Mighty Ducks? That's like him and Lathan right there. Those two together are like the Bash Brothers. They're so physical and it it's so fun to just be a part of that group and kind of fit into that personality. Thanks, guys. Appreciate it.

title: 2026 Panthers Training Camp Live | August 10th Practice | Carolina Panthers

title: Buffalo Bills Training Camp Review w/ Mike Catalana | Always Gameday in Buffalo
text: ON THREE. >> HEY, Bills Mafia, we know there's one thing on your mind every day. Your team, the Buffalo Bills. So, Matt Bob and S Kapacio are here to bring you the latest news, notes, and opinions straight from the source right here, right now. Because it's always game day in Buffalo. All right, welcome everyone to another episode of It's Always Game Day in Buffalo. Matt Bove here while S is in Coopertown with his son Max for a baseball tournament that they are very excited for. I won't be riding solo the entire way. In a couple minutes, I'll be joined by my dear friend and the captain of the Buffalo Plus team, Mike Catalana. So, he will join me to talk a little bit about what we've seen through 10 days of Bills training camp. And of course, there's that new stadium as well. Actually, I don't want to I don't want to jump to conclusions. I think he'll probably be upstairs, but we shall see and we'll find that out for you. Why would Keon be listed over Palmer?
