It it feels like it's Tommy Dolman's job to lose, but Wishnowski is the veteran. So, I feel like in this case, even though Josh Palmer has been in the league longer, I think because Keon has been in Buffalo longer. Also, I I do think it's legitimately a competition. I don't know right now if I would say it's definitely Keon or it's Jeff definitely Josh Palmer. So, I guess the tie goes to maybe just the guy who either in their mind has the slight edge or the guy who has just been around here a little bit longer. It's been a good competition because I think Josh Palmer has played well and Keon has been fine. And I don't say that with a positive or negative connotation. I think there have been good days and there have been bad days. Last year it was great and then we saw what happened in the regular season. So fine. I don't think there's anything wrong with that. All right, one more question. Uh what does this even mean? another. That's not my I don't even I'm not even going to read the question because I don't even really know what it means. And it it feels like it's somebody taking a shot. I don't know if it's at me or if it's at my TV station, but it's not even really a question. So, I don't know. All right, everybody. It's a weird way to end. I apologize, but I thought it was a normal question and it wasn't. Thank you everybody for listening to Mike Catalana and myself talk about the Buffalo Bills through 10 days of training camp. A lot of things to like. Josh Palmer's looked good. D Alfred has been really solid. Landon Jackson has been more noticeable. You know, I did a story with him in the offseason about him adding some size like 35 pounds. You can definitely tell DJ Moore has been great. You know, I really do think like buy your DJ Moore stock because I think he's going to have a very big role in this offense. Buffalo Bills only one more practice before their preseason opener on Saturday against the Carolina Panthers. I will get something to you either Saturday night or Sunday morning to make sure we've got some thoughts from the game while S is in Coopertown. I'll be holding down the fort here. Thank you to Mike Catalana, Mike Rabier, our producer. I am Matt O. Have a great rest of your day everybody. See you next time on It's Always Game Day in Buffalo.

text: [music] >> Dive into the [music] pulse of Bills football with Turf to Tape, where veteran sideline reporter Sal [music] Capaccio and Film Room Guru Eric Turner deliver a one-of-a-kind podcast experience. This is Turf to [music] Tape. >> This is Turf to Tape. I am Eric Turner, joined by my man Sal Capaccio from WGR. Sal, you're a busy man. I'm sure, you know, you're able to step back, take a breath, but welcome back to the show. We got a lot to cover from that blue and red scrimmage, man. >> Yeah, um it was It's a late night last night. Got back home at about 11:30. I've had much later nights inside that stadium. And when you're when you're inside the old stadium, the gates open for a game, and everyone kind of gets in and they rush down to the wall. They want to be down there by the players, right? They couldn't wait to take videos of the picture of the stadium. It was really awesome, and then they came down. Came down by the walls. And you know, you had your own seat. That's what's going to happen basically coming up. I I shouldn't say it's general admission, but you know, non-PSL only event is going to happen in the next open practice on August 18th. So, for me it was kind of watching the reaction of people and seeing that um the stadium itself, I just think it's, you know, it's beautiful, and there's so many little things inside the stadium to see, and you can't do it in one time there. Yeah. If you're going to games, I would definitely kind of, you know, encourage you to walk around the stadium, see some of the other cool parts of the stadium that you might not see going one time in your in your regular seat. >> And that's that's what's so interesting about in you know, the new stadium. It's it's not just utilitarian, right? It's not just And the at the old stadium, honestly, I would walk in, I'd get my food and drinks and go right to my seat. And now this is there's more to the game day experience with this new stadium. And it I love how you went around prior to the game and highlighted some of the some of those areas. But the field club area is really cool because that's the area behind the bench and that's corral that corral where the fans can stand if you have access. Now, I understand that the majority people don't have access to that, right? But the reason why is, Eric, in the evolution of all these new stadiums, and I've gone to a lot of these stadiums in their first year or second year of existence and things like that, that's been the trend. You have these areas on the field where people can sit. I mean, heck, if you go to SoFi, there's literally suites and lounges on the field with all these chairs and people can sit in. But, this is something new around the league, something that this stadium now has, that kind of goes in line with, you know, all all all the other stadiums in the league like that. So, I think the field club, and then having the access underneath there to the the food and where the players walk through the tunnel, kind of very similar to Jerry World in Dallas like that, that's one of them. Um I think the other one would be really in the in the end zone area where there's, you know, there's an overhang, but you go up, there's the Charge Bar, and >> Mhm. >> people have an opportunity, people have those seats have an opportunity to kind of hang out and congregate in that area and watch the game and um the circumference of the stadium and watching as you walk around to go to see your friends, that's a very very cool aspect for everybody. >> Yeah, I saw a video. I can't remember who posted it, but even when you're up going to your, you know, out of your seat and you're in going in the concourse, you're going to get your food and everything that you still have a pretty good view of the field as you're walking around, how there's a good view, um regardless of where you're walking in the concourse is there. Like that's kind of normal for a lot of these stadiums. So, that was where the the food was great there if we wanted to, you know, get in. There was just so much, you know, content to write and things like that. So, I see somebody I want to just highlight this. Frontier FC looks awesome, but let's get to what was told that was reality. It was it was modeled after Tottenham Hotspur, but from the beginning they said you can play soccer matches. I remember those things being said 3 years ago. Like no, you the dimensions aren't wide enough to have like a World Cup game, but you can have friendlies, but it definitely was modeled a bit after Tottenham Hotspur and I've been to both those stadiums and now, I mean, that stadium this one. So, that that was told from the beginning. >> So, when it comes back to now your role this year is a little different and where you're going to be accessing the field and what you're producing. I'm sure you're kind of working some of some of those kinks out and you probably, you know, had a little dry run yesterday. There was a change in radio and uh my buddy Steve Tasker is now the sideline reporter on the you know, new place where the radio's going to be, but guess what? We're still doing everything we're doing. I'm still going to every game. I'll still be at every stadium and giving you all the great content you need on WGR throughout the week. Um so, you know, just to dispel some myths from people. Um you know, so what is fact and what's reality sometimes uh gets in the way of how people want to perceive things, but look, I mean, I'm still covering the NFL. I'll still be at WGR every single day and talking about it and going to every practice and I'll still be at every game and doing everything on pregame and postgame like normal. >> I'm excited cuz I feel like we're going to we're going to be able to see or hear a little more of you at to the masses, you know, on game day experiences. Uh for me, someone that isn't able to attend all of the games, I'm excited about that. So, when it comes to the scrimmage last night, some news, some injuries, I want to get, you know, that kind of out of the way. Um Conor McGovern ended up uh hurting getting hurt. Also, Ty Johnson. Any updates on either of these two? >> I did not see it live uh until I saw him walking off the field with um head trainer Nate Breske. He had his arm around Nate Breske and they were walking off the field. So, later I did see some video that was posted by some fans who were in the stands and it looked to me like, you know, he was taking a one-on-one rep. He's going against Joey Andrissen. Initially I thought maybe did he slip? I don't think he slipped, but he definitely went down and you know, after a step on the grass and he went to the ground and he was clutching at somewhere near his leg, back of leg maybe. There were a couple different injuries, but we don't have an update on that. >> Yeah. >> So, we'll see what happens now. I mean, if if Ty Let's hope Ty Johnson's okay and he's not going to miss significant time. If he does miss any time, of course, Raheem Davis gets Raheem Davis gets elevated to the main backup. He always talks about him as being the best third-down back in the league. He plays a huge role in pass protection. He plays a huge role in some of those, you know, screens and those third-down situations. He's a pretty important guy um that sometimes kind of goes uh forgotten about. Uh Connor McGovern, I'm hearing that the hamstring popped and and that's why you saw him kind of grab his leg, kind of limp off after I think it was an interception by Benford. >> Um I'm hearing it's There's an MRI today and that they're expecting that it's going to be a few weeks for him. Again, go look what happened, folks. Matthew Bergeron signs, lays the foundation, suddenly Brandon Beane and Sibo's representatives go, "Okay, well, there's the there's the template. That guy got 96 million. Okay, well, how much we going to All right, here, let's do it." The other that I want to ask you, >> James Cook, leading rusher in the NFL last year. We know we've talked about mid zone. He's so good at that. How does Sibo fit with that? Like, you know what I mean? It's Yes, there's the Josh Allen piece, but what about what they've done in the run game and how they run their run scheme? >> Yeah, I I do think you're going to see a lot of the similar stuff. If we're talking concepts for the run scheme, I want to go back to cuz I didn't get to touch upon it. When you talked about involving the running backs in the passing game. And I saw a couple clips. I don't want to get too excited, but I saw a couple clips yesterday of the running backs kind of running those option routes, those Texas routes over the middle where they get lined up uh in the backfield on the backside of a trips formation. So, they're on the backside with a tight end, and it's the running back. And you see the the running back kind of release over the middle, and he can go in, he can go out, he can run that rail route, which we saw KEO actually shut down James Cook on. I think that Pete Carmichael, Alvin Kamara influence is is showing up early, and it's maybe the cat is not completely out of the bag, and we haven't seen the full arsenal of it. But, I think that's that's again, if you want to take this offense to the next level, it's incorporating the screen, which we saw a running back screen yesterday. We saw some of these option routes in the scrimmage yesterday. Um on top of again, adding in expecting Torrence to take another step, cuz they're paying him for you know, his ceiling. He's not there yet. He But, this is that that that time in the career of an offensive lineman that third to fourth and fifth year where they actually make the jump. There have been studies. I think PFF put a study out about the the projection of offensive lineman, and this is that that sweet spot when offensive lineman kind of take that jump, and I think that's why the Bills went out and signed and extended Osiris Torrence uh with this deal. Big money. Obviously, it doesn't happen all in year one, but they're expecting him to improve. They're expecting James Cook in these running backs to add in the passing game as well. >> And James Cook, you know, doing what he did last year in the run game, people ask me all the time, you know, can he replicate that? I mean, I I I would take you over 300 carries again like he had. I don't know if they're going to do >> But, with what you're saying and what we're seeing, and going back to when I mentioned it many times, Pete Carmichael is influence. He was in San Diego, LaDainian Tomlinson, Alvin Kamara, Norv Turner offensive tree. Um I wouldn't be surprised if James Cook has you know, more touches about the same amount of touches, maybe a little bit less, but they might come in a different form, no doubt. Um, but I think Torrence is a guy they feel comfortable with in any kind of run scheme that they're going to run and was a big part of what they did last year and how he fits into their zone run >> Yeah, and and real quick, as far as the run scheme goes, I I do think there are some question marks there because as we know, Aaron Kromer was the run game coordinator. Aaron Kromer called the runs and set up those runs on game days. So, again, that relationship between Pat Meyer, the offensive line coach, whoever's calling or designing those runs, who's in charge of that game planning and strategizing in during the week, that to me, that is a big story that no one's talking about and that we need to keep an eye on because that is, I think, where we're going to see some growing pains, some and maybe some of that synergy that we we're not going to have because Aaron Kromer did retire. >> For sure. And Pat Meyer worked under Aaron Kromer here in Buffalo the first time Kromer was here, but he is now the guy in charge of the offensive line. So, you know, a lot of the terminology will be the same, but you're right. Aaron Kromer not only was an offensive line coach, he had been an offensive coordinator play caller, he was an interim head coach. You know, he he he was very good at what he did and I think, you know, Pat Meyer is going to I I don't know if there's like I say like pressure on him to live up to that kind of standard, but I think he's got big shoes to fill. >> He does. Big shoes to fill. Well, with that said, Sal, great episode. Let everyone know where they can find you, what you got going on week, the schedule, what what's what's going on in on Sal's schedule this week when it comes to content. >> Folks, I will be gone this week, not covering the Buffalo Bills. Paul Hamilton's got you covered with the Buffalo Bills all week. >> He'll be at practice. But I can't wait. In the meantime, South Sports obviously on all social platforms. And maybe I'll be checking in on WGR every once in a while, right? Doesn't have to be It could be It doesn't have to be all play. It could be all a little bit of work, but cannot wait. Let's go. title: Jordan Love speaks on playing in preseason, learning from Aaron Rodgers
text: Yeah. No, there's always obviously, you know, what happened last year, uh, it sucked. It was very tough. You know, I'm glad [snorts] that, uh, the timeline was what it was and I was able to be good, uh, for week one, but, uh, yeah, it's definitely one of those things you got to take in consideration, uh, going into preseason, everything. So, um, I know me and Matt have talked and, uh, I think the plan is to play some limited role this week um, and see how it goes going forward, but that's always, you know, something that you got to be smart when you're out there uh, trying to avoid taking hits, things like that. Um, but you know, it is football. >> So, it's safe to say you play a little differently in the in if you're going to play in a preseason game, you're actually trying to play a little different than you would in a regular season. >> Yeah, I think the the main thing, uh, is to, you know, stay healthy, obviously, avoid taking hits. You know, if you get into a scramble situation, definitely not take any hits outside of pocket, anything like that. But, uh, really, it's just about being smart. Um, trying to get the ball out of your hands, find those completions, um, put together good drives. undo some of your uh footwork uh work that you've done this year and go back to the fall away jumper if necessary. >> Oh, you might have to. Um you know, you hope you're not getting any pressure like that. Um but like I said, if you're trying to avoid a hit, you know, whatever it takes to get the ball out, um throw it away, you know, so you might see it. We'll see. >> I know Matt was saying this because he thinks players benefit from playing at least a little bit in the preseason. It helps them early in the season. Do you like playing in the preseason if getting at least a few reps or >> Yeah. No, I think it's always good. I think it uh gets you in the right mindset. It just gets you back in that real game feel. Um obviously we've been going against each other in practice to be able to see, you know, new looks, a new defense, different guys out there. Um I think it's all good stuff that uh just gets you in the right mindset going into week one. >> How does that compare to like playing in a joint practice in terms of prepare preparing him? >> Yeah, I think they're they're both a little different. I think joint practices are great because I think you see a lot more a lot more coverages, a lot more pressures, things like that. Um, the teams want to show where I think in the preseason games, uh, you know, it's a little bit more basic. Don't want to show too much. So, uh, you kind of know what you're getting in the games where I think practice is, uh, definitely, you know, a real real game atmosphere in terms of the concepts and pressures, things like that you're seeing from a defense. >> Has he checked to see if the run's playing? >> I haven't checked. I have not checked. him or anything to make. >> Yeah, I haven't checked. We'll see. We'll be finding out soon. >> Um, speaking of, I know Tom prepares you for all these. Have you seen this clip of Matt Laflure talking about how you're the best to ever do it that he's been around at the line of scrimmage setting protections? Have you seen that? >> I haven't seen it. No, >> you've heard about it, I presume? >> Yeah. Yeah. >> Okay, >> Tom, let me know about that. So, how does that feel to uh that the student has surpassed the teacher and that he puts you he had a chance to say that Aaron was still better and he did not. So, what does that tell you about how far you've come and what does that mean to you that he would say that? Well, >> that's great. Um, you know, I think uh obviously appreciate Matt, you know, saying stuff like that. Um, and you know, it's something that obviously like he I mean he mentioned protection stuff like that's something I've worked at and you know we've gone and me and Matt together put a lot of work in just communicating on stuff and obviously he's got a big big part in that of you know my development and getting me better and us being on the same page with stuff. So um I think you know anytime you can say something like that is very cool to hear. Where do you think you were in that department coming out of Utah State and even the couple years, you know, when you were a backup >> protection stuff? Yeah. >> Oh man, it's come that's probably the the biggest jump I've made uh since being here. Um in college, you know, it was we didn't do anything. We didn't handle protections. Like we just we threw hot if we got pressure. We didn't make any change to the line of scrimmage. So getting to the NFL, that was the biggest kind of test for me, the biggest um area where I just had had never done stuff like that. So obviously, you know, I think being able to sit behind Aaron um and see just the way he was able to control the line of scrimmage, see pressures, make uh protection adjustments and pick stuff up uh was next level and it gave me something to build up and and to see and be like, man, that's what I want to be able to do. Um it's something that I had to put a lot of time in um in practice and scout team. Obviously getting my opportunities in the game to be able to understand what I have to work on to get better at, but it's definitely the area I've probably came the farthest in. Do you think Matt trusts you more, not just in protection, but just with doing anything that you want to do and do you think he'll let you even do more as you, you know, go into this season? >> Definitely. Um, you know, I think trust is something that's earned. Um, and I think the more reps I have, the more time we have together. You just keep building that stuff and he keeps, you know, he he'll give me more opportunities to to show that I can go do the right stuff out there and make the right decisions, get us the right plays. Um, and it's something that, you know, if you keep doing the right stuff, he'll keep trust you more and more with that stuff. So if you're doing it wrong, then you know that that trust kind of goes away. So um it's something that is earned and you got to keep doing it every day. But it's definitely grown >> with the with the protection adjustments. Is is Ganon testing you maybe more this summer than you've seen? I know you know you've been the starter with Joe Barry um half and now uh JG as the defensive coordinator. Are you getting tested more in that way than you have before? [snorts] >> Definitely. Um, we're seeing a lot of great stuff uh throughout training camp that JG's throwing at us. A lot of different pressures, a lot of exotic coverages. I think they're doing a great job kind of disguising stuff, holding stuff till the snap. Um, that, you know, it's just it's testing everybody's rules. It's testing the O line and pass pros, testing the running backs to make sure their eyes are in the right spot, quarterbacks, receivers to make sure we're seeing stuff, you know, doing all the little things right. um where I feel like, you know, in this time too in training camp, different coordinators we've gone against, you know, that's the time where they kind of open up their playbook as well. They try new things, try new pressures. So, you always know in training camp, you're going to see a lot of stuff. But JG, I mean, they it's just such an exotic defense. You see so much stuff and he does a great job just making stuff look similar. So, definitely test your rules. Jordan, did your responsibility with protections uh increase when Elton went down and then you brought in a new center and I know assume Elton knew a lot about protections and you guys were probably on the same page. Then Sean comes in. Did your responsibility change after that a little bit? >> I wouldn't say my responsibility changed. Um, you know, I think like you mentioned Elton, you know, he's been around. He he he knows, you know, inside and out the playbook, the calls. I think when Shawn took over, he's also a guy who's played a lot of ball. He's played at guard. Um so he he knew all that stuff just as well. Um you know, I think for centers obviously and pass pro, they're getting up, they're making all the um starting calls. And so for my job, it's really just overriding stuff if I see pressures coming, making adjustments to be able to pick stuff up. So for me, nothing really changed. You know, I think just making sure everybody's on the right the right page and communication kind of pre- snap. um that stuff picked up, you know, being able to hear what Sean's calling and um you know, if I need to make any adjustments making those, but it's it all stayed the same when we switched over. >> Do you have a preference for how many series you play on Thursday if you do play? Like is one enough? I know like in Cleveland, you only played that one series. Last year, you played two. Does it matter to you? Do you need one, two, >> man? I think uh you know, I think I like playing one series, but I think it always comes down to how how good you execute when you're out there. Um, obviously the goal is always to play one drive, go down and score a touchdown, you're good. Um, you know, something happens, you might go three and out and you're not feeling as good about that drive. So, there's there's things that come up in the game. Um, obviously you want to go out there and put your best foot forward. Um, but, you know, I don't think, uh, you gain anything or lose anything if you play more or less. Um, I think it just comes down to being confident, going out there, putting a good drive together. Um, and if not, I think everybody's going to feel like, hey, we we need to go back out there. We left something out there on the table. Have you talked about a number that you have in mind at least? >> No, we haven't talked about that yet. >> Jordan, we um obviously you played against Aaron last year when you guys played in Pittsburgh, but he's made it very clear this is his last go round. >> I'm just wondering when you kind of look back at your time together and then his departure, >> we've talked about how his ascension to the starting job was a crazy summer and it wasn't for you. How much did that help that you were just able to kind of take over and there wasn't controversy and there wasn't all that stuff that maybe he don't do? Did you guys ever talk about that? >> Yeah, I mean throughout our time together, you know, I've I've heard different stories and Aaron's talking to me about his time coming up um and obviously how he wanted to be um a little bit different his approach with me um which is great. But I mean at the same time, you know, I'm going through my own journey. I don't really I wasn't here to experience some of the stuff he went through. So, um, all I got is what I know and what I saw and, uh, obviously I've mentioned it time and time again, but nothing but, you know, great things to say about A-Rod and, you know, my time being behind him and watching him and just how much I was able to develop and and and grow in my process seeing him. Um, and then obviously like you mentioned the transition. Um, you know, I think for the organization that's something that's never easy. I think for the players it's not something that's never easy. A guy that's been here for that long um, and done so many great things. Um, so it's a, you know, it's a some big shoes to fill. Um, and for me, I try to focus on being my best and and doing the best thing that being doing the best job that I could for the team and just, you know, focus on that. >> Jonah, has it been >> what would you say is the number one thing you learned from him? Man, I always say the the consistency. Um, you know, when I was here with him, to be able to see, you know, coming from college, you know, you think you're you think you're good, you think you do a lot of good things, and then you see someone that just plays, you know, out of this world every single day in practice. He's making the right reads on feels like felt like every play, you know, he's making the right protection checks. Um, just doing the right stuff day in and day out. And just how consistent he was, you know, the stuff that he's doing in practice, it translates to the games. And I think that was my biggest thing to be able to see and be like, man, you know, there's a lot of growth and room to work on for me to be able to get consistently uh great. And uh I think that was the best thing I saw. >> You feel like you're there yet? >> No, I feel like that's something that uh you always got to grow every day. That's something that I'm still trying to work on to this day is just being the most consistent player I can be because there's always flashes, but um you know, I think you just want to be your best every single day. So I still think there's a lot of room for growth for me. Okay, Jordan, when you look at just this offense, you know, because of some of the injuries and things that you've been dealing with, is it tough to know fully, you can say, what you guys have right now, or do you still have a good, you know, pulse and feel on where things kind of stand just to stay with the overall offense? >> No, I have a great feel for what we got. Um, the guys we got, I know there's there's some injuries that happen, you know, during practice, things like that. Guys miss a couple days, which I still think is it's great for other guys to get those reps. That's that's literally how the season goes. you know, injuries happen, things happen, guys got to step up. And so, I think to be able to get reps with other guys that, you know, aren't getting the starting one reps, um, is just going to help us throughout the course of the season when things might come up. But, um, with the guys that, you know, are starting, like you said, maybe dealing with some injuries. I know what we got and, uh, it's just about getting those guys back healthy. >> Jordan, as you during mini camp, who you thought would have a big year that we weren't talking about, you said Sandy Williams, what have you kind of seen from him during camp? Are you excited about what he's been putting on tape so far? Yeah, I think uh there's definitely been a lot of growth. I think uh he had one of his best days the other day. Um obviously uh Jay Reed and MG were both out. So like we just mentioned, you know, that's when guys got to step up and you get those opportunities. Uh it's definitely cool to see guys making plays and uh a guy like Savon, I think it's just all about reps. You know, getting more reps, getting comfortable uh running every play, knowing what to do is is huge. And so the more reps he gets, you know, the more good things I'm seeing. Um so yeah. Were you surprised how open Bo was on that trick play yesterday? >> Uh yeah. I mean it's a trick play, so you never know how those are going to go. Um but uh he was uh pretty open. So I think that's always fun when your quarterback throwing a ball to a guy that's got like 30 yards away from everybody else. Um just hope that he catches it at that point. But uh yeah, trick plays. You you never know. That would work pretty well. >> Is that bag going to be deep this year? >> Trick plays? I hope so. I hope so. >> Two more. Jordan, how do you um how do you assess the camp you've had? I I know you're always wanting better at getting to like >> the throw today to Sky. I know it was an incomplete pass, but Simpsons coverage is great. It's a tiny little window to get it to where you want and it was right where it needed to be. >> How do you kind of what have you liked about your camp and what maybe have you felt like, okay, this has to get better before September 13th? >> Yeah, I think uh I think you know as a whole offense we've been doing some great things. cuz I think the consistency like we mentioned is something we got to clean up. For me um you know I think a goal for mine was being able to come through uh make sure I'm going with the right spot with the ball and then it just comes down to accuracy at that point and I think I've been doing a pretty good job of making sure you know I'm trusting what I'm seeing and uh making the right reads and uh I think at the end of the day you know I've been making some good throws. Guys have been making some contested catches for us. Um and that's the part you want to see. You know I think uh there's still some consistency. you know, there's been a couple throws, easy throws that, you know, I've missed. And that's where it comes down to just trying to be your best every day and making sure you're not having those those easy ones that you kind of let slip. And so, um, I think as far as the goal of me, just trying to trust what I'm seeing, making sure my progressions are on point and I'm going to the right spot, I think that's that's been a highlight. Is there a point in camp where you guys stop learning to do installs and start perfecting them or is there a certain point where that changes where it's not as much learning and more just executing over and over again? >> Yeah, you know, we're at that point. All of our installs are in right now. Um, you know, the other day we wrapped up our last one and that's where it comes down to now everything's in. Today is a day where you're just getting multiple different calls, you know, and that's when guys, especially young guys, you got to be able to lock in because, you know, you're not going over the stuff the night before and then um going out run those plays. Everything's in. So, you got to be able to focus and just know the playbook inside and out. Um for the older guys, starters, obviously, that's where, like you said, it just comes down to perfecting the stuff, running these plays versus multiple different coverages, and just staying locked in and knowing what to do, which is all great stuff. Um that's how the season is, of course. Um but we're definitely at that point right now. So then leadership wise, are you a little harder when harder on guys young or or vets, whatever it is, when things go wrong at this point? >> I mean, definitely. You're always, especially guys that have been here, um, you know, the leeway is always a little shorter on on things we're messing up. Um, but I think guys been doing a great job. I think it's just it's always little things, you know, little coaching points that you can get better at. You know, guy might not have ran the route perfectly, um, but he still did a good job on it, but there's always little areas that you can improve on. And I think that's the biggest thing. And like you said, if we're messing up, you know, simple stuff that we shouldn't be, that's where it's like, hey, we got to we got to really lock in right here.

title: Head Coach Matt LaFleur Press Conference
text: We had a hustle, [music] Rob. I like it. Morning. >> Morning. >> [clears throat] >> Matt, the the NFL says that they're going to allow head coaches to delegate the throwing of the red challenge flag. Do you enjoy that too much to give it up or what's your thought process? >> I I probably should give it up. Based on past actions, so um now I'll pro- I'll probably hold the challenge flag. >> Do you Do you feel good about it? >> If not, it's going to be Joe McKillop. >> Do you feel good about your process? I mean, obviously Connor's really been good for you, kind of calming >> Yeah, I think yeah. Yes. Where it gets challenging is if you leave, you know, and go to the um if you go talk to the quarterbacks or receivers or whoever, somebody on offense when the defense is out there and you have a bang-bang play, you got to But Connor's usually in my ear and then you just have to have urgency to get up there and throw the flag. >> Did you used to have Rich kind of watch the line if you had to go back and >> No, it's always been Connor. >> Didn't Donatell Jackson have core muscle surgery? >> Who told you that? >> Well, I knew the injury was core, so >> Yeah. Yeah, he did in the off season. >> Um any idea how much longer he'll be out? >> I I couldn't tell you. >> He I mean, he had been practicing. >> Yeah. >> I don't think I know he did not come back and I'm not sure. >> No, no, no. This is Yeah, that was in the springtime or whatever. Um he he just um has been trying to work through some of this stuff and hopefully he'll be out there shortly. >> Um I know I asked you yesterday, but Keyshawn not getting you know, not playing with the ones for the one pretty by play at the snaps yesterday. What's what's the thinking there with him and St. Juste? >> Just everything's a competition right now. So, we're going to put different guys in different situations and different spots and see how they respond. >> How's he handled it? >> I think he's had two really solid performances. >> What have you seen from St. Juste that's caught your attention so far this year? >> I think there's a lot of a lot of things he's done um in terms of coverage and also fitting up in in some of the run support things that we want to make sure we get from our corners. And so, it's going to be great to see him in live action. >> And what do you think about, you know, Jaylen Simpson sort of down with the opportunities he's had? >> Yeah, I think he's he's really making an impact. I think he's made a lot of plays. Certainly, you could see it on the last play of of practice yesterday where he picked that ball off. Um, but I think I see a guy that's growing, that's playing with more confidence. And he's like a lot of these guys, you're just excited to see him play in preseason. >> Did you guys see this coming last year? I mean, you didn't really see any of the competitive stuff once training camp opened. >> I think we've always seen a skill set in him that he possesses and I think he's got a knack for taking the ball away that goes back to his days at Auburn. But, um yeah, so we we've always we've been excited about him. It's just there's always a little bit of a transition there when you take a guy that's played safety predominantly then you move him to corner. >> Is there any timeline for Carrington Valentine? >> I'm hoping next week that he'll be back on the practice field. >> How's Jordan going to play on Thursday at Pittsburgh? >> He will. As of right now. I always have the right to change my mind. >> And to circle back to what you were saying yesterday or what what's your thought process there? >> What do you mean? >> About you know how many snaps in the preseason. >> Yeah, I we'll we'll we'll I'd say it's pretty fluid in regards to how many snaps. Um but I do think there's a lot of value for all our guys to just get mentally prepared to go play a game. Whether it's one play, whether it's three plays, 10 plays, the whole game. Um I think there's a ton of value in that. Just getting getting your process down. >> What's the difference you kind of saw last year you did play the play them a few more times in the preseason. What was the value you saw come out of that early in the regular season? You said they seem to play better. >> Yeah, I think but it's not just it's not just one guy. It's the collective, right? It's it's everybody that's out there. >> Matt, I realized you about the offensive line yesterday. Do you need to see those guys again understanding the risk versus reward of preseason play? Do you need to see those guys a little bit longer what even if Jordan's not in there like >> Yeah, I think there's there's certain individuals that will stay in the game. >> Matt, that slot position can have a lot of different body types whether it's the kind of smaller shiftier guys. You guys have kind of used that safety whether it's with Bullard or now getting Kitan Oladapo some looks there. What do you guys look for in that specific role? >> Well, it just depends what you're asking them to do but certainly um I think it starts with you want somebody that will go in there and fit the run. But also you he's got to have some coverage ability. So, um and then ultimately we got to play to their to the guy's strengths. >> The Steelers still uh embrace the camp in Latrobe at Saint Vincent and coaches and players. and I know why you had to make the change in 2020, but you know, is the And and is that in the back of your mind at all in [snorts] that period of bonding with the team? >> Yeah, absolutely. Absolutely. That that's why you're always trying to create ways. I do think it's a little bit different now if we were to go offsite. Yeah, then I think you get a ton of benefit from that, but being that we are here, you know, I just those guys have no choice but to go back to the dorms. Like I I was in LA, we we did the same thing. We went down to Orange County and you're there's no you know, you you go back to the room, you hang out with the guys. Um and I think it could be a little bit different here in regards to some of these guys, especially with I don't know if you've seen the number of guys that are our fathers now, but there's a lot of babies around practice, and I think a lot of these guys based on the time limits or whatever, camp's not like it what it used to be when you were here at you know, 7:00 in the morning till after 9:00 at night, and they would just go back and and go to bed. I think we get out um a lot of times 6:00 or 6:30, and these guys would go home and then just go back to go go to sleep. >> Matt, you mentioned yesterday to NFL Network that Jordan Love is the best you've ever been around when it comes to the line of scrimmage protections and things of that nature. When did you see that really take hold as far as going from really kind of studying under Aaron to really mastering what he's working with. >> Yeah, I think it it was definitely a process that's just evolved over time. I mean, he is so in tune with with everything we're doing and shoot, it happened today where he's in there and we're we're talking about different looks about what he could do and I was he said something that I hadn't thought of and I was like, "Oh, yeah, that's pretty good." So, uh I think he's just he's really grown in that facet and he can he has complete command at the line of scrimmage. Um and then he he just he trusts everything that we we talk about in that room and he goes out there and executes it. >> And Stacy gave you the chance to walk that back by pointing out that you coached Aaron Rodgers. So, when you say that, what did Aaron do at the line that is like he kind of had seemed like he had free reign to do whatever he wanted and maybe that's part of it, but what was kind of the what's the difference there? >> Well, it just depends on the situation. Without getting too into too many details, but Aaron was phenomenal, too. Don't get me wrong. and I think Jordan really benefited from watching him and how he operated and how quickly he could process things. Um but I do think our offense is is evolved over time, too. So, um that's all I'm going to say about that. >> Matt, what's the relationship been like between Jordan and and Tyrod in that room and just the you know, five-month span that you've had them together? >> Yeah, it's been great. I mean, you can't help but not like Tyrod Taylor. I mean, he is a he is a G. He's a great dude, really good football player. you know, just he's awesome to have in that room. >> We talked a lot about what he brings from experience and how he can help Jordan, but Jordan has missed time each of the last 2 years, so he may have to play. Look like he had a really good day yesterday. Is it clear to you that he can not just be a great mentor, but can still play at a high level? >> Oh, absolutely. I think yeah, he's and it's been fun to go through this process. Just I mean, again, not holding anything back and throwing everything at him and just to see how he's handled it and I think he's done a a heck of a job. >> Two more, please. >> Matt, I'm sure it's hard to game plan for preseason game number one with the new head coach or new offense, whatever it is. What do you >> There's no game planning going on. I promise you that. I mean, it's >> [snorts] >> there's Don't get me wrong. It's not like we're negligent and you have an idea of what somebody may do, but you're you're running just like base core concepts in in every phase of the game. So, cuz you want your guys to feel prepared when they go out there to have an idea of what they may or may not see, but I think what's been great about this camp is I think we've seen a lot of different things from from really both sides of the ball from our offense in terms of how we motion and and you know, use misdirection plays to our defense and some of the looks that we're getting. Um and I know it's typical a lot of special teams coordinators, they got their own little pack that they do going into the a lot of these games, so they don't try to expose somebody else. >> So, then with that being said, are you just looking at how they respond or just making sure >> you're looking at everything. How they compete, how they how they're able to process in the moment. Um there's nothing like it, you know, the pressure of just there it's a game. So, you're you're looking at everything. >> Is Josh Jacobs any closer to coming back or is he still going to be out a while? >> Oh, >> mean he's going to be out for at least this week. >> And um we last asked you about Keyshawn earlier. We were asking about Belton earlier in the week. What do you find out about guys when something like this happens and they're challenged or they lose their spot? What do you find out about them? >> Just how do you find uh respond to adversity? And there's adversity is basically the name of the game in this league. So, you just got to respond and and when given your opportunities go out there and and compete it to the best of your ability. >> Thank you, guys. >> Thanks, guys. >> Sorry.

title: Head Coach Matt LaFleur Press Conference
text: Hey, hey, hey. Hey, >> [music] >> Hey. Heat. Heat. >> Hey. Hey. Hey. Heat. Morning, >> Matt. I know you generally like practicing outside. Was there any benefit though with week one being on turf, getting practice indoors on the turf? >> You must have been talking to our guys because a couple guys said something to me about that. Um, you know, just with the field conditions and the shorter practice yesterday, we thought it would be best to go inside. But yes, I do like to go outside, but I do think to your point, there is some benefits, you know, in playing on the turf. >> You don't do one-on- ones inside, right? >> I don't want to say ever, but it's it's a rarity. Typically, we only do one-on- ones when we're in pads anyways. You've had a lot of defensive tackles rotated in with the ones and twos. Is why it comes back comes back. I'm sure it's a good problem to have, but how do you get is it a challenge to get everyone involved and how much you want to? >> Uh, not really. I think as long as we have enough reps um and we have uh many more practices and then also those preseason opportunities. So, I think we'll we'll be able to figure it out. You have enough corners available to go through team drills after some roster moves or you got some guys coming back maybe? >> Um yeah, we're getting a little thin at a couple positions for sure, which definitely makes it a challenge. Um we've had to modify some of the things with our schedule and with the number of reps today. I was hoping to get like 80 reps and we're we're not going to we're not going to reach that. I mean, you got you got plenty of time here obviously, but um >> there's never enough time, Bill. Come on. >> Okay. Well, it's a actually maybe it's the fair way to put it. Um you do have some battles going on up front on the offensive line. Is there I know it's not like a stepping stone in time. Is there a time where you like to get some continuity built there? >> Yeah, I think we've we've talked about that quite a bit in here, I think, right? About the importance of getting all five of those guys out there at the same time. But, you know, you got to adjust to the circumstances and the circumstances are we've had two guys that have started a lot of football games for us uh that haven't been available and obviously we're getting Zack Bako Be Wellle. I got to get used to that. So, I need to say it as many times as possible. Um getting him back in the lineup which was great yesterday. is does moving Jacob to if that's how it pans up does that give you maybe some different I don't want to say better options but for a lot of better options as far as backup tackle and all that with >> well potentially yeah and I don't want to you know just put anything in stone we got a lot like I just talked about we have many more opportunities for these guys to showcase what they can do and ultimately when it comes down to it we got we will make a decision after the preseason concludes. >> Matt, we we have talked a lot about the line here. How much time does a line typically need to gel in terms of being cohesive? Like how much time? >> Yeah, that's a great question. I think you know the faster the better. U but certainly I think you see it around the league. I think it takes it takes games for that to happen. So um you know the more these guys can play together then the faster it will happen. Can preseason games do that or >> I absolutely I think there's a ton of value in the preseason games and and getting those guys out there to kind of work out some of the kinks. >> And what areas do you need to see the most improvement from the line looking back at what they did last season? I I just think the consistency from down in and down out. Um you know, certainly the mental we had we had a lot of mental mistakes a year ago and that can't happen because you're just not giving yourself a chance. And then the carryover from indie to team. You want to see these guys playing with the proper footwork, with the proper hand placement, getting your eyes in the right spots um to give yourself a chance because the the creatures that they have to block on the other side of the ball um they're they're more athletic on the defensive line. So yeah, you just all of that, you know, all those fundamentals have to come together. Did Savon Williams practice look as good on the tape as it did standing on the sideline because it looked like he really took advantage of an opportunity? >> Yeah, he had a lot. I think he had eight opportunities in the past game and was seven of eight um you know catching the football and so yeah, I think um he had a good day. >> What you seen from Bullard this this camp and what do you think is sort of the next step for him as a drop? Hopefully he doesn't drop. >> Yeah. Um, yeah, Bull is he's a dog, man. He you talk about a guy that plays with the right mentality, the right play style, what we want to be about. Um, and so it's been cool just to see his evolution. I think we, you know, one thing that we've put him in more situations where there's been some some man coverage sit situations and I think he's really progressed. >> You said yesterday that anybody who's healthy better be ready to play. Do you [snorts] go back and forth on whether you want to play guys in preseason or not? Or do you have kind of a belief one way or the other? >> I think a lot of it's feel of where where your team's at. And I think just my experiences here and um is that when we've played in the preseason, we've been better earlier in the season. And you can't I mean you open up with a division opponent on the road, that's a tough task in itself. So, uh, I think, you know, we've got to keep that in mind. And plus, there's a lot of data out there that will tell you that if your guys get X amount of snaps in the preseason, I think it's like over three times less likely that they get injured in the regular season. >> So, does that data make you feel any less uncomfortable then when you are putting them out there knowing? >> I mean, yeah, anytime. It's just football is there's a lot of unknowns and you know you just sometimes you got to you got to push the envelope. >> Yeah. Um how does St. Juice fit into Ganon's defense? A lot of times these big tall guys are press guys, you know, they like to get their hands on people. What what has his fit been within the scheme, do you think? Yeah, I think anytime as a corner um you can get your hands on people, that's usually a pretty good thing. And I think there's a lot of difference different looks that our defense presents that puts them in some of those situations. But what I'm really most excited to see him compete in game, >> what's the snap count for hitting that threshold of players being three touch? Well, it it some of that is in combination with joint practices. So, it just depends how many joint practices you have. >> But is there a certain like what's what's the number that you try to target between the two? >> Um, well, since we I I know that the league data had like if you have one practice or one joint practice, you'd like to get 30 plus snaps in the preseason. >> Well, >> whether or not we hit that, I I remains to be seen. Will Reer Golden be back at practice today? >> I am not anticipating them. >> What's the What's the I know you don't have a timeline for for Valentine, but because of Kesha on the first day and Valentine since Cece's played a ton of number one snaps. Do you think he's potentially ready if you have to go with him as a starter on week one? >> Yeah, I think so. I think I think all those guys. We got a lot of confidence in all those guys and we'll just let it all play out. >> Two more, please. you had a series at practice yesterday where it was where Keshan was not with the starters. Um was that just different combination or something some sort of competition that you might want to start there? >> Well, I think there's there's always competition. All these guys got to be prepared for that. As far as the substitution, that's not something that I'm I'm always micromanaging. Um a lot of that's on the position coach. >> Matt, you get three preseason games. Do you evaluate the importance of playing guys any more differently in any of the threes or pecking order of those those three games for you >> in terms of >> like the first or second or third game more more important to get guys on the field? >> Uh not necessarily. I think the way it it shakes out just with uh the third preseason game having the joint practice were more likely to hold them there. I I think Goody had mentioned that he talked to McCarthy when you guys were thinking about the Parson's trade. It's kind of crazy that you're going to be coaching against the guy that used to have the job here. Did you do you have a relationship with him? You see each other at NFL? >> Yeah, I Yeah, at Certainly at the owner meetings. um you know and I've gotten to know him a little bit just when he when he came back here um you know a few times and I've got I'll say this I've got so much respect for him first of all how he's always treated me and secondly just by what he's accomplished here and it's it's pretty cool that when he got the Pittsburgh job I'm like Green Bay Packers Dallas Cowboys Pittsburgh Steelers I mean that's that's pretty special. So, Mike's a guy that I've got a ton of respect for. >> Thank you, guys. >> Thanks, guys.

title: Head Coach Matt LaFleur Press Conference
text: Do you start this week like it's our regular game week where you go like today would be like I guess Wednesday? >> Not necessarily. Just with what the volume that they came off of. So, we'll have a low day. Tomorrow will be a high day and then we'll have another low day, walk-through, and go play. >> I should have looked at Vaness after the scrimmage on Saturday. What did you think of him not yet? Did you have to go back and watch? >> Yeah, I thought he did a lot of good things and he's got to keep on building on his his performances. >> The first time we spoke to Za'Darius, he talked about how much he loves practice and being on the practice field. When you're out there with him or watching the tape back afterwards, do you do you see that energy out there doing >> Oh, absolutely. He brings it every day. He's a He's a real pro. Um Yeah, he just Uh you love to be around guys that love to work. >> Matt, I know after Family Night, you mentioned how human it was and kind of maybe how the extended time on the field maybe contributed to some of the sloppiness. Going back and watching it, was it a little sloppier than maybe you thought even watching live? Cuz I mean >> There was There was a lot of penalties. There was I think we counted like 20. Which when you're talking about 100 plays, now a couple of them occurred on special teams. I think we had four on special teams. Um the ones that are most concerning to me are like the pre-snap penalties. I mean, we had a couple offsides. We had a like seven false starts. Um So, that needs to get cleaned up, but I am happy and pleased that our guys had to go through and and you got to fight through fatigue. And um So, it's only a bad practice if you don't learn from it. And our guys got to learn from it, and we got to we got to clean that up before our first preseason game. >> How do you evaluate Warren Bryant's play Family Night and just a couple practices so far? >> Yeah, Warren always he he he flashes. He He does a lot of great things. I think just like any young player, it's about the consistency of what you do those things. Um but I I like his progress. >> Watching Friday night, um after Wiley at tight end, I thought, "Boy, how much this team is missing John Fitzpatrick?" >> Sure. >> So, tell me about what you you've seen so far in camp in terms of not a lot of experience right now, but you got at the tight end position. >> Yeah, I mean, it's it it's uh probably our youngest position on our football team right now. When you when you talk about Luke and Tuck not being out there, so you know, it's it's a lot of good learning going on. Some some uh learning through failure a little bit at times, but I I think the guys are making progress. I I I can tell the want to the desire is there. And you know, these are valuable reps for our guys. >> Matt, we saw Sean Ryan obviously have that half a season at center last year. With this being sort of his year two at that position, are you have you seen ways in which he's uh um taken steps upon taking more ownership of what's going on? >> Yeah, absolutely. He kind of got thrust in that role last year uh when Allen went down. Um but I think he's you know, he's he's really taken it. He's attacked it head-on. He's taken on the responsibility of leading that room, and I think he's done a good job with that. >> You made a decision yet on how much of your starters will or won't play in Pittsburgh? >> What I told everybody is get anybody that's healthy, better be ready to play. >> But um going back to the O line, uh what has Jacob Monk shown you at uh from center position to to challenge you? >> Yeah, I think he just you talk about a guy that plays the to the play style that we want. He shows that toughness, that gritiness, the strain. Um and I think he's done a a pretty good job inside, so he's a valuable guy. He He can play any of the inside three positions. Uh I thought we saw a glimpse of what he's capable of doing last year when he got some some action, especially significant action in that Minnesota game at the end of the season, and I thought he performed well. >> Matt, the extra work that he and Burton have got is great, but do you need Aaron Banks to be out there at some point? What's your kind of timeline with him? >> Yeah, I mean, uh the timeline is when the trainers tell me he's ready to roll. So, certainly, you know, you'd like to get your core guys out there to build the continuity. You know, early on I think in the season you you see it league-wide just some inconsistencies in terms of getting off on the snap count and in order to get that stuff worked [snorts] out, you need everybody out there. >> Have you gotten word yet from the trainers any of those guys that that are out that have been out like return to team reps? >> Yeah, we'll have a couple guys going today. Very limited. >> You had like four or five guys get banged up on family night. Are there any long-term concerns with any of them? >> Um I don't think long-term, no. >> What did you see from some of your other running backs? I mean, obviously we've all talked a lot about Marshawn, but when you watch the tape back, what did you see from those guys from Saturday night? >> Yeah, I thought I thought Jayden went in there and he had some good cuts. You know, he's a slippery back that's got good good speed. And Damien played to his strength. I mean, he's a big guy and I think you saw that in that live period just his ability to break a few tackles and I was happy that he lowered his pad level. I thought earlier in practice he ran a little high and then when it came to time to hit, he I mean, he dropped his pads and was able to, you know, break break a couple tackles. >> Where's Brennan Cox at and it was his third or fourth year and then you know, kind of his development and what he can bring to that edge room? >> Yeah, I think he brings an edge in that room to be honest. Like just his his style of play. He's a tough gritty guy and so I'm excited to see him get extensive action in the preseason. >> And you know, you said it's only a bad practice if you don't learn from it. It seemed like Anthony Belton felt like it wasn't his best night. What are your kind of expectations for him to bounce back? >> Well, I think he's a he's a really talented guy that's played a lot of meaningful snaps for us. Um, he's still a young developing player. I think with him, just like I've said many times, it's just he's certainly capable. It's just it's got to be consistent. And the better he gets at that, the better the player he's going to be. But, um, I I am excited about his future in this league. >> Is Ingram going to be closer to being on the field again? >> Yeah, I think he should be able to he's going to return to practice. >> That'll do. >> Thank you.

title: Zac Taylor Press Conference - August 11
text: Go for it. >> For the starters, >> we'll see. You know, we'll still get through tomorrow and make some decisions on some guys. Um, good amount of the starters will play, but I'm not there yet on um on everybody. I know you know um Joe will play um Jamar T but again we'll kind of announce everything for tomorrow at some point probably. Do >> you have an idea of how many series you'll want to get Joe? >> Um limited series so it won't be a ton of time but you know for fans to come out there. They're going to see Joe and Jamar T. They're going to see Dexter. Um so they they'll get a chance to enjoy some of our players there. But how long I keep them out there remains to be seen. I really have it work out the way it did last year in Philly where Joe gets that be the ideal. >> Yeah, that'd be ideal. But again, we'll we'll I'm not going to put a number on it yet and we'll just kind of feel it out and see where it goes. >> Today we saw I think Bobo and Cashes got in uniform. Both of them good to go for >> I think that's why I'm a little limited right now just on some guys that are we're kind of limiting dayto day and making decisions for on Thursday. So, I'm not I'm not quick enough right now to say who's gonna um be full go yet because there's just some guys that I just really want to manage through this week and we'll make some decisions if they're playing tomorrow or not. But those guys, there's nothing nothing longterm on them. It's just we kind of get out there some days, make a decision for that day if we're going to put them out. >> Dax, >> um they will not play in this game. So, we'll we'll get them through the week and then see where that lands going into next week. You >> put them on weeks a week. Is that probably fair? They they'll be out this week and then we'll go from there. >> How are it looks like BJ's doing more? >> Yeah, both progressing. Um won't put a timeline on them, but they're both progressing as we would hope that they would. >> With the rookie class, I know every year they kind of a rookie class brings something it feels like. Was there something to this year's class that you have felt uh from from that group? >> Well, I think no one's out of place, you know, number one. all those guys that we've gotten reps to. Um, they've all shown the things that the reasons we brought them here. Really encouraging class. Um, I want more practices under their belt before we start declaring anybody a future star in this league or anything because they've only got, you know, two and a half weeks in so far. But I think once you get to these preseason games, you'll get a better sense of where they're at. But really pleased with all of them. Um, they've all made their contributions. They all belong. They're all competing for different roles. They've all, I think, handled the above the neck stuff really well. They were very mature as a class overall. So, pleased pleased with the group by and large. >> Easier to work with them last year. I mean, you had three guys really that were kind of almost starters for you at this time of year counting. Is it easier to work with them and and have patience when they're not counted on to be in there immediately and they're just trying to earn that role? >> No. >> No. because you never know where when it can come up, where they're needed immediately, you know, and so that that's always in the back, I think, of a coach's mind is um they may be viewed as a depth player, a backup, but we all know they got to be ready in a moment's notice. And so, you always have that urgency to make sure that they're ready to go. Um so, I don't ever feel like the easing in, hey, we're not counting on this guy, so we can we can be a little more patient with them. Um usually feels the opposite. >> Conor Lou, you had him out there a little bit today. um what's what your plan kind of with him and what have you thought about how he's progressed thus far. >> He's progressed as we would hope. So being able to do more and more in practice. Um and really that's just more our decision with with the trainers. It's just how much we want to give him so far. Everything's been really good. He and Eric Hall would be two guys that we will not put out there Thursday. Um but they're both doing everything we'd hoped they'd be able to do. They're progressing. We'll make decisions on future games with them, but um just don't want to put them out there prematurely >> today. Just uh let's get him some snaps with Joe in and with the ones tight to get a little bit of a feel for that. >> Correct. >> Zach, you're going to see plenty of Dexter Lawrence the last couple weeks, you know, on the field or whatever. What's you've seen what he's like as a player. What's the mind of Dexter Lawrence like as you've gotten to know him over the last couple months? Like the football mind? >> Just excited to play football. Uh high understanding. He's played in this league a long time so he understands how people are going to attack him. and what his strengths are and how to combat all that, but I think just loves being out there. That's that's that's what the sense I get from him. Um, loves to compete. Um, there's a lot, I think, excitement to be here and be a part of what we're building. >> The Lions are known as one of the more physical teams in the league. Are you interested? I mean, I know the game means absolutely nothing, but are you interested in maybe just kind of how, you know, you guys, you know, dish it out with them? >> I think it's a good opponent. you know, a lot of respect for Dan and his coaching staff and the way that they play and um so I think it's a really good first preseason game for our guys to to see where we're at and you know, we'll get a feel. I I don't know what his plan will be for for all his guys, but um I think it's a good good first game for us, see where we're at. >> For those starters who do play, I know for a lot of those guys, it's it's, you know, a lot less about evaluation. What do you want to see out of them or what do you want them to get out of? >> I I want our our guys to come out in our stadium out of our tunnel where we play week one in front of our fans and our fans to be able to see the group that's running out there, these guys to again just be the 11 guys out there on the field by themselves, everybody else on the sideline, people in the stands, just get that feeling. Um, in terms of X's and O's, there's nothing earthshattering I'm looking for. I want clean operation, you know, from especially our veterans and those are things that always come up in in preseason one and we're doing everything we can to make sure that we're very clean there, but that's what I want to see. But then overall, it's just the atmosphere. I just want them out in the atmosphere kind of checking that box before we move forward to camp. >> Played more than he did last preseason, I think, than he has. Did you guys see a benefit of that early? >> Really hard to know. you know, it's um you can make an argument for whatever you want to make an argument for, you know, and so again, we'll we'll we'll get through this game and then make our decisions going forward after that. But it's it's challenging to know if okay, when you play a guy in the the third preseason game and we're not playing a game for two and a half weeks after that, how much did that help him? I it's really difficult to measure that. >> How much do y'all study that over the course of the offseason? Is that something that never comes up is like how much starters play and all that? How much y'all study all that? We just make our own decisions based on some information we have. >> In camp, it's felt like the offense will make some plays, the defense will make some plays. How have you felt kind of the team perform and kind of the level of the team in training camp? >> I think it's been really physical training camp. I I think, you know, as a head coach, there's there's been a lot to to be excited about when I walk off the field. Sometimes I think each coordinator is probably frustrated with their day. Um, but I I think that there's been a lot of improvement. I think the depth has really improved and so now we're just we're through the install portion of things. So now it's making sure everything's clean. Okay, which it's the install's in. Players are responsible for that information. Now we'll circle back through it. So now we expect to be very clean moving forward and usually that starts with this game. You know, you get a chance now to to breathe a little bit for the three days leading up to this game where we focus on the Detroit install and what we're going to do against Detroit. It's usually a lot simpler in preseason game one than what training camp has been so far. Um but then once you get through this game, we're repeating information. We expect our guys to be clean and and so I'm looking forward to seeing how our guys respond to that. Is >> this the most talented defensive line that you've coached? >> Yeah, as a head coach here, I'd say just just top to bottom, especially the depth. Obviously, we have high-end talent, but I think top to bottom overall, the depth is something that you're really excited about. It's there's there's nobody out of place. Um, everybody's made contributions over the course of practices and scrimmages and I'm really excited to see, you know, guys play in the second quarter, second half of of the game on Thursday night, see how they they play. >> Some of the guys were saying it's the most physical camp they've seen here. Is it even the most physical camp? >> You know, I just think um what we have up front on both sides of the ball has dictated a lot of that. There's just been a lot of challenging moments I think for both both units there. And so that's not necessarily anything I've done from the structure of practice that's made it that way. It's just I think it's just a lot of a lot of guys really going at it. And I love to get in the heat the other day in the scrimmage. I'd love to get that again next weekend, Saturday and Sunday. I hope it's the same. You know, I I want wear these guys out with some long drives and some heat and try to get them ready for September. >> Did you move that practice back on purpose to get a little more in the heat? No, no. >> What was your take on that practice so far? Was that it? Was it >> It was good work. It was good work. There was There was good corrections to be made. Gave us a lot to talk about, things that came up on on both sides of the ball. But overall, I walked away. We we got out of it what I had hoped to get out of it. When we got in there, we got some long drives in there. Um had some moments where each side won, which led to corrections, some key corrections on both sides of the ball. So, I think overall it was it was good. What have you seen from the competition in the secondary, Zack? We've had some opportunity with Dax out JD out. What have you seen? >> Yeah, I think we we'll continue to see more of it, you know, and we've had some guys that are that are a little bit dayto-day dinged up right now. Um, but I think those guys, they got a good understanding of what we're asking them to do. Not Not necessarily better or worse, but just how different does that make your defense? I think the pocket push for quarterbacks is is is really difficult when it's coming up the middle because now you're trying to escape outside and that's where the ends, you know, if they're beating the tackles around the edge, there's not a lot of movement there. Also, how much you learn scene just like play out on the grass. I think those guys have to my eye formed really good relationships where they're able to play off each other. So, meaning I was going to give them a call, but there's also tools that they need to have out there on the field to make the right adjustments. And I feel like right now we're we're really getting into that and that's going to help us. >> The league is going to allow a designated challenge thrower now. Doug's always thrown a challenge flag. So and and they know that. They ask you that in pregame, who's got the flag? So, it's never been an issue. I didn't even know it was frowned upon, I guess. Um, and I know that there's other coaches in the league. I'm not the only one that's done that. So, um, I saw that they implemented a new rule, so maybe we get a retroactive fine or something. Doug could have could have done it, but that's never come up. And um it's just part of our routine. I I feel better with Doug having it. And I could take it from him and probably do the same thing. But >> how's reaction time been? >> Really good. Yeah, he's on it. Yeah, trust me, he's paranoid. He doesn't want to He doesn't want He doesn't want to miss it. I've yelled at him plenty of times on it. There's nothing he can do to not get yelled at. It's just that usually it's a pretty tense moment. Um, but he's he's on it. >> How does Barry Carter compare this year to last year? >> He's playing really fast. He's got really good command of the defense. So, it's kind of just the point I was just making about guys being able to make adjustments. I think Barrett's been a really big part of that. um just the command and the leadership he's got in that room to be able to make some adjustments up front to help those guys win and to help he and Demetrius behind him. I just think you've seen a lot of highle thinking there um and adjustments that you see from veteran linebackers and we're seeing it from Barrett and Demetrius. >> Zach, you said Jaylen Davis also will not play or will >> I'm not sure. I'm not ready to declare all these guys yet. It's it's hard for me to say today. >> How about the twos and threes and you know, just what you want to see and do they have to pop off the video after Thursday night? >> Sometimes it's about being dependable. Can we depend on them? If they go in the game at that role, how' they play on special teams? Because often times if they're really compete for a roster spot, special teams is probably a big factor in that. So really uh a clean operation. I know that sounds just very coachy, but that's that's where I'm at with it. you know, guys that we can depend on that if they go in the game due to injury or due to due personnel package that we can depend on them to do their job and sometimes allow the others around you to make a big play and and so that that's a big part of being a role player and a lot of these guys are competing for those spots. >> Darren looking at a lot of different guys and you'll roll those guys on >> Yeah, we we try our best to match it up with the offense and defense with the play time to make sure Darren's getting them work at the right times on special teams. because of all the new people you've added to the defensive line group, two players we haven't really asked too much about are Mckenley Jackson, Chris Jenkins. Yeah. >> How have they played in training camp and what are you seeing in their progression? I >> I think they've had good camps and I think the guys around them have good camps, too. I think it's really healthy competition where it's not necessarily guys falling behind, it's guys surging forward. And I think I've seen the whole group. I think if competition breeds that, certainly they can all feel that competition and where things are at. It's been really good for that group. I think everybody's really elevated their play and taken taken a necessary step. >> On the topic of the challenge playthrough, I'm just curious, you make like thousands of decisions between the three-hour period of the game on Sundays. No, because you're you're just again there's information that's coming in over a 30 secondond period that you're relying on information. Ultimately, I have to I have to make the final call on if we're doing it or not. But but you got to rely on the right information coming from the press box on whether you can do it or not.
