So, um, whenever those start to slow down, right, you can only put in so much stuff, really start to get pretty comfortable in the offense and understand what the defense is doing, too. >> All right. Uh, good work today, uh, finishing up this week. Obviously, two weeks into it. Um, it's good practice today. I thought our guys brought energy. Um, obviously it's a grind and we got to work through that and the mental and physical toughness of it uh every day to get better, but uh happy and pleased where our team's at. Obviously got a day off or not day off, but we're traveling tomorrow. Um, and looking forward to the joint practice against New England on Tuesday. >> Better situationally there from Riley and Anthony. >> Yeah, it was good. That was a two-minute situation. It was an end of game situation. Kind of put us ourselves in that Seattle situation that we had last year um there. So, it was good work. There's one timeout. Offense was down by one. needed a field goal right there to win it. So, it was good back and forth. >> I know that you're not shy about challenging your guys. Have you had conversations with with those two quarterbacks about just raising their game at all? >> Yeah, absolutely. I think every day those guys are battling. You know, someone's got to win a job and go take it. Um, and those guys are back and forth. Um, and we'll continue to work that, you know, through camp and see where it goes. >> Shane, hold those to be the quarterbacks on Thursday for you. >> Uh, that's the plan right now. Yes. >> Down serious. >> Yeah, DS ain't serious at all. I think he might practice on Tuesday. Hey, we'll just be smart with him. Uh, so nothing serious there. >> As Buck has kind of got back into full team and stuff, have you started to kind of feel his presence a little? >> Yeah, of course. Of course. Whenever Buck's out there, you can definitely feel them. Um, so it's great to get him out there getting some team reps again, monitoring him through training camp. Um, you know, where his body's at, but he feels good. He feels good where he's at. >> We were just monitoring him too as well. Um, he had a little thing in practice, little hamstring, but it wasn't bad. Like, you know, we're just like, let's just be smart with him today. So, we just went through individual. >> How nice will it be to go up against someone who's not in an opponent's uniform once you get to New England? >> Yeah. No, that's huge. I think uh to go against another opponent, it really breaks up camp. Um guys will be excited, juiced up for that practice. Um so, it'll be a great practice. We're looking forward to that. Anytime you can go against different opponent, um it obviously raises the level, the energy. It's just human nature. So, it'll be good for our guys. >> Some some coaching film for you with sort of tips and um just not being short-handed, I guess, and the turnovers. D, it seemed like football were you. >> Yeah. No, he's Yeah, he did a good job. Obviously, we got to finish some plays there. Um, you know, that happens. I always tell the guys, you know, there's some things you can control and can't control and especially like tip balls and stuff and obviously we got to see the ball in on some of those things. Um, that's really what it comes down to. >> Do you guys feel like you need to add another? >> Uh, we're looking, you know, we're always looking and doing our research and that, but I like the group we got. Those guys are battling um right now and so we'll see where that all goes. What's your level of confidence with this team at this point in camp? >> Very confident. I think uh my confidence grows in this team every day to be completely honest with you just because I look at the level of execution on both sides of the ball and it's really not lopsided one side or the other. Uh it's great back and forth uh every practice and so that's I'm really pleased and really encouraged by that. >> Have you seen Rally stack up nice days here? >> Yeah, he's done some nice things, you know what I mean? And that's what it's got to be. It's got to be consistent, you know, at that position day in and day out. You know, making the right reads, uh, whatever it is, whether it's throwing or in the run game, getting us in the right checks if we got kills on the play. Um, but, you know, we did some good things today. >> Will you play any starters on Thursday? >> Uh, I'm working through that. I'll have that tonight and then I'll let you guys know on Tuesday. >> Great. Awesome. Thanks, Sh.

title: Colts' Josh Downs goes down with groin injury, wide receiver help needed
text: We finished up a hot steamy day eight here at Colts training camp here at Grand Park. I'm Nathan Brown, your Colts insider with the Indianapolis Star. He's Joey Erickson and we're here to recap today's practice here on Saturday from Colts training camp. One of the probably most important injury updates that we've gotten from camp so far, another receiver down in Josh Downs, Colts number two receiver if everyone is healthy, of course. Alec Pierce continues to work his way back from late March ankle surgery. He's been on the physically unable to perform list all of camp. Laquon Treadwell went down with hamstring a couple days ago and he's been out. Now Josh Downs out with a groin injury. He was out on the sidelines today walking around in a in a t-shirt, so it's good to see him out here, but we don't exactly have an idea yet when he will be back. And so that's now maybe three of the Colts top four or five receivers that are out with undetermined timetables. Puts this wide receiver group in a fairly precarious spot about halfway through training camp. What do you feel like that does for the team at the moment? >> Well, I I think you kind of saw it today in practice. It was a shortened session, so we didn't get a ton of passes, but Daniel Jones played well again, but they had trouble moving the ball down the field a lot because I I just think the receivers are have some issues. Ashton Dulin has kind of gotten into this rhythm in camp where it's been like he's had a drop early or at some point in the practice and then made several other plays. Nick Westbrook-Ikhine to my way of thinking has not really been able to keep it going the same way like we saw in the first in the first week. We'll see if he can get it back. But it's just with Downs and Pierce out today, a lot of times lining up you'd have Westbrook-Ikhine, Dulin, and Anthony Gould. And I think just going into a regular season game where they know they can key on Tyler Warren, they know they can key on JT out of the backfield. It's really tough for this passing game. >> It's yeah, you you don't maybe expect any one of these injuries to necessarily go into the regular season, at least we don't I don't I don't have any of that indication yet, but seems like this is more so a picture of what can happen. You can you someone could go down with a groin injury or hamstring injury or a twisted ankle at any point in the regular season. And when you even get a one or two of those to start to build up, this is I would say some of the the dire place that this receiver [music] group can be and I think that's why you and I have felt like it would behoove the Colts to go and make a move for a guy like Keenan Allen. Deebo Samuel and and Stefon Diggs are already off the board in terms of veteran free agent wide receivers that started camp on the market. Chris Ballard told us a couple weeks ago that the Colts would consider making a move like that, but wasn't something that was maybe on the the front burner when we came into training camp. We'll see if some of these injuries move the needle and get them to that point. They still have a good amount of cap space to deal with at the moment. We'll see if a move like that gets done. In the hour plus camp that we saw today, what was maybe the biggest play that stood out to you? >> One one big play for me, Laiatu Latu with the a nice sack of Daniel Jones. Beat Jaylon Travis off the edge. This is a little bit of an add to the one one play. He did have another another good rush like that. Got called for offsides one time, but that's the kind of practice we start to need to see from him more often where he's in Daniel Jones' face a lot. >> Mhm. We will be back here again on Sunday. The Colts have their ninth practice here tomorrow morning and be the last practice here at Grand Park for about a week or so. They head to New England. We'll have a joint practice with the Patriots on Tuesday in Foxborough and then their first preseason game of the season Thursday evening there in New England. We'll be back here at Grand Park next Saturday. But until then, we will have a lot more coverage on our YouTube page, videos like this, our interviews, our maybe some clips from our our podcast. Hopefully you guys continue to like and subscribe there. We also have a couple stories today on indystar.com not only from Colts practice, but Adam Vinatieri's induction speech at the Pro Football Hall of Fame with Carlie Irsay Gordon there to introduce him as well. I'll be writing about that this afternoon and some more stories throughout the next couple days as the Colts camp continues to move on. Until then, I'm Nathan Brown for the Indy Star. He's Joel Erickson. Thanks for watching this edition of our insiders from training camp. >> What are your impressions of this defense been and how nice is it to be out there with Mooney at the same time? >> Uh it's been great. You know, defense been bringing that energy. At all three levels, you know. Mooney, you know, he's been he's been doing his thing. We've been talking to each other, making sure we're on the same page. Just making sure we're all together as a defense. I think we've been doing pretty good. Especially secondary, you know, since that's how I play. I play at the secondary. You know, we're pretty complete. And so, >> What do you what do you make of Justin Walley? He's kind of been a guy that's standing out according to Lou and Mooney as well. What have you seen from him? >> I mean, he's nice, you know what I'm saying? His uh his IQ for the game, for him to be young and have that his IQ, it was great. Uh obviously, he got all the physical intangibles, you know, he's quick. Uh his instincts are top-tier, you know what I'm saying? I like his footwork a lot, you know, he uses his feet a lot. Yeah, he just make plays. >> You mentioned that you want to be able to get the ball more this year, but how do you stay engaged when you might not get tested as much as the other cornerbacks side of that? What do you all how you kind of deal with that when you know any any play could probably come back to you? >> Uh you know, I don't even I don't even give myself no more excuses no more. I just be like, man, if I get two targets, I need two picks. I need two, like, you know what I'm saying? That's how I think, dog. Because we were just joking. I think it was a uh it was a play. I don't know who ran it, but we had watched the game we played the Falcons. Drake London basically ran like a little out route and I had looked back, perfect position, The didn't get thrown. It was somebody else in the media and who had ran and the ball got thrown and made a play. I'm like, damn, I just wish I could have got the ball thrown to me on that specific play. You know, but you know, it's one of those things, whenever the ball is thrown, that's what coach Chris Heu will coach on. It's just like we all align right there. No excuses, the ball get thrown your way, make a play. I don't care if during the season I had 30 targets, they got to be 30 plays made on the ball. You know, that's where our mind is and that's how my mind has changed over the years and I feel like that's, you know, just a growth mindset, growth mentality, you know, so. >> What sticks out about Ashton Dulin and Mike Strachan? You're going up against those guys as well. >> Man, they've been giving me good work, all of us. It's just a blessing to just be able to go out there and just work against those guys. They're making me better, I'm making them better, but you know, um both of them present different challenges. Obviously, Mike E got pretty good speed. Ashton, he'd be rolling, rolling. Both of them got uh pretty good hands, you know, and got pretty good route running, so you know, it's just been great just being able to make them better, they've been making me better, so. >> What excites you most about playing in Lovie Smith's defense now that you've had a chance to be in here for your first training camp with the Colts? >> I mean, just the fact that, you know, I got some of it under my belt already from last season and that I've been able to start from ground zero this upcoming year, so I'm able to just diag- diagnose everything way faster instead of being in my head like, what I got to do here, what I got to do here, you know what I'm saying? >> And then after you after you've had some time to reflect on it, what was last season like you battling, you know, [snorts] injury here or there, get traded to a new team in the middle of the season, trying to pick up a new playbook for a team that um was trying to make the playoff? What was like, was it as chaotic as it as it may have looked out to us? >> Oh, yeah. Yeah, it was chaotic. Um I'd be lying if I didn't say if I said otherwise. Um you know, I can't make no excuses. I got to call on Tuesday. We playing in Berlin on Sunday. That's the That was the reality and wasn't nothing else to talk about. And you playing all the plays, like you know, so it wasn't like no grace period, no let's get you acclimated to the It was like learn all this in these three days, go do that. That's what you get paid for, basically. They didn't tell me that, but basically that's what that was, but um yeah, man, it's just it's just great to be here, you know, great to just be embraced by the fans, by you guys, you know, and just be able to just be my best each and every day. But I can't say the night scrimmage was a little crazy at 8:00 p.m., but like I said, no excuses, you know, talking about the injury from last year, like that's what really got me where I needed to be for that night scrimmage. Cuz I tried to take a nap, couldn't go to sleep, so then when I got out there, I was just tired, but you know, just on the way, I was just like, man, I didn't even get to finish the last season. You know, so it's really a blessing just to be out here at 8:00 p.m. playing the game that I love, got a true passion for, so >> So, you talked last >> last year about, you know, you didn't win a lot in New York, and you came here, obviously you didn't get a chance to play enough and win and stuff. Winning is why you play. Um how motivating is that for you right now? >> I mean, we going to win here. You know, that's just That's the reality, period, point blank, so you know, I don't really think about like the New York scene and all of that. This place we going to win here. We got, you know, coaches, you know, it's just We talk about going against like Doolin and Nick, like just being able to go against uh Coach Shane every day. That's really who I'm going against as well, cuz he a top three play caller. Like I've been like obviously spent time with different play callers at with the Jets. Played against a decent amount of play callers, but like he's top three, easily, you know, so you know, it's just great just seeing all of it come together and it's like that's making me better. You know what I'm saying? Like any cheats that I'm giving the offense so they know like, all right, let's run this against them. Let's run this against the defense. So, you know, it's just it's great. Like, we have everything that it takes to win here and you know, it ain't a doubt in my mind about that. >> What makes him top five? Last one here, James. >> Man, he just know how to dice the defense up. Like Y'all job, y'all going to be saying, "Oh, Daniel doing XYZ. Daniel doing this." I mean, Shane is really the the he's he's driving the ship, for real. You know, his play calling be great. And obviously, don't get me wrong. Daniel, he's playing like obviously, he's playing like a top five quarterback right now. You know, there's some throws that he's made here where I'm like, "Bro, that's a throw that I seen ARod make when I was in New York." You know, so it's just great just seeing everything come together. Just seeing the offense how how they're play calling, how Daniel he's he's leading the offense and you know, how us as a defense he's challenging him as well. So, you know, that's why when it comes to winning, I'm like, man, we got everything that it takes. So, we're just going to put it all together. >> I'll just get it kicked off. You know, obviously, I'm sure there'll be a little more conversation about the kickers. Not a huge update to give on the kickers. Obviously, big night Thursday night. As we come into today, you know, before we were kicking today, just looking at all kicks. So, in practice, pre-practice, all the kicks that we've charted or filmed, you know, there's highs and lows to both guys. I think it's been overall a solid work. Groovy overall's kicking 85% and Schrader's kicking 83%. The bigger difference situation's going to be when they go live. Schrader Schrader hasn't been kicking as consistently as Groovy when we've been going live. Obviously, everybody has seen those live kicks and and kind of discussed or known that. And Groovy's kicking 91% before today when we've gone live. But, we kind of look at, you know, the big picture overall like we talked about last time. Just to be able to see how are they kicking overall? What's their best ball look like? What are the the timing, the rhythm, the mechanics on their best ball? Versus is there an issue or something that we can highlight? Under the lights Thursday night, um Schrader was 7 for 10. Uh when we went live, Grupe was 8 for 10. Um I think we started off tonight really good. Obviously, we want to kick it over 90%, which we didn't do that, so that wasn't totally at the standard. Um we did miss, you know, some longer distance kicks as well. That's going to happen at times. Uh you saw Grupe miss from 53. He kind of opened his hips and pulled it to the left, which is the first time he's missed a live kick um in any situation since being a Colt both last year in the regular season. He never missed a practice or a game, and he didn't miss in OTAs or training camp up to that point. So, you know, he's no longer pitching a perfect game. We can finally get over that hurdle. Um overall, I thought he hit the ball really good. He ended up laying it short from 61. He kind of slipped into his plant a little bit. That's going to happen at times. He's not going to have, you know, he does He has a very good leg for his size, but it's not going to have elite leg strength. So, when he's kicking from 60-plus, he's going to have to get a little bit more into that at times, more so than what Schrader would have to do. Um today, I thought Grupe came out and kicked really well. He made two, you know, end of half, you know, situational kicks. He did miss one from 58. This is the first day we've really had conditions. We had a strong uh right-to-left wind, so there was a strong crosswind. Just his one miss today, he didn't quite play it in the wind, but that's great just for us to be able to get some conditions. For the most part, when we we've been out here kicking, it's been really good weather. It's really the same thing with Schrader. Like, it's unreasonable to think after not kicking for 8 months and not really kicking in a full operation for 10 months that he was going to come out here and everything was going to be perfect. You know, some of that I think is mental, which is going to be natural, especially with kickers that he wants to be kicking at the near-perfect level he was last September. It's going to take some time for him to be able to get there. Um all of his misses have been pulled to the left, so there are, you know, a little bit of an issue that we've addressed with some of those things. That's going to come down to rhythm, timing, and leg swing that he's looking to clean up. And we'll, you know, just expect to see him progress as we continue to go through things. It's a sprint, it's not a marathon. So, we're not judging who's the best kicker in the first 2 weeks. We're judging who is the best kicker to make us through the regular season that gives us the best chance to to score points and win games. Looking onto the preseason, uh first game, you know, in the joint practice in in the preseason game, we're going to try to get as many guys reps as we possibly can and see how they can handle those reps. I think so far, we've gotten more young guys reps, especially on the punt team, than we've ever had before. I think we have a really, really good young group of rookies that's done really well on punt, better so than any group that we've had in the first 3 years that I've been here. We'll continue to feed those guys as many reps as we possibly can. Usually in a preseason game like each preseason game last year, we play over 50 guys on special teams in the game. So, we're going to be rolling in as many guys as we can, give guys opportunities, see how they handle some of those things. It's very possible some young guys, right, are going to have some tough learning moments, but we'd rather have some of those learning moments in a preseason game than a regular season game. Gives us a chance to be able to evaluate guys that are going to be able to give us a chance to be successful in regular season. So, we're really excited about that next week. Based on some injuries and things, you know, returner-wise as we go into the first preseason game, I think punt returner-wise we'll be looking at Gold, Colquitt, O'Malley, and Haegens are going to be the main three guys that will be ready to go for that. We'll start off, you know, Gold and Colquitt O'Malley being more experienced guys that will probably start off as the kickoff returners, but want to get some younger guys, especially Burks and McAllen, a chance to show what they can do as kickoff returners in the first preseason game. That's kind of what we got coming up. >> You mentioned the mental side of kicking. How do you help coach Succop and Bullock through the mental hurdles of that position? >> Yeah, I think the biggest thing is you just need the same mental routine every time you go on the field. So, you want to be saying the same small phrase or three words to yourself, so you're not overthinking or thinking about things. And it can be easy sometimes if you're not in a great rhythm to be thinking about, you know, one issue you may have or to overthink and to hear the exact details you need to do. But you have to stay relaxed and smooth, so that you have good timing, you're not leaning in or too fast, or that you have a good leg swing. And the biggest thing is like the the holder is the catalyst, right? So, Rico does an unbelievable job of making sure those guys are relaxed and locked in and trying to make sure that they're thinking about the the phrase they need to be thinking about or staying focused on what they need to think about. He can also feel like usually Rigo can feel based on where their plant was and how the leg swing was. He can tell why but here's what happened and he can then help them out immediately. So Rigo is really the big key piece to that. >> What are those three words? >> Well, every guy is something different. Right now he's just thinking stay down and through the ball. Um but everybody's going to have that's just an example of like everybody's going to have I try to teach those guys to have something so they're not thinking about 10 things, they're not thinking about the crowd, they're just locked in on the one thing that they want to focus on the ball. >> Has Jonathan Edwards really taken like a a huge step forward as a gunner from last year to this year? >> I think he has and I think he you know some of the experience and stuff that he got last year was really good for him. Um you know he's a guy that in the first preseason game last year had an opportunity to make a tackle at gunner and you know we don't quite fit it correctly in coverage and they end up returning it to the house. Like he was the gunner that was right there. You know you go from that moment to where he is now and I think he's going to leap some bounds. He's extremely talented and has put in some extra work to get to the point where we expect him to have a really good year as being one of our top gunners. >> When it comes to this kicker battle, how big is the kickoff aspect of it directing kicks and getting them where you guys want them to go? >> I think they're both really good kickoff guys. Um I think they both have been working on a variety of different kicks. Both of them were good kickoff guys for us last year. Um and at the end of the day for us like we're going to expect our covers to be really good. We're going to expect ourselves to play gap down and play sound. Um very similar to what we did last year and we played three different kickers. So if they don't have a trick kick or they don't have something special that's fine. We're going to put the ball at the goal line. We're going to let the cover guys do their job. So the biggest part of the aspect of the evaluation is going to be field goal. I don't think kickoffs are really going to come into the evaluation because we know both the guys can do what we need them to do. >> Talking about Rigo, I mean going through a kicking competition where you have this consistent battery that's been together for almost a decade now with Luke and Rigo. Just how beneficial is that in evaluating Spencer and Blank? >> It's it's great, you know, you know, good question JJ just because you can expect that they're going to have a solid operation and it's going to be consistent at all times. So obviously it can be difficult sometimes if they're not kicking on the same day in the exact same conditions. You're trying to get them the same reps as best you possibly can so it's an even evaluation, but it certainly helps like hey, there's really not going to be an excuse with the operation. We know that even if it's not perfect the ball's going to get down and it's going to be correctly the way it needs to be and you guys can trust that. And you also know that hey, we don't have to micromanage Luke and Reid. They're veterans. They're in their 10th and 11th year in the NFL. Um they've been with the Colts for a long time. They know exactly what they need to do to be successful. So then you can spend more time focusing on, you know, the kickers and some different things that we need to do there knowing that those guys are going to take care of their business. >> Who's first? >> Louis, uh how are how are things kind of shaping up at linebacker? You know, CJ's been in and out and then you got a lot of guys kind of rotating. >> Yeah, it's still for us, you know, what was this practice eight, nine, whatever it is. So we're going to be rolling those guys constantly until you know, guys get healthy again and uh just kind of find out what best works, but I would envision that group. Uh we've got great competition and I think it's going to continue until it sorts itself out, but at the end of the day I think we're going to have a lot of guys in that room that play for us this year in different type of roles. >> So you could could you maybe be a little bit specialized? Is that what you're kind of getting at? >> Potentially, you know, not maybe overloading a guy early in his career with all of it. Maybe give him a uh little bit of this, little bit of that and as they get more comfortable the more we give, you know, so uh at least at least initially that's the approach. >> Are you overall pleased with that group with you've seen early on? >> Yeah, I mean again, it's it's a lot on their plates and um they're they're doing the great job. Coach Betcher does a great job with those guys. They meet above and beyond what they're supposed to and um you know, gets the extra time in and and they're really working hard. So, um feel good about it. But yeah, to answer your question, yes, I do. >> If you don't mind on the side, Cam Taylor-Britt's been really involved out here. Are you seeing a bit more of what you saw at Cincinnati? >> Yeah, I hope so. You know, so far he's been that way and again another guy that we're giving a bunch of different jobs to and he's approached it the right way. Uh Jerome and Chris Hewitt have done a great job there with him and you know, I know Cam for a long time. Obviously, he's played in the biggest games, uh started in the biggest games, uh championship games. So, he knows what the pressure's like um and I would just got to stay consistent. >> With the back seven in in general, do you feel like you have more flexibility to be versatile there week to week just with the depth of the roster? >> I think right now, you know, um I'm happy where we're with where we're at with that group. I think um you know, like I think any any coach would tell you the more pieces that are interchangeable, the more we can do as coaches. So, and the and the players have shown us especially back there that they can do that. >> What impact do you think Sauce can have for this defense on the field? Off the field, how would you characterize how he fuels this defense, leads this defense and um and affects it? >> Well, I think he's one of the one of the leaders that we have, one of the many leaders. That's the good news. He doesn't uh have to stand above anybody else. I think, you know, the you're talking about Buck and Grove, the guys that have been here uh that can, you know, lead this defense. Uh Arden Key has played a lot of years in this league. Uh you know, Cam Bingham. So, we have a lot of leaders. Uh he's in the long line of those and you know, happy he's with us. >> What's been your assessment of Bryce Young so far throughout camp? >> Well, I I think uh he's been good. So, to answer the question directly, he's been he's been good. He's a rookie. He's going to make error. Um we'll we'll have a a really good feel after we go to New England, after Atlanta comes here, we play some games and they're out there actually tackling people, running, hitting. You know, we're doing some of that here. Uh but until they actually get in game situations against, you know, a team that was in the Super Bowl last year and Atlanta offensively was a good team with a good running attack and one of the premier backs. So, um we have we'll have a chance to get a really good evaluation. What he's been uh put in front of his plate right now, he's done a good job with. >> Lou, do you plan on playing your starters in the preseason? >> Uh that's Shane. You know, Shane will make that call and we'll proceed how the how that goes. >> Did you feel a lot to out there a little bit more there on that final drive of final couple periods? >> I thought our guys today came out with the right mindset. Um you know, I think it's the middle of camp in some regard uh where, you know, they know they're a couple days from leaving and maybe look ahead. But, you know, we've been talking about just attacking the day that we're in and and I thought we did a good job of that today and I was happy and Lotu was one of them. >> This does make for a great opportunity for those guys. They're going to get a chance to run uh some of the routes that maybe they wouldn't get to run otherwise. So, you know, they're getting they're getting uh to operate them with Daniel or operate them with different quarterbacks and uh shoot, we're you know, if you can get open and make a play, uh you you you show up for the coaching staff and you show up for the quarterback, which is more important, right? Those guys uh kind of tend to throw it to the guys that prove they can go get open and make those plays. So, yeah, great opportunity for the for the uh wide receiver room. >> Jimbo, are you seeing any consistency from Anthony that you want to? >> He he's still working through it. There's there's really good days. There's really good periods. Um like like all of our guys, you're going to you're going to make a mistake here and there and try to go fix that thing, clean that thing up. Um so, we're working through that. Lou gives us a bunch of different looks on defense to create problems and uh sometimes, you know, uh the disguise can be difficult. So, they're you know, if if you're going out there and practicing, you're practicing perfectly, you're probably not getting enough out of practice. So, we're competing against uh Lou and that defense and you know, there's mistakes being made. There's plenty of coaching for us to do and uh for each of our players, uh you know, there's improvement to be made uh in all areas, consistency being one of those. >> Coleman, >> has been pretty productive practice over practice. >> What what does he do well on the slot position? >> Yeah, I mean kind of the core the core things that have to do with being a receiver, at least in the pass game, you know, get open, catch the ball, be where the quarterback needs you to be. Uh Coleman does all those things really, really well. Uh really uh does a nice job setting up routes and and marrying different routes uh so that it is tougher to cover him, you know, on a on a certain route he may have an opportunity to use the uh same stem and break two directions or sit. Uh but he's able to use that against the defense uh to maximum effect. He's doing a nice job right now getting open and uh you know, shoot, great opportunity here for him to get a bunch of reps and bunch of routes and you know, see if he can carry that forward. >> With with uh Sauce on the other side, you got a lot of receivers rotating going up against him. What what is the difficulty of that match-up with his length and the way he plays? >> Yeah, great question. He's obviously a great player. You know, some of those uh play calling situations where you might target an outside receiver one-on-one uh on Sauce, I try to you know, we try to be very cautious of what we're what we're asking our guys to do there. Sauce is uh you know, so long, he's seen so much even at you know, he's a young player but he's played a bunch of ball, he's seen a lot of things. Um kind of diagnoses things well, you got to be really careful about the tells you have uh that that he can pick up on. Uh but ultimately he's just a you know, high level cover guy who makes it tough on you to complete passes. Uh his length, his athleticism, all those things, his intelligence, all those things play a big role in how he's having success.

title: Colts Cover-2 Podcast: Reactions halfway through Colts training camp
text: Hey there Colts fans, this is Nathan Brown, your Colts insider with the Indianapolis Star here for another edition of the Colts Cover 2 podcast. Here with my beat co-beat reporter Joel A. Erickson. We've now seen seven practices of Colts training camp over at Grand Park. We're taping this on Friday morning. Joel got a chance to watch last night's night practice where Jonathan Jones lit up the field with some great action looking like the perfect non-injured version of himself that we've begun to grow accustomed to over the course [snorts] of these first two weeks of Colts training camp. We'll get into all that here in just a second. We're going to break down some of our reactions from the offense, the defense, rookies, some interesting position battles that have been going on in training camp. But before we get to that, some big news broke yesterday, Thursday morning. Some something that um we felt like might come at some point during training camp, but didn't really have any great feel on it. But the second and then and shortly after the the third big running back deal around the NFL. The second one going coming to Jonathan Taylor. That gets agreed to and finalized yesterday. A 2 million 2-year $44 million extension for the 27-year-old Colts running back. A fairly unprecedented, at least in modern day times, third deal for a running back for a team. He gets paid quite handsomely, more than the more than he's making on this 3-year deal that he signed back in October of 2023. He's contracted with the team through the end of the 2028 season. $39 million in guaranteed money. Joel, we we've talked to Jonathan a couple times across training camp. He said that part of the reason that he was there in camp at Grand Park with the Colts is that he felt like he had faith that something was going to get done. Felt like things were moving in the right direction. Um a big reason why he opted not to hold in, kind of like he did 3 years ago, like Bijan Robinson in Atlanta and Jahmyr Gibbs in Detroit had been doing, which helped get their deals finalized this week. Um one on Tuesday and then of course Jahmyr Gibbs yesterday. Um this gets done. Um this helps Taylor continue hoping to be the Colt for life that he's told us he wants to be. What was your biggest takeaway from this deal getting finalized yesterday? >> I it it just they kind of had to do it. There's not I there's there's this been this layer of thinking where if you're the Colts knowing that Ballard's in the last year of his deal, that you just kind of punt everything until um you kind of punt everything right there until the until the last second and you let all these guys go to free agency in case you want to let them go. The problem with that is what if the players themselves don't want to do that? Uh specifically the engine of your offense. Uh the guy that the offense essentially runs through. Um Wha- what about that scenario? Because that's where we that's where we were. With the other deals going on around the league, Jonathan Taylor having said, you know, he wants to be a Colt for life. Um and and what and knowing that normally guys sign an extension before the year before that they hit free agency. Like there was always the possibility with Taylor that he was going to force the Colts hand. Now, I I will say this, the Colts didn't let it get to it. Prob- probably mindful of what happened last time. Um where they they had a very public and messy and uh for a lot of Colts fans annoying um you know the protracted negotiation of 2023, they didn't do that this time. It was very quiet. Jonathan Taylor you know, stated his goals, but didn't hold in, didn't hold out, didn't do any of that stuff. I think I think they just kind of had to do this. They had to do it for this year to have her to credibly be trying for it this year. If if you tell him no and he decides to sit out, you're in I like Seth McGowan a lot, but he's no Jonathan Taylor. Um and you're already down a playmaker at playmaker or wide receiver. Like they they just kind of had to do this and I don't really think the flexibility is hurt going forward. >> That's that was That was That was one thing I wanted to touch on because I know the impression that a lot of us have had is that the Colts are kind of in this make-or-break season where um you know, Kaley doesn't use these, you know, these exact words or phrases, um but she has said through her motto of this team needing to quote find a way this season. Um it when you know that Chris Ballard is in a contract year, Shane Steichen is going into his fourth year even though his deal goes beyond the the pair together have not been in the playoffs and typically if you're a head coach from a team that isn't um just you know, being completely rebuilt from the ground up and in a fan base and an organization that has a ton of patience, four years without the playoffs um typically is not viewed super well. And so even as as glowingly as Shane is I think viewed pretty uniformly around the league for his offensive play calling, um it it would seem maybe a little bit long odds that he would be able to stick around after four years if they weren't making the playoffs. So, when you when you look at the books now, yeah, there's some exceptions to this, but for next year I'm I I just pulled up um the the salary cap um list on Over the Cap for the Colts for 2027. Um looking at some of these cap hits uh that some Colts that the Colts have hanging around for next year. They obviously have players like DeForest Buckner, um Quinnen Williams, Josh Downs, Jonathan Taylor of of course was uh another one. Colt uh players who were on expiring deals going into next season. You've got a a lot of very, very minimal deals, but you also got now some increasingly big ones. Um cap numbers next season, Alec Pierce just over 35 million, Bernard Reiman a little over 30 million, Sauce Gardner um nearly 21 million, Cam Bynum uh 18 almost 18.5, Daniel Jones 46.8. you'll have Jonathan Taylor, we don't quite have those figures yet. Um of course he's on a um average annual uh value over the course of his 2-year extension of $22 million. Um Mo Niang Ward's nearly 25 million. Uh when you hear those numbers, I mean, is that could that still be the type of team that if things just go terribly wrong where they could cut a lot a lot of these guys loose and you know, take a bunch of a big cap hits if they are trying to completely start over. Um in your experience in the league is does this feel like a team that still could a couple months from now be tearing everything down to the the studs and parting away with a bunch of big guys, or do you feel like this team is set itself up with some of these deals to um not maybe quite have the amount of star power change over that we might expect? >> Yeah, I I think there's a couple of things that would tell you that like we need to start reevaluating how teams are going to handle these these deals. Number one, Sauce Gardner's on the team. Um he signed a deal with the Jets last summer and was traded to the Colts in October. Like they they they structured it in a way where they could do that. We haven't seen the the structure on Taylor's contract yet, but um you know, that they that's the kind of deal with that you would normally think of as binding, and he was gone very quickly. Uh the other the other one I think around the league that would suggest that if a team wants to move on, they can. Is you just look at the Miami Dolphins. They're carrying if I have my numbers right, $7 trillion in uh dead money on the salary cap because they're they're rebuilding. They're they're going completely They're doing what a lot of Colts fans are hoping that the Colts do, which is completely re-rebuilding the entire roster from the ground up and taking on this massive undertaking. If the Colts decide to do that, I don't think I think anything's on the table uh in terms of in terms of finding ways to get out of it, finding ways to not pay that stuff. it I I think I've said this before. I'm not sure. But I think I've said this before on this podcast. If if they really want to tear it down to the studs, you kind of have to throw all that contract stuff and everything out the window because if a new GM wants to tear it down completely, he will. He'll find a way. Um because you're not if you're tearing it down, you're not expecting to be good in that first year anyway. So it's not like you need the cap space. >> That's a good point. Yeah. And and of course a lot of those figures there that I mentioned um aren't the the dead cap money if they were to cut a player loose, just the the cap figures itself. I mean, you look at someone like um trying to find a a good example here quickly. Um I mean, I guess like Kemoko Ebukam for example, um on the the books for cap-wise um almost 18.5 next year. Cut him loose, um you've only got 9 million in deadcap. Um, Daniel Jones a little bit more, but when when you when you look at his deadcap figure of 35 million, I mean, that's nothing. What was two of this year? Um, someone something like 95 million. Am I making that number up or is that isn't that like >> Yeah, it's at some point at some point the Browns are not going to have Deshaun Watson anymore and it's going to be an insane deadcap hit. Not this is like Not that this is uh yeah. >> 99.2 million dollars. >> There we go. There we go. Um, Moony Ward like do cap wise nearly 25 million dollars next year, but has a deadcap hit of not even quite 7 million dollars. So, there's ways to get around some of this. That was I think some of the reaction I saw on social media yesterday was um, you know, why why would a team do this when they could very well be um, you know, completely restarting next year. Why are you spending this money? Well, first off, um, any I mean, any money that um, they work towards going against this year's cap um, with some sort of a signing bonus or or anything else. They have more than 30 million dollars in cap space right now. So, they have plenty of of money to work with if that's in some way, shape or form how this deal is structured. and then I mean, when you when you think about a salary cap as as high as it is right now, I mean, yes, 22 million dollars for a running back is a lot, but in some ways I don't know that it's all that much when you consider how important it is to try to win this year. Um, if you if you think that Jonathan Taylor is in any way underpaid this year, some of that you could um, reason is incentivizing him this year, making him happy, you know, energizing the locker room. We talked to a couple We talked to um lineman Mag- Goncalves last night and he talked about um you know, seeing JT last night ahead of practice and just kind of how energized and and excited that that his teammates were for him to have gotten paid. Um I I think something like that a a token of appreciation like that can go a long ways in a locker room um versus feeling like feeling like um uh uh uh an an ownership group or the general manager is kind of waiting on bated breath to to see the the locker room prove it. Um they've they've clearly put their trust in Jonathan Taylor. They feel like he is the future for this franchise and um I mean, he told us last night in the short time frame that we got to talk to him um that he appreciated this commitment just as much as he felt like he was committed to this team and this franchise for the long haul. So, we will we'll see ultimately what comes of that. Um uh a lot of games to be played and decisions to be made before we find out if indeed he is on this roster through 2028, but um let's get to training camp. We've now seen seven practices. The Colts are off today before a couple of um weekend practices on Saturday and Sunday and then they head to Foxborough for a joint practice on Tuesday ahead of their first preseason game on Thursday evening. Um feel like we we finally got gotten away from um coaches or players being able to say, "Well, it's really really in camp." even though I think I think we probably even heard that a day or two ago. Like I I I feel like for the most part, except for um guys who have been injured, um Hinton, Alec Pierce, um we have a pretty good feeling of where a lot of these players are. uh a decent feel on at least where the offense and the defense are at this point in the season. Um and I think we had some pretty solid expectations of of where where we expected things to be um from a player standpoint, from a unit standpoint. So, let's start with Daniel Jones. Uh you wrote a couple days ago and I think it was really well put that coming into training camp, we felt like his his physical capabilities or a lack thereof as he was coming back from his torn right Achilles tendon was going to be the storyline that drove uh the entire training camp. And by now, seven practices in and really you'd probably even admit a a practice or two ago, this has kind of been put on the back burner. We felt like there were a lot of questions on him not even um I guess what was it? I Today is actually um the uh 8-month anniversary of when he tore this. So, he's been doing everything we've seen in camp still not even quite 8 months uh away from tearing his Achilles. Uh compared to where what your expectations were for Daniel Jones, um how have how has what you've seen him do on the field compared to those so far? >> Yeah, part of the reason that we're doing this podcast today is that it's a natural break. They had their night practice last night, which um the way Shane Steichen has handled that as a scrimmage, he's handled that as a scrimmage the last couple years. And so, um it's it's a clear first it's a clear like first point marking. Like for me, the points in camp that that mark certain things are uh you've got this this ends to me like the initial like lead-in part of camp. Uh this next phase is the joint practice part of camp. And then camp is essentially done after that. Um joint practices and preseason games and then you move to okay, finalizing the roster, regular season. Okay, so we're we're about to be in the second phase here with them having two practices on Saturday but then really going to before them going to New England and really really getting into that next phase camp. But Daniel Jones last night in in the the the night time practice, he was 21 of 28. Uh it's funny cuz on our video that we do for for the website, I said I think I don't have the numbers in front of me. I think he was like 75% and I nailed it without knowing the numbers at all. Like that's just it it felt like 75%. It looked like 75%. He was just really really good and I think the other thing is he pulled the ball down on two separate plays where he had to get out of the pocket and race up the middle and he really ran. Uh and looked like the Daniel Jones we saw last year when he ran. Um and it's just it's it's remarkable. He he's very accurate. He's been he's been honestly probably the most reliable thing in camp. It'd be close between him and like Sauce Gardner or or maybe Jonathan Taylor. Uh just Jonathan Taylor looks like Jonathan Taylor. But like uh outside of those two, I think it's really just Daniel Jones looking like Daniel Jones for for what's the most consistent thing in camp whereas all off season, you know, when I saw it when I talked to listeners of this podcast outside of when I saw you guys in the in in real life or or talked to you at uh moving around, it was always like, "Hey, what's what's when's Daniel Jones going to play?" I I got a text from somebody and they said, "Hey, I'm I'm uh >> [clears throat] >> I'm having a debate with my buddies. We're all going to put in a pool on when Daniel Jones plays his first game." And like now that pool seems like whoever has the earliest date wins because it's going to be the it's going to be right away. So yeah, it's just remarkable. He looks great. He looks great and and realistically it's there's a part of me that that wonders like he he's so far ahead of the other quarterbacks that it makes me think that maybe um like it's it's making me think that maybe like last year's evaluation where we felt like it was closer between him and Richardson wasn't was was missing some stuff. Like he he's just so far ahead of the other guys. >> So this is a thought that came to me and again I I wasn't at um I I got to the very very tail end of practice last night. I was doing something frankly rather silly. I drove to Canton. >> [laughter] >> Guys I got to listen to um Adam Vinatieri speak to the media. Um also stayed around for Drew Brees's um media session ahead of the Pro Football Hall of Fame induction this weekend, wrote a story, got back on the road and and literally pulled into Grand Park at like 9:53. Um so I did not get to see how great Daniel Jones looked and and in contrast um from reading your observations last night how underwhelming the backup quarterbacks looked. And this has been um kind of a a troubling trend I would say through these these first seven days of camp as great and um consistent and reliable as Daniel Jones has looked um his counterparts Riley Leonard and Anthony Anthony Richardson who we of course know are competing for that backup role the only consistency I think has been their inconsistency in the ways they've struggled. Riley Leonard continues to hold onto the ball too long. Anthony Richardson continues to bobble snaps um over overthrow guys or throw balls that are too high and just not look like the electric version of him that we had grown to expect over the first couple years of his career when he was healthy. do the Colts from what you've seen over the first couple weeks of camp, if you are the Colts and you both look at how great Daniel Jones looks, but also take a look at his injury history and know that it's frankly a little bit of long shot that you get him through the entire regular season, do they need to go and consider bringing in another quarterback? >> Uh I don't think there's not going to be anybody to to get. >> So >> we we actually have a a super like poignant data point on this. When when Andrew Luck retired in in 2019, it was 2 weeks before the end of training camp and they went out and got uh who was the Brian Hoyer who he was the best he was the best guy in the market at the And he was experienced, he was in his 30s, he played, he'd been a starter before. Like but the Patriots were kind of moving their that year was the year that the Patriots started moving around their backups a little bit behind Brady. And yeah, they they they you thought that um you thought that Hoyer was going to be good. And then when he had to play for the Colts, he was terrible that season. And Colts fans will remember the Dolphins game um that they lost to a Dolphins team that was very clearly trying not to win. They were they were trying Brian Flores was trying to win and nobody else was trying to win. Hoyer was very bad and that's that's the situation they're in now. I I do think that with either of those guys, there's a path if they have to play um a short amount of time. I don't think a long amount of time for any any team really is going to work out. Um I think you even see that with like Malik Willis with the Packers last year. Like he played well and they lost some of those games. but for a short amount of time, I think there's different ways you can use both of them. Leonard, there's a little bit of a gamer aspect to Leonard or at least there has been so far in the NFL where when he gets thrust into a situation or put in the starting lineup, he looks better than he does in practice. and I think I think that that might be partially just to he's a gamer. I also think it might partially be that he can take advantage of a game plan. Like they're not game planning stuff out here in practice the same way that they do in a game. They're not looking They're not dialing stuff up specifically to attack certain things on the other team. Um so I I do think that could help him in that way and that's one of the explanations for why he looked good against Houston. Um and really against Jacksonville, too. I think his stat line in that is misleading compared to the way he looked play-to-play. Richardson, I think the path is is the Malik Willis path. I think if Richardson's your backup, you have to have a a different offense essentially dialed up and ready to go. So there are there are ways to do it if you have each of the backups, but yeah, as far as the consistency thing, I I don't Leonard has been consistent in that he generally runs fairly high completion percentages. Um but a lot of it's to running backs and tight ends and short. Like I think he was 10 of 15 last night. And off the top of my head, I think only one went to a guy who could have been an outside receiver. Um there were a lot of passes to Ellis Bentley. There was a couple to Will Mallory. There were like three to Cole McDonald. Cole McDonald is interesting, by the way. I don't know if he's going to make this I don't know if he can make this roster with the way the receivers are, but he catches a lot of passes out of the slot. Um he's probably going to look good in preseason again. But, you know, obviously you don't want your guy just to be running check downs and running backs and stuff like that. But, Leonard has been somewhat consistent in that. The The variability with with Richardson right now is really stark. Um, there was an entire period in in last night's Part of it is because of this this Thursday night practice is fresh in my brain. But, there's also the snaps. Um, I don't remember if we talked if we did I think I don't think we did talk about this. >> No, cuz we had just we'd seen one practice when we did our last pod. So, >> There was a practice last week that he he bobbled or fumbled five shotgun snaps. Uh, those those issues with the snap have not gone away. The one he fumbled last night was an under center snap. And I was watching it. He I don't watch every snap through the binoculars at training camp because we're close. And I sometimes I want to be able to see the whole field. But, I happen to be watching that one through the binoculars looking at the pocket. And he just he just pulled his head out uh, and up to look at the defense before he really had the ball. Um, he didn't his body didn't stay down on the football. And so, that inconsistency with the snap is an issue. His inconsistency with his feet is an issue. Leonard has some of this too where he he has bouts of inaccuracy. With Richardson, I feel like he's There's times he just doesn't set his feet. Or he doesn't move his feet to his target and it leads to it leads to inaccuracy. They're both taking a ton of sacks. it's it's concerning, but I still think that in a in a actual game situation where they have to take over and start, I think there's ways that Shane Steichen can mitigate it for whoever he picks. >> Do you think if if we're heading into week one this weekend, do you think the backup pick is is Riley Leonard or do think Richardson is at all and could could be in play at this point? >> I think it's Riley Leonard. >> It's kind of like it's kind of like it's kind of like it's kind of >> Well, I don't think the snaps necessarily tell us anything cuz they kind of got back. There was one practice where Leonard ended up with 15 more snaps than Richardson. I think they've slowly kind of uh made up for that. But I just think if if the consistency's the thing, I think it's Leonard. >> And we'll get a chance to see really what they look like um in uh in in earnest during the preseason. Again, Colts have >> [gasps] >> their first preseason contest in Foxborough next Thursday. Um everything we've heard from training camp is uh I would not expect Daniel Jones to be out there at all. So, that means three games of getting a chance to see what um Anthony and and Riley um can can do out there. And that's I would imagine largely how that battle will will be decided um in you know, against opposing defenses. Well, you know, the the joint practices maybe they see a tiny bit of time in those, but I imagine a lot of that will be wanting to see how um first team offensive unit looks against uh opposing defenses on the other end of the field. So, um let's maybe expand our lens a little bit and look at this offense as a whole um take into account the state of the offensive line, the skill position players. Um what has your impression been of this offense over the first 7 days of training camp practices versus what you were expecting? Um what are where are some of the the high points? Where are some of the weak spots? What what what are some of your thoughts after watching these first 2 weeks of training camp? >> Um It it's It's a training camp where we haven't seen this a lot at Colts camp, but there there's a there's a clear disparity over the years, I mean, this this year we have there's a clear difference of talent level between the outside receivers and the cornerbacks. and I will say this, last night Ashton Dulin had five catches from Jones. Nick Westbrook-Ikhine had five catches. They did a lot of stuff over the middle. Um crossing routes. Westbrook-Ikhine is good at using his body. Dulin has Dulin has elite athletic traits. That's why he's such a great special teamer. Um but largely I think Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward and even Cam Taylor Britt are winning that battle. And so that that's one of the things that sticks out from camp is it just feels like this team needs another receiver. And this week uh since we last talked to you, several of these guys have gone. Deebo Samuel is gone. Stefon Diggs is gone. Keenan Allen is still out there, but I haven't seen anything on him. Um it it feels to me, and I think I said this last time, but even after watching camp, it feels like it more. It feels like they have fours. And if Nick Westbrook-Ikhine and Ashton Dulin were both active on game day and playing specific roles as a four as like co-fours essentially cuz they do that. They they especially with Dulin, the way Dulin works with the special teams stuff, like that's kind of the role he's been in where he's like a co-four. Um plays in the power packages, can can beat you deep, that kind of thing, and then they have another receiver. I I still I still think they need a three. Especially with without Alec Pierce. We we haven't seen Alec Pierce practice yet. And now, if he doesn't come back on we're taping this on Friday, if he doesn't come back on Saturday, I don't think we see him until after the Patriots cuz why you wouldn't bring him back for his first game in a for you for his first practice in a joint practice. that wouldn't make sense. So, um I don't know what to make of that. I don't know there's more time before the season opener after that first preseason game than I think people realize for him to get up to speed and get going. But, it's a concern. Anytime a guy's not practicing, it's a concern. And I just I just think they need another receiver. Specifically one who has You're not going to get like a super athletic deep threat at this point. But, they need somebody who cuz the guys that are available who are that type of player are are fours. They're fourths and fives. Like it's going to be a slower player, an older player like Keenan Allen. But, that's that's what Michael Pittman was essentially last year, you know? And I think this is this is the thing that we're you and I are talking about on the sidelines. We're talking about it in post-practice every day. It's just I just don't know about these receivers. >> So, you've been around this team, I mean, you've been here for Ashton Dulin's career. My my biggest impression on these guys is that in the in the condensed environment that we have, I feel like you can have a situation where an Ashton Dulin can look really great in a practice or two. Um and you can start to tell yourself that maybe he can do enough for you to be your number three. My biggest concern is if he was truly a number three caliber receiver, they would have used him more than the what, like six or seven catches he's had in the last three seasons. I I just I know you've had you've had Alec Pierce, you've had AD Mitchell, you've had Josh Downs, um a season of Tyler Warren. So, like there's only so many balls to go around. Um so, there's there's some level of argument to that, but I just I I have to think if he was a guy that you thought was deserving of catching 30, 40, 50 balls that you would have you worked him into your offense in some way more than they have in the last couple years since he tore his ACL and when he's been back healthy. Um you've got Alec Pierce who is still coming back. Again, even if he misses basically the next week and he doesn't come back until let's say um at the earliest next Saturday and Sunday's practices, you're still 4 weeks away from the start of the season. So, that still feels like a a somewhat reasonable time frame for him to come back. Yeah, Colton would not not have been very far in his move if he showed up to the show. >> Nick Whiteside >> [clears throat] >> all day. >> I I would be very surprised if Will didn't agree, and so I'm forcing him to pivot to a secondary option here, but the slow starter that has surprised me and and probably everyone that covers this team has been T.J. Clark. Uh there's there's this very true cliché. I mean, it's rooted in truth that the biggest jump for a player is year one to year two. We've seen a couple highlight reel type plays of him going up and over guys. But you kind of hope there'd be some more nuance to the route tree this year. And through the first week of camp, it's not there. And what does that mean? Well, I think we looked at Greg Dortch's addition as a supplement and not a 50/50 split like it was with Kalif Raymond. I I think it's Greg Dortch is going to eat more into the pie than maybe we thought originally because Greg Dortch has looked really really good where where Cephus has struggled. So, you know, maybe it's not going to be 80/20. Maybe it's going to be more like 60/40 at least out the gate. And so, a lot of time to kind of get this thing on track. But but right now, you know, Cephus has definitely been one of the slower starters in this game. >> Yeah, and if you don't think that's true, go listen to Dan Campbell talk about Cephus a couple days ago. He made it pretty clear that he's working through some things. He compared it to a a golfer trying to fix his swing and then overcorrecting in one area and ending up a little bit confused as to how to get himself back on track. And he said, you know, he he will, but there are kinks that he's working out. And when we talked to Tesla, I think this spring and asked him where he wanted to develop his game most in the off season, the two areas that he pointed to were short area quickness and releases. And that's good because that is where he needs to grow. We just haven't seen that growth happen yet in camp. Obviously, the size is there, the length is there, the straight line speed is there, but when it comes to, you know, shedding a defensive back off the line with those two things, releases and short area quickness, um you know, I'm sure Tesla will be the first to tell you that that hasn't been up to his liking, hasn't been consistent enough at all. And that is how Tesla can unlock the next level to his game. That's That's how he goes from just a red zone threat, just a deep threat to a more comprehensive receiver. And so, I think that that's a that's something to watch closely here over the next few weeks especially. And those one-on-one drills they have throughout at camp, and everyone likes to watch the receivers against the DBs one-on-one, you know, that's that's one That could be a a a telling area of Tesla's game, just watching him try and win those releases and and and how he kind of works that that short area quickness. >> And I'm going to be really quick with this point, but I it's it's worth reminder that development is not the same for everybody. And it's not linear. And for all the talk of year one to year two, sometimes it's year two to year three. And if you want an example on this roster, Derek Barnes. Right? Like sometimes it just takes a little bit longer for it to click. And I'm not saying that it won't click for Tesla by the end of camp or at some point this season, but if it doesn't, it doesn't mean you throw the guy in the trash. Like it the talent is immense. >> Yeah, and like Justin, not only did he play mostly slot receiver at Arkansas, he barely played much receiver at all in college before that. Like, this is still a player that is sorting through and and and perfecting honing the the finer points of playing wide receiver. So, um it is far far too early to be fretting about the slot
