title: ‘Starts and Finishes with the Offensive Line’: Lincoln Kennedy on Training Camp and Preseason
text: Hey, welcome to another edition a training camp edition of a pawn for the review brought to you by Coors Light. I'm your host Paul Gutierrez and I am joined honored to be joined by my co-author. We helped each other out on this situation here. Right here, right here Link. >> It's a beautiful book. I think >> Find it at any of your local bookstores or on Amazon or at triumphpublishing.com. And that's kind of what I want to talk to you a little bit about today Link is the stories that you told in this in this it's it's a it's a page-turner. It makes you want to talk about things that happen in training camp and we're starting to get into those dog days a little bit now. Not to jump too much forward here, but for you, what were some of the things that kept you going as you got to those dog days of training camp? >> Looking forward to the end. >> Yeah. I mean, look when I when I first started it was a little different back then because I had taken that tenacity that would be football for 6 months on and then football off. Not realizing that the game was starting to evolve to a year-round game. >> Right. >> And more importantly, I thought that training camp was a time that you got in shape. These days, if you're not in shape when you go to training camp, you're behind. >> You're behind everyone else. So, these are instances where you had to just, you know, understand the timing of when it happened, but training camp was that necessary evil no one enjoyed. >> Especially offensive line. You know, we're going to put on the pads a couple times a day, we're going to hit and stuff like that, but you had to get through it. You were you're going through everything that you need to go through just in hopes that you can make the team, whereas there were other guys who were trying to get a job. You know, I felt a little bit comfortable in my position what I had, but I was always looking over my shoulder cuz you know, there's somebody could come through and do it half as good as you cheaper. >> Cheaper. >> You'd probably be be replaced, but you know, your affiliation with the organization, your your understanding of the game, you know, literally, you think about this Paul, you can replace the entire NFL every year with the amount of guys that can be drafted. >> True. >> But you cannot put a price or an emphasis on experience. >> And that's the thing that's the thing that sets us apart. >> And that's coming from a first team all-pro right tackle, Lincoln Kennedy. Uh Link, and and when you see when you come to camp and you watch a practice and you see what these guys are doing right now. This what we just witnessed was practice number 10. >> Um no fans out there, right? Very little music, business as usual under new coach Clint Kubiak. What were some of your knee-jerk reactions to what you saw going on out there? >> Well, first of all, I said I wish they were hitting more. >> Yeah. >> I I wish they were getting physical more because it it's one as you ramp up to your first game, albeit preseason, you want to know that you have that physical tenacity built in. And you know, much to everything that I've seen in practices over the last couple years, you know 98's all over the place. The condor is swimming all over the place. So, you already know that's going to happen, but it and because there is so much going into this offensive line for me coming into the season, I watch the big boys up front. I watch if they can come together. I watch if they can be reliable on stuff like that. And we just saw a little glimpse of it. Today was my actual first practice watching start to finish, watching the flow. I thought they had a good tempo. I thought they had a good, you know, flow to them throughout the practice, but at the same point, I just don't think they're hitting enough. But that's I'm old school. >> How fine is that line between working on your own stuff, but also doing the team things to make the team better? >> Well, I I think that it it it goes back for me to communication. >> Mhm. >> So, I'm going to walk out to a defensive end and I'm going to say, "Hey, man, what what you trying to do today? We got pads. We got 907. We got 101. What are you trying to do?" "Hey, Link, I want to work on this arm over move. I want to work on it." "Okay, let's do it. You know, I'm I'm going to give you three hard steps. I'm going to allow you to get your stuff and get yourself ready. See what you can do." And I'm also going to show you as an offensive lineman what I would do to stop it. >> But it's all back to communicating. >> Factor in when you were playing. What were some of those battles that you played in that would be acceptable for of a family audience, I guess? >> [laughter] >> Well, I mean, I >> those battles, you know. >> You I I played against a lot of young guys that are trying to prove themselves, get themselves on film. And I would say it it's depends on how you want to do this. You know, as we can brother-in-law it throughout the practice and get through this practice, but if you want to shine, you >> there's something you want to work on. Okay, just let me know. So, if I line up in one-on-one and you're I know you're coming full bore, I'm going to pull every trick I have. >> Everything is legal. I've got a referee watching, he's not going to throw a flag, I promise you that. So, everything that's between that is legal play between the play, I'm going to show you because as a tackle, I'm going to show you what you're probably going up against in the league. >> Conversely, as a defensive end, you wiry, strong, well-strung, just you you you're wired like that, you're going to run outside to try to avoid me, I want to block that. I want to learn how to defend against that cuz I got to stay between you and the ball carrier. So, it's Again, it's but it's back to communication. >> If I had one guy that was trying to make me look bad, the first thing I would do would send a warning shot and then walk back to huddle, don't do that stuff again. >> That that type of thing. Hey, big man, you don't have to do it Bro, I told you, don't make me look bad. >> you. >> So, and that's that's the old school part of it. >> And when you look out here and and what Fernando Mendoza said in this meeting, he told me they're not the quarterback in the quarterback room themselves. >> They are not competing against each other, they're competing with each other. >> There's a very fine distinction there, right? But when you're going up against other guys and you're an old school guy and what were some of those old school battles like because the Raiders are getting ready to play their their exhibition opener. >> They're getting ready to go to Houston and have some uh joint practices. And uh you know, certain things happen in those joint practices. What were some of the the things the the better memories, the funnier memories of you when you would have those types of >> The first thing we all announce is that we're not punks. Don't allow anybody to punk you. Don't allow anybody to come off and take a cheap shot at you, you retaliate. And we know we had a we had a theory when when when Coach Bugel was around and may he rest in heaven, he's like, one of us fights, we all fight. >> Hm. >> So, there were times where we would have joint team practices where guys like, look, I'm going to fight next play, I'm tired. >> And he wanted to get out of it and you know he was going to be part of it, but it you always had to be if one person fought, you all fought. So, you were all there. And even if you had and I told you the story about Eric Williams and I may he rest in heaven, too, you know, what and in a case where we were we were fighting but we weren't fighting. We were just making it look good. Anybody seen it cuz the last thing you want and I had a coach who was like this. Turn on the film when they were filming the fight. Why aren't you in there? Why aren't you get Hey, hey, you don't want to do that. So, it it's supposed to be physical. We're talking about a a physical game. It's a game, but it's still physical. And when you get away from the physical nature, then that's when you start to see, in my opinion, offensive lineman that can't get in a three-point stance, can't fire up. Or you're on shotgun on the five-yard line. These are disgraces to me in the current game. I get it. I don't like it. So, you know, much quarterbacks are a little different brand though. Than any other position play. Quarterbacks are a little different brand because whether you're a defensive back that just got drafted and a and a slew of three, four defensive backs that got drafted or a team that's really starving for defense control and you're under a new system, you're going to there's going to be a little bit of a setback. You know, have a little bit of a progression. Um whereas you're an offensive lineman trying to come together, you've had many coaches over the last couple years, but you're trying to play consistently. First of all, you have to have somebody above your pay grade that decide who's going to be the five best guys out there. Two, you got to learn how to play together. You can't mix-match parts. So, there has to be level consistency. And that's where you would hope the guys that are really physical, the captains will stand up. You know, as I've said in the past when it comes to like JPJ, I think he's the most tenacious offensive lineman we have. Reminds me a little bit of Richie Incognito and see what he's doing and all those guys and all those guys back. What you need. I call them all in the middle. But you can't be against the team in the sense where you can't do stupid things. You can't have penalties, can't have miscues, can't be available. Need to be there. And I need to see that. And if you're going to be that guy that's going to get in everybody's face, you're going to be that one that spearheads the fight between us and the defensive lineman, so be it. I'm right there with you. Or if I'm there, I need you right there with me. But we haven't seen that sort of take off, sort of to control. I love Cole Miller. Cold Miller, don't get me wrong. There are some guys where you're waiting to see their growth and how they mature in that position, but the first thing is that we always said we don't take crap from nobody. >> That's what I was going to ask you for like your scouting report so far on what what you've seen. I know you only saw the one practice and and they were padded, but what what is your interpretation of what they want to do? Especially with with the new offensive line coach Rick Dennison and and the things and and what type of you know what type of scheme and it almost seems like this back in the day we'd always talk about well, is it a zone scheme is it a power scheme or a power zone? Now I remember last year talking with you and you you were seeing different elements throughout >> Throughout the Yeah, exactly. >> the game. >> I I still think you see splashes cuz you got to kind of have to test the water. >> Okay. >> I don't think they have Here here here's the way I would approach it. If I'm Kliff Kingsbury I'm coming in in my first year head coaching, that means I control the show. I don't have to have one way that's that's stellar. >> About the wide zone concept, the man concept, however you want to break it down. >> But you know what you're familiar with and that's what you try to teach. However, you got to have the bodies in order to make that work. >> A lot of times this is still an evaluation period. Once you get the pads on, you get a true definition of somebody's tenacity, somebody's physical ability to play this physical game. You don't know that and I've always said you don't know how good you are until you play against someone else. >> So, you know, in the Hall of Fame game that that we saw last week, I saw two very vanilla defenses. >> Very vanilla, just basics going through it. Made the offense looks like gangbusters. Cuz they were that much for it. But also I saw, you know, I saw a mirror image as far as offenses what I would see with San Francisco, the Rams, and Green Bay with those offenses and you see how effective they can be. If I'm Kliff Kingsbury I'm salivating cuz I oh, I've got some ideas. I got some things to do. Just have to have the men to implement it. Just and like you said, it you can have all the styles you want, but you have to have the pieces, the personnel to fit that. too. >> Absolutely. >> Uh lastly with you, when it comes to training camp, when it comes to what this team is going to do, how what's a realistic expectation for this team going forward? And Richie Incognito sat there last week and it was like, "Look, games are won and lost with the offensive line." >> Right. Right. >> And I got another offensive lineman sitting here right here and then I'm not I'm not have to convince you of that. What's a realistic expectation and really does it all kind of start and finish with that offensive line going >> Oh, it always starts and finishes with the offensive line because uh you know, there's there's a saying a running game is a quarterback's best friend. >> How do you get a running game started with the offensive line? Yes, that's the way you have it's also timing, it's also execution. When it comes to all the pieces that being what and you look at Seattle's team last year as they won a Super Bowl and what was remember memorable for me in watching them throughout the season is that their wide receivers have blocked. >> I've been on teams where wide receivers don't block. >> Or or you know, just just incapable. They're just not you know, but you have to be able to do that and especially with a wide zone concept because you're stretching you're stretching that line of scrimmage out so wide. You got to have people that are on perimeter that can block. So, yes, it starts and finishes with the offensive line. But to answer your your question, P.G., for me, I I would like to see this team competitive. >> Um and and I I can't necessarily because there's still so much I have to gather and watch and learn and how they play and especially the first month of football I think determines the identity of this team. >> Sure. >> I want them to be competitive, but my dream is if they can go and I know this is not a big deal for a lot of people because a lot of people want more. But I'm hoping that they if they can split the division games. That shows me progress. >> That would be huge progress considering >> Especially this division. >> Yeah, in this division last year they won one game and the year before they were winless in the division. So, yeah, that that that would be huge. >> Yeah. There are so many different intangibles that makes a team. My goal is I just want to see them competitive. >> Got you. Yeah, and I'm sure that's really the the ultimate goal you to to win, but you got to take those baby steps first and keep going. Lincoln, appreciate you stopping by. >> Love you, brother. >> Uh I saw you earlier today wearing your Eric Turner T-shirt and it just got me thinking about uh E >> Well, we're going to training camp, so I'm wearing my training camp gear, you know what I mean? I remember ET, may he rest in heaven, great guy. Gone too far, too soon, but you know, when I come to places during this time of year, when I when I come here, and I see it, it's different, obviously, than than I had back in Oakland and Napa and everything else, it's different. We all want to get better as a team. But, just I was ready to mess somebody up. >> And we want to get better at the podcast, too. Um so I think that could be said about a lot of the rookies that you know there's just a special bond. and they stay here longer in the offseason than the veterans do. Um, so those guys get really close and you know, uh, we have a big rookie group that we need them to we need them to gel with each other and get close and that's going to, you know, it's going to pay dividends on the field. >> What stands out to you about Mendoza's preparation? Coach Solo was talking about his note takingaking and his note-taking ability and like detailing each pass play during OTA. Just what do you like about his preparation? Yeah, that that position is that's the expectation is to be the most prepared guy in the building. Um, but you say that, but not everybody really acts that way. There's a different levels of of preparation and and I would say that u you know, I'd say the guy the young quarterbacks that I've been around, I think he has the upper upper hand on them in that in that area. Now he has to go do it in a live game. >> You talk about appreciating the moment and I'm just curious. It's been your dream for so long to be a head coach. Have you stopped at any point and just taken a moment and en thought about your first camp and enjoying and appreciating the moment? Um, I think the thing that I appreciate most is the coaches I get to work with because it is a group effort and um, you know, we work we work a lot of long hours together, but we have a lot of coaches that um, that are head coaches of their position and I rely on them to be the best at what they do and allows me to focus on my strengths and delegate the things that I'm not as good at. So, I'm grateful that uh, you know, that John and Mr. Davis allowed me to hire those guys so that we can get up and running faster. >> Following that, Thursday, um, running the team and calling plays at the same time. How do you anticipate approaching that for the first time? >> Yeah, I think it'll be baptism by fire. You know, I'll I'll be finding out pretty quick what it's all about here on Thursday. Again, I'm not doing it alone. Never called a game by myself. We do it with the whole offensive staff. Uh, relying on the defensive staff, on coach Jod Camilis, on special teams. Uh it is every NFL game takes uh takes the whole staff and and all the players. So we'll not be will not be uh on my own, but I'll definitely have a lot to learn real fast. >> Every coach and player that we've spoken to at this point have all echoed the same message. There's no I team. It's we. Everybody's really bought into what you've tried to establish here as an early culture setter. What does that mean to you being a first year head coach that this early on everybody is brought in? >> Yeah. Well, I think I would say compliment our players is that it's not so much about listening to me, it's about what it takes to win. We want to win. Our players want to win. And uh you know, the things that it takes to win is for us to be together and be connected and and operate as one unit. So, I think it just shows the maturity of our group knowing um you know, we're going to point things out, but at the end of the day, uh they decide what kind of team that they want to be. And you know, thus far they've showed us they're a mature group that you know, they want to go win games the right way. >> Clint, there for young coaches, there's so much learning [clears throat] about the head coaching, whether it's when to throw the red flag, hearing from upstairs. How much of that do you game plan with Mike with just in learning and how much can a practice like this and the preseason help prepare you for that? >> Be very important. uh Mike McCoy, you know, Ro hit, Joe D. Camilllas. Um you know, we're all we spent a lot of time together, our coordinators talking through situations and how things are going to play out and the mechanics of of all those things that you discussed. And you know, you can't uh you can't duplicate the game. You need to go do it in the preseason. And we got to go uh make sure our communication is very crisp and we're on point and ready for situations before they occur. That's what the offseason's about and we spend a lot of time with that. So, uh, you know, we're going to get put to the test on Thursday, so we got to go do our jobs. >> Let's wrap it up with Sam and then Vince. >> Will there uh will there be any limitations on Dramad um when he goes out on the field on Thursday? >> Yeah, I think you know, Dramad is he's he's been practicing almost every day we've been out there. So, we expect him to play. We expect him to compete and look forward to watching him play. And >> he he said that when he gets out on the field, it's going to be an emotional moment for him to to get out on the field after, you know, such a long time off. How do you manage that for a player who's kind of going through those emotions? >> Yeah. Well, I think uh I think it's all about how we practice. You know, we're not going to ask him to do anything in the game he hasn't done in practice. Um I'm really uh really excited for him. You know, he's worked his tail off to get to this moment. And I just, you know, want him to go be himself, go be the best version of himself on Thursday night. >> You guys talked about this week how they felt like there's gonna be a little extra feeling even though it is practice tonight. Do you want them to have that extra juice or do you not want them to make it too big of what it may be just being inside the stadium? >> Um, you know, I guess it's professional football, so like every practice and every, you know, every preseason game and every stadium practice, they should all feel really big. You know, it's this is these guys' jobs. This is our jobs as coaches. And, uh, you should have those butterfly fly feelings. And if you don't, sometimes to me it means you're not ready. if it's if you're not nervous about it, if you don't have a little anxiety, it probably doesn't mean as much to you. So, I think that's a good thing to have those feelings. >> Thank you, coach. >> Thanks. >> Thanks a lot, Clint. >> A lot of players and coaches talk about Clint Kubak's attention to detail. What What is that like? Is it more he's just very specific in terms of the routes and the plays? Just what when people say attention to detail, what does that look like? >> Yeah. So like um you know if our route if it's at 12 yards, you know, he wants it at 12 yards, he don't want anything, you know, cut short or anything too deep. And I feel like when you have a a head coach that is focused on little things is going to make the program and just it makes everybody just want to be, you know, really good. >> Are you able to appreciate how well you're playing right now or are you just so in the moment and focused you're not thinking about it? >> Uh yeah, I'm, you know, I'm not really too much, you know, think about. I just know like my hard work and my prepar preparation, you know, is is leading me to be able to come out and perform at practice. You know, just the help with the older guys just helped me, you know, be able to line up fast and to learn the playbooks. I feel like, you know, when they welcome me with open open arms, it made it easy for me just to sit down and learn the playbook and be able to play fast because, you know, I was able to, you know, gain gain their trust really >> With you and Fernando coming in together as rookies, how important is that that you guys are able to spend so much time together so early and develop that chemistry? Well, you know, I'm nothing without my quarterback. So, you know, obviously in college we battled out, but you know, we put all that aside. And, you know, when I first met him, we first met each other. You know, I met him at the combine. It just felt like there was just uh it feel like we were just like best friends from that moment. And then obviously, you know, I got drafted and he got drafted here. So he called me and you know I told him that you know whatever he needs if we got to watch more film if you need more you know if you need me to catch more just little things like that cuz I know like when it comes to Sundays when it comes to practice like you know he's going to rely on me to be in that spot and I'm rely I'm going rely on him to you know place the ball where it needs to be placed. >> You've also gotten a lot of reps of the ones. How valuable has that been especially working with Kirk? Uh honestly just for my confidence I feel like it is been really good for me just to you know show myself that you know I can do it but you know I'm I'm really glad that you know the coaches and my teammates you know they're giving me opportunity and they're trust me and I'm able to show you know that I can be trusted. >> Have you felt the buzz that is kind of building about you that the the excitement that the fans have about what you could be? I mean have you kind of been able to feel that while you're in camp? >> Uh I really don't pay too much attention to that. I just try to you know focus on my job and you know let everything else you know come with it. you you were making plays dating all the way back to to May or whenever you guys were here for rookie mini camp through through mini camp. Uh then you had six weeks off. How did you maintain that and put yourself in a good position to build on that and be at the position you're at now? >> Yeah, really just knowing that you know rookie mini camp that's one phase and then coming to OTAAS that's another phase. So, you know, just had to keep turning it up a notch and, you know, just staying in my playbook, you know, calling my coaches, calling my teammates, asking them any questions I have cuz I know that they're willing to help me and just really just trying to be, you know, just a complete receiver and just to come in and just really just be myself. >> You talked you talked Fernando up a lot about uh, you know, you guys' relationship and how smart he is. What What about him as a quarterback? What's impressed you the most about his? >> So, he's my first quarterback that, you know, if I've done something wrong, like he'll come up to me, he'll be like, "Hey, like you tripping. I need you to do And I feel like just that accountability to him being able to, you know, do that and he, you know, sees that he can get on me and I can get on him. I feel like that just makes our relationship even more better. >> Does he say that like you tripping in Malik? >> Yeah. Yeah. >> When you were coming out the draft, one of the concerns scouts had was physicality, but we watch you in special teams. We watch you, you know, downfield blocking. There is zero in that. Is that maybe a place of pride for you that you're more physical than people thought and you set out to prove that? >> Yeah. So, going through the that whole process, you know, that was what I was hearing a lot. So, I knew that no matter when I was going to get picked up, you know, I was going to get an opportunity to show, you know, what I can do and, you know, I got picked up by a great organization. So, you know, each and every day I just come with that chip on my shoulder to show everybody like if you think I'm soft, then you don't have to come out here and find out. on the back end of that sorry on the back end of that question with the physicality you know you were obviously a big speed guy and a lot of people probably thought that it was just kind of like only speed to your element but how much have you put forth into making sure that the route running and the releases are also you know equally combined with the speed and who are some people around the building that's helped you along with that as well >> yeah so just knowing that the NFL is you know it's another level up like the separation is going to be the biggest thing so obviously you know I'm a blazer and things like that but you know I can't just be a onetrick pony me. So really just in the offseason just perfecting my craft on, you know, getting out of my breaks, you know, I feel like that's that's really helped me a lot. But guys like, you know, Trey and Jaylen, you know, I've really leaned on them just because they've done it before. They've been the systems and, you know, I see their work that they do each and every day and, you know, they just impress me with how they come in the building. You know, they don't complain and, you know, they're just, you know, bought into, you know, the goals of the team and, you know, I just try to be, you know, just like them guys. >> Are there any receivers that you modeled your game after? Yeah. So, uh, you know, I like to watch like JSN. I like to watch Justin Jefferson, Jamar Chase, things like that. >> You and Hezekiah have built a really good relationship and he, like you, is shining in this camp. Would you talk about that relationship with him and what you see watching him? >> Yeah. So, uh, bring it all the way back to training for the, uh, combine, everything, you know, we trained at the same spot. So, you know, we built a good relationship there and then obviously once, you know, we both got picked up, you know, we called each other. super excited. And then, you know, also right now he's he's my locker mate. So, you know, I just told him straight up from day one like I'm going against you. Like, we could be buddy buddy in the facility, but we on the field like I don't really know who you are. Like, you know, I need your best, he needs my best. And, you know, just he gives me, you know, a lot of great looks. You know, I love going against him just because I know that when I step out there, you know, he's going to bring his all. And, you know, when you got two young guys that's, you know, trying to battle it out, that's just that's all you can ask for. Just great competition. where you expect tonight to be with practice at Allegent and how do you think that's going to help >> Could you repeat that? >> How different do you expect practice to be to feel tonight and how do you think that's going to help Thursday? >> Uh, you know, honestly, I feel like it's still going to be practice at the end of the day. You know, it's just in a different location. But, uh, I feel like it's going to help a lot on Thursday. You know, just getting used to the lights and everything like that. You know, I'm obviously going to have a wow moment just because I've never been in that stadium with a helmet on. But, you know, I'm just going to have to snap out of it and just know that, you know, we're here to practice. We're here to win the game on Thursday. >> Malik, you're just hours away from your first open practice at Allegiance Stadium. Can you talk to me about your emotions and your feelings coming from Austin Stadium to Allegant? >> Yeah. So, uh, you know, one thing, uh, you know, when I was at Alabama with Coach Saving, one thing he told me, he was like, you know, whether it's game or practice, you know, you just got to take it one day at a time and, you know, just don't let the moment get too big. So man, just going to go in there and just be grateful for my opportunity and just know that at the end of the day, you know, it's just practice, just a game. And, you know, don't let, you know, if good things happen, you know, next play, if something bad happens next play, just know that at the end of the day, like I'm blessed for this opportunity. >> You said similar things about both Mendoza and Masses that you kind of built a relationship through the draft process. So then when you're drafted by the Raiders, that give you some some comfort or ease your nerves a little bit already having a relationship with some guys in your class. Yeah, it made it uh so much easier, you know, coming in with guys that I've already, you know, already knew and talked to. So then when I get into the locker room, you know, we could just be smile. Everybody could be theirel. Not everybody's, you know, just all tight and you know, not trying to, you know, get to know the next person. But I feel like just as a whole rookie class, we've all done a good job of hanging out outside the facility and, you know, just getting to know each other outside of ball. >> Just being a six round draft pick, do you take motivation from that? >> Yeah, for sure. But honestly, you know, I feel like I've always kind of been at the bottom. Like, you know, I started junior college and things like that. So, you know, it's just a another stepping stone that, you know, God's, you know, showing me that, you know, yeah, you're sixth round, but if you just come out here and, you know, work hard and do what you got to do, you know, none of that really matters once you get drafted. >> All good, guys. >> Appreciate it. >> What's What's it been like acclimating to to the NFL? What's what's come easy for you? What are you learning? >> It's been great. Um been acclimating to, you know, the playbook. It's kind of a um you know, hard playbook, but you know, I was in, you know, Patrino's offense back in Arkansas, so um I was kind of able to pick started off slow, but been able to pick it up. Well, >> Mike, to have your combination of power and speed is very rare, and we've seen it a little bit. You can't when you blow the shoulder a little bit. How much are you looking forward to going against guys in a different color jersey where you can truly show off your physicality? >> Uh really looking forward to it. Um it's been, you know, some time since, you know, I put on the pads and went against, you know, another team. Last game, you know, I really played was last game of the Arkansas season. So, and that was, you know, some some time ago. So, really looking forward to it. >> What have you learned working with Ashton Jensen so closely? >> Well, one, he's a great mentor. Um, you know, I come off the sideline to him every time I, you know, have a run or a pass play. And, uh, you know, he coaches me up. Same thing with, you know, Dylan Lob and, you know, the other running backs. Um, they they're all great mentors towards me. >> What is the benefit of having a coach like Clint Kubak who's very like very focused on the details and, you know, being very intent on on that in that area? >> Um, well, it makes our room a better room. Um, like you said, he's very detail oriented. though, you know, he doesn't want us running a route how we run it, but how he wants it. Um, because everything is scheme based and concept based. So, um, it makes our our room, you know, a detailed room. >> What's it been like working in this run scheme, this Clint Kubak run scheme and kind of what are the big principles of you, you know, as a running back, what you're trying to do for the for the rushing attack? >> Um, really just being physical and, you know, coming in and running with that mindset. Um, when you run with a physical mindset, nobody, you know, really wants to tackle you. Um, especially, you know, being a bigger back. Um, you know, nobody really wants that deal with that physicality. So, yeah. >> Tony, you work inside Allegiance Stadium. How different do you expect that feeling to be and how do you think that's going to help for Thursday? >> Um, well, it's going to be an exciting moment, I believe, for everybody. It's our first preseason game, first game we get to, you know, show the world what we're capable of. Um, so I believe it's going to be exciting. >> Going back to, you know, you talked about running physically. How would you describe your your running style when you're in a groove carrying the ball? How would you describe that? >> Uh, downhill downhill runner. Um, punishing back, you know, able to run you over, able to, you know, make you miss and then, you know, once get to the second level, hard to catch. >> Something that's noticeable within this offense is how much the running backs also play in the pass game with a lot of screens and a lot of things like that. You know, how comfortable are you with that? Is that something that you still feel like you're getting better at or you think that that's a benefit to your game that you already came with? >> Definitely a benefit and definitely something that I'm still getting better at. Um, being in Patrino's offense back in Arkansas, he kind of put me, you know, everywhere. Um, and then coming here, it's kind of the same thing where like you said before, coach is very detail oriented. So, um, he wants he wants the best for us and he wants to puts us in he wants to put, you know, the running back room, all the running backs in different positions. So, whether it's in a slot or having us out wide, um, yeah, he puts us everywhere. >> Young running backs say, you know, the playmaking still comes naturally, but the hardest thing about adjusting the NFL is that the pass protection and some of the uh, lips pickups and things like that. How how's that been coming along for you? >> Really just been watching film, honestly. meeting with my running back coach, um talking to, you know, Genty and uh Dylan Lob. You know, like I said, they've been great mentors um with me with the with the pass protection and understanding the game cuz um you know, it is different compared to how it was, you know, coming out of college. All right. >> Thanks, Mike. Thank you.

text: get all the deserves. Ian Thomas is a guy coming into this camp, we knew what he did in special things. We knew how he blocked, but it seems to be really emerging as a passing threat. Am I seeing him right? >> Yeah. I mean, Ian's a guy we're going to count on this year. We needed him to do everything. So, um I know he's been kind of labeled in his career as a blocking tight end, but I think he's got a really proficient skill set as a pass catcher. Um, you know, there's a lot of lot of uh a lot of great skilled players on our offense and there's only one ball to go around, but but when the ball goes his way, we we plan on him uh catching it, making plays with it. >> Where do you think how do you how do you think this scheme Kubak likes to run best uses the tight end skill sets? >> You know, it's a very versatile scheme. I I love being in this scheme. I've coached in versions of this offense in the past. Uh I think our group in the tight end room really loves it. Um but for us, you know, it's just going out and getting better every single day. It's it's mastering this scheme. Uh we still got a long way to go before we play our first regular season game and um we're kind of exploring every angle of the versatility this offense provides and uh you know as the tight end's coach I'm really excited for for what it looks like for our group. >> Yeah. How how fun is it for you as a tight end's coach to be coaching in this scheme and coaching your guys? >> Yeah, I mean you know it's uh it's a lot of fun. It's a lot of fun. We we got a great team. We got a great staff. You know we're building that chemistry within the offense and as a team as a whole. And um you know, whether we ask the the tight ends to to catch 20 balls a game or catch zero and block their tails off in the run game, that's that's what we're going to do. We got a team first approach and whatever the game plan tells us to do that week, that's what we're going to do. And uh it's all about finding a way to win and and doing what's best for the team. >> Brock and Michael Mayer have such seems complimentary skill sets. How much do they make each other better? And what kind of that difficult is it for >> Yeah, it's it's it's a great tandem to have on the field, right? Two great players. Um, you know, I use this word a lot, but they're both versatile. I I don't think Mike gets enough credit as a receiver and I don't think Brock gets enough credit as a blocker. Um, so we can really move them around in a lot of different ways and uh attack defenses in different ways. uh you know, we're going to see multiple defenses to them because when we go out there uh and 12 personnel or 13 for that matter and we got Brock and Tai uh Brock and Mike and Ian and uh whoever might be Albert O out there um you know they they all got to play off each other and and those relationships start off the field and hopefully they translate when we get on the grass. >> What have you seen from Michael in particular? I mean he looks like he's in a really good place outside of busting his nose, but he still was back out here. >> Yeah, he's not the prettiest looking guy anymore but uh but he's had a great camp. Um, can't say enough good things about Michael Mayer. So blessed. I've had the opportunity to coach him for three years now. Um, just an unbelievable football player, unbelievable person. And, uh, you know, I think he's had the best training camp I've seen him have in my short time with him. Um, but I'm really excited to see what he does this year for himself and for this team. >> What is he and Thomas bring to your group? >> Yeah, just uh, you know, kind of a Swiss Army knife for us. Um, you know, he he's going to have to play a big role in the run game and pass protection and he's going to have to be a viable receiver for us. He's done a lot of that out here. Caught a lot of balls throughout camp. So, um, like I keep telling, when the ball comes his way, uh, we got to catch it and we got to make plays with it. >> Just brought up Chris Mig a couple days ago. What have you seen on the move so far? >> Yeah, big fan of Chris. You know, he's had to hit the ground running. He came in, you know, when the majority of our installs had already been put in, and that's obviously a tough situation for any player, but he's a veteran. He's been in this league. He's been on a few teams and played in a lot of different offenses and and he's been like a sponge ever since he got here. So really admire the effort he's put in to learn this offense and excited to see what he does on uh Thursday night. >> There's been a lot of changes with the organization with coaching staff, players, even for an office. But you, Brock, Mike, it's like you guys keep on coming back. How important is that continuity for you and the position? >> You know, it's it's a blessing. It's a blessing. U you know, coaches are just a reflection of our players. So uh when your players play well, you might have an opportunity to hang on. I've been so blessed to be a part of this franchise for three years. This is a special place. I've been able to work for four different teams in this league and there's just something different about wearing the silver and black. Um we're building something special. There's a foundation here. There's a history. There's a legacy and I'm excited to see what this chapter of that legacy looks like. I'm so grateful to be a part of >> What is it that makes it feel different? >> You know, uh it it's every year, you know, every year is going to feel different and obviously when there's change at the top, um there's going to be uh different things in the way we do things starting from the schedule to the offensive scheme, defensive scheme. Um, but you know, everyone around the league is optimistic at this point and and we're no different. Uh, we got a high standard and high expectations for our group and it's all about the team. It's all about the team. We're trying to get better every single day. Whatever that means for me, whatever that means for our tight ends, whatever that means for every player and coach in the locker room. Um, this is a team first approach and um, and that's the culture coach Kubiaak has set and I think everyone's falling in line pretty quickly. >> With that being said, it seems like coach Kubiaak's not a first year head coach. It seems like everything he's doing, it looks like it has a purpose to it. Yeah, he's uh he in my opinion, he's been qualified for this job for for a long time now. Uh you'd fool me by telling me he's a first year head coach. Um I know myself personally have already learned a tremendous amount for him. I think the players are responding to him. Like I said, uh he's the captain of this ship. He sets the tone for the culture of this building and um he's done a fantastic job so far. >> Hugh says that Brock's always open. He is. >> Uh obviously the skill set to do that, but what about the mental part that helps him with that? Uh, you know, Brock is highly highly intelligent. Uh, highly intelligent football player. He's such a natural player, instinctive player. Um, you know, some people were born to play football, and I think he was one of them. I think he could put a blindfold on them, and he'd find a way to get open. He just has such a great feel for space out there versus own coverage. He's got great uh great release plans versus manto man when they want to come down and press him. Um, but it all starts with the mental aspect like you're alluding to. He's an extremely smart player, but he also puts in the work. He studies uh all night, all morning. He never steps on this on the field with with a question. He he's got all his questions answered because he puts in the work, but he's a really intelligent person. So smart people that study end up doing pretty well and and he's no different. >> You say the overall attitude. >> Yeah. You know what? Uh I tell the guys all the time, we're we're going to lead from the front. You know, you can't call yourself a leader and be at the back of the line. So, we're trying to set the standard for this offense, um for this team. You know, that's the expectation. Uh, I try to hold them too and and I try to have them hold me too. You know, we're all a group. We're all in this together. It's about we and us, not I. There's no egos in this room. U, you hear our players say all the time, we don't care how many balls we catch, how many touchdowns we score. It's whatever we can do to help the team win. And that's going to be our attitude. And that's going to look different every single week. Some weeks it is catching balls and scoring touchdowns, and sometimes it's blocking your tail off in the run game and pass protection. Um, but we have a lot of humble guys in the room that are going to lead from the front and do what's asked of them and and hopefully it leads to wins. >> Would you say that Brock served as a leader this season? >> He really has. You know, everyone's got their leadership style, but I've really seen him blossom in that regard in this third year. Um, another thing we talk about is just being the best teammates on the team. His teammates love him in the locker room. Um, you know, he leads by example. His work ethic out here is is unmatched. One of the hardest players I've hardest working players I've ever been around. and uh it's really been cool to see him take more steps in that uh that area and I'm excited to see what he does from a leadership standpoint all season. >> So awesome. >> Thank you guys. Appreciate it. >> From a health standpoint, where are you right now? >> I'm feeling good. Yeah, glad to be back on the field. >> You look incredibly smooth. Just flexibility, hips, everything. Are you like pushing them a little bit? Come on, let's up my work a little here. Let's do a little bit more. >> Uh yeah, cuz I mean I I was on a little uh like I had a little limit or whatever, but like I've been able to exceed that. So I mean it's been going real good for me. >> How would you describe? >> Yeah, I think it's been a great process with them. uh like from the day I came in to now like it's just the way I feel is just so much better cuz like I I mean you know AG all the guys in there I feel like they just really uh kind of been pouring into me. I mean it's they done got me right. >> Can it be can it be tough sometimes trying to like buy into certain parts cuz you know you miss a lot of times during OTAAS and mentoring you know as a football player even be out there just like prove yourself. Can it be tough sometime when they say hey we need you to sit back for a day or sit back for this long period of time? Yeah, it can be tough, but I mean it's just part of >> Where are some guys that you've leaned on in that quarterback room or that safety room that's really been able to help you through this process of adjusting? >> Yeah, I say guys like Stokes. Uh I mean Stokes, Chin, Z, all those older vet guys. I mean, I ask them a lot of questions. Just trying to learn more about the game. You know, it's a way different from college. So, just trying to get myself to where where they at. >> I notic that you talk to Stokes a lot on the sideline and kind of, you know, go over technique and stuff like that. What's do you think is the biggest thing that you've learned from him so far? I'll say the technique part. Uh, and then just my like our key pre- snap keys. Uh, just ideing things that we see. So, I mean, he's just he's helped me a lot with all that. >> Those camp battles been between you and now Malik Benson so far. >> You said what? >> Camp battles. >> Camp battles. Oh, it's been good. Me and Malik, man. Like, every time I'm up against Malik, like I love it cuz I mean, you know, that's uh they love throwing to Malik. So, I know like against Malik ball probably coming there. So, I'mma, you know, try to make a play or whatever. Did you ever have any doubt personally you'd be able to play this year? >> No, I don't I don't really I don't really doubt myself. I always try to if I put my mind to something, I feel like I can always do it. >> Well, I know we asked you around the draft, but like what was it like hearing so many people have so many opinions and you're kind of sitting there like I'm me. Everybody has opinions, don't even know me. >> Yeah. I mean, like it's just part of it. Uh just keeping a level head with it. Just kind of some sometimes you just got to tune the stuff out. when you haven't, you know, when you haven't played for for a certain period of time, kind of what's the biggest challenge in terms of getting yourself reaclimated? >> Yeah, I say just getting myself back in football shape for sure. Uh, you know, first day out there, you know, I was a little tired, but I could see myself uh progressing more and more daily with my uh stamina and all that and just getting back into football shape and just I just I say the pre- snap stuff and then tech technical things. So, just uh getting back into all that. Was there a certain point like a play or just a certain point within training camp that you can recall where you were just like, "Okay, now I can feel it. Like I'm back now." >> Yeah, I'll probably say like it was my second or third day. Uh like I made a few plays and uh I mean I felt real good and I was like, "Okay, it's ball again." >> Have you felt rusty at all? >> Like the first little days, you know, a little it's always going to be a little rust, but just knocking it off. Was there any part of you that kind of developed like a chip on your shoulder based off of what happened through the draft? And does that fuel you? >> Oh yeah, that's something that'll it'll build me forever. >> And what would like just >> I'm going just always remember it's going to keep f fueling me to push forward. >> What kind of goals did you set yourself as a rookie? >> Uh well as a rookie like I definitely want to be uh like all rookie. Uh just make that team uh all pro, like things like that for sure. And then I want to get like three, four picks. Uh, you know, I love getting that ball back. Um, but, uh, that's really Yeah. >> Do you believe you were the best one? >> Yeah, 100%. >> What appeals to you also besides being a quarterback, what appeals to you about returning punts? >> Uh, getting the ball in my hands. Uh, being able to score touchdowns cuz, you know, it's a, you know, it's not a super high chance on defense. So, anytime I get the ball in my hands, I mean, I love >> You talked about loving getting the ball back. It seems like they the Raiders picked up a lot of guys who have talent for doing that. Has that been a focal point of Rob Leonard and Joe Woods and what they're talking about with this defense? >> Oh yeah, we're always trying to get the ball back, make plays on the ball because like I mean we want the offense on the field as much as possible, them putting points on the board. So whatever we can do to get the ball back and help the team do that, that's what we going to do. >> How does this how does this scheme uh fits kind of like what you do best on the football field? >> Uh I mean it's I feel like it's very similar similar to what I was doing in college, you know? I mean, it's a lot of I get to press a lot, play a lot of man. Uh, I mean, it's some zones in there, too. So, I mean, it's real similar, so it's nothing I'm not not used to. >> And what's it been like going against uh, you know, Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza out there? >> Uh, it's been good. I mean, I like going against those guys. It's uh, just helping me. And then I feel like I'm also helping them, too. So, just uh, uh, iron, sharpening iron every day. >> Your your 2024 film is about as good as a college could have. How close do you feel you are to that player right now? Uh, I'm still I'm getting there. Like cuz like I said, it's been a long time since I done really played football. So, I mean, that's really what I I'm taking all this like trying to treat this getting myself back to where I was. And I mean, I feel like I'm I'm really like almost there. >> You feel like there's going to be any emotions for you when you get back out there on the field on Thursday in our game? >> Yeah, for sure. It's going to definitely be some emotions. >> Do you is there a way to like deal with that? Like, do you plan on just kind of like taking it in? Yeah, just look around, take it all in, and just remember like at any point like this game could be taken from you. So, just always cherish in these moments. >> That you guys are really close. What's it been like kind of going through this journey with him together? >> It's been real good. You know, me and Zeke, we talk a lot about stuff that we see. Uh, I mean, try to coach each other up on things. Like me and Zeke, I feel like we we're like real similar with our mindsets. We both want to be the best. So, I mean, I think that's like two rookies coming in doing that is just it's something like it's hard to find that for real. I think >> how how surreal is it for you that you know, you haven't played in a football game in in over a year and your first football game is in the NFL. So, how like what are your emotions like that you getting ready for for Thursday? >> Got to lock in. Got to be ready for it. >> Yeah. >> Thank you guys. Appreciate What have you uh liked so far about the way you've been playing? >> Um what I like so far about myself is just me just going out there just playing confidence. Just my team just pushing me every day and I'm just being the best version of myself. >> You're getting a lot of work here with the ones. Just what is it like being a part of a competition like? >> Yeah, man. Just being with the one truly just a blessing. I want to thank my Lord and Savior Jesus Christ and just my teammates just pushing me every day and just the coaches trusting me every day. >> How has this whole experience been for you now getting through training camp you guys are going to play in your first game preseason game this week? >> Yeah, I'm just super excited, man. It feels so unreal, man. My first preseason game, I'm just happy for the opportunity. I'm just ready to play for Thursday for the game. >> Competition is something that's preached with every position group. How do you guys as DBs whole push each other to be better? Oh man, every day even Walmart every day we pushing each other. We trying to like get like each each we trying to get each other better every day. So we just pushing each other every day. >> Last time we spoke with you compare you to Dent. How does it feel to get such praise from a man with you know watching you play every day? >> Yeah man. It's much praise man. That's my coach. So he see what I'm doing every day and I feel like it's a blessing for um him to say like compare me to a guy like that a great guy that been in the league for a long time. So I'm just being myself just taking it day by day. At what juncture did you start to feel comfortable being OTA as many came you start to feel comfortable out there running first >> man just it just in me I feel comfortable soon as I step soon I put the cleats on I feel comfortable so it's just in me so as soon as I'm out there I'm just trying to be myself >> you the biggest criticism in scouting on you was how is he going to play with the physicality in the NFL you have clearly sent the message that's not an issue with you how excited are you to play somebody in a different jersey to show it even more >> oh yeah I'm trying to take the head off yeah so yeah that was a big like issue. They said I can't tackle. So, I'm going to show them. I'm going to show them. I'm very physical. I can do everything. >> Do you feel like you're in that zone? I mean, every day, every day I write, I'm tired of writing about this guy because it seems like I'm his cheerleader, but every day you're making big plays. Do you feel like you're in that zone? >> Yeah, I'm in that zone. Yeah, I'm in that zone for sure. Just 100%. I'm just out there just making plays and just being myself. They calling on great um calls and I'm just out there executing. How does it feel to have such like um a fan base from you know the Golden Bears and a lot of your like family and friends just be cheering you on on social media? >> Yeah man that's much love I Golden Bear I love you know Cal they treat me well and like they they come along like the way so whatever I do like they right behind me. >> You and M two rookies in this class you're going against them every day. What is it like to not only have him in your rookie class but he's playing across me and he's playing well as >> Yes sir. No great guy, great receiver. He can do everything. So, it's just iron, sharp, and iron. And so, soon as I line up against him, like we know we going at it every day in practice. >> Jaylen and Trey had great things to say about you as well. What have you kind of been learning about them as they've kind of helped you as you try to get better? >> Yeah, man. Both of them guys, twitchy receivers, man. Them vet, they can do it all. So, I'm just learning from them guys like trying to like just get better each and every day with them guys. >> A lot of rookies in the DV room. How cool is it for you not to just be maybe like the only one, but there's a lot of you guys learning not just being in the NFL, but the entire team together? Um yes ma'am. You know you got E Stokes. He he um big brother to me. He he um tagged me along the way. He teaching me the ropes. Um we got D cam DP and ch them like great Google guys and like they tagging me along. >> What's it been like? >> Oh yeah. So we came in together. So that's my boy. So like we got the same locker room. We right next to each other. So we talk to each other every >> Um Jeremy gave a lot of praise to you and you know ask questions about how he feels you're doing this training camp. What would you say his leadership and his mentorship has meant to you while being here? >> Oh yeah, it meant a lot. You know, Jeremy Chen, he been he been in the league for a long time, so he know the ins and outs. So he he get on me every day just make sure I'm doing the right things and being a pro. >> What would you say is the biggest difference from, you know, going from college ball to now NFL pro ball? >> Um, the biggest difference, um, I say really just the terminology. Football, football, it's the same thing. It's just the terminology, how the coaches speak, and then just me picking up their technique. >> Sorry. Oh, so I can ask one more. Anything I'm sorry if I missed this, but just is there anything like goals that you've set out for yourself to accomplish this year in your rookie season? >> Yeah, a goal for me is just make the 53 man roster and then just be the best version of myself, be the um best teammate I could be, and then just whatever I can do to contribute to help us win, that's what I'm going to do. Yes, ma'am. Thanks.

title: Klint Kubiak, Michael Mayer and Treydan Stukes Presser - 8.7.26
text: All right guys, let's do it. >> Is it Is that just a matter of that position tightening right now? >> It's just It's been the plan all along, you know, to get those guys competing and and get, you know, get guys mixed in there, see where our best five are. So, that's That's part of the plan. >> Some feistiness between Kirk and Max at the end of practice. Just what do you make of their passion going up against each other? >> Yeah, that's training camp, you know, those are those two leaders of our team going at it. Um so, that that is part of camp. Obviously, you fight in the game, you throw a punch in the game, especially then you're out of the game. So, we got to be smart, treat it like a game. Uh and I mean this honestly, I'm not really married to any position. I think, you know, we're we're a new staff here. We're trying to establish something and there's got to be competition everywhere. And we'll just sit here and let the tape reveal itself and um we know that, you know, with with Aidan O'Connell, too, we got three three NFL-ready quarterbacks. So, we need to keep getting all of them ready to play. >> How has Fernando, um you know, you've seen him a week and a half or so and obviously throughout the games, how what has his progress been like? >> Yeah, he's he's just continuing to to get better. He's improving. Every day brings a new challenge, crowd noise today. Um so, uh there's there's, you know, new things that he's learning every day. And um you know, again, he's working hard. He's like everybody, every other rookie. Um they have they're introduced to a whole new level of football. And there's going to be days of failure and days of success. And as long as they can keep getting better, that's what we're looking for. >> What can you tell me as you said, you know, you straight up said to the media, you know, I want to see what Aidan O'Connell does when the pads come on. You kind of challenged him. So, now the pads have come on and he's had a couple plays. What have you seen from him now that he's on? >> I see a young man that that's continues to compete, you know, he's he's the same guy that he was in the spring. Uh I see a competitive guy. I like I like where he's headed. He's putting a lot of pressure on that first group of corners. >> We're over deeper in the training camp, but what are you hoping to see these next few practices develop with your team? >> Uh just our situational football to improve. You know, we start using a lot more crowd noise, uh way more situations uh now that we start repeating installs and banking reps. You know, we just want to see those guys uh you know, those neurons fire faster now that it's not a new play coming at them. >> Malik Harrison is a young man that not only flashes on offense, but man, his toughness shows in special teams as well. That's something you like. Would you talk about him, please? >> Yeah, I think he's a just a young man that's coming here ready to compete for a job. Uh and when a guy can, you know, make plays on offense and then be be a four-core teams player, that says a lot to his teammates about what he's made out of. So, you know, any one of these young guys, they know how important special teams is and how uh you know, how it's going to relate to them making the team and being a successful part of our operation. >> We didn't see Jaylen We didn't see Jaylen Naylor out there. Is everything okay with him? >> Jaylen's okay. You know, we had a few guys nicked up and we're trying to be cautious with him. >> Is it the same with Dante Thornton with his injury? >> Yeah. Yeah, same same with Dante. Yes. >> When it gets into Allegiant Stadium practices next week, what are you hoping to take away from those with the team? >> Yeah, it's just uh you know, coaching-wise is guys being in the booth, okay, getting our communication down uh with the coaches, um just being in being in that stadium environment in front of the fans. Really excited about that. Um but we have a long way to go to get there. Want to keep getting better starting tomorrow at practice. >> Coach told us that um it's still early. There's still You guys are still installing your offense when it comes to the wide receivers and how they're performing, but what have you seen from the secondary so far in a few practices with pads that's kind of made life a difficult for a lot of them except maybe Greg Bowers? >> Yeah, I think uh you know, Joe Woods and Matt are doing a great job with our DBs. We have a lot of guys making plays on the ball right now. It's a very competitive room. >> Clint, talk about Hemingway, somebody who got here last year. Now he's having a good camp this year. It seems like every time we mention his name, he's making a play. What have you seen from Hemingway? Has he kind of worked his way up? Well, I give a lot of credit to Tanoh Kpassagnon for what he's done in the offseason to prepare his body. All the time he spent with AJ. He's made a lot of improvements physically and it's been you know, what he does in the weight room shows up on the field right now. >> What's it been like working with Mike Sullivan and is there anything that he brings different to coaching quarterbacks that >> I worked for coach Sullivan in Denver and I learned so much from him. I sat in his quarterback room and number one just the man that he is. I mean, he's an Army Ranger. He's a guy that's you know, been through a lot in his life and has a lot to offer these quarterbacks beyond just quarterback play. So, you know, our quarterback has to be the leader of the team and I think Mike Sullivan is a leader of men and so I'm really grateful that he's here and his lessons are rubbing off on all of our quarterbacks. >> You can only coach the players that Spy and his team get you. But there's a lot of even on the UDFA deep talent here. Would you talk about the job Spy and that group did getting you this roster, please? >> I think just making a decision to come here and being familiar with with Spy and our scouting staff. That's no surprise, you know. Those guys are are very professional and they're they're turning over every rock to trying to make the bottom of our roster better at all times and you know, it's a collaborative effort. We work together and really blessed to to work with him. >> You said you wanted to see a lot from Jack Best during this training camp. What have you seen from him so far? >> A professional guy that's continuing to get better. Guys make big jumps from year one to year two. Tanoh Kpassagnon is one of those guys and you know, Jack Jack Best is a is a guy that I see in there early every day that that's working hard. That's playing a lot of positions that can handle it mentally and I see a young player that's going to continue to grow. >> How difficult is it Go ahead. Go ahead. Go ahead. >> You two have been battling for a while. >> No, no, she's good. >> Uh Darnell Washington, he seems like he got a lot of good progress in what have you liked from him? >> I like how hard he plays special teams. You know, he's he's a guy that's going to, you know, challenge guys for spots in in many places on defense and on teams, but um I like that he's a team first guy and it shows up in the way that he plays teams. >> How difficult is it to come in off a day off like yesterday and try to get the energy level up as high as you probably wanted to and then a day like today with the pads on seemed like the energy level and intensity was more. >> Uh well, it's it's not it's not hard when the players get it going. Okay, they they play between the lines on Sunday. Uh we got to give them an organized plan and let them go execute. So, we're looking for leaders to emerge to take over and get here early and and get practice going at 7:30 in the morning. I've seen improvement there. >> You talk about that team first mentality. Michael Mayer is a guy that, you know, when you look at him and look at the stats and what he did in college, he's he's got number one tight end capabilities. Um obviously, the situation here with Brock Bowers, that's not going to be a reality. How is How do you feel like he has handled that his reality, but also come to work trying to figure out a way to help your >> I see a leader emerging on our offense. Put it that way. Simple as that. >> In what In what >> Um uh a standard-bearer in all things. I know I want to keep it short cuz that's the easiest way for that. I mean, he's doing great. >> Max brought up recently that when the trade was reversed, he you called him and said that you were going to take the entire coaching staff out for drinks. Did that actually happen and uh why was that a moment of celebration? >> Tell him he's in big trouble for revealing that. [laughter] Uh We did not go out that night. We really haven't gone out a bunch as a staff. We've been grinding. We probably need to do that more or have some more camaraderie. Um but it's uh the message is we were excited and celebrating that we had uh one of the best pass rushers in the >> Coach, I know you don't want to pat guys on the back too heavy two weeks into camp, but would you talk about Mike Washington who's just at everyday displays it? >> Yeah, we have a you know, a lot of young guys that are pushing guys for spots and uh you know, Mike's a guy that came in and has grown a lot since OTAs. Extremely coachable young man. Football is important to him and that was a big part of uh you know, you know, John's criteria for bringing guys in. The game's got to be important to for them to get better because they have to be self-motivated. So, I see a self-motivated young man that knows there's there's a lot of big football ahead of him and has a long way to go, but a man that's willing to put in the work. >> All right, wraps up. >> Coach, a lot of players have taken up the podium this week. I've really praised Kirk Cousins' knowledge and years of NFL experience. What can you say on how Cousins' um experience has benefited the team so far? >> Quarterback has to be a leader of the team and I see him leading out there. That's what we brought him here for, to lead and play really good football. So, I've been pleased with him and he knows he can get better. >> Thank you, coach. >> Thanks. >> Kind of cool to have pops out here yesterday? Thank you. >> Your coach just uh referred to you as a standard bearer, a leader that's emerged. What does that mean to you as a guy like you in the NFL? >> Yeah, I mean it it obviously means a lot. I think what I got to keep doing is keeping my head down and keep working. Um you know, there's some good days, there's some bad days and I think that's football. But at the end of the day, um at this point I'm going into year four, I need to be a leader. I need to be a leader um physically, mentally, um verbally. Um we got a great, great set of rookies that are coming in here and they've been working their tail off and um, at the end of the day I need to be there for them just like there were people there for me when I was a rookie and um, you know, lead them and show them and push them the right way. >> In your role, um, how else can you lead? How else do you envision leading? >> Yeah, well, I think helping the team win in any way I can. Um, I think being the best version of myself, you know, um, communicating out there. Um, you know, we got a whole new offense this year. That's not That's not new news, but um, there's a lot of communication and uh, the more I communicate with the tackle, the more I communicate with Brock when I'm in there with him, with Ian when I'm in there with him and even the quarterback, Kirk, Fernando, Aiden. Uh, communication in this offense is very big and I think that's something I've maybe slacked on the past couple years. So, um, when everybody's on the right page, uh, good things happen. >> You're going into year three, uh, with with Brock. Uh, oh, with Brock. With Brock. Year four, but you're going into year three with your relationship with Brock. You know, we've seen how you're being used out there in this new offense. Just how do you feel that your relationship on the field has grown? >> Yeah, I mean, it's grown tremendously. Um, you know, I just feel like we get closer and closer every single day together. Um, I'm I'm trying to get him out of his shell as much as I can. Um, um, you know, we're we both got engaged this summer, which is pretty cool. Our both our fiancées are really good friends, which is cool. So, we hang out a lot. Um, we'll play golf when it cools down a little bit, but um, you know, when you have a relationship like that off the field, it's pretty easy to have a a great relationship on the field with somebody like that. So, we want the best for each other. Um, we both want to be successful. We both want each other to be successful. At the end of the day we want to win. So, it's not about who has what catches, who has what this and that. We want to win. Um, we're out there communicating with each other every single day just trying to get better. >> Following that, when you when you when you guys are out there together, what kind of stress can that put on a defense? >> Oh, I think it can a lot. Yeah, I mean, I think we've we've already seen it a little bit with our defense. Um, uh, um, two big threats. I mean, we can both block really well. Um, I think, uh, you know, I think it's just going to be an interesting season in terms of that. I think we just got to keep working hard, keep our head down. Um, you know, Clint's got a plan, whatever Clint's plan is for us, we're going to, you know, we're going to trust in follow it, and we're going to, um, you know, do it to the best of our ability. >> You mentioned the communication. Was there like an aha moment that said you need to come to work on that? >> Uh, I mean, I think anytime a new offense comes in, you that's that's one of the big major kind of coaching points. Um, and I wouldn't even say that's a coaching point. I would just say that's a point just for me coming from myself. Um, there's just a lot of things that are happening and going on every single day, every play. You're getting tons of different looks from the defense, tons of different, um, coverages, and, you know, the more you communicate, the better things better things go. >> We've talked to both players that have been here as long as you've been here, and they've said that they're all going in the right direction. They're all swimming in the same direction. Do you get that same sense, and how does that feel? >> 100%. You know what? I I I think that the challenge is to stay swimming in the the right direction the entire season. You know, there's some good moments, there's some bad moments, but you got to stay going in the right direction. Um, even if you take a step back, you got to take three steps forward. I don't know, that's this league, that's the NFL. Um, so, and I do feel that, too. >> Maybe come up with a feed the comfort level that you were Notre Dame. It's been very obvious since training camp. Am I reading that right? >> I believe so, yeah. I really love this offense. I really love Clint. I really love, um, you know, Luke Steckel, the tight end coach, who's that's year three for him here, and, um, you know, when I heard he was coming back, I was very delighted. Um, I love that man to death, and, uh, he he knows how to coach. He's one hell of a coach, and um, it's just about it's about being comfortable, um, you know, being the type of player that I can be, and going out there and showing people, but, um, you know, Steckel gets me right. Clint's done a fantastic job and and really it's about me putting the best version of myself out there and um doing anything I can. >> His use with tight ends, how much do you think this offense is going to help you excel this season? >> I think so, yeah. I think I think it's on me though. I need to be ready. I need to know the offense, you know, like the back of my hand um and I need to keep my head down and I need to work. You know, I know there's going to be mistakes. I can't let mistakes ruin the day. I can't let them ruin the rep. I can't let them ruin the period. I got to move on. Mistakes are, you know, they happen. So, um I'm very, very excited for this season. I just need to keep working hard, keep my head down and um you know, good things are going to happen. Really good things are going to happen. >> Have you come up with any creative stories for the shiner yet? >> I haven't yet. >> No. You're going to get asked though. >> I have. I know. I know. Um yeah, I mean, I just actually somebody in public the other day said like something about it and I was like, "You should have seen the other guy." >> [laughter] >> But really I didn't I didn't get any I didn't get any punch back at him. So, >> they'll never know. >> Tussles, we saw Max and and Kirk get into it a little bit at the end there. Obviously, you don't want to see the quarterback getting fights, but is it is it good at this point of camp to see two veterans of this team kind of getting after it? >> Yeah, it's energy, man. It's energy. Um you know, we don't want to be throwing punches, but you know, I I think on any padded day of of camp, there's going to be some um you know, there's going to be some tussles um and you know, that's our starting quarterback right now and you want him to defend your team um and you want him to have some edge to him, which he does. He's always had I mean, since the first day I met him when he came in here. So, it's all I mean, I I don't want him getting thrown out. I don't want him getting a flag, nothing like that, but you got to be able to defend yourself. >> What have you seen out of Malik Benson's game so far? >> Oh, yeah. I love it. That's one of my guys. Um he's got great hands. Um he's quick and you know, he's dude, he's moving up. You know, he was in there with us for 2 minutes today and I love when he's in there with me. You know, we're communicating, we're you know, what's the digit here, what's the NASCAR word here. And he just wants to get better. He just wants to get better. He keeps his head down, works hard, doesn't say much. All he wants to do is get better and that's somebody when I look outside and I'm in a three-point stance, I trust. >> Something that's become clear throughout training camp is how spaced out the targets have been. What would you say is your thoughts on how passing game has really connected so far over this last week? >> Yeah, I think that's what you want, right? I mean, you want the targets to get spread around. I think that's how you move the ball down the field. I think that's how you kind of confuse defenses. You don't know where you're really going to go with it. You know, I think it's going to be interesting when we're in there in 12 personnel, what kind of defenses we're going to see, what type of personnel we're going to see. But Kirk, Fernando, Aiden, shoot, they've done a fantastic job of just spreading the ball around. And you know, I think that that that's play calling, too. You know, that's the offense we're building here. That's the offense we're putting in and that's always a positive for the offense.
