You'll you'll I'll be the tall guy. You'll be able to see me. >> I wanted to ask you about the >> He's off topic. >> What what have you seen from him in camp since he's come back from his injury where you think about him before where he's at right now? >> So, he's exceeding my expectations that were pretty high coming in. I think he is uh you know, much like uh unique feature to this team is you know, the best players seem to be the the guys that you want everyone to follow and he's he's uh everything you'd want in terms of a worker and you know, I he's highly talented obviously and I liked him coming out, but I didn't really recognize how talented he was until you you get to see that gigantic human play with pad level. Um that can't be understated. It's very hard to play football with leverage when you're that tall, but if you can, you're a massive human that can create a lot of force and move people. So, I uh it's been a I I had wasn't holding my breath or nervous about it. It's but it's been over the top pleasant surprise in terms of what type of weapon I think he is for this team. >> You you yelled today after he did something like good job, Joe Walker. Do you remember what he did that impressed you? Um No, he blocked Khalil Mack on a screen. Which up until this point it we had struggled to do that. He Khalil Mack is the one of the hardest people to throw a perimeter screen at if he's on that side of the screen. He generally makes play callers look pretty foolish because it's like a negative one yard gain. But he Joe had a very focused convicted mindset flashes hands to inside a pass rush move and then was able to do something that most wouldn't be able to do, which is why he got a first and last name call out I think at the time. I think I said great job Joe Alt, maybe an expletive, who knows. with the defensive line like Julie King or with the edge rush mainly with the whole front Justin and Tillery and those guys, have you been impressed at all as you know you focus on the offense but just watching those guys work maybe the three of them specifically. Yeah, the team too. >> It's really fired me up because I have long vision in the short term the you know the issues that they've created you know as the offensive coordinator kind of suck but bigger more important vision is you know I think we have a pass rush group that can go toe-to-toe with anybody. It's and and that's huge for everything takeaways third downs and setting the edge on first and second down. So the the training the iron iron has truly sharpened iron. I strength of the entire team is the edge defense and the edge blocking with the tackles and tight ends so that that work is been invaluable because it's a it it's the heartbeat of NFL production is the the the edge of the defense and the edge of offense. >> What are some of the problems that have made you adjust to? >> Well, they're uh you have to be very good with cadence. Uh they play uh you know, they play in a two-point stance a ton so that and they utilize their vision uh which is why you're not in a three-point um at edge. Uh and with with that they're uh super very they're all their pass rush moves are varied. They have the full um the full gamut, you know, I think uh the the whole crew uh is technique sound which is gigantic for that position. Um but then they'll also be uh very loose in terms of their uh pass rush or run fit uh run fit really responsibilities where they'll in a heartbeat come inside uh into the B gap through through uh uh Tex game or whatever. So uh to me it's uh you have a hard time in this league if you uh have to utilize other players at different positions to um set the edge or um you know, create pressure. Okay, uh those you know, outside of the quarterback, I think edge edge players um are the second most important position really that that exists. They're they're the quarterback of the defense to me because they uh uh allow if they're set in the edge, all the backers don't have to flow as much and if uh they're getting getting home and creating pressure, people don't have to cover as long. So, um uh huge huge um vital piece to an NFL team and a defense and we are fortunately very well served there. >> With all three preseason games being against opponents you'll see in the regular season, kind of the I guess group think is I can't really do anything or show anything. How does that affect how you'll call plays and and what you want to take out of that? Does that limit you at all with >> No, I'm comfortable going on the record and saying I'm just going to run the exact same plays that I run in the preseason. Exact. Uh you know, I think I think there's No, you're not going to show the the things that will give you a competitive disadvantage going into week one. You know, I think fortunately you know, I run a lot of plays in my day and there's you know, the a lot of things that are core to our to our technique fundamentals that that realistically is on tape and people know that I've I've done before. But yeah, you're you're you have typically have the majority of your play time is from younger guys that you want to see play to degree you want to see them operate. But I'll probably have less motions and there'll be some concepts that that I won't put out there. So to answer your question and again make sure you hit up the the opponent beat writers. It will be the exact same plays. >> Yeah, feel pretty good. You know, thankful for the opportunities that we get to go out there and practice and just continuing to do my best picking up the offense and doing exactly what coach Mike tells us to do and he's been really helpful so it's been it's been a lot of fun so far. >> Some of the stuff I've seen is you're just playing in different spots. I saw like pass yesterday out of the slot. How do you like having guys not stuck to certain points whether it be on the outside or you can play all over? >> I think we've always had >> a pretty good job of spreading guys around and making sure that they can play at different positions. I think, you know, Trey and Vlad, they they've done such a good job. Q has even done that as well. Um where we ask him to line up in a bunch of different places and I think they've done a great job picking it up and it's it's tough, but it's going to be helpful for our offense. >> So, in the new offense, how's your communication with Mike and the head coach been? Has everything been pretty clear there like calling plays and all that? All of that? >> Yeah, so far it's just been all Mike's band and and he tells me exactly what number, which which hash to run the play on. So, so far it's been pretty straightforward. >> Footwork, we think about passing, but just in terms of running, you know, the running game and stuff and footwork, how is that a lot different? Is that something that you're used to and is that chemistry that you have to develop with those guys in that part of the game? >> Yeah, it is different. Um and I think that the best thing is just reps and we get so many reps during practice, during um individual drills that we're able to line up with those guys and get a feel for each of them cuz they're all a little bit different, you know, how they um jump off the ball and exactly where they're going to be. So, as long as we can get it to as close as we can, um it's a pretty good feel, but uh getting as many reps as possible has been really helpful. >> And just with speed, like we've seen some deep shots this last week and stuff, is is that stuff How long does it take to kind of figure out how fast a guy is, where you're going to put it? Is that stuff that you figured out already or is that more reps that you would need to kind of sort that part of the game out? >> I feel like you're always continuing to work on it. Um I think especially with a new guy like Brennan, um you know, the first few practices you had to feel him out and and uh you know, understand where he's going to be and and exactly how fast and how quickly he's going to run. Um but the more that we're we're throwing to him, the the more comfortable you get and I think he's done such a great job of being exactly where he needs to be. Landmarks are so important and I think the coaches have done a great job coaching him. >> Staying with the running game, just I know you can't really see the the whole scope of it even with the pads on, but just how exciting the running back room is and just the versatility that they have. A bunch guys can do a bunch of different things. >> Yeah, I think they've done such a great job. We're going to ask so much of them to to catch the ball out of the backfield, to run it, to pass block, and to have, you know, four or five running backs that you really trust and and have faith in. It's going to be great for our offense. >> Uh Joe and Apple, what what has it been like for you having a back out there often against the last weekend? Is he a friend or teammate to have a back out there? >> Yeah, Joe means so much to our offense. You know, he does such an incredible job on that right side, on the left side when we ask him to, and you know, he's a great teammate, great leader, and he's a guy in the the huddle uh people listen to. And he's a great guy to have out on the field, um in the huddle, you know, you trust him, you have faith in him, and um it's definitely good to see him back out there having fun. >> He got a quite a bit of run with the ones for the past few days. What do you think of him as he kind of got in the rotation? >> Yeah, he Grant's put in a lot of great work this offseason. Um you know, he showed up a a different man, and uh it's been fun to watch and fun to see, and um you know, it's been cool to for him to get those opportunities to go run with the ones, and you know, we we expect a lot from those guys, and and he's picked it up really quickly, and um excited to see what he can do. >> Do you have a favorite part of this new offense? >> Uh it's it's all you know, it's all so great. Mike has done such a great job with the entire offense that uh I don't know if I could pick one one part. >> Is there anything specifically that excites you about what you guys are doing? >> All of it. Yeah, I think Mike has done such a great job with all of it that uh I'm looking forward to everything he brings, and um run game, pass game, play action game. He's he's done a fantastic job. >> We're seeing now how you've seen the offense. Well, Mike's always talking about conviction over pursuing perfection. How do you see the offense kind of understanding and applying his concepts out there going into the week one of training or preseason? >> Yeah, it's exactly the way he he calls it, you know, to go out there and play fast, react, and and you know, go out there and attack, and I I think as long as we're doing that, playing the way he sees it, talking about it, um you know, I think it gives us the advantage of of being able to know exactly as an offense, we know the snap count, we know the plays, um you know, we have that advantage and as long as we're able to keep that, um it's something we have to do as an offense. >> Does he What have you seen in Ladd Quinn uh as far as their development goes, it's uh Trey Sermon. >> Yeah, they're just >> uh just continuing to to progress their game and and uh they're going to make so many big plays and and Q's had uh three great years now and Ladd's going into his third year. Um they just make plays. They're they're fun guys to to be able to throw the ball to. Um pick up the offense really quickly. You know where they're going to be and uh we're expecting them to make a lot of plays this year. >> What do you feel like you're at now 11 days in? >> How many days in? >> 11. >> 11? Oh, damn. Uh 11 days in, man, I feel great. Uh doesn't feel like year 12 even though it is. Uh still feel like I'm running around like a young guy. I ask my coaches every other day like give me two things to work on. Um just working on my craft, man. >> What what are those things typically every time you work on? >> Uh just keep being a leader. Uh keep being a leader, make sure, you know, I'm doing what like what I need to do. And I keep asking them again and you know, it's year 12. You know, it's not much you know, they can't tell me but I always feel like, you know, there's something to get better at. Uh but in like pass covers, whether that's, you know, getting my feet in the ground quicker, uh maybe, you know, wasted movements, you know, eliminating wasted movements. just being, you know, gap sound in the run game. You know, just simple small stuff. >> Chris, O'Leary was saying that he doesn't pick favorites but last game with you guys a lot of linebacker reps. I saw you out there today. What's his impact been like on the linebacker group to you? >> Uh for me, I mean, it's been great. Like you said, there's no favorites. I I I'm not saying that, you know, our last coordinator had favorites or anything like that, but man, he just migrates and, you know, he's able to mingle and connect with all the players, honestly. And uh just in our room, man, uh he likes to come in there and challenge us a lot. So, um I mean, that just brings out the the competitor in everybody in our room and everybody on defense in general. >> With your room in particular, how do you guys not a lot, you don't have to just have anything like the majority of the group intact, but just how you guys kind of try to push each other to kind of grow up to another level? Just >> Uh I think you know, like the little bickering talk that we have in the room. >> Like we got a We got a fine board in the room. Like, you know, if you drop a ball, you know, we always yelling out rankings, so, you know, nobody wants to drop a ball, you know, we always, you know, pushing to make plays, you know, let's see who can make, you know, this many plays, let's see who can get on the board, you know, for separated, so uh we you know, we challenge ourselves, you know, with the simple things in football, I would say. >> What's your overall impression of what you're seeing from defense so far? >> Overall, man, uh I love it. I love it. Uh obviously, you know, we got some new pieces and uh you know, those new pieces just all forming to one right now. from spring to now, you can see the growth. Like, we all, you know, playing together, the communication is crazy. And, you know, for a defense, that's that's pretty big. >> What is this board that you mentioned? >> What? >> The board that you have, a fine board or >> Yeah, fine board. >> Do you get fined if you drop >> No, you don't get fined, but, you know, not bursting to the balls, you know, it's it's something that, you know, we hold ourselves to a certain standard in our room. >> So, what happens if you make a mistake, you get on the board or >> Yeah, it all depends It all depends on the mistake. Like, not bursting to the ball, like, that's pretty big. Like, dropping a ball, whether it's in the individual team period, you know, that's it, we yell out rankings. Like I said, you don't want to be at the bottom of the board. >> Okay. What is the fine for? >> Nah, just like a little board that we put up in the room every day. >> Where are you at on that right now? >> Well, I know yesterday I was at the bottom. I dropped two passes. Two. It was bad. >> What happens if you're at the bottom? Do you just get >> Nah, I mean, it's It's it's just it's not it's not good on the soul. Just look up there and see your name at the bottom. It's like, "Ah, all right. Got to do better tomorrow." >> Is it peer pressure? >> I wouldn't say peer pressure. It's more just pressure on yourself. >> What do you like about what Coyle's done to the defense? >> I think just the energy that he brings. I mean, y'all see him talking. You see him on the field like he's literally running around. Like he does the fourth-quarter finishes with us, you know, not just Coach Harbaugh. Like you know, he's out there running around with us, man. It's almost like if he wants to, you know, play with us. And um I think it's just the energy, man. It's very contagious. >> Is there anything, I know you have a competitive advantage so some stuff you can't say. Is there anything specific schematically that you can share that you enjoy about his twist on on the unit? >> Just able to play football. Just play fast and play football. The communication is not nothing, you know, complicated. Uh it's really just communication that was uh that's what makes and allows us to play that fast. So, it's football. >> What have your interactions been like with Mike McDonald? >> Been some funny, excuse my language, been a lot of like trash-talking. You know, he talks his little stuff and you know, we'll fire back, but I just laugh. It's It's It's funny to me. >> Is that fun? >> Yeah, it is funny. But, again, it just gets everybody going. Get everybody on that competitive edge. >> What sort of kind of stuff does he say? >> Uh like I know what the other day he told us like we better be dropping there like near the hashes. And I know one time he said that they was going to run 10 run plays to the C gap. So, it was just like, "All right. Well, I hope they got their mouthpiece in." Cuz like we would. But, you know, it's like little stuff like that, you know, it's just just get everybody going, man. >> You've been a lot of all off-season about just the specific hunger heading into this season. As a veteran, just kind of how have you felt that hunger? Not all off-season, but just throughout camp so far. >> Uh man, I think just looking at, you know, where we've been, uh you know, kind of like where we've been through like through injuries and like you know, how far we come. Uh I guess like you kind of see, you know, we just stay on track, we just stay healthy, you know, like what we can do. And I guess that's what brings out that hunger.

title: O'Leary, Njoku, & Eboigbe On Training Camp Physicality | LA Chargers
text: Maybe talk about just kind of getting into the install and see what it looks like. Like how far are you and seeing between the offense and the defense? >> Yeah, we're kind of at that same point. Um I would say for the most part our installs are in, they're done. Um so now we're going to start to see who can execute those things, um who can execute those things in competitive drills, competitive periods, um and then the preseason games. So that's kind of the stage we're at right now is starting to get into that evaluation period. >> Anybody in particular you're excited to see on Thursday? >> Uh a lot of guy I can name a lot of guys. Um we've, you know, we we anticipate what guys can do, but we're excited to see what they actually do when the lights come on. Um I mean an obvious one that that I've been asked about a few times, um Shelly and Avery Avery Smith, the corner young corners. I'm excited to see them go challenge. >> When you look at I'm just speaking preseason games, like what do you kind of put near the top in terms of evaluation when you're looking at like game game preseason game tape? >> Yeah, uh we talk about two things on defense, uh trust and production. Uh so each player we evaluate uh with that process. Uh trust, you know, how well can you execute our defense? Can you fit in the scheme? Can you do your job consistently? Uh and then production is being around the football, whether I'm getting quarterback hits, uh pass breakups, whatever it may be. How how much do you affect the game? >> You mentioned competitive periods today, a lot of red zone work. What do you like about that and what are you kind of looking at as you see your group down there? >> Uh the red zone is uh you know, it's kind of like you do or you don't. You either get a stop or they're scoring a touchdown. And so um you really got to execute, things speed up, you got to talk a little bit more down there. So uh anytime we can get in those situations in practice is great because uh to me big games and championships are won in situational football. Uh and a lot of times that's down in the red zone. You're a little tired, maybe you gave up a big play. Uh can we get our cleats in the ground and defend every blade of grass? And so those are awesome for us. >> You said a couple months ago a guy you were looking forward to in pads again. Now that the pads are on for, you know, a week or so, what's the good practice report? Where's he at? >> Yeah, he's uh very physical. He's flashing. He's getting around the quarterback. Um we've, you know, backed him up a little bit from getting around the quarterback, staying out of the cylinder, but uh he's done a really good job. He needs to use his hands a little bit more. Uh it's kind of what we're on him about right now, but as far as a guy that plays physical and really strikes people, like he brings that each day. >> Another young Edison, Kyle, just a couple, you know, flashing one-on-one and team drills. Where where do you kind of feel like he's at in what he brings to the program? >> Consistently getting better. Um you know, he has his flash plays, but just the effort has improved. Um a guy that's straining between the whistles. Uh he's he's developed some pass rush moves and uh a nice toolbox in the run game as well, so a guy that's getting better consistently. >> How was your >> Well, uh preseason game coming up, how much are you I just you personally looking forward to getting back in the call play at the at the level of that fast environment? >> Can't wait. Cannot wait. Like uh just want to get out there and do it, you know? Um want to let the guys play fast and fly around, and you know, it the the best part is you see guys really rise to the occasion, the guys that have prepared correctly, uh the guys that love the game, don't fear failure, and go out there and let it rip. Um so, I'm excited. Can't wait. >> Yeah, but actually are you going to be on the sideline or >> Yeah, I'll be on the sideline. >> What what do you like about that? >> Uh you can lead the guys. Um nothing gets lost in translation. I can communicate my message. Uh when things are going bad, I can get in the huddle and look them in their eyes. Um that's what I like being a part of, so for me, being on the sideline is more effective. Western >> Yeah. >> Is it exciting for you today to see like what play and leverage were in Justin, Tui, King, and Tui kind of burst through? I mean, they got through I think all of them got through at the same time. But like how exciting or is it exciting for you to be able to flood all those guys on the field at the same time? Is it a challenge to get them all on the field at the same time? >> Um not really a challenge. Like our we got to get our best guys on the field situationally. We got to get our best uh players for those situations. So when we have a chance to rush the passer, we got to get those guys out there. Um it's exciting for everybody on defense, players and staff when those guys get on the ball. Um so the more we can get that package out there and our best pass rushers, we're going to do it. >> How do you feel about him as a blocker? >> Really good. >> Really good. Um I think each day he's kind of like, you know, the first day or two he's kind of ramping up and then I think the last couple he's really rolling now. So I like I like how he looks. >> So how's it been first camp in LA? How's it going so far? >> Awesome, man. It's been awesome with Mike McDaniel. This new playbook is amazing. You know, our teammates are great. James great, you know what I mean? So yeah, we're having a whole lot lot of fun. >> Now that you've been with Mike for a little bit now, McDaniel, what is he like as a coach? How's it different from your old team? >> Very interesting character, you know what I mean? He's definitely no one I've ever uh experienced before, you know what I mean? And uh I I think he's just very intelligent when it comes to, you know, just plays the uh just everything overall. It's it's it's awesome. >> Is there something he's done like you laugh and smile when he when you talk about him? Like what stands out or is there a story that stands out with him so far? >> Probably shouldn't say. >> Do you do you laugh when you hear him chirping or Hill or Two Lee or something? >> Yeah, for sure. For sure. This is a great energy, you know what I'm saying? And I think that's what the the team needs. That they just that that big energy, you know? So yeah, it's awesome. >> We talked to you earlier on, but just now having a couple months with the rest of the tight end room, is there Cole Kmet and just how that's been so far and just how you guys kind of see >> You just see this combination of >> Yeah, for sure. I mean, they're all great dudes, you know, even Scott Matlock, you feel me? Just everyone has their own thing that they have to do and I think I think we compliment each each other. And we just push each other just to strive for greatness. >> On that same note, working with Justin now for a few months, what's it like working with him and catching passes from him? >> He's a he's a sharpshooter. Laser, you know what I mean? He's uh completely He's He's a great quarterback, you know, just very accurate, just mobile, everything, you know, very smart, too, so uh yeah, it's it's good to have him on our side. >> With the offense, do you just kind of feel like more and more comfortable with each passing day in camp or just how do you how do you feel from week to week in camp and just where you feel like you guys are succeeding now? >> Say it one more time. >> Just where do you guys feel like you're at now in terms of with the offense like and where where do you feel like you're clicking and where >> I mean, the first day that I got here, I was my my head was kind of spinning, you know what I mean? It was like it was just uh just just I guess bullets flying everywhere, but now I feel like it's settling in for everyone. I I feel like we're getting our rhythm, you know what I mean? So, it's really exciting to see. And yeah, we're we're just going to go one day at a time, just work each day and just see where where it goes. >> How's camp been so far for you? >> Uh I mean, honestly, my own opinion, um a stacking days type approach, like just keep trying to get better and better. my only competition is the man in the mirror. All I want to do is keep improving, keep having a good camp, have a better camp than I had last year, and just keep wagering my success based off what I did previously. >> Do you feel more comfortable going into year three now? And and you and your ability >> Well, I would say so. It's like anything, like the more and more you get familiar with something, whether you get familiar with the system, familiar with what the coaches want, Um you just be able to gain more confidence, more confidence in how you play, your ability, ability within the scheme, and that's all I want um and all I've been trying to do, you know, each and every year. >> In your at practice, do you feel yourself doing things twice to feel the improvement in you? Watching you with your flash from your time and your other last year or or that, and do you feel that in real time? >> Uh I wouldn't say in real time. It's all what I've done throughout the off-season. Um the little things, the the habits that, you know, I built, the hard work that I put in. It's just a just a cumulative of all little things that I've done that, you know, hoping that it'll be success. You know, I do all things in the off-season. Um all the habitual things hoping that, you know, it will be success even though I do them things not knowing that, you know, I will succeed in the way I want, but I just look at it like little things over a long time will build up to where, you know, you'll see improvement in anything. >> I was talking actually like the four times that the versus city having you down with Tiare, Jamarion, just the rest of the Eli group, just now seeing that in action with pads on. How was it How was it being like that? Just How exciting was it? >> Man, the excitement is everybody in that room is just competition, you know, not competition within the group, but competition within they self, you know. Tiare has something to prove, JC has something to prove, Dalvin has something to prove, I have something to prove, you know, Nick Barr has something to prove, you know, the undrafted guys have something to prove. So, just having that chip on your shoulder not worried about anybody else, but just worried about yourself. You know, the only person you can compete with is the man in the mirror, and that's how we look at it, you know, keep stacking days, you know, it's going to be good reps, it's going to be bad reps, but end of the day you just got to keep getting better, you know, don't harp on the bad times, but you know, just learn from it, and that's how our coach Alston has the room, you know, by just having that mindset of keep getting better just 1%, you know, figuring something out that you want to work today, whether it be pass rush and the run, whatever, just work something and try to perfect that or get better each and every day. >> And you mentioned Coach Alston, just you three working with him. Just what is that kind of match for for you and your career so far? >> Man, it's crazy cuz it's a full circle moment, you know, when he was at Notre Dame, you know, he recruited me out of high school and you know, I wanted to say I didn't want to go to Notre Dame, but it just was outside, you know, my mind frame at that point in time, but you know, just crazy from my last college game, the Rose Bowl, playing against Michigan, playing against Harbaugh, um Coach Alston, um Coach Minar at the time and just seeing, you know, full circle being able to be brought into that system, being able to, you know, see what makes Coach Alston such a good coach, the way he breaks it down, the way he teaches it. Um it's just such a great feeling, you know, it's a great feeling that, you know, from year one to now, just the complete, you know, full circle this of where I was as a rookie to now and continuing to keep growing. >> What's it been like for you with Chris Shorter? >> Uh I mean, this is second time around, you know, he was here my rookie year, but of course he's in a bigger role as far as DC, but he's very vocal, you know, he's harps on what has, you know, worked in the past as far as like one of the biggest things we talk about is our separators. That'd be communication, block destruction, tackling, ball disruption, efforts and angles and he harps on that. And just playing 11 as one, you know, at the end of the day it doesn't matter what he call as long as the all 11 is on the same page, we can beat anybody or we can beat ourselves, you know, by not being on the same page. So, just harping on the communication, harping on team unity, like getting to, you know, know each and every guy that's on the defensive side, the coaches, the players, the analysts, no matter what, so it means a little bit more when you um going out there performing your job, when you know what your brother um has has done getting to this point. And what what is his why, what, you know, what makes him wake up in the morning, the reason why he wants this so bad, so preaching team unity and trying to get us all to come together.
