title: DeMeco Ryans on What He Wants to See vs. the Chargers | Full Q&A
text: Hey, good afternoon. >> Is it still morning? >> Great. [laughter] >> Somewhere. >> All right. >> Did you like it? Did you like what you saw? >> Today's practice was outstanding practice for us. One of our better practices from just a standpoint of getting the operation down, right? working on the sideline, being able to get calls in from the sideline, coaches get off the field and let the guys just go play. It's real football, so we wanted to give the guys a dress rehearsal of what that'll look like on Thursday night so it's not their first time going through it. >> Are there any particular things that you're looking for tomorrow night that you like watching for this first preseason game? The main thing I look for our first game, our first time out for 2026 is are we displaying our play style, right? That's the main thing I want to see. No matter who you are, when you touch the field, are you repping the Texans brand? And that's what I want to see. Guys playing fast, playing relentless, finishing. That's what I want to see. And then you also when we dive into it into the fine details of it, like who can you count on to execute, right? When the lights are on in game time, are guys going to be consistent and they're going to take the same approach they've been taking over the past several weeks of how we've been prepping the guys, how they've been working, right? Can they go out and perform that under the lights under a little bit more stress? You know, how how do guys operate at a high level? That's what I'm looking for. >> Of course, of training camp, how have you kind of seen CJ with his pocket management and stepping up, making plays, and dealing with some of the pressure that the defense puts on it? The defense is making it very tough on us offensively and we know that we know we're there. Our offense is up against a challenge every single day going against Will Denil on the edges. I thought C I think CJ has grown from the aspect of being able to, you know, really maneuvering the pocket and not just maneuvering, but it's keeping two hands on the football. It's securing the football. It's stepping up in the pocket. It's still keeping his eyes downfield, right? Making the proper reads, still throwing strikes. Like that's what's impressive about him. He's he's not getting flustered if things break down. He's still able to maneuver and make those plays on the run that I talked about a couple days ago. >> You've indicated you're not not a huge fan of of kind of scraps during practice. Is there some value to to having a rookie like Keon Rutled who's not afraid to stick his nose in there even if it's, you know, involving one of the best players in the NFL? [laughter] >> Better be careful there. He's messing with Will Anderson. No, it's I love it, right? I love the scrappiness of Keelin. I love that his mindset is what I love. He's not backing down from anybody as he should. I expect that from every player on our team. We're not backing down from anybody. We know we're not physically fighting, but there is always chippiness in our game because it's a tough it's a physical violent game that we play and there's going to be some chippiness that goes on. But we just have to make sure we're smart, especially in game, right? We have to make sure we're smart and make sure we're not that second guy to cause the team to hurt ourselves and then coach is going to be really upset. >> When it comes to the game and philosophy you have toward it, you look at the playing time, how much do you want to see the back because you were mentioning this the other day, but as far as like also protecting starters in those early preseason games. >> What's the question? >> How much do you want to make sure that you're resting some of the guys maybe that are your first strength? Well, during the during this game against the Chargers, we'll sit out a handful of guys that have been designated sit out for this game and the other guys will get a ton of the reps, >> very competitive practice today. Uh, was it due to the fact that you all said, "Okay, so this is a game time situation." >> I think the guys were a little fired up, [laughter] you know, I had had to get after him a little bit yesterday. Hey, it wasn't our best practice yesterday uh by any means. That wasn't who we are, how we come out. That wasn't it. So, you know, everybody need a reminder just of what we're what we're trying to achieve. What what are we trying to accomplish, right? To do what we're trying to accomplish, it takes persistent work every single day. We can't have letd downs. We can't have setbacks. Like, we have to continue to press forward. You have to count on guys to be relentlessly consistent in what they're doing in their approach every single day. Yesterday, we took a step back. It wasn't good enough. But today, guys responded really well. All three phases did a really great job, right? Making plays, doing what they're supposed to do. So, I'm really proud of the work we put in today and we're ready to go for game day. >> What does the coach want to see from a running back on the back end of the depth chart as far as making the team and what have you seen from Noah Whittington who's kind of in that battle? Noah seems to make a play every day when he he has a really good feel for, you know, pressing blocks and his vision. Just knowing when to cut, when to take the ball outside, when to, you know, make a cut back up inside. Just you feel a guy I see a guy who has plays with really great vision, great feel at the running back spot. So, when you see guys that are lower on the depth chart in these preseason games, some of those running backs are going to shine. They're going to make some nice plays. Noah won't surprise me. Pittsenberg won't surprise me. Those guys have have done it all camp. So excited to see them play. >> How would you assess the ramp up in physicality? I know you're always trying to tow that line between intensity and making sure players are staying healthy, but are you pleased with that balance? >> This is probably our best year with that balance of of keeping guys healthy, but also playing our style, right? It is a lot of give and take there. Uh, but I can never sacrifice the the mindset and the play style that I want to exhibit. When we we play ball, you want everybody to continue to talk about how physical we are, how relentless, like, man, how do why do your guys run to the ball like they do? How do you guys finish that way? That's our brand. That's who we are as Texans. And we will always represent that. But the fine line is we have to protect the team. When we're practicing against each other, we are on the same team. no matter how upset guys may get at each other. And it's that point of camp, right, where I'm tired of going against the same guy over and over again. I know his moves. I know everything that he's going to throw at me, and I'm just tired of going in. So, Thursday's game is coming right on time for us. A >> lot of competition spots. How is third linebacker shaping up, and what do you hope to see from some of the guys that are trying to fill in that role? >> We have a lot of great depth at linebacker. Um it's we have a lot of capable guys who can go out and play, you know, defense for us, but also that that third, fourth linebacker spot, it comes down to special teams, right? And how valuable are those guys being able to play all four special teams for us. So it it'll be important for those guys in this game to go showcase that. >> In recent years, we talked about the undrafted free agents, especially the rookies. What have you seen from Trayvon Saunders and how he's been impactful and what did you like about him when he was coming on out? >> Yeah, Trayvon has done a really nice job of just, you know, being smart, always aligning in the right place. We throw a lot on the receivers when it comes to alignments, motions. I feel like he's handled that really well. He's fast, explosive guy who he can make some plays with the football in his hand. So, we'll see how he does on tomorrow night. >> Has been, you know, pretty effective pretty much all training camp. How impactful was it to see him make that play today and score that touchdown? >> It was a huge play. Huge momentum boost for our offense. Uh to see David is what he's done a really good job of is is route running, right? And him and Henry have had a lot of battles thus far in camp. So, it was cool to see, you know, David make a big play for us. And that's the type of player he is. That's why he's here for us. He can spark an offense, right? he can lift us with just making those plays or just by him being a leader, being vocal, right? Encouraging the other guys. >> All right, thank you. >> All right, thank you guys. Have a good one.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Kayden McDonald, Clowney and Preseason | Full Q&A
text: What's up, guys? Good morning. Caden's been progressing really well as a rookie. There was a lot of huge learning curve for him, but he's doing a a good job being attentive to what we're asking him to do and you see I see the steps of him towards getting better with this. Mainly just keeping his pad level low, that's what we've been straining him the most is just low man wins in football. He has to continue to work that. Very strong. Very strong kid. So, he just has to play to his strengths and he'll continue to get better. In the first preseason game, I'm really looking for those guys who are on the back end of the roster seeing them go out and and compete for an opportunity to be a part of our team this season. So, to see those guys get as many reps as they can handle, all right, and see who's going to show up on game day. All right, we've installed a lot. We've coached up the fundamentals and techniques. Now, can they go do it, right, when the coaches aren't on the field, nobody's coaching you up after every single play, but can you go out and be a true pro and execute your craft at a high level against different competition? So, that's what I'm looking forward to the most. Yeah, Patterson has done and Patterson's been solid since he's been here. Guy who we've counted on to do the center, also moving over to guard. He's played right guard, left guard. He's a smart player who's accountable. He's going to be where he needs to be and he fights. He's a competitive guy and that's why he's stuck around for a while. Clowney is still getting adjusted to how we do things. You see him the probably his first day you know I saw we were doing a two-minute drill the first day, and he just had a a one-on-one rush off the edge, and I'm standing back there behind the quarterback, and he got on me quicker quicker than I expected. So, I expect to see that from him, right? He's He had nine sacks last year, so still very productive late in his career. So, I'm encouraged by what I've seen so far in just his first few days of being here, uh, not having a full off-season with us, but to come in where he is right now, and it's only going to keep getting better. I'm excited to see where he winds up and how our rush group looks on third down. >> What determines whether they're not to have their hand in the dirt or whether they're standing up? >> With defensive ends and their stance, standing up, hand in the dirt, it it really goes to their comfort level. Uh, what's the situation? If it's obvious pass situations, I think you'll see more guys have their can stand up, right? Or they're working you know, some type of game, some type of stunt. Like, do they want to be in the dirt or it's it's From my point of view, it's completely optional to those guys, right? I let those guys have the freedom. I never played D-line and rushed the passer, so >> [laughter] >> there's a lot of creative freedom there, and whatever it takes for those guys to, you know, be connected, and as long as they're working together, going through the proper steps that we teach those guys, if they can operate it at a at a great pace and do it at the right timing, then it works for me. >> I only ask because I know that you know, throughout his career, Clowney has been effective with his hand in the dirt or with him standing up, and I see that Will has that same ability to be able to do it from from both stances. So, I only ask because is that a defensive thing or like you said, comfort level? >> Yeah, that's a great question. It It's truly, to me, it's about the player being comfortable. Or like, when you go to for me, when you talk about stances and all those things, like everybody is different, different body types, like they're different. So, I allow guys that freedom when it comes to rushing the passer or playing linebacker, whatever that is, wherever you're most comfortable is the position I want you to be in. The last thing I want is our guys to be in an uncomfortable position trying to go do something that's extremely hard. Marlon's progress every single day. His trajectory is definitely pointing up. Seeing him in the pass game, seeing, you know, you guys have seen him make a lot of plays out here in the passing game. He's He's still learning a lot. We're throwing a lot at him, but for a rookie to be, you know, where he is at this point in camp, I'm I'm very encouraged. I'm very pleased with where he is, and I'm excited to see him to continue to to progress. Um he's done a great job. So, I'm excited. At the line of scrimmage, he's done a good job, and also in the passing game. You see a guy, as I mentioned before, he's a he could be a big threat in the passing game. So, he's exciting young player to watch for this year. What sets What sets Sheldon apart is it's above the neck. Like, he is one of the smartest D-linemen I that I've had. And when it comes to us, like how we want to attack protections, right? Or protections change, how can we change our stunts? It's a lot of communication that goes on. I know it's It helps when you got great players, but it also helps when you have a guy, you know, in the middle who can orchestrate it and put it put us in a position that's advantageous to us. And Sheldon helps us when it comes to that. Yeah, we we decided to go with with Kroger right now. He's had a consistent He's done a very uh good job being consistent out here in practice and just wanted to get our operation as clean as possible with the same three guys working together uh getting us ready to go for the season. A few guys have stood out, but I can't tell the world all my secrets, all right? So, but a few guys have stood out. When it comes to our rookies, all right, the young guys, they have undrafted rookies that are really making a name for themselves here on the practice field. And those are guys that I'm most excited to see in the game because they've done it, they've been consistent. These guys do a great job of taking care of themselves off the field, so they've been going every single day working hard. I'm proud of the work that all of our rookies have put in. Why not? >> No, for for our for our preseason game against the Chargers, we'll have a select group of guys who will not go out and play. Now, we we were we were evaluating those group install periods really from a communication standpoint and an assignment standpoint. So, we we get a lot of work pre-practice uh at a slower tempo working those, and we also come back in the evening when you guys are not here. You guys are at home sleeping. We get a lot of work in, all right, in the in the evening time as well. Just joking. >> Breidenbach's dealing with a knee right now, so he's he's kind of day-to-day. We'll see how it goes with them. We'll get a lot of live reps when it comes to our competitive periods, our ones going against each other. I try to mix up situations a lot for our guys and kind of put them in stressful positions a lot and also we'll get an opportunity to have two joint practices. In joint practices is where I see you gain a lot of valuable reps going against a different opponent, different schemes so you get a chance to do a lot of different things during your joint practice as well, but our guys are our coaches walk through a lot with our guys. There's a lot of teaching that goes on behind the scenes at a walk-through pace and we get the full speed reps as well to make sure our guys are ready to go with all of the new things that we're installing. It was very easy talking to coach Kubiak. I think when the schedule came out I'm sitting in my office and I'm looking at the schedule. I'm talking to my assistant Jake. He's like, "Man, we should the Raiders I know Kubiak will be ready to go and like literally 2 minutes later my phone starts to ring and it's Kubiak. I said, "Hey bud, what you want to practice?" Let's go. He's like, "Oh man, this is way easier than I thought it would be." So it works out it works out well. We were both thinking just alike. All right. Thank you guys.

title: Sheldon Rankins on Will Anderson Jr., Clowney and the D-Line | Full Q&A
text: Good morning, Mr. Green. >> How y'all doing? >> When I see you working on the side after practice, staying here with David Longman, what do you what do you see in him that that makes that worth your investment and and what you're trying to teach him? >> Uh just a little nuances. I think um when you get so much thrown at you uh as a young guy, um completely different defense than he's ever played in, um it's it's being it's made, you know, it's knowledge that we're counting on him, you know, the the the the pressure that I'm sure he puts on himself to be perfect every day. Um a lot of things can get lost in translation, whether it's um alignment, whether it's hands, whether it's um you know, pad level on bull rushes or being able to skate blocks at this level, how different it is than, you know, college. Um so for me it's just pulling him aside and being able to being able to articulate a lot of those things in a way that that uh that is slowed down um so he can work through those things at a slowed pace, uh download those things so that when he gets out there um playing real football, um it kind of becomes second nature. >> You just see one of your really good friends stick his head inside of the tent and Will Anderson Jr. is someone that you've that you've seen grow in his game. You've also been around and watched a lot of defense in your career. What is starting to set Will apart from others? >> Uh it's the I think the turning point for for players of his caliber is like when they realize that when they want to take it over, they can take it over. And I think he's getting to that point where you know, he he realizes if he wants to shut practice down, he can shut it down. Like if if he don't want them to get a play off, they won't get a play off. He don't want them to get a pass off, they won't get a pass off. He want a TFL every play, he can go do it. So, I think he's starting to get to that point where he finally realizes that like man, like the game is in the palm of my hands. And he also understands the responsibility that comes with it. I think that's what makes him so special. Is that, you know, you get a lot of guys in that position of of of being that dominant, being that good, and you know, they kind of look at it like, you know, it was supposed to happen to them. Um whereas he looks at it as, you know, he's grateful for every chance he gets to be the player that he is. So, um yeah, I think I think he's starting to realize the the the power that he has, you know, that his hands, feet, helmet, all that, all the above. Um and he's letting it be known every day. >> You know, with the three of his four seasons now what have you observed that has allowed that allows him to be able to take over a game? >> Yeah, I think it's the just the relentless work ethic. I think he's he's never shy about looking for knowledge, right? I think, you know, certain guys get to a point where um they're so good or they're they're they're at a level where uh you know, they feel like asking for asking questions is weird in a sense. Um but that's not him, you know, he's always looking for ways to improve, whether it's film study, whether it's his recovery, whether it's uh pass rush moves, whether it's alignment in the run game. I mean, you know, from the first day he got here, the first thing he does when he gets in the locker room is grab the iPad, watch practice film. He still does it today. His locker's right next to mine, so we generally go over things. He's asking me about his alignment here, his hands here. So, he's always as good as some of the reps look to other people, none of it's ever is is ever good enough for him. And I think that's what makes him so special. Uh to be at a point where I mean he's, you know, highest-paid non-quarterback and no trade clauses and all types of craziness like that and to still be like, "Yeah, but what more can I do?" I think that that just speaks volume about who he is. >> You see pretty quickly how Logan, Jadeveon can make this defense creative and what all the things they can do? >> Absolutely. Yeah. I think Logan gives us that versatility. I think that, you know, we had with Autry in a sense, you know, if we needed him to he can go outside play in. He's stout enough, strong enough to to play from wide nine all the way to zero. Clowney, the resume speaks for itself. No matter where he's been, he's produced in the run and in the pass. So, adding both of those guys in to what we already had with, you know, myself, Will, uh Danielle, Tommy, adding in Caden as well. I mean, the the sky's the limit for where we could be. Um and we're seeing flashes of it out here, but the more we're able to to orchestrate together, you know, collab and craft together, we just hope to to get it up to speed to be humming by by week one. >> Mike Vrabel mentions about chasing perfection in the defense. Four guys on the interior, what does perfection look like? >> Uh disruption. I think uh we joke a lot in our room because it's a race every snap. And the race is more so inside guys to outside guys cuz you know, if we're not perfect, Will and Danielle are already there. Um and even when you are perfect, they probably still beat you there. So, you know, for us, um, inside man it's about disruption. Uh, it's about being able to clog lanes. It's about being able to get quarterbacks off their spot, not allow them to be comfortable. Uh, so those guys on the edge can rush freely and do what they do without thinking. You know, it's about, uh, always talk to the inside guys about, uh, beating blocks. I think, uh, you know, if you start looking at how many plays you made, uh, you often start skipping the process on defeating the blocks in front of you. Uh, I never chase the plays. I always chase beating blocks. Cuz if I beat the block, nine times out of 10 I'm going to get myself an opportunity to make a play. So, I think, you know, for us inside man, continue to be disruptive, continue to beat blocks, uh, and continue to to to collapse pockets, uh, be disruptive in the run game, and allow those specimens on the edge to to to do what they do. >> Got three more. Chance right, sorry. >> You've always been the elephant in the room, and now you guys have J.J. Watt. How has his presence used you? What's it like to continue to do it at this high of a level? >> Uh, man, it's great. Uh, I think it, uh, you know, it it it it in a way continues to drive guys like myself. Like, obviously getting older, but, you know, you still see a guy who's a little bit older than myself continue to still do it at a high level. Um, you know, it's great to add, you know, I think, you know, one thing he probably doesn't get as much credit for is his his football IQ. You know, he's already in the meeting rooms talking about things he sees, uh, as much film as he studies, and and and being able to bounce that knowledge off myself, Will, Danielle, other young guys in the room. Uh, it's been great. And then obviously once he takes the field, I mean, you see why he was, you know, the the number one overall pick, and and no matter what jersey he puts on, um, he's a highlight reel waiting to happen. >> What training camp in Houston is no joke. >> Right. >> What makes this worth it for you? Is it the end result? Is it wins? What makes this worth it? >> Uh, that's a great question, actually. I think it's probably a multitude of things. Some personal, some team-wise. I think team-wise, I just think being a part of something special. You don't take it for granted going into your 11. Uh, I think I was talking to somebody about this offseason like this team has a very college feel to it. Like with how close everyone is and uh, the inside jokes and how how much we clown each other and how much you can clown your brother, but it's not taken personal. It's that type of feel. Um, and that's hard to find in NFL. That's that's really hard to find, you know, because of the business of of it and everybody's generally out for themselves. But, I mean, this is a team that genuinely cares about each and every man uh, being successful as a player and as a person. Um, and that shows in the way we we play on defense, on offense, special teams. Um, that shows it in the way we cheer each other on. That shows in the way we um, congregate outside of the meeting rooms and in the field. Um, so I'd say that. And then personal is like um, now I've went through injuries in my career, uh, you know, that I felt like um, at certain times may have kind of knocked me off of you know, where I felt like I was ascending at the time or or different things like that or illnesses that I may have have went through. So, for me, like every day I I touch the field, whether it's practice, whether it's uh, game, um, I'm doing it for the men next to me, but I'm also like making sure I remind everybody like, yeah, I'm still that guy. Like I I can still do this at a high level. Uh, first down, second down, third down, crunch time, it don't matter. Like put me in the game. I can make a play playing with whomever, next to whomever. Uh whatever style is needed, whatever whatever is needed, like I've always shown throughout my career that I can make those plays, so even going into year 11, like I'm always finding ways to somehow make myself feel disrespected. So, that each and every time I step out here, it's like excuse my French, now that. Yeah, so. >> Sorry, last one. Along those same lines, you know, I've had conversations with Russell Wilson, DK Metcalf, Tyler Lockett, Doug Baldwin, talked to Kade McDonald now, and I've talked to Tom Cable about how much you are a perfectionist one, but you teach, you're always teaching, you're always teaching all the while while you're learning. You shied away from saying after this is all over with, you're going to be a coach. But, you but you see, even on the sidelines, we watch you still teaching. Are you starting to see yourself, once this once the the game is done for you, going that way? >> Uh that is that is not something I'm saying, but everybody I mean, and I do mean everybody tells me that's, you know, that's something I'll I'll get to. And, you know, we'll cross that bridge when I get there. Uh but, yeah, I think um I think I would be doing the game a disservice. I think I'd be doing myself a disservice if I didn't um impart all the wisdom that I have onto, you know, my teammates. I think uh beautiful thing is I I kind of understand I understand what it's supposed to look like. But, I also understand what it's supposed to look like if you're undersized. I also understand, you know, so I think I have the uh the ability to uh make it relatable to whatever the body type is whatever whatever the the skill set is so that's why you see me do that I just I understand that you know when it's over me just having all this wisdom and going home and just relaxing does nothing so if I can pull Tommy aside and help him make you know three more plays if I can pull Kate aside and help him make another player two I'm going to do that even if I can do it for Will if I can do it for De'Niel like whomever that I see if there's a chance there to to clean something up or make it a little more swift or something like that I'm going to do that I think uh I've had guys pour that into me so to be able to do that and give that back to the game I feel like I'm I'm supposed to do that >> All right guys thank you >> Yep No problem

title: LIVE: HC DeMeco Ryans addresses the media
text: Good afternoon. Is it still morning? Great. >> [laughter] >> Somewhere. All right. >> What were you uh uh uh >> hoping to accomplish at today's practice? Um and and did you like it? Did you like what you saw? >> Today's practice was a outstanding practice for us. So, one of our better practices from just the standpoint of getting the operation down. All right, working on the sideline, being able to get calls in from the sideline, coaches get off the field and let the guys just go play. It's real football. So, we wanted to give the guys a dress rehearsal of what that'll look like on Thursday night, so it's not their first time going through it. >> Are there any particular things that you're looking for tomorrow night that you're going to be like really watching for in this first preseason game? >> The main thing that I look for our first game, our first time out for 2026 is are we displaying our play style? All right, that's the main thing I want to see. No matter who you are, when you touch the field, are you repping the Texans brand? And that's what I want to see guys playing fast, playing relentless, finishing. That's what I want to see. And then you also, when we dive into it into the fine details of it, like who can you count on to execute? All right, when the lights are on in game time, are guys going to be consistent and they're going to take the same approach they've been taking over the past several weeks of how we've been uh prepping the guys, how they've been working. All right, can they go out and perform that under the lights, under a little bit more stress? You know, how how do guys operate at a high level? That's what I'm looking for. >> Coach, with training camp, how have you kind of seen C.J. with his pocket management and stepping up, making plays, and dealing with some of the pressure that the defense puts on him? >> The defense is making it very tough on us offensively, and we know that. We know we're there our offense is up against a challenge every single day going against Will, Danielle on the edges. I thought see I think C.J. has grown from the aspect of being able to you know, really maneuver in the pocket, and not just maneuvering, but it's keeping two hands on the football. It's securing the football. It's stepping up in the pocket and still keeping his eyes downfield, right? Making the proper read, still throwing strikes. Like, that's what's impressive about him. He's He's not getting flustered if things break down. He's still able to maneuver and make those plays on the run that I talked about a couple days ago. >> Because you indicated you're not not a huge fan of of kind of scraps during practice. Is there some value to to having a rookie like Keelan Rutledge who's not afraid to stick his nose in there, even if it's a you know, involving one of the best players in the NFL? >> You better be careful there. Messing with Will Anderson. But no, it's I love it, right? You know, I love the scrappiness of Keelan. I love that his mindset is what I love. He's not backing down from anybody, as he should. I expect that from every player on our team. You know, we're not backing down from anybody. We know we're not physically fighting, but there is always chippiness in our game because it's a tough it's a physical violent game that we play. And there's going to be some chippiness that goes on, but we just have to make sure we're smart, especially in game, right? We have to make sure we're smart and make sure we're not that second guy to cause the team to hurt ourselves. And then coach is going to be really upset. >> When it comes to the game and possibly after it, look at the playing time, how much do you want to see the fact as you mentioned the other day, but as far as like also protecting starters in those early preseason games? >> What's the question? >> How much do you want to make sure that you're resting some of the guys maybe that aren't your first string? >> Well, during the during this game uh against the Chargers, we'll sit out a handful of guys that have been designated to sit out for this game, and the other guys will get a ton of the reps. >> Very competitive practice today. Uh was it due to the fact that you all said, "Okay, so this is a game time situation?" >> I think the guys were a little fired up. >> And I had I to get after them a little bit yesterday. It wasn't our best practice yesterday by any means. That wasn't who we are, how we come out. That wasn't it. So, you know, everybody needed a reminder just of what we're what we're trying to achieve. What are What are we trying to accomplish, right? To do what we're trying to accomplish, it takes persistent work every single day. We can't have let-downs. We can't have setbacks. Like, we have to continue to press forward. We have to count on guys to be relentlessly consistent in what they're doing in their approach every single day. Yesterday, we took a step back. It wasn't good enough. But today, guys responded really well. All three phases did a really great job, right? Making plays, doing what they're supposed to do. So, I'm really proud of the work we put in today, and we're ready to go for game day. >> What does the coach want to see from a running back on the back end of the depth chart as far as making the team? And what have you seen from Noah Whittington as kind of in that battle? >> Noah seems to make a play every day. Uh when he he has a really good feel for, you know, pressing blocks and his vision. Just knowing when to cut, when to take the ball outside, when to you know, make a cut back up inside. Just you feel a guy I see a guy who has plays a really great vision, great feel at the running back spot. So, when you see guys that are lower on the depth chart in these preseason games, some of those running backs are going to shine. They're going to make some nice plays. Noah won't surprise me. Pittsburgh won't surprise me. Those guys have have done it all camp. So, excited to see them play. >> How would you assess the ramp-up in physicality? I know you're always trying to tow that line between intensity and making sure players are staying healthy. But are you pleased with that balance? >> This is probably our best year with that balance of keeping guys healthy, but also playing our style, right? It is a lot of give and take there. Uh but I can never sacrifice the the mindset and the play style that I want to exhibit. When we When we play ball, you want everybody to continue to talk about how physical we are, how relentless. Like, man, how do you Why do your guys run to the ball like they do? How do you guys finish that way? That's our brand. That's who we are as Texans, and we will always represent that. But, the fine line is we have to protect the team. When we're practicing against each other, we are on the same team, no matter how upset guys may get at each other. And it's that point of camp, right, where I'm tired of going against the same guy over and over again. I know his moves. I know everything that he's going to throw at me, and I'm just tired of going at it. So, Thursday's game is coming right on time for us. >> A lot of competition for spots. How is third linebacker shaping up, and what do you hope to see from some of the guys that are trying to get filled in that role? >> We have a lot of great depth at linebacker. Um, it's We have a lot of capable guys who can go out and play our defense for us, but also that that third, fourth linebacker spot, it comes down to special teams, right? And how valuable are those guys being able to play on for our special teams for us. So, it'll be important for those guys in this game to go showcase that. >> It feels like this year, more than in recent years, we've talked about the undrafted free agents, especially the rookies. What have you seen from Travon Saunders, and how he's been impactful? And what do you like about him when he was coming on out? >> Yeah, Travon has done a really nice job of just, you know, being smart, always aligning in the right place. We throw a lot on the receivers when it comes to alignments and motions. I feel like he's handled that really well. Uh, he's fast, explosive guy who He can make some plays with the football in his hands. So, we'll see how he does on tomorrow night. >> David has been, you know, pretty effective pretty much all training camp. How impactful was it to see him make that play today and score that touchdown? >> That was a huge play, huge momentum boost for our offense. Uh, to see David is what he's done a really good job of is his his route running, right? And him and Henry have had a lot of battles so thus far in camp. So, it was cool to see, you know, David make a big play for us and that's the type of player he is. That's why he's here for us. He can spark an offense, right? He can lift us with just making those plays or it's just by him being a leader, being vocal, right? Encouraging the other guys. >> All right, thank you, coach. >> All right, thank you, guys. >> Have a good one. >> You, too. >> Mhm.

title: LIVE: HC DeMeco Ryans, Sheldon Rankins, and Dalton Schultz address the media
text: Mhm. >> What's up, guys? Good morning. Caleb has been progressing really well as a rookie. There was a lot huge learning curve for him, but he's doing a a good job being attentive to what we're asking him to do and you see I see the steps of him towards getting better with this. Mainly just keeping his pad level low. That's what we've been straining him the most is just low man wins in football. He has continued to work that. Very strong very strong kid. So, he just has to play to his strengths and he'll continue to get better. In the first preseason game, I'm really looking for those guys who are on the back end of the roster seeing them go out and and compete for an opportunity to be a part of our team this season. So, to see those guys get as many reps as they can handle, all right, and see who's going to show up on game day. All right, we've installed a lot. We've coached up the fundamentals and techniques. Now, can they go do it, right, when the coaches aren't on the field, nobody's coaching you up after every single play, but can you go out and be a true pro and execute your craft at a high level against different competition? So, that's what I'm looking forward to the most. Yeah, Patterson has done and Patterson's been solid since he's been here. Uh guy who we've counted on to do the center, also moving over to guard. He's played right guard, left guard. Uh he's a smart player who's accountable. He's going to be where he needs to be and he fights. He's a competitive guy and that's why he's stuck around for a while. Clowney is still getting adjusted to how we do things. You see him probably his first day I saw we were doing the two-minute drill the first day and he just had a a one-on-one rush off the edge and I'm standing back there behind the quarterback and he got on me quicker quicker than I expected. So I expect to see that from him. Right, he's he had nine sacks last year. So still very productive late in his career. So I'm encouraged by what I've seen so far and this is first few days of being here. Not having a full off season with us but to come in where he is right now and it's only going to keep getting better. I'm excited to see where he winds up and how our rush group looks on third down. With defensive ends and their stance, standing up, hand in the dirt, it really goes to their comfort level. What's the situation? If it's obvious pass situations, I think you'll see more guys have their can stand up. Right, are they working you know some type of game, some type of stunt? Like do they want to be in the dirt or it's it's From my point of view is completely optional to those guys. Right, I let those guys have the freedom. I never played D-line and rusted passers. So there's a lot of creative freedom there and whatever it takes for those guys to you know be connected and as long as they're working together going through the proper steps that we teach those guys and they can operate it at a at a great pace and do it at the right timing then it works for me. >> with them standing up and I see that Will has that same ability to be able to do it from from both stances. So, I only ask because is that a a defensive thing or like you said, confidence? >> That's a great question. It It's truly, to me, it's about the player being comfortable. Or like when you go to for me, when you talk about stances and all those things, like everybody is different, different body types, like they're different. So, I allow guys that freedom when it comes to rushing the passer or playing linebacker, whatever that is, wherever you're most comfortable is the position I want you to be in. The last thing I want is our guys to be in an uncomfortable position trying to go do something that's extremely hard. >> What's your outlook on this guy in the group specifically following him? What's stood out about what you've seen so far in training camp? >> Marlon's progressed every single day. His trajectory is definitely pointing up. Seeing him in the passing game, seeing him, you know, you guys have seen him make a lot of plays out here in the passing game. He's He's still learning a lot. We're throwing a lot at him, but for a rookie to be, you know, where he is at this point in camp, I'm I'm very encouraged, I'm very pleased with where he is, and I'm excited to see him to continue to to progress. Um, he's done a great job. So, I'm excited at the line of scrimmage, he's done a good job, and also in the passing game. You see a guy, so I mentioned before, he's a he could be a big threat in the passing game. So, he's exciting young player to watch for this year. >> What's made Sheldon right for this guy you wanted in the front of your defense and also in your D-line? >> What sets What sets Sheldon apart is it's above the neck. Like he is one of the smartest D-linemen uh that I've had. And when it comes to us, like how we want to attack protections, right? Or protections change, how can we change our stunts? It's a lot of communication that goes on. I know it's It helps when you got great players, but it also helps when you have a guy, you know, in the middle who can orchestrate it and put it put us in a position that's advantageous to us. And Sheldon helps us when it comes to that. >> I talked to you the other day. Is that battle now settled with Hunter? Is that battle now settled or are we considering bringing in somebody else in here? >> Yeah, we we decided to go with with Kroger right now. He's had a consistent He's done a very very good job being consistent out here in practice and just wanted to get our operation as clean as possible with the same three guys working together, all right, getting us ready to go for the season. A few guys have stood out, but I can't tell the world all my secrets, all right? So, but a few guys have stood out. When it comes to our our rookies, all right, the young guys, there's undrafted rookies that are really making a name for themselves here on the practice field. And those are guys that I'm most excited to see in the game because they've done it, they've been consistent. These guys do a great job of taking care of themselves off the field. So, they've been going every single day, working hard. I'm proud of the work that all of our rookies have put in. Why not? No, for for our for our preseason game against the Chargers, we'll have a select group of guys who will not go out and play. Now, we we were evaluating those group install periods really from a communication standpoint and an assignment standpoint. So, we we get a lot of work pre-practice at a slower tempo working those and we also come back in the evening when you guys are not here. You guys are at home sleeping. We get a lot of work in all right in the in the evening time as well. Just joking. >> [laughter] >> Brevins dealing with a knee right now, so he's he's kind of day-to-day. We'll see how it goes with him. We'll we'll get a lot of live reps when it comes to our competitive periods, our ones going against each other. I try to mix up situations a lot for our guys and kind of put them in stressful positions a lot and also we'll get an opportunity to have two joint practices. And joint practices is where I see you gain a lot of valuable reps going against a different opponent, different schemes, so you get a chance to do a lot of different things there in your joint practices well, but our guys are our coaches walk through a lot with our guys. There's a lot of teaching that goes on behind the scenes at a walk-through pace and we get the full speed reps as well to make sure our guys are ready to go with all of the new things that we're installing. It was very easy talking to coach Kubiak. I think when the schedule came out, I'm sitting in my office and I'm looking at the schedule. I'm talking to my assistant Jake. He's like, "Man, we should the Raiders I know Kubiak will be ready to go and like literally 2 minutes later my phone starts to ring and it's Kubiak. I said, "Hey bro, what you want to practice? Let's go." He's like, "Oh man, this is way easier than I thought it would be." So, it works out works out well. We were both thinking just alike. All right. Thank you guys. Sorry, can you say that say the first part again? How's it look just in general? Yeah. It looks good, dude. We're we're excited. We are we're very much further along than where we usually are. Um so that's allowed us to do some different stuff, work some different stuff that we haven't been able to work in the last year. Um I'm I'm excited about the growth of like a lot of the young guys. Um especially picking up a brand new offense like they're almost falling in line with the guys that are in year two of the system in terms of just picking it up. So yeah. We're we're on a roll. So annoying. No, dude. I I've known Foster for a few years. Um having just another another veteran voice in the room is has helped a lot. Um helps me not feel as you know helps me feel younger. Like it it's weird when you kind of reach year eight, year nine and it's like you look around and you're kind of the old guy in the room. Um so having having Foster to kind of ping pong off of is I think helped us a lot. Um he brings just a great veteran presence but also like you know, a lot of shared experience. You know, whether it's playing each other, playing in the same systems. Um It helps when you've got, you know, not just one voice kind of saying something as a young guy. But having a couple of voices that we are reflecting the same ideas. Um I think that just kind of helps reinforce some of these teaching points in a in a new offense for some young guys. Oh, I'm excited about Demo. I love Demo. I think just the attitude that he brings, the attitude that he runs with. Um you know, being a guy that's, you know, been on the other side, like going against him for a few years, like I'm happy that he's on our side. Um just like again, just another big veteran presence. And I think at the end of the day, like we're all going to feel good handing the ball to to Demo and knowing that he's in the backfield running with the ball in his hand. So, I think anytime you can get a guy like that, especially in the backfield, like that's a workhorse and is a leader, it's good. It's football wise, dude. It's football wise. I don't ever think it's like like a smarter. I think it's just like a calmer. Like the freakout moments, like the one-off looks that nobody talks about, it's like when you kind of been around them and you've seen them and you've been in the big moments with those things happening, it's not so much of a oh, like what are we, you know, it's it's not a freakout moment. Um and I think just that like calmness of understanding, like okay, like I've seen this a handful of times, like I know what to do, I've been through the coaching points, like I've had years under my belt to see stuff like this. Um that always helps and then I think too, just like I've never gotten bored with like understanding that like I still don't know a lot. And like to me, I think that's been you know, more evident the longer that you're kind of in the in the league and you're around some of the some of the coaches and the coaching staff. Um you know, picking DC's brains about why they spin coverage the way that like there's so much more as a player that you know, you realize you're 9 years in that you still have no idea and you know, just kind of getting a glimpse in some of these conversations. I just I love learning. So like I notice those moments more than like the oh, like I've seen this before I got it moments. It's the moments of like oh, wow, like I haven't thought of that or like I didn't ever expect that. Like those moments I think are the kind of unique cool points like as a guy that's a little older older in the league. >> What about the music in the locker room is there like a music difference and are there some days where they like control the aux? Like as as the players get younger and younger is it kind of like you know, what the hell is this? >> Yeah, dude, what's my age again, man? >> I'm always calling for Blink 182. You know, we get one day a week. That's okay. We'll stick to it. But uh yeah, I mean there's a lot of stuff that I haven't heard that's consistent on the radio. I love it. So great. >> What about the locker room and the music and the football? What have you kind of noticed the biggest difference in terms of the people you've played with at that point and at that point in your life and how have you kind of seen that change through the years? Like what's the biggest change you've kind of seen through the years? >> Um I would say defenses are much more like athletic on the second level, especially like linebackers, like even the guys that came before me, like they're always you know, you have your Demeco types where it's just 250 haymakers, like feel the A gap, feel the A gap. Now, I mean you got guys like the rookie Wade who's as big as us, but is also like just as athletic playing like like you know, guys are much more you know, pass game, coverage focused like way more athletic than a lot of the guys that were kind of in the league when I was maybe a rookie. and as far as defense, I mean defense is like they go in trends. Like everybody kind of follows the trends and there's a lot of coverages and fronts that are trendy. but I'd say like you're getting a lot more like in nickel packages and people along that same line of like hey, we're just going to throw a bunch of like athletes out there and say like that we can still match up with the run. When you have a guy like Jaylon Peacher, you probably feel pretty good about leaving nickel out there to a two tight end set saying that you know, Peacher could probably fit the run. So, it's it's stuff like that where it's like maybe a little bit lighter, allows you to do a little bit more, and allows you to present different you know, different front structures, different coverage structures and and keep everything kind of blanketed. >> I apologize for a little bit making it in. Where where do you think the offense has made the biggest step forward in this year you guys headed into the first season? >> Man, there's so many. Um I think like along my same lines of like feeling like more calm as like the years go on. Like I would say that we've kind of fallen into just like a level of like, all right, heard the play call, we're good. Like I think the communication has been so much better than it's been and I think, you know, Pop has done a great job kind of drilling that into the line like you get up there, the front's declared, the Mike's declared, you know, we're re-IDing the Mike properly. It's like to be able to to run an offense like consistently well over and over, you have to be able to communicate and defensively too. Um, but I think just kind of like getting up to the ball and having that declared immediately as I helped get a lot of guys in the right spots cuz half the time do that's the hardest part when you have guys playing nickel defenses to to 12 personnel but you're only to your yours only supposed to block backers well it can get a little confusing at times like so I think just that level of communication especially from young guys like Kaelin up there being able to like ID a front make a mic backer and roll it's been huge. Um, I don't know if that plays into it. Like maybe it does, maybe it doesn't to me it's more about like you look at what you've done on the field. Like we have a lot of guys that have made big time plays and big time moments and have a lot of like good football under their career belts and I think when you have a locker room with a with this level of you know, that the standard just kind of gets higher and higher. Um, so I don't I don't know if that plays as much but when you have a bunch of guys that have have done it well for a long time for sure. You say the same offense back and turn Yeah, no there's there's there's continuity but at the same time there's a lot of like growth in that continuity and especially like I mentioned a lot of the young guys stepping in and being able to get that like there's a lot of growth to those guys to kind of get up to speed and so it doesn't feel like there's any newness. And it feels like there's continuity even though you might have three new guys. You know what I mean? So, it's like it does feel like there's that without actually, you know, on paper like, "Oh, it's the same guys." Dear brother, I wish I could give you like an accurate number because I think for my first 2 years I didn't know what the hell was going on in terms of like coverage. Yeah, like dude, I look at everybody like, "That's cover two. It's cover three." Would I Would I know the difference between palms and two and three match and fire zone and three like three hook I didn't know. I didn't know my ass from my elbow. So, I mean there was a ton of like growth process for me and I was very lucky to have vets in the room that were able to like you know, talk to me about stuff like that and I had a coach that was he was our tight ends coach but he was an offensive mind. Like he was a quarterback coach at heart. So, like he was teaching through the lens of like pass game and coverage and where you should be. So, like I came in not knowing a whole lot of that stuff. And I learned like everything in my first 2 years just about that. And then from there I was able to build out kind of a foundation. So, I I wish I could tell you like it's grown or or hasn't. Truth be told like I couldn't tell you, brother. Then the the switch coverage? Yeah. Yes. Yes. Show you one thing, flip another. There's a lot of guys that like will do that you know, opposite of their scouting reports. D- DCs that are like, "All right, we've played Tampa 2 in this this game, we're just going to literally play the opposite for those stat differences. And be like, "Well, you can't say we do it all the time." So, it's it's part of the game. It's part of the chess match. Like, as a player, you just got to be aware that that might show up. So, I I mean, we went out and we worked out prior to OTAs, and I think like I mean talking to him like after the season, like you could tell, but like when I really saw him and saw like the shape that he was in, like how much he'd been working, like just that level of focus. I think it was yeah, pre pre-OTAs. So, I think when you're able to do that, February, March, April, coming in April, and like continue to build off that, it's dangerous. And I'm I'm excited to see, you know, him continue to put it together through this camp. Appreciate it. What up? What up? What up? How y'all doing? Uh just the little nuances. I think um when you get so much thrown at you uh as a young guy, um completely different defense than he's ever played in. Um it's it's being it's made, you know, it's knowledge that we're counting on him, you know, that that the the pressure that I'm sure he puts on himself to be perfect every day. a lot of things can get lost in translation, whether it's um alignment, whether it's hands, whether it's um you know, pad level on bull rushes or being able to skate blocks at this level, how different it is than, you know, college. Um so for me it's just pulling him aside and being able to being able to articulate a lot of those things. Um in a way that that uh that is slowed down um so he can work through those things at a slowed pace. You know, it's about I always talk to the inside guys about beating blocks. So I think you know for us inside make a team to be disruptive continue to beat blocks and continue to to to collapse pockets be disruptive in the run game and allow those specimens on the edge to to to do what they do. It man it's great. I think it uh you know it it it in a way continues to drive guys like myself like obviously getting older but you know you still see a guy who's a little bit older than myself and continue to still do it at a high level. You know it's great to add you know I think you know one thing he probably doesn't get as much credit for is his his footwork. You know he's already in the meeting rooms talking about things he sees as much film as he studies and being able to bounce that knowledge off myself Will DeMarcus other young guys in the room it's been great and then obviously once he takes the field I mean you see why he was you know the the number one overall pick and and no matter what jersey he puts on he's a highlight reel waiting to happen. Uh that's a great question actually. I think it's probably a multitude of things some personal some team wise I think uh team wise I just think um being a part of something special you don't take it for granted going into your 11. I think I was talking to somebody about this off season like this team has a very college feel to it. Like with how close everyone is and uh the inside jokes and how how much we clown each other and how much you can clown your brother, but it's not taken personal. Like, you know, it's it's it's that type of feel. Um and that's hard to find in the NFL. That's that's really hard to find, you know, because of the business uh of it and everybody's generally out for themselves, but I mean, this is a team that genuinely cares about each and every man uh being successful as a player and as a person. Um and that shows in the way we we play on defense, on offense, special teams. Um that shows it in the way we cheer each other on. That shows in the way we um congregate outside of the meeting rooms and in the field. You know, so. >> Sorry, last one. Along those same lines talked to Kade McDonald now. And I talked to Tommy Togiai about how much perfectionist one, but you teach me you're always teaching, you're always all the while while you're learning. You shied away from saying after this is all over with you're going to be a coach. But you But you see even on the sidelines you're watching, you're still teaching. And you know, we'll cross that bridge when I get there. Uh but yeah, I think um I think I would be doing the game a disservice. I think I'd be doing myself a disservice if I didn't um impart all the wisdom that I have uh onto, you know, my teammates. I think beautiful thing is I I kind of understand I understand what it's supposed to look like. But I also understand what it's supposed to look like if you're undersized. I also understand You know, so I think I have the uh the ability to uh make it relatable to whatever the body type is, whatever whatever the the the um the skill set is. Um so that's why you see me do that. I I just I I understand that, you know, when when it's over uh me just having all this wisdom and going home and just relaxing does nothing. I think uh I've had guys pour that into me, so to be able to do that and give that back to the game, uh I feel like I'm I'm supposed to do that. >> All right, guys. Thank you. >> Yep. >> Good luck. >> No problem.
