So, you're going to get challenged on the edges and hand placement. You better get your hands inside, Marlon, and he's done a better job of that. He has. But I'm just using him as an example and and any other person could be our tackles, could be Keelan. It doesn't really matter. The everything's happening faster. Um you better be ready to use the release at the line of scrimmage and use your hands or your che- you're going to have hands in your chest. And so, all the speed, the violence, the the the chemistry that they they play with on that side of the ball, it challenges us every day. And it challenges us as an offense, which makes us better. I and and helps us refine things and helps us try to make things better from a a schematic standpoint as well. And and certainly trying to move guys around and put them in position, to answer your question. I I couldn't I'm sorry, I couldn't hear the Well, you earn the opportunity to play. And and consistent performance, that's what we're looking the most consistent guys that are dependable to perform. And and this, to be fair to what your question, this is the opportunity that you have to be able to display that from taking it from the meeting room to the field. So, the answer is yes, you want to have an opportunity out here to do that, to be able to move the needle. I think like last year, Jo War was a great example, right? We saw a consistent guy in training camp that had a great feel for the running game, that could set blocks, that just was steady and consistent. And and throughout the course of the year, it just kept getting better and better. And then he has an opportunity and he makes the most of it. And the way you practice, generally speaking, is the way you're usually going to perform on the field. And you And it's not always the case, but this is the truest indicator. You know, you're not going to practice bad 80% of time and go out and excel against Will Anderson's and all these players. It just doesn't work that way. Yep. Yeah, I think >> I think it's a couple things, Cody. I think first and foremost, it's get it's two-step quickness in the run game and tight hands. Like our guys are getting off the rock and you better be ready to get your get your hands tight and you better be ready to get your feet in the ground to get power on your second step. They've done a great job. Like Marlins gotten so much I mean he's had multiple blocks I've seen. Great Kades made a ton of improve Fosters and they're all they're all growing, honestly. I'm I'm really pleased. James Farents has done a great job with those guys. The second thing is route runners. Like you're going to be slow of speed. Like you're not going to have an advantage most of the time against safeties in this league. That's the reality. But what you do have is you have a size advantage. May not have a speed advantage, you have a size advantage. So learning how to work edges and not run through the middle of people. Learning how to use your size as an advantage to be able to create separation at the top of the routes. Some guys are gifted and can run away from dudes. Most I would say are going to have to play with technique. So the constant refinement of that against a really good secondary we get one-on-ones which is awesome. Um but it's it's it's all of that and that's a position obviously I I probably do have some natural biases but you're at the point of attack every play just about. You don't hide at tight end. Not in our offense like you don't. And so you know you're there's a lot asked. Protection, we put them in the back field, we put them at the end of the line, they chip, they do a lot of other things. So I would say it's a lot of things but it's really playing good fundamentals and getting your technique faster than the guy across from you. Whether that's in the pass game or in the run game. >> I see Jonathan Mingo have a lot of comments in the wide receiver room. >> Yep. >> What's the process of figuring out how to best utilize Jonathan Mingo? >> Yeah, I think just continue to bring him along and just continue to have exposures to to our route tree, to our different schemes in the past concepts that we have. And he's been he's been studying like crazy now for the last year. Like he's been he's been involved but it's different when now when he's out here, you know, he's soaking up more and more and I I just taking it day by day and just being able to build off of it. Not not having any expectations other than just continuing to grow and continuing to learn and soak up the details and then getting some real speed out here, too, is great. Especially the timing with the quarterbacks and stuff like that. Yeah, you know, he was he's on his Everybody's on their own program, so he's on his own program relative to that, but he's he's gotten a lot better. And I did see I think that I think you saw Jeudy when I talked about last year, when he got his ops, we saw what happened in practice manifest itself in the game. And I did think he hit this offseason with some confidence. And I And he's he's a He doesn't say a whole lot. He's steady as heck, but you're seeing a guy that's pretty confident, and he's done a really good job out here for us. So I certainly think the more you play, I mean, you get you're you're chomping at the bit to get more, and he's got he's wired the right way, for sure. Cool. Thank you, guys. Feels great.

title: LIVE: HC DeMeco Ryans, Tank Dell, and Danielle Hunter address the media
text: What's up? Full house today. Where y'all been? >> [laughter] >> All right. It's great seeing Jay Noll back out on the field. He's been working hard at it all all off season, so it's good to have him back out doing football with us. With CJ, what I'm seeing show up is just a guy who's confident in what he's doing. Like, that's how everything looks better because he's again it's year two in a system. So, anytime you're doing something for the second time around, you're more comfortable with it. Come training camp, we're able to install and add volume to our offense more so than we were able to do the first year and rightfully so. All right, everybody's just getting started. It's new, it's fresh, trying to see what everybody does well. But, CJ's done a great job of taking ownership of the offense, all right, really communicating to his guys, getting everybody on the same page, and you're seeing a confident player. Tank, he looks really nice out there. All right, you see him you know, being explosive. It's good to see him in routes on air, individual drills. He's getting back in the swing of not doing things on the side. It gets lonely when you're in, you know, the return to football program and you're just off to the side working with the trainers. Now, to get back in with your guys and actually do football things with football guys, it's a it's really that that big first step into the, you know, progression of getting back on the field. And so, we're taking taking our time with Tank, allowing him to come along uh as he needs to in his in his time. But, he's doing a outstanding job with it. He looked really nice today, nice and crisp running his routes. So, it's exciting anytime you see Tank on the field. Cuz everybody understands Tank's personality, like his joy and love for football, you want to see that comeback story you know, come to life. And we're excited to see whenever that happens. We're all going to be uh very joyful for him. Taylor has a chance. It's year two. It's the again, like like I said about CJ, it's just getting more comfortable with what we're asking him to do and what will be the defined role for him. How do we carve out that role to where he's doing that one thing and doing it really well. I thought he did a great job when we asked him to go back and return last year. Made some really nice productive returns for us in the punt return game. So, I'm excited to see him to continue to build on his punt return and also finding that role on offense. Like, how can we find a way to get the ball in his hands uh multiple times a game? Jerry Wayne is showing up every time he's on the field. He's always making plays, not just, you know, this camp. He's made plays since he's been here. Uh big tall target, smart guy. He can move around. He plays all three wide receiver positions. So, a guy that we can count on and he's he shows up making a lot of big plays down the field, a lot of contested catches. He finds a way to come down with the ball. Our team is doing a really nice job and what you look for in camp, for me, I talk about it, you look for that competitive nature. Like, back and forth, both sides making plays and that's what we see every day. You know, someone is making a big play, right? And if someone makes a bad play, nobody is down about it. It's okay, how do we come back? How do we respond in a positive manner with that next play mentality? That's how our guys are responding. So, it's been great going against each other. I think it's starting to get to that time where it's time to, you know, play a game against someone else. But, our guys they've done a great job all camp. With the undrafted free agents, you know, it's it's a tough hill to climb for those guys, all right? To get out on the field. And the thing for those guys is is getting those game reps in preseason. That's where you get to see the most of those guys. Here, we get a lot of reps with our first and second unit, so they don't see a ton of reps, but they'll get their action in the game. So, excited to see who shows up come game time. Preseason always important. Every year is important. It's a time for us to go out and get live reps. You can't shortchange. Like how do you get better at playing ball? You got to go do it in a live setting. No coaches on the field, nobody barking at you. You just got to go out and see who can play with the calm mind, who can respond and react the proper way when things are thrown at them a little different. They see a different scheme. Who can make those proper adjustments and still make plays without blinking? So, that's what the games are all about. So, we'll get to see that come next Thursday. It was important for us to sign Henry because he's a trustworthy and a consistent player. And then, a guy, you know, we drafted him my first year here and guy who's just gotten better every single year. So, Henry's very deserving of the contract that he's received. I remember just I remember Henry's rookie year being out here in training camp and no matter what I threw at him, he was always he kept signing with every rep. It's like, man, this rookie may be starting for us, right? Because he just he did things the right way. He did the things how I asked him to do it and you know, I saw right then that this would be a really good player for us. So, And he's from a really good school, right? Yeah, not his first school, but his second school. Yeah, really good school. Now, I'm I'm proud of Henry. I'm proud of him, man, and just to watch him in camp. Yeah, I talked spoke about this the other day, watching how he's so intentional, right, on getting better at the little things. Like every rep you make come over, "Hey coach, you saw I just got to keep my feet moving." He's he's coming to me, but he's coaching me up on the correction himself. Like that's that's a true pro and I love every bit of it. He's getting much better. He's uh improving his his man coverage, getting some good reps against D Mo and Woody. And he's doing an outstanding job. Look for his game to really take off this year. >> You talked about him coming from a good school, good program. The second one before you had that an advantage to be able to watch it a little bit more of that. But when you're evaluating some of these guys that are coming in that you all either drafted or undrafted players, how are you able to evaluate them based off of gifted I mean with them coming from different programs and different systems and just a fundamental standpoint? >> I I evaluate everyone equally. I was you know, it's uh when we get guys, at first it starts with our scouting department. Like those guys do such an exceptional job to where it makes my job easier. It's it's very easy when they say a player is this, is he's a he does this really well, that's what it's going to be. So I don't have to have any like second looks or have a second judgment on what those guys present to me. They know the type of players we're looking for. They bring them in and we coach them up the right way. And they know the style of guys we're looking for. So whatever however they get on our team, whether it's undrafted rookie or they're first round pick, I evaluate by what you do on the grass. All right, when you get here, how you how you show up every single day and how do you get better? That's how I evaluate guys. How are you taking coaching? Like how are you not making the same mistake over and over again, right? How are you truly excelling? That's how I evaluate guys and everybody, you know, they'll make a name for themselves just by showing up and being consistent every day. I'm sorry, who you say? >> I'm talking about Brevin Jordan. How you bringing him along this year >> Yeah, Brevin had a you know, he really had a good start to camp. He's still progressing along. We're still trying to take care of him the right way, but Brevin's done a really good job. Don't look at both guys the same. Each guy, you know, I think for Henry, as I really dive in on what he's doing for himself, like everybody you understand what are your strengths and weaknesses are as a player, right? And you work on the weaknesses more than you work on the strengths, and that's where his focus is, and that's where he needs to improve his game, and that's I saw him do it intentionally on his tackling. Like last 2 years ago, he was intentional about getting better at tackling starting at training camp, and it showed throughout this past season. So, the same way he wants to emphasize that, we'll see improvements of it come season. Whoever's out there at receiver, we're going to we're going to be good. As long as the quarterback puts it where it needs to be, we got a lot of capable guys who can go play at receiver. Yeah, Nico, we're everybody again at I can't come in and give you guys everybody's schedule, but everybody's on a different plan. Practice is one part of it, right? The meeting rooms is is more than just, you know, making plays on the practice field, right? Guys have to be able to show up in multiple areas, right? It's a culmination of a lot of different things that shows up to you being on the roster, making plays on game day. So, it's a process and we'll see how it continues to work itself out. When it comes to CJ moving, I think he's always had that capability, uh but I don't think he's faster. If he is, that's a great thing for us all, but I think it just goes back to me for decision-making. Like, are you making the right decision? If it's not there, or not being in a position of where you feel like you have to force something that's not there. And understanding like when you do use your legs, there's there's a ton of power in using your legs, and that's what the the trend in the NFL has taken off with athletic quarterbacks who can move around, escape the pocket, doing more keepers, doing more things on the outside lanes in the passing game. It's really allowed a lot of athletic quarterbacks to be successful in the passing game. We're taking a step back from the true traditional pocket passers. You got athletic guys who can move, making it very tough on the defenses now. That's the unique thing with CJ. CJ can be that traditional pocket passer. He's very accurate, pinpoint placement whatever he wants to put the football, but then he also has the capability of escaping, and that's what makes him a really, you know, really successful young quarterback, and he's still growing, still has room to improve, but he can do it all, and that's what makes him truly unique. Thank you, guys. Yeah, man. It's nothing short of a blessing, you know, um that's just a testament to all the work that I put in with the staff on my own and God first, so you know, it's great. >> Can you kind of take us uh through that process of during your rehab and your comeback? Every There's going to be certain stages in which you have to kind of test yourself, right? Like maybe how much you can uh put on, you know, put on the knee, how explosive you can be and stuff like that. How was that process like when you hit those milestones? You kind of mentioned before that you physically were kind of got to put yourself to the test. >> Um I'll say mentally, it's just about trusting trusting that the work you put in like prior to going out there to do those things like prior to going out there to put your foot in the ground, trusting the process with the um training staff and what they had set out for me, so when I got out here, I wasn't scared, you know, and I was talking to my doctor, Dr. Lowe, and I was just asking like he was just telling me let loose like and trust it and be you cuz it's 100% stable, so when he told me that, I just came out and was putting my foot in the ground. I didn't care about it, trying not to think about it cuz doing your process like the mental aspect of it is like the hardest thing you got to get over, so if I went out there like iffy about what I'm doing then I probably would never be able to come back to what I want to be, so I was just out there just trusting it, putting my foot in the ground, trying to be explosive, and um it's working in my favor, so. Nah, faith faith and trust is what I started with with God, you know, putting all my trust and my faith in him and my belief to get back here like um man, like when I got hurt, I wrote the goal down to just be be better than what I left off. Be better than what I left off that Chiefs game. When I come back, I want to come back not like oh, it's going to be the same. I want to come back better than what I was. So, that was never like a question in my head. Um And the thing I said was um when God want to build you up, he don't bring you comfort. So, he he put you through a storm. So, when I was in a storm, I just had my trust in him um knowing that I'd get back to where I want to be and just every every day getting 1% better, you know, working hard. Yeah, doing that. It'll It'll play out how it's supposed to, you know, um we're going to take we're going to take steps to get where I want to go, but how I vision myself, man, I you know how I come, man. I'm trying to I'm trying to make plays. I'm trying to be a big factor on the team. Um I know I am. I know I will be. Just trusting in it going out there and letting loose. So, God, you know, trusting trusting God. Trusting his favor, trusting everything that he has set out for me, you know, his plans can't be denied. Um so, that's all it was. Just trusting trusting my process, trusting God, and I had a wonderful coaching staff and organization from top down from Hannah and um Cal to Nick Demiko and the whole training room um Roll, Drugs, everyone, man. I had a a plan and and they was behind me 100%. They told me like take the time you need. We're going to be with you 100 like the whole time. And it just worked. So, I was a junkyard dog, man. I was just working all day. Um a lot of y'all didn't see the work that I put in. I know y'all didn't see it, but every day I was working, man. Every day. It wasn't one day that went by. On a Sunday I was working. It wasn't one day that went by that I wasn't out there or inside doing something to get better that day. And now I'm here, you know. >> You take take all these steps to this point. And now, like you said in the summer, did you see the light at the end of the tunnel? What does it look like for you this season ideally? When do you hope to get out there, be able to do more, and play in a game again? >> Yeah, right now we just taking it one day at a time. Um like I said, it's light at the end of the tunnel for sure. I'll be out there, but we're just taking it one day at a time. So, that's all we doing. >> There's a lot of talk about the system. Is that part of the work as well? How comfortable are you in the system? The offensive system. >> As far as like knowing my plays? >> Yeah, knowing the plays. Is that something that you feel like you have to get some repetition before you step on >> I feel like anything you do in life you going to have to get reps at it. Um so, but as far as knowing my plays, I'm a student of the game. So, every day like I'm in there walk-throughs. Um I know y'all know in OTAs I was doing like walk-throughs. They was implement implement implement Damn. Yes, to the offense. So, I was doing walk-throughs and stuff like that. And on my own, you know, I have like my brothers at home call the play out and I just walk through it on my own. And so, being a student of the game, that's easy for me because I love it. So, I would just taking the time by myself to, you know, learn the offense. So, it's cool. >> Take a Tae, you were the player where you got hurt. >> Jared Goff and I pretty much in the same position in the back of the back of the end zone. >> What was that conversation like? Have you had a conversation with Jared Goff? Because a lot got blamed on him for you getting injured. And he took a lot of the blame for it. He took a lot of criticism for it. What was that conversation like with you two? >> Yeah, um he wrote me like he wrote me like right after it happened but I wasn't on my phone like that so I ain't really say but then when I got back to him, you know, I told him like ease up, yo, like it's football. You know, and I know it was a genuine mistake. Nobody want to take out their own guy, not even another guy like to that. So It was a mistake. I told him, man, it's good. God got me like ease up, man. Go play go have fun play football. I'll be back. So it was cool, you know, and it's no hard feelings. That's my brother so we cool. >> What was the biggest moment or milestone in your recovery? >> Say that again? Who encouraged you again? >> Uh probably touching grass for the first time. When I first started back touching grass, it was It's a great milestone cuz people thought I would never be back to where I am right now. So just going out there and putting my cleats on and tying them back up. >> Sorry. >> It's all right. >> I know that you and CJ have been really close. He's talked a lot of us about, you know, the wonderful guy that he is. What is he meant to you in this long journey? >> Everything, man. This long process, he was with me the whole time from the first day it happened to today like long conversations. I go to his house, he come to my house like long conversations about the future that we want to build with each other on on the field and stuff like that but off the field, bro, just being a brother to me like um sending me scripture, praying for me just hanging out with me, you know, having fun so us off the court during our off season like I was with him a lot so it's the same like that's my brother like to the end with or without football so like you know how that goes so he was with me the whole time. >> Do you think you'll be ready for week one? And >> Yeah, sorry. We're going to take it day by day, baby. Day by day, you heard me? >> And then taking off the field for a second, another draft brother here. I know how close you are with CJ. I know how close you are with Nico but you have a little brother who looks up to you a lot. What was What was it like going through the process, you know, knowing that he is one of your biggest supporters? >> Yeah, that was like that was like my little mate around the house when I couldn't walk for a little bit. Like he was like if I like if I go to walk down the stairs, he'll be by me like trying to hold me and stuff. Like he was like, "Go get a water for me, bro." He'll go run to the back I'm going to run to the kitchen and get a water. So, that was my That's my guy, man. Um he a spitting image of me. He love the game. Um he love to learn. He love to go out there and play football on his own. With my brothers, they be in the house throwing a ball and I'll be telling them not to, but you know, he he love it and he love me. So, he was just with me the whole time, man. Uh he shed tears with me. You know, he was on my side every step of the way. When I get back when I was working out in the back, he he in the back trying to work out with me. So, you know how that goes. So, Um yeah, like I said, when when God put you through something, when he want to build you up, he put you through a storm. So, the patience, man, it was hard. You know, being out a whole year, I never in my life sat out of football for a whole year. So, it was so hard to like at first, but then at a at a certain point you got to like accept it for what it is and just get to work. So, it was it was a long journey, but I was patient enough and it's getting close. So, Yeah, I'm going to write back to you on that one. I I of course, man, since I was in college and high school, I used to write in my notes, but since college, I have sticky notes and put them on my mirror so I wake up and see them every day, but of course I got my goals, you know, I ain't going to write I ain't going to tell you now. I'm going to write back with you, but I got a lot of them, man, I'm on I'm chasing them. So, I was dead tired. >> Yeah. It looked like it it was real bro, you stopped. >> and you consciously and stopped and kind of bounced around for 7 seconds, man. But what were you kind of thinking? What was that kind of a special moment for you to to be back in in that setting? >> Yeah, it was it was I I really wasn't I really wasn't thinking like that. I was thinking like am I going to go out here and practice or go work out with gloves cuz I didn't want to go back over there. But man, I just wanted to I just thought like damn, I need to make a decision. But it was just something funny that I did. >> Last one, John. My question to you, you and the young man from Florida also here in Texas, do you have a message for all the blue chip top 100 guys out here as they get ready to start off their football season? >> Um yeah, um first and foremost, keep God first, but don't let anyone tell you what you can or can't do. You put your your mind to it and your head on straight and you focus on what you need to focus on and your goals, you can get anything you want in this life. On the field, off the field, um whatever you want to do, man. You put your your your eyes set on your goals, you can go get it. So, just keep working hard, trust God, and yeah. That's all. >> I think it's going to be fun cuz um you know, that's a lot of experience. A lot of guys that know what they're doing. And the biggest thing is just we just want to learn off each other. So, I And Clowning came in a few days ago and the first thing he was saying that how he wanted to like he's been watching me and he wants to learn new moves from me and Will and all and then the first day he practiced, I mean literally got a sack on the first play. So I mean I think it's going to be very fun with the kind of pass rush moves that we have all all three of us in the entire room. Oh, he's came McDonald he's came he's coming along well. He's going out there executing the game plan, buying into the brotherhood and he's buying into what we teach on defense with coach Demeco teaches us and the biggest thing is just we hold a standard on the D-line and he's starting to understand that every day you just got to keep up with that standard and doing your part. Oh, yeah. Vice versa. I mean he came in the league before me and I've seen what he was capable of. I've seen all his moves and all he's done. He's teaching me stuff and I'm teaching him stuff. So I feel like that's very beneficial for our defensive line. I think his quickness, you know. That's what we like on this defense, quickness and the power that he has being able to get off the rock and just rush the passer and being able to play the run with the kind of explosiveness that explosiveness that he has. I feel like it's going to be a major plus for us. I'm not too much on that side but whenever I do go over there, I mean they do a pretty good job of protecting the quarterback, you know. Big improvement from last year of where they needed to set and everything. So but for as far as I can see they've been doing pretty good over there. As Clowny continues to evolve and continues to get better this year >> Yeah, I feel like this this one of the biggest things of being a veteran. You can never get complacent. You always want to evolve because everybody is studying whatever you last did and trying to figure out ways how to stop you. So, the biggest thing that I try to teach all the guys in the D-line room is to always adapt cuz what you did last year, everybody is trying to figure out how to stop that. So, you always going to figure out new ways how to do your job and getting better and better as a Uh I I think it's pretty fun because the biggest thing about football is you always got to stay uncomfortable. If you're comfortable, that means you're not doing anything right. always be comfortable with being uncomfortable. Uh from my perspective, the biggest thing I do is I always start from the beginning. I always start from the little things, you know, the basics, the fundamentals and then once I keep evolving, once I keep going through those day-by-day steps, um the biggest thing is to focus on what my part is and what I got to do for the team, what I got to do for the defense and just basically just buying into the defense, what DeMeco teaches us. You know, um doing your part cuz once we all do our part, we know how we play. So. Yeah, we we love that, man. That's the biggest thing. O-linemen, they're supposed to be like that. Supposed to come in mean and aggressive and all that. So, we we love everything we've seen from him so far. So, the biggest thing for him is just being able to build up and get game experience, and he's going to be pretty solid. >> A lot of players on the offensive line are telling me that, you know, what you all accomplished last year was last year. Get all that and, you know, come in fresh and and improve on that. How much do you take from that loss to the New England Patriots in the division? How much did that play back in your mind? I don't know that to push you this season to get better. >> I mean, like everybody's been saying, last year's last year. I mean, we know where we we were, and we know where we need to be. So, the biggest thing is just keep on building and starting from the beginning and knowing what we need to do this year in order to get over that hump. >> You're a number 12 for you, right? >> Uh 12. >> You're 12. You're 12. How do you keep yourself in such great shape? >> I mean, I feel like the biggest thing is just uh just diet and just taking care of my body and being around the right people. Uh I feel like just some simple things like that. Staying out of trouble. It's about it. >> He was saying you have to spend a lot of money on your Not you per se, but he was saying that you have to spend a lot of money on your body if you want to play in this league. Is that true? >> Yeah, to an extent that's true. Yeah, to an extent. >> In terms of Geron Christian, what do you see in from him in his second season? How can you help him continue to grow on the path where he was going? >> Uh I've seen major improvement, you know, as a guy coming into his second year. Man, he has tremendous feet. That's first of all. I mean, like he's a guy where he has great power, great vision, great feet. Um you could definitely see a big jump from last year to what he's being able to bring to this training camp. And I think the relationship and the collaboration between himself and offense coordinator Nick Kaylee is better. And if Kayle's a better play caller with this personnel that they've invested in, maybe this offense could be a, you know, top 15 offense. And I think that's all they have to be to make a real deep layoff run. I was going to say when you look at the potential of this offense, they're always tweaking things and I spoke a little bit with Nick Kaylee and man all throughout this off season, he's d he's trying to find new things they can do offensively. How exciting is that knowing if they can get healthy pieces out there. They've got obviously a run game now that can open some things up. >> Oh man, it's terrifyingly exciting because last year there was games where you get to the end of the game, you're like, has he run out of plays in the playbook? Um, and so if there's two things that feel like they help that. One, there's a full complement of tight ends. In fact, maybe too many tight ends, which Nick Kaye having a tight end background, you can tell that his offense requires that to reach its full potential. Plus, you've heard it from a lot of different guys. They just have more plays that they've seen early on, which gives you more to pick from. All right. It's like having a bigger menu. You go into the Cheesecake Factory, you see all the different options. Now, we have opportunities to be satisfied with our selections come game day, and I think that that's going to help them as well. >> That bag is deep. But I think there's a lot >> I've got a hunch too that some of the plays there's some secret plays that they run in the bubble that we don't see because I always get this question. Where's the 13 personnel, the three tight ends? Where's the 12? It's there. We don't see the two zero personnel bunch with the two split backs. We haven't seen that, but he promised there would happen. I think they can be more creative with this bunch. And I'm liking what I'm seeing from Marlon Klein. I think this guy could be a weapon. Looks like a really good athlete. I know he's a little raw. He's a German import, Michigan man. Good story, but heck of a story and pretty good athlete. Good raw material to work with. >> So, you got Montgomery and Woody Marks. We can go on and on. We could talk two hours about Texas tonight, but but you look at this position. I love watching the running backs do their thing when I'm out there at practice as well. And just imagine regular season football, how much damage these guys can do together in different roles. They all have their strengths, but having that tandem, I think it's going to be big for the backfield. Yeah, I don't have any concerns when it comes to the running back core at all. It feels like they have consistent dudes that can do the job incredibly well. The question I have in the run game actually comes with the offensive line, which >> good point. >> How many of us have had questions about the offensive line? I think we'd all raise our hands. It's can they create the space? Can they create the gaps for those guys who are very good at finding those fates and running through it? right now, at least versus this defense, they haven't popped as many as you would want, but they also haven't like had tackles for losses and being blown up in the back field as much. So, in the same way we're talking about the offense in general, it's better than it was. I think there's room for improvement, which I guess is still okay, >> but it always starts up front. No doubt. >> And Saturday night, it went backwards a bit. Henry Toto and all these guys getting tackles for losses and zero gains for David McGomery. The guy that made a little bit of noise was Noah Whittington. And now he'll get more playing time because Jawar Jordan's out for about a week with a strained hip flexor. But I really look at the backs and I think there's going to be some division of labor where you're going to see mostly Montgomery and they're definitely going to have carved out a role for Woody Marks. I expect these guys to combine and they will not be one of the worst running games. I think they're going to be in the top half this year. >> Got a lot of battles going on too that are fun to watch. Keep an eye on. You guys were talking before the before the show. We were talking about what we had hit on tonight. You look at the linebacking situation, you got some studs, but you got some slots there that that are open in this race. LB3 is one of them. Uh this is fun. This is what I love about the competition of course during the course of a training camp. >> Well, 100%. And for me, this one is very intriguing because it comes on the defense where they have seemingly patched up any possible hole an opposing offense can get to. That linebacker three is the one where I go, how does that look? because Ryan likes a base defense with three linebackers where they can get real physical at times. EJ speed and you knew that he could do the job. Right now, it's a whole bunch of guys that in theory can do the job, but none of them has separated themselves. It's one of the reasons why I'm really excited for Thursday in the first preseason game versus the Chargers. >> I think the inside track goes to Marte Map and I thought Matt Burke gave away a few clues about a week ago. Some of his comments sounded like he favors Mapu. Wade Woodz may be heard from in this competition showing some physicality, a little feistiness last night, but in my opinion, Mapu because of pass coverage, converted safety, former Patriots guy, I kind of feel like they would throw Mapu out there first if the season began today. I also think with no EJ speed, third linebacker snaps are going to go down. It's going to be a lot of 425 alignments. >> Well, I meant to ask you guys too, Keen Rutled, how do you think he has looked so far in camp? you see all the reports and I mean he's he's getting the job done out there. >> Yeah, without question. Honestly, it feels weird to start with something that I'm not seeing from him as opposed to the things that I am, but I'm not seeing him fumble the snap and that seems insignificant, but it's not. He has not played the center position and snapping the football. Very crucial to that. So, he's done that very well. In fact, on our show, he told us that uh his wife has been catching some of those snaps from him. So, that's how he's getting the uh some of the mechanics. She does. I feel like if you end up in a place where all three of your quarterbacks go down, we call the Rutled household and we we see if we can get your fourth quarterback there. But jokes aside, like he's delivered in every way that you want. In fact, they talk about it. He looks like the guy that you saw on film from Georgia Tech, which is a gritty, nasty guy that's going to hold the line when it comes to his physicality, but also he came in on his first day here, his introductory press conference, and said, "I'm going to hold guys accountable." That's crazy to hear from a rookie, but he's doing it already there on the training camp field, >> right? and the way he plays through the echo of the whistle, intense, feisty, like you say, gritty. I watch this guy and I think he can be an intimidating type of center, like a linder bomb. And you watch those kind of guys, they get paid a lot of money eventually. To me, this guy will be a second and third contract guy here with the Texans. We're watching a cornerstone player. His really early moments as he's establishing himself in the NFL. I think he's eventually be the gold standard at center. We've been at a lot of these practices. Punting has gotten some attention or or should I say lack of punting. Uh that's surprisingly an issue right now. They've got to lock something down. They got time to figure it out. But that's been kind of a surprise. >> Yeah. When you look at what happened here, so they just cut Jack Stonehouse, the rookie, who had a stronger leg than Kai Krueger, but not as good at holding. And they told us that he would be the best holder that probably would get the job. He is the best holder, but he's not the weakest, you know, he's in a weaker leg. You watch the directional punting. That's okay. They tried out some punters, Jack Browning and Trenton Gil. They didn't sign either. And I think what they're trying to do now is build up his confidence and build up the kicking operation confidence. And we'll see how it goes. But Krueger wasn't very good for the New Orleans Saints last year. It's got to get better. Otherwise, they're going to have another gong show try out and Krueger is going to have to feel the pressure. But this took the pressure off of him right now. >> I I think the pressure has still got to be there, though, right? And I think that this is why I think they still keep turnurning that uh free agent market for more punters. It hasn't looked good. I mean, he might have been gotten the benefit of the doubt of having a little bit more um responsible or you know, accounted to him at this point than Jack Stonehouse, but even still, I haven't seen good punting yet out there at the training camp. I think you have to hope that the offense is better, the defense is so good that punting does not end up being much of the Maybe they should just resign Tommy Townson. How about that? >> Unfortunately, he's already signed up somewhere else. Well, maybe we can show up at 8:30 in the morning. We'll show see if we can have some skills and show >> Oh, boy. I mean, I it couldn't hurt at this point. Give it a shot. >> Hey, before we wrap it up, uh, one of the storylines that continues during camp is Tank Dell. Looks like he's making progress step by step. We heard from him at the podium this week. What a story that's going to be whenever he does come back. Gut feeling though, do you think he's ready week one or are we going to be talking more about few games into the season perhaps? Barring any setback? >> I think it's a few games into the season. they have done everything they can to give him as much runway as possible to come back and hit the ground running in the way that they want him to be. Even now, he's not participating in like team stuff. And so, there's still check marks to have. How does he look like when he has to catch in traffic and there's a possibility of legs tangling up? How does he look when he's actually taking that first hit? We don't know those yet. And yes, there's still time. There's joint practices which I think will matter a lot in his progress, but I think that they have shown abundantly in his case and in a lot of other cases that they're willing to air on the side of caution. >> No doubt. >> Nothing will tell the truth more than him getting tackled. And if he can get up and not have that dislocation again, that's the real real concern is dislocations cuz they do happen again and again. It's not about the ligaments. Those are sound and he is safe to be out there and not tear it up again. I think that he won't play in the first game and I think they'll do the injured reserve and designate him for return later. So maybe around week four, week six, maybe even week eight. That's when they'll try this and at some point this year I do think he'll play some football. >> Well, we wish him nothing the best. I mean, what a journey back close to what 20 months I think since that that injury in Kansas City. And hey, he's inching closer. He's making progress, staying positive, and let's see how that progresses in the coming weeks. But hey, we got football. We got a game coming up on Thursday. Yes, it's a preseason game. We don't know who's going to play, but it's going to be a lot of fun. Uh game time back at now Reliant Stadium on Thursday night. As always, appreciate you coming in. Reggie Edoula from In the Loop, Sports Radio 610 every day. And of course, Texans insider Aaron Wilson. And I've got big news coming up at Sports Radio 610 this week. >> Yeah, this Thursday you'll be able to hear us clean and crisp and clear on your FM dial. 957 the fan is what it's going to turn to. So, uh go ahead and put that on your preset so you can hear us clear. Congratulations on that. I know you guys are fired up. Going to 957. >> Yes, sir. >> FM Sports Radio 610. Now >> the fan. >> There you go. Good stuff, guys. Thanks for the time, man. Thanks. We'll enjoy the week here at the Texans.

title: Houston Texans camp news: Tank Dell takes important step, Jadeveon Clowney dominates
text: Heat. Heat. How y'all doing? >> What do you What do you see in him that makes that worth your investment? And what do you try to teach him? Uh just a little nuances I think um when you get so much thrown at you uh as a young guy um completely different defense than he's ever played in um it's it's being it's made you know it's knowledge that we're counting on him you know that the the pressure that I'm sure he puts on himself to be perfect every day. Um, a lot of things can get lost in translation, whether it's um alignment, whether it's hands, whether it's um, you know, pad level on bull rushes or being able to skate blocks at this level, how different it is than, you know, college. Um, so for me it's just pulling him aside and being able to able to articulate a lot of those things um in a way that that uh that is slowed down um so he can work through those things at a slowed pace uh download those things so that when he gets out there u playing real football um it kind of becomes second nature. >> We just seen one of your real good friends stick his head content in Will Anderson Jr. Someone that that you've seen grow in this game. You've also been around and watched a lot of defensive games. What is starting to set Will apart from others? >> Uh it's the I think the turning point for for players of his caliber is like when they realize that when they want to take it over, they can take it over. And I think he's getting to that point where, you know, he he realizes if if he wants to shut practice down, he can shut it down. Like if if he don't want them to get a playoff, they won't get a playoff. He don't want them to get a pass off, they won't get a pass off. He want a TFL every play, he can go do it. So I think um he's starting to get to that point where he finally realizes that like, man, like the game is in the palm of my hands. And he also understands the responsibility that comes with it. I think that's what makes him so special is that, you know, you get a lot of guys in that position of of of being that dominant, being that good, and know they kind of look at it like, you know, it was supposed to happen to them. Um whereas he looks at it as, you know, he's grateful for every chance he gets to be the player that he is. So, um yeah, I think I think he's starting to realize the the the power that he has, you know, that his hands, feet, helmet, all that, all the above. Um, and he's letting it be known every day. >> You've been with him for three of his four seasons now. What have you observed that has that allows him to be able to take over? >> Yeah, I think it's the just the relentless work ethic. I think he's um he's never shy about looking for knowledge, right? I think, you know, certain guys get to a point where um they're so good or they're they're at a level where uh you know, they feel like asking for asking questions is weird in a sense. Um but that's not him. You know, he's always looking for ways to improve, whether it's film study, whether it's his recovery, whether it's uh pass rush moves, whether it's alignment in the run game. I mean, you know, From the first day he got here, the first thing he does when he gets in the locker room is grab the iPad, watch practice film. He still does it today. His locker is right next to mine, so we generally go over things. He's asking me about his alignment here, his hands here. He So, he's always, as good as some of the reps look to other people, none of it's ever is is ever good enough for him. And I think that's what makes him so special. uh to be at a point where I mean he's you know highest paid non-quarterback and no trade clauses and all types of craziness like that and to still be like yeah but what more can I do? I think that that just speaks volume about who he is. >> You see pretty quickly how Logan can make this defense creative all the things they can do. >> Absolutely. Yeah. Um, I think Logan uh gives us uh that versatility. I think that, you know, we had with Autry in a sense, you know, uh if if we needed him to, he can go outside, play in. Uh he's stout enough, strong enough to to play uh from wide nine all the way to zero. Uh Clowny, the the the resume speaks for itself. No matter where he's been, he's produced uh in the run and in the past. So, um, adding both of those guys in, uh, to what we already had with, you know, myself, Will, Denil, Tommy, um, adding in Kaden as well. I mean, the the sky's is the limit for where we could be, um, and we're seeing flashes of it out here, but the more we're able to to orchestrate together, you know, collab and, uh, craft together, um, we just hope to to get it up to speed to be humming by by week one. >> Matt Burke mentioned about chasing perfection. the defense, four guys on the interior. What does perfection look like? >> Uh disruption. I think uh we joke a lot uh in our room because it's a race every snap and the race is more so uh inside guys to outside guys cuz you know if we're not perfect Will and Denil are already there um and even when you are perfect they probably still beat you there. So, you know, for us, um, inside, man, it's about disruption. Uh, it's about being able to clog lanes. It's about being able to get quarterbacks off their spot, not allow them to be comfortable. Uh, so those guys on the edge can rush freely, uh, and do what they do without thinking. Um, you know, it's about, uh, I always talk to the inside guys about, um, beating blocks. I think uh you know if you start looking at how many plays you made uh you often start skipping the process on defeating the blocks in front of you. Uh I never chase the plays. I always chase beating blocks because if I beat the block nine times out of 10 I give myself an opportunity to make a play. So I think you know for us inside man continue to be disruptive continue to beat blocks uh and continue to to to collapse pockets uh be disruptive in the run game and allow those specimens on the edge to to to do what they do. Chance, right? Sorry. You've always been the hunk in the room, but now you guys add Clowny, who you know has experience in years. What's it like seeing him continue to do it at such a high? >> Uh, man, it's great. Uh, I think it uh, you know, it it it in a way continues to drive guys like myself, like obviously getting older, but, you know, you still see a guy who's a little bit older than myself who continue to still do it at a high level. Um, you know, it's great to add, you know, I think, you know, one thing he probably doesn't get as much credit for is his his football IQ. You know, he's already in the mean rooms talking about things he sees, uh, as much film as he studies and and being able to bounce that knowledge off myself, Will Denil, other young guys in the room. Uh, it's been great. And then obviously once he takes the field, I mean, you see why he was, you know, the the number one overall pick and and no matter what jersey he puts on, um, he's a highlight reel waiting to happen. What training camp in Houston is no joke. What makes this worth it for you? Is it the end result? Is it wins? What makes this work? >> Uh, that's a great question actually. Um, I think it's probably a multitude of things. Um, some personal, some teamwise. I think uh teamwise, I just think um being a part of something special uh you don't take it for granted going into year 11. Uh, I think I was talking to somebody about this offseason like this team has a very college feel to it like with how close everyone is and uh the inside jokes and how how much we clown each other and how much you can clown your brother but it's not taken personal like you know it's it's it's that type of feel. Um, and that's hard to find the NFL. That's that's really hard to find you know because of the business of of it and everybody's generally out for themselves. But I mean, this is a team that genuinely cares about each and every man uh being successful as a player and as a person. Um, and that shows in the way we we play on defense, on offense, special teams. Um, that shows in in the way we cheer each other on. That shows in the way we um congregate outside of the meeting rooms and in the field. Um, so I'd say that. that in personal it's like um you know I've went through injuries in my career you know that I felt like um at certain times may have kind of knocked me off of you know where I felt like I was ascending at the time or or different things like that or illnesses that I may have have went through. So for me, like every day I I touch the field, whether it's practice, whether it's a game, um I'm doing it for the men next to me, but I'm also like making sure I remind everybody like, "Yeah, I'm still that guy. Like I I can still do this at a high level. Uh first down, second down, third down, crunch time, it don't matter. Like, put me in the game. I can make a play playing with whomever, next to whomever. uh whatever style is needed, whatever whatever is needed, like I've always shown throughout my career like I can make those plays. So, um even going into year 11, like I'm always finding ways to somehow make myself feel disrespected so that each and every time I step out here, it's like, excuse my French. No, that you know. So, >> sorry, last one. Along those same lines I've had conversations I've also talked with Michael I've talked to Rise talked to Katie McDonald now and I talked to Tom and Tobi about how much you are a perfectionist one but you're teaching you're always you're always teaching all the while while you're learning. You've shied away from saying after this is all over you're going to be a coach. >> But you but you see even on the sidelines we watch you still teaching. Are you starting to see yourself once this once the game is done for you going that way. >> Uh that is that is not something I'm seeing. But everybody I mean and I do mean everybody tells me that's you know that's something I I'll get to and you know we'll cross that bridge when I get there. Uh, but yeah, I think um I think I would be doing the game a disservice. I think I'd be doing myself a disservice if I didn't um impart all the wisdom that I have uh on to, you know, my teammates. I think uh the beautiful thing is I I kind of understand I understand what it's supposed to look like, but I also understand what it's supposed to look like if you're undersized. also understand, you know. So, I think I have the uh the ability to uh make it relatable to whatever the body type is, whatever whatever the the the um the skill set is. Um so, that's why you see me do that. I I just I I I understand that, you know, when it's over, um me just having all this wisdom and going home and just relaxing does nothing. So, if I can pull Tommy aside and help him make, you know, three more plays, if I can pull Kaden aside and help him make another play or two, um I'm going to do that. Even if I can do it for Will, if I can do it for Denil, like whomever uh that I see um if there's a chance there to to clean something up or make it a little uh more swift or something like that, I'm going to do that. I think uh I've had guys pour that into me. So, um, to be able to do that and give that back to the game, uh, I feel like I'm I'm supposed to do that. >> All right, guys. Thank you. >> Yep. >> No problem. >> Hey guys, Aaron Wilson, Texans training camp. Tank Dell participated in full team drills and the first time he was in a situation like that since he caught that touchdown against the Kansas City Chiefs and his knee was exploded with, of course, the dislocation, then the torn ACL, MCL, and LCL. So he looked fine. He caught the pass. It was over the middle from Davis Mills. It was a little bit behind him and no one tackled him in a game situation. There could have been some heavy contact there going across the middle. Obviously they are trying to advance this and get him to a point where can he play in a game? No. Do not think he will play against the, you know, Chargers in the first preseason game. I'll be surprised if he plays in these preseason games at all. We'll just see when do they ramp him up to a point where he's not offlimits to contact. Even though he's not wearing a red jersey, it's very obvious the underlying understanding about Tank Dell. Don't hit Tank. And I think it would be so unfortunate for him to have another catastrophic injury. So yeah, the hope is that he can continue to be comfortable out there. as he said structurally his knee is sound. The doctors have told him to cut it loose. So that's what they're doing. And I thought he looked good with some toe tap catches in individual drills and I saw similar ability from Lewis Bond to navigate the back corner of the end zone. So good things there. And let's get to some of the highlights of practice. Some of the things that we saw Colin Wright, you saw the interview I did with Colin always around the football and today he intercepts CJ Stra QB1 that's big when you're a rookie and you can do something like that. Anticipate throws, be instinctive, really really good. Manville graduate, local guy trying to make his hometown football team. Great story that I told the other day and he's paid his dues. He's out here doing a lot of the things for the vets, including buying them snacks, Skittles, M&M's, Sun Chips, he says the guys like. He's getting a lot of very valuable mentoring from from our last Derek Stanley Jr. and all the defensive backs. And of course, his position coach, Dino Vaso, who's outstanding coach. So, a arrow up for him. In the red zone work, we saw a great inbreaking route from Jaden Higgins and good timing with him and Straoud for what would have been a touchdown. So, I thought that was a good step in the right direction. I've seen them get into a better sync. There's a better rhythm and timing between CJ Strad and Jaden Higgins than a year ago when he was a rookie when he still caught six touchdown passes. It was a slow start, but eventually they got on the same page and they're still on the same page. So, that was interesting. A big hit by Pro Bowl Mike linebacker Aziz Alshshire knocking the football away from David McGomery on a passing route. Hard hit Aziz agent zero as they call him. He means business. Rough tough customer. Someone that you really you watch him and he's a big factor. One of his understudies, rookie linebacker Wade Woodz, is appearing to be more instinctive and active and reacting faster to plays. So, he baited Davis Mills with a pretty savvy move into an incomplete pass. I think it would have been tough for him to have pull it down for the interception. He tried to, but he wasn't able to corral the football. But nonetheless, encouraging signs getting better and doing a good job for Frank Ross on special teams where I think he'll be a mainstay. So, a couple of updates. Also, tight end Brevin Jordan misses his fourth practice in a row and I think it's leg related, my understanding, and know like he's had like a season ending situation, but they've had to back off of Brevin and get him rest and rehab time. And so we'll see when he gets back out there. Meanwhile, the tight end situation, it's pretty academic. Kade Stover capitalizing on the increased snaps after Brevin started camp hot and Cade started slow, but now it's gone in the other direction. A big day by Marlon Klein. A gigantic target in the red zone for the quarterbacks and he makes some plays today. The big catch. I feel like Marlin is someone that as you bring him along, you get him better. you help him improve and you can see the upside why they drafted the Michigan man and the German import to have him in the second round. You know, did they draft him higher than a lot of general managers had him rated? Yes, of course. But they like the player. They like his upside. They feel good about it. A couple other notes here, you know, with the passing aid, you know, Davis Mills made some good decisions. other ones I think he'd like to have back, but overall you kind of know what you're getting with him. You know, a steadiness with a backer quarterback signed a one year, $7 million deal, a pay cut basically with a restructure, saving a couple of million in cap space with them reducing the number for reserve lineman Jared Patterson. They feel like Jared's done a pretty good job, but it was going to make 3.746 million. That's too much. It's cuz he qualified for playing time to have that higher base salary in the final year of his deal. With the conversion they did, he got $400,000 in a signing bonus. So, they were able to give him some money. He's still not a lock to make the team. So, at least he gets the 400,000. And the salary is fully guaranteed. So, if he isn't here, he's going to walk with about $1.5 million if he doesn't make this team. So they did that. I think a lot of this too just to kind of thank him for his hard work and you know he's pulled them out of the fire several times. He's a effective player. As you guys know there's only one punter now. Kai Krueger and Kiko Ryan said he's our partner right now. I think they're very open-minded to looking around but uh they want to concentrate on the holding situation, the continuity of that. that was a concern for them and they just didn't feel like, as I've said before, Jack Stonehouse was the best holder or, you know, necessarily the best at directional punting. So, you would hope that Krueger will really embrace this opportunity. This is a golden opportunity for him to win the job right now. Sheldon Rankkins, we talked with him and we heard a lot from him. You'll hear from him in this video about mentoring, mentoring Kadan McDonald, mentoring younger players, how much this game means to him. It's really special to him to be a part of this defense and to continue to play the game. older player that still has a lot of game and can get in the end zone. You've seen him score touchdowns. We've seen a lot of good things from him. Versatile role for Logan Hall. They feel like Logan is doing a good job with the inside outside stuff. It's mostly inside, but they know that he can do that. Um Kenyon McDonald, they feel like he still plays with good low pad level, that he's learned a lot, that he continues to get better. I asked Ryan about him today. We'll hear from Demo as well. So, when you think about where things stand, we know the starting lineup. Guess what? How about this sub package? Jaden Clowney, lots of sacks today. Couple of sacks, they can't block this guy. It's very challenging with his speed off the edge and they're seeing that. And Deo Ryan's talked about that, too. So, you heard from De Mo on Clowney as well. Uh Naqucoin Jones has done a good job. They like Naquin as a rotational defensive lineman. Is are they going to be able to keep him? They have Mario Jr. of course and you have Kada McDonald and you have Logan Hall and then you have the starters Tommy Tigi who's been dominant along with Sheldon Rankin. So could he be odd man out? We're going to see and it's be interesting to watch that. Trent Brown continues to play a ton of right tackle and this competition is ongoing. I still think that they'll give the nod to Braden Smith at some point but not yet. We're seeing a bunch of Keelin Rage with the, you know, quarterback with CJ Strad. So, he's doing a good job. I think that's going well. It's progressing. And Weller had a false start today. So, the vet jumps. Uh, very rarely does that happen, but that's a mental error and got to avoid those. That can't be happening. And then, like I say with Lewis Bond, it's been play after play after play. He's had a great camp. They're very impressed with him and how he's done.
