So, it does feel like the offense is maybe pulling a little bit more of their weight this year. >> Right, and the other side of the coin, too, the defense looks even better than last year, and I didn't know that that was possible, but now having a Jadeveon Clowney and having him line up inside sometimes at tackle, but having him with Denil Hunter and Will Anderson Jr. Having a Reed Blankenship, this defense could take it to an even higher level, and I think the offense, like you said, they've held their own. It's like it's embarrassing the way it had been in years past. >> to circle back to the defense in a moment cuz I I want to talk cuz we talk about C.J. Stroud. I'm sure you guys do it on the radio on a regular basis as well. He is under the microscope in the spotlight each and every practice. We're seeing who he's throwing to, how accurate he is, the timing he has, everything that is part of being a quarterback is being broken down every What have you guys seen from C.J.? He's had his ups, he's had his downs so far in camp, and what can carry over you think here in this regular season? >> It's funny that you mention the ups and downs because it feels like it's been slightly fewer ups, but definitely fewer downs. Like I think that the thing that Nick Cayley, the offensive coordinator, has harped on, and it's not just lip service, you can see it, he's been a lot more consistent, and it feels like that's exactly what they want from him in this offense, which I think that bodes well as well, especially coming off of a a post-season run from him where it felt like he had been really consistent during the season and then had really bad dips with the multi-turnover games. So, it feels like that's been better. Plus, I mean, you've seen some connections show up a little bit better with him and Jayden Higgins, who's going to need to be a big part of this offense for the offense to take a step forward this year. >> And Nico he's come out of you don't know if it's a 610 or one of the interviews he's called out him saying, "Hey, he is going to be a star in this league." >> Right. And since that rocky performance, I think he's rededicated himself and I'm watching him. I see greater command of the offense. I see less mistakes. Like Reggie said, every now and then there's an interception and it's sort of a byproduct of who you're playing against, but also him pushing the envelope and they're running more plays that he likes and I think the relationship and the collaboration between himself and offense coordinator Nick Cayley is better. And if Cayley's a better play caller with this personnel that they've invested in, maybe this offense could be you know, top 15 offense and I think that's all they have to be to make a real deep playoff run. >> I was going to say when you look at the potential of this offense, they're always tweaking things and I spoke a little bit with Nick Cayley and man, all throughout this off season he's he's trying to find new things they can do offensively. How exciting is that knowing if they can get healthy pieces out there, they've got obviously a run game now that can open some things up >> Oh, I mean it's it's terrifyingly exciting because last year there was games where you get to the end of the game you're like, has he run out of plays in the playbook? [laughter] Um and so if there's two things that feel like they helped that. One, there's a full complement of tight ends. In fact, maybe too many tight ends, which Nick Cayley having a tight end background, you can tell that his offense requires that to reach its full potential. Plus, you've heard it from a lot of different guys. They just have more plays that they've seen early on which gives you more to pick from. All right? It's like having a bigger menu. You go into the Cheesecake Factory and you see all the different options. Now we have opportunities to be satisfied with our selections come game day and I think that that's going to help them as well. >> That bag is deep. I think there's a lot >> a hunch too that some of the plays, there's some secret plays that they run in the bubble that we don't see because I would I would get this question, "Where's the 13 personnel, the three tight ends? Where's the 12?" It's there. We don't see the two zero personnel bunch with the two split backs. We haven't seen that, but he promised it would happen. I think they can be more creative with this bunch and I'm liking what I'm seeing from Marlon Klein. I think this guy could be a weapon. Looks like a really good athlete. I know he's a little raw. He's a German import, Michigan man, but heck of a story and pretty good athlete, good raw material to work with. >> So, you got Montgomery and Woody Marks. We can go on and on. We can talk two hours about Texas tonight, but but you look at this position, I love watching the running backs do their thing when I'm out there at practice as well. Just imagine regular season football, how much damage these guys can do together in different roles. They all have their strengths, but having that tandem, I think it's going to be big for the backfield. >> Yeah, I don't have any concerns when it comes to the running back core at all. It feels like they have consistent dudes that can do the job incredibly well. The question I have in the run game actually comes with the offensive line, which >> Good point. >> How many of us have had questions about the offensive line? I think we'd all raise our hands. It's can they create the space? Can they create the gaps for those guys who are very good at finding those space and running through it? Right now, at least versus this defense, they haven't popped as many as you would want, but they also haven't like had tackles for losses and being blown up in the backfield as much. So, in the same way we're talking about the offense in general, it's better than it was. I think there's room for improvement, which I guess is still okay. >> But it always starts up front, no doubt. >> And Saturday night it went backwards a bit. Henry Toto and all these guys are getting tackles for losses and zero gains for David Montgomery. The guy that made a little bit of noise was Noah Whittington and now he'll get more playing time cuz Jo Ware Jordan's out for about a week with a strained hip flexor, but I really look at the backs and I think there's going to be some division of labor where you're going to see mostly Montgomery and they're definitely going to have carved out a role for Woody Marks. I expect these guys to combine and they will not be one of the worst running games. I think they're going to be in the top half this year. >> You got a lot of battles going on too that are fun to watch, keep an eye on. You guys were talking before the before the show we were talking about the what we had hit on tonight. You look at the linebacking situation. You got some studs, but you got a some slots there that that are open in this race. LB3 is one of them. Uh this is fun. This is what I love about the competition in court during the course of training camp. >> Well, 100% and for me this one is very intriguing because it comes on the defense where they have seemingly patched up any possible hole an opposing offense can get to. That linebacker three is the one where I go. How does that look because Demeco Ryans likes throwing out a base defense with three linebackers where they can get real physical at times. Last year you had a E.J. Speed that you believed in and you knew that he could do the job. Right now it's a whole bunch of guys that in theory can do the job, but none of them has separated themselves. It's one of the reasons why I'm really excited for Thursday in the first preseason game versus the Chargers. >> I think the inside track goes to Marte Mapu. I thought Matt Burke gave away a few clues about a week ago. Some of his comments sounded like he favors Mapu. Wade Wades may be heard from in this competition showing some physicality, a little feistiness last night, but in my opinion Mapu because of pass coverage, converted safety, former Patriots guy, I kind of feel like they would throw Mapu out there first if the season began today. I also think with no E.J. Speed third linebacker snaps are going to go down. It's going to be a lot of 4-2-5 alignments. >> Well, I meant to ask you guys too Keelan Rutledge, how do you think he has looked so far in camp? You you see all the reports and I mean he's he's getting the job done out there. >> Yeah, without question. Honestly, it feels weird to start with something that I'm not seeing from him as opposed to the things that I am, but I'm not seeing him fumble the snap. And that seems insignificant, but it's not. He has not played the center position in snapping the football. Very crucial to that. So, he's done that very well. In fact, on our show he told us that his wife has been to catching some of those snaps from him. So, that's how he's getting the some of the mechanics down. She does. I feel like if you end up in a place where all three of your quarterbacks go down, we call the Rutledge household and we we see if we can get your fourth quarterback there. But jokes aside, like he's delivered in every way that you want. In fact, they talk about it. He looks like the guy that you saw on film from Georgia Tech, which is a gritty, nasty guy that's going to hold the line when it comes to his physicality, but also he came in on his first day here, his introductory press conference, he said, "I'm going to hold guys accountable." That's crazy here from a rookie. >> rookie, yeah. >> But he's doing it already there on the training camp field. >> Right. And the way he plays through the echo of the whistle, intense, feisty, you say gritty. I watch this guy and I think he can be an intimidating type of center, like a Leonard bomb. And you watch those kind of guys, they get paid a lot of money eventually. To me, this guy will be a second and third contract guy here with the Texans. We're watching a cornerstone player his really early moments as he's establishing himself in the NFL. I think he's eventually be the gold standard at center. >> We've been at a lot of these practices, punting has gotten some attention or should I say lack of punting. That's surprisingly an issue right now. They've got to lock something down. They got time to figure it out, but that's been kind of a surprise. >> Yeah, I mean you look at what happened here. So, they just cut Jack Stonehouse, the rookie who had a stronger leg than Kai Kroeger, but not as good at holding. And they told us that it would be the best holder that probably would get the job. He is the best holder, but he's not the weak, you know, he's got a weaker leg. You watch the directional punting, that's okay. They tried out some punters, Jack Browning and Trenton Gill, they didn't sign either. And I think what they're trying to do now is build up his confidence and build up the kicking operation confidence, and we'll see how it goes, but Kroeger wasn't very good for the New Orleans Saints last year. It's got to get better, otherwise they're going to have another gong show tryout, and Kroeger is going to have to feel the pressure, but this took the pressure off of him right now. >> I I think the pressure is still got to be there, though, right? And I think that this is why I think they still keep churning that free agent market for more punters. It hasn't looked good. I mean, he might have been gotten the benefit of the doubt of having a little bit more responsible or you know, accounted to him at this point than Jack Stonehouse, but even still, I haven't seen good punting yet out there at the training camp. I think you have to hope that the offense is better, the defense is so good that punting does not end up being as much of the top priority. >> Maybe they should have just resigned Tommy Townsend. How about that? >> Unfortunately, he's already signed up somewhere else. >> Well, maybe we could show up at 8:30 in the morning, we'll shoot see if we have some skills to show them. >> I mean, I It couldn't hurt at this point. Give it a shot. >> Hey, before we wrap it up, one of the storylines that it continues during camp is Tank Dell. Looks like he's making progress step-by-step. We heard from him at the podium this week. What a story that's going to be whenever he does come back. Gut feeling, though, do you think he's ready week one? Are we going to be talking more about few games into the season, perhaps, barring any setback? >> I think it's few games into the season. They have done everything they can to give him as much runway as possible to come back and hit the ground running in the way that they want him to be. Even now, he's not participating in like team stuff. And so, there's still check marks to have. How does he look like when he has to catch in traffic and there's a possibility of like tangling up? How does he look when he's actually taking that first hit? We don't know those yet. And yes, there's still time. There's joint practices, which I think will matter a lot in his progress, but I think that they have shown abundantly in his case and in a lot of other cases that they're willing to err on the side of caution. >> No doubt. >> Nothing will tell the truth more than him getting tackled and if he can get up and not have that dislocation again, that's the real real concern is dislocations cuz they do happen again and again. It's not about the ligaments. Those are sound and he is safe to be out there and not tear it up again. I think that he won't play in the first game and I think they'll do the injured reserve and designate him for return later. So, maybe around week four, week six, maybe even week eight. That's when they'll try this. And at some point this year, I do think he'll play some football. >> Oh, we wish him nothing but the best. I mean, what a journey back close to what, 20 months, I think, since that that injury in Kansas City. And hey, he's inching closer, he's making progress, staying positive. And uh let's see how that progresses in the coming weeks. But hey, we got football. We got a game coming up on Thursday. Yes, it's a preseason game. We don't know who's going to play, but uh it's going to be a lot of fun. Uh game time back at now Reliant Stadium on Thursday night. As always, appreciate you coming in. Reggie Ettoola from In the Loop Sports Radio 610 every day. And of course, Texans Insider uh Aaron Wilson. And you I've got big news coming up at Sports Radio 610 this >> Yeah, this Thursday you'll be able to hear us clean and crisp and clear on your FM dial. 95.7 The Fan is what it's going to be. So, go ahead and put that on your presets so that you can hear us >> Congratulations on that. I know you guys are fired up. They're going to 95.7 >> Yes, sir. >> FM Sports Radio 610 now The Fan. >> There you go. Good stuff. Guys, thanks for the time, man. >> Thanks, Trenni. >> Enjoy the week here with the Texans. >> Tavier, you're playing for your hometown team. What's it like to be doing that to try to be out here and make this squad and this is a team obviously you grew up watching. You were at the player thing they had in the spring where they invite guys in and so kind of like you've been on this track to be a Texan for a long time. >> For sure, it's been awesome. I think I'm I'm so happy to be home. I I have my family come out every day. I'm I'm blessed to be able to to to play for such a great defense, learn from great coaches and obviously being one of the best rooms in the league. So it's it's been awesome to to to come back home and especially learning obviously get better as a >> You're making a lot of plays. That's what they Matt Burke, the defensive coordinator, was just talking about that every day going back to the spring he's seeing you make plays. Uh what is it about you and your ability to find the football and to disrupt the offense? >> I think it's credit to my coaching. I think since I came in coach DeMeco has really done a a a job of telling us to go get the ball and a lot of a lot of DB coaches out there don't preach that. So, I I I think for me personally I've always kind of been a little bit natural at going to get the ball. So, um just using those talents that I have and along with film study and coaching has been been awesome. >> Uh Derek Stingley and A.J. Bouye were your teammates last year. What's the mentoring like from them, from older corners that have had some success? They're not old guys, but they they've played in the league and they've been to Pro Bowls and things like that. What's the mentoring like? What do they teach you? >> Man, it's awesome. Just be myself. Um even when even when I came off the field just now, um K'Waun Williams told me, "Hey Colin, keep going, keep pushing, keep making plays, keep being yourself cuz at the end of the day that's what it's about and um just keep trying to find a way each day to get better, take one thing every day, and obviously try to find a way to keep improving your game. >> I look over your shoulder, I'm seeing your family. Who all is out here tonight? >> Uh tonight I have my mom, my dad, my aunt, my little cousin, and both my godparents. So, it's it's it's it's so cool to to have them uh be back home. They they've Texans fans as well my my entire life. So, it's full circle for them just like it is me being out here uh being at not NRG, but Reliant now and and and just taking this this entire environment in. >> someone about it cuz it was Reliant when I got here, then it became NRG, and now we're back to Reliant. >> Yeah. >> It's the Reliant the power company and that's who gets my bill. [laughter] >> It is crazy. >> When it comes to being back in this area and you know, the success you had at Manvel to kind of follow up on that, does it feel a little bit like that? Because you've got the cheering section of the family just like your high school football days. >> It does. It's awesome always have their support. Um kind of like I said, they're they're always out here. They come out here every day. And uh just when I'm not doing football, just be able to see family and go eat with them, go to go chill, Just be be able to do those things is awesome because when I was in when I was in school the last four years I I wasn't able to do that a lot being away in California. So, it's been awesome to have their support and obviously as a player I think all those things are just as important as as when you're playing football to just be able to stay grounded. >> Right. We see how you anticipate plays in the middle of the last picture of the game. How much does Stanford and the think tank that you're in there for football and of course educationally does that help you as a football player when you're around so many smart people and you're a smart guy yourself? >> 100%. I think it even goes all the way back to Manvel. I I've had great coordinators who kind of always instilled in me the the the foundations of of defensive back play. So, it started at Manvel and and Stanford's a whole 'nother beast. I learned so much from my coach Coach Paul Williams who who taught me so much over over my four years there and I've just been able to keep building and and and I'm so appreciative of having those those great coaches in my life. >> Best advice you've gotten about trying to make an NFL roster? What do people tell you? >> Keep going. Keep making plays. Be yourself and most importantly make sure you stay healthy. >> What are some of your rookie duties? Are you carrying pads and helmets or do they not make you do that? >> They haven't made me do that. I have to go buy snacks, a lot of snacks. So, >> What are what are what do you what do the guys want what do you normally buy them? >> Uh snacks we probably got some some M&M's, some Skittles, chips, SunChips, sunflower seeds, nothing too crazy. Just just some small basic things. >> Kamari, all the guys, all the vets? >> The entire room, yes. >> Dino, too? Or you don't have to get it for the coach? >> Dino, too. Everybody. Everybody Everybody involved. >> You got a good store to find this stuff, huh? >> Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. A lot of them to find in Houston. >> Have you had to sing? >> Not yet. I'm I'm I'm actually coming up here pretty soon. I actually might be tomorrow, Monday, sometime next week I'll be there. >> What's the song that you have ready that you would tee up for the vets and that you would not get the gong show boo and they'll boo you off the stage? >> I'm still thinking, but I would say probably "When I See You" by Fantasia. I'm probably going with that one. Yeah, I'm going with that one. >> I like that one. And last one for you. So, we were about all the tough things of camp, the long days. What's the fun part of the camp besides obviously making the plays, but what are some things that you enjoy about camp? >> Man, I enjoy just coming out here every day and and learning from guys like Sting and Kamari. Obviously, like we've said, two of the best corners in the league and me as a young guy, them being open to giving me all those little small keys to the game is has been so important and so exciting for me because I'm able to implement those things in my game and I've always been a learner, so for me I just have love to keep trying to find something every day to keep learning the game and get better. >> Years from now, what do you do when you're done playing football? What do you want to do with your Stanford degree? >> I want to do a little I want to do a little bit of film, some type of broadcast, kind of do what you're doing right now. Um I'd like to invest, so probably going to do something in some some type of finance/ real estate road. That's that's what I did with a lot of my NIL money, so those are probably two things two different paths that I want to go down. >> Colby, good luck. It's very nice to meet you. I've written a few stories about you and it's great to meet you tonight. >> Yes, sir. I appreciate it. Thank you so much. >> I'm sorry. >> That's all. >> It was all right. >> Oh, it was >> No I just realized I just realized that >> Why? >> It was just that >> It was a >> Mhm.

title: Texans' Saturday night scrimmage: key takeways, injury updates
text: Hey guys, Aaron Wilson. Saturday night under the lights. The Texans have sort of a modified scrimmage and it was [music] a day dominated by the defense. The NFL's top ranked defense from last season flex a little muscle. You should have seen the speed rush from Will Anderson Jr. going around Trent Brown for a quick sack on the play. Interception. CJ Strad throws it to Kamari Lasser. I think the play was dead, but nonetheless, a good play by Kamari Lasser. Interception for Kayn Bulock continues to make those plays. The ball hawking center fielder was also added to the Pro Bowl just like Kamari after last season as an alternate. And then Henry Toto, a tackle for loss, rewarded with a 2-year $17 million max value contract this week. Toto making plays. And in terms of some of the get back from the offense, we saw CJ Stout connecting very well with Jaden Higgins. And in the one-on- ones, also saw, you know, some pretty good throws to Higgins, not just in the full team, but I thought was very impressive in the one-on- ones was Kamar Lasher's coverage, locking down Nico Collins. This was a rest day for all pro corner Derek Jr. according to defense coordinator Matt Burke. Jawar Jordan did not practice. Brevin Jordan dealing with a minor injury. Still did not practice. So he continues to lose some of the early momentum that he was building. And of course this isn't as serious as when he tore his patellar tendon or when he tore his anterior crucial ligament. I'm told he'll be back at some point but still nonetheless not good to miss time. Jake Hansen ankle still wrapped up in a sleeve. There's some hope some hope that he'll be back for the first game of the regular season against the Buffalo Bills. the same similar timeline, I should say, for British Brooks with his broken hand that had to have surgery to repair the damage. And so they get British Brooks back hopefully. Before practice began this afternoon, the Texans called rookie punter Jack Stonehouse and told him that he was being released. So now we have one punter in camp. the punter competition. It's a prime opportunity for Kai Krueger who was acquired in a trade from New Orleans Saints to win the job. And Frank Ross discussion when I asked him why now and why make this decision because obviously Stonehouse a stronger leg and better hang time. He said it [music] comes back to the continuity of the operation. There's nothing more important. He said this early in camp, nothing more important than who's going to be the holder for Taim Fairbird, the Texans kicker. And yes, they tried out other punters, Jack Browning and Trenton Gil. At this time, they're not signing anyone. And they want to see if more reps will help Krueger get as confident and fluid as possible. It's one of the reasons he's here is because he's runs a smoother operation and he's a better directional kicker and he has that year of experience, pivotal year of experience with the New Orleans Saints. Had a couple of punts blocked. From what I understand, the operation, the kicking operation last year for the Saints was a mess and he was swimming upstream trying to learn it. He wasn't all-American at South Carolina. He's got some talent. He's a good athlete, better athlete than Stonehouse. So they wind up going with the better holder and the guy that they feel more comfortable with just in terms of his experience. Are there other punters out there? Certainly, but they don't do anything to upset the apple cart when it comes to the operation between long staff Austin Brickman and kicker Ka Fairburn. So they do that trying to bolster that position. So I get it. That's why they made the decision. It's logical and sometimes you have to do things like that. So you think about everything that they're doing, there's a reason. So, thinking about other situations, going over to the offense, CJ Strad throwing the football very well for the most part. He hasn't thrown a lot of interceptions, but you know, I think say overall he's had good command of the offense. He's been very steady and he's made some good throws. He's challenged the defense. I like the connection he's building with Jaden Higgins. Jaylen Null still not in the full team drills. They're ramping him up because he missed a couple of weeks with the finger injury, his right pinky, and that's gotten better and he's catching passes, albeit in gloves. So, you see what's going on there. And you look at the linebacker position. We're starting to see a little bit of toughness from Wade Woodazz. He got some praise today from Matt Burke and Frank Ross. It was a very physical special teams drill. I thought Woodazz kind of stood out in this drill which was very very physical, very intense. Uh there's a video up a short that I posted. I called it survival in the fittest on Texans special teams. So we're still seeing very physical play. That's how you make the team. But yeah, he's in the mix. I still think Marty Mapu has a bit of an edge, but that's something that can change. A Good Day by Marlon Klein, which excited the German film crew from his homeland. They're here visiting him and putting his high school offense coordinator. I think they're doing something of a documentary about Marlon Klein, the Michigan man via Germany in their second round draft pick. I think he's had a good camp. So, looking at a couple other situations, they're still very happy with Colin Wright. He's making a lot of plays. I interviewed him. I'll bring you that interview with Colin Wright, uh, undrafted rookie corner from Stanford. He was put his best foot forward, has worked against the top receivers on this team in practice. That was something he got to do today with Derek Stingley Jr. out. So, he steps up and he didn't look out of place with the defense. So, I was impressed with what I saw from Colin Wright. He's from Manville. He's a Stanford man and they were sort of recruiting him before the draft because he did this invited player thing they do with guys that they want to have in to, you know, kind of see if they might want to have them back as undrafted. So that's how he sort of came to be on the Texans. They put a fair amount of undrafted money into him and now he's a Texan and that investment is looking pretty good so far. Noah Whittington, good runs again. Noah Winningington continues to step up. Jawar Jordan didn't practice today and that was one of the reasons why increased reps, snap, score. Noah Winnington, the undrafted rookie from Morgan, he's got some speed and he's got a real good instinctive way of finding openings in the defense. So, I was impressed with him. And then continue to see Lewis Bond. It's like play of the day. Lewis Bond. Leis Bond touchdown beats Trumont Smith gets up the field and he is on a roll. He's got field speed. I keep talking about this. He's got field speed. He's able to get out and up and do a great job of really running his route, selling his route convincingly and making a play. So, he's someone that to me putting his best foot forward, trying to make the team. They don't have the same route sometimes for Justin Watson. a lot of things are shorter and intermediate that they do with Watson. So interesting to watch that, you know, because they're competing for this spot. Tangell still in individual drills, they're ramping it up at a certain pace and obviously what they're not doing is exposing the potential contact. It gets rough out here. And coming off of that two years ago disloated knee, torn ACL, MCL, and LCL, there's nothing they want to do to risk injury. So they're telling you with their actions and their words that he's not ready yet for that type of situation. Making progress as he says there's light at the end of the tunnel when it comes to tank. So Solomon Bird has made a lot of plays as a reserve defensive end. I feel like Solomon really deserves to be in the top four defensive ends. Uh has had more plays than Dominique Robin certainly and more plays than Dylan Horton. We'll see how that goes. But that's something that's very interesting. We're watching that closely. the depth behind this dominant trio, this triumvirate of pass rushers, none other than Will Anderson Jr., Denil Hunter, and Javian Clowney. I'm actually standing right by Clowny's shoulder pads on my left. So, some rookie will bring those in, our equipment manager. But, uh, Clowny, this was family night, and so we saw the players visiting with all of their, you know, families and their significant others. So, a uh fun night under the lights. So, kind of feels like old school, like high school football being out here at night. And of course, the weather. Great. For a change, guys. I'm not covered in sweat. I feel great. It's really nice to feel this weather. Few skeers out here. We did have a lightning scare early in the practice where they were delaying starting the [music] practice because they didn't want to have anyone obviously risk u being struck by lightning. So the Doppler radar eventually cleared up. It passed and they were able to have a full practice and we're out here somewhat late after the interviews. And it was interesting to hear Matt Burke talking about Clowny, talking about the Colin Wrights, Wade Woodz in this third linebacker spot, and some praise for Woodz and we'll see where this thing goes. I still think Mapu has that edge. So interesting to watch. They did sign Owen Wright, a running back, and obviously that probably is because of Jar Jordan, and he's going to be sidelined for a little bit. He's got a little bit of an injury history. We're not hearing about anything yet on the nature or severity of that injury. So, we'll see. We'll keep you posted. Thinking some other notes here. Jared Wayne. Jared's made a lot of plays. Jared's had a very good training camp. He's got a lot of praise. You heard from Tankdale the other day. No hard feelings about the accident that caused that catastrophic injury. Uh, you saw my video with Wyatt Teller, my interview with David McGomery, interview with Caitlin Bulock, and I'll bring you this interview with Colin Wright. So, I'm looking forward to that. title: Texans camp report: Jaylin Noel back, Tank Dell talks, news
text: Hi guys, Aaron Wilson. Texans training camp Friday morning and a very good day for the receiving core. Why? Because Jalen Nowell is back off of the non-football injury list, had a right pinky injury. Today we see him with his gloves on, all taped up, making sure he does not have any recurrence of that finger injury. And I thought he caught the football fine, but that's a real shot in the arm for the passing game and the return game because he's got skills in that area. DeMeco Ryans thrilled to have back Jalen Nowell and I think it really they can pick up the momentum from from the spring when he was catching a touchdown pass basically every day from either Davis Mills or from C.J. Stroud. And you think about this player, he's that vertical threat, he scored 3.9 in the 40-yard dash, he got a 40-in vertical leap and he can get deep, he can run after the catch, he can also return very well and he is their starting slot receiver as of today and I expect him to hold that job as their number three receiver behind Nico Collins and of course Jayden Higgins who's had a great training camp. A day off for Nico Collins and precautionary with Brevin Jordan keeping him out. They want to be real careful about that leg because he's had a torn patellar tendon last year and a torn anterior cruciate ligament the year before getting hurt against Chicago Bears. So for a guy that hasn't played a lot of football the last few years, sometimes they're going to back off of it and take it a little easier with Brevin Jordan. Meanwhile Dalton Schultz some pretty good catches today, touchdown, and I thought looked very good. So, we'll go through some of the highlights of the day, some things to know, some my observations. Of course, we're also going to hear from the comeback kid. Comeback story continues for Tank Dell. Tank Dell is thrilled to be back out there. Even though it's just individual drills, as he says, one day at a time, but he feels extremely blessed and excited to be back out there, doing what he loves to do. And he said he never doubted that he would play football again. So, it's interesting to hear from Tank. We'll get back more into that in a moment, but I want to tell you about some of the big plays of the day. So, there was a pick-six on the very first play of the 7-on-7. Jalen Pitre picks off C.J. Stroud, takes it back to the house, touchdown for the hard-hitting nickel from Baylor and Stafford, one of the best nickels in the NFL. Just ask Rashee Rice, right? So, with C.J. Stroud, there haven't been a lot of those interceptions. It's been a small amount, but any are too many, but overall, it's been a great training camp for C.J., but this was a day that I felt like the defense flexed some muscle. There was a Henry To'o To'o forced fumble, where he rips the football away in the open field from David Montgomery. David's got to do a better job of securing it, putting that three points of pressure on the football to hold it and keep it in. But, on that one, Henry To'o To'o, one day after the 2-year, $17 million max-value deal, he gets it done, and he forces the fumble. Very, very proud of him. DeMeco Ryans will sound a like a proud big brother or a proud dad for Henry To'o To'o, fellow Alabama linebacker. Tremon Smith, late in the practice, intercepts Davis Mills. So, lots of guys picking off passes. We saw a very good play where C.J. Stroud throws a touchdown, great throw to Jayden Higgins. We also saw a very good throw from C.J. Stroud to a wide-open Jarret Dillard. Jarret Dillard made plays all the time. We went to Jarret Dillard by the way with Tank Dell. Tank says that he and Jarret Dillard are good and Jarret wrote him an apology. This was of course because he was in the wrong place, he ran into Tank and this is what caused this devastating knee injury and he said that it's a mistake, an accident that's happened and he told him not to carry that guilt. I remember being in the locker room that day and Jarret Dillard was inconsolable. He was crying, he was upset. One of the other reporters tried to interview him. I thought that wasn't a great idea and I went up and just kind of gave him a Jarret a pat on the back and said, "Hey man, I would kind of get away from everybody. You might want to, you know, get out get a little privacy for yourself cuz he's just bawling in front of the whole locker room. Just kind of for his uh just as human beings want to see that for him to have some time for himself. But yeah, that's water under the bridge. It happened for him and now he's playing well and now Tank is almost back. So, we'll get more into Tank, but you guys saw some pretty good plays. I saw um you know, Nico Collins a day off as I said, they kind of designate that. They're going to rest their wide receiver one. They don't want him out there constantly having all of this time on, you know, his feet. They want to keep him fresh. I don't think the starters will play much in the first preseason game, but obviously they'll get some work. Couple other things going through you know, the tryouts. So, this was the full group of tryouts as I reported, no immediate signings. They work out punters Trenton Gill and Jack Browning, kickers Chris Fairbairn and Will Fairbairn, long snappers Jacob Bobenmoyer and Jake McQuaide. I'm sorry. And wide receiver DeAndre Carter was here before, good returner, former starter here. And two quarterbacks, Jake Haener, Seth Henigan, and a running back Owen Wright. None immediately signed. The punter competition here, which has not been amazing so far, needs to be a little better. They continue between rookie Jack Stonehouse, who's shown a stronger leg and needs to work on the directional punting, and former New Orleans Saints punter, Kai Kroeger. So far, no one has really set themselves apart in this battle. It'll be determined largely by preseason game competitions. still sign a kicker to give Ka'imi Fairbairn a break. As I reported before, British Brooks is out about 3 weeks with a broken hand and having surgery. Jake Hansen still out with an ankle injury, regarded as week-to-week. Veteran safety MJ Stewart still on the non- I'm sorry, on the physically unable to perform list with a torn quadriceps tendon. And Nick Caserio has said that maybe he could get back at some point. Time is ticking down so for MJ to get back out there. And Tank Dell still on a limited basis. And before we, you know, hear from Tank, I want to kind of set the stage for this a little bit. It's a miraculous comeback. It's a basically a 2-year injury, and they're not going to do anything to rush him back. They want to make sure that when he gets out there, that he stays out there. And that's why there's so much caution with Tank Dell. And they're just trying to make sure that he's all right. You do that for a reason. It's intentional because you don't want to have any problems with this injury. The dislocation is the real danger. What he said his doctor told him that he is structurally sound and to go out there and cut it loose. So, the doctor gave him the clean bill of health that he could go out there and that he could play. So, that's good to hear that. As DeMeco said, you want to see that comeback story. Tank looks real nice out there getting back in the swing of things, and they're taking their time with Tank. Allowed him to come along. Outstanding job, nice, really crisp in his routes. Called it exciting, and it is exciting. And as Tank told me over the summer, there is daylight at the end of the tunnel. When he was, you know, pinned down with some questions about whether that would mean the first game, he demurred. He said that, you know, it's really just about making progress. So, that makes sense. But, uh Tank said it's nothing short of a blessing. It's about trusting in the work you do to put your foot in the ground. And when he got out there, he wasn't scared. And that's really important to not be scared, to not have that trepidation. And, you know, I think about with Tank, it's just a matter of time. And whenever they feel like they want to put you out there. Very spiritual guy, and he says, "When God wants you built up, he puts you through a storm. It's a long journey, but he's being patient. It's getting close." So, Tank Dell, yeah, as he said, we're going to take it one step at a time when asked about playing in the first game against the Bills. Credited C.J. Stroud and his close friendship with him. He's very happy with him. And, you know, everything he's done for him. But, he says he emphasized he'll get there. And he said he was like a junkyard dog working every day. He's been through a lot. He said he's always thought he was going to play again, that he would make it back from this injury. When he got hurt, he wrote a goal down. Says, "Come back better than before." Get 1% better. And his doctor emphasized 100% stable, but mentally trusting it and being explosive, that's the big deal. Uh in talking with DeMeco Ryans, you know, he says that Brevin Jordan's off to a good start at camp, but they're going to try to take care of him the right way. That's why they did that. And again, on the Tytus Howard contract, very important for them to sign Henry. Why? Cuz he's a trustworthy, consistent player, quote. He's gotten better, very deserving of the contract. He's very pleased with the undrafted rookie class, by the way, led by former Manvel and Stanford product Colin Wright. He's made a lot of plays. Thinks they've done a nice job with the training camp. I agree with that. And he feels like Jalen Nowell that it's about defining his role, carving out the role, returns, and getting the ball on offense. Guys, listen, fantasy players, fantasy owners, multiple times per game on offense. That was the words of DeMeco Ryans. So, very interesting to hear that, but he likes what he sees from C.J. Stroud, taking ownership of the offense. So, guys, make sure to check out my interview with Wyatt Teller and a lot from him there, including his you know, thoughts on Keelan Rowland, C.J. Stroud, his running game, moving to Texas, and of course, being a gator hunter and a gator catcher, uh that legendary viral moment with the alligator that he had carrying a dead alligator across his shoulders. He still has the gator head in his house. And says he's had a few gator bites, not maybe from that gator, but he's had gator bites before. He likes to have gator bites. So, calling on a couple of things here. Um we'll go with Tank Dell, and then we'll hear from our sponsors at PM Law Firm, and I'll also tell you about Fants Geek. So, let's go to Tank, and then we'll get back to some more football talk from me. Right back after this. >> Yeah, man, it's nothing short of a blessing. You know, um that's just a testament to all the work that I put in with the staff on my own and God first, so you know, it's great. >> Can you kind of take us through that process of during your rehab and your comeback? Every there's going to be certain stages in which you have to kind of test yourself, right? Like maybe how much you can uh put on, you know, put on the knee, how much explosive you can be and stuff like that. How was that process been like when you hit those milestones? Kind of mentally before than physically where you kind of got to put yourself to test. >> Um I'll say mentally, it's just about trusting trusting that the work you put in like prior to going out there to do those things like prior to going out there to put your foot in the ground, trusting the process with the um training staff and what they had set out for me, so when I got out here, I wasn't scared, you know, and I was talking to my doctor, Dr. Lowe, and I was just asking like he was just telling me let loose like and trust it and be you cuz it's 100% stable. So, when he told me that, I just came out and was putting my foot in the ground. I didn't care about it, tried not to think about it cuz during your process like the mental aspect of it is like the hardest thing you got to get over, so if I went out there like iffy about what I'm doing, then I probably would never be able to come back to what I want to be, so I was just out there just trusting it, putting my foot in the ground, trying to be explosive, and um it's working in my favor, so Nah, faith, faith and trust is what I started with with God, you know, putting all my trust and my faith in him and my belief to get back here like um man, like when I got hurt, I wrote the goal down to just be be better than what I left off, be better than what I left off that Chiefs game when I come back, I want to come back not like oh, it's going to be the same. I want to come back better than what I was, so that was never like a question in my head. And the thing I said was um when God want to build you up, he don't bring you comfort. So, he he put you through a storm. So, when I was in the storm, I just had my trust in him um knowing that I'd get back to where I want to be and just every every day getting 1% better, you know, working hard. Yeah, doing that. It'll It'll play out how it's supposed to, you know. Um we're going to take we're going to take steps to get where I want to go, but how I vision myself, man, I you know how I come, man. I'm trying to I'm trying to make plays. I'm trying to be a big factor on the team. Um I know I am. I know I will be. Just trusting in it and going out there and letting loose. So, God, you know, um trusting trusting God, you know, trusting his favor, trusting everything that he has set out for me, you know, his plans can't be denied. Um so, that's all it was just trusting trusting my process, trusting God, and I had a wonderful coaching staff and organization from top down from Hannah and um Cal to Nick, DeMeco, and the whole training room, um Roe, drugs, everyone, man. I had a a plan and and they was behind me 100%. They told me like take the time you need. We're going to be with you 100 like the whole time. And just work. So, I was a junkyard dog, man. I was just working all day. Um lot of y'all didn't see the work that I put in. I know y'all didn't see it, but every day I was working, man. Every day it wasn't one day that went by. On a Sunday I was working. It wasn't one day that went by that I wasn't out there or inside doing something to get better that day, and now I'm here, you know. >> get to this point, and now, like you said in the summer, if you see the light at the end of the tunnel, what does it look like to you this season, ideally? When do you hope to get out there, be able to do more, and play in a game again? >> Yeah, right now we're just taking it one day at a time. Um like I said, there's light at the end of the tunnel, for sure. I'll be out there, but we're just taking it one day at a time, so that's all we're doing. >> There's a lot of talk about the system. Is that part of the work as well? How comfortable are you in the system, the offense? >> As far as like knowing my plays? >> Yeah, knowing the plays. Is that something that you feel like you have to get some repetition before you step on the field? >> I feel like anything you do in life, you're going to have to get reps at it. Um so but as far as knowing my plays, I'm a student of the game, so every day like I'm in there, walk-throughs. Um I know y'all know OTAs, I was doing like walk-throughs, they was implement implement implement Damn. Yes, to the offense. So I was doing walk-throughs and stuff like that, and on my own, you know, I have like my brothers at home call the play out, and I just walk through it on my own, and so being a student of the game, that's easy for me, cuz I love it. He took a lot of the blame for this injury. God got me, like ease up, man. Go play go have fun, play football. I'll be back, so it was cool, you know, and it's no hard feelings. That's my brother, so we cool. >> What was the biggest moment or milestone in your recovery after you got hurt? >> Say that again. in your recovery that encouraged you again? >> Um probably touching grass for the first time. So, just going out there and putting my cleats on and tying them back up. >> You talked a lot with us about, you know, your hard work and coming back from that injury and getting back on the field. What has he meant to you in this long journey? >> Everything, man. Um this long process, he was with me the whole time. From the first day it happened to today, like long conversations. Y'all saw us off the court during our off season, like I was with him a lot, so it's the same like that's my brother like to the end, with or without football, so like you know how that goes, so he was with me the whole time. >> Do you think you'll be ready for week one then? >> Yeah, sir. We're going to take it day by day, baby. >> [laughter] >> Day by day, you heard me? >> And then um taking it off the field for a second, another Jags brother here. I know how close you are with CJ. I know how close you are with Nico, but you have a little brother who looks up to you a lot. What was What was it like going through the process, you know, knowing that he is one of your biggest supporters? >> Yeah, that was like that was like my little maid around the house when I couldn't walk for a little bit. He love to go out there and play football on his own with my brothers. title: No, The Minnesota Vikings Are Not Rigging Their QB Competition
text: Minnesota Vikings training camp reps have skewed quite a bit toward Kyler Murray, but does that mean this whole thing is rigged or is something more going on? >> You are Locked [music] On Vikings, your daily Minnesota Vikings podcast, part of the Locked On Podcast Network. First question comes from Curious Noticer who asks, "Purple Daily, Eagan, Will Ragatz, etc. have all pointed out that the share of reps with the first team versus second team and the split of them between McCarthy and Murray during this competition suggests that Murray is head and shoulders in the lead. But is that really the case? McCarthy has played against the first team defense far more. If Murray was actually winning the competition, wouldn't you at minimum expect him to start warming up with a center that will more often be snapping him in the ball as well as getting Brandel more used to a smaller QB. Of course, the idea that McCarthy has consistently done warm-ups with Brandel." So, this also kind of points to a a take that I've seen around somewhere which and that people have put in like my YouTube comments, too, which is that this whole thing is rigged. McCarthy of bad-itis and that this whole thing is actually rigged to to to favor Kyler Murray and make him look super super good because we really want Kyler Murray to win or whatever. And that I don't think that's the case. So, a couple of things here. Kevin O'Connell was actually asked exactly this question. Hey, looks like it hasn't been 50/50. Looks like it's pretty consistently skewed toward Kyler Murray. The ratio, by the way, has been pretty consistently 2/3 of the first team reps go to Kyler Murray and 1/3 go to JJ McCarthy. And conversely, 2/3 of the second team reps go to JJ McCarthy, 1/3 of the second team reps go to Kyler Murray. So, when you add it all together, they're both getting about the same amount of work, but JJ McCarthy is working with the second team more often. But, there's a couple things. I don't know if he has gone against the first team defense more often, just a lot more often than you would usually see the second team do, but I don't know. It's I I I I don't know if twos versus ones has been more common than twos versus twos. It's just been a much more dynamic mix than usual. I mean, they've gotten centers ready in terms of snap chemistry and um especially like under center and all that stuff in a week. This shouldn't be that hard of a thing. However, the idea that Kevin O'Connell put forth is that JJ McCarthy getting a lot more like when you're with the second team, whether you're McCarthy or Murray, the question is can you elevate bad talent around you, right? Like the idea that they're they're giving Kyler Murray all these reps.
