What do you hope your teammates took from what you said? >> Uh I just wanted to talk to off- the off- the offense and just have a man-to-man conversation. Like, we got to understand this is a business and uh we got to take what we do personal. We got to take pride in it and we got to do it to the best of our ability, regardless uh if we're calling plays to beat the defense or not. We're not calling plays to beat the defense. We're calling plays that we we want to use throughout the year and we're trying to get better at those plays and whether we win the down or not, are we doing everything that we can do to execute the play call? Are we doing our job on the O-line? Are we doing our job at the receiver? Are you at the right depth? Regardless if I have to check it down or it's a touchdown. Is everybody doing the right thing? That's what it's about, building confidence in those things. So, when we get in those moments and we need them, we just revert to our training. >> How long have you been comfortable taking a step like that, getting up in front of everybody the way you did? >> It's just a conversation, more than anything. I don't know if you need some super courage or anything else. These are the people I work with every day. I go to work with. We're in the weight room. We've been together what, 6 months already? So, it's just talking to the guys. >> Malik, I got a two-part question for you. Number one, what part of your what percentage of your game would you say the run game is? 40%? 50%? And number two, will we ever see it before the season opener, understanding that Half wants you to stay in the pocket for part of training camp and then preseason, maybe you don't play that much, etc. So, what what percentage and will we see it before the opener fully integrated? >> Number one, I wouldn't say a percentage. You try to just take what the defense gives you, really. And uh try to do the best to like I said, execute the play. And whenever an opportunity arises to go and get a first down, you want to try to do that. More first downs you stack, the closer you get to the end zone. Uh and two, uh I'm not sure. I I so. Uh not until you play real games, then you got to protect yourself and obviously play football. That's what we we're here to do. >> What what advice did you get as a young player that really sat well with you? And what advice do you give young players now that that will help them during this process? >> Stay confident uh regardless of the situation because you are here for a reason. Obviously, there's only so many NFL football players and you're one of them, so you got to have that same mindset like the only thing that's different from the guy that's getting paid however much money and a rookie coming in is they've been in it a little longer. You know, they're a little older. They've seen a little bit more stuff, but the physical ability uh all the guys can play. >> Any other questions? >> Yesterday, halfway talked about having an unscripted practice. What were you able to take away from that that differs from a typical scripted practice? >> Uh it challenges the guys. They don't know what's coming, so uh obviously, they can't study really hard on just a certain play or a certain uh scheme, but they got to be ready to run whatever's called just like a true game or a true scenario where like we were going to second uh down into third down pass and we didn't have the third down pass script it. We had the second down pass or the second down play script it, so they knew going in what we were going to try to run and they just got to react to the situation like a true game. You don't know how many yards somebody's going to get on a run play or how many yards they're going to get on a pass play in second and long. >> Some days I've noticed your shoes. Can you give us the the story of did somebody design them for you or what what is the story on your shoes? >> Uh you know, they just fit the feet, they cover them and whatnot. Nah, but they're some shoes, you know, they're cleats. That's always good. >> [laughter] >> Yeah. Uh nah, but for real for real, Jordan uh love, he uh he put me on to like you can just get some cleats with any on anything on them and we would take them from like sneakers. So, he had the off-white ones last year and then I got a pair of those and we was we had those and then this year I picked another a different pair of shoes and just put them on my normal cleat. Uh it's a pair Air Force Ones. They're silver with the uh sparkles like that and uh I just put them in our colors.

title: Coach Jeff Hafley meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: New blood. >> Everybody have a nice day off? >> Great day. >> Yeah, sir. Does everybody know to everybody say happy birthday to Ann? >> Happy birthday. >> Ann and Sully. >> Did everybody say happy birthday to Sully today? >> When we see him, if we see him. >> Happy birthday Sully if you see him. >> Happy birthday Ann. Happy birthday Sully. >> Happy birthday Ann. >> How about that? Sully and Ann have the same birthday. All right, we have more Come on in. >> [laughter] >> Before you enter, you got to wish Ann a happy birthday. >> Oh, happy birthday Ann. How are you? >> And you got to wish Sully one if you see him today, too. >> Will do. >> So, that means nice articles today. >> Sully's >> That's the only thing I write. >> Be nice to Ann today. All right, anybody else coming that we have to So, if anybody walks in, you guys know the drill. Okay? >> Thanks, Ann. >> Happy in the transcript. >> All right, what do we got? >> I have a couple of uh >> Injuries? >> Yes. You love this. >> Of course. Let me ask you Can I ask you a question? When you guys get together, does everybody say you got the injuries? Is that like >> No, no, no. Actually, uh Yes, you usually take care of everyone he sees. >> We like to do the housekeeping first. >> All >> Gonzalez, Juju Brentz. >> Yeah, I would say Zane will be week to week. Um Juju, I don't think Juju will practice this week. Um but I don't think it's going to be anything long-term. But I would if I wanted to play it cautious, I would say Juju will be out this week. Anyone else? >> Kevin Ford? >> He'll be a few weeks. Yeah. He he will not be practicing today. He'll be a few weeks. Gosh, that's a lot of typing. Anybody else? >> Any Anything known on any of the guys who have been out, Kevin Coleman Jr., Dante Fowler? >> Yeah, uh I I don't expect for Coleman, I don't expect him this week. Um Sims getting close. I don't think he'll practice this week. And who's the other one you asked? >> Dante? >> Dante, I don't think he'll practice this week, either. They're getting close. Hopefully next >> By the time we're talking to you here before the game on Friday night, what what are your plans far as playing starters or or not playing them? >> Everybody who is on our team right now needs to be ready to play. That that's how I see it. Like, truthfully, what I'd like to see is um how many reps each guy gets in the Washington practice, right? And who comes out of the Washington practice healthy. The Washington practice is really important to me. I think it's a really good time with where we're at in the competition. Uh not really to evaluate the team, okay, but to evaluate the individuals. Now, I think you always want to evaluate everything, so I say that loosely, but I think it's an important time to go uh against a different color jersey, different stimulus, um change of environment. I think that's a really, really good opportunity to see, you know, where some of our guys are at in these competitions that we have. So, I want to maximize the reps in that practice. So, for example, if a player were to get 40-plus reps in practice, which might be a little bit high with only a day in between, how much can I really play him? Can we really play him in a preseason game 2 years later? We got to be safe there, right? So, what I'd like to do so we can kind of end those questions of who's playing is, let me see where we're at after the practice. I'd like for everybody to be available to play, and then if I have to pull certain guys or dial down certain guys based on the reps that they got in that Washington practice, then we'll do so. Make sense? >> Yep. >> So, I'll probably I'll I'll have a better answer to that Wednesday night at some point when we figure all that out. And that's just me being honest. >> Do you have a different, I guess, evaluation scale for rookies versus veterans in the joint practices? >> No. Not at all. It's I don't look at anything different between the rookies and the veterans in the competition scaled all right now. I just I want to see where our guys are at against different players and who can go up against a different color jersey and elevate themselves. Um and I'm very, very excited to see that. >> Raheem led the NFL in yards per rush last year. >> Okay. >> Um does that provide some level of encouragement relative to what the team might be able to accomplish in the run game this year? >> Yeah, for sure. I I mean, I think Raheem is a dynamic player. I think he's one of the best at his position in the game, whether it's in the backfield or catching the ball from the backfield, lining up as a wide receiver, wherever we put him. Um so, I'm excited about that. >> And sticking with Raheem, what kind of little things have you seen him done away from the practice field or even on the practice [clears throat] field since signing this contract that just make you feel even more confident in giving him that extension? >> Well, I think when you watch him that you watch him the backfield, I think it's his vision, it's his acceleration. I think what's overlooked with Achane is how smart of a player he is, and I've said that before. You can have some really awesome conversations with him about protection, about what he sees, about what the defense is doing. not just a really, really good football player, but a really smart football player. He's fun to be around. He's had a great attitude on the field. You know, there's times when him and I joke around, but then we have serious conversations, we go back and forth on what the defense was called, what the offense was called, and um what would would have worked, what I don't think would have worked, and um fun guy to be around. And then just I watch him help Hill in his own way go from player to player and and help them out and push them and lead them. I think he's growing as a leader, and we need him to do so. >> Did you remember the first time you were kind of exposed to his play? Like was it when he was in college or when do you remember first watching >> I remember it really well. It was 2 years ago when we were getting ready to play the Dolphins when I was in Green Bay. And I had not been exposed to him, and I said, "This is a guy that's not talked enough about in the NFL, and I don't understand why, and he's making me lose sleep, and I think he's the most dynamic player on the team." So, it's the first time, and just shh in my opinion, and I think I said it if if you go back and listen to my media, and I could be wrong, but I'm pretty sure I even made a statement like, "This guy should be talked about a lot more than he is cuz he's that good, and he should be considered right now along with the best backs in the NFL." >> You had a mic'd up that went out on our social channels the other day, and you talked to a lot of guys about taking chances in practice, being aggressive, using your length and pressing for cornerbacks on the outside. How do you develop the trust within players to allow them to maybe go outside their comfort zone, to maybe put bad tape out there? And then also, how do you How does that change the way you evaluate when they guys are trying new things in practice? >> Yeah, I mean, that's everything that I believe in. I mean, that's like when I talk about process over result. Um and that's all a of the process of practice. When we go out and practice, it to me, that's the time, like I made the example for the corner. Like some guys get so comfortable, right? And they're just they're so scared to make a mistake that they play things safe. How do you grow if you're going to make you're going to play things safe? That doesn't make any sense to me cuz you're comfortable or you don't want to look bad. It's not about looking bad. It's about like I really want you to try this technique because of who you are, because for that example, cuz you have length. Like try the technique. Sit in there. And if it doesn't work, that's okay. Try it again, all right? And then let's see if you can get better at it. Let's see what you can get away with in practice and don't worry about the result. Like worry about the process of getting better to be the best player you can be and not just being stuck like this because if you just go through anything in life, it's just nice and comfortable and I know it's okay, maybe not great, maybe not bad, you're not going to get any better. Like step out of your comfort zone. Don't worry about the results. That's what practice is for. That's why I get mad in practice. It's like I think bad coaching is when a guy gets beat and you just go up and you yell at him. Like no, like ask him, what did you do? What did you see? What did you try? Did it work? Let's go back and watch it on film. Like if you guys aren't running to the ball or he's lack of effort or physicality, then yeah, yell at him. But like this is where these guys get paralyzed in their minds and I just don't want that to happen. So when I see a long corner and I get a flashback, you're not using your length. Like step and punch and try something different. I think that's huge for everybody on our team. And it's just how we need to coach these guys. >> How is How is Bonner doing? >> Bonner's doing good. Very consistent. Very very quiet, very professional. And you guys have seen it. He he's made a lot of plays and it's not just like here or there. He's just really consistent right now. So he's a guy that I can't wait to see like line up in a one-on-one against another color jersey and third down cover another guy and um I'm very pleased with Bonner right now. >> After your defense is without two top defensive backs such as Juju Bruns and Dante Trader, do you expect the offense to take advantage and exploit that? Do you expect Malik to do that? Um what and and have you seen that? Did you see that on Saturday? >> Um I'm not really worried about that in practice right now. I mean there's so many things that are more important to me. Uh it's just in a game for sure. If somebody has a weakness, I think we need to attack it. And if we have a weakness, then what do we need to do? We need to figure out how to protect it whether we have to change scheme, do something different. But in practice right now, it's just the little things and the details and the next guy needs to step up and be able to you know, see if he can compete and take over. Those things are way more important to me. >> And sort of going back to I think it was your second answer, you know, how eager is this team to kind of I know you have the practice today, but get out to DC and get ready to maybe get chippy on the field. >> Yeah, I think anytime you're in camp this long and you keep going against the same guys and it kind of like let's be real, it kind of gets a little old and it starts to get a little chippy within itself cuz it's just day after day hitting the same guy and going up. I I think there's probably a huge level of excitement and I think for some of these young guys, there's probably some anxiety and I think that's really important get out of the way. Like as much as you can put them in different situations where there is some anxiety and they get uh they get anxious to see how they can handle that. It's even when we went in the stadium the other day. I mean, we put them in the locker room for an hour just to kind of give that pregame feel and you can see as I walked around, it felt like we were back in the season, back in a game. Then we went out in the stadium and there's some fans there, new environment and I said we're going to tackle and some guys got a little bit more. So you got to keep ramping that up so we get ready for the first game, but I'm excited for it. I I think that's a great question you should ask them today. >> What have you learned from Jaylen Sulber over the last few weeks or so? >> Um again, really good pro. I think he's had some really good moments and I kind of gave you this you guys the same answer the other day. Everybody just it's the consistency over time. Can they can they get all that done? But the one thing I know he's going to go out and he's going to work really hard every single day. Um I love the way he's blocking on the perimeter. I think he has a great attitude. I think he's really good with the young players and he's becoming dependable. >> How many periods did you go tackle with Saturday and did you get the desired result? >> We had two periods that we tackled. Um yeah, we got the desired results that we wanted. I got to see a different level of physicality. I think it cranked up. Um you know, whether it was a D-line, whether it was the wideouts blocking, the offensive line blocking. I got to see some guys tackle. We got to correct some guys in tackling situation. I think it's really important to understand that there's a lot that goes into it. I I think being a physical football team as you know is huge to us. Like we want to be a physical team. So I think you got to practice physical. Not all the time cuz I think there's a fine line, right? You need to balance, stay healthy, keep guys up. But then there's a safety. You got to you have to tackle in our game, right? And we need to teach how to tackle safely. There were some instances on film when guys were dropping their head and those are great coachable moments where we have to tackle in a safe way. You got to keep your head up. You got to see what you hit. So there were some really cool moments there. We got to see what I love in live periods is everybody thinks it's about like the running back and the O-line and the D-line. We got to see some wideouts like on a third and seven. Can you catch the ball and get the first down? And then if you're a corner, like in practice if it's third and five and a guy tags a guy at four yards, everybody thinks it's fourth down. All right, can you really make the tackle? Like who can make those tackles? And then I think it's important uh you mentioned live and I think all of a sudden the players are kind of like their heart start racing a little bit more. We got to do that on Friday. In my opinion, to make them do that the first time Friday is not fair to the players. I don't I don't think that's good coaching it for me. For other teams, I get it. I totally respect it, but just not for us right now. >> Speaking of your coaching, before training camp started, you kind of were saying you were going through checkpoints of where you want to be during certain times of training camp. Has that evolved as you get deeper and you're starting to see how the guys are kind of stepping up, building that confidence and that chemistry? >> For sure. I think right now we have how we want to practice, how we run to the football, how we're being physical. All that stuff I'm seeing. And now the next step is it's the details. It's the details within the scheme, right? Because we also need to be a team that does not have a lot of pre-snap penalties, does not have post-snap penalties, that does not go backward. We need to be a disciplined football team. And that's the next step that we really need to clean up as we go through these next 3 weeks of football. >> Pre-snap penalties have long been an [cough] issue with the Dolphins, it seems. How do you clean that up? Is it re-running a play if if a guy jumps or what do you do with it? >> Yeah, I I think it's an issue. I don't I don't think it's just an issue with the Miami Dolphins. I think it's an issue around the league. I mean, pre-snap penalties, it's All right, it's it's this early on in practice, right? So, I had this conversation with Bobby. Do you want to change the You want to change the count? Do you just want to have the quarterback go to the line and go on the first hut every single time? Because if you do that, you're not going to have many penalties. But do you want to change the count? Yeah, I want to change the count because if you don't change the count, the defense is going to tee off and get off the ball and it's going to be easy for the defense. Okay. So, then we want to change the count early in camp. Guess what? You're going to get the defense to jump or you're going to get your offensive tackle to jump, so you're going to see a lot of them. So, there's risk-reward and I'm okay with that right now. And that's what I told Bobby. If we're going to change the count and go on two, three on the first sound, we have to be willing early on to deal with some of those. But, to your point, now as we get going, we have to clean those up. You need to bring awareness to it. So, you've seen we've had officials at just about every practice, right? In my past experiences, when you don't do that and you might miss some as a coach or a player, you got to bring awareness to it. So, they're throwing flags. And then at night, it's consistently talking about it and showing them third and five just went to third and 10. We had a red zone play the other day that would have been a touchdown, but we were lined up and covered up with the tight end. It's called the guy out in the meeting and said, "Look, man, I love you, but you can't This was a touchdown. This is seven-point penalty. So, you got to bring awareness to it. And then if they continue, you got to take them out. And if that continues and you have those penalties where you're costing yourself big plays, you got to you got to find a different way to coach them. You got to find a different player, too. So, it's constantly just coaching it and preaching it and showing it. Um but, there's risk reward to what we want to do. >> I was looking at the Commanders defense and it looks a little bit better on paper, at least, than people are giving it credit for. I guess, what do you want to see out of Malik Willis, Devon Achane versus this defense? >> Just I I I I have a ton of respect for Dan Quinn as a defensive coach and as a head coach. Dan Quinn's teams are going to play great defense. I don't I don't know all the names on it, but I'd be willing to bet with Dan, they're going to play good defense. Um I'm just whether it's the Giants, the Falcons, I I don't care what team we play right now. I just that's just it it's again more process than result. And I know none of you guys want to hear that. I think you gave a great example of it. Um I just I want to see us go out and compete. I want to see us execute and be detailed and I I to see us be extremely physical and run and hit and and play the game clean. And I want to see us better against the Giants than we were against Washington. And I want to see us better against Atlanta than we were against the Giants. Because I just think we have to keep building this thing. So when it's all said and done, we're way better than we were when we started. That's the most important thing to me right now. >> I know what you said about penalties. I was curious to know, um how do you walk that line? And how long does it take you to make that determination we need to coach him better or he's not the guy and get rid of a guy? How How do you kind of go through that process? >> Put it more on the coaching and teaching and hopefully it never gets to that point. Um very rarely will I ever say it's the guy and he can't learn and he can't do this. I'm not big on that. I just I think we need to bring them along and bring them along and coach it better or find a new way to coach them or a new way to teach them. Um So hopefully it doesn't get to that point. I mean, if a guy is going to continually make us go backward, we need to we need to do whatever we can to fix that. But hopefully it does not get to that point. I think that's our job as coaches to teach, to walk through, to show on video, to be demanding, you know, to let them understand the importance of it. And hopefully we'll get to that point. Um That's like the last resort right there. >> Will you guys bring in a fourth quarterback? >> Better question for Sully. You want a fourth quarterback? >> We need one. >> Okay. Well, you and Sully can have that conversation. Happy birthday, Sully. >> Mhm.

title: Coach Jeff Hafley meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: gentlemen >> I got a little knee injury there half. I got to >> Can I ask? >> I'm very very sore. I'm out for a week. >> How did you do it? >> I'm out for a week to week. >> you do? >> But he's a full participant. >> What did you do? >> So I had a massage therapist and she was trying to I backed into [laughter] you. So she was trying to Guys, has this ever happened to you? So she brings my knee all the way to my chest and now I think I sprained my knee. >> [laughter] >> So I need a good Maybe that guy that's in charge of performance. >> We're we're live on the >> This is actually this So you're going to be out there today? >> Yeah. [laughter] >> Will you be in a red jersey? >> I'm only only doing it for a special day. >> Are they Are they going to Are they going to report on what they see and how fast you're running and when you're going to be back and >> I'm not ready to cut. >> Okay. >> All right. >> Thank you. >> I I hope you feel better. >> Thank you. I appreciate it. >> Half, I know you you still got one today, but uh what are you looking forward to for the stadium practice and getting the guys in that setting? >> I am looking forward to today. Today's going to be a hard practice. Today's a high day. Today's going to be a lot of unscripted move the ball, see where it lands, coaches call it, players respond without having the script. Because sometimes when you go into practice, the offensive defensive coaches can hand them the script, they can look at the plays, they can think about, "Oh, I'm in on this play, I can run it." Where today's really the first time that we're going to do a lot of we're just going to call it like a real game and they got to think and respond and the coaches have to do the same thing. So, first things first with today. Today's going to be a long hard practice and I'm looking forward to see how they respond to that. And then it'll be fun to get into the stadium. Um really, it'll be my first time in there. you know, in really any mode on the field. So, I'm excited for that. Um but it won't be like going through a game routine and doing the stretching and all that. I don't I don't want there to be any distractions and I don't want to take away from their routine. I think it'll be fun for the players with some fans there. It'll bring more excitement, more energy, more juice, closer to a pre- season game. Maybe some of the young guys will have some anxiety. but [clears throat] besides that, we have a lot of work to do and we cannot afford to make that anything else but a hard, good, productive practice. >> Coach, are you happy with what you've seen so far? You happy or satisfied with what you've seen so far from the team? >> [clears throat] >> There there's a lot of aspects that I'm really happy with and I am very satisfied with and there's others where we have a ways to go, if I'm going to be honest with you. I think the buy-in, the attitude, the effort, the strain, the how hard they're trying to do all of the little things that we ask to do. Guys are showing up on time, they're where they're supposed to be. I think they're connecting. I think we're building the foundation as far as our culture goes and what it wants to be. Um but we've got work to do. We've got work to do as coaches, we've got work to do as players, scheme, details, consistency. You know, just like everyone else around the league, there's there's injuries where you're trying to find out your depth and um So, I I think there's some things, yeah, like there's some nights I go to bed and I'm like really proud of of where we're at and how hard we're working and then you wake up and you're like, "Okay, we got a long ways to go." So, it's kind of a balance. >> Coach, can you give us an update on Dante Fowler? We noticed he didn't practice yesterday. >> Yeah, I would say he will not practice today. Um he'll be more day-to-day. I'm hopeful we'll get him back next week. There's nothing long-term with him. >> Coach, I'm curious with the with the cornerbacks. I know you had Revis a couple times, Sherman, Hayden. Out of those guys, is there a common thread or anything you learned specifically from those great corners that you try to apply to this group or in the past? >> Yeah, not only are they like the best ever play at their position. Um I mean, you just you mentioned one guy who's in the Hall of Fame and another one who will be in the Hall of Fame. Um They're it's it It's their mindset. Take away the talent. Like, those are some of the most talented guys ever play the game. I just think it's their mindset. When you think back to Revis and Sherman and some of those other guys you mentioned, it's the way they approach every day. It's if a ball was ever caught on them, it wasn't okay. Like, it was not good. If, you know, they missed a an assignment or the receiver, you know, even I remember in scout team, if like the receiver didn't give them the precise look, they had a problem with that because they wanted to be perfect and they wanted to get better and they wanted to be challenged. And if it was a walk-through and I was like, "All right, guys, this is a period where let them catch the ball. It's a walk-through." That wasn't okay with them and regardless of what I said, they just had this mindset that they weren't going to lose. They were going to compete on such a different level than everybody else and I just think that's really rare. Um and I think that's what separates the really talented players cuz there's a lot of them from you're talking about Hall of Fame guys. Um So, I was very fortunate to be around a bunch of those and throw Ronde Barber into the mix, another Hall of Famer, and you learn so much from them. Not how Not only how they play on the field, but how they approach the game. And those real guys will send you videos and texts at 11:00 at night and they're studying and they want to be better and they want to know about their opponent and there's just this It's just a different mindset that they have. >> Coach, I've got a social media question for you. Yeah. >> So, >> Are you a big social media guy? >> No, not at all. Not at all. Um, but I always ask the players about it. And so, I found out yesterday there's a group of your players that have decided to stay off of social media right now. You were a college coach, you're an NFL coach. So, three things, uh, is there a difference between college players and NFL players' use of social media? What do you tell your players in general about social media? And what have you told this group during training camp about social media? >> Well, there's certain things I don't want posted, you know, whether they're in the building or in the locker room or things that we say or things our coaches say. I think that's really important. What's said here stays here. This is a This is a place where I want peo- people to feel comfortable that what they can say is going to stay in the building and that's really important to me. Just like pictures in our locker room or pictures in our space. I think it's a very private space and really that's all that I touch on. When I have one-on-one meetings with guys, I mean, going back to college, I mean, there's so many guys that would come in my office and I'd be like, "What's going on, man? What's wrong?" And it's you know, social media. Guys are destroying them. Guys are beating them up. The whole world's telling them they can't play and that's when you really have to pick guys up and you try to tell guys to stay off of it and not listen, but let's be real, that's so much easier said than done. Right? Chris, what was like the one thing you felt like you needed to work on the most from last year to this year? >> Uh, I feel like definitely my my foot speed. It starts with the interior defensive line and and then you know it becomes a whole unit. You know it takes a whole unit to stop the run also but it starts with us up front and uh you know we got to lead the charge and then even in the pass rush game you know we got to be that middle push. Uh, so it all works as one, I feel like. >> On the the run game last year, I know the the total numbers said one thing, but kind of that per rush efficiency was there for y'all. What what >> uh I think, you know, just being more comfortable in the system. Uh whether it was the offense or the defense, you know, or the special teams. So, we was playing from behind a lot and uh you know, we tried to catch up and try to stop the run, but I feel like, you know, we did well, especially in our base package. Uh that was our main run stopper and I feel like this year we're going to take where, uh our nickel defenses got to take that next step to be able to stop the run with just four defensive linemen instead of five. Chris, >> what's it kind of like just being around watching Chase Young kind of doing his thing? >> Yeah. Uh what I take from Chase, I would say just, you know, he's a dog, you know, on that field. you know, he talk a lot of trash. So, you know, it's, you know, I got that dog personality, too. I'm sure you're >> Yes, sir. It felt good. Blessed for the opportunity. Um just a little hot out there, you know, has get out there first day back, but felt good. Good. What's kind of the um the adjustment been like for you getting into your actual training camp now as opposed to all the earlier workouts? >> Um for me it was kind of like just coming in learning from the Vex and taking everything in different techniques and everything. Um, I just seen the past game using the different techniques David Els taught me. I've been watching them since I was at or my last two years using some of the different techniques and kind of helped me in my game today. >> You talk about uh watching David Edwards. What was it about his game that drew you in and you wanted to learn from >> him being a very older guy? him. He's like a technician for me. Smooth, not overdoing it. For me, I know sometimes I'm aggressive guy, so I like I can overdo it sometime, but for him, just being under control, controlled aggression, and just get to my spot and like I say, I'm a big guy. Nobody going to be ready to go down the middle of me. So, just being able to hone me in on the details, small things help me. you talked about your uh your technique and whatnot, but um what's like the process been like also of just, you know, kind of getting up to speed with this offense and the expectations, all that. It was similar to what I had at Auburn. So like kind of thank you to my coach then for helping me, you know, stay ahead of the game. But just coming in just ready to work. How does it felt for you just coming out here and having some success winning and then some one-on- ones and just like feeling it and being able to do it, you know, at the public? >> Like I say, I just go out there and be me. Remember my why. Go out there and dominate. I don't go out there and be timid and frigid and everything. I just go out there and just be Jay, right? >> Who's your why? >> My why, my family. Just my family. I'm big on family. That's another reason why I chose to go to Auburn. And just all about family. I was talking to Brandon Nougat. Is that >> Yes, sir. Like I said earlier, that's like controlled aggression. Me just being aggressive sometimes and just got to be able to play under control. I've pretty much been doing a good job on that. Learning from the old guys and the vets. I don't say old guys, the vets, you know. But yeah. [laughter] How confident are you in in you know your ability to come in and be plugged in once the season you know comes around and and make a contribution you know right away to this offense? What makes you very confident that you can you know do that for this team? >> Another reason why they drafted me coming here and help the team win be a mer and yes just be confident be right. DNS sometime the different um I just say defensive looks that they give us different personnel. It's just all about knowing who you going against and yeah, you hate to see teammates get hurt going against. How has this been a um like how do you do this like the Jags and the Rams and and then uh Dallas all of a sudden different competition. So there not much film you can watch. Just go out there and compete and >> yeah just go out there and compete. Be me or go out there try to overdo nothing. Go out there and be Jay Wright. I'm always just BJ Wright. Loud vocal guy. Uh love to express myself. That's me. You going to hear Jay Wright on the field. win, lose or draw, you going to hear me. So, just going out there, being under control, learning from my teammates, and going out there and compete, be the best version of me that I can be. >> I know you don't want to see teammates get injured, but how much do you look forward to the the increased rep, you know, practice, you know, joint practices, preseason games. >> Um, looking forward to it. You know, going up against a different team and and getting to practice against other NFL guys. How much do you think that could be helpful for you and your development being a young guy in the league? >> Yeah, very helpful because, you know, we going against each other each and every day. Um, know the cadences and everything. So going against different team, getting different looks, going against different guys, learning different, you know, moves and just different techniques and stuff I can try and go out there and and learn from that. >> You say you like to talk, what do you say inside? >> What do I say? Uh, you kind of like got to come out here and watch practices know what I say. Uh, right now I'm kind of like me, a big bear. Uh, all smile, jolly. Don't take it for granted. >> What you do in the talent show? >> Um what I did in the talent show, I saw Alicia Keys. This girl is on fire. >> Did you get Did you get a big applause after that? >> Yeah, I definitely did. Definitely did. Went good. Went good. How y'all doing? >> We just heard from Jeremiah about his talent show. >> What did you do for the talent show? >> Uh I did uh Magic by Charlie Wilson. >> Yeah. Yeah. Um, the experience was awesome. I mean, just getting back on the field. I think that was the first time I've played real football on the field in like two and a half years, I think it was. So, for me, it was just getting back on the field, uh, getting a feeling for it and really just just getting comfortable playing on the football field again. So, that was it was a great experience. >> Did you have to ask for seven? >> No, I did not ask for seven. No, no, I did not. That was not something I I planned at all. >> So, you didn't have to run it by chase? No, I actually had no when I came back, I had no idea I was getting that number. >> How do you feel being in the ball? It's kind of sad. >> Yeah, I mean obviously Taesm is means so much to this this this team. Um, so it's something obviously that is super important. Uh, but it's it's a really cool feeling, but it's obviously something you have to live up to for sure. >> How maybe, but how did your UFFL stand go? How did you feel like that? >> Oh, it was great. Um, just playing football again was awesome. Obviously getting injured wasn't wasn't on the was on the plan, but when I was playing, it was awesome. It was it was one of the best things I could have done. >> You got her in your back, right? >> Yes. Yes. Yes. I was out I think four or five weeks with a AC joint uh sprain on my throwing shoulder, but when I came back, yeah. So, I played I think three more games after that. >> How did you feel like you like accomplished the most? Like was it just getting live reps or aspects of your game you felt like not? >> Um, honestly, I would just say getting live reps was the biggest thing going back there. Uh, but just getting just getting the comfortability of being back in a pocket um during a live setting was something that I really wanted to get and I felt I felt that I accomplished that there for sure. >> What do you feel like you learned the most from your year here that you were able to apply in the UFFL and was different for you? >> Um, I would just say the knowledge of the uh of football. I mean, being sitting here for a whole year uh studying defenses, studying our offense, um, was something that I think helped me tremendously going into that league. What's it like like being in the classroom and then not being able to go out in the field and apply it and then kind of like on home waiting to Yeah. show all these lessons and everything. >> Yeah. Um I think to a certain extent that kind of plays a part into the backup position at quarterback. Um not everyone's going to get a bunch of reps. So I think um it's just something you kind of have to understand. You kind of have to stay ready cuz you don't know when your number is going to be called. Uh so I got to prepare like I'm [snorts] the starter each week because when I go when I go in I can't be messing up the play calls. I can't be messing up anything. I got to go in there and act like I know it. And so that's something I got to take pride in for sure. >> And there was like the every other week every at least like back. >> Yeah. What are the logistics of that? Like are you like do you have an apartment you're just staying in and like knowing you're coming back or like what's >> Yeah, I had I had an apartment here already. So uh it was something where it was kind of just a waiting game. Um it was it was unfortunate but it was something that obviously I was willing to do and that was kind of just a waiting game. You >> feel like the communication though was like you knew you were coming back? Um yeah, we were we I communicated uh with the whole organization, so we were all on the same plan. >> You kind of look forward to the preseason games when you you know might get more opportunities. >> Definitely. Definitely. No, that's something that I'm definitely looking forward to. Um if I get the opportunity to play, uh definitely going to be ready for that. >> Did you uh get to I guess y'all watch Drew's speech. Y >> uh how was that? What was your impression? >> Man, that was uh one of the coolest things we could have done um as a full team. just just watching that and listening to him uh listening to the stories um is something that is super super cool to watch. >> Hey man, >> appreciate you guys.

How did your UFL stint go? >> Oh it was great. Um just playing football again was awesome. Obviously getting injured wasn't wasn't on the wasn't on the plan, but when I was playing it was awesome. It was it was one of the best things I could have done. >> You got hurt and then came back, right? >> Yes, yes. Yes, I was out I think four or five weeks with a AC joint uh sprain in my throwing shoulder. But when I came back yeah. Felt like constantly >> Um honestly I would just say getting live reps was the biggest thing going back there. Uh but just getting just getting the comfortability of being back in a pocket um during a live setting was something that I really wanted to get and I felt I felt that I accomplished that there for sure. >> What do you feel like you learned the most from your year in the UFL that you were able to apply in the NFL in the future? >> Um I would just say the knowledge of the the of football. I mean being sitting here for a whole year uh studying defense and studying our offense um was something that I think helped me tremendously going into that league. >> What's it like like being in the classroom and then not being able to go out and be able to fly it? >> Yeah. Yeah. I think to a certain extent that kind of plays a part into the back up position at quarterback. Um not everyone's going to get a bunch of reps. So I think um it's just something you kind of have to understand. You kind of have to stay ready cuz you don't know when your number's going to be called. Uh so I got to prepare like I'm the starter each week because when I go when I go in I can't be messing up the play call like can't be messing up anything. I got to go in there and act like I know it. And so that's something I got to take pride in for sure. >> And there was like the every other week there was at least like that. >> What are the logistics of that? No that's something that I'm definitely looking forward to um if I get the opportunity to play. Uh definitely going to be uh ready for that. >> Did you get to I guess y'all watched Drew Brees >> Yep. >> Uh how was that? title: TJ Hall Press Conference | Saints Training Camp Day 10
text: I think it's something Jeremy I had about his talent show. >> Yeah, yeah. >> What did you do for the talent show? >> Uh I did magic by Charlie Wilson. Yeah, yeah. We start with tackle the ball, punch outs, you know, try to get that ball back for the L. >> Do you try to translate that mentality in the passing game? >> Yeah, definitely. Yeah, definitely. If If they get a catch, as soon as they turn, we want to punch that ball out, you know what I'm saying? Make them regret catching the ball. >> Appreciate you, man. >> Appreciate you, too. Yeah, yeah. >> [laughter] >> Yeah. Uh so, my dad played for Don Patterson at Western Illinois, who was a coach for Iowa. And uh during the process, you know, we reached out, sent my film over to the Iowa coaches, and they ended up reaching back out, and kid from Fresno ended up all the way in the Big Ten in Iowa. >> Have you gotten used to this summer heat here? >> Yes and no. title: Marcus Jones & TreVeyon Henderson Talk 2026 Patriots Training Camp on NFL Network
text: All right, we got a party here after the joint practice. Marcus Jones, Tayvon Henderson. Guys, thank you very much. I don't know who wants to start, but how good was it to hit somebody else? >> Oh, um, it it was great. Um, just out the fact of seeing, you know, a different offensive scheme and everything from our end. Uh, and then letting guys see things they never seen before. Um, Indie is a great organization, you know, great, um, people and players and everything like that on that side. So, it was great to compete for sure. Yeah, like Marcus said, um it was great. Um we had a good time competing with the Colts. Uh they got a great defense, gave us some different looks, and it was good to just compete compete against um some different guys. And so we we enjoyed it today. >> Trey, we know linebackers like to hold. >> There's a lot of holding going on today. You don't have to be shy about it. Linebackers can't cover. They're there to stop the run. You guys had a great drill, though, with one-on-one pass rush and then you guys went into one-on-one pass routes. Uh you did an awesome job. explain to us kind of the the the mindset going into that and and then what was the execution of it? >> Yeah, I think the biggest thing uh we we know what they expect. Uh we know sometimes that the linebackers are going to hold and so I mean it's good for us as well. You know, we got to work through that. We got to be physical because at the end of the day sometimes ref they see it, sometimes they don't. And so the coaches don't really care. They want you to get open. So, um it was just good to get some work against the linebackers though. >> This was a pretty physical practice. How have things been? We all hear about Super Bowl hangovers for teams that don't win that it's hard for the team to get back up. How has the team been just in these first few weeks of training camp? >> Yeah. Um it's been great. You know, we know and everyone has said it before, we're now the hunt when it comes down to that. Um but taking it one day at a time is our big motto. Uh understanding that u we want to make sure it's effort and finish every single time that we do stuff. Do the little things right and just stay disciplined. Take it one day at a time is the most important thing. And don't look too far. Stay where our feet are. I have to ask you uh Marcus, a couple years ago you were getting some offensive snaps. Terrific return guy. Give me some for that because returners we we don't we don't get enough love for the return game. But I didn't see you on offense last year. Well, are we going back to McDaniel saying, "Hey man, like I I could do this, too. Give me a bubble screen. Give me a little Oregon screen, receiver screen inside." >> Yeah. No, it's funny cuz people always, man, when are we going to get that? And um it's funny, man. However I can help the team, I'm definitely down for it. Um, I've been like that ever since my rookie year and I'm still like that. So, you know, I have I'm a priority and I always let everyone know I'm a defensive guy first. But, um, whenever I do get the ball in my hand on part return, that's my that's my offensive snaps for me. So, >> I don't want to I don't want to kick off returns, too. Yeah. Yeah. Return guys. The returners are here. Uh, for you, Trayvon, you're competing, right? Raandre Stevenson, you guys had a great duo last year. What was it? What was your off seasonason like? And how do you feel your your reps are going to be? Is it going to be 50/50? Is it going to be where he got banged up last year? You took over and did some great things. Uh what is the expectation for you expectation for you Co going into year two? >> Honestly, um I just try to come in each and every day and just try to earn a role on this team. Uh do whatever the coaches ask for me. Just look looking for ways to get better um and enhance my game. And yeah, having Mandre in the room, it's it's great because you know, we compete every day and we make each other better better. And so um I don't know how things are going to go this season, but I just know I'm going to just continue to come to practice each and every day. Mandre will as well and just continue to push each other, man. And so I'm happy to have him in the room and play alongside of him. >> They're using you more in the passing attack we saw earlier in camp. Deep passes to you. Is that something you're comfortable with? Do you want more of that kind of role, too? >> Um, I mean, like I said, it's just, you know, whatever whatever opportunities the coaches give me. Um, I'm going just continue to look to improve in every aspect of my game, whether that's running the ball, catching the ball, blocking. Um, and yeah, when opportunities come, just try my best to take advantage of them. You guys are going in the red zone here, Marcus, and uh it was very competitive. Tyler, we just interviewed Tyler Warren. He talked about how it's a lot of contested catches. Was that something you guys were looking forward to going against an offense that tries to attack the middle of the field? And then how how was it for you all? >> Yeah. Um it's been great. You know, especially whenever it comes down to we know that we has we have to have tighter coverage when it comes down to the red zone. Uh the windows are tighter and then also, man, we're always trying to compete and contest when it comes down to it. Uh you never know what play it might be. Uh coach always talk about effort and finish because you fly to the ball, the ball might go in the air and then it's a turnover. So you know uh it was great because Indie they do a lot of pick routes when it come down to it. So those are things that we have to practice and get ready for cuz those were things that you know whenever we got in the red zone last year teams were doing that and they had success and then later during the year we kind of caught on. So we're trying to make sure to implement those things and understand what the offense is trying to do. >> Marcus Trevian, thanks so much for joining us. Can't wait to watch you during the season. Appreciate

title: Drake Maye & the Patriots Compete in Joint Practice vs. the Indianapolis Colts at 2026 Training Camp
text: The Patriots and Colts got after it today for joint practices and there was a lot going on. We're going to try to break it all down for you. Let's do it. >> [music] >> Welcome everybody to the Patriots Camp Cast presented by New Balance and yes, the Patriots and Colts were out there guys for joint practice today. A lot going on both fields coming fast and furious. Paul, what were you >> Head on a swivel Mike. Lot to watch. I thought I thought there was some good work really all around. I I you know, I always think back I joked when we did our PU you know, podcast earlier during the practice that you know, I I I base everything off of that Philadelphia Eagles one here in Gillette Stadium where it was like, "Oh my god, we're in trouble." Nothing like that. You know, there was some periods of time that I thought the Patriots looked really good. Thought Drake Maye got settled in you know, for for some periods and there were other times I thought quite frankly he got a little sloppy with the ball. I thought his mechanics maybe got away from him. He's a little casual. Defensively I I I I would say similar. I thought there were some open receivers but I thought they were pretty physical up front. I didn't think they they they allowed themselves to get gashed a lot and with Jonathan Taylor he did crease them a couple of times. Dangerous guy but overall I thought it was pretty even. >> Yeah, as he is known to do. Yeah, I mean overall though Drake Maye sticking on that side is pretty good start for him. >> Yeah, I thought he the explosiveness of the passing game was there. He made a handful of downfield completions. Maybe not consistent every single throw like Paul was talking about but a really nice go ball to Romeo Dobbs along the sideline. Couple of play action shots to the tight ends Henry Reardon. AJ Brown down the sideline for another one. So it was that big play Maye stuff that we're so used to seeing but the Colts got the last laugh. They got the exclamation point. Their starting offense and Daniel Jones drove right down and I'm sure we'll talk about Tyler Warren here in a second and scored and the Patriots ended with an interception. So I I know everybody's going to declare a winner of practice in a lot of these wrap-ups. I guess the Colts got the the last laugh there at the end. >> Just a few names to throw at you guys I thought stood out. Pop Douglas continuing his really solid camp, had a bunch of catches including down at that last team period. You know, we're seeing Eli Rerdan continue just, you know, not a ton of volume but ones, twos popping up a little bit for him and then at a point probably the play of the day Tommy DeVito again downfield to Kyle Williams who had a really nice day another really nice catch. >> I mean I would agree with all of the things that you pointed out. I would throw Romeo Doubs in there. The play that Evan referenced to me was vintage Doubs. He's just, you know, kind of a fade down the sideline, down the field effortless. The hands are so strong. You put it on him and he's going to catch it. He doesn't need a ton of separation. He had a little on that play. But I think that he's starting to to stack days now. We're starting to see the guy from Green Bay on a more consistent basis. >> Yeah, he I agree. He shook a Colts defensive back in the end zone during the red zone work as well and scored there. I think two days in a row we Romeo Doubs looks more comfortable. Looks like Drake Maye is understanding the routes that he wants to be running and where he wants to be targeted on the field. I thought the go ball is a just a great example. The Colts loaded up with pressure on the line of scrimmage, showed a bunch of pressure. They had Henry and Ramondre in the backfield together to pick up the pressure and then it was just go routes on the outside and just pick take your pick with no safety a deep and he hit Doubs on the sideline. So, some good answers to pressures, you know, take your shots when you get that cover zero look and Doubs has just been better and better. >> Yeah, Mondre did some good things today too as well. Couple catches for him in the end zone as well. >> Blitz beaters, you know, and that's something we've been talking about all summer. You know, they can't they still seem like they're struggling with some of those overload blitzes. Well, that's the best way to make teams stop doing it. >> Yeah, and then on the defensive side of the ball of course the headline we didn't see Christian Gonzalez today. This point we're not sure exactly. Did land hard yesterday after that contested catch in the end zone by Doubs. Maybe an ankle injury. We don't know. We know his contract is up in the air, but certainly without him. Carl Davis was back, but he didn't participate. Felt like the Patriots defensive backs, they were down the depth chart a little bit. They They were having some trouble. >> Yeah, it was a funny day, right? It was the you know, none of the Patriots I mean Marcus Jones really was the only corner that you would expect to see out there regularly for the Patriots. And virtually none of the receivers for the Colts other than Tyler Warren who's a tight end. Um and I thought if if we're going to compare backups here, I thought the Colts backups got the better of the Patriots backups. They were open consistently. >> Yeah, I would say it was kind of a wash cuz Josh Downs did practice against Marcus Jones. So you kind of wash that one out and then it was backup receivers against backup corners on the outside. I I would just highlight Warren. Uh we kind of knew this was coming Deuce because last summer it was T.J. Hockenson in Minnesota doing the same thing to the Patriots defense. And that two-minute drill by Daniel Jones, all three plays to get them down there on the goal line were all Tyler Warren, you know, over the ball, wheel route down the sideline. And he was open consistently and then Downs, you know, got the actual touchdown. But I I think covering tight ends in this scheme in this defense, I still feel like it's a little bit of a enigma of how exactly they want to plan for guys like Tyler Warren. Uh you know, you he's a rare breed. Like he's one of the best tight ends in football, but it's still something you got to worry about. >> Mike, I felt a little like you uh on the field after practice. Um you know, Tyler Warren was probably about 20 ft away from me and I I think I had Derrick Henry vibes from you. That dude was big. >> Yeah, he he's a specimen, but you know, no Gonzales, no Davis, no Christian Barmore up front for the Patriots defense. So they were missing some key players on defense. The Colts didn't have Alec Pierce, but the other receivers were out there. >> Yeah, let's just talk about that last two-minute drive too for Drake, which I don't know what you saw. I have I was a little bit blocked by the pole there as he launched up that final pass, but he did throw an interception to close out that period. >> Yeah, looked like again they they showed pressure inside and someone on the interior, I couldn't tell exactly who, but it was in the inside got immediate pressure and kind of rocked him back off his spot and then he tried to go to his right and kind of reload and reset and throw the ball. I thought he had Douglas, but it was going to be a tight window. Like he was going to have to really fit it over the safety, but because he kind of threw off platform a little bit, he didn't have enough on the ball and and Cam Bynum ended up picking it off. So, probably one he said it after practice that he thinks it was second down. Probably one you throw out the back of the end zone and and live to play another play. >> I'm looking back. I I I cuz I took note of his explanation. He sort of made it out to be kind of a desperation play. There was 24 seconds left. You know, it was second and 13. So, it wasn't quite you know, do or die. And I I just think it was a bad throw. I mean, he underthrew him. I thought I thought Douglas was open. >> What's the thing I feel like we've done enough of these joint practices where if you don't get lost in the details, it's up, it's down. It's just it's just really good work for these guys to go against another team, to go against another scheme. There were some ups and downs for both sides of the ball, but over overall, I think they go back there with a lot of film to break down and a lot of good stuff happened >> I'll bet both coaching staffs are pretty pleased with what happened. There wasn't really a a ton of, you know, John back and forth. There was a little here and there, but not a ton. I thought they got some good reps for a lot of different guys. >> Yeah, it was just a little competitive. Like I thought both sides kind of traded punches, not literally, figuratively. And that was pretty clean. Like Paul mentioned off the top that Eagles joint practice was so one-sided. All over the field, offense, defense, whatever. This one felt a lot more like the one we were in Minnesota last year, Deuce, where it was like, yeah, the Vikings made some plays, the Patriots made some plays, the Colts made some plays this here today, but I I thought overall, like I said at the beginning, I thought Drake Maye was really good until the pick at the end, you know, and that that kind of puts a sour note on it. >> Yeah. All right. Well, Mike Vrabel also said we probably won't see Drake Maye on Thursday night against these Colts, but hey, first preseason game of the season getting underway. Be sure to tune into the Patriots pregame show with Paul and myself and a new cast that we have. We're excited to introduce everybody to that new cast. We'll see you on Thursday night.

title: New England Patriots Prepare for Joint Practices With the Indianapolis Colts at 2026 Training Camp
text: The Patriots are back on the practice fields after 2 days off as they get ready for joint practices with the Indianapolis Colts. Let's break it down. >> [music] >> Welcome everybody to the Patriots Training Camp Cast presented by New Balance and yes, we had a weekend off. We're back on the fields today. Intensity dialed down a little bit after a bunch of padded practices in a row. Paul, I'd say this was as you said walking off the field, maybe putting things in place to have a good practice tomorrow against the Indianapolis Colts. >> Yeah, that's what it looked like to me. It was some prep work for what they're going to see with the Colts. It looked like the first offense and defense were working separately against you know, some of the backup players. My inference there would be that they were probably running against Colts stuff on both sides. I thought the tempo was a little slower as well even when they did you know, ones against ones later on. A lot of red zone work with that some two minute stuff, some situational work. So all in all, you know, kind of uneventful but you know, you got you got to have you got to cross these days off. >> It's coming together. >> Yeah, I'd say most of practice was at best three quarter speed. Like they weren't going full speed but first scout team type of stuff as Paul said I thought of really training camp and not only the practice tomorrow but a lot of these guys are obviously going to play on Thursday night in the preseason opener too. So you don't want them going in completely cold without knowing at all what the Colts are going to run and what they're going to do. So not a full game prep like you will see in the regular season but they at least get a little bit of taste of what Indianapolis is going to bring here tomorrow. >> So you know, a couple of highlights. Carl Davis being back was exciting. It was good to see that but for the most part it was more about participation and attendance than what actually happened. >> I was a little surprised to see Davis based on what My Grewable said on Friday about not seeing him till the end of next week. Maybe he meant more in terms of you know, the full full Carl Davis cuz he did little more than positional stuff today. >> Yeah, no no Christian Barmore as well. That's the second practice he's missed. Charles Woods wasn't out there. Kendal Vickers taking his snaps. I thought he had a couple nice plays there down in the red zone. Also thought Eli Haroldson getting some chances. The two tight ends set down in Caught some caught some passes there from Drake. But again, a lot of rotation going on with these guys. So, it's hard to like, you know, really discern who's rising, who's falling, all that kind of stuff. But it is obvious who's getting the chances with Drake Maye. I think that's what's, you know, most important. But Eli Haroldson, and we got to mention too, of course, Hunter Henry signing a two-year extension today, reportedly. So, Haroldson now in the mix, maybe. I think we'll probably see a lot of him over the next couple days, you know, tomorrow and then into the preseason. >> Yeah, I mean, I think it is, you know, we keep talking about the cliche of, you know, Haroldson is more of a pass catcher, you know, Arkin is more of the blocker. So, you're starting to see now when it's two tight end looks and it's Haroldson and Henry, it's probably spread, you know, maybe some some some passing going on. When Arkin's out there, a lot of first downs that we've seen in these team periods have featured Tanner Arkin. Obviously, you're looking more to the run game. So, probably looking to get some of those trends bucked a little bit, figure out some ways around it. But yeah, I think Haroldson is is made some slow but steady progress, if that's fair. >> Yeah, I would say the same thing about Romeo Dobbs. Just little baby steps each day. It's not, you know, gangbusters quite yet, but I think that he's getting a little bit better and better each day. And I see Drake Maye figuring him out a little bit more. You know, he's more of a strong at the catch point, go get the ball, put it on him type of player than what they had with Stefon Diggs, who was more of a route runner and separator. So, just a little bit of a transition there in that Z role. But I see every day Dobbs kind of getting a little bit more and more comfortable. I thought he had the highlight of practice at the end over Christian Gonzalez in the back of the end zone. That was a really nice catch, maybe his best play at camp today. And I thought that he got behind Kendal Vickers, but the ball was thrown a little bit inside. If that had been on his outside shoulder, I think that might have been a deep ball, too. So, a little bit of flash from Romeo Doubs. You know, I've been small c concerned about it, but I'm It was like 12 size bomb, maybe now it's like 10. You know, it get a little bit smaller each day, which is what you want to see. >> Yeah, it helps when you make a catch over Christian Gonzalez, but again, you know, just showing up and it's a good sign, Paul, too, cuz he missed a couple days. We don't know exactly what. Michael Vrabel said it was a good thing, personal thing, uh that he was not out there. Little worried briefly that he was maybe hurt, but seemed like he picked right back up and and he's building some momentum. >> Yeah, and I would agree with Evan's assessment. I thought he was uh he was open at times and then he made plays uh that you show that that kind of physicality that he has at the at the catch point. And the one in the end zone, I I I was not quite as impressed, but but almost so with a little two-minute work, very end of practice, catches a little sideline route on uh you know, back shoulder kind of a a route with with Gonzalez again, you know, tightly in coverage. Uh you know, Christian's been pretty physical in his coverage. That's Doubs's game. He's able to sort of show his strong hands on those. So, I would agree. >> Arrow up on on Doubs a little bit. >> I know it wasn't full speed, too, but it seemed like they were getting A.J. Brown away from Gonzalez a little bit today. You know, not just the one-on-one stuff, but the team stuff as well. How do they hold up against, you know, real NFL competition? >> Yeah, I think that Lomu right now is in a little bit of a competition with Marcus Bryant. I I really do. And I know that people are going to say, "Oh, he's a first-round pick versus a seventh-round pick. It shouldn't be a competition." But, that's where we're at. And Marcus Bryant today was kind of a left tackle day for Caleb Lomu. So, Marcus Bryant taking a lot of those Morgan Moses snaps at right tackle. And Moses was, you know, load managing or whatever we want to call it. So, we'll see. I thought in one-on-ones, Lomu looked a lot better. So, the question is is, you know, how does his development on the right side catch up to where he's at on the left side? But, Marcus Bryant continues to be in the mix for that swing tackle job.
