title: Breaking Down a Competitive Scrimmage at 2026 New England Patriots Training Camp
text: With the 12th day of Patriots training camp and their seventh in pads, they had a little fun today, guys. Blue-white scrimmage, who stood out? We got you covered. Welcome to the Patriots training camp cast presented by New Balance. And yes, today was day number 12, seventh day in pads, and it was the second annual blue-white scrimmage. Little different than last year when they were inside the stadium. We had all kinds of point totals going left and right. We just tried to keep track of the score, Ev. But there were some red zone, there was some two-minute drill, they worked in some situations, too. So, it wasn't quite a straight-up scrimmage, uh but a lot of fun to watch for us and for the fans. >> Yeah, it was nice to kind of break up the monotony of camp where the practice scripts are pretty similar and this is a little bit different. And I thought as far as training camp scrimmages go, this was pretty competitive. Like usually these things are just a way to get in the stadium and, you know, fit work on sideline and substitutions and things like that. Uh but they got after it a little bit today and it was good to see a big victory for team blue and Tommy DeVito. I think we have it at 23-16 if you include all of the periods, all the red zone stuff, everything like that. So, uh a couple of nice Drake Maye drives in there that we can get to, but give uh give DeVito credit. I think he's thrown the ball really well going all the way back to the spring. Uh and he's uh shown that he can be a capable backup. >> Yeah, Paul's favorite target, Pop Douglas today. Another good day with him. He had a bunch of catches. >> He continues to impress me and I know that we've been down this road uh during the summer before with Demario Douglas, but I I just feel like it's been a little different. Um you know, just anecdotally, I feel like he's been running more co- corner routes. Like he gets downfield for a big play in the two-minute drill, um which was uh you know, I kind of wondered, I was joking around with the the guys on that. Like you you're in a two-minute drill, there's 1:05 left and you get 50-plus on the first play. I'm not sure. Like great play, but I wonder if the coaches rather see, well, I kind of want to see him matriculate the ball down the field a little bit uh and get him work on that. But anyway, I agree with you. Tommy DeVito was impressive today. I don't think that was his only really good throw and that was pretty perfect. The deep ball to Demario Douglas. >> Yeah, dropped it right in the bucket to Douglas and I agree with you. I think the difference between this summer and last summer to me is that it's all three levels of the field for Pop right now. I think last summer was a lot of those inside option routes where he's getting open on quick hitters over the middle of the field which are great, but this has been, you know, intermediate crossers, deep crossing routes. Today I call that a shoot route right up the middle of the of the field, right up the shoot. And >> backs usually say, "Shoot." When a guy runs by him. >> he ran right by him. So, I I I think that might be a little bit of a line of demarcation compared to last summer where I thought it was a lot of those little dump-offs over the middle. This summer it feels like Pop is getting open deeper down the field. So, I thought he was the player of the day today. I thought he was the best player on the field. >> Yeah, a little bit of context how they divided the teams up though. DeVito was working with Hunter Henry, with Mac Hollins, with A.J. Brown, with Pop Douglas who had the big day. Meanwhile, on the other side Drake May kind of forced I don't want to say forced, but had to work with Kayshon Boutte, with Romeo Doubs who was back today. Mike Vrabel said that was just a personal thing and it's all good. So, that's a positive sign. He wasn't hurt. He was back in the mix today. And then also Kyle Williams was part of that group. So, guys though a little bit of a slow start I felt like for Drake May, a little bit of a continuation of what we've seen in the last couple days and then, you know, they get down to the final two-minute drill and and he moves the ball pretty well. They were able to to put up a field goal there at the end, but just what did you guys think of Drake May's performance overall today? >> Yeah, another slow start for sure. I mean, I think he started one for six if you're into that sort of thing in terms of the practice stats, but I thought the the couple throws that stood out to me from him I were the one to Henderson in the end zone. It was a little bit maybe underthrown, but got it there and Henderson made a good play on the ball. And then Eli Ricks I thought he a couple of catches, especially one up the seam with classic Patriot play action pop pass right over the linebackers head to the tight end and those are the types of plays, seam routes, crossing routes that you expect Raridon with his size and speed to be able to pick up quickly as a rookie. You mentioned the the 2-minute drill or the minute and 5-second drill, if you will. What I've liked about what I've seen from cuz I know he ended on Thursday's practice with the pick in the 2-minute, so it wasn't great, but the early part of the drive, he's taking those profits underneath the defense and getting that first first down that Polly likes to talk about. So, a couple of completions to Raridon underneath, one to Dobbs in the flat underneath, and then it was the big chunk to Kyle Williams on the deep in cut to get them into field goal range. I think a lot of times when you get into those situations, you want to get it all in one play cuz you're worried about the clock and you're up against it and that easy money with teams playing off coverage and prevent is all right there for the first 15 or 20 yards. So, I like liked his approach to the 2-minute periods that they've had. Maybe didn't end as well yesterday as it did on Friday, but I thought overall, I think he's doing the right things. >> Yeah, I thought there was some active guys in the front seven on both sides, too. I thought there was a little bit more pressure, you know, on both quarterbacks, but I thought Drake dealt with a a little bit, too. On the edges, you know, no Will Campbell. He did not participate in this scrimmage today. Lomu, it looked like he got retaped and missed a couple of plays on one series, but I did find it noteworthy that he was at left tackle today in his group. So, I thought a guy that we haven't really talked a lot about, Xavier Holmes, kind of flashed to me on a few occasions as an edge rusher. You know, that's a spot that, you know, continues to be, you know, a concern for me cuz I don't see a lot of depth there. Maybe this is another undrafted free agent that can maybe carve out a role. >> Yeah, Elijah Ponder last year, you know, did the same thing. I think what's crazy about Holmes is that he was a tryout player at rookie mini camp. So, he wasn't even a a UDFA that they signed in April or late April, early May. >> Malcolm Butler. >> Yeah, they signed him for rookie mini camp as a tryout player and then signed him to a contract after he had a good rookie mini camp. So, a long way to get here for Xavier Holmes, but I I agree. I think his number's been written down a couple of times in team periods, but also in one-on-ones he's flashed and plays hard, plays with like an aggressiveness and a type of variable demeanor that he always talks about. So, an interesting guy that maybe could, you know, be the fifth edge rusher if they want to keep five of them. >> Yeah, just, you know, big point. We we talked yesterday, guys, about just this has kind of been a back-and-forth kind of camp and I have I thought you made a good point about just kind of become a grind a little bit. Felt like more of a grind today, but, you know, seventh pad padded practice in 12 total practices, Paul, and you know, we go back and look at what we've seen in recent years. It's been a tough camp. It's been especially last two days it's been hot, it's been physical, and I I think the theme that we heard from the players is they're ready to face the Colts next week. >> the most part the ones that haven't been padded have been walk-throughs. So, when they practice, they've generally been in pads. I do agree, you're starting to see every player, young, veteran, young, doesn't matter, they're all just talking about we need we need to see somebody else. We need to go against another guy. And I think that's part of the struggles offensively when we're starting to see them because I just think there's such a familiarity with what the Patriots are doing offensively. It's it's not just sort of knowing what the plays are, but you know the tendency of the guy that you've been covering for 12 straight days. So, I thought it was interesting to hear A.J. Brown talk about that battle with Gonzalez a little bit, you know, sort of a you know, recognizing how good it is and what a plus it is to go against the guy of that caliber. He's singing the praises of Gonzalez, but also sort of recognizing that, you know, Christian seems to have a little more when he's going against me than everybody else. So wait guys, we're going to be live uh during that Colts joint practice at least for the start of it, but we won't really do one of these videos probably before that. So >> Yeah. >> What are you looking for Evan? What what what's going to interest you as we get into the joint practice against another team? >> Well, I think it's all the stuff that we've been talking about on the positive side now translating against another team that like Paul's point maybe you don't know their tendencies, you don't know their plays as well. But I look at hopefully he's back out there. I look at Will Campbell who Mike Vrabel did say on Friday morning should be back out there by the joint practice. You know, La'e Tui Latu maybe against him who's a pretty good edge rusher, not you know, an all-pro edge rusher, but solid player there for Indianapolis who's a really good pass rusher. I would like to see him against some other edge guys and see if this year two leap that I think we've seen in Patriots practices starts to translate against some other players. Not to you know, take any shots at our the Patriots edge rushers, but not exactly you know, the the best group right now on the team. So we get to some of these other joint practice especially against the Eagles, you're going to see some better players than I think what he's seen in these practices. So looking for that, you know, always in the trenches with Will Campbell, Gabe Ikard like those types of guys because now we're going to get into a different part of that training camp. >> going to look at the secondary too on both sides. I you know, I want to see how the Patriots receivers are able to uncover and I want to see you know, if the the secondary which I think has been a a pretty good strength for New England here in our practices, if that carries over against you know, Alec Pierce and Josh Downs and some of those guys. >> Yep. >> All right, well close practice on Monday, but if you're around Tuesday it's going to be a joint practice against the Indianapolis Colts. Come on down. It's always a highlight of the summer. It should be a great test for the Patriots.

title: Milton Williams, Efton Chism III, Tommy DeVito & Dell Pettus Address the Media | Press Conference
text: So, what's it like going up against another team? >> Oh, no. It's fun. It's always fun to go against go against somebody different. Um, you know, you go against your same guys, you know what you're going to work, you know, the moves that you've been trying to work and, you know, it's good to go against somebody else cuz they don't know what you're trying to work on and, you know, you get a get a a fresh look on, you know, what you continue what you need to continue uh to get better at. Did >> you get a good feel for the run defense and maybe some areas of need needed for improvement? >> Oh, 100% 100%. That's a good team. That's a good running football team. They got a good offensive line and a great back. Um, so we got some work in today. We uh definitely got some things we need to correct and continue to get better at, but um it's just a good day's work. Good days of work. >> How do you feel like you guys did today? >> I feel like we did okay. Um like I said, it ain't going to be perfect. Whatever we didn't do right, you know, we're going to go talk about it and correct it and make sure know we don't make the same mistake twice and move on. that their name changed for you guys as a defense as a whole on the back. >> Oh yeah. Um I I didn't notice until um once he got a two minute he wasn't out there. But you know it it it definitely changes um you know what they do on the back end because they got a lot of trust in him so they can you know lead to the other side and maybe you know change up their coverages and and let Zero do his thing. Um but y'all know the type of player he is, how special he is and what he mean to our team. um when he not out there um we gonna feel it. >> Is there one thing about training camp joint practices that you appreciate more now as a veteran that you might not have appreciated as a rookie? >> Is it all just sort of the same? >> No, I mean it's going against somebody else. um and just competing against somebody else like um you of course you get up to you know go against your guys but when it's somebody new you know they coming into your building and you know you got to be ready for that challenge and you know I feel like we was ready for that challenge today I go look at the tape and see what we can correct but um just the competition aspect I I think feel like that's the the funnest part about uh training camp >> how different does it feel when you're going up against another team and it's less structured compared to what you guys have been doing against each other the last couple weeks. >> It's different. It's different, but it all goes back to how we want to play as a team, man, and how we want to do things. We can't worried about um you know, how they practice and how they run their plays or whatever. We got to stick to our details, techniques, and fundamentals, effort, and go off of that. >> How's it different for you guys up front when Bar out there? >> Oh, it's different. Um same thing with Gonzo. He a hell of a player. Um, and when he not out there, you know, we got to step up and and and um and carry that weight for him. Um, I was I was down for a couple weeks last year, so he had to do the same thing. Um, so now we as a unit, we got to do the same thing for him like they did for me when I was out. So, um, just try to pick up pick up the slack and, you know, do what we got to do to get the job done. >> What's going on? >> So, Mike, you asked Mike about you earlier today. share a little bit about how that started kind of nickname. >> Yeah, probably uh my first or second week here that became the nickname. Originally he was calling me Cutlets and then he saw me wearing two gold chains that I always have on. I never take them off and turned into two chains and that's been it and that's that's how it is throughout the building now. >> Do you feel like you graduated from the Cutlet nickname to the two chains thing or do you always feel like that's just going to be part of who you are? >> No, I think that's always part of who I am. That's that's just what it is. Talk us through the touchdown to um that from the end of practice, the deep ball. What did you see? How did it develop? And again, walk us through. >> That was awesome. Obviously, everything starts with the play call. Uh play that has multiple answers in it. You have the guys on the field to give you the protection, perfect coverage for it. Mac runs a great route, O line blocks, put it up to him, that's it. >> What's been the biggest challenge for you moving from number three to number two this spring? >> Yeah, I think um it's it's the same for me. I mean, I got exposed to that early on in my rookie year being a three on practice squad and then a couple weeks later being elevated to be the two and then the week after that to starting a game. So, you know, that that whole prepare like a starter thing was very real to me uh my rookie year when I was young. So, I treated that as such whether you're the two or the three because even two years ago when I was in New York, I was the three one week and then the next week I was starting, you know. So, um you always got to stay ready. So, I always just keep that mindset and move forward. Tom, it seems like you had steady improvement throughout this summer, especially the last couple weeks, really finding a groove. What is it about this offensive system that challenges you in certain ways and also has allowed you to kind of have that same >> Oh, it's still challenging me. I'll tell you that. There's still so much things that I can grow on and I'm looking forward to doing that, especially even today just going in there and watching the film. But I think um the way that this offense has run, it gives you just it gives the quarterback all the rain. You know, you make all the decisions whether you want to get in and out of a play, whatever you want to do, everything flows through the quarterback. So for the coaches to have that kind of trust in you, um it's awesome. And like you said, to grow from where I was at OTAAS to now has been tremendous amount of growth and that's just testament to the coaches, the players around me pushing me and then just ultimately reps, just getting reps in it. >> We've seen you have some nice chemistry with Eton out there and he's making some like leaping catches day after day. Do you see anything different with him physically or his approach compared to last year? >> Uh I wasn't here last summer so I'm not sure how he looked >> compared to his rookie. >> Yeah. Uh, I'm not, like I said, I'm not sure how he looked last summer, but I assume he had to have looked the same for him to make the team, uh, being an undrafted guy, especially a receiver when they have a stacked room already. So, testament to him. You know, I know he always gets uh grouped in with Mack, if you will, but uh, you know, I think he found a routine. He sticks to it, and he's one of the hardest workers, if not the hardest worker that I've been around, and uh, it's impressive to see, and it's awesome to see everything pay off for him. >> Can you compare your comfortability level at all, just, you know, I know you came in at the start of the year last year in September, to where you were on your own? Is it Is it a different world? >> It's day. Yeah, it's a different world. It's a different world. It's one, like I said, it's one thing to be in the classroom and be in it and learn and everything, but it's another thing to get reps in it because last year I didn't get any reps in the offense. You know, my first rep was during OTAAS. So, to be able to actually take everything from the classroom and then bring it to the field and like physically feel mistakes and go, that's personally how I learned my best. So, it was good for me. >> Do you know what your role is going to be in the preseason game? Do you know? >> I do not. No idea. >> I have no clue. I think about my rookie year. I was told that morning that how much I was playing in the game. So, you know, I never I just prepare like I'm gonna play the whole game and then whenever they tell you whatever you do, that's how it is. >> How's How have you acclimated to this area year two compared to year one? How have you liked this area after moving from the New York area? >> Yeah, I love it. I mean, it's not too far from home. It's not too much culturally different, if you will. I think uh Boston is a little cleaner than New York. I will say that. Still finding my sp my food spots, though. I do bounce around uh in the Boston area a lot wherever I want to go eat. So, still looking forward to that. But I love this area. It's It's awesome. The fans are awesome. So, >> what's your favorite food spot right now? >> Ah, right now it's Mar. I enjoy Mari. They have a really good kacio pepe. Fire. >> Ashton Grant. How have you seen him grow just as a positional coach from last year? >> Yeah, son. I think um number one, the thing that I noticed the most is he's more vocal. Um, I think that that just that goes with everybody with having more confidence and being in going into year two and just having been in so many situations already last year. I think that gives him all the confidence and especially with how Drake played last year and then to come in and, you know, really assert himself and to help and any like, you know, it's just a growth from year one to year two. You can see it for him even the same thing being in the classroom and then on the field. I mean, it's awesome and I'm happy to be part of it. >> All right. >> Good. Thank you guys. >> How nice is it to go against another team for the first time? >> Oh, no. It was definitely It was definitely a fun practice. I mean, I think sometimes like you get used to your own like your own offense and like, you know, vice versa for them. So, it was nice to like have a new competition, somebody else to study, somebody else to compete against. So, I I enjoyed it. It was fun. >> U Mike told us before practice anyone who throws a punch was going to be ejected. Did you guys have any conversation about your tempers as you're going against a team that's not you guys? Uh, I mean I mean this like he definitely said that and I mean like we we listened to our coach so I mean everybody kind of knew what the knew what the plan was, knew what the objective like come out here and practice hard but be smart and like don't do anything that's going to hurt our team. So there wasn't too much conversation. I think we got I think we have guys who are competitive but guys also know how to make smart decisions. >> We didn't see Christian out there today. How much does the dynamic change for you guys in the secondary when you don't have someone like Christian? I mean, as great as Gonzo is, we have a expectation just on our team in general that there's no drop off. So, like, everybody's expected to be able to come in and compete at the highest level that they're able to compete against. So, I mean, we love having Gonzo out there and like if he's just not able to go for whatever reason it is that day. Uh, whoever comes in next is supposed to come in and be held at the same level as he is. So, I mean, love Gonzo, need him out here every day, we can, but whoever's next up, we like we expect the same greatness out of them. >> What is the growth? What has the growth of John Saunders meant for this secondary? What have you seen from him this year that you might not have seen >> Uh John's just like he keeps getting better. I mean, I think he's always been a playmaker when it comes to getting his hand on the football, but uh you know, he just continues to grow and learn like just like the rest of us. And I mean, I love having John as a teammate. Like, we go out there, we push each other, and we compete with each other. So, I mean, John's doing great, and I'm I'm excited to see him keep growing. Last time you talked to us, you said that Kevin had the meeting about getting turnovers and then you guys got the turnovers and then you had the practice where you ended it with three straight picks, got the one to end of practice. Just how do you feel like the turnover is how how do you feel like you guys are doing in terms of course? >> I mean, I think we can always get more because you always go back and you look at film and you're not as great or as bad as you thought you were. So, I mean, I think there's been plenty of opportunities where we looked at our details and techniques and we're like, well, if we could have been in a better like better spot, we probably could have got another turnover. So there's always room for improvement, but I mean the more turnovers we get, it like energizes our defense. It energizes the the secondary. Uh so it's I don't think it's ever going to be good enough, honestly. >> For for us from the outside, um it seems like Christian is a lot more talkative, particularly with AJ Brown. Obviously, he wasn't out here today, but this camp, is that something that you've noticed him having an uptick? And do you feel like it's AJ Brown specific or he's just talking a lot more in camp? >> I think it's just Gonzo being competitive. I mean, you got two two like two guys in this league on the same team who are at the top of the game for the like for their positions and everything like that. So, uh I mean it just like you know competition breeds greatness and that's I think that's all that's going on. I think they're both competitors. So, I mean any sort of competition however it comes uh it fuels our team offense and defense and it's fun to have. >> Getting a guy like Kevin Byer, what have your interactions been like with him? How has he helped you grow as a player? >> Uh I think it's just a bunch of learning honestly. I mean, like I said uh previously, like he's such a resource for us, like everybody in the room. I mean, he's like basically a coach on the field for us. He has so many years of experience in this league at a high like high production rate. So, I mean, anytime he speaks, like we all listen >> as a guy who's going up against Tommy over the last year or so, how have you seen him grow, evolve, and really devel I kind of see him as like the same guy like like I think the talent's always been there, but like I think he's just in a flow state right now. Like, he looks fantastic. I love practicing against them. I mean, when you practice against like two great quarterbacks, two quarterbacks who are very talented, it makes you better. It makes your defense better because, you know, you have to be at the top of your game, too. >> Awesome. Thanks, everyone. >> Thank you, guys. >> Thanks. >> How good was this for you, for the group? Uh, getting out there. >> Shoot. It It was awesome. I think anytime, you know, you get to go against another opponent. You know, we've been going against the same guys for two, three weeks. So, you get to get out there and, you know, kind of game plan a little bit before practice, kind of figure out, you know, ins and outs of who they got. you know, kind of getting in that routine of a of a game. So, it was awesome. You know, I enjoyed it. >> How do you feel like the offense came out of today? What impressed you? What maybe you guys leave out there? >> Yeah, I thought I thought we did good. I, you know, I thought we played hard. You know, that's kind of we're trying to, you know, build that identity and, you know, I think, uh, every year is a new year, so we can't just, uh, go off of last year's identity. So, just try to build a new one and continue to strive forward. >> What do you think that identity is or >> I think that's what we're trying to, you know, we're still trying to figure out. Still trying to build. But I think it's trending in the right direction. But, you know, that's uh that's up to us to, you know, kind of figure out and for to put on display so everyone can see. >> Seems like you had a productive training camp. How do you feel like this summer's gone for you? Your second time around. >> Yeah. I mean, it it's been awesome. I feel so much more uh more comfortable, more uh just I just feel like, you know, I'm being myself out there. You know, I'm not trying to uh you know, do be pitcher perfect. Sometimes I can, you know, they're giving us some freedom to switch things up. And, you know, I feel like um it's allowing me to just kind of play more free. You've told us that you and Mac like to play in you care to comment. >> I I don't know what you guys talk about. No, but uh we started doing it. Uh shoot. I think it's been helping me, you know, just we talk about being able to run all day, you know, making sure those lungs are good. So, we be in there doing exercises and stuff like that. So, all kinds of things. But yeah, >> some of the exercises like >> So, I mean, we start with after practice, we go in there and just kind of like move our body around. So, we're doing like high knees, things like that. just making sure like active recovery and then uh kind of the off days we uh we do like some diving and stuff like that. So >> can you describe what he brings to the world? >> I mean for me I feel like I you know I say this all the time like man he's one of my best friends biggest role models on the team. You know he took me under his wing um when he did not have to at all and you know I so I have so much respect for him and everything he's done for me but then like just for everyone that he's around it's his energy is so contagious. Um, you'll see him. He's always got a smile. He's always lifting people up. He's always kind of giving it to you a little bit if you're not bringing it. And, you know, it it like like I said, just bring the best out of everyone. >> How would you describe the balance between independ room and also you mentioned the relationships and caring about one another, you're also kind of competing for for spots in a lot of ways. >> Yeah, I think that's kind of the the cool thing we got about our room is that shoot, everyone cares about each other. You know, obviously we all know it's a competition at the end of the day, but we all want to see each other succeed. So, um, when we see each other making plays out there, you see everyone celebrating. I think that's the cool thing about this room. >> How much value do you place on live reps like these in terms of, you know, trying to solidify a spot on this roster? >> Yeah. I mean, I think it's huge for for really everyone. I feel like it's kind of a game, you know, that's kind of the mindset I take and, you know, when I come out here, like I'm getting ready to to play a game. That's kind of how I always kind of attack practice and and whatever we got. And so, when we get to go against another team, it's it's awesome. >> What kind of adjustment you have made in the offseason to making more effective run. >> Yeah, I just think just getting bigger and stronger, right? Uh, you know, you see Mack doing all this stuff or he's getting in there and blocking guys and, you know, um, I feel like just because, you know, I'm I'm smaller or not as big doesn't mean I can't do it. So, you know, having that, you know, obviously trying to put on a little bit of muscle, but also just having that mindset and having that heart to go in there and just try to hit something and, you know, uh, get give the running back a lane. >> Did you change your Did you change your diet or workout routine or anything like that to get bigger and stronger? >> You know, I think a little bit. I think uh I have a great coach back home, Michael Bumpus. You know, we do a great job in the offseason of just, you know, what do you want to work on, sitting down, planning it out, and then pretty much going seven days a week and from there just I I I say I can't thank him enough for everything he's done and all my coaches back home. So, continue to try to do that. >> How big a piece of the puzzle is that? Yeah, I think for me it's huge, you know, just kind of being inactive a couple games last year. I think anything I can do to to have a a have that jersey on Sundays and be so valuable to the team that I got to be out there if it's kick return, if it's punt return, even if I'm not returning, if I'm on just kick return or on kickoff or on punt returns, doing the doing the little jobs that, you know, a lot of people might not see, but it's it's a huge important role. So, I think all those are huge for us. >> It seems like you've been toasting guys, making crazy catches on corners, going back to the Shrine Bowl. Feels like you do it every day out here. What is it about that route specifically that made you feel comfortable with and has allowed you to just have so much consistency since >> shoot I think uh you know when you get out there just kind of having that freedom just to to go play ball and I think that's kind of what what I was kind of saying earlier last year it felt like I was just trying to run lines on pages where now it's like just go out and play ball east west shrine game same thing just play ball you know put put our talents on display you know I feel like that's kind of what we're all doing and you know um once you kind of get in that get in that flow trust try to stay there >> appreciate you guys thank

title: Drake Maye: "We Challenged Our Guys to Try and Be Consistent Throughout the Day." | Press Conference
text: All righty. What's going on? How you guys doing? What's up, Karen? >> Hey. Uh, so how did you think your day went in the day of the offense uh against the Colts defense? >> Yeah, I think I was proud of the guys for first of all the effort. I think um first off, you know, seeing somebody new for the first time and uh seeing some different things. I thought we did some good things and I think we got to finish off better. That's speaking on my part um in the two-minute drill. Um, but you know, I really think it's we challenge our guys to be try to be consistent throughout the day and I think, you know, they they uh they responded to that and I'm uh I think we got some things to work on, you know, obviously and I know that's a good defense over there and they do some good stuff. So, I'm looking forward to, you know, watching the tape, but I'm proud of the guys and the energy and I feel like sometimes even when we lacked it sometimes, I think the guys kind of brought it back. >> Jake, how have you learned to use these to your advantage to get ready here in your third year now with the joint? >> Yeah, I think it's great because you don't really scout, you know, these joint practice. take a a mini look at them and, you know, kind of an idea of what the defensive coordinator does, but really it's just going out there and kind of feeling what I see and trying to make some plays. So, I think that's one of the coolest things about joint practice. You get to see somebody else and um you know, don't really scout them and game plan them really hard. So, um it's good for you to kind of see and react and and try to get your guys going. >> On the road interception, was that third down? >> Do you remember? >> Um that was first, second, I believe maybe been second down. So, I got to protect the football. We were second and maybe 13. and we got a false start and you we got 25 seconds left and we got no timeouts trying to score a touchdown. So, I gave a shot to the end zone and got to give our guys a chance. >> When it comes to seeing and reacting, how did you feel you did in that realm today? What did you what did you like about the decision today? >> Yeah, I think we made some big plays down the field. I think we, you know, picked up some third downs, the first rack of third downs. Thought we could have done a better job and um you know, speaking on my part to make some throws, but you know, I think we hit some big plays. I think we were consistent in the run game. We got a hat on a hat and it didn't really feel like we had some, you know, free hitters to the football, you know, in my group. So thought the you know the front the guys up front did a great job in the pocket. You know I felt you know pretty good all day. So um and then from there just continue to build on it. >> Learn anything about the offense tonight. >> I think you just learn about you know who's kind of stepping up to the occasion. I think you know a lot of the guys responded today and I think I'm you know we a lot of different guys made plays. You know a lot of guys in the red zone were making plays and I think you just see you know time and time again when we can use everybody how hard it is on the defense. >> George with Hunter Henry his contract extension. He's sticking around for a few more years. What does that mean to just have I know you guys are very close both on and off the field. What does it mean to just have him around here for a few more years? Man, >> it's a blessing to play with Hunter. Um he was one of my my veterans, the first guy who reached out to me when I got drafted when I got drafted. So, um it just, you know, the guys like Hunter are, you know, some of the best teammates I'll be around in my career and I'm just not taking that for granted and, you know, trying to pick his brain and and how many stories he has back with Antonio Gates and Philip Rivers and uh just using that and just kind of continuing to build the friendship. He's got a great family. He's a a great dude and a great person. I'm, you know, glad to every time I go out the field with with Hunt. It's a it's a pleasure. >> You've seen you and Romeo hit on some plays the last couple days. Just how do you feel like that chemistry is growing with him? >> Yeah, I think he's continuing to, you know, catch a kind of a stride and kind of how we do things and how we want it to look and the details and um he's just continue to get better and better. So, I'm looking forward to, you know, seeing him go and I think he's been, you know, a great addition and looking forward to see what he can do. >> With Jared accompany, how was communication up front? >> Yeah, communication has been great since Jarrett took over. you know, I think, you know, him learning from Garrett last year. You know, Garrett was, you know, one of the best at it. So, just, you know, being on our, you know, P's and Q's up front and me and him talking and, you know, him seeing things and getting out the calls, I thought he was great today. And, you know, it's just going to get better and better as the year goes on within, you know, kind of playing the first time this offense at center. >> You have a deep group of receivers, the two tight ends, the two backs. How much easier is life for you when you have diverse group? >> Yeah, our room's great. You know, I think our skill position room is great and we got a lot of depth and a lot of guys that, you know, really want to get in there and make plays. So, I think that's the the best thing about it is competitive in there. You got guys that, you know, are making plays all across the board. So, you know, it's my job to get them the ball and and and you know, they're better runners than I am. So, get them the football and let them do their thing. >> Drake, how was it to go up against uh different fronts, different coverages, how how was that for you two weeks into practice and and trying to get acclimated to seeing something different? Yeah, it's it's a great kind of mixup, you know, for us kind of seeing our defense and our defense does some great stuff, but you know, seeing somebody else and and seeing what they do and how they try to exploit our problems and kind of what their kind of, you know, deal is on defense, what they like to do on third down or, you know, two-minute when we're kind of trying to score. So, little things like that, you get to kind of see, you know, some overriding themes in defensive football that you can kind of compare to our defense and, you know, just football in general. So, kind of mix matching that and seeing what they do and I think it was great for us to, you know, get a new look and I thought we responded well. So, talking about the amount of weapons that this group has and are there challenges in that as well as quarterback and trying to make sure that everybody's everybody's happy, everybody's engaged, everybody's getting the football in addition to obviously all the positives of the different um groups you can put out there. >> It's I think it's the best thing, you know, for that is winning. I think nobody really, you know, tries to complain when you win when you win games. And I think nobody's, you know, really, you know, that, you know, prideful in this sport about, you know, personal stats or achievements when, you know, we're winning games. So that's our job as a team and, you know, come together and try to win games. So I think that's the biggest thing that coach is preach preaching and, you know, we're trying to, you know, be, you know, second voices of of him and and knowing that, you know, protect the football team and, you know, do things the right way. But, uh, no, I think, you know, my job isn't to try to make everybody happy. You know, I think my job is to, you know, have the offense, you know, you know, move up and down the field and score score points. >> We've seen It's a big place. Spend a ton of time on like the fundamentals whether it's release, arm position. Do you The last guy who was here 20 years was just on it all the time. Do you obsess over it? >> You have to at our position. You know how many different you know little things, a little extra, you know, you know, power on the throw, a little extra, you know, torque in the ground or, you know, arm angles and trying to, you know, mix up arm angles. I think if you have to, you know, go back and see, man, what could I have done or, you know, why was this ball a little right? Why was it a little high? I think you have to at our sport. You know, kind some of the kind of biggest things with our with my position as well is you're not always going to be in a stationary spot. So, being able to, you know, be on the move and still get your arm in the right spot and um you know, watching individual drill and watching little things and just trying to see, hey, maybe why was I, you know, too much on the front foot or little things like that. >> How much fun since you arrived here in April in April of 2024? >> In April of 2024, >> how much has your fundamentals? >> Yeah, I think my throwing has been, you know, pretty similar. I think I maybe shortened it a little bit, you know, from college, but um you know, really just trying to get more torque and, you know, use more legs. And I think, you know, you know, Lord bo willing my arm has never really, you know, gave me problems. Um, you know, having to ice it or do much. So maybe as I get older it may do that, but you know, right now I'm be able to gunsling it and just trying to be as accurate as I can. >> Coach said you won't play on Thursday. How much does this prepare you today for what's to come with the Eagles next week with a couple? >> We had to have a good practice. We had to have a good practice and show coach, you know, we we can get work in throughout the week and I think we'll have that, you know, same deal with, you know, Philadelphia coming. So, looking forward to, you know, coming out here and having a couple days with them. So, I think it's on us to, you know, be, you know, players that have played in this league and know what it's like to, you know, handle practice the right way. And I feel like we did that. Excellent.

title: Mike Vrabel: "I'm Really Focused on Our Improvement Individually & as a Team." | Press Conference
text: Okay. You bringing it up? Nobody bringing the phone up? >> No, I'm good. >> Okay. Normally, you bring it up. Okay. How you doing? >> Good. How are you, Mike? >> Good. >> Uh, you've completed a couple weeks of [clears throat] training camp practices against each other. You're hitting a new phase today with the joint practice. What What are you looking for from your team? Well, hopefully that we can continue to take some strides in in what we believe or hope that our identity is going to be. Uh the fundamentals that are critical. Um being able to do it against a different team, one that we haven't game planned against, one that we haven't seen, uh one that we have a lot of respect for as a team and and what they do. Uh so, you know, that we can work together, that we can compete, that we can also take care of each other. Uh these are great opportunities uh for for good reps for for individual reps, for team reps, you know, red zone, uh situational work, um good special teams work. So I think it'll be good for, you know, some of our young guys that haven't seen some of those, you know, special teams drills and situations against against another player. So we've always talked about that a skill set that, you know, may be slightly different than some of the players that they're seeing uh that they go against on a daily basis. This will give them a good chance to, you know, adjust and and try to, you know, figure out how to either block him or get open or, you know, whatever it may be on a special team situation. >> Mike, with only one joint practice, do you plan on playing Drake Thursday or >> I wouldn't anticipate seeing Drake out there on Thursday. So, you know, but that's all subject to change. That's kind of where my mindset is right now standing here today. Um, you know, really it's just important that we get the work in and get, you know, get things accomplished that we're looking to get accomplished. Um, so, but that can always change, but I wouldn't anticipate that happening right now. >> Mike, you talked to Charlie on last week and he said that the game's going down for him and that he feels more patient and he's seeing it better. Have you seen that? had a few nice cuts and again um you know I I think I've always said that the the best receivers have the ability to play at different speeds and not just be fast all the time but being able to to play at different speeds and I would say that you know for a running back with with his speed sometimes it's important that you know he kind of sees it and much like linebackers that uh no step is is better than a bad step And um I think by understanding the front that is out in front of the run or what it may look like at the beginning um whether there's movement and then what his adjustment. So I think some of that is starting to slow down for him and and being able to see the picture of what it looks like and then potentially what it could look like, you know, a couple couple strides into the run. So he continues to work at it and the only way to to improve at it is to work at it and see it. and he's getting a lot of different looks from our defense, you know, in the run game as well. >> Just somebody that continues to work. I mean, he carved out a role last year. Made it hard to, you know, made it, you know, easy for us to say that we needed him on this football team. Um, you know, I think he's got a good skill set of being able to get in there and block, but also marry some of that with, you know, with some of the run action passes. Um, you know, he [snorts] competes. He he he always takes care of the guy, protects the guy with the ball the best that he can. And I always see him looking to finish when he doesn't have the football in his hands and continues to make big plays and kind of show up when when we need him. >> Mike, you mentioned that Drake is likely not going to be playing on Thursday. I don't know if there are other players who fall in that same category, but I'm wondering if today then is the day you sort of look to see how they do against the competition. >> Yeah, I mean that's really the only reason that we do these joint practices. will be a lot of the frontline players and whoever's available. Uh some of the guys that um you know maybe won't get as much work today will get you know extensive work in the game on Thursday. That's just kind of how it goes. So um but let's see how today goes and we can always adjust and and plan accordingly. >> Kayen Taylor with ESPN. Um you said this offseason that you were seeking counseling. I wanted to follow up on that and see what did you learn from that counseling and is that how did you balance that personal commitment with getting ready for this season? >> Well, I think we always look at improvement, you know, as we talk about getting ready for the next season. Uh we always look at improvement and ways that we can improve individually and you know how we can improve as a team and it's really critical that uh that we continue to do that on and off the field. I believe in that. I believe in everything that we can do to help this football team, to help our coaches, to help, you know, myself and everybody else included, and how we, you know, this journey that we're going to go on, you know, is going to be completely different than the one we went on last year. Uh, and that's, uh, all of our jobs is to prepare for it now. So, really focused on our improvement uh, individually and as a team. And that's something that we can do today. You know, you look at the O line and, you know, we talk about them and their ability to play together as a unit. There's so many combination blocks that they're involved in and we have to be better. And again, 50 linemen have to be able to sustain the line of scrimmage. And I just walked into that meeting room and said, "How do we improve? How do we improve our combination blocks? It's not asking you to block everybody one-on-one." So, I think we all have areas that we can improve on and and that that includes the the coaches. something that's continuing throughout. >> Well, we're going to always try to find ways to to prepare and and focus on our mental fitness and, you know, that's going to continue with with me, the coaches, the staff, and our players. So, you know, I love what Dr. JJ uh does for for our football team and our ability to to use that as as a resource. >> Do you see that joint practices nowadays can give you a better chance to evaluate your team and the players and Uh you probably just get more reps to be able to do it as far as you know we're going to have you know probably 24 first team reps today and I don't know if they would get that many in the game. So say that that's probably pretty accurate statement um outside of live tackling um you know some cut blocks on the offensive line that you're not going to see today that you may see situationally in a game. So, as far as the volume, that's a great way to to be able to evaluate them here in a joint practice. Uh, but there are also some things that that guys have to be able to play. And, you know, even pass rushers, uh, being able to try to finish on the quarterback. You know, it's so difficult to to work the pass rush and then say stay away from the quarterback and then, you know, they translate that into the game and have to be able to finish on the quarterback. uh running backs have to be able to run through some contact and be able to you know break some tackles which you know I don't know if we necessarily get to see that um without being live >> I mean we just have to be able to play um and make great decisions after the whistle you know we don't want to we don't want to do anything that puts anybody in in jeopardy we want them to compete Um, obviously there's going to be some some pushing and shoving. You know, I mean, you throw a punch, you just have to head over and, you know, run hills or do something with with Frank and his crew because that's what's going to happen in the football game. And I don't anticipate that happening. I want us to play, you know, as physical as we can and be as competitive as we can, but but also be smart and and try to take care of each other and understand that we have to go back and and and figure out a way to play the next snap because, you know, that's what happens in a game. What's your what's your impression of where the Colts were last year before Daniel Jones uh suffered that injury and just what are some ways that they could test your defense today? >> Well, I you know hard to evaluate them just from last year before Daniel Jones and everything else. I know they're a physical football team. They're they're well coached. Didn't have a lot of you know I guess crossover games with them. Didn't see them a ton. Saw them a little bit um you know multiple on defense. Offensively, it's it's a it's a good run football team that will run from, you know, the good tight ends, multiple tight ends packages. Um, you know, an elite runner. um you know so again these are all looking for fundamentals today looking for you know the ability to um be firm at the line of scrimmage transition into the pocket when when they you know have their play action passes and you know be able to set edges and build walls and then you know run our third down package and you know figure out what the cadence is figure out how much we can disguise those things we've been going against our offense so you know figuring out what their rhythm is on third down and when they want to you know try to address the defense and how our disguise looks and everything else. >> Where do you stand with Christian Barour's availability? >> I would say that he's going to be um only a participant and individual today. Uh just still trying to get him back knowing that we have some time and you know it's [clears throat] a long season. You know, he's played a lot of football and he's played a lot of football for for us um was was disruptive for us. We just have to to make sure that that we're smart about what we're doing right over the course of the summer. >> Uh two chains is doing a nice job. He's uh he um I think continues to learn and with it being a new system. Um I think it got his attention a little bit better, you know, as opposed to saying, "Hey, I know what this is." And kind of taking it for granted. I think it's he he's really um done a nice job. did a nice job in the in the in the blue white scrimmage uh operating and and doing things exactly the way that uh Ashton and Josh are are coaching those guys to do it and um you know we we'll see how he responds today but excited about uh where where Tommy's been without knowing what Phil call obviously how do you expect coach to challenge for today >> I'm sure it's going to be a lot like our defense there'll be multiple coverages there'll be non-traditional Tampa looks there'll be simulated pressures. There'll be, you know, load fronts on third down. Um, I but I don't know. I don't have They only give me our calls. They don't give give me their calls. So, >> when you were a player, do you think you guys could have done a cooperative event with the Colts like you guys are doing today? >> Well, that's probably a little different. you know, being, you know, in the division or being in the, you know, um, being so closely tied to that football team, I think you have to just be smart on the teams that you pick and, um, you know, figure out how how you work together and, you know, played this team 12 times when I was in Tennessee and got a lot of respect for him. >> Any update on Harold? >> Final question. >> Just his process. >> Uh, continuing to improve. Uh, but again, uh, I don't think we want to rush anything. Harold uh stays locked in in what we're doing uh in in our defense and you know just again want to want to give him every opportunity that he can to uh to get back and and feel good and feel confident uh before we you know start his clock and take him off of uh you know the PDP list. Thanks guys. Appreciate it. Starts.

title: Hunter Henry, Marcus Jones, Caleb Lomu & More Address the Media | Patriots Press Conference
text: And uh congratulations. >> Thank you. >> What uh what does it mean to you to be a patriot for years? >> Means a lot, man. Uh this place is, you know, means a lot to me and my wife and just organization as a whole, man. Um the craft family has taken me in. They've been so good to uh me and my family. Um given me a chance kind of in the middle of my career um to come over here. Um you know, and we've just appreciated the whole time, man. We really have. We've enjoyed the area. um enjoyed this fan base, man. Uh that I feel like I've, you know, just really appreciated things um a lot and it's uh it's just a blessing, man. It really is. Uh it's it's a true blessing and to be able to do this 11 years and, you know, coming up. This is my 11th year and then, you know, some more years to go. Um I'm excited. I'm excited to be part of this team. I feel like we we have a really really good football team, too. And um excited to kind of be a piece of that. >> Why do you feel everything's worked out so well? So there's some difficult years football-wise who've been a part of seeing a turnaround, but overall aspect of things, why do you think this has become kind of home for you? >> Uh first personally, I mean, I've had three kids here. Uh so raise a family here, that's always going to mean something to me, uh for the rest of my life. Um then just football-wise, you know, come in, um and kind of I feel like get things going in the right direction my first year and go to the playoffs. obviously didn't end like we wanted to, but just felt like we were going in the right direction and then obviously hit a lull there for a few years and um just weren't able to kind of get on track, get things going and you know kind of builds and builds and builds and to get to what we got to last year and then continue to try to build um to this year is just it's it's been a lot of fun to be a part of that process um to be kind of a piece of that, you know, in the grand scheme of things. So um man, it's just like I said, it's a true blessing to be a part of it. >> What goals do you have for yourself in the next goals. Uh I don't like publicly, you know, declaring my goals. I like to keep those kind of internal, but um just keep being myself. Uh try to be as consistent as I can be um on a day-to-day basis as a person, as a player, um as a father, as a husband. Um and just continue to grow. Um you know, and try to build relationships, try to, you know, bring young guys along. Um, you know, it's very important to me. So, uh just excited to do that. >> Has it been what you expected when you came here and Bill signed reflect on Bill at all together? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, me and Bill had a great relationship, man. Um, what a blessing it is to play for such a great coach. Um, and and a guy that just saw football and I I feel like I grew so much as a player under him. Um, I feel like in the middle of my career, I had a lull a little bit maybe of like complacency and just, you know, I was a solid player and, you know, I saw the game in a good way, but I feel like he really opened my eyes to a lot of different things and how to see the game. Um the game I mean the game was slowed down for me a little bit but it really slowed down for me in a big you know just seeing how Bill saw the game and um how he tested us and how he was able to you know just make us better football players. Um you know so I have a lot of respect for Bill and just thankful for him bringing me over here giving me a chance and uh yeah it's it's pretty cool to be sitting here six years later. >> Does Drake play a factor in in you want to be here for a few more years? >> Yeah I mean that that definitely helps. Uh, you know, Drake is a good friend of mine, obviously a great quarterback man, and um just excited to continue to build with him. >> I was going to say he posted immediately for you right after the contract was signed. What's it like to have his support? I'm sure he was quite excited, you know, finding out that you'll be around a little bit longer. >> Yeah, I mean, we we we kind of talked about it a little bit. Um, so it's uh, you know, that's my guy and uh, just a special person. um just a guy that you know we've grown really close to over the last few years and excited to kind of build that relationship off the field but also on the field. Um you know he's just a special player to be around and you know uh excited to continue to you know build that. >> I got you. Not only have you been an Iron Man since you got here but you're tight in team history. What have you learned about being consistent throughout your career? >> Yeah. Uh I feel like I've always I've always wanted to be a consistent guy. Uh, I try to just be the same guy every single day, day in day out. I want to be available. I mean, the best ability you can have in this league is availability. Um, and unfortunately, early in my career, I, you know, I battled some injuries, some like real injuries, though, like things that kind of out of my control. Uh, you know, broken bone, a torn ACL, I had a a kidney. Like, it was just kind of just some freak stuff that uh, you know, it just I kept battling things and kept battling and chipping away and chipping away. Um really I feel like I came here and kind of retoled myself just my my body uh my mindset just different things like right around yeah middle of my career like year six and um I've been blessed to be able to just you know avoid some some big injuries and being able to be out there for the guys and um yeah it's just been it's been really fun to just be able to be consistent and just try to be that consistent guy out there that no matter what you know my guys can rely on me being out there. I mean, that's I think that's the first thing. And then obviously, um, trying to make plays and just do my job on a day on a, you know, play-to-play basis is obviously the biggest toll, too. >> Joint practice joint practice tomorrow, what do you see the value in that and how much you're looking forward to an opportunity to see what this offense can do against a team? >> Yeah, it's always it's always, you know, in the middle of the camp, it's it's fun to do that because you've obviously been, we just been going against each other for two and a half weeks now, uh, over and over and over again. You're going against the same guy over and over again. And it's kind of cool to just like it's the first time we're a a full team. Um and you know, we're all going to wear the same color and you know, cheer on each other in a way. Um instead of going against each other um so it's always it's always fun to kind of have that have those battles throughout camp and all of a sudden just kind of come together as a team and try to build >> Going against Kevin Buyer the way you have. Um what are a couple things you picked up from him as two guys who've been around the block for a while? >> Yeah, man. Shoot. He's he's uh he's a really really good football player, man. I've always had so much respect for uh Kevin. Um obviously you you see the production he has on the ball. Um you just you can't argue that uh a guy that just continues to make plays plays year after year on the ball. I mean you just you can't ever argue against that. Um that's hard to do. He's you know good football players know how to you know be around the ball and take the ball away especially at safety. And then just in man-to-man coverage he's super smart. He picks up on tendencies. cuz he picks up on things like once he sees something he's going to like be able to really know things. Um, so you have to change things up on them, give him different looks, you know, he makes he makes our our Titan room a lot better, man. Um, and then just what a guy. I mean, he's just a great guy to be around, too. I mean, he's just really easy to be around and I've enjoyed my time with him so far. >> What advice would you give Tanner Eli this week? >> Uh, just maximize every single rep, man. I think that's that's what it is, you know, when you're young, too. Um, is just maximize every single day, every single rep. um you know, never slacking. I mean, you just have to keep plugging away. Every day is a new day. Every play is a new play. Um it's kind of what have you done for me lately at this level? Um and they've been doing a lot of good things, man. And I'm I'm excited to continue to build with them. Um they're doing, you know, they're just continuing to get better. Um and seeing things and understanding the offense, understanding how they fit and, you know, where, you know, different routes or blocking schemes or whatever it is. Um they're doing a lot of good things. >> Good. All right, guys. >> Yeah, we've been um having a lot of uh competitive days, you know, um especially having a great organization like the Colts and everything come up here, joint practices, you know, a lot of people are happy to go against other players and get better day by day. So, >> how important are those competitive days and how how important is it for you guys to be kind of going after another and developing that competitiveness? >> Yeah, I would say very important. And the reason why I say that is because we get to see other schemes. You know, whenever we pract practice against each other, you know, we get to know how our offensive guys work, the offensive line, you know, their checks and everything, but now we get to see how different offensive schemes get to be. And then also on the offensive side, they get to see other defensive schemes as well. >> Marcus, throughout this camp, it seems like you've been matching up with Pop a lot. Uh, just how's that kind of match up going and what have you seen from him? >> Yeah, it's been great. Battle of the little guys, you could say, but me and Pop, man, we're competitive every single play. uh he'll make a play, I'll make a play. So, I love going against him because uh his route recognition, knowing the things that he needs to do at certain areas and his craftiness as well is getting me better and then I'm also getting better as well. Is >> there some trash talking between you? >> Oh, yeah, for sure. But it's all love. >> When we talked to you on reporting day, I think you mentioned something about being instead of the hunter. What have you observed or not just 13 practices at camp? Yeah, I feel like it's been a great response because every single time that we come in day by day, we feel like we need to prove more and more every single day. Um, there's nobody in the building that thinks about complacency. So, that's great as well. So, like I said, man, taking it one day at a time has been very important and everything that we haven't got right, we've went in, corrected it, and then our big thing is not making the same mistakes. >> Just to follow up on that complacency, not feeling it. What do you think that is? what's an example that you might be able to share as to, you know, what's not there? >> I think, uh, the main thing is the leadership in the building. You know, only because we get it once right doesn't mean that we're going to get it right all the time. You know, um, I would say every single time that we do get something wrong, we're always harping, hey, we need to make sure that that this doesn't happen again. And having the leaders that's in the room, you know, saying those things on the daily and then also understanding that, you know, you're going to lose some reps, but at our position is always how you respond. So, always making sure that we have the right head on our shoulders and then go from there. Do you feel like this is one of the more competitive and evenly matched camps that you've been a part of here? >> I feel like this year has been very competitive, I would say. Um, just off the fact of a lot of guys, you know, feeling like they need to prove themselves. No one on the team feels like they've made it and that's great. So, uh, we love to have that in the locker room. >> Marcus, what advice would you give to some of the rookies that either in the joint practices or Thursday in that first preseason game get their first taste of that? >> Yeah, I would say, man, take it one play at a time. You know, you're not going to make every single play, but the main thing is how you respond. Uh there's going to be some times where you don't catch the ball. There's going to be some times whenever you give up a big play, but at the end of the day, it's minimizing that and making sure confident confidence-wise that you have it because at the end of the day, you're playing against the one of the best. You know, it's not college anymore and you're playing in that 1%. >> Marcus, when it comes to Hunter as a fellow leader on this team, what does his presence mean with the contract extension that he's sticking around? >> It means a lot. I mean, um having him here, man, ever since my rookie year, we've always been on the same page when it comes down to always checking in with one another and everything. and then also the excitement that he has in the uh in the locker room and then also whenever we're working out and everything like that too. So his leadership has been great for us. >> Whether it comes to your position group or the team overall, what are you noticing about the depth this year compared to previous years and what's stood out here? >> Yeah, I would say everyone in our position room and just DB in general. I feel like we all have the confidence. You know, we want to see each other win every single play. whenever someone makes a play, you see us running off the sideline, you know, cuz we understand how hard it is to get turnovers in this uh in the league just in general. So, having those guys see that, you know, those rookies see that the leaders are excited for them to make plays, you know, that get that gives them even more confidence for the next play that they can make. >> What have you seen from Karan and Shannon so far this camp? >> Yeah, I would say guys that's applying things from the classroom onto the field. Uh, whenever you are a rookie, you know, you're learning the scheme, you're learning the game speed, you're learning a lot of different things when it comes down to the playbook. the playbooks are bigger than it is in college. So, those guys, man, they've been asking questions, uh, how can they get better? And then also, man, you got to be a film guy. So, making sure that they're watching the film and stuff, and they've been doing that and, uh, correcting the mistakes so then whenever they come back out here, they're not making the same. >> Those guys that you feel like you've taken or like you and the other quarterbacks, some of the vets in the room take under your wing and kind of help them out, give them some tips after each reps. Is that something you guys feel like you you do? Yeah, I feel like whenever we are in the DB room, um, whenever those guys that's talking, whether it's Gonzo, whether it's CD, whether it's me or KB, like we're always trying to talk to the room of like, hey, I know this might be a new space for you. And whenever Channing is in the slot, I teach him about different things of playing outside and playing inside. Those are two different worlds. Usually, you are guarding guys to where they have way more field to work with. On the outside, you don't have that much field to work with. So, just knowing where you are and different play styles for different receivers. >> How hard is it to take the mistakes and get him correct out here in a quick time span. At the end of the day, you look to your left, you look to your right, you have guys who are the best at their best um in college and now they're playing with you in the league. I think that's my strong suit and just leaning into that and and trying to better my details and fundamentals each day will definitely help me along with just being as physical as I can be. >> Tanner, what's the most frequent specific piece of feedback the coaching staff has given you? >> I think like I said, focusing on a lot of little fundamentals, not being over aggressive. Just like that. Yep. >> For sure. I think breaking the play call down and really focusing on what your job is first and then after you know what your job is that that's when you master the the whole play the whole offense and then you know what the defense is doing so it slows down just taking it bit by bit mastering what you got to master first and then moving on from there. >> What are your expectations for tomorrow for yourself and for what you think you're going to see? So, I think there's hopefully there's going to be a lot of great energy out there. Uh great competition. I'm excited to just put my best foot forward and and uh attack attack the day really. So yeah, wasn't the smoothest high school career for me but I think coaches saw what I brought to the table and few games of film I had and I got my shot at at Colorado State originally. It was. Yeah, I was just I was playing defense mostly. I think I was just >> dominating, I guess. So, but yeah. >> Yeah. Thank you guys. >> Yes, sir. >> Good to see all you guys. >> What's it like for you kind of catching up a little bit and getting out here? >> Uh, it's it's really good. Uh, of course, y'all seen I miss like the first two weeks. It's been good to be around the team and getting back and just creating that bond that was there before and and really just getting back to the old ways. >> How comfortable do you feel in this offense now? It's it's, you know, your first year that you actually have the same offense back to back years. How do you feel? >> Uh, I feel really good, man. Anything significant? >> Uh, no. Like and then when I took a time, sat back and I just was like, man, I'm going just be patient with everything. Just let God work out his ways of what he's going to do. And this patience is the biggest thing that I learned. >> Well, thank you. >> Thank you, guys. Thank you.

title: Winners and losers from Patriots-Colts joint practice
text: It's completely fine for Christian Gonzalez and the Patriots not to have Christ Gonzalez practice today, which is why I'm not bothered by this at all. text: All right, the big question after any joint practice, who won? Pats Colts, I think, was a draw.
