title: Aaron Glenn Training Camp Press Conference (8/8) | New York Jets
text: All right, good morning. Let me get the injuries out the way. The one evaluation that we did get up I did get news on was V.J. Payne. He has a a pretty good bone bruise. All right, so he'll be out about 3 to 4 weeks. So, player that was playing real well for us. All right, and we expect uh he's really building a role for himself, right? But he'll be fine. All right. Two guys from today's practice, Jonathan Kingsley uh thigh bruise, he'll be fine. And then David Bailey, man he got up after the ankle. He'll be fine, too. We just got to keep him away from quarterback. So, um other than that, man, this was a really really good practice. I mean, obviously you saw that was the physical part of it came out. And that's something I got to continue to monitor. We know what we're trying to create when it comes to how we practice. Again, this was the third day, but it was a competitive day. Um man, it really came out with the offense. I thought they did a really good job of starting fast, and they were moving the ball pretty well. And then the defense picked it up right in between, and those guys played really really good. They executed exactly what I wanted them to execute. Um the pressures uh was really really good. Our guys were dialed in. And then towards the end of practice so the offense started picking back up, which was [clears throat] outstanding. And man, I tell you what, that throw that Cade had to to to Isaiah. And I told you guys about Isaiah, man, he's a dude. And let me say this, um I think it was third and 21 or something like that. And here's what I I heard from the offensive guys. Man, let's go score. That's exactly the mentality that it doesn't matter what the score is, it doesn't matter who we play, it doesn't matter where we play at. Guys, we always got to have the mentality and I love it. I love every And that tells me a lot about where we're going as a team. So, listen, we have a long long ways to go, right? But the mentality of the guys, they understand there's no quit, you know, so um we got to continue that. We got to continue that. So, other than that, I thought it was a good day. Do you have any questions? >> With uh with Bailey, is he like day-to-day or how would you >> Yeah, I would say he's day-to-day. Let me make sure cuz I don't think cuz he got up and I think he jogged off. So, I would think it'd be that. >> Did you have the day you were talking about where you were pissed off cuz one side of the ball dominated the other? How you guys today, you know, did the defense bat offense in some of those periods, the starters I'm talking about specifically? >> Yeah. Yeah, I was at the beginning of practice. I thought um again, I thought the offense started fast and that's what you want, you know, um you know, our defense, we didn't start as fast, but man, we really picked it up. So, um I really want to look at the tape and see exactly what happened just in totality. Um come back to me. I I I I answer that for you. >> Did you see any some penalties? >> Yes. Yes. Absolutely it did and that's the uh that's the discipline part that we got to get out of and a lot of that happened towards the end of practice. And when I think about that, you know, just right off the top, it's the part that we get tired. You know, once you get fatigued, mentally things start to get jumbled. So, um and we got to do a better job with that and that's what I'm glad that we had this type of practice. I'm glad that the heat was out there and I'm glad that we had the refs out there. So, those guys did a really good job. Uh man, listen, it's it's a game. You call it like you see it. >> You mentioned Isaiah. You mentioned Isaiah and Aaron and you have >> You got to ask the same question. >> [laughter] >> You guys invest You guys invested a lot of money in in Garrett. We know what he can do. Invested a high draft pick in in Coop and then you traded for AD. >> Yeah. >> What does it say when you have someone like Isaiah who seems to just be like clawing to say, "No, I'm getting my own reps with the starters, too. >> Yeah, well, >> [clears throat] >> players like that demand respect. They demand reps. Um, and that's what you want. And you want that in every player. And it's no surprise to anybody, coaches, players, that, you know, he's he's he operates the way that he operates. Um, I think that makes what makes him such a special player is because, I guess from the outside in, everybody looks at him as a special team player. You know, but man, there's room for him on our offense. And there's a number of things he can do for our offense. So, um, even though I love the kick returning punt returning ability, man, there's some things he can do on our offense that's Listen, we're going to have to give him the ball somehow. We're going to figure out a way to make sure that he's involved because he's an explosive player. >> What does it say about him, especially having the moment that he had last year and then bouncing back from that and having a the training camp that he's having right now? >> Listen, it it just goes back to what I was saying when you guys asked me, man, he's a dude. And the more guys you can have like that on your team, and we have a we have a number of guys like that now, you know, the more guys you can have like that, the better your team will be. >> Klubnik ended on a high note, you know, had a few hiccups before that. How would you assess the whole competition with him and and Bailey, you know, with that number two job? Where does it stand? >> That's exactly what it is. It's competition. And listen, we're just in the second week, you know, we haven't even played a preseason game yet. So, um, I still look at it like that. You know, those guys are still competing. Um, they're going to get a lot of plays in the preseason. Um, and we'll see how it how it goes from there, you know, but it's exactly what it is. It's it's a it's competition. >> What do you want to see and into the joint practice against Tampa next week? >> Um, improvement. Improvement and like the discipline of what we do on both sides of the ball and including special teams. Um, obviously we talked about we have two different schemes that we're coming in with. And now, once you bring in another element from another team, um, cover structures, um, run plays, pass concepts, man, it really test your discipline on how you're doing things because at some point you get used to your offense, but when you have another team come in and that's the good thing about joint practices is you get to test what you do, you know, against another team. So, I'm just looking for our guys to improve and be disciplined by what we're doing. >> Do you look at joint practices like for Geno as enough or you think >> Say it one time. >> Do you look at the joint practices for Geno as enough or do you think he'll get into some preseason action? >> Um I will answer that um more in the week, but I will tell you right now my mentality is that everybody's playing. And I can't tell you how long. Um but these these these joint practices are meant meant our first team guys going to get a number of reps against their first team guys. That's how me and Todd wanted it. Um and man, we want to get really good work. Like two days two days of really good work against these guys. Listen, this is a team that's been to the playoffs I but they didn't go to playoffs last year, but it's a team that's been to the playoffs for a number of years. So, um I'm looking forward to seeing our guys go up against this team, you know, so and Todd's a good friend of mine. Um I don't I know exactly how he coached. We're on the same page of what we're trying to create and what we're trying to get out of these joint practices. So, we're both looking forward to it. >> What is your relationship like with like what kind of how did it start? When did you guys connect? >> Say it one more time. >> Your relationship with Todd Bowles. >> Well, he was my coach. >> Yeah, so like when like I guess then going back to that to >> Yeah, he he coached me um actually with the Jets and he coached me in Dallas. I think it was my last year in Dallas he was there. Um and then when he got the job here he actually tried to hire me as the DB coach here and when I was in Cleveland and um and I ended up staying in Cleveland that year. So, um and I thought he was a outstanding coach. Um X's and O's wise he's he's outstanding. Um he's demanding in his own way. Uh he has this this this quiet persona about himself, but you know exactly uh where you stand and he does he doesn't BS players either. That's what I like and I've learned that a lot about him. You know, don't BS players. Be up and honest with players. Um he's a good man. He's a really good man. >> When he was here, he would be up in the party. He would give us nothing. And then But then you'd see little >> That's the farce sales in it. >> Yeah. But then But then you'd see little fractures where like you'd see who he really is and his personality come out and show it. You'd get occasional snapshot thing or >> Listen, do not get it twisted at all. Now, he's a um he has an edge to him. He's a really funny guy, now. So, I think you you guys get a chance to know him, you will. I don't think I need to tell those stories. >> But it Listen, he he he's a good man. He's a really good man. >> Couple more. Off track, but the quarterbacks are not wearing the GoPros this year like last year. I know last year it was kind of a made a big deal out of it. Is there reason why they not >> No. Listen, I um I turned Frank and I turned Musgrave and I turned Merkow over to that. You know, how they want to train these quarterbacks and um just like last year, defensively, we didn't have a down-the-line view. Um and what that is is man, we usually really just see where the D-line is lined up. And that's something that I I really liked in Detroit as a coordinator, what I want to bring here for our guys. And um you know, sometimes my guys say that I lined up offsides, but the film doesn't lie. So, we get a chance to watch it that way. So, I think every coach is different. Um Listen, I want those guys to be able to coach the way they feel like they can get those guys to improve. So, that'll be the reason why. >> You guys asked me so much questions off-season being asked about changes you made and all that stuff. I'm just curious, though. Now, 2 weeks in, just how much more comfortable are you in the second year in terms of just knowing what to expect every day, knowing what you want, knowing how to get what you want? Just what's your comfort level this year compared to last year? >> Obviously more comfortable. but let me say this is there are some things that that we I did last year that I think were really really good and we just got to get better at those things that we're doing. And obviously each year um I don't want to say change, I'll say pivot. When you see things that that you have to improve on, when you see um decision tough decisions that you got to make, you got to pivot. Now, I think the um the men that's not afraid to do that uh in my opinion are the ones that that creates Chris success for themselves because you don't really care about the outside noise. You don't really care about what people say. The only thing you care about is man, how do you make the team better? How do you make the organization better? And that's the one thing that I focus on. So, when things are not to my liking, I'mma pivot. And I'mma make sure that um I make the decisions that get this organization going in the right place. And that's that's what I think about. >> Okay. Thanks, everybody. >> All right. Appreciate you guys. >> Mhm.

title: Aaron Glenn Has More To Prove Than Anyone on the Jets...
text: He's number one on all these lists and for good reason. It was an unmitigated disaster last year. We don't need to pretend otherwise. So, he's got to prove that he's, you know, a legitimate coach. He fired both coordinators. He's taken over the defense. He, you know, he's he's got a lot of pressure on him. And I think as we've talked about to get off to just a good start and give Jet fans a season. I mean, the the Jet fan didn't get a season last year with the 0 and 7 start. Can you be 2 and 2 through 4, 4 and 4 through 8 and at least just be relevant going into November and December for the first time in a couple of years. >> Yeah, you mentioned getting off to a good start in the season. How about getting off to a good start in a game? Their first-half point differential was historically bad last year. So, give yourself a chance in the game. You know, they're they're out of these games by halftime. You know, that neutralizes your pass rush. So, then guys like Bailey and McDonald can't utilize their strength because no one's throwing the ball on you. They're just running the ball in the second half. You take away your strength on offense, your running game because you're so far behind. You put too much pressure on your quarterback and your offensive line. Stay in the game. And so, I think that goes directly to coaching, being mentally and physically prepared for games, not getting blown out in the first quarter. >> Amen to that. Super chats cut the line. We got two to hit and then we're going to wrap this baby up. So, last chance to get your questions acknowledged or your comments read. F Let says, "If we all wanted the Jets to tank last season then they tanked like we asked, why do we give Glenn so much a hard time for doing what we wanted?" Well, I think when people say this, they ignore the fact they started 0 and 7 when they had Sauce, when they had Quinn, when Aaron Glenn said, "It's coaching, man. It's coaching. Justin Fields, we're going to unlock him. We're We're going to let him play quarterback." All the All the just boisterous things he said and then they started 0 and 7. So, you could say, "Oh, they're playing Brady Cook at the game." Who cares? But, they were breaking NFL records, Rich, for point differential and how they were losing. So, it's not just that they lost these games. It's how it looked throughout the year including the Brady Cook games that concerns fans. >> Yeah, I don't blame them at all for the Brady Cook games. I mean it was pretty apparent what was happening there in the last four games. All right, call it what you want, tanking, whatever. Uh those were throwaway games. I don't blame Glenn at all for that. It's the 0 and 7. It's mangling the clock and the timeouts in London against Denver when you had a chance to beat a really good football team. I mean, they had They could have had Denver on the ropes and there were just too many of those instances. You know, all right, you lose to Buffalo week two. Buffalo's a really good team. You know, going losing in Miami, games like that. You know, teams that you should have been, you know, better in your weight class and you got beat by. So, it's the 0 and 7 start and then once they traded Tae Davis and Quinnen, you know, then we knew what was going on there. They were in rebuild mode, but they weren't in rebuild mode at the beginning. >> Do you remember the London game when Adam Gase did not know how long the potential game-winning field goal was? He's talking about it being a 67, 68 yards. It was 62 and Nick Folk had hit from 62 weeks prior against Miami. We know Jeff Fisher famously said a big regret he had was that he didn't delegate the play-calling responsibilities when he became the head coach. It just might be too much for some people and that's my fear with Glenn. >> Yeah. I mean, it's a fair concern. Uh if you're a Jet fan, you hope that look, we we all learn our jobs. I think we do our best jobs better this year than we did last year. You're always trying to improve and I know Adam Gase was probably his own harshest critic in the off-season. Knowing him as well as I do, I think he probably spent a lot of time soul-searching and trying to improve by talking to his mentors, by just picking people's brains on X's and O's and team management and so forth. He didn't want to take the chance on him getting hurt, like dropping a weight on his foot or something like that, and then them being on the hook for his entire salary, you know, becoming guaranteed. Neil Neil Leigh Steinberg leaked that to Gary Myers, my my colleague at the Daily News, and we wrote a big story about that. I mean, this this franchise has just been snakebitten and has had some of the most bizarre injuries to quarterbacks you'll ever see. >> Yeah, Glenn Foley got hurt one year. How about Chad Pennington in the pre-season game? I mean, he basically it was Brandon Short. I'll never forget the Giants linebacker and Chad, you know, basically it was like a compound fracture. The bone came out of his hand on his wrist. It was his left wrist and he was out I think about 10 weeks and that was the '03 season. So, that season was pretty much shot. Then of course Chad had the two shoulder surgeries which you know, just derailed a very promising career. >> Mark Sanchez in the Snoopy Bowl also on that one. >> Another one. title: Matt Nagy on Jaxson Dart’s Development at Training Camp | New York Giants
text: Put those two things together. >> Yeah, it's a it's a great question for us. It's the number one question we talked about when we got here with coach Harbs and how we how we saw this thing. You go through it every every team, every new coordinator, every new head coach, every new quarterback. You got to decide, you know, what's best for for that player and for our offense. And so but at the same point in time, we want to also look at, you know, schematically where do we see this thing going and and then trying to fit everything together. And that's been the process for us going through this that that started way back in in you know, in February and March and now it gets to this point where we're just trying to load up as much film as possible, as many plays as possible for us to put on tape to evaluate and and try to see, okay, what do our players do well and how do we accentuate their strengths and and make us the best team possible as we kind of create this identity of what and who we're going to be. >> Obviously, looks a lot different than what they did last year. How do you think he has made that acclimation to this point? >> Jackson? >> Yeah. >> Yeah, he's done a great job. He's going to there's going to be highs and lows through this process. We talk about it as a staff like you can't we have to make sure that as we go through this journey, we never get too high, we never get too low. Today was an average practice, maybe below average. It wasn't good enough. He knows that, we know that. We'll put it on tape, but we also talk about success through struggles and that's kind of we're going to there's going to be some struggles as we go through this now in training camp and and during the season, but how do we react? And when you get it on tape and evaluate and try to you know, show show them what they're doing right and what they're doing wrong, it happens quicker and I think that Jackson per se one of the most impressive parts of his game right now is the volume we've given him to to get in and out of that huddle and and some of the things we're doing and he's aced that. Now, there's other areas that he needs to get better at, but we need to help him as coaches too and and and and our job. >> How How long does it take a young quarterback, like you're teaching him new footwork, new offense, how long does it take a QB for it to start slowing down mentally so they can play at the speed that they want to? >> Every quarterback's a little bit different based off of what you're doing in the offense. I would say if we're evaluating Jackson, which we are, and you sit there and you look at I just go back personally to to OTAs and when we were first teaching this thing, we spent phase two just kind of trying to teach this thing ground up and in in in buckets and phases and not necessarily plays. So we spent several weeks of just teaching the concepts and teaching whether it's run or pass circles. We called it musical chairs, not not positions. So everybody had to know the concept. So we weren't running plays. So we spent some time for them to understand, "Hey, if I'm in this spot or this spot, what do I do?" That's how you understand the basis of an offense. And then now we get to the phase three and you take it to training camp and now we're running plays and we get to see like, "Okay, not only are we doing what we do, but now we get to see a crazy defense with Dennard and what he does." So you put it all together and and I think that every quarterback's a little bit different. But my biggest thing with him was being able to get through these practices and and and get in it it sounds simple, but be able to get in the huddle, call the play, get up to the line of scrimmage, see the defense and play fast. He's calling every play, he's seeing it. When he says it, he's not just listening and memorizing it. When you can get to that point and you start seeing guys talk like this in the huddle, they're speaking to the person, he's there. So he's aced that part. Now we got to get it to the part of seeing the defense and taking it to the next level because the kid is super talented. >> What is it about Dennard's defense that you call crazy? >> Well, I mean he he he he does he's I've always had a ton of respect for Dennard. And now now to come here and get to meet him and see what he's about and how he ticks and what his staff is about. Uh you know, they do a lot of good stuff. So, without getting into scheme, I'll just say that um it's a very challenging defense and it's it's uh it's something that for sure is going to make us be better in the long run as an offense, even though it's going to look at times like it's not very good. We got to balance that and understand that's okay, you know, and and that uh he's going to give us some difficult looks, whether it's protection, whether it's run game, whether it's a coverage back end disguising things. So, that's the nature of the beast. We got to stay patient. And our message with Jackson right now is just stay right here. Just stay even keel. Never get too high, never get too low. And um just be yourself. >> Why do you think you I mean, this is just by look, you haven't been able to hit a lot of passes downfield early in camp. Is Is it Is that support part of the learning process for Jackson? Is it What do you make of that? >> No, I Well, you know, most of these practices are scripted. So, there's an intentionality of being able to like we started out trying to protect their legs a little bit for the first probably three or four days and there was probably a little bit of more possession throws. So, there's not even chances for downfield throws early on. But then when you do get an opportunity, um whether it's play action or drop back, for those those throws, um again, it's never going to They're They're still learning this this offense. They're learning it. There's There's things that um that they're familiar with and there's There's things that there's not. There's things that our staff is familiar with and things that they're not that were that I'm not. You know, we're growing together in this process. And that's the beauty of all of this. So, um I just have a lot of trust in our offensive staff. I have a ton of trust in Coach Harbs and I know he has a a plan. I I I know internally what he wants. And now it's it's growth every day. And so, if it's a big shot, if there's one or two of them, um great. But when you do get a chance, you got to make it. >> Can Can a young quarterback being under center in a new um offense be helpful to him? >> Absolutely. Yeah, just being under >> Yeah, absolutely. It's Um I think most people will tell you I played quarterback my entire life and having a run game isn't the the friendliest thing in the world. I mean, you want to be able to run the football. Everybody says it, but you got to be able to do it. So, being under center um is going to protect you with some of the play actions and different things you do, but I would say absolutely. Uh and and Jackson's had no issue with that. I mean, we're doing a you know, a bunch of different things with it. >> What do you make of the the run game and especially the running back depth so far? >> Yeah, it's Well, the [clears throat] players I I I like our room. I think we got a good group of guys. Getting Scat back and trying to get him healthy and getting him to where a point he's at. He looks really good. I think he's he's um slowly every day improving, which is great. Um and then and then Trace back there you just he's a super smooth guy that just does everything the right way and you get uh Singletary and and these young guys in there. It's a great mix. So, we like where we're at there. Um you got to have you know, holes when you run the football. You got to have some space and I think that uh coach Bloom and Gero uh and coach uh Newsom have done a great job with um the protection stuff and and or with the uh the the run blocking and protection. It's been good. I mean, I like what we're doing. Again, you know, we're we're halfway through camp right now. We have still 2 and 1/2 weeks. We're halfway through our run stall and halfway through our pass install. If it gives you any perspective, like this isn't We still have a lot left and we're trying to just figure out, okay, what do we want to do as we go through it and we we think we have a good idea. >> How do you stay patient with it? >> Yeah, you've been in a situation where that that first game comes quick. >> Yeah, it comes Well, we we have When I say that, we're we have an idea of what we want to do. Um I'm talking play-wise. Uh big picture we know. Play-wise, you start to build a little bit of a library of what our guys do well. Um we're not going to give them stuff that we just want to do because we want to do it. They're If we do something, it's because they like it and and they do it they do a good job at it Um in any phase of the game. So, putting it all that together and cutting loose, it's going to be here quickly. So, getting as much stuff the one thing coach Harbaugh's does is get a ton of reps of plays. So, whether it's walk-through, group install, or or competitive, we have a lot of stuff on tape right now that we're able to pull and look at and decide what do we want to do. >> It seems like Malachi has kind of made an early impression just with what everyone says he can do with his catch radius, his size. Just what do you make of his progression so far as a rookie learning this offense? >> It's impressive. Um he's a he's a kid that literally every install that we do, run and pass, he's one of he's a kid that when when you're walking up in front of the the group and you're teaching, his eyes never leave you. And and never, I mean, he wants to know everything. Then he gets on the field and he does a he does like almost everything right. And then he's talented. So, it's impressive. He's got to be able to do this moving forward every day in the games, but I'm really I think that I think a lot of them and I think Chad Hall's done a hell of a job with him. >> Last one. >> When you have a player like Isaiah Likely already, you can tell Jackson sees what kind of safety valve he is. How much of a weapon is that? I mean, you've you've worked with some good tight ends. How much of a weapon is that in the middle of the field? >> It's it's nice to have because Isaiah's had he has some experience here and so there's a comfort level of a guy that knows there's a trust in this thing, right? So, there's a trust level of you've done it. You you've you've done these routes and and so now they're going to test it out and just kind of build their own library of what they want to do. But when you have that, that's that's special. And Zay's done a great job. He's super smart. Gets it both in the run and pass game, competitive. So, it's been it's been good. I'm really really happy with our guys and I think that, you know, it's slowly every day getting a little bit better and better and I can't wait to get get to it, you know, in games and on the field. Go ahead. >> I was going to ask what you want to see from Jackson next. You kind of mentioned that there's still areas to that you want to see improvement. >> Well, it'll be really good to get out there, um you know, as we get going here with getting closer to these preseason games and just the the prep slot of it, uh making sure that he can take some of these things that we're finding in the process that maybe we want to get his eyes to a certain spot in the progression and he and he's struggling to get to that point. See it finding those plays. Like if there's one or two plays where he might not be seeing it well, let's get to let's figure out why you're not and if you're not, let's just get rid of the play. Let's go to a different play. We got enough plays. And so we're we're digging through that right now. We're filtering through that to figure out um what does he like? What's he feel comfortable with? And so now when we find those plays and we figure out what that is, now you got to go execute and and make them happen on the field and and I think like that's what the biggest um probably obstacle that we're going through right now, which is fun as as a coaching staff.

title: Giants Nation Show LIVE from West Virginia
text: Are we live? Oh, we are live. Welcome to the Giants Nation Show live show from West Virginia with all of our closest friends. All right, so here's what I want to start with because I didn't do a practice recap today and people can listen to us BS for a while, but we do want to talk about practice today. Dan, I'll kick it to you first since you just got the trophy. What is your thoughts on the offense today and how they've been throughout this entire camp? >> Yeah, well today was different. >> Uh-oh, Dan's not plugged in. Again, here. We good? We >> Here we go. >> We know he doesn't realize how to use headphones. The other day he was sitting there like this for like 30 minutes. >> I said I don't have a podcast. >> You need to turn your ear piece around. >> I don't have a podcast. >> It's that UMass education. >> Exactly. Anyways, as I was saying, no the offense did not look good for most of camp. I know Bobby you've been here for some practices, not all of them. >> I've been say I went to the caverns. It's been a great vacation for me. >> Sure, you mentioned once or twice you've been all of them, but yeah no, it didn't look good really for the balance of camp. Today was different. And I mean the numbers was 16 to 19. I think we all kind of had the same numbers. Even looking back through my notes he started 1 for 3. There was a stretch where he completed 13 passes in a row. A lot of that was like a third long period and he was hitting underneath routes and sometimes you might say, oh well he's just checking it down, but it's like that's also just playing real football. Like you can't just chuck it down field. He was getting the ball out quickly, wasn't taking sacks. And then that last drive I thought he did a really good job which again felt like real football. It was good they were going against the ones and he was just methodically working down the field, had a deep out to Mooney, had I think Thielen on another deep out. Um even the check down to Turbo that got him way down to set up the touchdown. That was again just quick, got the ball out, let your playmaker make a play. Put them out there and then if you do that you got to deliver and he hits Slayton on on out against Banks for a touchdown. So just a very good way to end a positive day for the offense. >> The reason for me that it's so important is because this is an offense they're learning a new offense. Jackson Dart and company are learning a new offense. They don't have Malik neighbors. They have some stuff working against them. They're putting together a bunch of different schemes, right? You have Matt Nagy over there coming from Kansas City. You have Harbaugh and Greg Roman bringing like the running game in the Baltimore part of it. And then you have Brian Callahan who you know worked was the coach of the Titans and brings that West Coast concept from that he used with Joe Burrow in Cincinnati. And they're merging it together. title: Matt Nagy dishes on Jaxson Dart’s progress
text: Go on. >> What's the balance of fitting like what what works well for Jackson to what you guys want to run and like how do you how do you meld those two things together? >> Yeah, it's a it's a great question for us. It's the number one question we talked about when we got here uh with Coach Harbs and how we how we saw this thing. um you go through it every every team, every new coordinator, every new head coach, every new quarterback, you got to decide, you know, what's best for for that player and for our offense. And so, but at the same point in time, we want to also look at um you know, schematically where do we see this thing going and and then trying to fit everything together. And that's been the process for us going through this that that started um way back in in uh you know, in February and March. And now it gets to this point where we're just trying to load up as much film as possible, as many plays as possible for us to put on tape to evaluate and and try to see, okay, what do our players do well? Um, and how do we accentuate their strengths and make us the best team possible as we try to create this identity of what who we're going to be? >> Obviously looks a lot different than what they did last year. How do you think he has made that acclamation to this point, >> Jackson? Yeah. >> Yeah, he's done a great job. Um, he's going to there's going to be highs and lows through this process. Uh we talk about it as a staff like you can't we have to make sure that as we go through this journey um we never get too high and we never get too low. Today was an average practice maybe below average. It wasn't good enough. um he knows that, we know that. Uh we'll put it on tape, but we also talk about success through struggles and that's kind of uh we're gonna there's going to be some struggles as we go through this now in training camp and and during the season, but how do we react? And um when you can get it on tape and evaluate and try to, you know, uh show show them what they're doing right and what they're doing wrong, it happens quicker. And I think that Jackson per se, one of the most impressive parts of um his game right now is the volume we've given him uh to to get in and out of that huddle and and some of the things we're doing and he's aced that. >> Now, there's other areas that he needs to get better at, but we need to help him as coaches, too, and and do our job. >> How uh how long does it take a young quarterback like you're teaching them new footwork, new offense? How long does it take a QB for it to start slowing down mentally so they can play at the speed that they want to? Every quarterback's a little bit different based off of um what you're doing in the offense. I would say if we're evaluating Jackson, which we are, and you sit there and you look at I just go back personally to to OTAAS and when we were first teaching this thing, we spent phase two just kind of trying to um teach this thing ground up in in in um buckets and phases and not necessarily plays. So we spent several weeks of just teaching the concepts and teaching whether it's run or pass circles. We called it musical chairs, not not positions. So everybody had to know the concept. So we weren't running plays. So we spent some time for them to understand, hey, if I'm in this spot or this spot, what do I do? That's how you understand the basis of an offense. And then now we get to like the phase three and you take it to training camp and now we're running plays and we get to see like, okay, not only are we doing what we do, but now we get to see a crazy defense with Dinard and what he does. So you put it all together and and I think that every quarterback's a little bit different. But my biggest thing with him was uh being able to get through these practices and and and get in. It it sounds simple, but be able to get in the huddle, call the play, get up to the line of scrimmage, see the defense, and play fast. He's calling every play, he's seeing it. When he says it, he's not just listening and memorizing it. When you can get to that point, you start seeing guys talk like this in the huddle. They're speaking to the person. He's there. So, he's aced that part. Now, we got to get it to the part of seeing the defense and taking it to the next level because the kid is super talented. >> What is defense that you call crazy? >> Well, I mean, he he uh he does he's I've always had a ton of respect for Dinard and now to come here and get to meet him and see what he's about and how he kicks and what his staff is about. Uh you know, they do a lot of good stuff. So, without getting into the scheme, I'll just say that um it's a very challenging defense and it's it's uh it's that for sure is going to make us be better in the long run as an offense even though it's going to look at times like it's not very good. We got to balance that and understand that's okay, you know, and that uh he's going to give us some difficult looks, whether it's protection, whether it's run game, whether it's a coverage back end disguising things. So, that's the nature of the beast. We got to stay patient. And our message with Jackson right now is just stay right here. Just stay even keel, never get too high, never get too low. And um just be yourself. Why do you think you I mean this is just just by look you haven't been able to hit a lot of passes downfield early in camp. Is it is that part of the learning process for Jackson? Is it >> what do you make of that? No, I well, you know, most of these practices are scripted, so there's an intentionality of being able like we started out trying to protect their legs a little bit for the first probably three or four days, and there's probably a little bit of more possession throws, so there's not even chances for downfield throws early on, but then when you do get an opportunity, um whether it's play action or drop back for those those throws, um again, it's never going to they're they're still learning this this offense. They're learning it. There's there's things that um that they're familiar with and there's there's things that there's not. There's things that our staff is familiar with and things that they're not that we're that I'm not. You know, we're growing together in this process and that's the beauty of all of this. So, um I just have a lot of trust in our offensive staff. I have a ton of trust in coach Harbs and I know he has a plan. I I I know internally what he wants and now it's it's growth every day. And so, if it's a big shot, if there's one or two of them, um great. But when you do get a chance, you got to make it. >> Can Can a young quarterback be under center in a new um offense helpful to him? >> Absolutely. For sure. Yeah, absolutely. It's um I think most people will tell you I played quarterback my entire life and having a run game is the friendliest thing in the world. I mean, you want to be able to run the football. Everybody says it, but you got to be able to do it. So, being under center um is going to protect you with some of the play actions and different things you do. But I would say absolutely. Uh, and Jackson's had no issue with that. I mean, we're doing, you know, a bunch of different things with it. >> What do you make of the the run game and especially the running back depths. >> Yeah, it's Well, [clears throat] the players I I like our room. I think we got a good group of guys getting Scat back and trying to get him healthy and getting him to where point he's at. He looks really good. I think he's he's um slowly every day improving, which is great. Um, and then and then Trace back there, you just he's a super smooth guy that just does everything the right way. and you get uh Single Terry and and these young guys in there. It's a great mix. So, we like where we're at there. Um you got to have, you know, holes when you run the football. You got to have some space. And I think that uh Coach Bloom and Jro uh and coach uh Newsome have done a great job with um the protection stuff and and with the uh the run block and and protection. It's been good. I mean, I like what we're doing. Again, you know, we're we're halfway through camp right now. We have still two and a half weeks. We're halfway through our run stall and halfway through our passing stall if it gives you any perspective. Like this isn't We still have a lot left and we're trying to just figure out, okay, what do we want to do as we go through it? And we we think we have a good idea. >> How do you stay patient? >> How do you stay patient with it? >> Yeah, you've been in a situation where that that first game comes quick. >> Yeah, it comes Well, we we have when I say that we're we have an idea of what we want to do. Um, I'm talking playwise. Uh, big picture, we know playwise, you start to build a little bit of a library of what our guys do well. Um, we're not going to give them stuff that we just want to do because we want to do it. They're if we do something, it's because they like it and and they do it. They do a good job at it um in any phase of the game. So, putting it all that together and um cutting loose, it's going to be here quickly. Uh, so getting as much stuff, the one thing Coach Harbs does is get a ton of reps of plays. So whether it's walk through, group install, or or competitive, we have a lot of stuff on tape right now that we're able to pull and look at and decide what we want to do. >> It seems like Malachi has kind of made an early impression just with what everyone say he can do with his catch radius, his size. What do you make of his progression so far as a rookie running this offense? >> It's impressive. Um he's a he's a kid that literally every install that we do running past he's one he's a kid that when when you're walking up in front of the the group and you're teaching his eyes never leave you and and never he wants to know everything. Then he gets on the field and he does a he does like almost everything right and then he's talented. So it's impressive. He's got to be able to do this um moving forward every day in the games. But I'm really I I think that uh I think a lot of them and I think Chad Ball's doing a health job with them. >> Last one. >> How go um when you have a player like Isaiah likely already you can tell Jackson sees what kind of safety valve he is? Like how much of a weapon is that? >> I mean you've worked with some good tight ends there. How much of a weapon is that in the middle of the field there? It's nice to have because Isaiah's had he has some experience here and so there's a comfort level of a guy that know there's a trust in this thing, right? So there's a trust level of you've done it. You you've uh you've you've done these routes and and so now they're going to test it out and just kind of build their own library what they want to do. But when you have that, that's that's special. And and Zay's done a great job. Super smart. Um gets it both in the run and pass game. Competitive. So it's been it's been good. I'm really really happy with our guys. And I think that, you know, it's slowly every day getting a little bit better and better and I can't wait to get get to it, you know, in games and on the field. Go ahead. >> I was just gonna ask what you want to see from Jackson next. You kind of mentioned that there's still areas to want to see improvement. >> Well, it'll be really good to get out there. um you know, as we get going here with getting closer to these preseason games and just the the prep side of it, uh making sure that he can take some of these things that we're finding in the process that maybe we want to get his eyes to a certain spot in the progression and he and he's struggling to get to that point. See, finding those plays like if there's one or two plays where he might not be seeing it well, let's get to let's figure out why you're not. And if you're not, let's just get rid of the play. Let's go to a different play. We got enough plays. And so we're we're digging through that right now. We're filtering through that to figure out um what does he like? What's he feel comfortable with? And so now when we find those plays and we figure out what that is, now you got to go execute and and make them happen on the field. And and I think like that's what the biggest um probably obstacle that we're going through right now, which is fun as as a coaching staff. >> Appreciate it. Thank you.

title: “Elite physicality:” Pat goes 1-on-1 with tone-setting Giants fullback Pat Ricard
text: All right, we're here with all pro six-time Pro Bowl fullback Pat Ricard of the New York Giants. Pat, it feels like you've brought violence and physicality to this camp. What does the fullback position bring to an offense like especially when you and all pro first team all pro fullback is on it versus when an offense doesn't have that weapon to deploy in the running game? >> Um I think it just it just brings uh elite physicality. I think it's just kind of infectious with a team. If you have someone who can hit play after play, I think it starts showing guys that like I got to hit like that. I think that's what it kind of initially brings and it kind of brings a whole culture to an offense to where you just have a physical group and you know, hopefully you can run the ball really well and that's what I pride myself in and I'm happy to be here to you know, show the way and and help this team. >> Do defenders get a dick different kind of look in their eyes when they try to fill a hole or fill a gap and you're you're coming you know, head first at them there? >> Uh I would say so. I mean, they know that it's going to be a long day and that they have to get low and you know, really bring it otherwise you know, I'm going to be bringing it every play. >> I know it's friendly competition. I noticed a play the other day where um you blocked Abdul Carter and then you kind of finished him to the ground and it looked like he's saying hey, are we doing this? And you just kind of walked back to the huddle like this is what I do. Is it is that something where you can't just turn it on in a real game? Like you're going to have to do that in camp and in the preseason in your position to work on finishing the play so that you're going to do it when the games count? >> Yeah, I mean especially in my position like I have to do it full speed. I have you know, it's a very physical ask of what a fullback is asked to do. So in in training camp, it's my time to actually practice and get to do it. So it's really you know, being low hitting hard, driving my feet and you know, you know, it's my teammates but at the end of the day I have to do what I have to do to be ready to for Sundays and you know, it's good practice for me. It's also good for them so that when they face other other offensive players, you know, they got one of the best hitting them. So, it's it's a it's just competition at the end of the day. >> Do you think your offense will have a punishing identity for defenses in what you're building? >> Yeah, of course. I mean, ever ever since I was in Baltimore, I feel like every defense didn't want to play the Ravens. They knew that it was going to be a physical downhill running game and you know, we always had Lamar, but we also had Jackson Dar, who's an upcoming quarterback and I think that's going to be, you know, very similar here. It's just going to be you know, teams are going to see the Giants and be like, "Shit, I don't want to deal with that physical running game and, you know, this dynamic quarterback." >> Shifting to a team-wide question, you know John Harbaugh as a coach better than anybody. It seems like in camp he is running a meritocracy, meaning if players perform, they earn more opportunities and that is how he runs his team. That's how you make a roster. What does that do for a team's culture when there's no agendas about who's getting playing time? It's just about what ball you're putting on the field and when a player walks into the meeting room, it's recognized and rewarded. Like, what does that do for everybody for the group? >> I mean, look at me, right? I was an undrafted defensive lineman and he gave me an opportunity to play fullback, you know, he they needed a fullback and they wanted the best fullback that they get on the team and he saw me, gave me the opportunity and I was able to fill that role. And I think it's just as a team in general, it's just kind of gives everyone a clean slate. Uh, surpassed at least 80 catches and at least 1,000 yards. So, he's a really productive and consistently productive guy. And so, to see him go against our two uh Zion McCollum and um and Jacob Parish is, I think, one of the more interesting battles today as well. And then um from the Bucks offensive perspective, we've kind of highlighted the interior of that offensive line, you know, of course no warps right now in camp, but the those three interior offensive linemen have been out here, have been practicing together. Good to have them all back after injury issues a season ago, and to have them going up against the interior of the Jets defensive line. >> Yeah, it's one of the biggest stories for the Buccaneers this year. It doesn't get talked about a ton because people don't talk about guards and centers a lot. But um one of the reasons the offense uh which was top five in many many categories in 2024 really kind of slumped last year was because pretty much the well Graham Barton played most of the games but our guards Ben Bredesen and Cody Mock between them missed probably 75% of the season and there was a lot of um you know back and forth and different lineups and so on. Having those people back and healthy headed in is really encouraging for the Bucks defense. But this is a pretty good set of interior defensive linemen that the Jets have assembled here. They have Harrison Phillips. They traded with Tennessee for Tavandre Sweat who's a good young player. And then here we go. Doesn't matter where we go. We can't get away from David Anamada. I mean every team, it doesn't matter who we play every year. There's David Anyamada, who we have long considered one of the better uh interior defensive linemen. I know our scouts love the guy. They think he's a fantastic player. So, those three together, that's a pretty good crew. So, to see how in tandem our three guys hold up against those three guys should be pretty interesting. >> Yeah, Sweat has not practiced yet this year. They are thinking that they might get him back this week. So, we'll keep an eye on that whether or not he's able to be out there and it should be um a fun match up to watch. >> I think their first round pick, David Bailey, is now practicing as well. fourth overall pick or third. >> Yes. Yeah. In the top uh fourth, I think it was fourth. So, it's going to be a lot of fun to see the Bucks actually go up against somebody else and we will uh keep our eyes on all of it and we will report back to you tomorrow. >> Tomorrow, we'll let you know who won those battles. >> Yeah, absolutely. So, looking forward to it and we will talk to you then.

Um but [snorts] just realize why we're here and obviously fighting isn't the reason we're here. Um whether it's in the run game, pass game, switching up sets, they've definitely been doing a solid job. I mean, he tried power a few times, I think. Um Yeah, mostly speed guy, twitch guy. Yeah. He kind of just bounce off ideas and get feedback from. What what is your experience been like with Reuben as he kind of navigates his way through this process? >> Yeah, um he will ask me like if I what I'm seeing, like if he's giving anything away. Um kind of what I'm feeling like on his rushes and stuff like that. Uh and just kind of like what I'm seeing. Like I said, if he's showing anything. Um so that we kind of discuss and go over. Um talked to him before practice. I mean, I got to see how he did during practice. I hope he did great, but uh just told him play your game, man. I mean, it's no diff- it's no different than college. I mean, football's football. >> Okay, thank you. >> Thank you guys. Yep. Take care. >> You know, fairly consistently you you had some good runs. What did you see out there against the Jets in this scrimmage? How did I believe >> Um yeah, we definitely had some good runs out there. Um you know, going against another team for the first time. I mean, you know, with E-Rock coming in with this offense, definitely a lot more um outside zone, I would say. Um you know, getting used to that. Um you know, and having that ability to definitely stretch it outside more is uh kind of my alley. Yeah. >> And then the involvement in the passing game with the running backs, it looks like that's going to happen, right? >> Yeah, he definitely uh got a lot of different um routes and uh new plays, you know, for us. You know, especially with the addition of Kenny coming in. Um you know, putting his uh abilities to use and um you know, a lot of us backs just catching up and uh getting the plays down. >> Anyone else? >> Appreciate it. Appreciate it. >> Had a Had a pick six today. >> How'd you feel like you did on top of that and any other small things? >> Uh came in a little slow, little sluggish, but started picking it up, caught the pick, took it back to the house, had to line back up on defense, you know, catch my breath and keep going. So, today was smooth, got a lot of stuff to work on, to stack stack better days. >> What are you trying to work on? Anything specific? >> Uh holding holding my leverage, being more patient, uh things like that and just having good eye discipline. >> The time that Moore's been out has given you and others some more reps. Uh I've been on a couple of teams, Baltimore, Seattle. Uh ended up here last year mid-season. Uh since I've been here it's been like just pretty much work. You get in. I mean they rotate rotate guys just to give different looks, stuff like that. So, I mean whether you're one, two, three, you're going to get in the rotation regardless. I mean that's how the coach Bowles likes to like pretty much give you a a different look and see how you respond to it. So, that's a good thing here. They don't do that in a lot of places. >> Was that time that you had here valuable for you even though you Yeah, it was it was very valuable because I'm from Miami originally, born and raised. So, to be back in Florida and playing ball like it's a blessing for me and I'm very happy for it. >> You speak about the the aggressiveness of the defense and how that's kind of led to not just the play that you made but a couple of turnovers throughout the past couple of practices. >> Uh it's the standard. So, that's the standard we we we we building in in Tampa Bay and that's the standard we're going to keep. >> What was your reaction to the medical incident with one of the players? You guys had to stand around there for a while. What what was your or your emotions when that >> I mean it it it with this sport a lot of injuries happen but when that when that when stuff like that happen, we all just come together, pray, hope for the best, you know, we got to get back to work. >> Anything else? >> Thanks. Thanks.
