So, certain questions I can answer for people who are just now getting here. So, I guess that is a leadership role. Sometimes you get out here and you just got to have the most energy. Sometimes I'm I'm following asking questions. So, I kind of move around. I'm in I'm in limbo. They say good leaders follows as well. So, I guess I'll be in a leadership role if I need to. >> You mentioned agree with Vic. Um, >> you've been here the whole time. He's got this core group. Have you noticed any changes? Is he more willing to give out more responsibility? Has anything changed from that perspective? >> No, I think that's the the thing we love about Vic. He's so constant. He doesn't change regardless of who's in the room. It could be the GM, could be the head coach, be the owner. He's himself and he's confident in what he's put together. He's got 40 plus years in it. I think 40 to be exact. I don't know, something like that. But he's he's built his he's built his confidence and preparation over 40 years. So he's he's so consistent that whoever's in the room or whatever position may be open or whoever needs to be called upon in that moment, he's going to put somebody there who he feels he can call upon. >> You mentioned the prototype the defensive ends here. How would you define? >> Uh the first one would be attacking attacking and and not scared of physicality and our defense. If you attack and you're not afraid of physicality, we can work on everything else. So that's across the whole D line. That's in the back. That's in the secondary. You know, our our safeties will come down and hit if they want to hit. So everybody in the defense, that's kind of just the baseline for the prototype. >> Appreciate y'all. >> Hey, what have you thought of uh Willie Lanin, a guy that with that build is kind of unusual. What's it been like going against him? >> He he a dog, man. I've been telling him since day one that he a dog. I seen it last year when we had reps against him. Uh little story, his first day here, he called me out one on one's and he actually gave me a little challenge. I'm like, "Oh, it's not that dog in him." And um it's really showing the coaches are giving him, his props, the players are seeing and it's all on film. >> What have you, what have you made of the, you know, just the offensive line and how the offense is changing like that and how how they're uh you know doing in that. I like that they uh doing a lot of moving, you know, running, cutting people off or, you know, just beating them to the edge and beat them to their spots and stuff like that. Uh they seem happy. It's it's a lot of good stuff I'm hearing in the locker room and stuff like that. So, I feel very confident in the offense right now and the whole line and offense per >> one of the things was saying is he's noticed that you're in much better shape. I mean, are you kind of noticing it compared to last year in training camp, like how much better you've been? >> Yeah, I feel better. you know, uh, me and Coach Big had a little thing going where he wanted me to come in at a certain amount of weight and I made that weight. We had a little bet or whatever going on. It's all funny playing games. It's all principles and stuff like that. But, uh, you know, it just came coming in with a mindset that also shows that, you know, the contract wasn't my my biggest focus. My biggest focus was putting a smile on coach Vic coming in at my weight and he was happy and we ded. We hugged it out and uh, you know, we doing good. We just working on working every day. >> What did you win in the bat? What did what did you win in in the back? >> Really, did I? Yeah, >> but it it really more of the principle, you know. Yeah. Bragging rights and, you know, just coming air like, "Hey, made my weight on seeing a smile on his face." >> Kind of like shown up on the field and everything. Say, >> have you noticed that shown up on the field with how you've been playing so far? >> Oh, yeah, for sure. I feel better out there. Uh, you know, getting out the stacks, feel much better, you know, especially with what I was going through last year with the shoulders and all that. You know, everything just feel good right now. Was there anything different you had to do um to get down to that weight in terms of conditioning and what you ate or? >> Yeah, mostly eating, you know, and drinking. I like juice, so you know, I might drink some juice, but I had to slow down on the juice. Most of it was just all water and juice in here, but uh I just slow down on most of the main things and eating like once a day, maybe twice, but making it small portions, not big big daddy meals, you know. >> What flavor? >> What flavor? I like minads. You know, they got man made like the raspberries and all stuff like that. But >> how much lighter are you than last year? >> Lighter probably like 10 pounds. Not too much, >> but uh but it's a a difference where I can feel it though. Yes, sir. >> And what's the ideal weight you said out there? >> Uh the weight they have me in there. >> I don't know if I want to say that out loud. Folks know my my weight claus. I a say that. But just know I'm I'm looking good. I'm feeling good. And you know, it's a new season. Like I said, >> how's that? >> What's a big daddy meal consist of? >> Boy, just fill the plate off. Tell you, whatever it's rice, whole thing, right? Everything. Just I need everything you cook. That's it. >> How do you think it's going to help you during the season being being a little lighter? >> Oh, just moving around, getting out the stack. You know, I already play a lot of plays, but being less tired throughout throughout the plays and learning how to, you know, save my energy from on some plays to help throughout the game, stuff like that. >> We probably won't talk to you before the joint practices. Yeah, we probably won't talk about practices, but uh you know, how do you feel like typically you've been a kind of an energy guy when when you guys have gone against other teams in those settings, you know, what what are your objectives against team that that went to the Super Bowl last year? >> Say it again. My bad. >> What was your objective against the during practices, you know, um I know a little bit further out, but and previously you've brought energy and gotten a little bit of, you know, some altercations I guess occasionally with with players from the other teams. What's your objective in these joint practice with? >> There won't really be none. you know, I come out and, you know, play my game and have fun. You know, try to bring that little edge to where they can give a boost in the D line or the whole defense or the whole team at that. You know, if I was to get any alter altercations, I don't try to start them, you know, I just finish them and stuff like that. So, you know, I just move on with my day. >> Is there are there conversations with you about like, and I think Vic has said this publicly, they want you to bring that edge to the defense, you know, the obviously what's the line you they don't want you going over when it comes to bringing the edge. I think see I can't I can't really troll how I want to but uh no I I think I pretty much know the lines where you know where it's a little all right I'm pushing it but it's really ain't too much I can do you know it's it's football you know except for fighting that's the main thing we don't want to fight we want to know get contact get aggressive and all this but fighting is the last thing we want to do >> how much help is Jordan as he kind of worked on your conditioning during the offseason >> me and JD we haven't really got a offseason workout together. He's been in Atlanta. I've been in Florida. I stayed here first and then I went to Florida. So, you know, it's different. Plus, we got to see families and stuff like that. So, we never had the chance to get together in the offseason. But one season, we go we go get together. We going to see how that work. >> Can you tell the pace of the offense has changed going against them? >> Oh, yeah. The pace. Yeah. I see how they trying to get on the ball faster and stuff like that. And, you know, I like you know, I like teams that go fast. You know, I played at George or we played Tennessee who likes to get on the ball fast. And that g me a little boosting edge in my game which is is testing me and my strength and my uh you know my you know tiredness or whatever you want to say to uh just keep going keep pushing. >> Several of the offens players talked about that cadence is a new weapon and over the years we've seen you kind of learn cadence against opponents. Have you noticed anything about this game? >> Yeah, they still working and you know getting things pieced up together. I'm I get the cadence a little bit. You know, I got off the ball a couple times where I felt like I knew the cadence, but uh they still got different things they're working on, which I still got to be humble at home to where I don't jump off size to give them a first down and stuff like that, but they're doing a very good job over there. >> It looked like in the winter you were finishing first among the linemen. Is that is that always the case? Was that the case last year or is it was that something this year? >> I wasn't even paying attention. I was just running, you know. I I didn't look to my left or right. Just ran straight and came back. If that's what what it was, that's good from, you know, my hand. I just got to keep that going. Anytime we have sprints or anything like that, try to be the first one. >> What about Vick said that he looks faster? >> Yeah. Have you had an opportunity to chase him? Do you feel like he's any >> Oh, yeah. I had him coming out on a little play action roll out and I'm chasing down a couple times where he he al he be moving like I don't know what it is, but when I'm watching him, I'm running. It's like a movie. Feel like I'm going slow, but he he be moving, man. He's been working hard and you know he's he's the one. >> On that note, >> sorry on on that note, there are a few times here where it seems like the defensive guys want the whistle blown sooner. You think it's a sack, the offensive guys throw it. >> What's the thought in the in the defensive room? Is it is it generous in terms of how the plays go off sometimes? >> Man, we really can't do too much. You know, it's this it happens in the game, too, where we might want to hold and call. We might want this and that, but we we you know, defense pretty much don't get everything we want. So, you know, we just got to go up here and keep playing, keep competing, and keep doing our job. That's pretty much it. >> It looked like you It looked like you and Joy Davis had like had some fun with Wayne Johnson and Jordan, like waiting for Team Joe. What are those moments like? >> Oh, yeah. This is all fun moments cuz, you know, we can keep it competitive and when it's time to get in that zone, we all locked in and, you know, play our part, play our techniques and stuff, but we also have little moments like that where we can talk and just joke around and stuff. I was actually telling him I was like, "Hey man, when you walk up to the line, man, give me pass or run." He was like this. I was like, "Play action." Like it was all fun playing stuff like that. We just be choked. Sometimes you can't tell. >> Yeah, they got good stuff. >> Uh just just more confidence, more continuity with the guys cuz you know, all of us have been here for the past three or four years and since I've been here and so we all understand how to play with each other. So, you know, that's the that's the big thing. >> In the vision, where do you feel like you've improved? >> Say that again, please. >> Where do you feel like you've improved based off last year? Um, you know, I think one thing I've improved is play action conversion. That was a big point of emphasis for me um during the offseason regular just pass rushing on third downs and that's a lot of what I was focusing on this offseason. Obviously coming in in better shape, losing a lot of weight. Uh that was the biggest thing for me >> seeing this offense that uses that so much. Does that help you a lot? >> It definitely does. You know, this is the kind of offense that we've had issues with. You know, you go back to when we played um Atlanta my first year here. We had some issues with them and you know, seeing how they run is just something that is going to help us to get better every single day. You talk about your confidence being uh greater. What goes into that? What what made you more confident? >> I think it's just the work, you know. I think confidence comes from putting in the work. So the more work you do, the more confident you become. And I think that that's what it is. >> It it when you're not putting when it's not you're on the field making plays in games, when you're not having the opportunity to do that, does does that weigh on your confidence? Does that play in your play on your mind at all? >> No, because I mean I know the situation I'm in with two of the highest paid defensive linemen in the NFL. two of the best guys and really three of them cuz Morrow is is just as good as them in my opinion. And so I understand that, you know, those guys are going to get a lot of reps when the game come, but when my turn time comes, you know, I hold myself to the same standard as them, just like everybody else on the defense does. So knowing that I'm in the room with those guys and competing with those guys every single day to get better, you know, that just makes me more confident. >> Byron, you just touched on the conditioning aspect and shedding some weight. What specifically did you do to be able to make that happen? >> I hired a shelf. Um did a lot of conditioning. Stayed in Texas this year during the offseason. worked down there at the Exhost, worked with BT Jordan a lot and just, you know, did a lot of stuff. Did a lot of movement. >> How good is this room? How good is your DT room? >> I think it can be the best in the world. >> Yeah. Well, how deep is it? Is it I mean, you look around and you go, "This guy's great. This guy's great." I mean, is it single literally every single guy you're looking at? >> Yeah. You know, I think we've all improved a lot over the years, man. I think you see that just with how we're able to practice and how the drop off at practice, there's really no drop off. You know, we don't expect any drop off. And if there is drop off, then the person who, you know, is responsible for that drop off has to improve. So I think it it comes from the standard that we set for ourselves. And that starts with me, that starts with Jordan, that starts with JC and Morrow. We're the older guys in the room. And so we set the standard every single day. >> What's it like to see uh Jaylen and Jordan get compete this off seasonason as, you know, being around them and seeing how hard they work. >> That was great, man, cuz you know, I see how hard they both work. I see how how much they put into this. I see how much they care about every single day, every single practice, every single lift and every single game. So, it's great to see those guys get rewarded with what they deserve. >> What's it like facing Willie Lan? >> Willie, man, Willie is a a great player. You know, he's gotten a lot better since he first got here. Um, you know, he's a a pest in the run and the pass game cuz he's he's so short. You know, he was a wrestler when he was in high school and so he understands how to stay low and he kind of just even though he's so small, he can engulf you whenever you run right down the middle of them and he has great hands, great feet. So, he's going to be a really good player. Were you kind of curious to see what it was going to be like with him because it's like I've never really seen an offensive lineman. >> Yeah, definitely. Definitely. It's definitely a challenge adjusting to him whenever you see him come in versus, you know, the traditional size offensive lineman. But, you know, he's he's he's really good. >> What are the things technique-wise you have to do when you're going against a 5'11 lineman? >> Um, I mean, you really have to play with extension. Uh, cuz his arms aren't as long as most other guys. So, that's the biggest thing is playing with extension, not let him letting him get his hands, you know, around you and grab you. That's the That's really the biggest thing. >> Ty Robinson, second year. Where have you seen him grow? >> Just I mean, same thing confidence-wise. He's a lot more confident than he was when he first got here. And I think that comes with being in the room for a whole year, having, you know, other guys pour into him and and working his craft and having coach Herk pour into him and becoming confident in the moves that he can, you know, work when he's doing pass rush or even just the run game. He's become a lot better. >> You mentioned just how nice it was to see those guys get paid. Is it a motivator for you to to play with those guys? And >> definitely, definitely. It's always, you know, motivating motivation when you see, you know, your peers get paid and really your friends get paid. Um, it's something that I I look forward to my time coming at some point and, you know, I'm sure Morrow is looking towards the same thing, but right now, I mean, we're focused on the season. >> It's been fun. It's been different obviously. Um, I kind of was assuming it was going to be like the way rugby preseason is, but it's actually different cuz we never do I call it full contact or like live pads this often. So, the body's still getting used to pads dayto day like back to back, but I feel like I'm slowly improving. So, I'm about >> How do you have to go about that process of taking care of your body then? Like more contact. I think obviously working in the offseason we had like I think eight weeks um between OTAAS and training camp so I felt like I came in in good shape and then I don't know you just adapt. I don't really know. I think everyone's kind of going through the same thing where it's like almost getting contact toughness or contact fitness. So I don't know you just go through it. I don't really know the deep part about like adapting to it. >> What do you think of Philly so far? >> I've enjoyed it so far. Um, I've been staying in South Philly, so away from a lot of the action, but I like it. South Philly is peaceful. Um, just staying in kind of this area is nice. Um, yeah, I I feel like I haven't maybe gone around as much as I could, but I'm sure I will. >> Did you stay here between OTAAS and training camp? And what was that time useful? >> Yeah, I was here um throughout basically all of um the time between OTAAS and training camp. I went to Kenya for like a week. Um, but outside of that, I was here working in the gym. So, the strength coaches were watching what I was doing. I felt like what I said, I got into good shape because I mean, getting into OTAAS, we'd traveled so much. So, I kind of felt like I got some time to almost build. >> Can you take us through like your the first time you explored the idea of American football? >> It was actually when I was 16. So, I was in boarding school in England and I played I was playing rugby. I was playing academy rugby and one of my favorite players called Christian Wade. He joined the same program that I joined this year and it was crazy because he played in the preseason and scored a touchdown I think on his first or second drive. So I kind of watched that story and I always knew I was like athletic. So I kind of always had it in the back of my mind but I had rugby as an option and the only when I really committed to it I think it was when I was I think 19 about oh no when I'd just turned 20 and I was supposed to be playing rugby in France but that wasn't working out and I was like I'd watched Last Chance You which is funny and I just thought let me try and walk on as a college player. So that was another interesting journey in itself. >> What's been the difference in rugby tackling and NFL tackling because in rugby you know you have to put your leg forward like um you know wrap around the legs and you can't hit really above anywhere above the chest or really adds regions. What's an adjustment? >> Yeah. So we actually haven't gone live scrimmage yet so to where we're doing full tackling. We've done tackling drills and for the tackling drills kind of the body positioning is basically the same. Um, coach Vic is really big about kind of not just studing or throwing your shoulder and actually making those low tackles, which is similar to how rugby is rugby. In what way? >> So, it was that was a very funny part of my life. So, I think the team didn't want to I I don't really want to badmouth them, but they didn't want to basically bring me over as much as I signed with them. So, I was there training, but they kind of weren't getting me my visa over. So that was a tough time for me because I I technically in my mind should have been there but they basically weren't getting me over. So I was just in Kenya training waiting for an opportunity to play. >> How do you feel that you like you're going to have kind of experience here with the Eagles with your own? How do you feel like everything has gone in that regard coaches and staff? I just feel really supported because um I've talked to some other guys who I mean I've gone through the program with and just even hearing stories about how training camp is for rookies for people who maybe aren't in the first and second team and I've been lucky to get so many reps like and every rep I get the more I see I feel like the better I'm getting. So I've been given that opportunity to actually develop which I feel like many other places wouldn't give me that opportunity. How have you done in those reps? I guess compared to what you would have expected, you know, with this volume, >> I think it's been mixed. Um, I try and be positive because I know it's so new to me. So, I kind of look at the good reps and I I'm actually happy about the good reps. I think there's a lot going on in my mind. So, when we isolate some things, I feel like I'm doing slightly better than when it's in the full team period. But, I've been happy. Um, my vets are supportive, but also hard on me, which is perfect. So I know the mistakes I'm making and I just feel like I'm improving dayto-day. >> How special is it to have here with you going through everything? >> Yeah, it's fun because I mean obviously we we met in October last year when we went for like the LRA combine to basically be chosen for the IP program and from that time I mean I knew he was a crazy athlete from that time. So seeing how he's developed and I'm sure him seeing how I've developed has been crazy. And then also just having someone in the locker room who you know is going through the same things that you're going through like just good to have. >> What was it like watching him get drafted and then finding out that you were going to join in here? >> Yeah, it was crazy. We were sitting next to each other like we didn't really know what was going to happen and um I was just so happy for him to get drafted because I mean I've seen the work and we've talked about the work that he put in, the pain that he's gone through, all the suffering that he had before he actually got that opportunity. So seeing that pay out for him was good. And the same thing for me is I got a call from Howie like almost straight after and how much they were willing to show that they're actually willing to invest in both of us was just like I I just felt confident and safe coming together. >> You and No trained together. You and Noir trained together in Florida before the draft. Correct. I know Jordan Milada came down and met some of you guys and you guys. What kind of influence did he have on you and his story given he also went through the I think the biggest thing for Jordan is like he's a pioneer of this thing of he's an he's one of the best if not the best left tackles in the league and actually seeing someone who's gone through the same process as us be so successful like it's kind of like I I always remember the story of like is it the 3minute mile or 4-minute mile I don't know what it is but how the first person who broke it and then I don't know how many people broke it after or actually were able to go through that point I think that's kind of how it is with Jordan. Well, we believe that it can happen because I mean we're seeing it every day in the locker room and every day on the field. So, yeah, that's a big thing for us. >> How have the guys in the extra room helped you? How have they been influential? >> Yeah, I mean technique tips all the time, attitude tips, just I mean watching the guys and how selfless they are with tips. It's not kind of like negative competition to where they're not trying to give me the inside inside knowledge or whatever it might be. So I can all I can see that all of them really want me to succeed. So that really helps me. >> I'm sure all of them have been helpful, but Jix was just talking about how he's you know taken a vested interest in your development. You guys kind of have a similar build. So how much have you taken from his game and you know the kind of his like that? >> Yeah. No, Jix is one of the best vets obviously. is one of the best bets cuz I mean what you're saying like body type is similar. Um I would say rush style would probably be similar and seeing how he's winning and kind of seeing like yeah if if I sort myself out I can actually start winning like that is I mean it's just inspiring. >> Would your answer change? >> I'll probably I'll have said the same thing. They asked about Jix and I was like that's my guy. So >> that's my guy. Okay. Yeah. >> How do you stay patient when when things might be taking a little bit longer to to work than you want? >> Yeah. I think that thing that I was saying is I actually celebrate my wins because I know I can sometimes be hard on myself, but when I actually make a win, it's good to kind of take a step back and be like, you want to rep in an NFL practice? Like it's not nothing. So, as much as I might be feeling like the overall plays might be going against me, um, I'm just taking my wins and learning from my losses to actually make those wins. Yeah, I feel like I'm not really putting too much stress on myself when it comes to that.

title: Jalen Hurts On the Team's Overall Growth
text: How are we doing? >> John, to ask you about the uh the concept of pressure. Um we've seen in the past when the stakes have been at their highest that you have had some of the best games of your career or when you had your first NFL start, you played one of your best games. Um do you feel like that is a fair narrative? And if so, why do you think that has been the case over your career? Um, >> I just I think about the work. Think about the work when I think of any concept of the game. Just making sure you're going out there and you're as prepared as you can be. Um, you know, you take pride in wanting to show up, putting the work towards, um, you know, the daily deposits and the daily efforts so you can, uh, do what is needed to ultimately win. And so, um, just focus on the work right now. Um, I appreciate the bigger picture question. It's hard to think about any other thing than just improving every day. Um that pressure that you're talking about, that opportunity, those opportunities that I relish in, they start right now in these moments. And so just the the pride and the hunger and the thirst that I have to improve in this moment right now. Every day I step out on the field, every time I put the number one on, and every time I lace up my cleats, just trying to learn and improve and be the best that I can be. said earlier today that he thought you looked faster in this offense. Is there anything you did in the offseason to maybe try to re, you know, get faster or lose some weight, anything like that? >> No, nothing specifically. Just uh went on my regiment as normal. >> Do you feel faster? >> No, I feel I feel good. I've always felt good. I don't feel any different than I felt in the past. >> Hey Jaylen, you've been uh through a lot of joint practices over the years. Probably won't talk to you before New England. What do you get out of those kind of workouts? Great competition, new competition. That'll be a really good team. They had great a great run last year, so that'll be good for us to go out there and compete against them. I just think um carrying on the same things that we've been able to do to this point, continue to exercise what we've learned, continue to improve, continue to coach and detail things out, get that alignment that we've been talking about all camp. You always want Devonte out there and I'm sure Mai as well, but those extra reps you've been able to get with guys like Elijah Moore, Darius Cooper, how how valuable are they in you developing their chemistry? >> Words can't describe how valuable they are. You know, I've had a um put an onus on, you know, the time that we spend the summertime and that's always been a very important thing to me. So the time that we've been able to take advantage of in that time and carry that on to where we are now and you know the game happens, right? Injuries happen and so in all it's about how you respond, who steps up and who's able to fill that void. And so um I've been excited with the time that I've had with all of my teammates just to be able to build and grow. It's a long season. It's a long year and you want to be able to have equity in everything, build trust in everyone. So you can go out there and, you know, play fast. >> Talking about the new offense, a lot of the offensive linemen have talked about being the aggressor again. There's less, in their words, playing chess at the line. >> When you get up to the line and in in the passing game, how has that changed for you? Is it quicker? Is it more condensed? How would you describe that? >> Uh, I I would just describe it as as what I've described it in the past. Um, I think, you know, philosophically things are a little different. their approach is different, but you know, our old lineman is they've had the same coach for a very long time. So, I think that that's always been to their benefit because they know what they're getting. Um, you know, I think in all as an offense, it's just about learning, immersing oursel into the new perspective, the new coaching, and then, you know, getting the reps and being able to build off those things. J, now that you guys have had the pads on for, you know, the last several days, are you able to get a sense of like how Saquon and Tank especially have kind of looked in the run game so far? >> I think they've been running very physical, you know, obviously two very physical runners, dynamic runners. Doesn't do justice when it's just a tag off or a thump, but everybody's just been chipping away. Chipping away. So, I think those two have had really good chems. >> Another week almost down. What has impressed you about Shawn Manning in this set training camp? >> Just taking it a day at a time. Taking it a day at a time. I I can go on and on about the things that I've already said about him. Um, we just want to continue to build. >> Lane shared with us the other day his news that this is likely going to be his last season. What has he meant to you and to the team throughout your career? Yeah, Lane. Lane is uh Lane's a special player. He's had a very special career and, you know, to to get to know him and to, you know, for him to immerse himself into, you know, my career and me developing um ever since I walked on walked into Philly. um working out together, the times we spent together. I take pride in those things. And so, you know, I I I want to make sure it's a special year for him. You know, I know it takes um great courage to say this is the last dance going in into it. And so, um you know, I hope I hope he gets everything that he desires out of this year. I [clears throat] think he's pretty good already and I think he's going to continue to grow. Um I can make you a promise and say that he's going to be XYZ. I just think he's going to continue to develop into the player he's shown he he is and um you he has very strong hands. He's always been really good at the deep ball from his time back in small small uh small college Texas ball. So, I think that's the realness in the situation. >> Could you ever have imagined, you know, in a million years like when you guys were playing together like like that that something like this would have been possible? >> Um, the fact that I, you know, I didn't despise talking to the media, but you know, I hated talking to groups of people and crowds and, >> you know, I just, you know, you know, Mayor Parker mentioned it doing eight years at Fox and and doing TV, you know, I felt like God was always challenging me to be better, to grow up. um you know standing in front of your team every day when you got everybody looking at you and hanging on to every word that you say you know that's uncomfortable in the beginning everything was was new. I if I knew what I was about to get myself into I probably wouldn't have did it. But I'm so glad that God gave me the strength to move forward to do it. And now you know year two feels totally different than year one. And I'm more excited when I wake up in the morning. get the butterflies to to be, you know, at work, similar to when I played. And and so now I just I'm just looking at everything in hindsight and just appreciating the path that God is allowing us to walk and the people we are being able to affect and the and the generations that's going to come and be able to to model the same things that we're doing now. So, um just so much respect for Desawn. um you know I mean obviously taking a team from he was one and 11 year before to a eight and four season and coach of the year like anything is possible. So I don't think you know from where we coaching at the experience that we're getting is going it's going to shape well for us you know moving forward down the road. So we're doing great things that that we know we can do and we just got to continue to push the envelope. >> Mike you talked about Philly is always kind of a home for you. You talk about when you signed here, I mean that was obviously very pivotal time in your life personally, difficult time. You talk about um your relationships and being welcomed here by the players, by by Donovan, by Andy, by by the organization. Can you just talk about that experience a little bit? >> I mean, it was amazing experience just having a chance to meet new people. um Donovan welcomed me with open arms and obviously Des Sean, Andy Reid, you know, Dom, Frank, all the people that you see here today was was was there back then and I don't take that for granted. Um, you know, for them, I'll continue to, you know, push the envelope and try to be the best version of myself because I know they watching. And like when people pour into you like that, you got to always continue to take them into consideration when you making decisions, you know, um, when you trying to seek advice, you know, just trying to, you know, follow that same chain of command. And so, like these the people I just named and and more to add, they'll always be influential in my life and I appreciate them. What's the trash talk like leading up to the to the game for week two? >> No, we making agree. We don't tr we don't talk trash to the week of the game. We we kind of we got too much other stuff to talk about. >> He trying to start early. He was trying to talk trash on the field. I said, man, we ain't doing that, man. It's too far out, man. [laughter] Trying to get my get back. >> Did you guys get to watch practice today? And what' you think? >> Definitely, man. Um, you know, I came a little later. I think Mike was here a little earlier, but it looks fresh, man. That defense is going to be dangerous, man. I'm excited to see what the defense does this year. Um, you know, defense wins championships. Always offense win games, but defense wins championships. Um, but um, you know, they look pretty good, man. Um, you know, got a few receivers down, but, you know, I got a chance to talk to Mai a little bit. Um, it was just one of one of those things. This is his first year in the NFL. The workload is very different from college, you know. So, you know, you you can't be rush, not to say rush back, they rushing back, but you got to with hamstrings, you got to be cautious. If you come back too early, man, it's going to prolong that injury. So, you know, just kind of always having a great relationship with the players, man, and being in a situation where I'm realistic and understanding. But they look they look pretty good as far as what I saw. >> All right. Thanks, everyone. >> So, right now, we're going to take some group photos.

title: Jake Elliott & More on Their Training Camp Focus
text: What's up everyone? >> Good to see you. >> All right. >> Michael Clay spoke the other day about he feels like you got your love for football back and that kind of thing. I don't know if you saw those comments, but do you feel like you have a different approach maybe this year than than last year the last couple years? >> Um I don't know that I have a different approach ever really. I think every offseason's kind of the same. you um you go back and look at what happened the year before and try to learn from it and um look at certain situations, you know, where where can I get better, where can I focus and um that's kind of where I'm at every year. >> A little bit of a different operation with Rocco. Um how does that affect him? >> Uh I mean, we've gotten a lot of group work in. He's he's a talented talented kid. He's he's big. He's physical. Um he's kind of stepped in and not missed a beat. So, uh, really happy with the way he's performing and how he's just kind of fitting in and messing with our room. >> How much does it mean to you to have the Eagles express a lot of confidence in you to just make you the only kicker in camp knowing that you can do the job? >> Yeah, I mean, it's always it's always good to be here. I mean, I I love being here. I've been here for 10 years now and um feel like I have great relationships and um I've earned earned the trust and and confidence in them and um but you're always competing, right? It's there's 32 of these jobs in the world, so you're always competing with everybody. Was there an element though of needing to refine your love of the game or your job and what you do? And how'd you go about doing that at 10? >> I don't I don't know if it's refining my love of the game. I think it's you you go back and you you learn from the prior years. You learn from your experiences. I got a lot of experiences to pull from and um I've always loved the game, always will love the game. I don't think it's ever um necessarily that's in question. It's just um how can you be better? When you look at the ones that didn't go your way last year, what did you learn from them? Any common themes in in the kicks that you did miss? >> Um, honestly, a lot of them. We played in a lot of really windy games last year, so um it was it was a tough year conditionwise and I think um the more I can put myself in those situations and try to try to counter that. How can I hit a better ball in the elements? Um you know, I'm uh fortunate enough to play in the in the great Northeast and um have to deal with stuff like that. So, um I think a lot of the times when I'm going out in the offseason this year, I'm I'm figuring out what's the hardest wind I can kick into today and and just refining that that contact, that ball flight, and um trying to improve. >> How much do you tweak or change your off season regimen to get ready for a season if any? Um, it's, you know, I've done it for a while now, so I feel pretty confident in my process and how much I'm kicking and when I'm, you know, loading up my my work days and, um, I feel like I'm in a really good place right now. So, I don't know if it's how I regiment it. It's it's certainly more of how am I refining my fundamentals, what do you think I can get better at, and that changes year to year. So, um, take a deep dive into that kind of stuff, but not necessarily like what's what's regimented. picks up. >> Braden has talked about liking to train in the offseason in Dallas because of the conditions there. Where do you train in the offseason? >> I'm here. I'm here. I think the best best place to train is right here. >> What were I guess you said you try to get out in the windiest conditions you can. What were some of the conditions that you >> Yeah, it it's not necessarily like I'm seeking after windy days, but if I am and there's two sides of the field, I'm going to pick the harder side and work there the most. So, um, it's not necessarily like, oh, I'm going to go up in Canada to train, but I'm going to, you know, I'm I'm going to stay here and I'm going to kind of work on the things like in that stadium over there, you get a lot of winds into you um from left to right. So, if I can find that wind the majority of the time and work into that. >> Where you you like to go to to find that type of >> high schools where they're wide open fields where it's the windiest and then I'll go over to Penn um kick at Franklin Field because it swirls a lot there. So, um yeah, bunch of different spots. I understand very >> um honestly I've gotten a lot of the longer kicks later in the years in the last couple years which which hasn't necessarily helped. Um but no I mean I I still they're all the same kicks to me so I'm striking them all the same way whether it's a 45 yard or 58 yard like all of them are the same mindset same strike. So, um, I feel like I've I've been really good over the last couple years inside of 45 and, um, feel like I'm striking the ball really good and, you know, sometimes you strike it well and it doesn't go your way from that far. So, um, obviously a very black and white position, but um, would obviously love for more of those to go through. >> Who snaps and holds on these uh, practice days? >> A lot a lot of it's just by myself and then once we get closer to OTAAS and those guys are in town, I'll I'll go with those guys. So, no doubt in your mind you can still be that 90% kicker that you were. >> Yeah, I'm extremely confident myself right now. I feel like I've had a great off seasonason. I'm putting together a good camp. Feel like I'm striking at best I have in a while and um every day is a new day. So, um just trying to build on it. >> All right. Thanks, guys. Now, as several of the offensive players have talked about how using pace, getting to the line quick, and you know, cadence can be kind of a weapon being the aggressor. How have you noticed that in this offense? >> Uh, it's very important. Uh, just to line up fast, get an edge on the defense, and ultimately, you know, we know what we got, and coming out, you know, executing and starting fast is big. >> How does that a receiver? Uh, ADA is good cuz you know it's hard to get a beat on what we're doing when we come to the line, line up, move quick, we could be running, we could be passing, but if everything looks the same, it's an advantage for us. >> Is that common across the teams? >> Uh, not every team. Some teams are like that, but not every team. >> Yeah, our feet just got crossed up. But it was a good play, great design. We just, you know, we got to stay on our feet, execute that one. >> Hollywood, uh, Nick said earlier today that he believes the best players on his roster are also the hardest workers and that sets the tone. What have you just noticed about the culture uh, since you've been here and playing for this organization? >> Uh, that's like the standard here. U, I feel like all the guys in these in this building, hard work. Uh, the extra is not really extra, it's the standard. And, uh, that's what I learned here. Uh it's a standard to work hard and you know I fit right in because I try to you know value myself as a hard worker. >> What what have you noticed from uh Darius Cooper so far through training camp you know and also in the spring like you know how how what are your impressions of him? >> Uh I told him when I first got here that uh I like this film from last year. Uh he's improving every day. Um strong to the catch point. Uh he's been making plays when the opportunity is presented. So uh he's been big for us. like the room as a whole. Nick had said it's a lot of different traits that kind of fit together. Do you do you kind of see it that way? >> Oh, yeah. Uh I love this room. Um very competitive. Um we talk a lot helping each other. Um you know, we all learning the offense. So, just the communication in this group. Uh we meshing meshing along like real well. >> You spent some time with the Ravens. I guess I don't know if you're going to play Saturday night. any going back to Baltimore? >> Uh, no. I mean, it's all love in Baltimore. I mean, I done played those guys a few times in my career, so it' be fun, you know, see some familiar faces. Um, and yeah, it's I don't really look too deep into that. >> Take away. >> Uh, I mean, seeing, you know, Lamar, Eric, uh, Dcasta, all those guys, even Jesse, you know, he was there when I got drafted, so it's cool. design you spoke to us about how you're not just a field stretcher, right? You can do more than that. How hard is it in this league to kind of shake a label, right? Like when you're viewed as as one thing to be viewed differently as your career progresses. >> Uh I think it's not really paying attention to how you view. It's kind of like just going to work every day and uh laying the foundation and ultimately showing what you could do to your coaches and to your team and building that trust uh for you to do, you know, other things. What have you seen from a guy behind the scenes? What has he showed you? >> Uh Ma, he's been very engaged since since he got here. Even, you know, when he can't be on the field, he's engaged. Uh come over, talk to him, ask him what what he seen, you know, try to get an input from everyone. And uh he's he's engaged. He's in a meeting room. And I know, you know, when he's able to take the field, he he'll be ready to go. >> You like to play Saturday night? Are you a guy that likes to play in any preseason games? >> Uh, any chance you get a you get an opportunity to play in this league, uh, you take advantage. So, I mean, I don't know if I'm playing or not, but, you know, if I do play, you know, I'll be grateful. Uh, cuz, you know, you never know when it's your last play on that field. >> What are your impressions of uh the offense the Eagles are installing? >> So, what are your impressions of the offense that the Eagles are installing? >> I like the offense. Um, it's definitely uh it's been a lot of fun. Um, and just learning and meshing the run game and the pass game together. It's uh been a lot of fun. >> Yeah. Can you talk a I'm a lot of guys are saying it's a it's fun a fun offense to be in. Can you talk about that a little bit? >> Uh, it's fun for for I mean for receivers cuz you know we could play all over the field. You know we could be inside outside you know running different routes. So that's a lot of fun. >> Yeah. A not serious question. I I I hear on the sidelines some people call you Maris, some people call you Hollywood. Who gets to call you Maris and who gets to call you Hollywood? How's that? >> Uh I give everybody the [clears throat] I give everybody when coach Nick say what you like to be called. I you know I say Hollywood but you can call me Maris. Same you know standard to everyone. Uh you know that's my name. So >> you played with obviously Lamar Jackson and Patrick Mahomes. What what are you seeing from Jaylen Herz in the time that you've been together? >> Uh Jaylen is a hard worker. uh he set the standard, you know, from the day I I got here and uh just being around him in the offseason, how how much works he put in. Um that that was something big that that I seen that he puts in a lot of work and it's uh it's not by chance, you know, he has achieved what he has achieved and so I'm just proud of him and I'm looking forward to working with him. Hollywood, a former Eagle is coming here today to be the coach to promote the game, the black college game to Shawn Jackson. Did you at any point watch him or were you two young? >> Oh, yeah. Uh, the Eagles was my favorite team growing up. I remember getting to Kansas City and telling Coach Reed that. So, uh, yeah, seeing those guys, um, I remember when I got drafted and, uh, seeing, you know, Michael Vic, that was a big moment for me. Uh, so seeing those guys out here and just being a part of this organization, uh, it's been like a full circle moment for me. Uh, and I've been happy since I've been here. >> Appreciate y'all. >> Good afternoon. >> What's up? What's up? >> It seems like you guys really like situational football at the end of this practice. Can you talk about that a little bit? How much it helps you? Uh, honestly, it helps us out a lot, you know, cuz whenever you got situations in the game, it comes second nature. So, to be able to do it at practice, go over those drills and execute them, you know, it's just another way to hone in on those situations so when game day come, everything, you know, is second nature and it doesn't feel like a panic. >> How do you think you're settling into this the big defense so far? Uh honestly, you know, uh being on his defense, it's a lot of know ins and out to it, but uh some similarities to where I came from, but you know, different verbiage, different terminology, you know, different little things to criti critique and play a certain way, but at the same time, this defense is making me better as a player and you know, I'm excited. >> This a learning process where you'd want it in some preseason play? Uh, shoot. Whatever the coach asked me to do, I'mma I'mma do it. I mean, if I go out there and have to do it in preseason game, that's what coach asked me to do, I'mma do it. If I just got to do it within my practices, then I'mma do it. So, >> uh, no, in Seattle, I did not play preseason. >> Had some nice battles with Darius Cooper, a young receiver out there today. What What have you seen from him from a cornerback's perspective? >> Uh, Cooper is a great receiver, man. Uh, I feel like just that whole room, they feed off each other and he continues to grow. I know I got here in OTAAS until now and every rep I have going against him, there's no shortage of hard work. He always goes 100%. And whenever you go against him, you know, you're going to get a great look. So, uh, Coupe is a great receiver and to be able to go against him and battle with him and see him grow throughout training camp, it's a lot of fun. When we first talked to you, you talked about how you like playing off ball a little over this defense >> last couple weeks. How's that looking? >> Um, >> honestly, it's been so so I mean, it's still part of the process. You know, whenever you growing and whenever you uh, you know, striving for something, you know, it may not look like a straight line. You know, sometimes it go all crazy, but I'm still going in the right direction. So, as long as I keep going the right direction every practice, it's going to be reps where, oh, I can slow down in my pedal or I can, you know, break at this time in my pedal or something like that. But at the same time, it's going to be reps where I have great reps as well. So, I just got to keep going in the right direction and, you know, as my off game continues to improve, then it'll be helping me out. >> You're adapting to the timing. >> Mhm. just uh just adapting just just getting a rhythm you know throughout playing off and the more reps I get the more better I'll be. So >> in practice you had that nice PBU it looked like you were frustrated after play. Did you think it should have been a pick? Is that >> Oh yeah that's why I was frustrated just I played it so nice and you know it's a thing like as a DB you'll play a route so nice and the ball don't come your way and then it's like a ball come your way and you play the route nicely. It's like you want to get an interception. So, uh, that that's just the game within the game. You know, as a DB, you get all these plays like run plays and then it's pass plays and you playing around real good and the ball may never come your way and then you know, you play around real good or you don't play the ball or the route real good and the ball comes your way, you know? So, that's just the life of a DB. So, whenever I do have a chance, I'll be want to intercept it. as a former wide out, how much um I guess pride, for lack of of a better term, do you take in your ball skills? Like like do you think if the ball hits your hands, it should be it should be a pick? >> Uh yeah, just because who doesn't like interceptions? I mean, they rare and when whenever you get a chance to get them as a quarterback, you know, you want to take those chances and run with it. So that's why I was kind of a little frustrated, but at the same time as a PBU, so I'm happy. >> Are recognized in team meetings after practice? Mhm. >> How how do they kind of discuss that? >> Oh, yeah. I mean, anytime you do well, you know, it deserves to be celebrated just like if you do a bad play, we going to put it up there as well. So, uh the the good plays are celebrated. So, those interceptions will be shown and uh Q had a nice one today. >> It seems like in this game we haven't had a ton of balls go your way. How do you stay patient when they're not? >> Um, honestly, that's just the name of the game, man. It's like it's kind of weird, you know, like I was telling them as a quarterback, you get all these plays and a ball may not come your way and then the one play where you may kind of slack off for a little bit, the ball will come your way. So, it just makes sure you just on top of your game and just making sure you stay sharp. >> Interceptions. My bad. >> Q has had a couple so far in training camp. What have you kind of noticed from him just working with him so far? >> Um, just his patience, his confidence. Uh, you know, when you whenever you're a quarterback, you got to know your game and he has a real understanding of his game. He's been in his defense and he's played in his defense a little bit. So, he has a good understanding of how he can play certain techniques and certain coverages. So, being able to watch him make plays, it inspires me to make plays just because, you know, I got to build off energy from those from those guys and they feed energy to me, I feed energy to them. So, being able to see him make plays, you know, is motivational to me. when you're in a position to make a play like you were talking about and you want is that the receiver in you that thinks you should that you should come down with? >> Yeah, receiver in me but just you know the competitor too, you know, I feel like anytime you get a chance to take the ball away, it helps the team out a lot especially uh whenever you know you can give the ball back into a great offense, you know. So being able to, you know, give the offense a chance, especially when you take the ball away, it's a big thing. There's been some moving parts in safety behind you with Cooper there in base and then you know Marcus coming in sometimes Michael Carter like how has that group handled all of that and like the communication with the rest of the DBS? Um, honestly, it's been pretty well. You know, as we go through camp, we going to keep continue to to grow. Like, um, today, you know, me and Coop, I was telling him on certain stack formations just to kind of anticipate an end or I was communicating with the safeties and the backers just because the low guy in the stack kind of always goes in. So, being able to play off each other and uh, communicate one one another, it helps out a lot. And as we continue through camp, uh, we're going to continue to grow closer. Thank you. >> Y'all have a great day. >> Um yeah, totally changes my like perspective on a lot of stuff. She's >> uh she's incredible. Uh it's just like fatherhood's the best. So it's it's made me better in all aspects of life, I think. >> Roco's going there. What change in operations? How is that? How do you think that's going? >> Yeah, Rocco is doing really well. He's uh he's excited to get to work every day and just um get better. You know, it's none of us are ever come to work complacent. He's doing a really good job just being like these are things that good on and I want to maintain. These are things that I want to work on. So, he's he fits right in into the group and been working hard. >> What did it mean for you to get the extension this off season? >> Yeah, it meant the world. I mean, it was uh it was I think I said it when I first got it was it just means the world they want to keep me here for uh you know, four years like that. Have the confidence in um Howie and everybody in the building. It was it was awesome. So, I'm super thankful and happy to be back for another four. We feel like uh our family's found a home here. So, we're >> Why are you so much better than when you with the Jets? >> Uh yeah, I think there's a lot of just different things that go into it. I think experience helps uh the more years you go and um just the more you kind of figure out about your game. And then the people here have been amazing. Coach Clay and all those um and all the coaches and the whole staff, they just do such a good job of pouring into you. Uh so I think that helps. And then um just learning a lot from different partners and different players around the league and um yeah, I think just working on my weaknesses as much as I can. >> I mean, if I just follow up because like the numbers just jumped as soon as you left and got here. Mhm. Um, >> is there one thing? Is your leg stronger or same leg or? >> Uh, I don't think it's necessarily stronger. I think it's just more I got more control under it over it. I think I think it's um Yeah, I was probably stronger in the weight room, much stronger in the in college. I think I think it's just more of uh your mis hits. It's kind of like golf. I mean, some of the longest hitters aren't necessarily the best players. It's kind of knowing your game and knowing how to hit certain balls and um yeah, just adjusting to the conditions, too. I know you you work out in different places, so you didn't really spend the entire offseason with him, but what's your impressions of of Jake and how he's handled his season last year and how he's come back to camp. >> Yeah, Jake's always a workhorse. I mean, he's he comes to work every day and just uh has fun doing it and works hard every day and um definitely someone I look up to in terms of the way they work and um yeah, got all the confidence in the world of Jake as always. >> What have you noticed from Rocco as he's getting used to you and Jake working together? Yeah, I think he came in and uh fit right in in terms of um just like a culture fit for us. He's uh fun guy to talk to, fun guy to work with, and then also just just comes in and works every day. He knows um things that he's good at, wants to maintain those things that he needs work on, he comes in ready to work on those. So, I think uh it's been a smooth operation so far and looking forward to working on the rest of the year. >> Is that a tough thing for a young kid like that to come in to a specialist group that's of the veteran caliber that you and Jake are at? Um, when I came into the league, I had a couple vets and it was it was helpful for me because they kind of uh knew the whole like knew the ropes and everything and had a little bit of advice to offer. So, that's helpful. We're trying to help as much as we can there. There's certain things as the rookie though, you're just going to learn by doing. I know it was my case. So, uh yeah, we're trying to help as much as we can, but also things that he's going to figure out just for himself. >> You said other partners you learned from. Anybody in particular that you kind of really paid attention to? >> Uh, yeah, I just try to take a lot of different stuff from different people's games. Um, I mean, in terms of hitting like different punts, Johnny Hecker, uh, he had some years there where he just like he was hitting all sorts of crazy weird punts and then a lot of the Australian guys have good control over their Aussie style punts. Um, looked at a lot of I try to do a lot of like outdoor punter stuff because they know how to punt in conditions. It's easy to say like in a vacuum and an indoor like, oh yeah, it's a perfect thing, but it's just a different game I think outdoor. So, just trying to learn from a lot of guys who've done it in bad weather. you do you have a lot of pride in the fact that your numbers are so good compared to indoor punters and you're in the northeast all the conditions. >> Yeah, I think the numbers are honestly just uh >> I don't know the numbers don't tell the whole story too cuz like some years you might have 80% of your your punts open field punts so that's not really your numbers going to jump obviously and then some years you're going to have more inside the 20 or whatever. So I think it's not always just the numbers that tell the story. I think that one tells a lot of the story too. I know there's maybe like always a level of anxiety being in the NFL, but do you feel more comfortable than than you've ever felt here in the situation you're in? >> Um, I mean, in this building, I've I've felt comfortable since pretty much the day I walked in. Just everybody's done such a good job of making you feel at home and like family. It's it's really cool. So, I don't think necessarily it's more so this year than last year. Anything. I think really since the day I got here, it's just been I got into a nice environment, not complacent, but just like comfortable to walk in and have confidence every day.

title: ITB: How Greenard Injury, Stowers Slow Development Will Impact Eagles Roster Decisions
text: Inside the birds is back. What's going on every is Jeff Mosher, Adam Kaplan. We are in the middle of the week. And Adam, you and I want to hit on some really um pressing subjects coming out of uh Vic Vic's press conference and of course what's going on at OTAAS before we really get into the preseason game later this week. Uh the first bit of news and it's not new news, but it's to me something that puts it more into perspective and that's really about Jonathan Gennard. You know, he started camp on PUP. Um, I know you and Andrew discussed it and the belief he'd be out two to four weeks because of the pec strain that he had from weightlifting, right? Well, we're already two weeks in, a little bit more about next week would be week three and Vic Fangio said this guy is weeks at least away from being able to come back and Vic basically put the gibash on Jonathan even coming back before camp. So, Adam, that would mean that the season would start with Granard having absolutely no practice, no camp, and he's already coming off last year's shoulder injury. So, I think it's a it's a it's an unfortunate thing for him for the Eagles. He was their biggest offseason addition, but really it kind of puts into question what their edge rotation, a what they're going to do from a 53man standpoint at that position, and b what it's going to look like at the for the first few weeks of the year. All right, Gernard is coming back from major shoulder surgery. Let's call it like it is. Okay. text: It is the OTP here with you once again and I am joined by my friends Jim Wyatt who's in charge of Tennessee Titans.com. That works for you, doesn't it? Total control. >> I don't know about that. A lot of people are involved. I know my writing appears on that, but there's a lot of people working on that side as well behind the scenes and out front. >> And I'm a part of >> And our lead sideline analyst / reporter Brad Hopkins is on the field for us this season. >> Taylor, don't let Jim fool you. There's no one that knows more about what's going on in this organization than Jimmy Wyatt. >> great seeing you this past Friday night hop on the field with the headset on doing interviews for us and I of course and Taylor Zars are doing the play-by-play and we're here every Monday on the OTP. We are here and we've been doing Monday OTPs for you the past few weeks. We're going to keep this going through August and then Robert Saleh is going to join us each week on the OTP once the season starts in September. First and foremost, Hop, you've been out there just about every single day. What have you thought of training camp so far? >> You know, I wasn't surprised to see the big catches that we were seeing from the receiving core, but what I was surprised was that the defense getting their hands on a few of the balls that were thrown in the air. Obviously, Cam was picked off a couple of times. We saw Trubisky was picked off a couple times. The point being turnovers was something that the defense could have used last year and it seems like they're getting used to that identity this year. >> Brad was an incredible offensive lineman that Jim Wyatt used to write about back in his Tennesseean days when Brad was an all-pro and a perennial Pro Bowler protecting Steve McNair. Jim, the pads are back on, which means the Brad Hopkins now have a fighting chance because the offensive lineman without pads on were definitely at a disadvantage. What did you notice in this past week? >> Yeah, I mean you can tell things get ramped up when the pads come on. I think teams obviously look crisper being in camp for now eight practices. You can see some things, you know, develop where it looked more like it's supposed to look like. That's at the receiver position, that's at the quarterback position. I think the offensive line still you know, we'll find out a lot more about those guys and everybody once we are hit San Francisco here later this week, but I think things are starting to come together and and working through a lot of things. >> Friday night at Nissan Stadium was a lot of fun. Started thinking about some nostalgic things at Nissan Stadium knowing it's the last year of the current stadium and then getting excited looking next door at this massive mon- enclosed monstrosity with all of the lights on what is going to be new Nissan Stadium. The fireworks show was a lot of fun. Great crowd on hand as well. As for the actual competition, Jim, what did you see? >> Yeah, I mean I thought and it is going to be a nostalgic season. Hard to believe that that that stadium is going to be coming down and a new one's going to be opening up. Brad remembers playing in those in that stadium when it was at its best and it's can't believe how many years have passed. Hard for me to believe, but what I saw at the stadium practice, I thought Cam looked good. You know, him and Whandeo Robinson I think connected. I don't know if Whandeo caught all nine of his passes from Cam, but he had nine catches in that practice. Cardinal Tate put on a show, you know, with a one-handed catch and made some other really nice plays. I thought offensively the team, you know, did some really good things and then you know, as Brad mentioned, I think the defense is showing some great signs in these practices as well, getting hands on the football. And um And those guys, you know, they're ready to get after it and tackle somebody instead of touching them. >> I was really impressed by Cam, especially the way he moved the other night when he was facing pressure from Jeff Simmons and others. >> Taylor, one thing that I noticed was that the drives were longer in the beginning of the scrimmage, meaning when the ones took the field, we saw them putting together six, seven, eight-play drives. Jimmy, you saw that. And the reason why is because they were staying out of the negative down and distances. I thought that we saw Cam moving the ball efficiently. He was playing with that element of speed that, you know, Brian Daboll is going to require for this this offense to be effective, right? So, I didn't see them committing many penalties. You know what I mean? I didn't see Cam starting with third and like forever to go, you know, to complete a series. And that's why we saw them being able to put up points earlier. Now, of course, as the scrimmage waned and you got the younger guys in there, we saw a few more mistakes that were being made and then the and the series were becoming a little bit shorter. But when Cam was in there, Taylor, I thought I saw a guy that knew what he was doing with the offense. And this is just his first couple few months in this new system. >> You uh opened that stadium, Brad. You were a Houston Oiler. You became a Tennessee Oiler and then a Tennessee Titan. I'm going to be selfish here because the last padded practice I saw Brad Hopkins was the most impressive thing I have seen in practice in the first few weeks by any player, and his name is Carnell Tate.
