And [laughter] day two of scrimmages in the preseason, you are asking for trouble, and I will never forget as long as I live being on the Atlanta Falcons practice field last year on day two, and him saying, "Taylor, come stand over here. There's going to be a fight right here." And 3 minutes later, there was a fight right there. And four different times he moved me during practice cuz he knew not only he knew there's going to be a fight where the fight was going to be. So, yeah, trying to avoid that here and only practicing and scrimmaging as 49ers, Seahawks, and Bears once before you play them in the game. >> I remember coach Mac and I you're right about him just having a birthday. I still remember last year in Tampa, he had his birthday when we were at the joint practice against the Buccaneers. A lot of people were coming up to him wishing him a happy birthday, and he didn't really even want to acknowledge that it was his birthday. He was almost trying to throw people off the scent. >> at me right now. >> I I will never I'll treasure that trip, too. John Gruden and him going back and forth throughout practice. That was That was great. He'd be so fired up that Brad Hopkins and Ramon Foster are part of Titans Radio with us now. He loves both of them like we do, and we're excited to be on Titans Radio with us. Jim Wyatt's going to be on Titans Radio in the pregame show as well. Let's get to the plane, boys. Let's go to the Bay Area, take on those San Francisco 49ers. 8:00 local time is when you can listen to Kick. We'll be on the air at 7:00 with the pregame show, and I can't wait to get out there and join you for that. Jim Wyatt, Brad Hopkins, I'm Taylor Zarzour. Thank you for watching the OTP.

title: Cam Ward, Jeffery Simmons & Peter Skoronski After the Titans Scrimmage
text: Operating in all three phases, how did you feel about the offensive phase, the execution? >> I think we've had a pretty solid day. Um especially running football. I think the guys up front, you know, they did their job from the first group, the second and the threes, you know, they all did their job moving. You know, the defensive line today up front, um even in the in the drop back game they were real good. So, um we were able to make some big plays, some some intermediate game plays as well just because of the O line. Um but it's good to see. >> Yeah, it seems like you're like everything's speeding up for you you're working through the progression and knowing where you want to go etc. Do you agree with that and if so, what is it you feel is is behind you? >> Uh I do. Um because I'm seeing the the game in a different aspect uh especially being with Coach Day and Coach Shay. Um trying to see the game from everybody's perspective just mine. Uh you got to be able to help the old lineman out, you know, not when they're not at their best. Um and you also got to help the running backs and receivers out when they're not at their best and that's when I have to be, you know, pinpoint accurate with the football. Um so it's a lot to it and I think just the system is allowing, you know, everybody to play at a faster rate. Um we're able to get to the line of scrimmage faster on all ends. Um but I think it's, you know, the system is a part of it as well. >> How's that process been as far as I know in the past that he's challenged quarterbacks to extend plays, do do what you do personally? But you also got to limit those turnovers. How's that process been as far as like him getting you to understand how to how to balance both of those out? >> Well, it's been great. Um and Coach Day he lets me be me. Um he he he warns me uh when I need to be a a better decision maker um but he but he never holds me back. He always wants me to go out there a confident gunslinger um whether that's throwing it down the field, checking it down, throwing it across the middle. Um but he he continues to give me pointers on knowing the situation when to do some of the things. Um and I think that's what's going to help myself and the team this year. >> Mitch was talking Mitch was talking about some of that stuff. He said in in some of his stops he feels like he's been asked to be robotic and that that Dayball doesn't ask that at all. Do you feel a difference from that? Were there times when you felt like you had to do things a very precise, robotic way in the past, and now you have more freedom? >> Um, no. Um, David doesn't want robots, and I'm I'm not a robot, so um, he just kind of continues to emphasize the the the play and how you have to play as a quarterback. Um, he emphasizes every each and every situation, um, each and every day, whether that's watching our stuff in practice situationally, or as watching other NFL teams, you know, across the league. Um, and so, you know, he's doing a big study, you know, to help us a better offense and a better team. Um, but I mean, he he's been good. He's been helping me and Mitch out a lot. >> And all the confidence and confidence that you talked about being a confident offensive Is that having a guy like Wan'Dale in the slot and guys like Cornell that you can trust that are going to catch the ball when you get open and you're making those plays and you're kind of extending them and getting the >> Uh, for sure, all of them. Um, even Richie and EL and Chim as well. Um, our whole receiver core can do different things. They can do it all at a high level. Um, and the I think the the confidence for me is knowing that they're always in the right spot at the right time. And so, you know, the more that we continue to, you know, have a have a just a the continue to build the connection with me and Wan'Dale, um, cuz he's new and I think it's just going to be, you know, better for everybody. And you know, I think the the best thing is that we continue to get better at scramble drill. Um, we had some of our best plays just in camp today, uh, scramble drill. And so, you know, it's good to have those guys with me. >> Where do you think Where do you think you got in all of the offensive standpoint at this point in the year and the practice before you go to California, but where do you think you are at this point and how much will you find out next week against the 49ers? >> Uh, I think we're at a great point. Um, I think we're very physical offense, um, and I'm I'm excited to go against, you know, a very physical team in in uh, San Fran. So, you know, it's going to it's going to be a great joint practice. It's a great um preseason game. Uh and I'm I'm excited to, you know, go there as a team, go there and uh you know, try to compete with and win a game. >> How happy were you to see that guy take make it a one-hand grab without ever breaking stride? >> Um no reaction. Um we got back to the huddle, told him the same thing I tell him every time, "Good catch." Um that's stuff that I I expect out of him. He's He's made some crazy plays, you know, in our in the offseason, just me and him throwing when I didn't have, you know, a best ball. So, uh he he has he has great hands. He has great feel for space. Um but I mean, what what he did, you know, right there, that's nothing I haven't seen before. >> Damn, how happy were you to see Peters still get it done? >> Uh it was great. He's the best left guard in the game. Um he he's been there for me since, you know, I got here last year. Um and, you know, he's a he's a he's a leader on the offensive line. You know, he's someone that people can look to, you know, when times are tough to continue to have the the same attitude each and every play. Um and the best thing about Peters is that he wants to win. Um and so, you know, everything that that that he get, you know, he deserves it. He works hard for it. Um and, you know, I'm excited that, you know, I got him, you know, blocking for me for a little minute. >> Just for practice back out on the stadium turf, kind of you were pretty vocal about that last year. Are you doing anything different to deal with the turf this year, or is it just something you kind of have to live with one way or the other? >> Uh I mean, something you got to live with, honestly. you know, we have, you know, minimum eight games left in the stadium trying to, you know, make it somewhere in the playoffs, but um end of the day, it's football. You can't let that be, you know, a factor of our process, a factor of, you know, how we play. We just got to adjust to the situation. And, you know, try to, you know, do our best when there. >> You jealous of those World Cup players who get grass wherever they go? >> Uh I was jealous. Um just because, I mean, I mean, who wouldn't want to play on grass? It's It's natural. It's from the earth. Um God created it for us. And so, um I mean, it it I It is sad, but, you know, at the end of the day, you know, I I play football. My job is to, you know, be the quarterback for the Tennessee Titans and not to worry about all the other stuff. >> Talk about your relationship in terms of growth from you and Gunner Hoak. >> Oh, it's been great. He's one of the guys that I continue, you know, hang off the field, getting reps in, in and out of practice. And you know, he's a big body, especially in the red zone. And he he just silky smooth, especially whether it's on double moves, option routes. He has a great feel for zone. He doesn't get credit for how, you know, well he can actually block. But you know, he's going to have a great year. We're going to continue, you know, make some more plays. >> In joint practices coming up, of course you guys have seen each other as a unit. But does that competition and intensity ramp up as you guys go to face a different team and get more dollars and different looks than, you know, just you guys and Gus Bradley and guys like that and you? >> Uh, for sure. It's exciting because you know, we finally get to to have a have a game where there's practice or the pre-season game. And you know, we get to go there as one. We get to to talk, you know, to the other team as one instead of to each other. And we get to continue to be ourselves and express ourselves, you know, in a world of how Coach Saleh wants us to play football. You know, it's going to be exciting. >> How much do you want to play in the pre-season games? You know, you guys will get a lot of work in the joint practices, but in the actual games, how much do you want to play? >> Uh, it's not how much I want to play, it's how much Coach Saleh and Coach Day will want to play me. And so every time they need me, and I'm available, I'm there. And so you know, we going we going to get some good reps in. But some other guys get some good reps in. It's going to be a good turnout. >> How much do How much black and forth I guess you do after a scrimmage like this? >> Say that again? >> And then did Marcus, the guy that got his hand on the ball on the two-point conversion late, and what's the banter like after a competition like that tonight? >> Um, it's great. A A of words being said, especially with me and Marcus. Um but I mean that's just competition at an all time high, you know, I didn't do my job, you know, by getting it over. Um so, you know, so it's a lot of things, you know, right after that moment happened that I wish I could have had back. Um but I mean that's where, you know, I just got to be better um with the getting to a better play, um with getting it around him and, you know, giving my guy a chance to win. >> How much more difficult is the screen game in this system than it was in the previous system? >> You said the screens? Um they're very different. I think we're allowed to sell them more. Um we're we're faster on our screens, especially with the count the old ones going on. We're more explosive, I believe. Uh and I think every screen ties to, you know, a certain person um depending on the defensive end if we want to screen off him, you know, or or receivers. Um then I think David has a great feel for calling them as well. >> Coach >> Jeff, how did you feel about the tempo tonight with the defense and the defensive line as well as the offense? >> It was great, man. It's just the reason why we play the game um to be able to come out here and just put the ball down and go play football. Um I love it. Um you know, in the past, you know, you get them type of um mock games, but I mean, I think coach said we was close up to like 50 plays. Like when when you're going, it's just like a regular game. When you're going, you don't realize how many plays you actually have and have played, but I mean, I I I liked it. I I liked the um the scrimmage um set up. Um you know, he came in and told us I'm going to let you guys play football and I'm got in you got to love it um to be able to compete, you know, um and I I even said it after we got done, way to compete because at the end of the day, we're trying to get each other better. We got cuz we got one ultimate goal. Um and you know, you got to love it. Um so today was fun. >> Y'all the scrimmage, Jeff, and how happy were you to see that Pete got his PR in? >> He deserved it. Yeah, he deserved it, man. And um that's a lot of people don't know, man. I I had like last I think it was last week I told Pete, man, I got I enjoyed going up with you. And I told him, I said, "You want to even after practice, you want to get that extra work in, you want to get It's something you saw at practice, like ask me, you know?" So, to be able to battle against P these last couple years at practice have helped me so much. Um I don't give P his props enough. Um especially to you guys, you know, um you just know Some of you guys just know that we practice against P, or is he over Jeff some, but man, P have helped me got better so much, and vice versa. And so, and I told him that to But to see P one of the most humble guys, you know, he came in, he put him on the board, you know, Solly announced it to the team. Um you know, no one's Of course, we were in a meeting, so we didn't know, but Solly put it on the team um in the team meeting today, and the excitement from the whole team because we know how hard P worked. Um but one of the most quietest guy in the building. So, man, I'm happy for P. Um happy to uh for him to keep getting better, um and helping me getting better, especially um going into this season. I'm going to need it, and he going to need it, so especially with this new front, you know, he came up to me last week, he was like, "Bro, like keep going. Like come to my side." Like cuz a lot of plays last week, I wasn't even on his side. He came to me, he was like, "Is Is you going to always be over to the left?" But I'm like, "Nah, P, like you want me to come over there, let me know." So, I'm excited for P. Um it's going to be really good. Um I'm sure his family and himself really happy. So, happy to have him as a teammate much longer. >> With your contract and and his and some of the others, how do you like the way the value is now being placed on the interior part with you and he both working? >> Man, I've been saying forever, the game is The game is going to be won in trenches. I mean, we can look at each team who have won Super Bowls. You look at these teams that very successful, it start up front. And we we see where this where I mean, look at the defensive side. I mean, we go get JFM, we go get Jermaine, we go get Jake, we go get guys to win up front. And so, I'm excited about it. I'm excited to see that And I would That's the reason why I said it early on. I mean, all upstairs, Mike Vrabel, Jon Robinson, they have a vision and it's up to us to go out there and just do our job and let them do their job and I'm I'm very satisfied with what they're doing. You know, starting with Miss Amy, of course, you know, let's appreciate her for everything she's doing for this franchise. And she let Vrabel, Jon Robinson and them cook and that's what it's all about. We just need to go out there and play football. >> You're talking about that you're talking about that vision. It's been a long time since somebody like yourself got a contract here. Just is it encouraging to you to start seeing some of these younger guys as come up behind you and players that you're seeing build or kind of actually at that point now? >> I mean, I think that's the and I go back to saying like you got to appreciate it especially for myself to have been in this building. It's a lot of guys that have came and gone. They're they're gone now. And I haven't I How many I mean, me and Hook is probably the longest tenured Titan here and you see things like that. Like I'm and that's why I say I'm happy for P. I'm happy for guys who we drafted. Now it's up to us especially the cornerstone players. I mean, P is not a guy that going to talk a lot. He's not going to be a big vocal guy, but when he goes out there on Sundays, you know, he going to show that he's a leader of the offensive line. Vice versa on the defensive side, me and Hook, like we've been here the longest. So it's up to us. I mean, it's been 4 years since I haven't been to the playoffs. So it's like I want that feeling again and None of that matter, of course, but to be able to see, you know, guys like myself, P, Hook get that sec that next contract. There's like myself, three contracts here. Like that's exciting. It's a step ahead of you know, what we have installed in the past and props to like I said starting with Miss Amy. >> How much How much progress do you think the defense has made so far in camp and how much you're looking forward to just kind of gauging progress against them? >> [clears throat] >> It's going to be good. You know, we can go out there and hit on other people other than our teammates. It's always It's to see especially during training camp to see a different offense. Um I mean, playing against played against them last year, we kind of know the offense a little bit. Well, myself um and some of the guys that was here, we kind of know a little bit what they going to do, of course, but at the end of the day, it's it's one of them things to where it's still the game of football. Um you know, I think as a defense um we started out a little flat today. I even said that at the half time. Um it's for us as a defense to be able to hold to that standard, the fast and violent, to be the best defense in the in the NFL, we have to start fast. And um that's been one of our problems here in Tennessee. Um sometimes we start fast, finish slow. Um it's vice versa. So, it's one of them things to and you can hear us talking about it each and every day. Coach Gus come in there, solid talking about it. White Cotton is how can we, especially the front, how can we take over practice? How can we go out there and dominate? And, you know, I don't you know, we talk about I I sometimes say something to the DBs and trying to get them going, but and I told his coach um on the sideline I know the damn like, "Hey, man, if they could do all the reverses and stuff in that nature, blame the defense line." So, that's our mindset is we control the game up front and, you know, that's what we focus on. >> What you and J.C. got into the other day, it's not the first time you guys have sparred. Is that kind of in a way, your way of trying to push him to reach the next level and maximize his potential? >> I mean, I push everybody. I think at the end of the day, um my actions, I should say, wasn't appropriate um with the the taking a punch and swinging a punch. Um but at the end of the day, man, I'm I'm a competitor guy. Um when when we talking about the game of football, especially in the trenches, I think sometime people on the outside can blow things up. Um you know, we I I see I see the things. I see, you know, my family like, "Oh, you Listen, I I'm When I play this game, I'm passionate. Everything I got, I leave it on the football field. I mean, that's just the that's all I know. I know the game of football. When I when I touch that field, practice, game, I don't care. I I like to play fast. I like to play violent. I like to compete. And so, when I I attack the field, it's nothing against JC. It's nothing against At the end of the day, like I just said earlier, we are in this thing together. I'm trying to get him better. He trying to get me better. Yeah, temper flare. And like I I go back to taking accountability to taking a um swing at JC. But at the end of the day, it's no beef. My job is to continue to get JC better. His job to continue get me better. Same thing today. We talked smack. Me and JC had been there 2-hour talk the other day. Just talking like talking football, talking off the field things. Like that's what the game about. And Of course, if you guys didn't know what I just I mean, without me saying me and JC had a long talk. You guys don't know that. It's just oh, Jeff said me got a hot head. This and that. It's the game of football. Things happen at practice. Throwing a punch is not appropriate, of course. But at the end of the day, no, it's no it's no personal beef, none of that. We here to continue to get each other better. >> Why would that If you want to make Cam and and the E check the ball down, that's generally a win. What's it feel like though when they So, they checked it down to Pollard a bunch and kind of marched down the field with that? That like a semi win or >> It's football. I think at the end of the day, I mean, we could get Cam to not throw the ball down the field to coordinate tape, great. Um if he could get a check down, we just got to rally to it. Um sometimes TP may just be in the flat by himself. Um it depend on the coverage. Heck, I don't really know sometime what coverage in. I'm hearing what I need to do. I'm trying to get to the quarterback. Half of them may be in a sack. Who knows? So, I think at the end of the day, I mean, it's practice. Um that's the reason why they talking about we need to be in the best shape. We need to be able to I mean, that's the reason why they say you may not be able to play more than four snaps. Cuz they want us to run it running out the stat. Cam throw a check down. It's up to us to get out the stat. Up to all the linebackers to make sure we get to the ball, so I mean it's practice things happen. >> Thanks man. >> Yep. >> How do you feel to know that they want you to be a part of the future going forward? >> Yeah, it's it's unbelievable feeling. Um, I think every player's goal is to to be a part of a franchise and to help a franchise win and um, I guess really be wanted. You know, I think cuz this is such a transitory league that you know, people are in and out and to have a team commit to you like the Titans have I'm just really blessed and um, feel really lucky to be a part of this and super excited. >> I think you've done pretty good. >> Um, I didn't really have any specific timeline in a timeline in my head. Um, got a great agent and I kind of just let him handle everything and the Titans were great too and so I kind of just picked up a little bit ago and um, we got it done but there was never like a you know, September 1st deadline or anything like that. It just kind of happened when it did and um, definitely grateful to have it over with now but yeah. >> Did you expect highest >> Um, honestly like I said I I kind of stayed out of the process. Um, you know, I I consider myself to be in that group. I strive to be in that group of of the best guards in the league. I think you know, if [snorts] if that's where I'm where my goals are I think that helps our team. So I think from a personal standpoint and skill standpoint that's where I aspire to be. So um, you know, the numbers and the stuff are great but like this stuff changes every year. So like what how much can you really invest in that? Um, but very fortunate very lucky with that too. So I I'm I'm very grateful. >> A couple of years ago you talked a little bit about how the interior line of prize is going up. How do you like the way you know, you were able to kind of set the floor of the table for for the next >> Yeah, I mean just speaking broadly I mean you can't tell me the position's not important. Um, just look at the guy on our own team who who changes games, you know, big Jeff. So I mean you can't tell me the guys who have to block that guy aren't important too. So um, it does start with guys like that being so highly valued and they are they are super valuable. Um, but yeah, I mean, I think >> [snorts] >> that's always a good thing to to help the market along and help other guys along, too. I think that's a positive thing, but um, yeah, there's a reason because we have a tough job and I think defense is now key on that, too, that the interior line is kind of where the pocket starts. And so, um, that means the position's important. Yeah, I I think that's a good way to put it, but I you know, for me personally, I think my process has always been my process and to just be the best player I can be. Um, you know, the team rewarded me by picking me high 3 years ago and um, or they sorry, they rewarded me by picking me high 3 years ago and um, and that's been my process ever since to just try to be the best player I can and help the team win. Um, you know, this obviously a huge blessing, but for me, the process stays the same and um, just being I can. I think that's that's all I can do to probably to reward the team as best as I can and and to give back to what they gave me. Yeah, I mean, I'll I'll kind of just recycle what I said a little bit like you know, obviously, it's a huge it's a huge deal for sure and I'm very lucky, but you know, I I think if if I'm someone who's got to change something right now, um, that means my process probably wasn't very good to begin with. Um, and I think the team believes in me and what I've done. And yeah, the expectation raises a little bit, but you know, for me, the goal is the same, that the standard is the same as when I came in is to to be the best left guard I possibly can and and help the team win. And um you know, I I've just got to do that and do that at the very very best I can. And um yeah, I mean it's just it's just that. I think if you're someone who oh, shoot, I have a contract now I'm going to change everything I do. I'm going to try to do a million things. I think that's, you know, going to get you nowhere. And um I'm going to keep trusting the process that I always have. >> What did tonight tell you about where this offense is so far? >> Yeah, I like their execution. Like their ability to move the ball. Um this is a really great defense to go against. Um a huge huge challenge in terms of what they do up front. Uh [snorts] but proud of the way we moved the ball. I think Cam converted a few third downs that was really good. You saw Tape making plays. Um I think converting in the red zone is another huge deal. Um we had the one touchdown, but it stalled out a couple times. Um that feels like a little bit of a broken record of what I've said up on these podiums for a few years now. So, I think great teams do that. Um that stands out for sure. Uh decent job in the second two minute. First one was just okay. Um but got to protect. And I think by and large a decent job of that, too. But um yeah, this is still just August 7th right now. We're still learning and growing and getting better. Um we've got a huge challenge next week with San Fran. So, um but I think the group's really competing hard, and I think you're seeing that. So, it's good. >> What are you looking forward to the 49ers practices and how much will that tell about where things are? >> Joint practices are really cool, I think. Um like you said, it's a it's a big measuring stick for sure. Um obviously a great way to almost have like a game, but in a controlled environment. And you can always kind of tell where you stack up a little bit um with other teams cuz, you know, after 2 weeks like we're kind of just beating each other back and forth with our own team. Um so, you kind of see where you're at, and also get a new looks and stuff. So, um a huge challenge for us. Be great to see guys compete and adjust to what they throw at us. Um you know, we're just going to compete and try to get better from there. Uh like I it's not the be all end all next Thursday or next Tuesday when we practice, but um definitely a great opportunity and looking forward to it. >> Looking back on it, what was it like going through the process when the Titans drafted you and you've been a college tackle and they said, "No, you're you're going to be a guard for us." >> Um there there wasn't really much to it. I pretty much went right to guard. Um there wasn't a whole lot of deliberation there. I just they just slot me at a guard and that was it. Um you know, I appreciate all this this current staff and the staffs that came before and letting me stick to guard. I think that was a really critical thing for me. with Brave and even Kelly, too. They really let me stay in there and develop as opposed to moving around and then having to learn new things and go back and um that was a huge benefit to me. So, very grateful for that. But yeah, there was never really another option. I I was pretty much left guard from day one and um stuff have been a process. There's been a lot of ups and downs and there's still going to be ups and downs, but um the goal is to keep getting better and feel like I've done that up till now and going to keep trying to do that. >> How much faster is it going against this attack front every day? How much faster is it actually from your vantage point? And is there a counter to it or do you just kind of have to know they're trying to >> It's what It's way faster. Um it's funny enough thinking about my rookie year when I watched teams like this on film, I would just be like in that our defense was very good our rookie year, but they didn't play like this up front. There's still a little more reading style and um not the same philosophy, which is neither here nor there, but when I watch this style defense on film, I'd be like, "I don't think I could block them." Like I didn't think I had the ability to handle going against them. Like that's just they play so fast, so explosive. Um what do you call it? Rush and crush. I mean, they're just trying to blow stuff up. Um it's really hard. It's the pace of the game is super fast. Um you've got to be able to play with technique. You've got to be able to adjust on the move. Um it's been a huge challenge, but um what I think is a good thing is, you know, going into, you know, the best best team in our division was uh one of the best teams in our division was Houston and they play the same style. So, you know, what a great way to practice going against a really good defense and the rest of the defense in the NFL, too, but it's a huge challenge and then look at the personnel we have, too. So, um, yeah, it's it's a grind and really challenges the offensive line. >> How has Austin been able to kind of help accelerate the running game or which is our offense and trying to, you know, give it the speed? >> Yeah, I think accelerate is a great way to put it because he knows everything and that's really what you want in a center is a guy who knows everything. Um, there's a lot of volume in this offense and so that's been a challenge for everybody to learn and which is which is a normal thing, but thankfully Schotty knows it and you know, there's a couple times where we're moving and getting up to the ball fast and barking calls and thankfully he's the guy who knows all this stuff and has been in the system and gets us on the same page. Um, it's been a huge advantage so far early on. I feel like I'm finally feeling like myself and playing like how I did in college and just playing free and really just a shout out to to coach Hines and AD because they work with me the most and I probably wouldn't be anywhere close to where I'm playing now, you know, without their help. So, they've been awesome. >> Are they pulling you aside to do extra things or is it just the coaching that you get during practice time? >> Yeah, all of it. Like me and AD will meet in the mornings and we'll watch film and he'll give me just little things to think about through the day and then coach Hines like we're on the field even pre-practice like we'll be working together on you know, technique or kind of anything just, you know, things that I need to work on. He's been super helpful and he's done a great job, so I'm pretty pumped to have him in my corner. >> What is your competition level in those one-on-one pass rush drills? What does that bring out in you and the guys? >> It's great. I mean we got we got a great O line and we got great guys to go against. Like for me personally I love going against uh you know, AB and going against Gray. They're guys that are stars in the NFL and they play really good football and I feel like for me I get a chance every day to go against, you know, one of the best offensive lines in the NFL. So, I love the competition and, you know, I love just to compete every day. >> Do you have to vary your moves day-to-day like a regular opponent or do you just run with your best stuff? >> I always go I'm I'm a big power guy, so I go, you know, if if it if it's not broke, don't fix it. So, I'm working on that. >> Well, you've got a pretty impressive group of defensive ends in your position group, both outside linebacker and defensive line. A bunch of guys with 10 plus years in the league. What is what is that like for you as a young player to have those guys around you? What do you learn from them? >> It's great. I think the coolest thing about having like, you know, J-Reed, Leo, like all those guys that have taken all those snaps is I never feel like I'm alone, you know, if I make a mistake or if I see something cuz I mean they've had like 9,000 I I don't know, 15,000 snaps between the two of them. Like it's been great. So, anytime I see something if I have a question like they've gone through it and they've dealt with it and, you know, it's been super helpful for uh me cuz they I feel like they have all the answers. So, I'm going to them just trying to learn as much as I can. >> How much are they proactive where you don't even have to ask the question, they are just willing to offer advice? >> Yeah, definitely. I you know, it's been cool cuz Leo we're both taller than tackles, so he'll always kind of pull me aside, you know, tell me a couple things about like, you know, how to use my length and how to use my size to my advantage, so it's been super helpful and I just appreciate them taking the time to do that. >> Leo spent some time talking to great stable last year helping the opposite side. You talk to the offensive lineman at all? >> Yeah, I you know, I definitely all the guys like Mason and then Gray and you know, AB. I I talked with all of them and I kind of what things are you seeing and you know, I think it's great. I think out here it's like we compete our ass off and you know, every day you're trying to win, but I think it's always for the better of the team, so it's been super awesome. We've got a great culture and there's nowhere I'd rather be. >> What was that one-v-one like in front of the team a couple days ago with Mason when you guys went back-to-back? >> It's good. It's I love to compete, so anytime you get competitive out there, you know, for me always, you know, got to find a good I always try to go on the edge, so I got to find a good place to be, but it's good. I It makes me better and I feel like Mason's a hell of a player and he's gotten a ton better you know, from this offseason and he's been balling out, so I It's great competition and I love it. >> Riley, go back. You said this is the first time you felt Is this the first time since you were injured that you felt good like even go back to the Super Bowl like your health compared to now to then? >> Yeah, I mean the Super Bowl I had a a brace, so I was a little, you know, kind of hobbling out there, but I I feel like now I feel 100% like I feel I can bend off it and you know, I feel like the way I move and I feel, you know, honestly better than I did in college, so you know, that's that's a shout-out to the the strength staff and you know, all the guys here like Sam and you know, Andre and everybody that's kind of helped me along the way. Um, it's awesome to kind of feel like myself again and just feel like I haven't lost a step. >> The social media team had you do a little grip test a while ago. Look like you won that. One, like you joke to guys about that at all and two, does grip strength play into into your position? >> Uh, yeah. Uh, on the first part, I don't know if a lot of people brought it out, but every now and like me and Mark, uh, the strength coach, I mean he'll come out and rip like, you know, 230, so he's a beast. So, I'm just chasing him. Um, but definitely I think in the D-line room like you got to play with your hands and for me I pride myself on just having heavy hands and you know, so I I don't know, I think grip is definitely a a it's better to have it than not. >> Finish last season on the field given the injury and the long road back that it took you. How did you close out the year like you did obviously having a big moment? >> Yeah, I think that moment for me, uh, that was really everything. Like the moment I got hurt, the first thing I thought of was like, all right, like after I got the news was like I can't wait for that next snap. Um, and I know it's kind of funny I got hurt on a sack and then I was always kind of like, "Man, I'm chasing that next one." And I think that was just for me it felt like a storybook ending like I got to go out there and, you know, play in the NFL, play in the Super Bowl and get a sack. Like I have it really doesn't happen to a lot of people to get that kind of closure and feel like I just kind of put that chapter behind me and now I'm like, "All right, cool. I can put my best foot forward." >> Literally. >> Anything else, guys? >> Thanks, thanks.

title: Mike Macdonald: "That Was A Great Showing By The 12s" | Seattle Seahawks
text: Glad to see everyone. Thank you for your patience.  It's always nice, always fun to practice at Lumen Field, and, uh, we worked really hard today.  I'll tell you, it was a great, just a great show from the "12s" (fans) , considering that there was a Mariners game going on at the same time and, I think, it was the Seaforth last weekend , so, uh, we really appreciate everyone taking the time to come and showing such enthusiasm.  Really felt the love from the "12 " today, it was very nice;  and besides, I think we did a great job.  It wasn't the longest training session ever, but we did a lot of useful things, and we'll be ready for next Saturday. And, as we just talked to Adrian, for him… Yes. A year ago, he was taken off this field on a medical cart, and the fact that he made an interception today is just cool, it's nice to see that. Yes, it was incredible.  I am incredibly happy for him .  He worked extremely hard .  He has been a great teammate all this time. A year ago at this time, he was , you know, desperately fighting for his role, so he was back in the thick of things again, and, you know, he was the one completing the command circle at the end, which I thought was really cool.  But, I don't know.  It's one of those things, you know, how does a coach deal with it?  Is it worth mentioning this?  Or not?  We are thinking about him.  I don't know if Ed spoke to him this morning , but we were all thinking about him in preparation for this.  So that was really, really cool. When he stayed here for rehab, you said he tried to come to practice a few times a week to stay in shape. Yes.    Did you notice that? Yes.  Oh, yes. And what does this give, what are the advantages for the player when this happens? Well, you know, guys have the right to choose where they go to rehab, you know?  But when someone chooses us, it's very nice.  We have wonderful professionals here to help them through this process. Of course, we would like everyone to do this, and I think it reflects true team spirit.  I mean, this is a complicated situation, man.  This guy is trying to carve out a role for himself in his career, and he, um, it just shows how fragile everything is, you know. So, um, give me a minute.  I wouldn't just be incredibly happy for him. Blanco, a lot of players mentioned Montario Hardesty before today, and then he goes out and scores a couple more touchdowns.  What have you seen from him so far in camp? Uh, I see the same thing as you guys.  Uh, that's great, you know.  He's doing great. That's true.  I mean, I don't know. I mean, I have nothing to add except that he does a phenomenal job. Therefore. For a position like that, how much more important is practice than preseason play or just as important, since the number of attempts per game may be limited at such a crowded position ? Uh, I don't know, I don't know if we weigh that.  Apparently, we don't weigh it.  Simply. How do you rate this: the main part of training camp versus performing when the spotlights come on? Yeah, I think it's probably independent observations, you know, just the situation with what's going on around the player.  Where are they moving to?  Uh, you definitely don't want to devalue the work because they didn't do it right away, you know.  You know, you can't judge everything just by what happened in the last preseason game.    It's definitely not worth doing, but, um, I want people to move in the right direction , develop and so on .  I think this is also important. What is it like to conduct one-on-one exercises with everyone watching? Yes, it's just a fun period. Guys just get excited.  Told the team today that it was an exercise in remaining yourself in a different environment. So, we're trying to trust our preparation, to do what we know how to do, but now we're doing it in our stadium in front of our fans and in front of a lot of people, and, uh , so there's a lot of things to take away from that, which is pretty cool. You have training, the fan festival here, pre-season games, joint training. How are they different for you in terms of the goals you set for these different conditions? I think these are all possibilities, I think this is exactly what I was talking about.  This, this, um, these are kind of ways of overlaying how we want to build our team from the beginning, you know, from training camp ( OTAs) and as we enter the season, how we want to train our mindset and how we want to operate under different variables and different conditions.  Um, that's how I, that's how I think about it .  And hopefully we take that as, you know, I think that was a common thread in last year's experience, you know, how we wanted to deal with these situations and experiences that we did n't naturally have. What, what can you tell us about D'Wayne Eskridge?  Yes, I think we're dealing with...legs, is that pain in the upper leg?  Is this lower body pain ?  Somewhere between upper leg and lower body pain.  I don't, I don't, I don't take this lightly.  This, this, um, this is a bit of a problem right now.  This... we'll see.  This, this is a matter of a few days. So he will return. Yeah, um, he just keeps progressing every day.  I mean, I don't want to sound corny right now, but he just keeps progressing from where he started to where he is now. But he seems to be constantly making important game-changing moments, you know?  He continues to be effective, you know, in his style of play, which is He, what he brings to the game is , um, exciting. There's a physicality to his game, a weight, that, that, um, is nice to have on offense . How is John Jr. doing?  He obviously came in and played big games last year, but you guys played musical chairs with him: running back, receiver, but what have you seen in how he handles all of those roles where we need to use him in this training So, when he, when he's there, you, you, you know , you understand that he's there because he can, he can move.  And, um, he's another guy who just, working hard, you know.  I think, I think he deserves, I think Thomas Hammock deserves a huge thank you for what he does with his group and how he develops all these guys.  This is an competitive group.  Um, it seems like the guys are making big moves every day, which is really cool, and they're not satisfied with what they've achieved.  You know, they just keep working hard and keep striving for more, which, actually, I appreciate. Have you heard any comments from the rookies about how cool it was to get on the field? I didn't hear it, well, you could feel it.  I didn't hear it verbatim from them, but even guys like Dante Fowler...I went up to him afterwards and said, "Hey, man, that was pretty cool, right?" » It must be a bit strange for you, but no, he had a big smile on his face, so I know everyone shared these impressions, not just the newbies. For example, we saw this the other day in our running game.  It seems like we've been blocking the lanes well for big runs in the last few practices. What progress do you see in the running game? Um, I think our running game is on the right track, and I actually think our run defense is getting better every day.  So I think both of those things are good. Therefore.  I don't see as many explosive runs as you've seen in recent days.  That's good.  Sometimes they are stopped.  You don't want too runs.  It's not...it's not good for the cause, but I like how our offense communicates and how the offensive line picks targets, working on three levels of our offense.  Um, dealing with defensive builds and movements.  Um, I think we...I really, like I said, I think I was telling Greg the other day that I'm really happy with this.  We just working hard at it. I think you worked with Thomas Hammond before.  What do you like about him? First of all, he has the best laugh in the world.  So when he starts, you can hear him all over the office, but first of all , we were close.  He taught me a lot when we were together in Baltimore.  His first year in the league was my first year of internship.  I think he was in Wisconsin before that.  Um, he about defense, so I was always in his office and asking, " Hey, what if we do this?" "What if we do that?" " How will that affect the game?" And we somehow became friends , and he also told me to marry my wife, which was cool.  So thanks to him, I got my thoughts in order.  Um, you know, we just kept in touch since he was in Northern Illinois.  I think what he has done as a head coach is simply amazing.  So, having all these qualities— the experience of the head coach, the endurance, the expertise, the ability to find a common language, our common approach—all of this, I think, corresponds to what we are striving for.  So, he turned out to be a huge asset to us.  I am very much counting on this We saw Bud Clark continue to get game practice when he came out today.  What did you see in his game last week when he got… Yeah, go ahead. Continue.  Bud had excellent ball skills back in college. We haven't seen it yet, but it's something we want to work on with him .  I think when the game slows down a bit for him, he will be able to act ahead.  Now he thinks: "What am I doing? " "Come on, I'll do it the best I can."  He tries and learns in the process, but it takes time.  We are excited to see his progress, but now he is competing with other guys, so it is all very positive .  He has a great fighting spirit.  A very smart guy.  But ...he has a bright future.  I want, we want to get to this point , we want to move forward.  Go ahead, man. Mike, John Lynch was here tonight .  Did he offer to stretch someone's neck?  And what does his presence mean for the guys in the locker room? Yes, it was great to see "Beast Mode."  He didn't cause any surprises on the sideline , and that's a good thing. I saw him at the 50- yard line.  There were just a bunch of people with him.  I don't know if it was for "Hard Knocks," or if it was a Marshawn Lynch thing, or something for " Madden."  I forgot what we were talking about.  It just flew out of my head.    To Mike, regarding Elijah: obviously injury slowed him down last year, but tonight he made an interception over Julian. He has landed some strong shots in training recently.  What have you seen in his game now that he's back to full speed? Yes, when Elijah is on the field, he is very productive for us. And it's not his fault that he's had some minor injuries sometimes, but if he can continue this trend of sticking to the routine, working on the details , making these small gains every day, then I think he's capable of that, and he can go even further, you know?  So, the task is to continue in the same spirit, you understand?  Let 's not, let's not be complacent after 2 weeks of meetings about what your role is.  Let's, let's say , shatter all expectations of what he's capable of and go for it, you know?  So that's what we expect from him and he's doing all of that, but it's only been 2 weeks so let's keep moving forward. And speaking of not being complacent, AJ Boye remains on this team.  What have you seen him capable of despite his injury? Yes.    It's like he's taking the next step. Yes, AJ—he's talented.  I feel about AJ , you know, he's one of us, to the last one. His attitude, his physical preparation, how he approaches rehabilitation.  Um, the mentality he gives our offense is just great, you know.  And he does these things.  He was working to get back to it.  I think it's a process now.  I don't think he's where he wants to be.  But he's doing a lot of great things on the field, and I expect that to continue to grow over the next few weeks before the season starts. Are you happy with your options at fullback, or do you still need to add someone? Well, I think, I think you're going to look at what happened last year.  I think you can have an effective offense with different selection of players.  So whether Robbie is part of this equation now or later—we just have to let this process happen. But there are other ways, as Brian said, there are other ways to create additional breakthroughs, and we have guys who can do that. Anything new about Robbie?    Uh , no.  No, not yet. No questions, thank you. Thank you.  Nice to see you.

title: How the Seahawks' Offense Is Challenging the Defense in Camp
text: I was just thinking as Mike was talking and Rob was talking, part of the reason I am not so wound up about where people have Sam Darnold ranked is I'm watching him spin it day after day on the field. and this offense that theoretically should have been behind the number one ranked defense with the wonder, you know, defensive coordinator and Adam Dury and Byron Murphy who I've been glowing about and Riley Mills will talk about like all these guys. They should be maybe a little bit behind given the new offensive coordinator. It's just not the case. I sense the defense today starting to get frustrated because the offense just keeps having answers and it's a lot of it to do it's not just Sam Darnold. Sam Darnold's been playing really really well. Has not been putting the ball in harm's way. Has been mostly on time. Today was like if you've seen training camp practices before and you see a few days where one side is kind of ahead of the other, it almost always swings. Like the coaches almost want it to swing and you could feel today Mike McDonald put his finger on the blitz button a little bit like, "Okay, you've been enjoying your your time back there. No longer." And they got to the quarterbacks a few times, but not nearly as many times as I think they were hoping to. And Sam is getting rid of it quick. He's using his dump offs. Like Flurry is giving him options. And I'm kicking myself because I had a question I wanted to ask him that I forgot to ask him. But luckily I'll hopefully be able to ask him next time. But we're learning about Brian Flurry. You know, when I'm when I'm watching this and the fit with Sam Darnold so far looks like a continuation and if anything an evolution of what he did with Clint Kubak last year and Kevin Oonnell the year before that. So people can have him at 14, they can have him at three, they can have him at 29. When he gets out in the field, the Seahawks are going to win a lot of games. And I think that's ultimately all that really matters. >> It's really cool, too, Brian, not just to hear your perspective on Sam Darnold and what you've seen, but also just like the push and pull of like the energy tensions of between offense and defense, especially in this time of their season, because it can be that way. and and even in in past years, you'd think, like you said, it would be more the defense that is leading the way, especially when you have a new offensive coordinator, but I think it was Gray Zable who commented on Brian Flurry and said he he's a guy who sees football differently than 99.9% of human beings. title: Why the Dallas Cowboys can be 'a force' in 2026 NFL season | Dan Patrick Show | NFL on NBC
text: Cowboys locked up Quinnen Williams yesterday. And that's a great move because I think he's a really good player. What does that give you? That gives you an average season. The Cowboys with the offense and an average defense, they will be in the playoffs, and they will be a force. So that's that's our preliminary plan. >> Mike, what do you look for in that preseason game number one? Is just getting in and out of the huddle and stuff like that? Well, operation. Yeah. Yes. Clearly, most important thing for me is play style. You have to get your play style established. You know, you practice in a structured um environment, you know, starting with the um you know, the ramp ups. Um you know, just, you know, a little safer approach. So, now it's time to cut it loose. So, uh starts up front. So, number one, the number one objective for me is establishing your play style. Mike, how do you value the the opportunity for starters in preseason games? >> How do I value >> Yeah. Do you I mean, do you value >> I think there's a number of variables that go into it. I think it's it's a where you are as a program. This is obviously our first year together. Um this is a veteran football team. This is the you know the most experienced team I've coached in my in my tenure as a head coach. Um who's playing with who, you know, the combinations of how they're going to play together. So I I look at all those things that that's why frankly uh this is a padded practice. You know we have a full slate you know uh we wanted to have a competitive two drills today and two minutes. So we you know I definitely want to evaluate this today and and make some decisions you know from that. So um I mean I'd love to be here and give you all the answers to the quiz your questions but it's you know this is this practice is important and frankly you usually don't have that big of a practice this close to the game. I get it. Uh but it is preseason so uh we'll see how we come out of today. >> Mike, you touched on it a little bit there, but do you approach this preseason a little bit differently being the first year head coach here implementing a brand new offense as you differently I guess as you would maybe a few years in? >> Definitely. I mean, there's times in the preseason that you may have a new system on defense, you may have a new system on offense. So you may play your starters, you know, two series or you may have a a play total that you want want to hit with with players, but really frankly the most important part is the health of the team. That's that that drives these decisions. That that's where um it tends you you tend to maybe pull back and and uh you know, not maybe not play the the veteran, the older guys in those situations. You know, you just lean on their experience. um the quality of practice. I mean, everything that we've done out on the field in pads, um it's it's detailed. I have comparables, you know, I have things that have gone back to the early years. Frankly, I've just paid attention really to the to the last four or five years of how we trained in this this schedule that we're on. It's very similar to the the schedule that I was on 21 through 25. So, um I look at all those things. I I it gives me a an idea of where we are as a team, you know, mentally. Um, you know, volumewise, you know, because both the offense and defense are new. Um, I don't like where we are as far as, um, the number of missed assignments we've had, they're higher than a little higher than normal. You know, they're not totally out of bounds. So, you look at all those things and then at the end of the day, you you just set a plan and go with it. >> As far as Aaron's potential play, whose decision is that going to be? Is that a joint decision between you and him or just yours? I mean, I mean, definitely it comes it comes down to to my decision, but we've we've been talking about playing or not playing since he signed. I mean, he he prefers to play. I I you know, Brett Favre wanted to play. I I don't I've never had a quarterback that did not want to play, you know. Um so, yes, but it's it's really what how it all fits together. >> When it comes to the rest of the quarterbacks on your depth chart, you know, what things [snorts] are going to have your attention? What will we be looking for from those guys, especially the young ones who have yet to appear in >> Well, I just want to see these young guys play. I want to see how they play, you know, you know, connected to each other. Um, you know, it's, uh, you know, the pre- snap of the operation, have, you know, understanding what's in front of them, but, uh, the finish, you know, this is, this is what these games are for. You know, it's how these guys are finishing plays, what goes on at the end of the play, and that leads to production. So, play play style and production are are the two blinking lights that that I I put the most emphasis on. >> Will be the second guy, right? >> Excuse me. Will will be the >> we'll make those decisions tonight. >> Mike, yesterday I believe the plan was that you told us was that Maxi Hanachur would not practice, but he was out there suited up going through individual drills. Where is he in terms of recovery and do you anticipate him playing in the preseason? >> Yeah, I think it's I think what he accomplished yesterday kind of tells you where he is. You know, we used the individual drills to to see what he can do, you know. So, um he's just working his way back. You know, I think when you, you know, it's just like any, you know, um, return from injury. You know, there's a strength component that we're trying to get over and there's some things we wanted to see him do, you know, in his pads and a helmet on. And, uh, he's making he's he's he's he's making he's making progress. Uh, I I do not see him playing, you know, Thursday night, but he's he's getting close. I know that it's just the preseason, but is there something special for you to play against Green Bay with Aaron whether he starts or not or whatever the plan is, but is that kind of a a full circle moment at all for you? >> Uh, definitely. I mean, it's there's no, you know, there's no doubt about it. I mean, our history there is obviously long and and and you know, the success we had there and um so, you know, it's it you get to spots like this, you know, the personal relationships are, you know, the that it's the people you think about um you know, obviously having personal and you know, a professional connection to Green Bay is, you know, that's part of my life, but I'm I'm more worried about my our pre-nap penalties right now to be honest with you. So, uh, that that'll be my focus of of, you know, playing playing good football, you know, doing a good job for the players. You know, I have a job to do, too. So, uh, it's getting them prepared to play in the preseason game. I'm excited to see our our young guys. I'm excited to go out there for the first time. You know, I'm excited to walk out on the stadium. So, I mean, that's definitely real. U, but I'm I'm really just trying to focus on keep moving the needle through training camp. And you you frankly, you kind of always feel this way going into the first preseason game. Mike, I know um it's your first game now preseason game or not, but it's your first game here in Pittsburgh. Does that uh are you as excited as Will? How is excited? >> Yeah. Um yes, definitely. Uh it'll definitely mean a lot more Thursday, like I said, when I'm driving into the stadium. So, just got a lot of work to do. >> Mike, when you say establishing play style, what's the criteria you use to to evaluate that? >> Well, I mean, I think the the common the common emphasis is how you play the game. you know, it's uh you know, it's the physicality and the finish. Um, you know, the that's those are the two things you don't really totally get to do in in this practice environment. So, uh, that's what I'll be looking that that's what I'll put the most emphasis on. >> Like, you said you got some bad news about the weather. Do you guys anticipate being out on the field today as long as [clears throat] you can, getting work in, and potentially having things be fluid like yesterday? >> I'm going try to make a decision by frankly, when I walked in here yesterday, they told me that lightning was going to hit at 2:00 and then when I got done, they said the lightning was going to hit at noon. So, uh, hopefully, you know, hopefully get some more information here. >> Mike, what do you attribute the missed assignments mostly to? Is that are those mental errors? When what are you looking at to correct there? >> Well, um, that that's frankly, it's installation football. It's it's normal. I've charted this my whole coaching career. I have I have um you know things that date back to n you know to in the early early days but the ones I pay attention to more is you know since the last CBA because you know it's it's a schedule of of how you put it in you know you used to be able to put your offense in in in 15 installations because you had the time you know you were we used to go to River Falls for five weeks when I was in Kansas City so now you have to get everything done in in eight installations. Frankly, I'm already thinking about going to seven installations next year just because I think it's a it's uh it's it's difficult when you don't have everything in before the first game. So, um so that I attribute mainly to the high volume of of what we're asking these guys to do, which is is is a a challenge which they need to go through. Um so that that's that's part of it. we concept teach in the spring to make sure they have a strong foundation, but to get everything in seven, the volume of of scheme that they've absorbed in seven installations is impressive. So, um, and that's that's just the facts of, you know, the training, but you you have to you have to, you know, you have to get your playbooks in, you know, so I I attribute more to that than anything. >> You've seen guys take practices off, but not Aaron. Is that reflection of his quarterback's performance? Is that, you know, person by person? Is that their choice to or how's that? >> Well, a combination of all that. I mean, it's it's definitely, you know, um the position they play, you know, I've been super blessed as a head coach to have quarterbacks that practice every single day. Uh not only is it good for them, it's it's good for the offense, but it's outstanding for the football team because it because it's a there's there's a level of competitiveness um that goes with having veteran quarterbacks that go every single day. and um and and I've had that through my whole co head coaching career and it's and it's something that I appreciate and and emphasize to the younger guys because it's it's important for that quarterback to be out there every day because it's because that he he sets he sets a standard for the for that practice. That two-minute drill is different when he's in there. So all those things, you know, that the cadence, the challenge at the line of scrimmage, you know, all those factors come into play. So, um, but yeah, I mean, Cam plays down in the trenches, you know, you know, TJ's a So, you look at all those things, too. You look at, you know, where they are in their training and, you know, you're really trying to get these guys to a point that they're ready to play, uh, you know, for the season. Um, it's very difficult to have a challenging training camp and not to leave anything in the trobe, you know. So, I do the best I can to make sure we're training appropriately, um, pushing the envelope and the mental toughness and and things that the team needs, but um, just trying to make sure hopefully we don't leave anything here in Latro. >> Mike, with the with the Franco moments, they're obviously a surprise to the players. They don't know when they're going to happen. >> You, I assume, know at one point in practice they're the the sound's going to go on. >> That's Pat go today. So, there you go. There's scoop. Have you ever considered not being in charge of that and you also being surprised by a Franco moment to control kind of the >> that I I would enjoy that. There's a lot of things I wish I was in charge of and that's not that's definitely not at the top of the list, but uh um yeah, that's that's a good that's a good thing. I mean what once again we're we're in install install mode. I think the Franco moments will be better once we get out of this mode, you know, moving forward where it's just, you know, what do we need? Um, you know, but frankly the decision on what we do uh in the Franco moment matches the install. Um, and then really it's what the defense needs too. Like, hey Patrick, do you think you need, you know, four minute backed up or you want to do another two-minute drill? You want to, you know, we have them done get back on track. So, we just, you know, we just look at all of our situations. We have a menu and we just try to make sure we're, you know, giving the guys what they need. >> All right. Thanks, Bill. >> Thank you.

title: Steelers Training Camp 2026 All-Access (Ep. 2) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: [music] >> Welcome to Steelers Training Camp all access sponsored by FedEx. >> It's become a right of Steelers Training Camp. It's the night [music] practice at Latrobe Memorial Stadium normally on a Friday. This time it's on a Saturday. They were lining up. A lot of fans are here and so are we. Good evening everyone and welcome to Steelers Training Camp all access. Bob Pompeani along with Charlie Batch. What a backdrop this is. Charlie, this must take you back. You spent a lot of time on this field. >> Absolutely. This is one of the biggest practices of training camp because you know there's going to be over 10,000 people here and this may be the only opportunity they get a chance to actually watch you. So you want to put on your best performance here today at practice. >> A lot of people are here and that may be an understatement. We started shooting video tape well after a lot of people were here and I'm talking about hours. Look at how many people are here. 27 different states accounted for. Multiple countries. They come from all over and they started very early this morning. >> We got here at 8:00 a.m. Biggest reason is this is the most high energy plays. Being here, we're lifetime fans. We've got over 30 autographs so far. The whole thing, the fans, the fun, the little games they set up. Just I know I don't have all of them with me. We got a whole crew of kids, grandkids, brought the whole family. >> Um just to see the team and see what what what we have in store for the season. Just excited. >> And we've been doing this since my boys were probably third and fourth grade. We come every year. >> Just a tradition, the you know, hanging out with the meeting fans and I actually met somebody that I kind of knew from social media and we actually met in person today. So it's just nice to connect with the fans. Everybody, you know, just Steeler Nation I guess. >> Well Charlie, these people here going to see a great practice. High intensity. The one thing they will not see, however, is tackling. Mike McCarthy doesn't believe in it. It's become a trend in the NFL, but that doesn't mean it can't be physical. >> Yeah, I mean, it's I mean, it's fall camp, you know. Uh We're getting into the dog days of camp. People are tired. People are sore. Um we're just competing. We love each other. Brothers fight all the time, so um you know, someone messes up, we get into it a little bit, then you know, we'll be in here eating lunch in 30 minutes together. >> Charlie, this is a deviation from what we've seen from Mike Tomlin before him, Chuck Noll. No tackling. Does it make a difference to you? >> It doesn't necessarily make a difference because this is where you're seeing a trend of NFL teams. They don't want to tackle all the way to the ground, but you better believe things are going to start to get chippy. As you saw this week during camp, DeShawn Elliott, he gave the DK Metcalf nice little thud, and everybody woke up. And even Aaron Rodgers noticed, "Oh, this is what we're doing." So, this is a time of camp you're ready to start hitting somebody else, even if it's just thudding at this particular point. So, I don't look at it as a big deal. >> And it's good to have a preseason game coming up because now they can take out their their anger on the other team, if they have that. Meantime, let's talk about the tempo of this camp. Again, very crisp. Uh that's one thing if you come up here to Saint Vincent College, you'll see that, Charlie, that they they run a lot of drills. They're very, very good about moving guys around. Nobody's ever standing around. There are no seats. You got to just be engaged all the time. >> And that is a big part of Mike McCarthy's uh camp theme this year. He wants to be fast. He wants to play with tempo [music] in anticipation of what they're looking to do in between the lines. So, this is probably the fastest practice that you have seen in many years only because of the style that Mike McCarthy plays with. >> That means a lot of pressure on the quarterbacks. They got to get all the passes off quickly. You know, we've been following quarterbacks for quite some time. Aaron Rodgers is the man. He's going to be the starter, but after that, there's a pretty good battle going on. One of them vying for that job is Ohio State's Will Howard. Rich Walsh had a chance to catch up with him earlier this week. >> Thanks a lot, guys. I'm with Will Howard. Will, how's training camp going so far? You missed some of it last year, so, you know, and you got a the coaching staff, too. >> Yeah, no, it's been it's been great just to get back out on the field and and get some live reps. Um you know, I still haven't I haven't played a in a football game since college. And I feel like I came back in in great shape and and feel really good going into this year. >> Taking nothing away from last year, but it has to be a good thing for a quarterback and maybe all the offensive players to have an offensive-minded head coach, right? >> Oh, absolutely. I mean, you know, it it feel like, you know, during the 2-minute drills, you get a couple extra calls go your way. Um when it was the other way last year. Um you know, which is always good, but no, I at the end of the day, I think, you know, just having an offensive-minded coach like coach McCarthy who's so detailed and and uh you know, so um just just in into everything, you know, he's he's the play-caller, you know, and I think everything we have is uh you know, catered to the quarterback. >> What's this last year and a half been like for you? You've become like a fan favorite. People are chanting your name out there. Will Howard is a is a big name around here now. What's that like for you? >> No, it's it's exciting, man, but you know, it it motivates me cuz I it makes me want to give them something to cheer about cuz you know, I I feel like all the all the excitement right now is just kind of anticipation and and seeing what I can do. Um but I know what I can do and I and I know that I'm ready to go show that on the field. Um and I just want to want to show these guys, you know, that I don't just do it out here on the practice fields, I can do it in the game, too. >> You'll have a chance to do that August 13th, and I imagine that's what you're really looking forward to right now. >> No, I I can't wait, man. I I got the Packers, you know, that that one's circled on the schedule cuz that's the first one and uh no, I I can't wait, man. I'm chomping at the bit. >> All right, Charlie, from a quarterback's point of view, you've seen all these guys. Will Howard out of Ohio State achieve the ultimate goal, he won a national championship. This is different territory for him. He didn't get a chance last year. What have you seen so far from him? >> Yeah, I've been impressed with Will Howard. This is the guy who's pushing the ball down the field. It seemed like this offense is starting to slow down, and he's able to get in and out of the huddle with the verbage. That's something [music] that Mike McCarthy is getting excited about. The downside of it is we have not seen him in preseason games, so I expect to see him a lot throughout the preseason. >> And Charlie, that preseason means it continues at the Saint Vincent College fields because there won't be a practice on Sunday, so mark that down. No practice, they'll be back to work on Monday 11:00 a.m., Tuesday 11:00 a.m., then off Wednesday before [music] the first preseason game on Thursday here on KDKA with Green Bay, then back after an off day Friday, Saturday 10:15, Sunday at 11:00 a.m. Coming up, we're going to speak with a man who has a name you all recognize, Rooney. This will be Dan Rooney. >> Welcome back to Steelers Training Camp All Access, sponsored by FedEx. All Access, joined by our special guest, Mr. Dan Rooney, Vice President of Strategy. Dan, this tradition's gone on. Now, it's always been on a Friday, but today it's on a Saturday. But nonetheless, the response has been terrific, hasn't it? >> Great to be here, Bob. Beautiful night here in Latrobe, and nothing better than this. It's truly football season once this kicks off, and we couldn't be more excited to be out here in front of a packed house. >> And it is a packed house. We saw people as far away as Alaska, 27 different states, countries. They all make this trek to come here. Great thing about this is always a lot of people, but there's always been a lot of people to a training camp. Even though the change in schedule with Mike McCarthy, how's that been for you? >> Yeah, attendance has been up this year. So, we're we're seeing the black and gold out in full force like we always do, and practice has been exciting, and and the fans are into it. There's just so much to do when you when you come out to Saint [music] Vincent's for for kids on up. You know, we we have our our football fan zone, and the food and drink is fantastic, and the weather's been very good so far as well. So, it's just fun to get the fans around our players like this this time of year. >> And international games, they are big throughout the NFL, along with the Steelers here. Big game last year in Ireland, and then another game this year in Paris. And the had the experience in Dublin. How are you going to take that? Are there anything that you can use now with this Paris trip against the Saints? >> Yeah, the the Dublin game was incredible. Just you ask the players, the coaches that were there, that the fans. You know, that one was special, and and we're expecting [music] big things from Paris as well. Back-to-back seasons we've had a first and a first regular season game in Dublin, first regular season game in Paris. We're we're honored to be a part of it. >> And Dan, we're seeing more and more of these games. Like for example, the 49ers are playing San Francisco in the first game in Australia. What is the league's goal when it comes to international play? >> Yeah, you know, it's grown the game of American football, delivering our game to fans internationally. And and what better way to do that than to have games in in these stadiums they have overseas. So, Paris is an incredible market. We were able to do a visit a few months ago and you know, rich culture, [music] rich history, and our fans are going to love it. We're we're pumped up. >> And I know it's been a busy offseason for the Steelers front office, starting with the new head coach Mike McCarthy, but also the draft that came here in Pittsburgh and the success of that draft. Can you envision, because the fans want to know, can you envision the draft coming back to Pittsburgh anytime soon? >> Still still glowing over the draft. That experience was was truly incredible. You know, the the fans had a fantastic time. The imagery of our city that that was able to show off to the world. So, I know the NFL thought Pittsburgh handled it, you know, just as good as any city that's done it. So, I believe they would bring it back, absolutely. >> And the weather was great, too. You I mean, you carved out a couple of days which fit. >> We did. >> Let's talk about Mike McCarthy. Last question for you. It's a whole new era here. New coaches, a lot of new players. What's your experience been like with Coach McCarthy? >> Coach Coach McCarthy's been fantastic. You know, detailed guy, super organized throughout practice. His staff has been been fantastic as well. So, we're pumped up for the season, you know, kicking off on on Thursday here coming up and you know, we we got the right man at the helm, absolutely. >> Dan, really appreciate the time. All the best in 2026. >> Thank you. >> There's a lot more yet to come, including Mike McCarthy's coaching staff. You may not know who they are, you're going to find out because Jerry Dulac, our Steelers insider from the Post-Gazette, will join this show next. Stick around. >> Welcome back [music] to Steelers Training Camp All Access, sponsored by FedEx. All access. As you can hear Renegade is going. People are getting excited to see their team on the field. They're going to see a lot of familiar faces there, but they're going to see a totally different coaching staff led by Mike McCarthy. You may know a lot about him, but what about some of the assistant coaches? Rich Walsh is joined by our Steelers insider Jerry Dulac of the Post-Gazette. >> All right, thanks a lot, guys. I'm with our Steelers insider Jerry Dulac. And Jerry, you know, there's been a lot of training camps for you and I, but it's the first training camp for Mike McCarthy and his entire coaching staff. You know, how have the players adapted to those guys right now? >> You know, Rich, the one thing I liked what Mike McCarthy did with his staff, it's a nice mix. You know, he brought in some veteran guys who have been with him for years like James Campen, the offensive line coach, been around 20-some years. And then he hired a couple guys from college to come in as well. And he hired a chief of staff that you don't see in the NFL very much, but he does it to organize his practices and everything else. Mike McCarthy is as detailed a a coach that I've ever been around. >> Well, there's a couple position battles this year. One of them is that third wide receiver, the slot wide receiver. You would think Roman Wilson would have a leg up. Does he? >> I would say that, Rich. I think eventually that might be Jeremy Chinnard, but we'll see how it plays out.
