Either way, you're looking at four guys. Uh Roman Wilson has been kind of inconsistent at camp. We've seen some flashes as we've seen in games. And then we see other times he runs the wrong route. Maybe he loses spatially where he is like on the end zone or the sideline. But I will tell you he had his best day of practice on Thursday. And he seems to get better every day. >> Now switching to the defensive side of the ball, no Jalen Ramsey out here, no Joey Porter. Has that affected the defensive backfield at all? >> Rich, I have to go back a long way to find a time when they've had a second a cornerback group that's as deep and as talented as this one. And we haven't even seen Joey Porter, of course, on the field and Jalen Ramsey. But you know, they went out and got Jamel Dean. They gave him a big contract. They re-signed Asante Samuel who they believe is the MVP of training camp so far, but that cornerback group on paper is as good as they've had in a long time. >> All right, thanks a lot, Jerry. As always, great stuff. Back to you guys. >> All right, gentlemen, thank you very much. One guy mentioned in that piece is a guy we've been watching a lot. We didn't see him at all last year, Roman Wilson, but he's made a pretty good statement in this camp. How do you explain the fact that he's become the most targeted guy not named DK Metcalf? >> Yeah, sometimes a change of scenery always work better, but sometimes [music] a change happen within the organization works well with players. A Roman Wilson is a prime example of that because now using his skill set in a past West [music] Coast system, this is setting his skill set exactly where he was hoping it's going to be. He had the second most target thus far in training camp, and right now, let's see if that carries over because the coaching staff loves what they're seeing from Roman Wilson. >> Another guy that we're talking about, too, is a guy they drafted, Riley Nowakowski. Charlie, they moved on from Connor Heyward. This guy has the tools to become that guy, an H-back. He could do a lot of different things. What have you seen from him so far that makes you think he's going to make this roster? >> Yeah, when you look at where his physical stature is, he's that combination of tight end fullback and that hybrid type that you need at that position. He has done a great job understanding the offense, knowing where to line up, and the coaching staff is trusting what he's doing out there at this particular point because he's getting more and more reps. So, as we get ready for the first preseason game, I expect him to be a part of the game plan. >> Yes, and we have an opportunity to talk to him. Mike Persuta, steelers.com, spent some time with Riley Nowakowski. >> Riley, uh I'm not sure how familiar you were with Pittsburgh before the Steelers drafted you, but I got to tell you, Nowakowski is a Pittsburgh name. Are you Are you fitting right in accordingly? >> Yeah, yeah, the fans been awesome, you know. I I think they like, you know, a little bit of Polish, you know. I I I don't think they mind that, so I've been fitting in well, and things been super welcoming, so I've been enjoying it. >> I talked to you during OTAs and asked you what kind of role is the fullback going to have in the offense, and you said, "No pads, I don't know. We'll find out then." Pads have been on 3 days now. What are you learning? >> Uh you know, it's a lot of hitting, you know what I mean? We want to be a downhill offense, you know, and that that all kind of starts with with me and and bring the physicality. So, every day I just try to show up and and you know, bring the juice. >> You're playing fullback and tight end. Is it 50/50 or a little more of one than the other? >> Uh a little bit more uh fullback just cuz, you know, I'm kind of the the main guy right now, but you know, I get a little bit of tight end work here here and there, too. >> Pre-draft uh reports on you said that uh you were probably a better receiver than people thought or maybe your your contributions in the passing game are underrated. You feel that way and you feel like you're holding up that end out here? >> Yeah, I'd like to think so, you know what I mean? Obviously, everybody can judge for themselves, but you know, I think I've been doing a pretty good job in the pass game. >> And last thing for you, Riley. Uh 3 days in pads, have you gotten somebody where you thought, "Yeah, that's what I do." and has anybody gotten you and made you think, "Ah, that's what it's like in the NFL." >> Yeah, for sure, you know, I I got a few, you know, myself and today uh Payton Wilson swam me, you know, so yeah, I was playing first in the ground, so you know, definitely got He got me a little bit there, but you know, that's what it's all about is just, you know, trying to sharpen sharpen the sword every day. >> All right, Charlie, we've been talking about quarterbacks. You heard from Will Howard earlier. Coming up next, Drew Allar, the rookie out of Penn State. You're going to hear from him when Steelers training camp all access continues. training camp all access, sponsored by >> Welcome back to Steelers training camp all access here at Latrobe Memorial Stadium. Always talking about quarterbacks, it seems that's what most of these people have questions about. You know Aaron Rodgers is the starter this year. What about next year? They're going to get an indication of what they have on this roster. You heard from Will Howard. Right now, Rich Walsh had a chance to speak with the other guy who's battling him. That would be third-round pick Drew Allar. Drew Allar and Drew, how's camp going so far? >> It's been good. It's been a really fun week and a half here so far. The guys the vets have been great to us. Um it's a lot of fun just being out and playing football again. >> This seems like a really good situation for you. I mean, you had a chance to work with Mike McCarthy, a QB guru, and now Aaron Rodgers. How much has that helped during the the spring to get that one-on-one time with a guy like Mike? >> Uh, it's been huge. Um, they did they did a great job of being very specific and detailed with me. And then, you know, after OTAs and mini camp ended, they gave me a, you know, things they wanted me to work on uh, throughout the summer. And feel like I've done a good job of that. And now it's just about stacking stacking good clean days. And uh, you know, if I have any mistakes, learning from those and not repeating those mistakes. >> And now you're in a QB room with one of the greatest quarterbacks that ever played this game. How much has he helped you? How much are you learning from him? >> Yeah, I mean, Aaron's been nothing short of amazing with me. And really the whole quarterback room. Uh, he goes out of his way to, you know, take us aside and give us tips and and pointers, whether it's on footwork, mechanics, or just progressions in general. Like, I can I cannot be more grateful for to have a guy like that in our room. Um, and really same with Mason and Will. They they all three of the guys have done a great job of, you know, helping me and answering any questions that I have. >> I mean, it's a competition, but it seems like it's a friendly competition. All you guys get along. That's a good thing, I would imagine. >> Yeah, for sure. I mean, we all want the best for each other. Um, and, you know, our job is going to be supporting Aaron when he's out there. And, you know, with this preseason uh, is opportunity for, you know, all of us to, you know, go out there and play real games against another another opponent. So, that that will be a really good switch up for, you know, I know for me personally. So, I'm really looking forward to that. >> Charlie, there are a lot of guys on this roster who just want to stay here when it counts. One of them is another kid who we've been following pretty closely out of Mount Lebanon by way of the Naval Academy, Eli Heidenreich. He's put up big numbers down there at Navy, and he was the darling of the draft. Uh, what an amazing night it was for him. He would like to continue that as a member of this roster. You might find this also interesting, despite being from Pittsburgh and being a Steeler fan, he never made it out here to the Trough. >> I've I never had the chance to come out here in all my years living in Pittsburgh. I you know football is always starting up and never had the chance but you know you see pictures and videos of it so to be out here um you know it it really is an honor to you know share this field with so many Pittsburgh legends that have come here before me. I I have some some pretty cool jerseys back home that I I was looking through the other day as I I was leaving packing up for camp. I have my Troy Polamalu jersey and I have a Rod Woodson jersey too. So just looking at those and thinking you know out there there's there's kids that you know might have my jersey. It's pretty special to think about. >> Eli Harold has put up quite a record at Naval Academy. You can call him the Swiss Army knife cuz he does everything. He catches, he runs, special teams, you name it he does it. You see these numbers and remember he did not play as a freshman. Pretty impressive stuff. Charlie very interesting story here and everyone locally would like to see him make this team. The one thing he does do is offer versatility. He can do it every way you want including special teams and when I talked to him earlier he was down on special teams. He wanted to do it. >> And that's how you make the roster especially as a late round draft pick. But also what are the other intangibles, right? When you talk about running back, receiver, this is a guy who could be a match up nightmare and this is [music] what gets this coaching staff excited because of the quickness and the route running ability of what he brings to this offense. [music] So look for him to be a big part of it. >> We'll look for him on Thursday night first preseason game. I'm sure he's going to get plenty of action. When we come back here at Latrobe Memorial Stadium we're going to talk about what lies ahead here and some training camp notes. All next on KDKA. Training Camp All Access sponsored by >> Welcome back to our special here from Latrobe Memorial Stadium. You know training camp is always a [music] great time for fans to meet players but it was especially important for Lucas Golar who is awaiting a liver transplant. He received a surprise visit [music] this week from Alex Highsmith, Zach Frazier and Mason McCormick after a practice [music] this week and it left him smiling ear to ear. >> It was fun. It was exciting It was very exciting. I was a little bit nervous at first. >> This is a great opportunity for an improvement of mental health, encouragement as he waits for a liver transplant. This would be his second liver transplant. So, his suffering and in his 13 years has been immense with a tremendous amount of suffering. So, something like this just really brightens his day. >> What a special moment there for that young man who never forget it. One thing we will never forget is being in a light box. For those of you who never done it, Charlie, this is 2 years in a row now. What is a light box? We'll take a look. You can see for yourself. This is all in advance of the preseason games we're going to be televising. It is done by Steelers media and it puts us in a different light. >> It really does and anytime you start getting into the light box, that lets you know preseason football is here. Obviously, it's it's exciting time to be a part [music] of it and doing everything behind the scenes and I'm just glad to be a part of it with you, Bob. >> Me too. It's been how many years now? We're at 12 or 13 doing this together. Missy Matthews as well. And you can see some of that coming up on our preseason coverage. Speaking of that, let's get right into it. Starting with this Thursday. It is the first preseason game. Green Bay, of all teams. Mike McCarthy, one of his older teams this year. August 13th, we'll kick it off at 7:00 p.m. Pregame before that. And then 8 days later on the 21st, the New York Jets also at Acrisure Stadium. We'll wrap [music] it up with a trip to the new Highmark Stadium in Buffalo, New York on August 27th. Steelers-Bills at 7:00 p.m. All right, Charlie, it brings us to the end of the program here and I know you're excited about the first game, but overall, your feeling about this Mike McCarthy led team so far. >> Yeah, I thought it's been a phenomenal camp. Mike McCarthy decided, especially changing culture, understanding change of times and understanding his principles with this camp. I'm excited about what's going to happen here and as we all are, we're going to learn a lot about this team throughout the preseason. For the players, there's not many more opportunities as we approach the game. You are now approached three games to hopefully make this roster, make the most of your opportunities here. >> And it all starts game-wise on Thursday night, once again, 7:00 p.m. right here on KDKA. Charlie, it was a pleasure. Look forward to the games coming up, and thank you for joining us. That's going to wrap it up, our third and final Steelers training camp all access. Thank [music] you for joining us here on KDKA-TV.

title: Samuel Jr., Howard, Rudolph & Harmon Press Conference (August 10) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Sante, you've been pairing basically with everybody, every receiver they have out there. How have you felt about how you've competed and the back and forth you've had with these receivers? >> I feel like uh we've competed well. You know, it's uh it's good good on good and um we have great receivers and we have great uh defensive backs. So, I feel like it's been great competition so far. >> Sante, I'm sorry. The coaches have been very auditory the way you've performed here. You feel you're back to the level where you were prior to your injury or even or even better? >> Oh, yeah, for sure. For sure. I feel like um kind of even better, you know, just trying to um build off what I did last season, you know, coming off the surgery and um just now I feel like I had a full off seasonason like I said before and um you know, just feel good um feel confident and um and I'm confident in the the scheme and my teammates around me. So, just lets me play a little bit faster. >> What have you shown them that's had them be so complimentary and uh auditory of what you've done? I feel like uh just consistency like day in and day out of my work work ethic and um just coming in here grinding um keeping my head down and just doing what they asked. >> Asante uh last Friday after a goal line drill there were like eight DBs around Aaron Rogers and he was giving him sound looked like tips. Were you in that group and what was he saying? >> Oh yeah, for sure. you know, uh, A-Rod, every time he sees anything good or bad, he's going to say something, you know, so he was just compliment on DBs on how how we've been doing and, uh, he gave us some tips as well. You know, what he sees as a quarterback, being a Hall of Famer, he is. And, um, you know, every tip from Aaron Rogers is a great tip. So, you know, >> how rare is that for a quarterback to bring the DBs around and and talk with you guys like that? >> Uh, well, I haven't been around. I haven't been around a Hall of Fame quarterback like that, so you know, I can't really tell. But, you know, I'm I'm always open to anybody that has anything to say. You know, I'm all ears to anybody that wants to give their two cents about any situation. >> How much does it help you guys as a defense and as a secondary to be going against Rogers every day, especially with the wrinkles he throws in with the hand signals and things like that? >> Oh, it's it's it's it's an amazing opportunity to go against a quarterback in that caliber. you know, he's a great guy, you know, and uh he always he's a competitor and he wants to be perfect on the offensive end. So, and we want to be perfect on the defensive end, so that breeds competition. >> Building off of that, Patrick Graham talked about how um with you guys work to disguise what you're doing in the secondary and in the defense a lot. It helps going against Rogers, but also Mike McCarthy's offense to test things out and learn, you know, what does and what doesn't work. What are what are things you've learned as far as you know trying to sell one look versus transitioning to another to another look against this offense? >> Yeah. Um just trying to like you said just disguising that's that's a big key in u today's game in general. So you know the more you can disguise and more you can uh uh show different things post snap and pre- snap that will make the quarterback's job a little bit harder. So that's what we trying to do as a defense and um I feel like that's been working for us and um he's going to give us our best shot. So, you know, we just trying to just compete up there. >> What habits are you trying to build as far as communication goes in the secondary? Cuz I know there's a point of emphasis where you want to get better from last year was the communication aspect, even though you guys have had some injuries so far in the secondary. How's that going? >> Uh it's been it's been good. You know, uh it's a long season, so you know, it's a lot of things that happened during the season, so you don't know who you're going to be out there with. And uh you just you have to be able to communicate effectively with anybody out there. So, you know, just uh it comes with trust. You know, you got to trust your brother out there and um I feel like that we do that. We trust each other. >> Asante Mike McCarthy said last week that you had position flex kind of implying you could maybe play inside if you wanted to. You haven't done that, I believe, since you know you were at Florida State or at least very early in your NFL career. How comfortable are if you had to move inside the sub packages right now? >> Whatever the team needs me to do to win the games, that's what I'm all for. you know, um, the headman said it, that's what that that's what goes. >> As much as I'm sure you've enjoyed going against Rogers and the receivers in this room, how much are you looking forward to facing another team and actually having that true game competition come Thursday? >> Uh, you know, it's nothing like going against a different uh opponent, you know, going against uh the the your guys that's on your team is you're going to get some good competition, but it's you still trying to take care of each other. Still trying to, you know what I'm saying? like uh not not hurt each other and not you know what I'm saying? But we we I can't wait. >> You mentioned that you feel as though you you're better now than before. Um why do you say that? What makes you better? Why why do you feel that way? Uh mentally uh I was away from the game uh for a long time. So mentally I feel like I'm more prepared, more mentally stronger. And um uh I just see the game a little bit slower as as the years go on, you know. Uh that's that's what typically happens when you get older as an older player. You have to use your your your your um yeah, you got to use your mind a little bit more. >> You've had a lot of playing with a number of different guys next to you because of some of the injuries. What's it been like having those young guys kind of be coming to you looking for for advice and and what have you told them and how have they taken to it? >> Uh if they have a question for me and you know I'm always open to uh answer the question. Um they they've been doing a great job so far all the rookies from the from the top to the bottom. So I'm just glad that they I'm to be able to source of information for them and um they're doing great so far. >> You you've had a lot of good battles against DK Metaf. There aren't many receivers in this league with that combination of size, speed, and strength. What are you getting out of those matchups here in practice? >> Uh DK has been a a great uh great receiver in this league for a long time. You know, every time we go against each other, you know, we we talking before and after the play like what he's seen, what I seen, and uh we just it's it's it's a great competition and I feel like iron sharpers iron. Like what they said, steel, sharper steel. So, you know, we just trying to get better each and every day. >> What do you see on that low on Saturday night? uh it seemed pretty perfect coverage. You reach around, you had the one-handed grab there. What do you see on that play and what do you learn from that? >> Uh uh like I said, it's a Hall of Fame quarterback with a top top tier receiver. You know, uh it's going to be some plays in the game that uh you going against top tier quarterbacks and top tier receivers. You just got to get back in the huddle and um play the next play. You know, it's it's football is always a up and down game. You just got to stay levelheaded. Listen, uh Tom Art said that this is the best he's ever seen you play. Now, I know it was a year in 23 and got the team in the playoffs, but um >> do you feel that way about yourself? And if so, how much is that credited to a lot of the fundamental work that that QB school that Mike employs puts you through? >> Yeah, I mean, um I think uh I think just another year older, uh another year worth of lessons learned last year, uh good and bad. and then, you know, a year with a year with Aaron and being able to really uh pick up a lot. Um he's so open and so [clears throat] easy to talk to, easy to ask questions. So, that's been a valuable resource. And then uh absolutely uh you know, Coach McCarthy's uh just his detail and the footwork. I mean, even down to like the the PDFs that we get the installations and how many how many little notes there are for the receivers and break points and um landmarks and uh just extra notes that really give them a lot a lot a lot of information that's valuable. So, that's been great as as we go through the installation, learning learning all the different u concepts and packages he has. And then obviously the footwork's been great. I've spoken to that already that, [clears throat] you know, I switched from right foot forward to left foot forward and and um I've really enjoyed the ch the change. It took a minute in the spring to get comfortable with, but it's been good. >> As you guys prepare for this first preseason game, what have you been told about how they may split up the the reps among the four quarterbacks? >> Yeah, we haven't really been told yet. So >> uh Michael Pitman said the other day um he thought he knew football until he talked to him. [cough and clears throat] >> Say what I mean what do you learn from that guy? What are you amazed at how much he knows or how his mind thinks? >> Yeah, I think I think just globally he understands the run game um really intricately well. Um he understands protections like the back of his hand. He's um obviously [snorts] just I think he he would in in season he would take like a Thursday after practice and just go through the meeting and sort of a pop quiz but no coaches so it was very relaxed environment and just asking guys um questions and a um kind of popcorn around the room and it was just amazing the level of uh detail with with with break points and he just the way that he is able to articulate relate to the receiver, you know, the quarterback's perspective. And, you know, this is going to be a much harder throw for me if you break here opposed to to there. Um, so that really I hadn't never heard, you know, a veteran articulate like that and and in a calm manner and a and, you know, without a dict dictatorship, you know, just a very um kind, you know, and I think guys received that really well. Um, so I understand why Pitman would would say something like that. Mason, we were talking to Mike McCarthy earlier about sort of his approach when there's a turnover or something like that in practice. He seems pretty calm, cool, and collected to us. Have you guys seen a different side or how's he approached uh the offense when things aren't going the way we planned? >> Yeah, I think um I think you'd be correct. I think I mean he he he absolutely does not throw a a you know, a tantrum or a hissy fit. He's I think as a as a play caller for so many years, he he probably can't spend a lot of time uh riding the roller coaster himself just because he's got to get ready for the the next play, the next series, the next drive. Um and so I guess we you appreciate that about him, but um you know, he he absolutely, you know, he he wants to keep the ball secure just as much as any other coach. So that we we respect that about it, too. Um, so yeah, >> four with four quarterbacks, how much does it help you guys to do the two spot uh system when you guys are in team periods to kind of split those reps and and get more time on the field? >> Yeah, big time. It's that's been great. Um, just double the reps, you know, and u so I know, you know, the younger he's Mike's been with the younger quarterbacks um and I know they've appreciated that that wisdom. when we would when we've been with Tom Arth and coach an who've been great and then obviously Aaron I get to pick up on a lot of the protection conversations anything that he's thinking about adding I've been able to kind of be privy to that which has been fun but uh yeah the more reps you can get in training camp by splitting it up two spot the better was asked about players that impressed him the most in person as opposed to what he may have seen previously on film and he said your name first uh Why do you think that was? What did you do to make a positive first impression in year nine, which sounds kind of funny to say, but as a ninth year vet, what's the importance of making a first impression this year with four quarterbacks you play with? >> Um, I mean, I think you'd have to ask him. I I don't know. I think, um, you know, I think just making the most of each rep you get. Um, I didn't get a lot of reps in the spring. I think that was, you know, uh, intentional to to really give, uh, Will and Drew plenty of work. Um, obviously Will not getting any preseason last year. They wanted to really, you know, uh, take a, you know, give those guys plenty of plenty of work, plenty of, u reps. Um, but I don't know. I I I've tried to, uh, pick up the new offense, the new cadence, the new footwork, and, um, I think it's been a good transition, but, um, that's a question for him. >> Mason, you've been through a lot of different scenarios with the Steelers. How would you describe this this opportunity? uh different but also not I think um you know every year you're you know I remember the [clears throat] the headlines back from my my rookie year of Landry Jones and and Josh Dobs and um all the talk on who you know who's going to be the backup or uh and so you know I think you learn quickly after you know after my rookie year that [snorts] you know there's always going to be this you know this this is the time of year where where the depth chart is most talked about and that's just normal. That comes with the territory and all you can really do is um you know make the most of each each of your reps. I remember there was a time in 2020 uh probably three when I came back and Mitch and Kenny were getting just about every rep. I think I took one one pass in the spring of 23 and I was frustrated. I was down. I was like golly, you know, I know I'm better than I know I'm better than just getting one rep. But I think I had I had to change my mentality that year and say, "Lord, I'm just going to I'm just going to take every rep that I get and make the most of it and and don't complain about not getting the reps." And and and that year it worked out for me. And I had, you know, I extended my career and played some of my best ball. And um I've tried to keep that mindset with me as as hard as it can be sometimes of just uh just do the best with what you've been given. And I think that's that carries over in football, but as well in life. And that has bo I think that bodess well for people when they they stick it out. You look at people across the league. Sam Darnold, you know, just won a Super Bowl and was a backup a couple years ago. And so it's that's a the way I've tried to live. >> Mason, with this new offense being installed, are there some similarities to what you've done in the past or is it vastly different? And has there been a change in terminology? Have you had to pick up the way they explain things compared to the terminology you used in the past? >> Yes. Yes. There's a lot of the sim similar concepts uh I had in Tennessee, which was kind of a West Coast system. Brian Callahan by way of Zack Taylor, by way of Shawn McVey. Um and then and then Arthur Smith had some of the similar concepts that we've installed this year. But um the footwork definitely different. Um there's a little bit more leeway on like hey do whatever's comfortable last year which sometimes you appreciate as a player but McCarthy's been very like you know this is what we're going to do in quick game intermediate drop back play action nakeds and so I I appreciated the the structure because I I you know my first two years I didn't have a quarterback coach and and um it was kind of a free-for-all a bit and so I I I appreciate the structure. >> Jim told us that Aaron's big into pranks. Can you tell us about one? Do you kind of do those to him, too? >> Say that again. I didn't hear the end of it. >> Damn told us that Aaron is big into pranks. Could you share one with us? And did you kind of do them back to him as well? >> Yes. Um, you know, he put some bumper stickers on some guys cars without their knowledge and it was about a month or so. Um, some funny things that I won't repeat, but hilarious stuff. And I put then I put one on his car. Um you know uh yeah I I you'll have to ask him about the piece of art that I got him for uh Christmas sometime. Ask him about my Christmas gift. He'll he'll appreciate. >> Did you put on his car? >> Uh I don't think my mother would want me to [laughter] air it out. So I'm going to say I'm going to save that one. >> Did you go like >> was a sticker? >> It's a little bit harder to remove. But his security guy saw it. Unfortunately, a security guy saw it the day he got home and so it got it came off quick. I said, you know, that sucks. I was hoping for at least a week, you know. >> Can you kind of take us through how it went from on field getting the indoor how you guys heard about weather, everything like that? >> Yeah, I think it was really smooth. Honestly, that was our, you know, first time having to deal with that uh today. Um, but you know, we got in there and all of our, you know, turf shoes were ready and everything was all set up and we still got a lot of the the reps we were supposed to get out on the field on the indoor and having that indoor is uh, you know, a big advantage for us this year compared to last year. You know, we were kind of just up in the gym doing like more of a walk through, but and you know, we're still kind of half speed in in the indoor just because we don't have a ton of space, but we we have more space and it it's way more real and you can kind of still see those looks and see those reps. Um, and I just, yeah, it was really, really smooth and I thought they handled it really well. >> Obviously, you guys wouldn't want to have inclement weather, but how much does it help your What does it prepare you for as a team to have to kind of change course like that in the middle of practice? Yeah, I mean I think it it represents that, you know, kind of sudden change and we've been doing it really with the Franco moments, you know, kind of just, hey, sudden change, you know, twominute um you know, whether it's backed up like it was today um or, you know, something happens and you know, sometimes you're going to have to go into the locker room for a couple minutes and then come back out and you know, just just dealing with different changes, different sudden you know, adversities um you know, that obviously aren't ideal. I think, you know, obviously the rain is is one thing, but you know, just kind of dealing with that change of scenery and change of pace, you know, I think we did a really good job of it. >> What's the week like for you, you know, coming back off night practice? I mean, with being in game week, you being healthy and being able to play, what's your level of anticipation, excitement to show off where you've gotten better since the last time we all saw you playing the game? >> Yeah. No, I mean, I I'm I'm so fired up. I I can't wait for the game. And obviously I'm trying to take it day by day and it's still camp. Um but you know sometimes you can't help but look forward a little bit and start getting excited. Um you know just to be out there and and live live game reps cuz I haven't played you know in in over a year in in live game reps. You know I think the last time was a national championship. So um I've been chopping at the bit for a while to get out there with the guys in real um you know game game game-like settings with the uniform on with the helmet on. Um, and I'm I just can't wait, you know. I I I think tomorrow we're going to start looking at Green Bay a little bit and and uh doing, you know, some some planning a little bit and and I'm just I'm just really really excited. >> What have those game days been like for you not being able to participate being dated? >> Yeah, it's it's very different, you know, when you're on IR and you're not even dressed and then even when you're the emergency third quarterback, you know, that the mindset's a little different. Yeah. you want to talk about, you're always staying dialed in and I tried to be as much as I could last year. But, um, you know, it's definitely different when you know you're playing and probably gonna get a get a good amount of reps and, um, you know, I'm just I'm just excited, man. I I can't I can't express enough how fired up I am for for Thursday to get out there and and just to get some some live reps again just to play football because it's you know we we get paid for the work from Monday to Monday to Saturday and talk about Sundays are for free you know that's why we why we do what we do so know it's a Thursday but same same deal >> as much as wanting to play is is there a sense like hey with this competition I need to go out there and be able to show these guys what I can do Yeah, absolutely. I mean, I think that's one of the biggest um you know, just measuring measuring tapes is the is the preseason reps and you know, camp is great and you know, going against the ones and the twos is great, but you know, getting out there in a live setting and a real football game I think is just different. You know, it's it it is at the college level and it is at this level and, you know, I still haven't seen it. So, I'm excited to get get out there and experience it. I know everyone says preseason isn't isn't real football, but to me it is, you know, and I'm going to I'm going to treat it as such and and go out there and make the most out of my reps because I know it is important. >> Will, now that you've had some time to work with Coach McCarthy, where are you seeing the biggest differences in your fundamentals from where you started with the initial profile tape to where you are right now? >> Yeah, know that's a great question. I mean, I think there's there's been a lot of different uh areas I've made strides in. I think my consistency in my mechanics has been a lot better and just the consistency of how I'm throwing the ball, where my arm slot is. Um, and just the the way the ball's coming off my hand feels really good right now. And then I think the second thing is the footwork and just kind of dialing that in and and not not only, you know, the the punch reach drop, the build a drop drills that we do every day, but like, you know, from the gun and and feeling out, all right, this this drop, you know, on a on a gout route is a little different than maybe, you know, a deeper out route. you know, there's certain little nuances that I'm kind of starting to figure out and what I like, you know, versus what Aaron may like. And, you know, because there there are, you know, obviously it's very uniform, but there are a couple little differences where you can kind of pick and choose how you want to um, you know, make it your own. And I think I've, you know, through the last couple days and the last couple weeks here, it's been, it's been good to kind of just fine-tune that stuff. And I feel really good about >> Well, bu building off of that, uh, you know, you guys focus a lot on your fundamentals. How what has been the challenge of focusing on that while also working on the progressions and like the way you use your eyes and the decision- making getting used to that with all the disguises they're throwing at that this defense is throwing at you. >> Yeah. You know, I mean, we talk about the fundamentals are are very important and we we focus on those in Indie and before practice. Um but when we get in the game, like you're not thinking about that at all. We we talk about that. you're not you're not worried about, you know, where your footwork is and where your, you know, front shoulders pointed like you're you're just playing ball at that point. And the, you know, the the mindset behind that is like we're going to drill it so much in those indie drills and through OTAAS and mini camp and then, you know, the first couple weeks of camp here and get so many bananked reps that it's second nature and it's starting to become that um for really all of us and especially me. [clears throat] But yeah, when we're in there in the, you know, seven on seven or team or or twominute and we're not thinking about that. That's, you know, you can look at the tape and say, "Hey, I could have done better here and there in hindsight, but in the moment, yeah, we're not worried about that at all. We're trying to focus on it in Indie, focus on it before practice, but then once the once the bullets are flying, man, we're playing ball. Mike feel like you're more mid year more comfortable like in the huddle as much as you are in practice or after a player after a rep. You seem like you're [clears throat] more demonstraed your body language. Do you feel that or is that just your personality coming out than you were as a rookie last year at this time? >> I think it's a little bit of both. Um you know I think it's a little bit of you know just com comfortability with the guys and knowing the guys and not being a rookie I think makes a big difference. You know when you're a rookie you know you can get shot down easy. Hey, shut up, Rook. You know, but um now I really feel comfortable kind of just being myself. And myself, I've always been a, you know, I like to have a little bit of fun. I like to, you know, bring the juice, you know, for practice and and get the guys going, you know, especially when we have a big play. I'm a big encourager. So, like I I just feel more comfortable kind of um letting my true colors shine through this year. And I feel like um you know, when I do that, I think it's good for good for morale for myself. Um, and for the guys around us, you know, and we all just, you know, bounce off each other and make each other better. I think Ryan McCollum's a great great energy guy at the center spot, you know, especially with the twos group working with him. He's done a great job of of getting the guys going and, you know, we just, like I said, you know, I'm just getting more comfortable and more comfortable in the system, more comfortable with the guys, and just more comfortable being me. >> Well, has Mike has Mike told you [cough] how many snaps [clears throat] to expect or throughout? >> Not exactly. Um, you know, I I know I got to be ready to to play a good amount, but yeah, we haven't we haven't talked about exact numbers and who's playing when, all that. >> Have you given any thought? >> Have you given any thought to um spend uh the season with Aaron this last season in the inter? >> Yeah. No, I mean, it's special. You know, I we weren't really sure if it was or wasn't last year, but we, you know, we kind of tried to treat it as such. um just because you know we knew he was kind of on the fence still. Um and you know I felt like we didn't finish the season the right way last year. So you know I just I just want him to have you know the best final year he can possibly have and you know for him to have you know the long 22 career 22 year long career that he's had. Um you know it' be really special for him to finish it the right way. And I think we all would, you know, everyone on the on the team would agree that, you know, it's special to be with a guy like that, you know, for his last year. It's like, you know, a little, you know, whatever victory tour or farewell tour um for him, but um yeah, it's it's special to be a part of and and just just want to make sure that we can do everything we can to make it as successful and special as possible. >> Well, we were talking earlier with my McCarthy about turnovers in practice. What's he been like with you guys when whether it's back in the huddle or in the film room in terms of when things don't go right? What what what's his demeanor been like in his approach? >> You mean like when we throw interceptions, >> you know, I it was a exchange the other day or something like that. Yeah. What he does he yell? Is he you know what's what's those moments like for you? >> Well, it depends on the play, you know. I mean, the the play on on Saturday, there was a little miscommunication of what the play was. certain guys were running one play, certain guys were running another, kind of called it wrong. So, you know, that one, you know, I I took the blame for. And, you know, there there's different reasons for everything. And, you know, he's not just going to scream and yell at you right away for no reason. He's he's more of a guy I feel like that, you know, let's get back to the film. Let's look at what happened, diagnose, you know, why did you make that decision? Why did you make that throw? Why why did you know, the call not come in correctly? like and then and then we um handle it from that perspective. I think he does a really good job of staying pretty levelheaded. I mean, you know, he he he'll he he'll get um he'll get a little fiery when things start dropping down in energy, but you know, in terms of just like mental errors or, you know, interceptions or turnovers on the field. Um you know, he I think he likes to just go back and diagnose it on the film. And I think that's a a big emphasis that he's put on this off seasonason is, you know, we we really put a lot of a lot of emphasis on that film and how much that matters and and using that, you know, for our benefit. We talk about mis assignments versus mental errors and mis assignments are, you know, lining up the wrong way or pre- snap penalties and not not knowing what you're doing. And then mental errors are more, you know, like in the play making a mistake, making the wrong read. And we we talk about we can't have misassignments, but mental errors we can deal with. You know, that's that's football. We're going to make mistakes. It's not going to be perfect. Um and those are the things that we clean up in the meetings, but mis assignments are unacceptable. >> How big a difference from last year? Where are you? Do you feel coming into year two just from a comfort factor or playing standpoint? >> Yeah, I feel like um the game slowing down for me this year um going into year two um just um still harping on the older guys help um getting help from older guys like Cam. Um, but yeah, I feel like things are slowing down this time around. >> What's it been like working next to Hawaii on the first team so consistently? You guys came in together and now you guys line up next to each other a lot. >> It's cool, man. Like you said, we came in together. Um, that's my that's my uh guy right there and it's cool to have him out there with me. >> Derek, how how different is this for you guys on defense this year? >> Far as what? >> Just from obviously new coaches, but play style, how you guys attack, those type of things. Um, I don't think real difference. Just a new coaching staff. Um, we got that out the way during OTAAS. Now it's just ball, man. Kind of the same thing as far as like the uh scheme and alignments. Some little tweaks and things that PG br. But like it's same same for us. Um, got the playbook down and it's just time to execute. >> PG was saying on Saturday that he's a D lineman at heart basically since that's what he played and uh he likes to spend a lot of time in your room with you guys. is uh what what are the things you're picking up from him and how's that been having so much kind of hands-on work with the DC? >> It's been a blessing for that DC to be in the room. Um then we get on the field, he's running some of the drills. Um it's really a blessing cuz he's coming right in um when we watching a team rest from practice and he's really helping us pointing out things. He see how he wants it done. And what I really love about PG, like he's going to tell you what you did well, he's going to tell you what you did bad also. And he's not going to run away from or shy from it. Um, and that and that's been a great help for the guys in the room, including myself. >> People in different positions, different individuals, whatever. But last year, first round pick, you got hurt during during [clears throat] the preseason, missed practice time. Max was missing some practice time here just what did you were you able to apply that time? Do you remember coming into the league and trying to learn the game even though you couldn't maybe have practice field or anything? >> Yeah. Um, I got hurt in preeason then, um, and when I was in the season, um, it's really just got to show to the meetings. um really get your mental reps cuz you can't physically get your reps. So the me it's really mental game once you're on that sideline not be able to practice and be with the guys. Um you got to understand it's part of the game. That's something I didn't understand at at first and and I had a good group around me, good teammates around me to help me understand that. >> Derek, I had a practice today. Mike McCarthy said that there was some more work that you guys really wanted to get done and get accomplished before tomorrow when you start looking at Green Bay. Were you guys able to kind of accomplish everything with the weather today or was it a little bit more of hey having to move with all the changing parts tonight? >> Yeah, we got some we got some good reps. We got inside run um Franco moments um right before we went out uh indoors. I feel like just for the offensive line, defensive line that inside run really helped us um we got alive period in that and um cuz you don't get too many far as real practical pass on for the O line D line and really collide like that. So that was very helpful. We got was able to get that. >> How have you felt about those clashes? I mean the D line and the O line are two of the most highly invested groups by this front office of the last few years. So you guys are going to clash a lot. How have you felt about how that competition has been when you guys put the pads on whether goal line Franco moments etc. >> It's been it's been amazing man. Um some plays we're getting them some plays are getting us and it's just really iron sharp and iron right there man. Um I can't really express enough how how much we really working and even after like one-on- ones or team periods like guys are coming over and asking what did you see? and I'm going over the O line. How did you see that rep? And things like that. And it's really just a cuz it's a team at the end of the day and we want everybody to be great. >> Do you have a rival that you that you have or like a person that you look for like, hey, I know I'm going up against Zack or Mason. I know I'm to to expect this X, Y, or Z. >> Not far as a rival, but of course you want to go against um one of the best guys on the O line and I'm I don't got no rival, but I just want to go against the best. >> One of uh Mike McCarthy's Steelers six fundamentals that he pointed out was blocking. or in your guys case getting off blocks. What do you think the defensive line has worked the most on to improve in that area or get through blocks penetrating the line? >> As far as getting off blocks, you >> really just shing. You got to shed. You got to be um as a point of contact. Once you get your not bad, you got to be able to shed off a block. You can't stay block for too long cuz if you stay blocked for too long, that mean the ball's hitting your gap or something. You're not doing your job right. So, that's something we've been doing far as with coach PCO on the sleds, really shedding off those blocks and um practicing those reps. There is something that really sticks with you from what coach Pek always said and and how aware are you are you guys of his career? >> PC says a lot of things, man, because he has 13 years in the league and you got to respect that end of the day. Um cuz he had his hand in the dirt just like we do and and I can't just pinpoint one thing he said because he says a lot and we try to soak up everything because like I said 13 years in the league and and playing those so anything he says everybody in that room ears are open and really listen to coach P. >> You ever seen >> last one here? You ever see any of his highlights go on YouTube or anything? >> I haven't. Not yet. No, sir.

title: Coach Mike McCarthy Press Conference (August 10) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Mike, you didn't have much tape to go off of Dylan Cook last year and what he played. What have you seen from him in these first two weeks that you didn't maybe see in those training snaps last year? >> Uh I'd say Dylan's been consistent, number one. I think clearly the I really felt him in the pass protection first, you know, and which which is a good thing, you know, because um to be able to do that early in camp and without the pads, um >> [snorts] >> you know, so I was impressed with that and you know, just like the rest of the guys, I think they're starting to get their pads underneath them, you know, getting the pad level down, you know, really we need to get our pad level down as a the whole front, um but yeah, I think he's having a nice camp. >> Mike, with um three of your top defenders not practicing, is it when you put in anything new, is it is that much of a setback or not? >> Uh man, I wouldn't say it's a setback because, you know, they're they're still in the room, you know, they're still part of the communication. Um and, you know, I I think just like anything, you know, we need everybody and and this is actually a very healthy, normal exercise uh when when younger players get opportunities. So, I mean, you know, when you have [snorts] veterans that are going through injuries, um it's important to get to get them back, you know, obviously they have there's history there, um you know, but they are part of the meetings and the communication and so forth. So, um I I just think it's it's really a good opportunity for the younger players. >> Any guy in particular taking advantage of that opportunity? >> Oh, yeah, I think all the young guys. I mean, it's >> [sighs] >> uh >> [gasps] >> I mean, um going through last night, and I mean, you know, I'm I'm I'm a little bit focusing on the pre-snap right now because we're not we're not where we need to be, you know, there, but um yeah, I I think, you know, um you know, with the injuries in the practice Saturday night, I thought Jeremy really stepped up with his extra his extra reps, you know, in the receiver room. Um but yeah, I mean, I don't I don't have anybody specific. I'm I good. Other things I'm focusing on right now. >> Mike, is Max going to practice today? >> I'm sorry. >> Is Max going to practice today? >> No, Max will will not be He won't be out there today. >> Do you have any timeline as far as when we might see him back? >> Uh no, I don't. Sorry. >> Mike, what's different for you guys this week as you're preparing for the first game of preseason? >> Well, today is install recall seven. So, we have one more install today. So, we we have a lot of going in as far as you know, this is our last third down uh installation. Uh we're going to work backed up. So, we'll have a a segment where we you know, we'll have a competitive backed up situation. We have three series of that. So, just trying to make sure we're hitting all you know, all the situations, highlighting them, you know, getting reviewing them in the team in the in the team meetings and you know, the meeting part of it and we'll we'll hit that again today. So, uh and then we'll we'll shift gears tomorrow and start trying to focus on you know, who's going to play and and and how we're going to play and you know, what we want to do against uh Green Bay. >> Mike, when you're having a lot of turnovers [cough] in practice, can you say hey, good for the [clears throat] defense or are you mad at the offense or sometimes does it depend? >> I think that's the beauty of being the head coach. You get to you get to answer those questions, you know, standing on the fence. But uh you know, I I you know, obviously as as a offensive player you or coach you you don't want to have giveaways like that and I think the biggest thing that I look for is you know, how did the giveaway or takeaway happen? You know, so when they're self-inflicted giveaways, that's it you know, that's you know, that's we're not looking for that. Um but when the defensive guys make a tremendous player, you know, and they're definitely taking the ball away. You know, there's a difference between a giveaway and a takeaway. So, um you know, that's that's the way we break them down. That's how we calculate it and that's how we present it to the to the team. >> Mike, when we talked to you back in the spring, you talked One [snorts] thing you said you were excited about this roster was like when the first guys off the bus would be the big guys on on your team. Gabriel Rubio seems to be getting a lot of work and doing well. What have you seen from him as a rookie, like late-round pick who's been able to impress upon the team? >> Well, I I think the biggest thing, you know, done in the trenches, you know, for all the guys when they first get in there and and you can throw Max in in the in this same category is, you know, do they belong? You know, can they and you know, they jump out there in the their first one-on-one, their first, you know, inside run type situation and so forth. And And Gabriel's definitely that guy. So, I think he definitely belongs. Um and but he's young. You know, he he's young, but he's got great veteran presence around him. Um you know, I think the you know, the one thing we're trying to focus on is getting more reps for those guys. You'll see us walk the field after practice is over with the with the younger players and just doing focus more on two-minute and so forth, but um but he he definitely belongs. >> Mike, what's been your history keeping nine or 10 offensive linemen? And when you keep 10, what are the reason that you want to keep that extra guy? >> Well, I think the roster the overall roster, you know, answers that question. You know, it's you know, I'm really focused on you know, 68 players. You know, we need to come out of here. You know, it's a it's a it's a good 90-man roster. I'm I'm really focused on how to you know, who who are those 68 players and and obviously those there's decisions and you know, projection that comes, you know, down to that there at the end. So, uh but I I think we definitely can make a case for at least 10 making our team. >> Mike, it had been a while since Roderick had played. How have you seen him progress, [cough and clears throat] especially with the pads on? >> Well, Roderick picked it up the last two the last two practices, you know, I I think you know, obviously with the opportunities, you know, the reps available with Max not practicing. Um you know, we had a conversation about his ability to play both left and right. You know, you know, but you got to remember he's coming back from a significant injury. You know, he's he's not 100% back and then you know, so um but I I thought he definitely picked it up the last two practices. >> When it comes to the uh quarterbacks, especially the two young guys, I mean, is there a way to kind of gauge or simulate or evaluate their play making, sack avoidance in a practice setting, or do you kind of just have to wait for >> I mean, to a point, yes. I mean, to a point, I mean, we that's why we do the drills that we do, and then and and it's how we practice in team periods, you know, there's when a when a when a defender rushes the passer and and wins the pass rush, you know, and gets the sack, he's taught to, you know, run by it, you know, and then and he's credited with a sack when we grade the tape, but, you know, there's still 21 other guys working, so um you know, you'll have eight times a game where the quarterback's going to have to slide his feet, scramble, and make a play, so uh we try to simulate that the best we can in practice, and so that's why you you'll see the scrambles and extended plays in the team periods, and and those are important reps. >> Mike, both uh Pecko and Jarred have played [clears throat] in this league a long time. How have you seen their coaching translate in the messaging to the players, and what does that mean to them? >> Uh it's it's fun to watch, you know, both those they're outstanding men, number one. I mean, it's obviously their playing career speaks for themselves. I mean, it's you're talking about two Hall of Fame caliber uh type careers, but they're they're just high-quality men. Uh they're great examples for our players, uh and I just really enjoy watching them work, the one-on-one relationships. You know, their voice in you know, and in their voice will in how they handle the room, and you know, and they'll find their voice more in in a in a commanding, demanding way as they grow as coaches, but they have done it I thought I think an excellent job, particularly in the one-on-one opportunities. >> Last year uh Will Howard talked a lot about how Aaron was such a willing mentor to him. Um now that you've had a chance to be around this, just what stands out about the way that Aaron has worked with these two young quarterbacks? >> You know, Aaron always has done that, um which which I have a lot of respect for, and I think it's an >> an important component of your quarterback room, the dynamics of the quarterback room, and and and developing everybody, the coaches included, and in the you know, keeping the accountability, you know, throughout that process. Um but it's at a different level now. I mean, he's uh you know, he he he shares constantly. Um he's um you know, I think he's very reflective and and obviously as you make tweaks cuz it's it's not really about the plays we decide to run. It's it's it's it's really dialed into them and the specifics of every single one. So, you know, and cuz you got you have an offense that's um you know, there's some things in the past you'd like to grow with the guys that have been here. You know, obviously we we've always built the in in my time built the the offense around making the quarterback successful. So, you know, he his input is is very important important, but really, you know, tailoring down it's in in trimming and get the little things, the details, and you know, he he's he has tremendous history in these concepts. Um you know, how they were defended 15, 20 years ago and how they're being defended now. So, it's a it it's it's a fun it's a it's a it's a lot of fun to be in that quarterback room. >> Mike, you've talked a lot about position flexibility. How's a young player [clears throat] like Noah Kalaski progressed in that regard as far as some of the things you guys might ask him to to do? >> I don't know if Riley could do any more. I mean, just in a short time he's been here. Uh he's he's done a hell of a job. I mean, he's you know, he's uh competing uh for, you know, [snorts] spots on all four core. Um he's you know, he plays in the backfield, he plays at the on the line of scrimmage, uh play plays the displaced. So, he's doing a great job. >> Two more. How's uh how's Dunker progressing uh throughout camp so far? >> Good. I mean, I I think just, you know, opposite of you know, um you know, some of the others, he's he's probably better in the run right now than the pass pro, and I think that's leads towards his history. You know, he's uh he's a powerful man at the line of scrimmage, and when he gets on you, you know, it's it's a it's a problem. So, but um you know, that's why we're here. Big powerful man with a bright future. >> Mike, how have you seen Robert Spears Jennings kind of embrace those first team reps and playing a ton of different roles in the secondary? >> I mean, very well. I mean, we talked to someone about you know, the position flex opportunity and just you know, making with you know, >> the coordinators and Danny crossed me yesterday. I mean, he's definitely an impactful player in special teams. So, you know, you want the flexibility where you know, a safety can come down and and maybe play some big nickel and do do different things and cuz at the end of the day when we get to the games, you know, the matchups will will be a big part of how we play each and every week. He gives us that flexibility. >> All right, thank you. >> Thank you.

title: Underrated RB DAZZLES, big injury updates, Yahya Black improves, Gennings Dunker | Steelers Rewind
text: What's going on everybody? Welcome back to Steelers rewind here on pennlive.com. Nick Farabaugh here with you all. The Steelers had a disjointed practice day about an hour outside on the fields, then they had to evacuate inside to the indoor stadium. The whole field was evacuated due to severe thunderstorms around the area. But let's talk about today cuz I think we actually got a lot in that one hour. We got backs on backers, we got inside run, we had a goal line drill, we had a Franco moment, we had all of these different things in this one hour. And so let's talk about injuries first. Michael Pittman Jr. and DK Metcalf didn't practice. Pittman had his right leg looked at on Saturday at Saturday Night Lights, so that's injury-related. And Mike Tomlin even mentioned that. So Jeremy Bernard got a lot of more run and more playing time today. I thought that's very important to get a rookie there. Certainly feels like if one of those guys goes down, Jeremy Bernard's first up at outside wide receiver, while Roman Wilson might be the starting slot receiver. And so let's see how that continues to go. In terms of injuries, DeQuan Brisker, Maxi Haughton, Steven Sims, and Eli Harold were all back in pads and helmets. They did not do a lot in team if any in team. Keanu Benton, who had been wearing a big wrap on his right hand, did end up actually doing some team reps. That was the first time in about a week we've seen that from Keanu Benton. But those four injured guys getting back into the fold, Brisker only missed one practice, Haughton has missed a few, seems like he is on the mend, it's starting to come back. So that's really good news. You know, you add Pittman, but you get guys like Haughton on those back. Maybe Haughton can even play on Thursday. That'll be really important for him to get that first preseason game. So this inside run period was physical. I thought we saw a lot of really good things. Yaya Black continues to flash the pad level. And you know, he has these moments sometimes where the pad level still swells and it's a real big issue, but there's other times where he really gets low and you see the dominant force you think he could be with that size and that brute strength he carries. Him and Derrick Harmon are strong as oxen. Um they are really hard to move if they play with good pad level. And Harmon's more consistent, but I think you can look at Black with his movement skills at his size, with his strength, if he can fix the pad level, this guy could be that type of of two-gapping nose that you wanted for a long time. So, he stood out. Azazio Teewo is someone that we haven't talked about a lot, but we should be talking about more, you know, as a kind of penetrating three-tech, someone that can move out in the sub packages, made a nice TFL. Jacoby Windmon made a few nice plays. Um I really like Jennings Dunker in this drill. He got a few really good blocks and movement downhill. Um there was one where he really cleared out the B gap and Riley Nowakowski came in, filled in on the lead block, and Lou Nichols really was allowed to run right behind that, lower his shoulder, and get a touchdown. I thought Lou Nichols was exceptional today. Um he was great in this team run drill, and he was great in backs on backers. He had like four out of five wins, and I thought it was just really impressive to watch Lou Nichols. I don't know if he has a spot on this roster, but he is someone that really has a uh the mental makeup, the physicality, the ability to do multiple roles. He's good pass pro back. There's a lot to like there. Travis Homer, Jaylen Warren also looked really good. I thought Rico Dowdle struggled in the backs on backers drill. I think Windmon looked great. Payton Wilson continues to look great. He had another great tackle for loss in the team run drill, and then he comes out in backs on backers and just dominates. I mean, this guy keeps stacking days where you look at Payton Wilson and you're just like, "Is this the year?" And so, we always talk about best, you know, kind of best uh best of your life season, right? This is the type of of time where you're look like that. Payton Wilson's having a heck of a training camp. And so, kudos to him. Let's see if it translates in the regular season games, but he's off to heck of a start so far. Will Howard said he's really excited, chomping at the bit, fired up to play his first NFL game. He has not played an NFL game because of the injury he suffered to his hand last year. So, Thursday will be Will Howard's first NFL game, preseason or regular season. So, this should be really fun to see. They don't know the rotation yet for the quarterbacks. We'll probably find out more from Mike McCarthy tomorrow. But, seems like a guy like Will Howard really, really fired up to do that. And we'll see where all of that goes. Folks, make sure to like, comment, subscribe, turn the notification bell on, and thanks for watching.

title: Drew Allar IMPRESSES, two rookies dazzle, Broderick Jones bounces back, WRs shine | Steelers Rewind
