Um that's why we try to generate as much as possible in practice. >> How much adjustment how much adjustment do you have to make in terms of preparing for the season when Kyle use is not there given he's kind of singular in terms of the position he plays for you guys? >> Um not really any at all. Um we have other guys because we've been Juice has done an awesome job staying healthy so it doesn't happen much but um you know Jake Tonis couldn't do that stuff. Um we've had Luke Frell do that stuff. We've had KD do some of that stuff. Um, sometimes we give DVO the ball and we've had Christian do some of that stuff. Um, so guys all have to do it, but Juice is very similar to, you know, what we said about Christian when when guys prepare the right way and they've been through this so long as long as they're prepared the right way and not counting on camp to get them in shape. Sometimes it can be somewhat of a benefit for those guys to get some things that keep him out that don't allow him to get hurt worse when it's, you know, he's got a frustrating thing like I do right here that's nothing but it's just annoying for him. but I think could maybe help them in the long run. >> They made some plays today. What are you your thoughts on their tight ends this camp so far? >> I thought they've done a real good job. I think um you know I think they've all the guys that we've had here in the past, guys like Braden, Jake, Luke, I think all of them look better than what they were last year and I was happy with them last year, but you're always getting better or worse and um I think they've taken the cutups, they've taken the offseason and I think they've all improved in the pass game and the run game. Um it's nice for them to get more opportunities without KD out there. And then I love all the new guys we brought in too. We've had some good competition there and you know it's always tough when you're missing a guy like George. Um and then you miss a guy like Juice which as Juice will let you know um he still was playing the tight end position also. Um so those guys are down two spots of key contributors which gives them a chance to do more and more and they've been ready for that um just um conditioning wise and that's why I think they're all getting better. >> All right, thanks guys. Hello >> said that you're like a creative player and that was his compliment to you. What was it like to see him back up there? >> It's great to see him. You know, he's trying to butter me up. made me feel good so I go easier on him. But uh I'm happy for him, his opportunity, all the all the times that we've shared together. I I'm indebted to Sala and everything that he's given me. So um excited for his opportunity with with their team the way you guys came out like three scuffles in the first six plays. Was that a calculated thing to kind of let the Titans know that you know they're on your turf? >> No, I promise. like we're we're not trying to fight and do all this other stuff. Like we're trying to play football. And that's what I had to try to tell the guys early on. I brought everybody together and told them like, you know, we're not going to get through today if we if we continue on this path. You know, we got to play football, right? If you you end up on the ground, then that means you didn't win your rep, right? And you better you got to run it back. So, um you know, I think we kind of found our groove a little bit after some of that that fiery business going on in the beginning. Um but you got to watch the tape to really see how how it was. your first sort of rough stuff since your your injury. How how did you feel today out there? >> I felt great. I felt great. Um, you know, I think it was good to just finally like just be going against another jersey. Um, because, you know, all camp you talk about protecting the team, protect the team. No, you know, just wanting to keep guys healthy, but then you finally get an opportunity to play like real football. You're still not taking guys to the ground per se, but like it's it's going to bring another level of like, all right, let's see who can really like make a thud tackle in the flat, you know, or in a whole strike shed. Um, you know, and really just played more actual football. So, uh, it was it was fun to just get out get out there and get better. >> What did you see from your your teammates in that regard? You know, tackling in the flat, things like that today. >> Yeah, I mean, it's hard to say, right? And when you're in the in the heat of it, especially when you're on the field, I definitely don't know. I don't know what what it feels like cuz I'm too busy trying to focus on what I'm doing. But it felt like, you know, we definitely have some things to work on. You know, I think Thursday is going to be a really great opportunity for a lot of young guys who may have not had that opportunity to to, you know, be in those positions to see like, you know, what they got in in a live action setting, but today was as close as that's going to get, right? So, that's why I love joint practices to really have an opportunity in a game-like setting uh to work on your craft and really see where your team's at. Um, you know, we got a long ways to go and I think that's going to be the case all the way leading up to week one. You know, we're just trying to find how to be our best version of ourselves for when the time matters most. >> You got enough time on the field with Jaden Duggar to to form an impression yet early on in camp. >> Absolutely. I I love Jaden. I I love I I never even called him Jaden, though. That was the first time I ever said his first name. He's just Doug to me. But, uh, yeah, I mean, he has a skill set that's that's rare. you know, the fact that he's, you know, a true 6'5, long arms, can can run like a deer. Um, he's not afraid of contact, right? He can play several different positions on the field. Um, you know, his retention of information, instincts. I think those are all things that can get you, you know, really excited about a player, but he is still a rookie, right? You know, he makes rookie mistakes just like anybody in that position. Um, but, you know, I think as a rookie, it's honestly just about being present, right? and just having the the uh the mindset of wanting to really continue to improve and get better every single day. You're not going to be a finished product and everybody knows that. So, um you know, I think like I said, Thursday's a really good opportunity for him and a lot of young guys to get in really in a game setting to see how you perform under the lights, right? And that's that's really what we all get graded on in this in this league is when when you cut that tape on on on Sundays or in this case Thursday, what do you look like? So, >> how do I see him absorb all the positions he's learning right now as a rookie? And like in meeting rooms, is there something that stands out just about how he how he handles his business? >> I wouldn't say necessarily in the meeting room because he is more of a quiet individual, but he uh you see it just in the way that he plays. It's not a it's not it's not too much for him, right? For a rookie to be asked to do, you know, a lot of different things, play a lot of different positions, whether it's off the ball, whether it's on the ball, whether it's on the edge, you know, where he's being asked to do a lot of things. And the fact that it's not too much for him, that's how you know that he's he's got a good feel of the game and been able to retain a lot of information. Um, so I think he's done a great job thus far. >> Talk about DB's. Uh, what have you liked from that group particularly today? Would you please >> Yeah, I've loved our our defensive back group. Uh, you know, I don't know if I felt as confident about a back-end group in my career as I have right now. That's not even a knock on any on any teams that I played on before. But I think just the way that that group is kind of meshing together, the way that they're playing sticky in coverage, playing the ball in the air, being able to, you know, play in the run game or ball thrown to the flat, the ability to cut to tackle, um, I think it's one of the best I've I've seen thus far. I'm I'm really excited about what I'm seeing and we just got to continue to to gel and and mesh that thing together to where it's the best version like I said for when the time comes. >> Raheem has talked a little bit about Brock's ability to layer the ball. I know you make it a point to get your hands on some and you have in this camp just as as the guy generally that is going to be the one who would be getting layered over. What is the frustration level of a quarterback who is capable of doing that as consistently as he is? >> Um frustration level, man. You know, me and Brock have our battles every single day and I love it, honestly. You know, we're we're getting the best out of each other. Um, you know, where he'll he'll layer a ball over or I get my hand on it like you said, and that's honestly what camp is about. That's what this whole preseason before getting ready for week one is about because at the end of the day, you know, I'm not going to see a better guy at doing that than Brock Pury when it comes to go going into the season. And I don't know, you know, you have to ask him if he's going to see somebody better at being able being those windows. But um at the end of the day, it's all just trying to free just trying to have iron sharpening iron every single day, right? So um you know, I love the competition and we're going to continue to work at it and develop the best team possible. >> That get over your hands. I mean, you have to be thinking as it's coming to you, you're going to have it though, right? Like this. >> Yeah, I mean it's uh I'm still waiting for that one to just beautifully land in my fingertips, but he makes me work for it. He's one of the best. He's the best in my mind, but you know that's for a different that's another discussion for later. >> Some uh jawing today with with Cam Ward. Um it seemed pretty lively at times. Is that calculated on your part to sort of ratchet up the intensity so that you're having a a very intense practice? >> Yeah, I mean I think it's all just in good fun competition. Um, I think Cam is one of the unique quarterbacks where he's not afraid to to sit there and play that game with you. You know, whether that's a positive or negative, I think that's uh still yet to be seen on for their side. We'll see. But for me, you know, I'm always trying to get the quarterback out of his game. And anytime I'm in that mode, that's only going to amplify my game, right? So, um, I love joint practices, though. It's the best. >> So, Brock, what do you mean by that? Are you saying like either either he takes the high road or he gives it back and that kind of determines his mindset to play this position? >> Um, what I mean is is he he is one of the few quarterbacks who will sit there in the pocket like not actually in the pocket, but I'm saying like sit there and actually like get into that ver that verbal back and forth, right? Where a lot of quarterbacks aren't really necessarily wanting to do that because they're so focused on wanting to just obviously just execute the offense. But some guys, they elevate their play too when they they get into that. And I think he he's probably one of those guys who he does elevate his play when he starts getting into that that type of thing. But listen, that talking at the end of the day, you got to go out there. You got to play football. And it's 11 on 11. It's not just me versus him, right? So there was situations where I wish I could say something to him, but then we're we're giving up a touchdown or something, right? And it's like it's it's a it's a team game at the end of the day. You got to go out there, you got to play the game. All that talking is just it's talk. Me and Brock had plenty of our conversations on the field. >> Cerak told us the other day that that he thinks the guys really like playing for Raheem Morris and that he comes in and he builds culture. He's real positive. What What's your takeaway? How does Raheem kind of win over the room and kind of earn his stripes with you guys? >> Uh I mean there's not a whole lot of stripes to earn. You you look at his pedigree, right? I mean and what we're trying to do here, we say we're trying to win a championship. He's done that already, right? He's coached some of the best defenses in the NFL. Um, but yeah, at the end of the day, it's really about connecting with the room, right? And I think he just he's has a unique ability to kind of connect with each guy. Um, you know, and really demanding the best out of you, and that's all you can ask for as a player, right? And so, we keep trying to detail this thing up to make sure everybody's on the same page. Um, and it's not a finished product by any means. I don't think it'll be a finished product even by week one, right? It's a whole season thing. It's a full season thing, but um you want to make sure that it's obviously humming uh for when the time when you need it the most. >> Thank you guys. >> Yeah, I love what I've seen from Nick. I think he continues to get better, which is what you can only ask for from a young guy, right? I mean, he has such a freakish ability in his body to just run through people. So, when it's all when it's headed in the right direction, that's it's a scary sight. Um you just got to continue to keep staying on it, right? And be consistent. Um because that's that's the truest measure of performance in this league. good and bad things you saw today. >> Um, I think just going going up against a different scheme obviously like practice against Solo and his scheme all last year and whatnot, but it was it was nice to switch it up. um go against those guys and their wands and feeling the the physicality, the the violence uh from just another team. Um and then also being able to move the ball on them kind of thing and get some good reps with Debo dribbling and and stuff like that. I think for me was was huge. Dro had a great day. Um having the offensive line feel the run game and just the urgency with that. They did a great job. So I think that was good. um some stuff to work on is is I guess for me just feeling like um how I have at practice the last couple days. Like when I went up against a new defense for the first time this year, it's like still being aggressive and and being quick in my reads and stuff and uh so that's something that I'll watch the film and see where I was at today. But um those are just my initial thoughts. >> How big a step is it to see he's all seen dribbling in practice and then to see him make some plays against another team. How big a step in your mind is that? >> Yeah, it's huge. Um, I mean, obviously like going up against our guys, I mean, it's starting NFL defense and he's shown that time and time again. Um, but it was cool just to, you know, switch it up today, go go up against different guys that we haven't played against and, uh, see him make plays and, um, you know, run our offense and be on time and do his job and things like that. So, it was good. I know there was a couple routes that we could still uh talk about and whatnot, but um it fires me up that we have stuff that we can keep getting better at. But he showed a lot of uh flashes and stuff today, so I was excited about it. >> You hit him on a you hit him on one over the middle on a cross and then Tonis on the next play where you also layer Kingdom over a linebacker. Did you hear Rahee Morris give you that nickname of the layer king and uh do you take that to heart that that's a great asset? Um yeah, I mean he he had told me I guess on the field that he said that to the media and then our quarterback coach Mick Lombardi, he doesn't like the word layer. Um he thinks everything should be driven and and you throw the appropriate ball. Um so I can't really say anything about the layered ball, but um yeah, it's it's cool that Raheem notices that and stuff like that. So um I guess it's a part of my game, but you know, obviously I like to think I can make any throw on the field, not just that one. But yeah, >> you mentioned D Rob. He did have a pretty big day today. What makes him so such a good receiver. Seems like he's had a lot of success in his career in the red zone. >> Yeah, he's um I think he's just one one of the best receivers that I've played with in terms of the one-on-one matchup and his feel for the game. And um you know, we'll have something drawn up like, hey, the receiver needs to get this many steps and be here on time. But um sometimes there's situations where you cut it off short or you push up into a guy a little bit longer and then get out of the cut. like he has a good feel for the game when it comes to that. He's played for a while. He's got a lot of savviness to him. Um and obviously in the red zone and stuff like he's got length. He's got uh just the ability to go up and get the ball. So um you know, obviously I learned a lot about him last year, but you know, this offseason and stuff watching film on him, it's like, all right, we can give this guy more ops and and uh have him be a huge part of our offense. So he's had a great camp. He's been out there every day showing up, making plays and catches. Today against the Titans, too, same thing. So, um, I'm really excited for him. >> Last time you were here, you you talked about just with Kyle's situation, if if need be, you wanted to make sure you could step up and be the guy, the voice that everyone here and all that kind of stuff. How would you just assess this camp for you, not only in terms of performance, but in the way that you've maybe had to, you know, take on a little bit more in terms of leadership or whatever, however you view it. >> Yeah. Um, you know, obviously with Kyle being out and stuff, like he you you could feel Kyle, um, out there as a coach, um, when practice is slow, when guys aren't on top of things, like he's a he's a voice and a presence. Obviously, he's the head ball coach, but, um, you know, he will bring us together sometimes, be like, dude, we need these next two periods, we need to be on it. We need to bring it. Um, and so I think when he's been gone and stuff, I've had a couple opportunities just to be able to, I guess, use my voice and just my actions with with the guys on offense and um, just being able to pick guys up and and um, and also hold some guys accountable with things at the right time. And um, I think just hearing guys in the locker room and stuff like they like that. They feed off it. Um, knowing that we care. It's not just to go out there and rip guys, but I care so much that, you know, all these little things matter and they show up in the season at some point. And so, um, I think for me just being able to take that next step, you know, especially with Kyle being gone, like being a voice out there for the guys, get guys going, get them moving, getting in and out of the huddle, picking up the tempo, I feel like I've I've had to take that step this year with that and and it's been good. >> How how do you know when it's the right time? And how did it how did you figure that out? I mean, um, just at practice, you know, the coaches have us playing situational things. Uh, it's third down, we don't get it. Now it's fourth down and a guy runs the wrong route and it's like, dude, you know, it's fourth down here and I need you to be where you need to be and I need to make the throw. And um, but also like, hey, I'm going to get on you and it's not just to make an example. It's because I trust you and know that you can make that play. So, let's let's get together and let's let's get it done. Um, and I'm glad it's happening now at practice when it's fourth and seven so that in season when a game's on the line and we need a win, like you're going to be there and I'm going to make the throw for you and all those kind of things. So, I mean, working we're working those things out right now in camp, which is good. >> This offseason with specific things that you wanted to improve on at this point in camp, how do you feel like where you're at with those things, especially now going against another defense? >> Yeah, I think um just like playing with urgency with my feet, having a good base, those are like the fundamental things. Um, you know, Mick, Clay, Kyle, and I had watched early in the offseason when we came back for OTAAS. And, um, I just I've been trying to hone in on that all off seasonason. And I think coming out to camp, like, it's just allowed me to play fast. It's allowed me to be on time with my throws and, um, make any kind of throw with where I'm in the pocket because I have a good base and my feet are good. So, um, that's the one thing that comes to mind. There's some other things, but um I feel like if I can just continue to do that um I can continue to take my game to the next level. >> On your side, but did you notice what was going on on the other on the other field or at least early on? And does that kind of get to, you know, up the motivation up to whatever the intensity on your side when you see your defense kind of slugging it out every other play on the other side? >> Yeah, I mean going into these kind of days like, you know, we have meetings before and stuff where Kyle's like, "Hey, protect the team." and it's about getting better and stuff like as players we all know that you know these are this is going to be a really high competitive intense kind of day and so yeah at one point you know we had a little scuffle going I look over in the other field they're scuffling and I'm sitting back there with Christian McAffrey and we're like dude like this this this happens but um at the end of the day being smart not trying to get hurt by punching a guy in a face mask or something like that like um you know try to be smart protect the team but I mean it is NFL football they came all the way over here to practice against us and I'm glad it was, you know, um you know, you could you could feel the energy and stuff and we all feed off that, but yeah, I mean it's it's a camp scrimmage for you. >> How important has it been for able to be out there, especially in the run game with your top four guys out? >> Yeah, it's been huge. Um obviously what Debo can do is is awesome. He can run routes on the outside of the slot, come back in the back field, run routes, can run the ball from the back field. So having him being able to, you know, help out with the run game right now, just with our numbers and stuff at running back has been huge. And it's good for him, too, to be able to come back into the system and and get those reps and have him being able to read out a run and bounce back gaps and make cuts. So that's been good for him. But also, like it's been fun, like I said, having him back there to be able to run routes and have really good matchups. And um, you know, he's still explosive and still the same Debo that we know. And um, made multiple plays today even where if you get him the ball, man, he's going to break tackles. like if we're alive I was like that's a broken tackle that's a touchdown or whatever like uh he's a playmaker so glad to have our guy back preseason reps in every game or have you guys talked about that how many series do you think you need in the preseason to prepare for week one >> I mean you know last couple years it's been the last two games I get a drive or two uh depending on the situations and just try to you know have that mindset of getting ready for a game getting in pads getting hit um but also you know you want to be smart and safe and get to the regular season healthy. Um so those are things that you know we'll talk about and whatnot, but um I I do think it's it's big uh just in terms of getting a feel for an NFL game and uh so that's what we've done in the past. We haven't really talked about anything yet. I'm sure we will soon, but um I guess we'll see. >> You've outlined in the past the importance of the timing component with your receivers, especially with a young guy and you're still kind of getting to know that in that way. How has he been, you know, early on and how's that progressed for you too >> for his timing purposes? Um, yeah, like I've said, he's he's a really smart dude. He gets the game of football. Um, you know, sometimes guys come in, they're talented and stuff, but to understand like the speed of the NFL and how defenses operate in the NFL, like it's it can be hard for guys to sort of get with it quick. Eventually, they they get there, but um, Stribb has been a guy that has come in and like has shown like he he understands it. He understands leverages, he understands coverages and our concepts and stuff and where he needs to be. And um not only that, like the effort and everything too. Like he's he's come in and like run multiple routes and reps back after back and then getting in the run game and blocking like um so all of that for me as a quarterback when I see that I'm like, "All right, dude." Like this guy's building my trust with him and uh we've connected and made plays together, too. And and we just got to continue to talk and be on the same page and communicate uh moving forward. But um I'm really excited for him. I've said that time and time again. It is preseason and everything. So I mean we'll see once we get to the season, but right now I have a lot of trust in him. >> So thanks

title: Klay Kubiak and 49ers Players Address the Media Following Day 10 of Camp | 49ers
text: on Thursday. >> Yeah. Um, first definitely still an open competition. I mean, those guys are going to compete all camp. You know, and I know Connor was in there initially and then Jones is now in there playing a little bit more with the ones, but those guys are going to keep keep battling, keep competing. Um, I don't think we ever set out to say, "Hey, whoever's in there the first day is going to take it all the way." Those guys are going to compete. They're both going to play in the preseason a lot. Um, and so that's just got to play itself out. They're both doing a good job and and it's not no slide on Connor or anything like that. They're just competing and we're going to keep rotating those guys through and see where it comes out. So, >> you've seen a lot of receivers step up recently just with people moving around and being injured. What have you seen from some of the guys that are getting more reps? >> Um, those guys are all doing a good job. You know, it's Yeah, we've had to bring in some new guys with some of the injuries, but I think collectively that group's done a good job. They're working. Um, you know, we've challenged those guys to step up and try to make more plays given the people that are out and just challenging those guys every day to, hey, look around. There's some guys missing. People got to step up and make plays. People got to step up and and own the playbook. Um, you know, the contin the continued challenge every day for those guys is we get to unscripted periods. How well do they know the offense? You know, how fast can they play without having a script and knowing what's coming. So, um, but I like where that group's at. They're working. It's going to be fun battle in preseason to see kind of where that thing shakes out. So, >> from guys like Pauling and and Grimes, uh, >> those guys are doing a good job. You know, those guys both undrafted guys who, you know, we're really pleased with where they're at. you know, they're they're both totally different guys in terms of their size and bodies, but they're tough, they're physical, they compete, they got a long way to go, too, just like, you know, most of our rookies. And so, but I'm happy with where they're at, and I like like how they compete every day. So, >> how is this >> how is this camp differentiated from McAffrey than any others besides him being out today? >> Um, I wouldn't say much. I mean, Christians always kind of has his rep count, you know, uh, in in any camp and, um, you know, we've, you guys are aware of the adjustments we've made to our schedule to kind of keep them from having too many off days, but um, you know, in terms of his rep load, he's we're we're right on track where we want to be. Um, and just, you know, he's he's a veteran player, so you got to monitor him and and get him ready for the first week. So, >> any any concern with him not being out there today, or is he just kind of managing? >> No, just managing. Uh, a little sore, but he's he's doing fine, so just kind of managing him as we go. How is that running back situation? I mean, your your top four guys are all, you know, dealing with something, including today. What What has that been like just kind of trying to cycle through and figure out what >> Yeah, I mean, it's it's twofold. It sucks because you want those young guys out there who we drafted and who we we want to see compete and want to see get better. Um, and those guys will get back out there, you know, they're they're not far away, but it's given guys opportunities to to get better, too. And you talk about guys like Patrick Taylor, Sincere McCormack, and Khalil, who we brought in. Uh, gives us a chance to get Debo in there a little bit and get some touches. So, and anytime guys are out, it it lets guys step up and uh gives them opportunities. But, you know, we're looking forward to having those guys back, too. And we want to get them out there and keep getting them better. So, so that's why they're here. >> Have you gotten a sense that Debo at 30 kind of what he could what he could do, kind of like touch count he could have? Um, you know, um, have you gotten any better sense of of maybe what could what his workload could be since he got here? >> Yeah, I mean, Debo's in great shape. First of all, he looks he looks really good to me in terms of where his body's at. Uh he can run all day. Um so no issues there. And Debo still looks like like Debo to me. I mean, when he has the ball in his hand, there's nobody more explosive, more dynamic on the field terms of managing his load. Like Debo's got to be able to affect the game in a lot of ways. And um that's our plan with him. And and he's going to keep, you know, being out a year. There's things he's still catching up on in the offense a little bit. Um but we're going to keep getting him the reps he needs and getting him ready to play a multitude of spots. and um you know being a versatile player. So I just feel really good about where he's at physically and um he's out there every day working and getting better. So it's all we can ask for. >> When you guys have a joint practice like this coming up uh tomorrow, what what type of guy are you looking to to see uh you know, a rookie, a secondyear guy, uh who will you have your your eye on? >> Man, I'm I'm not going to single out anybody, you know, um and say I'm this guy. I think there's a lot of young players on our team, a lot of offensive young players who we need to see where they're at, you know. Um, it's always good to go against a different opponent. You know, you don't really know the style of play they're going to have. It's just it's an adjustment, and you're going to see different defenses and different techniques, and you just want to see go guys go out there and play confident, play fast, and do their assignment. So, it's a good test to kind of see where we're at. Um, you know, all positions have guys we're evaluating closely. Um, and it's going to be a fun day. I'm looking forward to it. I love these days. I love going against somebody else. And um you know it should be fun. >> Clay, even when Brock was a rookie, guys would talk about like he'd snap at guys in the huddle and so even though he has this nice guy persona and everyone everyone realizes, you know, and has realized for a long time this is he has this other part to him. The other day he snapped at Watkins for doing something wrong. Um I don't know. Do you like given his kind of I guess stereotypical reputation, do you ever find this humorous uh when you see him or or is it just like no that's cool that's what we need from our leader? >> No, I I don't find as humorous. I I just I appreciate who Brock is as as a leader and as a guy. He's not a, you know, he's not a rahrh guy in terms of, you know, he he's bringing a lot of vocal energy every day, but he's he quietly goes about his business and he tries to hold people accountable. And yeah, Brock, he he'll snap. He'll he'll get on people. He'll get on himself probably more than anyone. Um, if you guys hear hear some things being said out there, it's probably him talking to himself a lot of the time, too, which you love that. A guy who's holding himself accountable. Um, but no, I mean, that's who he is. That's who he's always been. You mentioned it. from the day he got here, he he kind of had that personality and um that edge to him and we love it and it's what makes him a great competitor. So, not taking that away from him and and you know, I love that he's himself every day. So, >> when you think and consider the conversations about the work quote when it comes to Christian McCaffrey and then you have the younger guy, younger guys like you just mentioned that are missing some time. How much harder for it for a guy like Kalon Black does it make them to catch up this catch up to the system catch up to the style of play their first year they're not out there because of the joint pract for the joint practice I guess what I'm saying is how hard is it for them to kind of catch up as with this time missed as they season >> I mean it's a setback you know an injury is a setback no matter who it is you know and especially when you're a rookie and you're still learning the ropes and you're still going through everything the first time you you want to be out there and you want to be getting those reps So yeah, it's a setback, but Kalon specifically, he's he's the right kind of guy. He's made it the right stuff. He he prepares the right way. He's taking care of his body. He's out there at the walkthroughs. He's in the meetings. He's locked in. So he's doing everything he can do to keep himself ready to go when he's healthy and and he will be and and we have full confidence he'll be ready. So I'm not going to lie and say it's it's not not a problem. It's it's always a setback, but the good ones and pros will overcome that and they'll get themselves ready to go. So that's what we're looking for. with Striveling. I know you like to to work those guys at at all the positions and maybe it's too early, but has it kind of revealed itself yet where where you'd like to use him early on or is that still, you know, kind of a big >> Definitely still something that we're we're trying to see out there. We've only had him back out there for a couple days and so we're moving him around. Uh we're putting him outside, putting him inside, you know, doing different things with them, you know, giving them touches in different ways. So, we got to it's a lot of evaluation. So, to go the preseason's going to tell us a lot too about where he's at. So, the thing is challenge him every day, put him in new spots, and see how he handles it. Is >> he a little advanced in terms of just his ability to to handle everything that you're asking of him right now? >> Um, I I think so. I think that's why one of the reasons why we we really loved him coming out is he's he's very intelligent guy. Uh, football's smart. Um, it just absorbs football naturally. And so, that's that's why we love him. That's one of the reasons why we love him. And so, again, we're going to challenge him every day and see what he can handle. And um hopefully that that you know reveals itself down the line about kind of exactly where we want to put them. >> You mentioned Debo has to learn you know what he missed last year. Is that just every year in this offense or or was there more you know installing or whatever last year? >> Yeah. It's more like you know everything you tweak things year to year. You might change how you call a certain motion. You might change how you call formations. Um you might change how you call protections or like there's always little things that are changing and evolving. Uh, and when you're gone, when you miss a year, like that stuff you got to relearn. So, that's that's what I'm that's all I'm saying. It's just little things that he his his foundational understanding is really good, but there's little things that just you're relearning and that are maybe a little bit new this year. So, >> uh, Chris Fster said a couple weeks ago he thought you were the most prepared of the guys that have been in your role. And I think what he was saying was that you've come at a time when Kyle is delegating a little bit more. So, you're getting more opportunities than maybe a guy in your role would have 5 years ago. Do you feel that? Do you feel like you're getting more prepared um as you get this, you know, version of Kyle now that's in his 10th year here? >> Um, you know, I I try to prepare the same way all the time to be honest with you. Um, yeah, I think, you know, what Kyle's gone through has presented some new challenges and some some new areas where I've had to step up and and and be ready in certain areas. But to be honest with you, my mindset has never changed in terms of how I prepare, uh, what I'm putting, you know, my brain through every day to be ready to call plays, um, to install the offense, to communicate with players. I I I truly think of that's that's my job every day. And whether Kyle does it on the field or he doesn't, I put myself through those those stresses, too, just so I'm ready for it. So, um, you know, I I I'm grateful for all the opportunities that Kyle's given me. and then yeah in step and just being ready in these moments when he hasn't been around as much but um my mindset's really focus on the same thing every day. So >> on Hard Knocks they showed this Seahawk Super Bowl rings which are are fairly obnoxious. Have you seen your brother? >> Uh I've seen a picture of it and it's really big. But yeah, good for them. That's it's a cool ring and um hopefully we can get one of those here pretty soon. >> Thanks coach. >> All right. Appreciate it, guys. the second time around and then you're with a new defensive coordinator. What have you liked about this this training camp and what's been different for you this time around? >> Um I just feel with Raheem, he's allowing us to be more aggressive um play to our skill set um in the defensive back group. Um, and I just feel it's allowing us to use our skills. >> A lot of your position mates have talked about how this new scheme has allowed you to play faster and freer. What What do you see as the simplification of your job? >> Um, I just feel it's specific for everybody. Um, it's making it um for us to just not think and just allowing us to be playmakers. Um, and I just feel that's better for us. Um, I feel we have the type of guys to just go out there and play and not react. There's some ups and downs in your first year. What are you taking out of training camp this year? >> Um, just to be me. Um, just to go out there, um, do the plays that they want me to make, uh, or make the plays that they want me to make, um, and do my job and make sure I'm protecting the back end. >> Played a lot of snaps early on last year, started the first eight games, and then you didn't come back in uh, into a full-time role until that that Eagles game. Um, and you had a a really a great game in that uh, in that playoff game. Do you feel like the the time you spent away or you were on the bench ended up being valuable in the in the long run? >> Um, I'm not going to say it was valuable, but I took it as valuable. Um, just for me to learn myself, um, learn what I needed to work on, learn what the coaches wanted me to work on, and just when I got that another chance to be ready for it. >> Do you remember what exactly it was that you were working on? >> U, I feel I just always was in the right spot, but just had to make the play. And so that mindset in practice and film study is just to be one step ahead instead of one step behind. >> Are you a little bit bigger this year? Looks like you put on a little bit of weight. >> Um, yeah, I gained a little bit of weight. I gained about I'll say 8 to 10 pounds since last year. >> Did you feel like that was a missing kind of piece last year? >> Um, no. I just felt it was better for my skill set being more a true safety. um just for blocks, dealing with tight ends, just to be more physical and fit my speed um and be at a weight where I can still keep my speed. >> Is there anything specific that you worked on during the offseason to prepare you for this? >> I'll just say film study u and working on my breaks. Um being in the post, um make sure I'm getting in and out of my breaks. everybody you leaned on in the locker room a little bit more this off season to understand the system here and like how to kind of better display your skill set and what you needed to do coming into this season. >> Um I'll say I take um a little bit from everybody. RG um just how he played man, how aggressive he is. Demo just how smart he is with the break points. Um Jier Brown just how he's getting out of his breaks in the post. Um Malik Mustafa just how he's in and out of his breaks. Um, so it just throughout the whole offseason I just took one piece from each eye. >> Did you hear guys talking about Dre Green Law in the locker room last year and and what's it been like now seeing him in practice? >> Oh yeah, they always talked about just how aggressive he was, especially when we was going against the Broncos last year in the first joint practice. They just said, "Oh yeah, he going to bring it, so we better bring it." Um, so we love that he's back with us. Um, and we love the aggression he brings to the team. He wakes guys up if they waking or they come in in the morning tired. So he brings that energy for us, what we need for the defense. and um and he's going to go out there and um make plays. You >> feel like you already knew him a little bit when you met him for the first time just because what you'd heard about him? >> Most definitely. Just cuz his energy never left. His energy never left. Um he stayed in this room. Um even though he wasn't here. >> How does he wake guys up? >> Um if he sees sleepy eyes, he's coming up to shaking, shouting. He's come he making sure you awake just because he knows he's going to bring that energy. He wants to he expects the most from you. >> What is Jerry Graven like as a coach? amazing. Um he's taken my football IQ to another level. Um just what he brings, just his wisdom, his ball knowledge. Um just learning it bit by bit. >> Like a father figure as well. >> Definitely. Definitely. We laughing there, we joking there, but it's time to be serious when it's time to be serious. >> Has he simplified the game for you? Like what you're seeing when you're out there? >> Um definitely say he's definitely simplifying the game, making it way easier. I feel that's where we are able to make more plays because Jerry's trying to simplify it the best for each guy just for them. So, he's definitely been a big improvement with that. >> We haven't uh we haven't seen Malik Mustafa on the field in a couple weeks because of the hamstring. Is he in meetings and what's the relationship with with you guys and and him right now? >> Um yes, he's still in meetings. Um I don't know his schedule and all that. So, I can't really speak on that. >> All good guys. >> Is he a guy that you've leaned on also? >> Um yes. Um he's been in the system for three years. So, I just take um the little bits I get from him, just his balls. I'm always asking him questions. We always talking, seeing what he sees, what I see, just comparing notes. >> Well, good. >> All right. Thanks, Maris. >> Thank you. Forester, he's mentioned a bunch of times how big of a step you've taken, how much slower the game is for you. How does it feel? This is now year three, but how does it feel for you out there? You said you when it came to getting better, you really focused in on doing those this off season. >> Yeah, I feel a lot better. Um, a lot more comfortable this year just trusting. I feel like halfway through the second or my second year on, you know, I kind of found something that works for me. Um, you know, my rookie year, I mean, he he's right. I was kind of just flying by like just doing what I did in college and it was working. Um, so the second year some guys get some tape on you and they kind of realize where your weaknesses are. So I I think I spent maybe half the year just trying to find something that worked for me in my second year. So, um, you know, I found something later on that season and I came in, really attacked it in the offseason and, um, worked with coach Fister and, uh, we just been getting better at it ever since, and I feel a lot more comfortable knowing that, you know, I have a technique that I can go to. I have a couple things, a couple counters that I know. Um, so I just feel a lot better. >> The knee injury last preseason sort of maybe hamper that ability to get up to speed early in the year that you >> I don't know. It's impossible to tell because like I said, there's there's a lot of things I still need to work on the first half of the season. So whether the knee impacted me or not, it didn't really impact my technique as much. Um maybe athletically, maybe. I don't know. I don't think it did too much though, honestly. >> At what point in the season did you feel like yourself where it wasn't an impact on your play? >> Um I couldn't really tell you like a week I felt like myself cuz like in the season you just you never really feel too good. Um >> I don't know. I couldn't really give you a week, but just like I said, technique-wise like I don't know. some halfway point through the season, I just kind of found something that worked and just kept working at it. >> When you say like in effect guys kind of maybe figured a defensive lineman, you know, could study you and figure you out to some degree. Were you ever surprised last year like beginning of the season like this used to work? What's going on? You know, was it surprising? >> Uh, [sighs] you know, like a coach tells you like, man, like you keep doing that, man, you're probably not going to get away with it too much longer. like if it's working like in my head like you're just going to be you're just going to keep doing it and like it's it's hard to listen when something's working but then when it stops working that's when you you really start listening to coaching and like you got to find something else to do. You can't keep doing this and getting away with it. Um so yeah just like I said just keep working on technique >> first like ever say I told you so. No, he didn't say it, but uh you know he he's so smart. He he seen so much players and so much ball like he knows what's not going to work in the future and if if you keep doing this it's just it's not going to pan out. Um so you know he kept harping on me every week and you know as towards the end of my first year actually just it started not to look too good and then beginning of second year kind of trended the same direction. So I was like you know something's got to change and um so I really worked with him a lot and um continued to the offseason now training camp. I know these are like top secret things, but can you give us any insight into kind of what you were doing that I don't know, maybe Dance Alignment had a book on all of a sudden? >> Uh, yeah, you're good. >> He give you a list of things to work on or like film to watch, things to do. >> Uh, I mean, it's just every week you watch the film from the game and you write down your notes, you look back at it and it's Boom, boom, boom. There's a progression. You fix one thing, there goes another. You fix that thing, maybe this thing comes back and bites you, maybe another thing appears. It's like it's just like a head game with the D lineman and like there just counters everything. And um when you get in that game, it it can get kind of ugly. But when you really find something that works for you, that's when you can really try to elevate your game. >> You started watching film of Aaron Donald yet, >> huh? >> Aaron Donald yet? >> No, I have not started watching film yet. Are you curious to see what it would be like since you didn't get to face him when before he retired? >> Yeah, I mean, yeah, he's probably the greatest D lineman of all time. So, I mean, yeah, it' be pretty cool to go against him. >> What have you seen from Alfred Collins coming back this in his second year? >> Uh, I see a lot, man. I see a lot of growth. You know, he's just getting back out there and, you know, I had the knee last year, so I know how it kind of feels to be a little rusty and um but you can tell like even today he was working some really good moves. Um, just getting more comfortable with his timing. Um I'm excited to see him in year two just be an absolute like guy in the run game and um just keep working on some pass rush moves. >> A lot of first and second year guys at defensive tackle on this team you go against them every day. Um what have you seen from that group? Um you know who among them have kind of uh impressed you so far? >> Uh Edge and Inter. >> No just you know >> just inter you know Grayson Halton the two undrafted rookies. um Valdez from last year. >> Yeah. No, I mean Grayson Halton has some juice to him. You know, he's obviously a big body that can that can move side to side. He's agile. Um I'm excited to see what he can bring to this team. Um Valdez, I think he's I think he's going to take a step this year. I think he went through a lot of work in his rookie year. Um just grinding uh his practice squad, but just getting those reps and team he never took a day off. He always made me better. He's probably he's probably my favorite guy to go against um like during scout team week. Um he's just he's just a good opponent to go against in practice. Um but he's I think he's starting to put it together. He's he's really figuring it out. >> He would give he would push you um during the scout team practices. >> Yeah. Yeah. He does a really good job and he actually will uh get some pretty good looks on like what the D lineman during the week is going to do. Um you know, he takes a lot of pride in that. So I was very happy with the looks he was giving me during the year. How much of an impact can Osa Dazua make in the game? >> A big impact, man. He's he's super strong. Um he'll he'll set the edge on the inside. Like he won't let me he won't let a guy like reach him and just and just keep blocking him, you know? He's going to get vertical. He's going to set the edge on like the B gap edge. Um and he can pass rush. I think I think he was like leading the league in pressures from interior. I don't know if that's true. I don't know. I think I heard that. But uh you know, it shows in practice like he he's a very strong guy. He'll push the pocket. um he's hard to get his hands on and and keep them on him. Um so I'm excited to see what he can do this year. >> Feeling like um four or five down front is going to help you guys practice and prepare for different looks during the season. >> Yeah, I mean I think uh a lot of the teams in the league are training towards that defense. Um I feel like we saw it a lot last year. Um so you know I'm excited. My first two years was um uh Sorenson and Salah. So that you know that four down jet um get off the ball 43 that was pretty much all been going against all camp. So you know it's fun to do this this year because you know like there's teams in our division that run that defense. Um a lot of teams we'll see this year run that same defense. So I'm excited. >> How would you describe Brock's leadership style? >> Man, he's just a guy. I feel like every time you guys ask me it's like it's just in my answer never changes. He's a guy, man. Like he he gets in the huddle. He commands the huddle. Um he never waivers. know any bad play in practice, he's just on to the next play. It's like he didn't even talk about that play. Um, you know, he's always keeping us energized in the huddle and just make sure we work. If we if someone messes up, you know, he's on them. Um, so I can't ask any more of Brock as a leader. >> You mentioned by the end of your rookie year it wasn't quite as good and then it starts your second year that way. Did you ever have like a I don't know um affect your confidence? Like did you ever wonder, oh shoot, maybe I'm not as as good as I thought or you know these thoughts start going through your head. >> Yeah. Yeah, for sure. That's normal I think for any player um who's had a lot of success. You know, I had a lot of success in college and my rookie year and you know, when it starts to fade a little bit, you start to kind of question yourself like, you know, have you been figured out? Like, can you even come back from this or like can you like can you get better? And you know, the challenges like it just hit me throughout the season. You just stop thinking so much and just go do what you do. Um, whatever you need to do, what that technique is, do what you're coach. And if you get beat doing what you're coached, I mean, it's the defense guy just got you. like you get got in this league, but I think it's just you got to keep sticking to the fundamentals and just keep doing what you know. >> I realized Carver Willis was out for a little bit, but uh he's back now. What's your early impression just since he's been in the building of the young kid? He's been going, you know, from guard to guard spot and trying to learn everything. >> Yeah. No, it's not easy in this offense. You know, he's he's learning guard both guards and center. Um and as a rookie, I don't know if centering this offense is not easy. So, you know, you get a lot a lot of credit to Brendle because he he rarely messes up calls in the season. Um he just does a great job all the time. Um so for Carter to have a vet like that in the room um that he can ask any question to is amazing and um seeing him at guard, man, he he's talented kid. Um he he he's very developed coming in for a rookie. Um he's just got to learn the playbook and he's doing a good job of it and just keep working, just keep getting reps. >> What's Debo Samuel's energy like in the in the puddle and on the field? I mean, you guys know Debo is it's the same in the locker room. It's the same on Sundays. It's he's just Debo. Like he came back in the locker room just he just started yelling everyone's name and like it was just good to see him. Good to have him back. He's like I think he's like two lockers down for me my rookie year and um you know I I miss his energy in the locker room and it's good to have him back. >> You in a different spot now? >> No. No. Yeah, he is in a different spot now. Yeah. Yeah. Sadly. Can you tell? I don't know if you can tell during the game, but certainly when you watch film. >> How would you describe Christian's vision um what he sees, what's available, what he makes out of it. >> This camp in the game >> with McAffrey. Yeah. During the game, >> I mean, his vision's unreal. Um he he sees the gap opening before it's even there. Like he he just has such a feel for it because, you know, he's played so many so many years and so many reps stacked under his belt. Um it's hard for me to describe his vision. I don't really know what he sees out there, but um he does a good job hitting the gaps and he's he's starting to hit it full speed now and you know he he feels really good this year. >> Are there any plays that come to mind that you think you remember watching maybe on film going up? I don't know how we >> No, no, not one that like comes to mind, but I mean he makes a lot of great plays. Um but no, not not one like I don't like remember. I'm always it's hard to like remember in the game because I'm just trying to block my guy. So yeah. >> I know you're a stuff guy. There was some smoke that LeBron was maybe going to come to the Warriors, too. Did you want to see that happen or you kind of >> Yeah, I did want to see that happen. Yeah. But now it's not going to happen now. So, I'm kind of sad about that and like to see Steph get somebody alongside him to, you know, is what it is. I'm not a GM or a coach. So, I'm a Steph fan. You know, I love him. So, maybe we'll get someone else. Anybody in >> particular in mind if you had like a dream scenario? >> That's a good question. If I was a Warriors GM, I don't even know anymore. I think it was all it was either Brian or nothing. Maybe Brian AD, but it was a fever dream. So, yeah. >> Yeah. Thank you guys.

title: Members of the San Francisco 49ers Players Address the Media Following Day 9 of Camp | 49ers
text: that, so I've just picked and choose a little bit more, but as far as the film and everything being out there for all the practice periods of going against each other, um those are to me the most important things in my job, and I've been able to do those every day. >> Is it your intention to [clears throat] coach the first preseason game next week, or is that still kind of TBD? >> Oh, yeah. No, I'm doing the same stuff, guys. I just um I try not to come in here every single day cuz I feel if I did, that would that would take I want to be able to pull off my normal routine, which is watching hours and hours of tape and getting to the walk-through, and I even be able to watch stuff after that. Um eventually I will get there. I would have told you I was there 7 days ago, and they're like, "Just chill. Wait to see how you feel tomorrow." And then I wake up the next morning, I'm like, "Damn, I'm glad I didn't say that cuz sometimes it's a good day, and then sometimes the next day is a little bit harder." But as far as the stuff that I think is the most important parts of my job, uh I've been doing that since day one. >> What's been your impression, Kyle, 2 weeks in of the of the team overall from your perspective on the field? >> Um I mean, I I I like our I like our team, you know, I feel like we came into this camp um better on paper than we did last year. Um just with a number of rookies we were depending on last year got to play more, and I love the guys that we've added this year. Um by no means do I, you know, see how we are come week one. We still got a lot of work to do. I mean, some days we take a step forward, the next day we take two steps back, um but that's training camp. And a number of the guys that we really want to push to work with, those guys aren't always out there. Um so, just find through those things. >> Such a grinder for so long, is it weird having a a bit of an abbreviated schedule for yourself? >> It is. I mean, I was a little insecure about it at first. I mean, I've been a guy, like all of us are, that you could be deathly sick and we're still insecure to go home. Um so, that's kind of just how we are. So, it was hard on me. but when I saw kind of the results of some of it, it became easier. Um what people tell you is kind of right. I was like, "Yeah, all right. I'll be able to tough through that." And you kind of can't tough through anything, but then then when you pay for it the next day and you're not as good at something else, you start to be like, "All right. I didn't have to tough through that cuz it made me worse the next day. So, those are the things I've had to learn a little bit to be better at. >> You watch practice now from like kind of deep middle. It's a different perspective. Do you enjoy it? Do you like it? Is there anything that you see in the deep middle next to Lynch that maybe you didn't see when you're up behind the quarterbacks? >> Um a little bit. I mean, sometimes it's harder to find the quarterback. Sometimes it's harder to find the running back. They just pop, but you can see the holes and how everything develops. I mean, that's where I watch it throughout games all the time. Um wherever I am on the field, I'm always about 30 yards away from the line of scrimmage so I can see it, and I'm So, I got to stand on both sides during games, so I'm used to that. Um things look backwards a lot to me when I'm sitting right in the middle there, but um I like to be more on the offensive side. That's the perspective I like, and um I always like to talk to the quarterbacks and things like that, which you can do more, but it's been good to be able to communicate with Raheem back back there and see it from a little different angle. >> Well, I can ask two questions. Um we used to have For starters, how long is the mustache going to be with you? >> It's day-to-day. It's probably not going to stick. Eventually, too many questions about it, I'll probably get rid of it pretty fast. It's something I always have in the summer. My friends have been trying to challenge me to keep it for like the last 4 years, and I always shave it the first day back, but once they all started joking that it saved my life in the crash, I felt like I owed it a little bit longer, so I'm just going to keep it a little bit longer. >> Um next question is I want you to feel comfortable, so I wouldn't injury question. Get you back in your routine. But as far as Bosa, you know, taking off last week due to soreness, is there any reason for concern there? >> Um no. I mean, I never, you know, he was doing great, and then he got sore just um going through some of the individuals. So, I mean, you wish that didn't happen. Um but no, there's no concern. No worries something's happened that um is a big setback or anything, but we'll wait until that soreness goes away and evaluate and why the soreness has happened, and um but I still feel pretty good about that. >> As I was saying the other day, how are you mad at yourself for get getting in the situation? >> Yeah, I mean, anytime you cause an accident that can be avoided, you feel pretty stupid. I mean, especially when you have a chance to hurt someone else. And so, like, I mean, I think you get mad when you get a ticket at yourself. So, So, it's kind of the same. You know, things that you know, I think everyone's done to a degree what I've done. But, um you know, dropping a phone and falling all the way to my back seat where I have to fully take my eyes off the road, you know, it's something that I normally want to do. I've had autopilot for 9 years, so I'm pretty comfortable with it. And um you know, who knows what happened when I turned around, whether it malfunctioned or whether I knocked it off. That's something I don't know yet. Um but, regardless, that's it is always your fault, whether you're in autopilot or not. You can't take your eyes off the road. Um it's a partnership driving. You don't just turn it over to a computer. And um it's a good lesson on no matter how comfortable I am with that that I believe someday could save my life or someone else's or um it's really helped me have perspective on that stuff. >> As a leader of this >> team, obviously, you're asking your players and your coaches to be responsible. title: 49ers DE Nick Bosa Dealing With ACL Tendinitis
text: What's up? Welcome to 49ers after dark presented by prize picks as Jesse Naylor. I'm Grant Con. We got about a half show for you today. I'm still down in Santa Clair. What do you think of this news? >> Yeah, it's interesting because I feel like you have to almost force the 49ers hand to give you information. It took all of us speculating. Oh, maybe he wants a new contract. I bet you it's a new contract. Bosa wants a new contract. And finally they're like, "Oh yeah, great practice. A lot of great news to report. Nobody else is injured. Bosa is out for week to week." I It's Every single time this happens, they can never be forthright. You have to force it out of them. It's not surprising though and I would say, you know, with the contract issues or or perceived contract issues that could have been there and then now you look at this injury in place, I think the contract would be the lesser of two evils. If Nick Bosa was fully healthy and wanted a rework deal, yeah, I probably wouldn't give it to him. Yes, it would be a pain in the butt, but at least you know that he's healthy. Tendonitis, he hasn't even put a lot of pressure on that ACL in practice. He didn't do any of the 11 on 111 stuff. He didn't put on pads. He didn't hard practice. And now he's week to week, which tells me, Grant, he most likely is just going to show up and be asked to play week one without any real conditioning, without any real testing of that knee. And I don't know how well that's going to go. >> Well, I mean, it didn't go so well in training camp, and he didn't even play. He did individual drills, which is like >> doing scales on the uh piano. It's just getting warmed up. And we thought maybe he shut himself down because he showed how healthy he is and he wanted to leverage that against the 49ers. But it turns out like it's even worse. It's it's been almost a year and his knee is still bothering him. And it's not the first time he's torn his ACL. It's not the second time he's torn his ACL. It's his second ACL tear in this knee. >> And he's almost 30. And um he couldn't even get to the one-on- ones in 11on1 section of training camp. This is really disconcerting because he's been slowly declining since 2022. Every year he's been a little bit worse. Last year he basically didn't play because he just broke, you know, fell apart. And now it's like should we really expect him to have another durable dominant season ever again? Or is he sort of becoming like his older brother? >> Well, and one thing that we we talked about during the whole angle of is it the contract situation, is it not? is the simple fact that either way the 49ers are on the hook for a Nick Bosa who's going to be 30 years old and is gonna account for like 54 million against their cap next year. One way or another, they have to rework that deal. They have to move on from Nick Bosa. They have to extend Bosa. title: The Good and Not So Good from Day 11 of 49ers Training Camp
text: The 49ers just wrapped up day 11 of training camp, which was a joint practice against the Tennessee Titans. Here's who stood out. Keep in mind that after practice, head coach Kyle Shanahan said Nick Bosa is dealing with knee tendinitis that is related to his ACL recovery. More on Bosa in a minute. The good wide receiver Dejon Stribbling. He outplayed Titans rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate, who was the fourth pick in the draft. Tate didn't catch many passes, and when he did make a catch, he often had to lay out as opposed to dribbling, who caught a team high seven passes during 11on1 team drills and caught them in stride. He was Brock Pery's go-to guy, particularly outside the red zone, where dribbling speed stretches the field and stresses defenses. Quarterbacks give him such a big cushion, which opens up underneath routes for him. He's a terrific compliment for Demarcus Robinson, who's more of a possession receiver and red zone specialist. Stribbling isn't currently a huge threat in the red zone, but he could develop that part of his game in time. Expect him to get a ton of playing time and targets this season as long as he's healthy. Wide receiver Demarcus Robinson. He's not particularly fast, but he's big and tough and dependable, similar to Jawan Jennings. Robinson is also fearless over the middle. He has a big catch radius, and he's at his best in the end zone where he made two catches today. Theoretically, Mike Evans can do all these things even better, but he's been injured for most of camp while Robinson hasn't missed a day. Don't be surprised if Robinson outproduces Evans this season simply because Evans is older and breaking down. Tight end Jake Tongis. It's funny when the Niners practice against themselves, Tonis often is an afterthought for whatever reason. Maybe the coaches want to see what other players can do. But today, in a competitive practice against another team during which Christian McCaffrey is not participating, suddenly Tandis is Pertie's security blanket. Today, he caught multiple passes downfield. He needs to be a constant fixture in the offense this year, even after George KD comes back, because KD is coming off a torn Achilles and won't be able to carry the offense the way he has in the past. Quarterback Brock Pury, he shredded a talented defense while missing a starting running back, a starting tight end, and two starting wide receivers. With the exception of one day, Pertie has been lights out in training camp as opposed to Titans quarterback Cam Ward, who never seemed to know where he wanted to go with the football. Safety Gier Brown. He undercut and intercepted a pass over the middle thrown by Cam Ward. Brown isn't the fastest safety and he has a troubling tendency of giving up long catches over his head, but he also breaks confidently on passes in front of him as he did on this play. Unfortunately, after the play, he ran over to Cam Ward, mockingly handed him the ball and got flagged for taunting. In fairness to Brown, he doesn't make good plays that often, so he was excited. Quarterback Renardo Green. He's not going to intercept passes, and he will get beaten by practice wide players occasionally during one-on-one drills, but he's also the cornerback on the 49ers who's best suited to match up with number one wide receivers because of his size and speed. And today he used those traits to shut down rookie first round pick Carnell Tate. We've also seen Green shut down Pro Bowlers such as Devonte Adams as recently as last year. Green clearly raises his game when it matters. [clears throat] Quarterback Jacob Robinson. He made a diving interception on a pass thrown by Will Levis. Robinson is the Niners's most intriguing young quarterback. He has an outside chance to make the 53man roster if he has a strong preseason. Linebacker Jaden Duggar. The Niner starting defense started practice using a fiveman front with Duggar standing on the line of scrimmage as the third linebacker. This is the look the Niners want to use against two tight end formations this season. And Duggar is the key to it because he's built like a defensive end and yet he played safety in college. So he's a hybrid player. He can set the edge against the run and drop into coverage as well. He just might start right away. Left guard Carver Willis. He returned yesterday from a concussion and instantly became the second string left guard, which means he's one injury or benching away from becoming the starter. as opposed to Connor Kby who has been demoted to backup right guard behind Dominic Puny. I expect Willis will finish the season as a starting left guard because the current starter is Robert Jones and he's a veteran stop gap who won't be on the team next year. The not so good Nick Bosa. He still hasn't practiced or shown up to practice since last Monday. Today, Kyle Shanahan revealed that Bosa is suffering from knee tendinitis that is related to his latest ACL rehab. Shanahan said that tendinitis is common during these recoveries. Still, it seems Bose's injury is worse than the Niners initially let on. And that's a problem because he essentially is their pass rush. The Niners should trade him before the season starts if they can find a taker. Maybe they can trade him to the Raiders straight up for Max Crosby. Running back Christian McAffrey, he missed his second practice in a row with tightness. Shanahan said McAffry's injury is nothing to be worried about, but that's what he said two years ago when calf tightness ended McCaffry's training camp early and eventually caused him to miss the first eight games of the season. And just today, Bosa's soreness magically became knee tendinitis. It's impossible to know what's really going on with McCaffrey and how severe his issue truly is. I guess we'll find out soon enough. Wide receiver Mike Evans, he suited up for practice but didn't actually compete against the Titans. He watched dribbling and Robinson compete and play well. Two years ago, Evans was way better than those two. Now he moves around as if everything hurts.

title: Instant Analysis of the 49ers' Joint Practice with the Titans

Then on defense, it was interesting. No Bosa, no pass rush. What were the 9ers going to do on defense? And what they did was tackle. Hit the Titans really freaking hard. Knock them down. Maybe the 9ers were were toughening up the Titans or maybe the Titans were learning some discipline. Either way, um didn't learn much. It's the freaking Titans and the 9ers. But what I did I mean, we know we know the 9ers can't run the ball without Christian McCaffrey. And the fact that he missed two days in a row with tightness after a day off is giving me um you know, uh flashbacks of 2024 when he missed like nine games because of tightness. So, I don't know.
