title: 49ers REACTION: New rookie AND a new position emerges...
text: I just met with the 49ers coaching staff here at the facility. And how's this for a development at the wide receiver competition? Listen to Leonard Hankerson talk about the rookie Will Pauling. >> He's the hammer, you know, in the running game, right? He's probably the I'm not right now. He's been the most physical receiver. I tell you that much. really, >> you know, as far as in the blocking game, you know, putting his hat on folks, finishing, not only putting his hat on him and and falling off, it's easy to do that, but no matter if he's going up against a DN, a linebacker, or DB, he's been sustaining blocks, you know, and that shows up a lot. And in the past game, he got to continue to work as well. You know, I've been impressed with him that he's shown some speed, uh, shown some ability to make the play, but he has to continue to work on his technique as far as not slipping. fell down a couple times, you know, and uh we'll keep working him there and and I can't wait to see him take a step there. >> The hammer. Love that term. I also love the feverback position. That is a new defensive position name for the 49ers that KJ Wright can tell us about. >> Why is it called feverback? >> Yo, honestly, because the way I interpret this, it's you're so inter like you're it's a sick position. like you're you're off the ball, you're on the ball, you get a fever, you're sick. So, it's a sick position to be and you're not just a micro wheel. Like you're a sick man. It's like you [laughter] can do so many things. That's >> a football sicko, right? >> It's a football stick. It's a sick position that you want to be a part of cuz you can just be in space on the ball, stack back. So, that's how I interpret it. >> You were. So, a lot of exciting things happening for the 49ers schematically under the new defensive coordinator, Raheem Morris. But first, back to the hammer because we can talk about Jaden Duggar, who obviously is a candidate for that feverback position at much greater length. I think the big surprise coming out of today's meeting is Will Pauling, the rookie out of Notre Dame, just 5'9, but apparently has been impressing the 49ers with his physicality ever since the pads have come on. And remember that the 49ers were second to worst in the NFL in terms of explosive run rate last year. And most of the blame could be placed on the fact that the receivers were not blocking as well as they normally do. So, the 49ers have sought to improve that and maybe Will Polling can beat out a Jacob Cowing, maybe he can beat out Jordan Watkins, maybe he can beat out Junior Bergen because of the toughness that he might bring to the table. Along those lines, the 49ers top pick this past season and one of their top receivers already is Dejon Stribbling. And we've gotten so many different nuggets about why the 49ers liked him, why he stood out above those who were picked to go ahead of him in mock drafts, why many teams, it sounds like, according to Adam Shfter's report a couple weeks ago, many teams have thought that Dejon Stribbling was the best receiver in this draft. Well, the 49ers just gave us another reason why they fell in love with Dejon Stribbling. Listen to Hankerson on the pre-draft process. >> And I can tell right away, you know, Stril was the type of player that we wanted here. You know, the IQ level, you can see it. the recall that he had when I talked to him about plays you, you know, the personality, you know, when you turn on the tape, you know, in the running game and, you know, he's going up against uh >> uh Bane over there in in at at Miami now with the Bucks and certain guys and he's playing against Georgia and they putting him on his tail and then he popping up and he's putting his face in there again. Yeah. >> I knew, you know, he was the type of player that we we wanted in our receiver room, you know, who can who can fit right in. So, uh, he's been nothing but, you know, a standup guy. >> Did you say Ruben Bane? He he went against >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. That's a couple times. You see it on tape, you know, and, uh, it it it was good to see, you know, >> what were they asking him to do? >> They was asking him like to cross sift. >> Oh, okay. >> You know, he line up on one side of the ball and then go across the and and and sift the end, you know, and I mean, I'm not saying it worked in his favor, [laughter] you know, but he he he would not turn it down. He would not turn it down, you know. So, uh, when you see guys like that on tape, you know, script what had 800, 900 yards, you know, as a receiver, you know, pick 33 and you going in there sticking your face on on top five DNS or first round DNS, >> you know, it speaks a lot about you. >> Ruben Bane is 263 pounds, pick number 15 overall in the first round of the 2026 NFL draft. And when the 49ers saw Dejon shribbling trying to cross sift Ruben Bane, when they saw him not back down, even though he got knocked down, he still wanted a piece of Ruben Bane who's got a good 40 to 50 pounds on him. They said, "This is our type of guy." Because, you know, it's not just about the blocking, even though that's so so important to how the 49ers run this offense. It's about making tough catches over the middle. It's about the courage required to play wide receiver in the National Football League. One thing that we're seeing at practice right now is that Dejon dribbling is catching footballs everywhere. Not dropping anything. He only dropped one pass last year at Old Miss. Jordan Watkins, however, yesterday he dropped one coming over the middle. Looked to be a a place where it could be a little bit contested. We could put it that way. where it could take a little bit of toughness to hang on to the football. And I know that the pads are on, but we're not seeing the 49ers bring players down to the ground yet. So, it's not quite as difficult as it's going to be once these preseason games start on Thursday. But you could still get a gauge of who is making the tough catches over the middle, who can be trusted in those situations and who cannot be trusted in those situations. And I would say right now, Dejon Stribbling has established himself as a receiver who can be trusted in those situations. And some of the clues that the 49ers got didn't even come on pass plays over the course of college football. The game when Miss was playing against Miami and we saw Dejon Stribbling cross sift Ruben Bane get knocked down but get back up because he was straining to get things done. So, the 49ers have a tough tough wide out on their hands. All right, I'm going to flip it back over to the defensive side of the football. The feverback position emblematic of a shifting 49ers defense under Raheem Morris. the other day he said that Upton Stout is this team's starting star, which is a nickel quarterback, but somebody who's also playing linebacker who's playing safety who's roving around the back end of the defense. >> Stout can play whatever he wants. You know, Stout can play linebacker. Stout can play safety. Stout can play corner. You know, right now he is our starting star. He's our starting nickel. and u him going out there playing at a very high level with his hand uses his ability to get up to the pass rushes his ability to pass rush his ability to use us short space quickness um defend anything whether it be zone whether it be man um highly competitive young man um stays angry every single day I love him like he's um he's got the mindset of a football player and he's got the mentality of a football player and he certainly has the movement the skill set of a football player and then to just talk about being versatile with guys I think we kind of did that a little bit you know switched to corners with Demo and Ronaldo made those guys go opposite, make JackJ Jack play opposite, you know, making those guys, you know, whether it be Son playing a little bit of safety, being able to play corner, you're creating versatility across the board because you just never know what happened in the game. You know, Demo playing inside a little bit for us the other day, being able to do some different things for us. You know, when things happen in the game, something goes out through the course of the game, you want to be able to have an answer and it's our job as coaches to have an answer for our head coach when something goes wrong, what we going to do and what our plan is. May not be the right plan, may not be the right decision, but you better have one. Well, feverback is the nickname given to the linebacker who's a similarly adaptable rover. The ultimate goal, and KJ Wright is going to get into all of this, is to create a sense of amorphousness on the back end that opposing offenses who have seen their adaptability reach stratospheric levels over the past decade. I mean, Christian McAffrey is playing all over the formation. The goal is to develop the true antidote to these amorphous offenses. And when you look at the 49ers linebacker level, somebody like Jaden Duggar has already played both stack and outside linebacker at practice. And he even was inserted into the edge rusher group, the defensive end group for one practice a few days ago. What did Duggar take out of his day working with the edge rushers? >> Yeah, it was um it was good for him. It was really good for him. Like when you take a linebacker, this happened to me in Seattle. I got I was mad. But you take a linebacker, hey, you a linebacker, linebacker, linebacker, and I go with the D line, you know, your mind shifts kind of shift like first thing is like why? No, like why are you moving me? Why are you touching me? But it was good for Duggar for a day. Go down there with Chris Casser, you know, learn pass rushing, learn setting the edge, right? because I could see like down the future. Hey, we lose a guy on third down, Dger, go rush the quarterback. You did it in college, go rush the quarterback. So, that's when I talk about versatility as far as what a guy can do. And um you know, when you first introduce it to him, you're like, hold up, I'm a linebacker. Why am I going with Cass? But in in the long run, it be really good for him. It's great to ask KJ Wright about Jaden Duggar because KJ was a 6'4 linebacker, an abnormally tall linebacker for the Seattle Seahawks. So, he understands the challenges and the benefits that a very tall linebacker can get. Somebody like Jaden Duggar has got a wingspan of 7 feet, the longest wingspan I think in NFL history for a stack linebacker. His wingspan's even longer than Alden Smith's. and Alden Smith obviously played edge rusher for the 49ers, but there's a reason why the 49ers are interested in getting Jaden Duggar in on that edge rushing action. Well, the cool thing about this that because the the position lines are becoming more and more blurred with the 49ers defense, I can ask multiple position coaches about the same player because they're all getting a chance to crossrain that one player. So I asked KJ Wright about Jaden Duggar at the edge and naturally I moved over to the 49ers Dline coach Chris Caceric right after that. >> You had the Duggar in your room for for a day or at least for a practice. How what was that like getting somebody who'd been working exclusively with linebackers and and what do you think he took out of that? >> Yeah. Well, you know, we we brought him here to be a linebacker, but he also, you know, showed a lot of versatility in college and um you know, just being real, we were we were low at numbers at DN that day. It's something that we kind of planned anyway, but then we were low in numbers, so we found, you know, that day was going to be a really good day for him to come help us out. You know, we met with him the day before and kind of explained what we're thinking. and you know just being able to utilize his versatility on game day cuz we've gotten into pinches where we've you know two guys have gone out and [clears throat] next thing you know we're moving DT tackles out to play DN and you know throughout my 17 years I've seen a lot of crazy stuff where we've you know almost been out of had one DN left to finish a game and you know you got 320 lb guys out there playing on the edge to try to finish a game. So with him, you'd hope that that that would never, you know, happen. Like, hey, Duggar, we've used you in practice. Probably won't be the last time we do it. Like, uh, you know, we we we've shown you the techniques and the skills and for you to go set edges in the run game. You're doing it as an onthe- ball backer anyway, which is very similar to the way we set edges, you know, out of our four down front and five down front. So he loves that versatility to never, you know, hopefully never get in a pinch to where we're having to throw, you know, D tackles out at the end to finish a game, you know, because of injury or whatever, you know. Um, so it was nice to have him for a day and um really like what he did. Then just, you know, as a pass rusher, you can't never have enough of those guys, you know, for on game day. Like two-minute rushing when, you know, guys, you know, guys need to need a spell, like let's throw a fresh player out there instead of, you know, having a guy stay out there for a whole drive and and just be dead by the end of the drive. Let's put possibly put him out there and let him rush, you know, two or three snaps, give the guys a break, you know, spell and then rotate them back in. So, just utilizing his versatility is big. Hopefully we can get another day uh as camp goes on. >> What stood out to me is that Caceric said that this was always part of the plan. Even though the 49ers were obviously short on edge rushers that one practice, so it made most sense to toss Jaden Duggar in there for that one session, they wanted to do it entering training camp because they're trying to make this guy as adaptable as possible. He also ended that by saying hopefully we get another practice to stick Jaden Duggar in there. They set the edge in a very similar way as a defensive end as they do at linebacker. So there is that compatibility between those two positions. The unifying theme here defensively is length. We've seen this proliferation over the past decade plus on the offensive side, especially in Kyle's offense of, you know, guys like CMC do everything. you know, KD's lined up at all bunch of different positions. So, is it even necessary now for defenses to to counter with with what we're talking about this kind of versatility to combat those offenses? >> No, you have to. Yeah, you have to. When you look at I don't know offensive teams game plan, but I I figure it's really easy. You kind come up line up, do the same thing over and over. But if you take a guy from here, put him there, a guy from here, put him there, like why is he in this position? What's happening? Who do I set the protection to? Do I say it to Fred? Do I say it to Romelo? I said the duggery like I think that's presents the challenges for um for offenses and so for Raheem to come here bring this versatile package to us versatile scheme to us for John Lynch and you know kind of draft these type of players like telling you it's going to be some really good stuff for years to come and so we're just getting started. I think KJ Wright has a very very bright future when it comes to coaching and he thinks the 49ers have a bright future as a defense as they evolve into this new era. Combine the talent, the tall talent that they've added and of course they've got a good prototype in Fred Warner, somebody who arrived way back in 2018 as a much taller than average linebacker who obviously has succeeded beyond anybody's wildest expectations. But now they're doubling down on that freakish blueprint and they're doing it at multiple positions and they're trying to blur the line between those positions. And I think that KJ Wright, 37 years old, not too far removed from his NFL career, somebody who understands the vision, somebody who played against Fred Warner, Andre Greenlaw, and now gets to coach guys like Jaden Duggar and Larry Worth and Nick Martin. He was a very complimentary of Nick Martin, who's also in that feverback competition. Really, really neat to see how this is all uniquely developing. 49ers assistant coaches, they do this during OTAAS. They do this during training camp. We get to hear from all of the highest level 49ers assistants. So, I'm going to take you into that room to give you as much intel as possible. >> You were unusually tall for a linebacker. So, is Fred. Now you've added Jaden Duggar, Larry Worth. This it seems to me that this is this linebacker room has unusual length. Obviously that's >> Yes, it's hard. >> I know. I'm I'm following. >> Oh, well it and it's obviously an intentional kind of focus from from the front office. Uh do you think that this is the sign of an evolution in the game where I guess more length clogged passing lanes is is huge? >> I'm telling you, it's hard for quarterbacks, man. Fred made a play yesterday. I don't know if y'all saw the layer king, >> but yeah, it's like this this versus this. It's it's a game of interest. And so when I look at linebackers in college, I look at their wingspan. I look at their height, you know, I mean, I just see how much ground and space that they can cover. That is really hard for quarterbacks. And imagine you got, you know, a a Fred and a Green got long arms, too. And a Duggar like just covering all this grass, you know what I mean? So when I look at guys, this is something that intrigues me about them. um their personality, their their physical traits. So, I'm a huge fan of tall linebackers, but like I said earlier, does have its pros and >> cons. Nate Hobs, you you spoke of raising the game. I was that fair to say that yesterday was his best practice with all those pass breakups so far. >> Well, yeah. You know, to me, I think, you know, Nate had uh he he had missed the last part of OTAAS and he missed a little bit of part of the uh coming into training camp. So, I think that's kind of like he's getting his feet under him now. he understands what we want him to do. He's doing those type of things and I think that's what's going to make Nate a lot better football player. You know, again, I knew Nate when he was with over with the Raiders. So, I knew Nate and then I knew, you know, I watched him a little bit at Green Bay. He's, you know, what he did over there. So, we understand the type of player he is. Now, let's put him in a position to where he can go out there and play the way we had him or they had him when he was with the Raiders. >> Obviously, yeah, he saw a lot more success with the Raiders. What What does this staff attribute that to? I know he played inside more with the Raiders. Is that something that that you guys have taken note of as well? >> Well, the good thing is he got the ability to do both, you know. So, you know, we try to cross train our guys because we know on any given Sunday, you may have nine or 10 guys up. And so, you can't just say, "Hey, this guy can only play one position." You know, most of the time, corners like Demo, uh we're we're going through that right now with with Stout, uh uh Nate has that ability. Um, uh, TIG has that ability. You know, we looking for other guys say, "Okay, can you play two positions? Can you play this position and be good at that position?" So, if a number goes down during the course of a game, this not the first time you're going out there. It's not the first time you played that position. So, we're looking for those guys to do that. And we could see that Nate has that ability and now we adding to what we've always done in other places. >> What was Stout in particular? I know Raheem calls it the star position, right? That's what Ramsay play for the Rams kind of all over the the formation. >> So you're saying that that the goal is to get >> multiple guys able to play in different spots. You could kind of make it more amorphous and adaptable. >> Yeah, you can because now not only do you have nine or 10 guys up, you may have 12 guys because if one guy goes down, hey Stout, I know we had you at training camp. Can you go outside? Hey Demo, we know you had you at training camp. Can you go back inside? Can you do those things if you lose a guy? And a lot of times we're not waiting for that game to show up. We want to experiment during the course of training camp where there's really no spotlight, there's no danger. You're just getting them experience and exposure. And and you know, yeah, the star position is what we, you know, everybody call the nickel, but really it's just it's a nickel position, but at the end of the day, it's our job to make sure that our guys are crossrained and not just playing one position. >> How are the safeties looking? I know we talked so much about the corners. The safeties in particular, have you been happy with them? >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Those guys are doing fantastic. You know, when you look at uh you know, the guys that we got back there, we we brought in a couple of guys. We got some other guys kind of moving over. So now we got some we created competition there and that helps us a lot. You know, I know when I watched their tape last year, I seen like five or six guys back there, you know, on tape. So now we're trying to solidify that position. Hey, can we get, you know, can we get our guys to play for 18 or 19 or 20 weeks other than having a guy play here four got five games, another guy play four or five games. You know, to me, I think that kind of hurts you because that guy doesn't get consistency. You know, you create that consistency during OTAAS and then training camp and now he can talk to his friend that's out there. He understands what's going on and that's how you actually get communication between the safeties and get better. We touched on this really briefly the last time, but your last year in the league, you were teammates with John Lynch. >> Yeah. >> Right. John watches practice from the safeties vantage point. He loves it in center field. How much like specific GMs don't normally give coaching feedback, but because he played safety, how much do you get to talk to him about that position in particular? >> Oh, a lot. I mean to me, you know, like like he he may come by and ask, you know, uh not about what we're teaching, but about what he may have seen on film, like, oh, okay, I seen a guy did this, you know, uh what is his thought process? Because he wants to know how how is he evaluating the players correctly and not through his eyes, but through our eyes. And and to me, I think that's only fair that he gets a chance to come in and say, "Hey, you know what? I'm not going to tell you how to coach your guys. I'm not going to tell you what to do, but again, if you explain to me what he's doing, that helps me evaluate better.

title: The BEST 49ers news of the season just hit...
text: I just left that 49ers practice field. The best practice and the best news so far of this young season. Kyle Shanahan retook the lectern for his first post-accident press conference and that was right after the 49ers truly got after it, their longest session. Back and forth it went. Upton Stout, I have to say, is going to be a star in two senses of the word. That was the position that Jalen Ramsey played under Raheem Morris in LA. Adaptable, all over the back end. Pick six today for Upton Stout and he flipped over the goal line. A little bit of superstar style for the young player. More superstar style coming from De'Shawn Skribbling. Neon green shoes for the 49ers rookie wide receiver. Bold fashion choice, something that Deebo Samuel did in his first practice back with the 49ers. Normally, you don't see a rookie put on those types of shoes because well, you've got to deliver if you're making a fashion statement like that. And De'Shawn Skribbling, first practice back at team drills, did deliver. Brock Purdy's first throw today, outbreaker, complete. De'Shawn Skribbling who just looks the part. The guy is big, he moves well, he catches everything thrown his direction. >> I wouldn't really say nothing's been easy, you know. Um just kind of adapting to how everything is up here, you know, just the tempo of everything. Um nothing has been too hard um for me, but I also feel like just the play speed level, you know, kind of just timing the snap, being able to jump off the ball full speed and get into my route, you know, it's definitely different from college and just clapping, you know, or just you know, having like a silent count versus having an actual cadence. >> You can tell he's a humble guy, very buttoned up. Son of a marine and you know, maybe you could even say the anti-Brandon Aiyuk. 49ers didn't want any drama at that receiver position. De'Shawn Shrubling is a no-nonsense guy. Does have the flashy shoes, but so far when he's been available during team drills, he has performed up to the fashion choice. A lot happened at practice today. Headlined by Kyle Shanahan's removal of sunglasses. Didn't have sunglasses when he was out there on that field for the 49ers. That indicated that big progress has been made since the concussion. And then Kyle Shanahan surprised us by taking the lectern in the media room instead of Clay Kubiak, the offensive coordinator, who was scheduled to go today. And I'll have to say that Kyle Shanahan seemed very sharp and fresh, which is big big news. He did say that he's going to coach the 49ers preseason opener against the Tennessee Titans, which is coming up on Thursday. So, Kyle still has some headaches and fatigue from the concussion suffered in that car accident, but by and large, it looks like the 49ers leader is back and ready to go and there cannot be any news that is better than that. Here are Kyle Shanahan's initial impressions of this 49ers team. >> I like our team. You know, I feel like we came into this camp better on paper than we did last year. Um just with a number of rookies we were depending on last year got to play more and I love the guys that we've added this year. Um by no means do I, you know, see how we are come week one. We still got a lot of work to do. I mean, some days we take a step forward, the next day we take two steps back. Um but that's training camp. And a number of the guys that we really want to push to work with, those guys aren't always out there. Um so, just fighting through those things. >> Now, as far as the car accident, there isn't much more to talk about on that front. It was an accident. Kyle Shanahan took responsibility and those of us who are normal move on with our lives very rationally. Shanahan did add one more piece of information that he had not wanted to be public up until this point. He said that he thought that his Tesla's autopilot feature was on. He's not sure if he accidentally turned it off or it malfunctioned. He still took full responsibility for the accident. He said, "Autopilot or not, I needed It's my responsibility for the car to stay on its side of the road, but just one more detail added." Remember that when I was in Kyle Shanahan's office, that was not even 2 weeks ago and he was looking in much rougher shape back then. Today, again, you saw him up there. He might shave the mustache, by the way, even though he says it might have saved his life with the visor splitting his his face nearly in half there, but Kyle Shanahan said that the the mustache might not last [music] even though his friends have said, "You got to keep it because it might have saved your life." Anyway, business as usual for Kyle Shanahan at the podium is a good thing. On to what happened at practice. There's Grayson Halton. I want you to keep that rookie number 93 in your mind here as we go through this video of the sled drill with Chris Kaseereck because there's a cool little twist at the finish. Romello Height, we'll hear from him today. 49ers rookie second-round pick. There is a look at James Thompson and Sebastian Valdez. Two defensive tackles, young defensive tackles and Bryson Eason on the left there. Another young defensive tackle turning heads. There's Grayson Halton coming back in for round two. He volunteered for round two. So, 49ers Chris Kaseereck's going to like that. There was only one defensive lineman set to go there at the very end. So, one of the sled spots was open. Halton, who went at the start of the drill, decided to go in for more. And when we talk about what happened in practice today, Grayson Halton, he might be the most vocal player out on that field. He had a big run stop during the very competitive session and let out another bellow. You can hear it on the sidelines whenever Grayson Halton out of Oklahoma makes a play. He definitely has been impressive for the 49ers over the course of the last few practices ever since he came back from that bone bruise in his knee. If you go up to my X account, I've got a long long list of highlights from today's practice because it was a long session, but we'll begin with Brock Purdy who had been essentially flawless against this 49ers defense, what 24 of 28 missing his top five wide receivers over the previous two practices. Today, Purdy threw a pair of interceptions. Maybe even two pick-sixes. One of them was a pick-six for sure. I told you about Upton Stoutt flipping over the goal line. The first one though came during a timed period of hurry-up offense in the red zone. So, what they did is they put the score the score up on the board. It was 26-21. Defense was ahead of the offense. They gave the offense 20 seconds. Essentially two plays with no timeouts from the 10-yard line. And the first go-round, Purdy hit Sneaky McCormick, a running back for about a 7-yard gain to the three. Clock was ticking. Purdy got the hurry-up offense all sorted out and got the snap off with about 7 seconds left. So, it was the final play, fourth down from the 3-yard line. He found Luke Farrell for the touchdown. Now, Farrell, that's that's quite the story. He only had 11 catches last year. Wasn't very good for the 49ers last year. Was a big-time free agent pick up for them, but they needed more from him, and it looks like they may get more from Luke Farrell. He's become one of Purdy's most reliable targets over this training camp, including the recipient of the touchdown pass from Brock Purdy on that fourth down. Then the first team offense went at it again, and on fourth down Purdy was looking for De'Anthony Robinson. Nobody was open. Clock was expiring down 26 to 21. So, he had to force a ball in there. He can't just throw that away. Deommodore Lenoir cuz Robinson wasn't open stepped in front of it and it would have been a 100-yard pick-six. So, Lenoir's had a good camp. The 49ers DBs, I think, really enjoy playing under Raheem Morris. And in this particular instance, Deommodore Lenoir got a big play. Second team went, we saw Mac Jones roll out and he took advantage of the rookie receiver Wesley Grimes' height, 6'2". On the roll out, we saw Mac Jones toss one high up into the air and Grimes climbed the ladder to make a nice touchdown catch. The Up and Stout interception came later after the 49ers had finished that ultra-competitive red zone time period. They're back to normal move the ball stuff and Up and Stout in front of another pass from Purdy to De'Anthony Robinson, returned it maybe 25 yards across the goal line, flipped over the line for the touchdown. And I just remembered what Raheem Morris said the other day about Up and Stout. >> Stout can play whatever he wants, you know, Stout can play linebacker. Stout can play safety. Stout can play corner. You know, right now he is our starting star. He's our starting nickel. And him going out there playing at a very high level with his hand usage, his ability to get up to the pass rush, his ability to pass rush, his ability to use his short space quickness um defend anything, whether it be zone, whether it be man. Um highly competitive young man. Um stays angry every single day. I love him. Like he's um he's got the mindset of a football player and he's got the mentality of a football player and he certainly has the movement and the skill set of a football player. >> Remember Jalen Ramsey for that LA defense? I think that Brandon Staley actually introduced that when he was the defensive coordinator of the Rams in 2020, the star position, playing everywhere, inside, outside cornerback, some linebacker, some safety. That is what Upton Stout is going to do for the 49ers. Even more confirmation from Raheem Morris, who coached Ramsey in 2021 when the Rams won a Super Bowl, even more confirmation that the 49ers are going to be emulating some of that blueprint. And up Upton Stout is with his build, I mean, he's a ball of muscle. I think that his lack of height might help him close to the line of scrimmage cuz he could squeeze in between blocks, but he still is extremely physical. His ability to even cover to the boundary, as we have seen now over the course of this training camp, I mean, he even tried to go toe-to-toe with Mike Evans. It wasn't a very fair fight with that jump ball, but this guy is a stud. And I think that he's going to fit that role that Raheem Morris asked of Jalen Ramsey in the past and is obviously an ask of this 49ers defense now. He wants to make that back end much more adaptable. Stout also had a pass break up today, a diving pass break up. Watkins was Jordan Watkins was the receiver. Reminded me a lot of Upton Stout's pass break up on fourth down in the playoffs against DeVonta Smith and the Philadelphia Eagles. That was really a a big big introductory moment for Upton Stout on the national stage. We're probably going to have several more of those highlights this season. Now, speaking of the secondary, today was Nate Hobbs's best day of practice by far. Veteran defensive back, who I think is much better playing on the inside than on the outside. I think the Packers played him out of position, but back when he was with the Raiders, he was a better inside cornerback. He had three pass break ups today. One against Jordan Watkins, one against Junior Bergen. I mean, Nate Hobbs, we hadn't heard from him all that much over the course of this training camp. We heard from him today. Jack Jones was the veteran addition at the defensive back position at cornerback who we we had actually heard from a little bit more. I mean, he's been very very active, made another play today. But, today was about Nate Hobbs on the back end. Good arrow up day for the 49ers cornerback depth. The past couple days I've been talking a lot about the offensive line because there's been a major shift there. Connor Colby is no longer taking first team reps. Connor Colby is now the second and the third team and they're also playing him at right guard on top of left guard which tells me that they're auditioning Connor Colby for a backup spot, not the starting left guard spot where Robert Jones is currently taking the first team reps. Today during one-on-ones, Connor Colby did not look good. He's not looked great throughout any of the padded portion of camp in one-on-ones. Today, he lost essentially every single rep including two that he lost to James Thompson, the defensive tackle out of the University of Illinois, the taller of the two undrafted free agent defensive tackles. It is looking rough right now for Connor Colby as the 49ers try to figure out what they're going to do at that left guard position. Will it be Robert Jones, played under Mike McDaniel in Miami? Is the option even on the roster right now? I did find out about Brett Toth's injury. I know I've done a couple shows talking about this and we I've been saying it's an undisclosed injury for Brett Toth. It is a concussion. The 49ers did disclose that today. Toth was standing on the sideline watching practice with Carver Willis who's also in the concussion protocol. Those are two potential options to compete with Robert Jones and Connor Colby at left guard, but those guys are both out of practice with concussions as we speak. So, that's something that the 49ers are going to have to resolve moving forward. They did not yet sign one of the three centers whom they worked out yesterday. A possibility is signing one of those centers and then moving Brett Toth into the starting left guard position. He might be the 49ers' best left guard option. He started a couple games for Philly last year at left guard and was actually fairly good. Then we have Romello Height. We've got to talk about Romello Height, who today had a very, very interesting few reps against Colton McKivitz in one-on-ones. But first, listen to the advice that Romello Height is taking. >> The practice I go pick Trent Williams, you know, ask him ask him what he's seeing on, you know, a certain rep and things like that. And he give me great feedback, so. >> So yes, sources tell me that it is smart to consult Trent Williams for feedback after practices. And that is what Romello Height is doing. But during one-on-ones, he had a match-up with Colton McKivitz working against right tackle. First rep, Height lost his footing, McKivitz won the rep. So then Height lined up against against McKivitz again, and he jumped offsides twice. This is something that Greg Scruggs, who's the assistant defensive line coach, and Chris Kocurek, obviously the head man in the room, they've been really, really hammering home over this training camp. They're trying to run a bunch of hard counts during these one-on-ones, trying to get these young defensive linemen to uh read those hard counts and stay onside. It didn't work two straight reps for Romello Height. Finally, he got a clean one off against McKivitz, and it went much better than his first rep. Worked outside first, but then a wicked, wicked spin move. I You know, I could even do a little bit of a spin move here. It was about that fast, actually, for Romello Height against Colton McKivitz. Spin move inside, it would have been a relatively clean win for Romello Height, who is very, very fast. Maybe the most impressive rookie on the defensive side of the ball for the 49ers of this training camp. Here is a quote from Romello Height about the cross-training happening. We talk about the 49ers' defensive roles, so versatile and adaptable under Morris. Well, one of the the key changes is that edge rushers playing and dropping back as an outside linebacker much more often. Listen to this. >> That's um, you know, I spent it coming in here, you know, to be moved around with my body type, you know, so um, I've just been, you know, being where my feet are and, you know, wherever they put me, wherever they move me around it, I just I I do it. >> Now, why don't we move to the most impressive rookie on the offensive side of the ball, De'Shawn Shribling? I've mentioned this a few times. Big for the 49ers. With height, it's been huge as well. Six colleges, six years, a lot of different schemes that he's had to learn and succeed in. Well, the 49ers believe that has made him more ready to perform right away. Same thing with Shribling. Three different colleges, three different schemes. Here are his thoughts on how that's benefited him. >> Yeah, it's kind of um, having the mindset to learn different things. Um, be able to come in and listen, ask questions, take a lot of notes, just to um, have a better understanding of offense. >> Now, since Kyle Shanahan did take the lectern today, I think it's smart to hear from Kyle Shanahan on Shribling and of course, the big injury, the one that will hurt the 49ers for this entire season, Ricky Pearsall. >> I mean, losing Ricky was a real big deal. I mean, that's um, you know, we've had a number of injuries in camp, but that's really the only one that's actually been um, not just a camp injury. Um, and losing a player like Ricky is a huge deal. Um, it ties to everybody, so um, and you you'd hope for Shribling, you hope for Mike, uh, you hope for all of that whole whole group, you know, a lot of people have to step up, but people no one here is wired exactly how Ricky is. They're all a little bit different, so you do lose a big part of what we were planning on. Um, that's where guys do have to step up. That's where it gets frustrating when guys like Shribling, you know, hurt tweak a muscle and stuff cuz yeah, you want guys to step up, but you got to train them to do it, they got to work to do it, and they got to be out there to be able to do it um, at an NFL level, which is coming real fast. >> And here is more confirmation of what I've been telling you ever since the 49ers signed Deebo Samuel, even what I've been telling you since before they signed Deebo Samuel. This is not a plug-and-play, let's put Deebo into Ricky Pearsall's old Z receiver role. They have Deebo to be Deebo, which is, I would say, a glorified gadget weapon on this offense. And again, I mean that as a compliment because Deebo is such a unique player. But Kyle Shanahan was asked about if Deebo Samuel will fill that Ricky Pearsall role. And his answer is confirmation of what we've been saying. >> Um, not really. I mean, they're just two completely different types of players. Um, so, you know, Deebo is someone that, you know, as we were hoping it would work out, you know, depending on Deebo's other opportunities and what it could be here, but that was something that we were hoping for a long time could work out and and ended up working out for both of us. Um, but that, you know, the Ricky thing changed nothing. >> And as we speak right now, back in Canton, Ohio, Roger Craig inducted into the Hall of Fame. Big congratulations to the first man to go 1,000 1,000 and great, great group of 49ers on hand for Roger Craig, one of the nicest people you'll ever meet. Extremely, extremely deserving of being inducted into the Hall of Fame. In fact, that one would argue I definitely would. I think many surrounding the 49ers would argue that it is way past time for Roger Craig to be inducted into that Hall of Fame. Sad news has become public, though, and this came via Roger Craig's induction speech. >> Today, there's another chapter I want to share. I've been diagnosed with vascular dementia that my doctors believe may be related at least in part to the concussions I experienced during my career. >> Our prayers are with Roger Craig and his family. I am very happy that he was able to enjoy his induction into the Hall of Fame, that it didn't take Our prayers are with Roger Craig and his family. Happy that he was able to enjoy this induction into the Hall of Fame. And this means a whole heck of a lot to 49ers fans and the organization, but obviously it means the most to Roger Craig. And congratulations to him. Obviously a sobering note delivered at his Hall of Fame induction speech. Make sure to check out the post on X and all the work on the San Francisco Standard for the full rundown. I know I give you guys almost everything here. There's a lot to go through. Even another Junior Bergen catch today thrown a little bit behind him by Curtis Rourke who seemed a tad late on some of his throws, but Bergen tough tough receiver. I still think I still think he's going to make that 53-man roster. We will see with some of these preseason games. They're going to be big for the defensive tackle competition. See James Thompson, Bryson Eason, Solano of all that the Hulk work, but we're going to get to see Bergen. Hopefully Jacob Cowing can be back by then. Only one injury added today. It's Luke Gifford the linebacker with a hamstring injury for the 49ers. Otherwise, you're getting eight guys back like a De'Shawn Shribling. And the 49ers now are going to have a players day off Sunday. Block three of practice is finished, so we're essentially halfway through training camp. Starting on Monday, it's going to be block four. Remember, they're going two days on full practice. So, Monday will be a practice here at Levi's or at the facility across from Levi's. Tuesday will be a joint practice here with the Tennessee Titans and their coach Robert Saleh. Wednesday's going to be walk-through day. Thursday, Levi's Stadium. I guess this is time to flip this around. We can take a look at the helmet and we can take a look at the stadium on Thursday, the preseason opener against Saleh and the Tennessee Titans will happen right here. So, thanks for watching. title: 49ers just signaled that new TROUBLE's brewing at a key spot...
text: A big update on DeJon Shribling and the 49ers receivers from Sonoma. And a word on Laken Tomlinson, possibly the most durable 49er of the Shanahan era. Started 80 straight games for them over five seasons. The left guard tells me that he had a procedure to remove a bone spur from his left heel and is feeling as good as he has had in years. He's been training hard and hopes to join a team needing a veteran guard soon. But some worse news for the 49ers. They worked out three centers. Ominous news at center, just like the fog coming in over the Golden Gate Bridge. Three centers, Doug Kramer, Joe McKalaski, and Lecitus Smith worked out for the 49ers today, likely because Brett Toth, the backup center, is going to be out for a little while longer. Look, Lombardi yourself makes a cameo from Sonoma. Foggy in the city this morning, sunny in Sonoma. Then then you guys know I like to feature Bay Area eateries, the Sunflower Cafe in Sonoma. That was the chicken and avocado grilled cheese and then the steak and eggs. And look, it's the star of the show. Anyway, let's get on with it. Let's get on with the news. Back in the city, 49ers made these three workouts today. We'll see if they sign one of these centers, but Brett Toth has missed the last couple practices and it's been an undisclosed injury. He is the next man up beyond Jake Brendel at center, which is very, very important in this 49ers offense. Think back to the disaster of 2020. I know that so many guys got hurt that season, but one thing that was really, really bad for the 49ers is that they got to like their fourth or their fifth string center and it turned into an absolute disaster. It's not like the other offensive line positions where you could plug somebody in and you know, of course you got to teach him the assignments of that particular spot. They're not though at left guard, left tackle, right guard, or right tackle, the communication nerve of the entire offensive line. The center is responsible for making sure that the protections are called right for all five offensive linemen. Really the conduit of communication between the quarterback and everybody else. In this Shanahan scheme, the center is really important. And once centers start going down, you run the risk of absolute catastrophe at that position. And with Brett Toth, right now the 49ers working these three guys out, it really signals that Brett Toth might be out for an extended or, you know, period of time or or a few practice. I don't know how long it's going to be, but I do remember 2020 was so ugly for the 49ers. So, we should look to establish exactly where the 49ers are at at this center position because right now as it stands, they haven't signed one of these tryouts yet. But as it stands, the next man up might be the rookie Carver Willis who currently is in the concussion protocol. I am about to share the 49ers 90-man depth chart with you. There you go. We have a close look at it and you could see here at center Toth is hurt, undisclosed injury. Next man up might be Drake Nugent who actually has been impressive in the 49ers over the course of this training camp, but he is an undersized player. There's no question about it. That's why he is exclusively a center. The 49ers aren't even thinking about Drake Nugent to play the guard position. And then of course there's Carver Willis. I talked so much about him in the off-season. He already did some cross training at center in his final collegiate season at the University of Washington, but the issue there is that center has got such a large cerebral load. It's, you know, I don't remember a single time over the course of the last decade that a rookie has stepped into center in a Kyle Shanahan offense. So, you know, I think this is the final season under contract for the 49ers starter, Jake Brendel, and maybe the 49ers are thinking about grooming Carver Willis to play that center position in 2027 and beyond, but I think it might be ambitious to expect him to step in there here right away in 2026. Hence, the three workouts today. Kramer, McKalaski, and Lecitus Smith, all players with center backgrounds and center experience, and essentially centers at this NFL level. Doug Kramer has actually played some fullback as well, goal line fullback in the NFL. And we know that the 49ers like their centers to be athletic. That is imperative for San Francisco. You've got to be able to reach block, you have to reach the second level. It's important at guard as well, but that level of guard position it's going to be more of an enforcer's spot. That's going to be your strongest interior offensive lineman. You might be okay with a little more of a finesse orientation for your right guard, and especially your center, but there's got to be cerebral mastery at that center spot. Other otherwise things can get ugly very, very quickly. So, that is a position of alarm, I think, to watch right now for the 49ers. You guys know me, I'm balanced about these injuries. I'll tell you that a lot of them are overblown, and especially at receiver. I told you this would be a big receiver update, and and it certainly will be. The receiver position for the 49ers is not in a in a dire spot at all. Both De'Jon Stripling and Mike Evans, I don't even have the injury shades for these two guys, because if there were game tomorrow, both would play, both would be at 100% capacity. The 49ers are managing them, and hamstring stiffness for Stripling, and what they say is a quad strain for Mike Evans as they should manage a quad strain for Mike Evans. He's 33 years old. He's the walking Hall of Famer. He doesn't need to be on that practice field anymore than you actually need him there to install a few plays and then you can move forward because he's going to be fine for you over the course of the regular season regardless of how much he practices in training camp. So a receiver you're essentially waiting for Christian Kirk right now and I think in the case of Jacob Cowling we can get into this over the course of the show. And I think that he's in the midst of being leapfrogged on this depth chart by somebody like Junior Bergen, maybe even by somebody like a Will Pauling. That is a punt returner competition as well. So whereas the injuries at receiver are definitely overblown, the injuries along the offensive line are quietly threatening how the 49ers may operate in times when they need to break glass in case of emergency. And there are always emergencies in the NFL because injuries are going to happen over the course of the regular season. So for example, we've talked about the dramatic shift at left guard over the course of the past couple days. Connor Colby no longer taking snaps with the ones. Connor Colby instead now taking snaps with the twos and the threes. That has meant Robert Jones is taking snaps with the ones. Left guard is the one starting position that is still not determined for the 49ers. Uh would the 49ers be comfortable with Robert Jones starting? Is the starter even on their roster? Is somebody like Carver Willis uh an actual candidate for left guard? Is that being put on hold by the concussion protocol? I mean there's so many different ways to to look at what's happening at left guard. And then you realize you need depth at both left and right guard and that's probably why Connor Colby is now playing at right guard during practice. But now you have this center issue pop up. And I think know, when we didn't know Brett Toth's injury, we still don't, but we didn't want to jump to any conclusions. Now though, the 49ers are working out centers, and the only reason you'd work out centers is because Toth might be out for at least a few more practices. Worst case scenario, he's out for a longer time beyond that, and you realize that you need to fill a backup center spot that is in a sketchy, precarious position as we speak. And that has burned the 49ers in the past before. So, I think that whereas receiver is going to be fine with Stribling and Mike Evans. Even without Ricky Pearsall, if you have both of those guys, you've now signed Deebo Samuel, you're going to get Christian Kirk back. You have De'Anthony Robinson, Jordan Watkins is having a good camp. Somebody like Junior Bergen might be emerging. And Brock Purdy, I wrote about this on the San Francisco Standard. And this is something that is worth putting up on the screen right now. This is the article that came out today. I'm going to go ahead and toss this into the description. I'll send it to Mike. Brock Purdy was down his top five receivers over the past two practices. So, that is Mike Evans, that is Ricky Pearsall, that is De'Anthony Stribling, that is Christian Kirk, and that is George Kittle, who I think very clearly fits in with the 49ers top five receivers. Despite being down his top five receivers, Brock Purdy went 24 of 28 with several perfect deep dime touchdown passes. Two of the receivers who have caught bombs over the past two practices in that 24 of 28 stretch are Kadeem Hardison two days ago and Malik Turner, who's better known as a gunner on the 49ers special teams unit. So, Purdy is going to be able to make it work to a certain degree regardless of who's out there. We I mean, we saw it last year for the 49ers. They won six straight. They beat Philadelphia in the uh NFC wild card game. Purdy put up numbers like this. This was his third down performance. Further to the right and further up is where you want to be. I mean, it it was an awesome awesome performance for Brock Purdy. But, the main line of my article, the main graph of my article is here. text: curious where you feel like the defense is at compared to maybe where you thought it would be. What do you want this defense to be? Uh definitely again stressing the fundamentals and techniques uh tackling defeating blocks. Uh elite communication is one of our standards. Just occupying more uh gaps up front. some of the younger guys on your defense like Kane Madano and um Ali, you know, h how do you feel like they're progressing in your system? Uh you know, compared to their skill sets because they're athletic guys. Are those guys flashing for you? >> Uh well, let's start with Ali. Ali's been good. And with Kane, you know, Kane missed uh the first part of camp. But what we're looking for our guys is the one to be close competing. Uh having the proper footwork, great eye placement, um not playing with their hands, but playing with their feet, you know, and I challenge them to just if they're close enough and still competing in a one-on-one where then you throw, you know, 20 other guys on that in that on that field, the timing changes. You know, maybe it's not a perfect throw and you have an opportunity. So the biggest thing is, you know, I don't want to see them winning without using technique. I want to see them winning with technique. So we're still stressing the techniques and fundamentals. >> And my next question, um, you mentioned elite communication. Have there been some examples or some players that have stood out that are really exemplifying that elite communication? >> Yeah, there there's always times where you see guys going in from uh, >> you know, we have some checks within the uh, the offense. I mean, within the defense, if you can see guys communicating, getting us into one call or out of one call based off what they're seeing and having that flexibility, but to do that, you got to make sure everyone's on the same page. And so, we call it the communication hub. Has to be uh in line with each other so that everyone gets to communication and on the same page. So, it's been good for us. >> Morning Donte. Um, I think one of the things you emphasized during OTAAS and mini camp was your communication skills, teaching and the learning process for the players. Now that we've shifted into pads and actual practices and stuff like that, how have you seen that kind of play out as far as them picking up what you're teaching them in the film room? >> Yeah, you know, as a coach, you just want to look at the progress, you know, and see, are we are we ascending in the right way when it comes to that? And again, it's not perfect by a long shot, but it's much better than where we were. So that means there's progress in that way. And so from a coach perspective, that's one of our evaluations in terms of, you know, where were we in the spring compared to first week of training camp to now. And from coaches, we want to see that ascending uh course, so to speak. And as long as we're not going backwards and we continue to move forward, uh then we're on the right path to getting to what we want eventually. >> On those days where you maybe do go backwards, how do you kind of rectify that situation for the next day? >> Oh, that's easy. And they're kind of still playing kind of tentatively a little bit. But then, you know, letting that just let just go. I'd rather you go full speed and make a mistake than to be too slow and be right, you know. Uh and so in doing that in doing a lesson plan, when you create a lesson plan, you have to pretty much hit on everyone's learning styles because everyone learns differently. And so whether I'm an audio learner or visual learner or I'm a read and write learner or kinesesthetic learner, you got to be able to tap onto each person's learning style within that lesson plan. Uh so that everyone feels connected. And so we try to do that as coaches so that you're hitting on every player in that room. Uh and then you get out and you walk through and that's our process. >> Is that difficult with like 40 to 50 guys at this point in the season? >> Yeah, of course it is. Those guys, I don't know if that's surprising or not. Um, you know, there's some expectations there with those two guys. And then getting Dorance back has been great for us as he continues to work his way back through. Uh, we talked about Josh earlier. I think that he's shown some things, but I would like to just, you know, I think John Baptist has done a few things the last couple of days that's really caught your eye and you can see his athleticism and so, um, that room is continuing to grow and kind of like the depth in that room right now. So, I'm excited about the competition that's flowing in that room. >> Yeah. >> You talk a lot about the competition, joint practices. What do you like most about having a joint practice with another team where you get to kind of get a little bit of a different look than maybe take it on the same team every day? you know, it goes whether it's another team or our or our offense, you can never lose sight of the physicality of the game and the fundamentals and techniques. And so, what we'll be looking for as a staff is making sure our guys don't lose their mind and lose their techniques, uh, because there's another color jersey across from them. And so, uh, that's where the time on task would come in and the majority of our guys come together and just, hey, listen, we don't know, we don't care who's in front of us. It's about what we're doing, our assignments, our alignment, and our execution is what's most important. >> And mindset wise going into a joint practice and then going into the preseason game on Friday for you as a defensive coordinator for the first time. What's your mindset going into both of those types of, you know, atmospheres? >> Just want to see guys with great effort, guys competing, uh, and all while doing so with great effort, great technique, fundamentals is what we're looking for. But the competition is going to be there. So that'll be great for us to see and just see who can do what. You know, it's not going to be, you know, all this. We just want to see, hey, who can line up, just play football, show some physicality. Uh, and that's a great it'd be a great evaluation for us from a personnel standpoint. >> Coach Adam Epste 910 the fan. Do you want your secondary taking more chances in a joint practice rather than Friday's preseason game? >> Uh, more chances in terms of >> turnovers. Well, that's a mindset even if they're sitting in the locker room talking. Um, we want to have that creative create takeaways in both practices, our practices against each other, joint practices, uh, games. It doesn't matter if you're if you're on the grass, you got to have a create takeaways mindset. No matter who you're going against, >> how would you break down the competition at linebacker right now in your mind? >> Oh, I'm enjoying it. I'm enjoying it. You got guys of all ages, all experiences, and guys are just uh fighting their butts off, giving great effort, talking on the football field, and uh I love where that competition is in the room right now. >> Appreciate it, coach. >> Thank you.
